H1: A primitive word; father, in a literal and immediate, or figurative and remote application). In the KJV it is rendered: chief, (fore-)father(-less), X patrimony, principal.
H2: (Aramaic) corresponding to אָב. In the KJV it is rendered: father.
H3: From the same as אָבִיב; a green plant. In the KJV it is rendered: greenness, fruit.
H4: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֵב. In the KJV it is rendered: fruit.
H5: Of foreign origin; Abagtha, a eunuch of Xerxes. In the KJV it is rendered: Abagtha.
H6: A primitive root; properly, to wander away, i.e. lose oneself; by implication to perish (causative, destroy). In the KJV it is rendered: break, destroy(- uction), + not escape, fail, lose, (cause to, make) perish, spend, X and surely, take, be undone, X utterly, be void of, have no way to flee.
H7: (Aramaic) corresponding to אָבַד. In the KJV it is rendered: destroy, perish.
H8: Active of participle of אָבַד; (concrete) wretched or (abstract) destructin. In the KJV it is rendered: perish.
H9: From אָבַד; concrete, something lost; abstract, destruction, i.e. Hades. In the KJV it is rendered: lost.
H10: The same as אֲבֵדָה, miswritten for אֲבַדּוֹן; a perishing. In the KJV it is rendered: destruction.
H11: Intensive from אָבַד; abstract, a perishing; concrete, Hades. In the KJV it is rendered: destruction.
H12: From אָבַד; a perishing. In the KJV it is rendered: destruction.
H13: From אָבַד; a perishing. In the KJV it is rendered: destruction.
H14: A primitive root; to breathe after, i.e. (figuratively) to be acquiescent. In the KJV it is rendered: consent, rest content will, be willing.
H15: From אָבָה; longing. In the KJV it is rendered: desire.
H16: From אָבָה (in the sense of bending toward); the papyrus. In the KJV it is rendered: swift.
H17: From אָבָה (in the sense of desiring); want. In the KJV it is rendered: sorrow.
H18: From אָבַס; a manger or stall. In the KJV it is rendered: crib.
H19: From an unused root (apparently meaning to turn); brandishing of a sword. In the KJV it is rendered: point.
H20: Of uncertain derivation; a melon (only plural). In the KJV it is rendered: melon.
H21: From אָב; fatherly; Abi, Hezekiah's mother. In the KJV it is rendered: Abi.
H22: From אָב and אֵל; father (i.e. possessor) of God; Abiel, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Abiel.
H23: From אָב and אָסַף; father of gathering (i.e. gatherer); Abiasaph, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Abiasaph.
H24: From an unused root (meaning to be tender); green, i.e. a young ear of grain; hence, the name of the month Abib or Nisan. In the KJV it is rendered: Abib, ear, green ears of corn (not maize).
H25: From אָב and גִּבְעוֹן; father (i.e. founder) of Gibon; Abi-Gibon, perhaps an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: father of Gibeon.
H26: Or shorter Abiygal; from אָב and גִּיל; father (i.e. source) of joy; Abigail or Abigal, the name of two Israelitesses. In the KJV it is rendered: Abigal.
H27: From אָב and דִּין; father of judgment (i.e. judge); Abidan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Abidan.
H28: From אָב and יָדַע; father of knowledge (i.e. knowing); Abida, a son of Abraham by Keturah. In the KJV it is rendered: Abida, Abidah.
H29: Or prolonged Abiyahuw; from אָב and יָהּ; father (i.e. worshipper) of Jah; Abijah, the name of several Israelite men and two Israelitesses. In the KJV it is rendered: Abiah, Abijah.
H30: From אָב and הוּא; father (i.e. worshipper) of Him (i.e. God); Abihu, a son of Aaron. In the KJV it is rendered: Abihu.
H31: From אָב and הוֹד; father (i.e. possessor) of renown; Abihud, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Abihud.
H32: Or (more correctly) Abiychayil; from 1 and חָ֫יִל; father (i.e. possessor) of might; Abihail or Abichail, the name of three Israelites and two Israelitesses. In the KJV it is rendered: Abihail.
H33: From אֲבִיעֵ֫זֶר with the article inserted; father of the Ezrite; an Abiezrite or descendant of Abiezer; -- Abiezrite.
H34: From אָבָה, in the sense of want (especially in feeling); destitute. In the KJV it is rendered: beggar, needy, poor (man).
H35: From אָבָה; provocative of desire; the caper berry (from its stimulative taste). In the KJV it is rendered: desire.
H36: From אָב and טוּב; father of goodness (i.e. good); Abitub, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Abitub.
H37: From אָב and טָל; father of dew (i.e. fresh); Abital, a wife of King David. In the KJV it is rendered: Abital.
H38: From אָב and יָם; father of (the) sea (i.e. seaman); Abijam (or Abijah), a king of Judah. In the KJV it is rendered: Abijam.
H39: From אָב and an elsewhere unused (probably foreign) word; father of Mael (apparently some Arab tribe); Abimael, a son of Joktan. In the KJV it is rendered: Abimael.
H40: From אָב and מֶ֫לֶך; father of (the) king; Abimelek, the name of two Philistine kings and of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Abimelech.
H41: From אָב and נָדַב; father of generosity (i.e. liberal); Abinadab, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Abinadab.
H42: From אָב and נֹ֫עַם; father of pleasantness (i.e. gracious); Abinoam, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Abinoam.
H43: Contracted from אֲבִיאָסָף; Ebjasaph, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ebiasaph.
H44: From אָב and עֵ֫זֶר; father of help (i.e. helpful); Abiezer, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Abiezer.
H45: From אָב and and an unused root of uncertain. derivation; probably, father of strength (i.e. valiant); Abialbon, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Abialbon.
H46: From אָבַר; mighty (spoken of God). In the KJV it is rendered: mighty (one).
H47: For אֲבִיר; --angel, bull, chiefest, mighty (one), stout(-hearted), strong (one), valiant.
H48: From אָב and רוּם; father of height (i.e. lofty); Abiram, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Abiram.
H49: From אָב and שָׁגָה; father of error (i.e. blundering); Abishag, a concubine of David. In the KJV it is rendered: Abishag.
H50: From אָב and שׁ֫וֹעַ; father of plenty (i.e. prosperous); Abishua, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Abishua.
H51: From אָב and שׁוּר; father of (the) wall (i.e. perhaps mason); Abishur, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Abishur.
H52: Or (shorter) Abshay; from אָב and שָׁי; father of a gift (i.e. probably generous); Abishai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Abishai.
H53: Or (shortened) Abshalowm; from אָב and שָׁלוֹם; father of peace (i.e. friendly); Abshalom, a son of David; also (the fuller form) a later Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Abishalom, Absalom.
H54: Contracted from אָב and יָתַר; father of abundance (i.e. liberal); Ebjathar, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Abiathar.
H55: A primitive root; probably to coil upward. In the KJV it is rendered: mount up.
H56: A primitive root; to bewail. In the KJV it is rendered: lament, mourn.
H57: From אָבַל; lamenting. In the KJV it is rendered: mourn(-er, -ing).
H58: From an unused root (meaning to be grassy); a meadow. In the KJV it is rendered: plain.
H59: From אָבֵל; a meadow; Abel, the name of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Abel.
H60: From אָבַל; lamentation. In the KJV it is rendered: mourning.
H61: Apparently from אָבַל through the idea of negation; nay, i.e. truly or yet. In the KJV it is rendered: but, indeed, nevertheless, verily.
H62: From אָבֵל and בָּ֫יִת and מַעֲכָה; meadow of Beth-Maakah; Abel of Beth-maakah, a place in Palestine:--Abel-beth-maachah, Abel of Beth-maachah.
H63: From אָבֵל and the plural of שִׁטִּים, with the article inserted; meadow of the acacias; Abel hash- Shittim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Abel-shittim.
H64: From אָבֵל and the plural of כָּ֫רֶם; meadow of vineyards; Abel-Keramim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: plain of the vineyards.
H65: From אָבֵל and מְחֹלַת; meadow of dancing; Abel-Mecholah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Abel-meholah.
H66: From אָבֵל and מָ֫יִם; meadow of water; Abel-Majim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Abel-maim.
H67: From אָבֵל and מִצְרָ֫יִם; meadow of Egypt; Abel-Mitsrajim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Abel-mizraim.
H68: From the root of בָּנָה through the meaning to build; a stone. In the KJV it is rendered: + carbuncle, + mason, + plummet, (chalk-, hail-, head-, sling-)stone(-ny), (divers) weight(-s).
H69: (Aramaic) corresponding to אָ֫בֶן. In the KJV it is rendered: stone.
H70: From the same as אָ֫בֶן; a pair of stones (only dual); a potter's wheel or a midwife's stool (consisting alike of two horizontal disks with a support between). In the KJV it is rendered: wheel, stool.
H71: Perhaps feminine of אָ֫בֶן; stony; Abanah, a river near Damascus. In the KJV it is rendered: Abana.
H72: From אָ֫בֶן and עֵ֫זֶר with the article inserted; stone of the help; Eben-ha-Ezer, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ebenezer.
H73: Of uncertain derivation; a belt. In the KJV it is rendered: girdle.
H74: Or (fully) Abiyner; from אָב and נֵר; father of light (i.e. enlightening); Abner, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Abner.
H75: A primitive root; to fodder. In the KJV it is rendered: fatted, stalled.
H76: (by reduplication) from an unused root (meaning to belch forth); an inflammatory pustule (as eruption). In the KJV it is rendered: blains.
H77: From an unused root probably meaning to gleam; conspicuous; Ebets, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Abez.
H78: From the same as אֲבַעְבֻּעֹת; splendid; Ibtsan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ibzan.
H79: A primitive root, probably to float away (as vapor), but used only as denominative from אָבָק; to bedust, i.e. grapple. In the KJV it is rendered: wrestle.
H80: From root of אָבַק; light particles (as volatile). In the KJV it is rendered: (small) dust, powder.
H81: Feminine of אָבָק. In the KJV it is rendered: powder.
H82: A primitive root; to soar. In the KJV it is rendered: fly.
H83: From אָבַר; a pinion. In the KJV it is rendered: (long-)wing(-ed).
H84: Feminine of אֵ֫בֶר. In the KJV it is rendered: feather, wing.
H85: Contracted from אָב and an unused root (probably meaning to be populous); father of a multitude; Abraham, the later name of Abram. In the KJV it is rendered: Abraham.
H86: Probably an Egyptian word meaning kneel. In the KJV it is rendered: bow the knee.
H87: Contracted from אֲבִירָם; high father; Abram, the original name of Abraham. In the KJV it is rendered: Abram.
H88: Plural of אוֹב; water-skins; Oboth, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Oboth.
H89: Of uncertain derivation (compare אֲגָג); Age, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Agee.
H90: Or Agag; of uncertain derivation (compare אָגֵא); flame; Agag, a title of Amalekitish kings. In the KJV it is rendered: Agag.
H91: Patrial or patronymic from אֲגָג; an Agagite or descendent (subject) of Agag. In the KJV it is rendered: Agagite.
H92: Feminine passive participle of an unused root (meaning to bind); a band, bundle, knot, or arch. In the KJV it is rendered: bunch, burden, troop.
H93: Prob of Persian origin; a nut. In the KJV it is rendered: nut.
H94: Passive participle of אָגַר; gathered (i.e. received among the sages); Agur, a fanciful name for Solomon. In the KJV it is rendered: Agur.
H95: From the same as אָגוּר; properly, something gathered, i.e. perhaps a grain or berry; used only of a small (silver) coin. In the KJV it is rendered: piece (of) silver.
H96: From an unused root (meaning to flow down or together as drops); a reservoir. In the KJV it is rendered: drop.
H97: Dual of אֶגְלֵי.; a double pond; Eglajim, a place in Moab. In the KJV it is rendered: Eglaim.
H98: From an unused root (meaning to collect as water); a marsh; hence a rush (as growing in swamps); hence a stockade of reeds. In the KJV it is rendered: pond, pool, standing (water).
H99: Probably from the same as אֲגַם (in the sense of stagnant water); figuratively, sad. In the KJV it is rendered: pond.
H100: From the same as אֲגַם; a marshy pool (others from a different root, a kettle); by implication a rush (as growing there); collectively a rope of rushes. In the KJV it is rendered: bulrush, caldron, hook, rush.
H101: Probably from נָגַן; a bowl (as pounded out hollow). In the KJV it is rendered: basin, cup, goblet.
H102: Probably from נָגַף (through the idea of impending); a cover or heap; i.e. (only plural) wings of an army, or crowds of troops. In the KJV it is rendered: bands.
H103: A primitive root; to harvest. In the KJV it is rendered: gather.
H104: (Aramaic) of Persian origin; an epistle (as carried by a state courier or postman). In the KJV it is rendered: letter.
H105: Of uncertain derivation; a basin. In the KJV it is rendered: charger.
H106: From גָּרַף (in the sense of grasping); the clenched hand. In the KJV it is rendered: fist.
H107: Feminine of אּגְּרָה; an epistle. In the KJV it is rendered: letter.
H108: From the same as אוּד (in the sense of enveloping); a fog. In the KJV it is rendered: mist, vapor.
H109: A primitive root; to languish. In the KJV it is rendered: grieve.
H110: Probably from אָדַב (in the sense of chastisement) and אֵל; disciplined of God; Adbeel, a son of Ishmael. In the KJV it is rendered: Adbeel.
H111: Probably an orthographical variation for חֲדַד; Adad (or Hadad), an Edomite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hadad.
H112: Of uncertain derivation; Iddo, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Iddo.
H113: Or (shortened) adon; from an unused root (meaning to rule); sovereign, i.e. controller (human or divine). In the KJV it is rendered: lord, master, owner.
H114: Probably intensive for אָדוֹן; powerful; Addon, apparently an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Addon.
H115: Dual from אָדַר (in the sense of eminence); double mound; Adorajim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Adoraim.
H116: (Aramaic) of uncertain derivation; then (of time). In the KJV it is rendered: now, that time, then.
H117: From אָדַר; wide or (generally) large; figuratively, powerful. In the KJV it is rendered: excellent, famous, gallant, glorious, goodly, lordly, mighty(- ier one), noble, principal, worthy.
H118: Of Persian derivation; Adalja, a son of Haman. In the KJV it is rendered: Adalia.
H119: To show blood (in the face), i.e. flush or turn rosy. In the KJV it is rendered: be (dyed, made) red (ruddy).
H120: From אָדַם; ruddy i.e. a human being (an individual or the species, mankind, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: X another, + hypocrite, + common sort, X low, man (mean, of low degree), person.
H121: The same as אָדָם; Adam the name of the first man, also of a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Adam.
H122: From אָדַם; rosy. In the KJV it is rendered: red, ruddy.
H123: Or (fully) Edowm; from אָדֹם; red (see Gen. 25:25); Edom, the elder twin-brother of Jacob; hence the region (Idumaea) occupied by him. In the KJV it is rendered: Edom, Edomites, Idumea.
H124: From אָדַם; redness, i.e. the ruby, garnet, or some other red gem. In the KJV it is rendered: sardius.
H125: Reduplicated from אָדַם; reddish. In the KJV it is rendered: (somewhat) reddish.
H126: Contracted for אֲדָמָה; earthy; Admah, a place near the Dead Sea. In the KJV it is rendered: Admah.
H127: From אָדַם; soil (from its general redness). In the KJV it is rendered: country, earth, ground, husband(-man) (-ry), land.
H128: The same as אֲדָמָה; Adamah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Adamah.
H129: From אֲדָמָה; earthy; Adami, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Adami.
H130: Or (fully) Edowmiy; patronymic from אֱדוֹם; an Edomite, or descendants from (or inhabitants of) Edom. In the KJV it is rendered: Edomite.
H131: Plural of אָדָם; red spots; Adummim, a pass in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Adummim.
H132: Or (fully) admowniy; from אָדַם; reddish (of the hair or the complexion). In the KJV it is rendered: red, ruddy.
H133: Probably of Persian derivation: Admatha, a Persian nobleman. In the KJV it is rendered: Admatha.
H134: From the same as אָדוֹן (in the sense of strength); a basis (of a building, a column, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: foundation, socket.
H135: Intensive from the same as אָ֫דֶן; firm; Addan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Addan.
H136: Am emphatic form of אָדוֹן; the Lord (used as a proper name of God only). In the KJV it is rendered: (my) Lord.
H137: From אָדוֹן and בָּ֫זֶק; lord of Bezek; Adoni-Bezek; a Canaanitish king. In the KJV it is rendered: Adoni-bezek.
H138: Original (prolonged) Adoniyahuw; from אָדוֹן and יָהּ; lord (i.e. worshipper) of Jah; Adonijah, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Adonijah.
H139: From אָדוֹן and צֶ֫דֶק; lord of justice; Adoni-Tsedek, a Canaanitish king. In the KJV it is rendered: Adonizedec.
H140: From אָדוֹן and קוּם; lord of rising (i.e. high); Adonikam, the name of one or two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Adonikam.
H141: From אָדוֹן and רוּם; lord of height; Adoniram, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Adoniram.
H142: A primitive root; to expand, i.e. be great or (figuratively) magnificent. In the KJV it is rendered: (become) glorious, honourable.
H143: Probably of foreign derivation; perhaps meaning fire; Adar, the 12th Hebrew month. In the KJV it is rendered: Adar.
H144: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֲדָר. In the KJV it is rendered: Adar.
H145: From אָדַר; amplitude, i.e. (concrete) a mantle; also (figuratively) splendor. In the KJV it is rendered: goodly, robe.
H146: Intensive from אָדַר; ample; Addar, a place in Palestine; also an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Addar.
H147: (Aramaic) intensive, from a root corresponding to אָדַר; ample, i.e. a threshing-floor. In the KJV it is rendered: threshingfloor.
H148: (Aramaic) from the same as אּדְּרֵי, and גְּזַר; a chief diviner, or astrologer. In the KJV it is rendered: judge.
H149: (Aramaic) probably of Persian origin; quickly or carefully. In the KJV it is rendered: diligently.
H150: Of Persian origin; a daric or Persian coin. In the KJV it is rendered: dram.
H151: Contracted for אֲדֹנִירָם; Adoram (or Adoniram), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Adoram.
H152: From אָדַר and מֶ֫לֶך; splendor of (the) king; Adrammelek, the name of an Assyrian idol, also of a son of Sennacherib. In the KJV it is rendered: Adrammelech.
H153: (Aramaic) an orthographical variation for דְּרָע; an arm, i.e. (figuratively) power. In the KJV it is rendered: force.
H154: From the equivalent of אֶדְרָע; mighty; Edrei, the name of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Edrei.
H155: Feminine of אַדִּיר; something ample (as a large vine, a wide dress); also the same as אֶ֫דֶר. In the KJV it is rendered: garment, glory, goodly, mantle, robe.
H156: A primitive root; to tread out (grain). In the KJV it is rendered: thresh.
H157: Or raheb; a primitive root; to have affection for (sexually or otherwise). In the KJV it is rendered: (be-)love(-d, -ly, -r), like, friend.
H158: From אָהַב; affection (in a good or a bad sense). In the KJV it is rendered: love(-r).
H159: From אָדַשׁ; meaning the same as אֲהָבִים. In the KJV it is rendered: love.
H160: Feminine of אֲהָבִים and meaning the same. In the KJV it is rendered: love.
H161: From an unused root meaning to be united; unity; Ohad, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ohad.
H162: Apparently a primitive word expressing pain exclamatorily; Oh!. In the KJV it is rendered: ah, alas.
H163: Probably of foreign origin; Ahava, a river of Babylonia. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahava.
H164: From the same as אֹ֫הַד; united; Ehud, the name of two or three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ehud.
H165: Apparently an orthographical variation for אַיֵּה; where. In the KJV it is rendered: I will be (Hos.
H166: A primitive root; to be clear. In the KJV it is rendered: shine.
H167: A denominative from אֹ֫הֶל; to tent. In the KJV it is rendered: pitch (remove) a tent.
H168: From יַאֲהִיל; a tent (as clearly conspicuous from a distance). In the KJV it is rendered: covering, (dwelling)(place), home, tabernacle, tent.
H169: The same as אֹ֫הֶל; Ohel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ohel.
H170: In form a feminine of 'ohel, but in fact for.Oholahh; from אֹ֫הֶל; her tent (i.e. idolatrous sanctuary); Oholah, a symbol. name for Samaria. In the KJV it is rendered: Aholah.
H171: From אֹ֫הֶל and אָב; tent of (his) father; Oholiab, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Aholiab.
H172: (similarly with אָהֳלָה) for Oholiybahh; from אֹ֫הֶל; my tent (is) in her; Oholibah, a symbolic name for Judah. In the KJV it is rendered: Aholibah.
H173: From אֹ֫הֶל and בָּמָה; tent of (the) height; Oholibamah, a wife of Esau. In the KJV it is rendered: Aholibamah.
H174: Or (feminine) ahalowth (only used thus in the plural); of foreign origin; aloe wood (i.e. sticks). In the KJV it is rendered: (tree of lign-) aloes.
H175: Of uncertain derivation; Aharon, the brother of Moses. In the KJV it is rendered: Aaron.
H176: Presumed to be the "constructive" or genitival form of -av; short for אַוַּת; desire (and so probably in Prov. 31:4); hence (by way of alternative) or, also if. In the KJV it is rendered: also, and, either, if, at the least, X nor, or, otherwise, then, whether.
H177: From אַו and אֵל; wish of God; Uel, and Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Uel.
H178: From the same as אָב (apparently through the idea of prattling a father's name); properly, a mumble, i.e. a water skin (from its hollow sound); hence a necromancer (ventriloquist, as from a jar). In the KJV it is rendered: bottle, familiar spirit.
H179: Probably from אָבַל; mournful; Obil, an Ishmaelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Obil.
H180: Or (shortened) ubal; from יָבַל (in the sense of יִבְלֵי); a stream. In the KJV it is rendered: river.
H181: From an unused root meaning to rake together; a poker (for turning or gathering embers). In the KJV it is rendered: (fire-)brand.
H182: Or (shortened) rodowth (only thus in the plural); from the same as אוּד; turnings (i.e. occasions); (adverb) on account of. In the KJV it is rendered: (be-)cause, concerning, sake.
H183: A primitive root; to wish for. In the KJV it is rendered: covet, (greatly) desire, be desirous, long, lust (after).
H184: A primitive root; to extend or mark out. In the KJV it is rendered: point out.
H185: From אָוָה; longing. In the KJV it is rendered: desire, lust after, pleasure.
H186: Perhaps by permutation for עֻזִּי, strong; Uzai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Uzai.
H187: Of uncertain derivation; Uzal, a son of Joktan. In the KJV it is rendered: Uzal.
H188: Probably from אָוָה (in the sense of crying out after); lamentation; also interjectionally Oh!. In the KJV it is rendered: alas, woe.
H189: Probably from אָוָה; desirous; Evi, a Midianitish chief. In the KJV it is rendered: Evi.
H190: Feminine of אוֹי. In the KJV it is rendered: woe.
H191: From an unused root (meaning to be perverse); (figuratively) silly. In the KJV it is rendered: fool(-ish) (man).
H192: Of Aramaic derivation and probably meaning soldier of Merodak; Evil-Merodak, a Babylonian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Evil-merodach.
H193: From an unused root meaning to twist, i.e. (by implication) be strong; the body (as being rolled together); also powerful. In the KJV it is rendered: mighty, strength.
H194: Or (shortened) rulay; from אַו; if not; hence perhaps. In the KJV it is rendered: if so be, may be, peradventure, unless.
H195: Of Persian derivation; the Ulai (or Eulaeus), a river of Persia. In the KJV it is rendered: Ulai.
H196: From אֱוִיל; silly, foolish; hence (morally) impious. In the KJV it is rendered: foolish.
H197: Or (shortened) ulam; from אָלַם (in the sense of tying); a vestibule (as bound to the building). In the KJV it is rendered: porch.
H198: Appar, from אָלַם (in the sense of dumbness); solitary; Ulam, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ulam.
H199: Apparently a variation of אוּלַי; however or on the contrary. In the KJV it is rendered: as for, but, howbeit, in very deed, surely, truly, wherefore.
H200: From the same as אֱוִיל; silliness. In the KJV it is rendered: folly, foolishly(-ness).
H201: From אָמַר; talkative; Omar, a grandson of Esau. In the KJV it is rendered: Omar.
H202: Probably from the same as אָ֫וֶן (in the sense of effort, but successful); ability, power, (figuratively) wealth. In the KJV it is rendered: force, goods, might, strength, substance.
H203: The same as אוֹן; On, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: On.
H204: Or (shortened) On; of Egyptian derivation; On, a city of Egypt. In the KJV it is rendered: On.
H205: From an unused root perhaps meaning properly, to pant (hence, to exert oneself, usually in vain; to come to naught); strictly nothingness; also trouble. vanity, wickedness; specifically an idol. In the KJV it is rendered: affliction, evil, false, idol, iniquity, mischief, mourners(-ing), naught, sorrow, unjust, unrighteous, vain, vanity, wicked(-ness).
H206: The same as אָ֫וֶן; idolatry; Aven, the contemptuous synonym of three places, one in Coele-Syria, one in Egypt (On), and one in Palestine (Bethel). In the KJV it is rendered: Aven.
H207: Or (shortened) ;Onow; prolonged from אוֹן; strong; Ono, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ono.
H208: A variation of אוֹנָן; strong; Onam, the name of an Edomite and of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Onam.
H209: A variation of אוֹנוֹ; strong; Onan, a son of Judah. In the KJV it is rendered: Onan.
H210: Perhaps a corruption of אוֹפִיר; Uphaz, a famous gold region. In the KJV it is rendered: Uphaz.
H211: Or (shortened) Ophiyr; and Owphir; of uncertain derivation; Ophir, the name of a son of Joktan, and of a gold region in the East. In the KJV it is rendered: Ophir.
H212: Or (shortened) pophan; from an unused root meaning to revolve; a wheel. In the KJV it is rendered: wheel.
H213: A primitive root; to press; (by implication) to be close, hurry, withdraw. In the KJV it is rendered: (make) haste(-n, -y), labor, be narrow.
H214: From אָצַר; a depository. In the KJV it is rendered: armory, cellar, garner, store(-house), treasure(-house) (-y).
H215: A primitive root; to be (causative, make) luminous (literally and metaphorically). In the KJV it is rendered: X break of day, glorious, kindle, (be, en-, give, show) light (-en, -ened), set on fire, shine.
H216: From אוֹר; illumination or (concrete) luminary (in every sense, including lightning, happiness, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: bright, clear, + day, light (-ning), morning, sun.
H217: From אוֹר; flame; hence (in the plural) the East (as being the region of light). In the KJV it is rendered: fire, light.
H218: The same as אוּר; Ur, a place in Chaldaea; also an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ur.
H219: Feminine of אוֹר; luminousness, i.e. (figuratively) prosperity; also a plant (as being bright). In the KJV it is rendered: herb, light.
H220: By transposition for אֻרָוֹת; a stall. In the KJV it is rendered: cote.
H221: From אוּר; fiery; Uri, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Uri.
H222: From אוּר and אֵל; flame of God; Uriel, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Uriel.
H223: Or (prolonged) Uwriyahuw; from אוּר and יָהּ; flame of Jah; Urijah, the name of one Hittite and five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Uriah, Urijah.
H224: Plur of אוּר; lights; Urim, the oracular brilliancy of the figures in the high-priest's breastplate. In the KJV it is rendered: Urim.
H225: A primitive root; properly, to come, i.e. (implied) to assent. In the KJV it is rendered: consent.
H226: Probably from אוּת (in the sense of appearing); a signal (literally or figuratively), as a flag, beacon, monument, omen, prodigy, evidence, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: mark, miracle, (en-)sign, token.
H227: A demonstrative adverb; at that time or place; also as a conjunction, therefore. In the KJV it is rendered: beginning, for, from, hitherto, now, of old, once, since, then, at which time, yet.
H228: (Aramaic) or iazah (Aramaic); to kindle; (by implication) to heat. In the KJV it is rendered: heat, hot.
H229: Probably from אֵזוֹב; hyssop-like; Ezbai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ezbai.
H230: (Aramaic) of uncertain derivation; firm. In the KJV it is rendered: be gone.
H231: Probably of foreign derivation; hyssop. In the KJV it is rendered: hyssop.
H232: From אֲזִקִּים; something girt; a belt, also a band. In the KJV it is rendered: girdle.
H233: Probably from אָז; at that time. In the KJV it is rendered: then.
H234: From זָכַר; a reminder; specifically remembrance- offering. In the KJV it is rendered: memorial.
H235: A primitive root; to go away, hence, to disappear. In the KJV it is rendered: fail, gad about, go to and fro (but in Ezek.
H236: (Aramaic) the same as אָזַל; to depart. In the KJV it is rendered: go (up).
H237: From אָזַל; departure; Ezel, a memorial stone in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ezel.
H238: A primitive root; probably to expand; but used only as a denominative from אֹ֫זֶן; to broaden out the ear (with the hand), i.e. (by implication) to listen. In the KJV it is rendered: give (perceive by the) ear, hear(-ken).
H239: A primitive root (rather identical with הֶאֱזִין through the idea of scales as if two ears); to weigh, i.e. (figuratively) ponder. In the KJV it is rendered: give good head.
H240: From הֶאֱזִין; a spade or paddle (as having a broad end). In the KJV it is rendered: weapon.
H241: From הֶאֱזִין; broadness. i.e. (concrete) the ear (from its form in man). In the KJV it is rendered: + advertise, audience, + displease, ear, hearing, + show.
H242: From הֶאֱזִין and שֶׁאֱרָה; plat of Sheerah (i.e. settled by him); Uzzen-Sheerah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Uzzen-sherah.
H243: From הֶאֱזִין and תָּבוֹר; flats (i.e. tops) of Tabor (i.e. situated on it); Aznoth-Tabor, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Aznoth-tabor.
H244: From אֹ֫זֶן; having (quick) ears; Ozni, an Israelite; also an Oznite (collectively), his descendant. In the KJV it is rendered: Ozni, Oznites.
H245: From הֶאֱזִין and יָהּ; heard by Jah; Azanjah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Azaniah.
H246: A variation for זִיקוֹת; manacles. In the KJV it is rendered: chains.
H247: A primitive root; to belt. In the KJV it is rendered: bind (compass) about, gird (up, with).
H248: A variation for זְר֫וֹעַ; the arm. In the KJV it is rendered: arm.
H249: From זָרַח (in the sense of springing up); a spontaneous growth, i.e. native (tree or persons). In the KJV it is rendered: bay tree, (home-)born (in the land), of the (one's own) country (nation).
H250: Patronymic from חֹבָב; an Ezrachite or descendant of Zerach. In the KJV it is rendered: Ezrahite.
H251: A primitive word; a brother (used in the widest sense of literal relationship and metaphorical affinity or resemblance (like אָב)). In the KJV it is rendered: another, brother(-ly); kindred, like, other.
H252: (Aramaic) corresponding to אָח. In the KJV it is rendered: brother.
H253: A variation for אֲהָהּ; Oh! (expressive of grief or surprise). In the KJV it is rendered: ah, alas.
H254: Of uncertain derivation; a fire-pot or chafing dish. In the KJV it is rendered: hearth.
H255: Probably from אָח; a howler or lonesome wild animal. In the KJV it is rendered: doleful creature.
H256: Once (by contraction) Echab (Jer. 29:22); from אָח and אָב; brother (i.e. friend) of (his) father; Achab, the name of a king of Israel and of a prophet at Babylon. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahab.
H257: From אָח and בִּין; brother (i.e. possessor) of understanding; Achban, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahban.
H258: Perhaps a primitive root; to unify, i.e. (figuratively) collect (one's thoughts). In the KJV it is rendered: go one way or other.
H259: A numeral from אָחַד; properly, united, i.e. one; or (as an ordinal) first:--a, alike, alone, altogether, and, any(-thing), apiece, a certain, (dai-)ly, each (one), + eleven, every, few, first, + highway, a man, once, one, only, other, some, together.
H260: Of uncertain (perhaps Egyptian) derivation; a bulrush or any marshy grass (particularly that along the Nile). In the KJV it is rendered: flag, meadow.
H261: From אָחַד; united; Echud, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ehud.
H262: From חָוָה (in the sense of חֲוָא); an utterance. In the KJV it is rendered: declaration.
H263: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַחֲוַת; solution (of riddles). In the KJV it is rendered: showing.
H264: From אָח; fraternity. In the KJV it is rendered: brotherhood.
H265: By reduplication from אָח; brotherly; Achoach, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahoah.
H266: Patronymic from אַחֲוָה; an Achochite or descendant of Achoach. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahohite.
H267: Perhaps from אָח and מָ֫יִם; brother (i.e. neighbour) of water; Achumai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahumai.
H268: Or (shortened) achor; from אֲחִירַע; the hinder part; hence (adverb) behind, backward; also (as facing north) the West. In the KJV it is rendered: after(-ward), back (part, -side, -ward), hereafter, (be-)hind(-er part), time to come, without.
H269: Irregular feminine of אָח; a sister (used very widely (like אֶזְרָחִי), literally and figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: (an-)other, sister, together.
H270: A primitive root; to seize (often with the accessory idea of holding in possession). In the KJV it is rendered: + be affrighted, bar, (catch, lay, take) hold (back), come upon, fasten, handle, portion, (get, have or take) possess(-ion).
H271: From אָחַז; possessor; Achaz, the name of a Jewish king and of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahaz.
H272: Feminine passive participle from אָחַז; something seized, i.e. a possession (especially of land). In the KJV it is rendered: possession.
H273: From אָחַז; seizer; Achzai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahasai.
H274: Or (prolonged) Achazyahuw; from אָחַז and יָהּ; Jah has seized; Achazjah, the name of a Jewish and an Israelite king. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahaziah.
H275: From אָחַז; seizure; Achuzzam, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahuzam.
H276: A variation of אֲחֻזָּה; possession; Achuzzath, a Philistine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahuzzath.
H277: From אָח; brotherly; Achi, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahi.
H278: Probably the same as אֲחִי; Echi, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ehi.
H279: From אָח and אֵם; brother of the mother (i.e. uncle); Achiam, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahiam.
H280: (Aramaic) corresponding to חִידָה, an enigma. In the KJV it is rendered: hard sentence.
H281: Or (prolonged) Achiyahuw; from אָח and יָהּ; brother (i.e. worshipper) of Jah; Achijah, the name of nine Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahiah, Ahijah.
H282: From אָח and הוֹד; brother (i.e. possessor) of renown; Achihud, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahihud.
H283: Prolonged from אָח; brotherly; Achio, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahio.
H284: From אָח and חוּד; brother of a riddle (i.e. mysterious); Achichud, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahihud.
H285: From אָח and טוּב; brother of goodness; Achitub, the name of several priests. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahitub.
H286: From אָח and יָלַד; brother of one born; Achilud, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahilud.
H287: From אָח and מוּת; brother of death; Achimoth, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahimoth.
H288: From אָח and מֶ֫לֶך; brother of (the) king; Achimelek, the name of an Israelite and of a Hittite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahimelech.
H289: Or Achiyman; from אָח and מִן; brother of a portion (i.e. gift); Achiman, the name of an Anakite and of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahiman.
H290: From אָח and the equivalent of מַ֫עַץ; brother of anger; Achimaats, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahimaaz.
H291: From אָח; brotherly; Achjan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahian.
H292: From אָח and נָדַב; brother of liberality; Achinadab, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahinadab.
H293: From אָח and נֹ֫עַם; brother of pleasantness; Achinoam, the name of two Israelitesses. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahinoam.
H294: From אָח and סָמַך; brother of support; Achisamak, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahisamach.
H295: From אָח and עֵ֫זֶר; brother of help; Achiezer, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahiezer.
H296: From אָח and קוּם; brother of rising (i.e. high); Achikam, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahikam.
H297: From אָח and רוּם; brother of height (i.e. high); Achiram, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahiram.
H298: Patronymic from אֲחִירָם; an Achiramite or descendant (collectively) of Achiram. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahiramites.
H299: From אָח and רָע; brother of wrong; Achira, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahira.
H300: From אָח and שָׁ֫חַר; brother of (the) dawn; Achishachar, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahishar.
H301: From אָח and שִׁיר; brother of (the) singer; Achishar, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahishar.
H302: From אָח and תָּפֵל; brother of folly; Achithophel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahithophel.
H303: From the same root as חֵ֫לֶב; fatness (i.e. fertile); Achlab, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahlab.
H304: The same as אַחֲלַי; wishful; Achlai, the name of an Israelitess and of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahlai.
H305: Or achaley; prob from אָח and a variation of לוּא; would that!. In the KJV it is rendered: O that, would God.
H306: Perhaps from חָלַם (and thus dream-stone); a gem, probably the amethyst. In the KJV it is rendered: amethyst.
H307: Of Persian derivation; Achmetha (i.e. Ecbatana), the summer capital of Persia. In the KJV it is rendered: Achmetha.
H308: Of uncertain derivation; Achasbai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahasbai.
H309: A primitive root; to loiter (i.e. be behind); by implication to procrastinate. In the KJV it is rendered: continue, defer, delay, hinder, be late (slack), stay (there), tarry (longer).
H310: From אָחַר; properly, the hind part; generally used as an adverb or conjunction, after (in various senses). H311: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַחַר; after. In the KJV it is rendered: (here-)after.
H312: From אָחַר; properly, hinder; generally, next, other, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: (an-)other man, following, next, strange.
H313: The same as אַחֵר; Acher, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Aher.
H314: Or (shortened) ;acharon; from אָחַר; hinder; generally, late or last; specifically (as facing the east) western. In the KJV it is rendered: after (-ward), to come, following, hind(-er, -ermost, -most), last, latter, rereward, ut(ter)most.
H315: From אַחַר and אָח; after (his) brother: Achrach, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Aharah.
H316: From אַחַר and חֵיל; behind (the) intrenchment (i.e. safe); Acharchel, an Israelite:--Aharhel.
H317: (Aramaic) from אַחֲרֵי; other. In the KJV it is rendered: (an-)other.
H318: (Aramaic) or (shortened) :ochoren (Aramaic); from אָחֳרִי; last. In the KJV it is rendered: at last.
H319: From אַחַר; the last or end, hence, the future; also posterity. In the KJV it is rendered: (last, latter) end (time), hinder (utter) -most, length, posterity, remnant, residue, reward.
H320: (Aramaic) from אַחֲרֵי; the same as אַחֲרִית; later. In the KJV it is rendered: latter.
H321: (Aramaic) from אַחֲרֵי; the same as אָחֳרִי; other. In the KJV it is rendered: (an-)other.
H322: Prolonged from אָחוֹר; backwards. In the KJV it is rendered: back (-ward, again).
H323: Of Persian derivation; a satrap or governor of a main province (of Persia). In the KJV it is rendered: lieutenant.
H324: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנִים. In the KJV it is rendered: prince.
H325: Or (shortened) Achashrosh (Esth. 10:1); of Persian origin; Achashverosh (i.e. Ahasuerus or Artaxerxes, but in this case Xerxes), the title (rather than name) of a Persian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahasuerus.
H326: Probably of Persian derivation; an achastarite (i.e. courier); the designation (rather than name) of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Haakashtari (includ.
H327: Of Persian origin; a mule. In the KJV it is rendered: camel.
H328: From an unused root perhaps meaning to move softly; (as a noun) a necromancer (from their soft incantations), (as an adverb) gently. In the KJV it is rendered: charmer, gently, secret, softly.
H329: From an unused root probably meaning to pierce or make fast; a thorn-tree (especially the buckthorn). In the KJV it is rendered: Atad, bramble, thorn.
H330: From an unused root (probably meaning to bind); properly, twisted (yarn), i.e. tapestry. In the KJV it is rendered: fine linen.
H331: A primitive root; to close (the lips or ears); by analology to contract (a window by bevelled jambs). In the KJV it is rendered: narrow, shut, stop.
H332: A primitive root; to close up. In the KJV it is rendered: shut.
H333: From אָטַר; maimed; Ater, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ater.
H334: From אָטַר; shut up, i.e. impeded (as to the use of the right hand). In the KJV it is rendered: + left-handed.
H335: Perhaps from מֵאַ֫יִן; where? hence how?. In the KJV it is rendered: how, what, whence, where, whether, which (way).
H336: Probably identical with אַי (through the idea of a query); not. In the KJV it is rendered: island (Job 22:30).
H337: Short from אוֹי; alas!. In the KJV it is rendered: woe.
H338: Probably identical with אּי (through the idea of a doleful sound); a howler (used only in the plural), i.e. any solitary wild creature; --wild beast of the islands.
H339: From אָוָה; properly, a habitable spot (as desirable); dry land, a coast, an island. In the KJV it is rendered: country, isle, island.
H340: A primitive root; to hate (as one of an opposite tribe or party); hence to be hostile. In the KJV it is rendered: be an enemy.
H341: Or (fully) owyeb; active participle of אָיַב; hating; an adversary. In the KJV it is rendered: enemy, foe.
H342: From אָיַב; hostility. In the KJV it is rendered: emnity, hatred.
H343: From the same as אוּד (in the sense of bending down); oppression; by implication misfortune, ruin. In the KJV it is rendered: calamity, destruction.

H508: From אֵל and פָּעַל; God (is) act; Elpaal, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Elpaal.
H509: A primitive root; to press. In the KJV it is rendered: urge.
H510: Probably from אַל and קוּם; a non-rising (i.e. resistlessness). In the KJV it is rendered: no rising up.
H511: From אֵל and קָנָה; God has obtained; Elkanah, the name of several Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Elkanah.
H512: Patrial from a name of uncertain derivation; an Elkoshite or native of Elkosh. In the KJV it is rendered: Elkoshite.
H513: Probably from אֵל and a masculine form of תּוֹלְדוֹת (compare תּוֹלָד); God (is) generator; Eltolad, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Eltolad.
H514: Or (more properly) Eltqeh; of uncertain derivation; Eltekeh or Elteke, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Eltekeh.
H515: From אֵל and תָּקַן; God (is) straight; Eltekon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Eltekon.
H516: From אַל and שָׁחַת; Thou must not destroy; probably the opening words to a popular song. In the KJV it is rendered: Al-taschith.
H517: A primitive word; a mother (as the bond of the family); in a wide sense (both literally and figuratively (like אָב). In the KJV it is rendered: dam, mother, X parting.

H519: Apparently a primitive word; a maid-servant or female slave. In the KJV it is rendered: (hand-)bondmaid(-woman), maid(-servant).
H520: Prolonged from אֵם; properly, a mother (i.e. unit of measure, or the fore-arm (below the elbow), i.e. a cubit; also a door-base (as a bond of the entrance). In the KJV it is rendered: cubit, + hundred (by exchange for me'ah), measure, post.
H521: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַמָּה. In the KJV it is rendered: cubit.
H522: The same as אַמָּה; Ammah, a hill in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ammah.
H523: From the same as אֵם; a collection, i.e. community of persons. In the KJV it is rendered: nation, people.
H524: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֻמִּים. In the KJV it is rendered: nation.
H525: From אָמַן, probably in the sense of training; skilled, i.e. an architect (like אָמָּן). In the KJV it is rendered: one brought up.
H526: The same as אָמוֹן; Amon, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Amon.
H527: A variation for הָמוֹן; a throng of people. In the KJV it is rendered: multitude.
H528: Of Egyptian derivation; Amon (i.e. Ammon or Amn), a deity of Egypt (used only as an adjunct of נֹא). In the KJV it is rendered: multitude, populous.
H529: From אָמַן; established, i.e. (figuratively) trusty; also (abstractly) trustworthiness. In the KJV it is rendered: faith(-ful), truth.
H530: Or (shortened) >emunah feminine of אֵמֻן; literally firmness; figuratively security; morally fidelity. In the KJV it is rendered: faith(-ful, -ly, -ness, (man)), set office, stability, steady, truly, truth, verily.
H531: From אָמַץ; strong; Amots, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Amoz.
H532: An abbrev. for אָמוֹן; Ami, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ami.
H533: Or (shortened) ammits; from אָמַץ; strong or (abstractly) strength. In the KJV it is rendered: courageous, mighty, strong (one).
H534: Apparently from אָמַר (in the sense of self- exaltation); a summit (of a tree or mountain. In the KJV it is rendered: bough, branch.
H535: A primitive root; to droop; by implication to be sick, to mourn. In the KJV it is rendered: languish, be weak, wax feeble.
H536: From אָמַל; sick. In the KJV it is rendered: weak.
H537: From אָמַל; languid. In the KJV it is rendered: feeble.
H538: From אֵם; gathering-spot; Amam, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Amam.
H539: A primitive root; properly, to build up or support; to foster as a parent or nurse; figuratively to render (or be) firm or faithful, to trust or believe, to be permanent or quiet; morally to be true or certain; once (Isa. 30:21; interchangeable with תַאֲמִין) to go to the right hand. In the KJV it is rendered: hence, assurance, believe, bring up, establish, + fail, be faithful (of long continuance, stedfast, sure, surely, trusty, verified), nurse, (-ing father), (put), trust, turn to the right.
H540: (Aramaic) corresponding to אָמַן. In the KJV it is rendered: believe, faithful, sure.
H541: Denominative from יָמִין; to take the right hand road. In the KJV it is rendered: turn to the right.
H542: From אָמַן (in the sense of training); an expert. In the KJV it is rendered: cunning workman.
H543: From אָמַן; sure; abstract, faithfulness; adverb, truly. In the KJV it is rendered: Amen, so be it, truth.
H544: From אָמַן; verity. In the KJV it is rendered: truth.
H545: Feminine of אֹ֫מֶן (in the specific sense of training); tutelage. In the KJV it is rendered: brought up.
H546: Feminine form of אֹ֫מֶן (in its usual sense); adverb, surely. In the KJV it is rendered: indeed.
H547: Feminine active participle of אֹ֫מֶן (in the original sense of supporting); a column. In the KJV it is rendered: pillar.
H548: Feminine of אָמֵן; something fixed, i.e. a covenant. an allowance. In the KJV it is rendered: certain portion, sure.
H549: The same as אֲמָנָה; Amanah, a mountain near Damascus. In the KJV it is rendered: Amana.
H550: Or Amiynown; from אָמַן; faithful; Amnon (or Aminon), a son of David. In the KJV it is rendered: Amnon.
H551: Adverb from אֹ֫מֶן; verily. In the KJV it is rendered: indeed, no doubt, surely, (it is, of a) true(-ly, -th).
H552: An orthographical variation of אָמְנָם. In the KJV it is rendered: in (very) deed; of a surety.
H553: A primitive root; to be alert, physically (on foot) or mentally (in courage). In the KJV it is rendered: confirm, be courageous (of good courage, stedfastly minded, strong, stronger), establish, fortify, harden, increase, prevail, strengthen (self), make strong (obstinate, speed).
H554: Probably from אָמַץ; of a strong color, i.e. red (others fleet). In the KJV it is rendered: bay.
H555: From אָמַץ; strength. In the KJV it is rendered: stronger.
H556: From אָמַץ; force. In the KJV it is rendered: strength.
H557: From אָמַץ; strong; Amtsi, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Amzi.
H558: Or Amatsyahuw; from אָמַץ and יָהּ; strength of Jah; Amatsjah, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Amaziah.
H559: A primitive root; to say (used with great latitude). H560: (Aramaic) corresponding to אָמַר. In the KJV it is rendered: command, declare, say, speak, tell.
H561: From אָמַר; something said. In the KJV it is rendered: answer, X appointed unto him, saying, speech, word.
H562: The same as אֵ֫מֶר. In the KJV it is rendered: promise, speech, thing, word.
H563: (Aramaic) perhaps from אֲמַר (in the sense of bringing forth); a lamb. In the KJV it is rendered: lamb.
H564: From אָמַר; talkative; Immer, the name of five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Immer.
H565: Or memrah; feminine of אֵ֫מֶר, and meaning the same. In the KJV it is rendered: commandment, speech, word.
H566: From אּמֵּר; wordy; Imri, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Imri.
H567: Probably a patronymic from an unused name derived from אָמַר in the sense of publicity, i.e. prominence; thus, a mountaineer; an Emorite, one of the Canaanitish tribes. In the KJV it is rendered: Amorite.
H568: Or prolonged Amaryahuw; from אָמַר and יָהּ; Jah has said (i.e. promised); Amarjah, the name of nine Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Amariah.
H569: Of uncertain (perhaps foreign) derivation; Amraphel, a king of Shinar. In the KJV it is rendered: Amraphel.
H570: Time past, i.e. yesterday or last night:--former time, yesterday(-night).
H571: Contracted from אָמַן; stability; (figuratively) certainty, truth, trustworthiness. In the KJV it is rendered: assured(-ly), establishment, faithful, right, sure, true (-ly, -th), verity.
H572: From מָתַח; properly, something expansive, i.e. a bag. In the KJV it is rendered: sack.
H573: From אֱמֶת; veracious; Amittai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Amittai.
H574: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of מָתְנָ֫יִם; well-loined (i.e. burly) or mighty. In the KJV it is rendered: terrible.
H575: Or manah; contracted from מֵאַ֫יִן; where?; hence, whither?, when?; also hither and thither. In the KJV it is rendered: + any (no) whither, now, where, whither(-soever).
H576: (Aramaic) or .anah (Aramaic); corresponding to אָ֫נִי; I. In the KJV it is rendered: I, as for me.
H577: Or mannah; apparent contracted from אַהֲבָה and נָא; oh now!. In the KJV it is rendered: I (me) beseech (pray) thee, O.
H578: A primitive root; to groan. In the KJV it is rendered: lament, mourn.
H579: A primitive root (perhaps rather identical with אָנָה through the idea of contraction in anguish); to approach; hence, to meet in various senses. In the KJV it is rendered: befall, deliver, happen, seek a quarrel.
H580: Contracted for אֲנַ֫חְנוּ; we. In the KJV it is rendered: we.
H581: (Aramaic) or (feminine) inniyn (Aramaic); corresponding to הֵם; they. In the KJV it is rendered: X are, them, these.
H582: From אָנַשׁ; properly, a mortal (and thus differing from the more dignified אָדָם); hence, a man in general (singly or collectively). In the KJV it is rendered: another, X (blood-)thirsty, certain, chap(-man); divers, fellow, X in the flower of their age, husband, (certain, mortal) man, people, person, servant, some ( X of them), + stranger, those, + their trade.
H583: The same as אֱנוֹשׁ; Enosh, a son of Seth; --Enos.
H584: A primitive root; to sigh. In the KJV it is rendered: groan, mourn, sigh.
H585: From אֲנָחָה; sighing. In the KJV it is rendered: groaning, mourn, sigh.
H586: (Aramaic) or ganachnah (Aramaic); corresponding to אֲנַ֫חְנוּ; we. In the KJV it is rendered: we.
H587: Apparently from אָנֹכִי; we. In the KJV it is rendered: ourselves, us, we.
H588: Probably from the same root as נַ֫חַר; a gorge or narrow pass; Anacharath, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Anaharath.
H589: Contracted from אָנֹכִי; I. In the KJV it is rendered: I, (as for) me, mine, myself, we, X which, X who.
H590: Probably from אָנָה (in the sense of conveyance); -a ship or (collectively)a fleet. In the KJV it is rendered: galley, navy (of ships).
H591: Feminine of אֳנִי; a ship. In the KJV it is rendered: ship((-men)).
H592: From אָנָה; groaning. In the KJV it is rendered: lamentation, sorrow.
H593: From אָנָה and עָם; groaning of (the) people; Aniam, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Aniam.
H594: Probably from an unused root meaning to be narrow; according to most a plumb-line, and to others a hook. In the KJV it is rendered: plumb-line.
H595: A primitive pro.; I. In the KJV it is rendered: I, me, X which.
H596: A primitive root; to mourn, i.e. complain. In the KJV it is rendered: complain.
H597: To insist. In the KJV it is rendered: compel.
H598: (Aramaic) corresponding to אָנַס; figuratively, to distress. In the KJV it is rendered: trouble.
H599: A primitive root; to breathe hard, i.e. be enraged. In the KJV it is rendered: be angry (displeased).
H600: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַף (only in the plural as a singular); the face. In the KJV it is rendered: face, visage.
H601: From אָנַף; an unclean bird, perhaps the parrot (from its irascibility). In the KJV it is rendered: heron.
H602: A primitive root; to shriek. In the KJV it is rendered: cry, groan.
H603: From אָנַק; shrieking. In the KJV it is rendered: crying out, groaning, sighing.
H604: The same as אֲנָקָה; some kind of lizard, probably the gecko (from its wail). In the KJV it is rendered: ferret.
H605: A primitive root; to be frail, feeble, or (figuratively) melancholy. In the KJV it is rendered: desperate(-ly wicked), incurable, sick, woeful.
H606: (Aramaic) or renash (Aramaic); corresponding to אֱנוֹשׁ; a man. In the KJV it is rendered: man, + whosoever.
H607: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַתְּ; thou. In the KJV it is rendered: as for thee, thou.
H608: (Aramaic) plural of אַנְתָּה; ye. In the KJV it is rendered: ye.
H609: Of uncertain derivation; Asa, the name of a king and of a Levite. In the KJV it is rendered: Asa.
H610: From סוּך; anointed, i.e. an oil-flask. In the KJV it is rendered: pot.
H611: Of uncertain derivation; hurt. In the KJV it is rendered: mischief.
H612: From אָסַר; a bond (especially manacles of a prisoner). In the KJV it is rendered: band, + prison.
H613: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֵסוּר. In the KJV it is rendered: band, imprisonment.
H614: Or maciph; from אָסַף; gathered, i.e. (abstractly) a gathering in of crops. In the KJV it is rendered: ingathering.
H615: From אָסַר; bound, i.e. a captive. In the KJV it is rendered: (those which are) bound, prisoner.
H617: The same as אַסִּיר; prisoner; Assir, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Assir.
H618: From an unused root meaning to heap together; a storehouse (only in the plural). In the KJV it is rendered: barn, storehouse.
H619: Of uncertain derivation; Asnah, one of the Nethinim. In the KJV it is rendered: Asnah.
H620: Of foreign derivation; Osnappar, an Assyrian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Asnapper.
H621: Of Egyptian derivation; Asenath, the wife of Joseph. In the KJV it is rendered: Asenath.
H622: A primitive root; to gather for any purpose; hence, to receive, take away, i.e. remove (destroy, leave behind, put up, restore, etc.). H623: From אָסַף; collector; Asaph, the name of three Israelites, and of the family of the first. In the KJV it is rendered: Asaph.
H624: Passive participle of אָסַף; collected (only in the plural), i.e. a collection of offerings). In the KJV it is rendered: threshold, Asuppim.
H625: From אָסַף; a collection (of fruits). In the KJV it is rendered: gathering.
H626: From אָסַף; a collection of people (only adverbial). In the KJV it is rendered: X together.
H627: Fem of אֲסֻפִּים.; a collection of (learned) men (only in the plural). In the KJV it is rendered: assembly.
H628: By reduplication from אֲסֻפִּים; gathered up together, i.e. a promiscuous assemblage (of people). In the KJV it is rendered: mixt multitude.
H629: (Aramaic) of Persian derivation; diligently. In the KJV it is rendered: fast, forthwith, speed(-ily).
H630: Of Persian derivation; Aspatha, a son of Haman. In the KJV it is rendered: Aspatha.
H631: A primitive root; to yoke or hitch; by analogy, to fasten in any sense, to join battle. In the KJV it is rendered: bind, fast, gird, harness, hold, keep, make ready, order, prepare, prison(-er), put in bonds, set in array, tie.
H632: Or riccar; from אָסַר; an obligation or vow (of abstinence). In the KJV it is rendered: binding, bond.
H633: (Aramaic) corresponding to אּסָּר in a legal sense; an interdict. In the KJV it is rendered: decree.
H634: Of foreign derivation; Esar- chaddon, an Assyrian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Esar-haddon.
H635: Of Persian derivation; Ester, the Jewish heroine. In the KJV it is rendered: Esther.
H636: (Aramaic) corresponding to עֵץ; a tree or wood. In the KJV it is rendered: timber, wood.
H637: A primitive particle; meaning accession (used as an adverb or conjunction); also or yea; adversatively though. In the KJV it is rendered: also, + although, and (furthermore, yet), but, even, + how much less (more, rather than), moreover, with, yea.
H638: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַף. In the KJV it is rendered: also.
H639: From אָנַף; properly, the nose or nostril; hence, the face, and occasionally a person; also (from the rapid breathing in passion) ire. In the KJV it is rendered: anger(-gry), + before, countenance, face, + forebearing, forehead, + (long-)suffering, nose, nostril, snout, X worthy, wrath.
H640: A primitive root (rather a denominative from אֵפוֹד); to gird on (the ephod). In the KJV it is rendered: bind, gird.
H641: The same as אֵפוֹד shortened; Ephod, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ephod.
H642: Feminine of אֵפוֹד; a girding on (of the ephod); hence, generally, a plating (of metal). In the KJV it is rendered: ephod, ornament.
H643: Apparently of foreign derivation; a pavilion or palace-tent. In the KJV it is rendered: palace.
H644: A primitive root; to cook, especially to bake. In the KJV it is rendered: bake(-r, (-meats)).
H645: Or hephowe; from NONE; strictly a demonstrative particle, here; but used of time, now or then:--here, now, where?.
H646: Rarely oephod; probably of foreign derivation; a girdle; specifically the ephod or high-priest's shoulder- piece; also generally, an image. In the KJV it is rendered: ephod.
H647: Perhaps from פּ֫וּחַ; breeze; Aphiach, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Aphiah.
H648: From the same as אָפֵל (in the sense of weakness); unripe. In the KJV it is rendered: not grown up.
H649: Dual of אַף; two nostrils; Appajim, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Appaim.
H650: From אָסַף; properly, containing, i.e. a tube; also a bed or valley of a stream; also a strong thing or a hero. In the KJV it is rendered: brook, channel, mighty, river, + scale, stream, strong piece.
H651: From an unused root meaning to set as the sun; dusky. In the KJV it is rendered: very dark.
H652: From the same as אָפֵל; dusk. In the KJV it is rendered: darkness, obscurity, privily.
H653: Feminine of אָפֵל; duskiness, figuratively, misfortune; concrete, concealment. In the KJV it is rendered: dark, darkness, gloominess, X thick.
H654: From פָּלַל; judge; Ephlal, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ephlal.
H655: From an unused root meaning to revolve; a turn, i.e. a season. In the KJV it is rendered: + fitly.
H656: A primitive root; to disappear, i.e. cease. In the KJV it is rendered: be clean gone (at an end, brought to nought), fail.

H658: From אָ֫פֶס and the plural of דָּם; boundary of blood-drops; Ephes-Dammim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ephes- dammim.
H659: From an unused root probably meaning to breathe; properly, a breath, i.e. nothing. In the KJV it is rendered: of nought.
H660: From אָ֫פַע (in the sense of hissing); an asp or other venomous serpent. In the KJV it is rendered: viper.
H661: A primitive root; to surround. In the KJV it is rendered: compass.
H662: A primitive root; to contain, i.e. (reflex.) abstain. In the KJV it is rendered: force (oneself), restrain.
H663: Or Aphiyq; from אָפַק (in the sense of strength); fortress; Aphek (or Aphik), the name of three places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Aphek, Aphik.
H664: Feminine of אֲפֵק; fortress; Aphekah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Aphekah.
H665: From an unused root meaning to bestrew; ashes. In the KJV it is rendered: ashes.
H666: From the same as אֵ֫פֶר (in the sense of covering); a turban. In the KJV it is rendered: ashes.
H667: From פָּרַח (in the sense of bursting the shell); the brood of a bird. In the KJV it is rendered: young (one).
H668: Probably of Egyptian derivation; a palanquin. In the KJV it is rendered: chariot.
H669: Dual of masculine form of אֶפְרָת; double fruit; Ephrajim, a son of Joseph; also the tribe descended from him, and its territory. In the KJV it is rendered: Ephraim, Ephraimites.
H670: (Aramaic) of foreign origin (only in the plural); an Apherasite or inhabitant of an unknown region of Assyria. In the KJV it is rendered: Apharsite.
H671: (Aramaic) or Apharcathkay (Aramaic); of foreign origin (only in the plural); an Apharsekite or Apharsathkite, an unknown Assyrian tribe. In the KJV it is rendered: Apharsachites, Apharasthchites.
H672: Or Ephrathah; from פָּרָה; fruitfulness; Ephrath, another name for Bethlehem; once (Psa. 132:6) perhaps for Ephraim; also of an Israelitish woman. In the KJV it is rendered: Ephrath, Ephratah.
H673: Patrial form אֶפְרָת; an Ephrathite or an Ephraimite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ephraimite, Ephrathite.
H674: (Aramaic) of Persian origin; revenue; others at the last. In the KJV it is rendered: revenue.
H675: Or Etsbon; of uncertain derivation; Etsbon, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ezbon.
H676: From the same as צֶ֫בַע (in the sense of grasping); something to sieze with, i.e. a finger; by analogy, a toe. In the KJV it is rendered: finger, toe.
H677: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֶצְבַּע. In the KJV it is rendered: finger, toe.
H678: From אָצַל (in its secondary sense of separation); an extremity (Isa. 41:9), also a noble. In the KJV it is rendered: chief man, noble.
