H680: A primitive root; properly, to join; used only as a denominative from אֵ֫צֶל; to separate; hence, to select, refuse, contract. In the KJV it is rendered: keep, reserve, straiten, take.
H681: From אָצַל (in the sense of joining); a side; (as a preposition) near. In the KJV it is rendered: at, (hard) by, (from) (beside), near (unto), toward, with.
H682: From אָצַל; noble; Atsel, the name of an Israelite, and of a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Azal, Azel.
H683: From אָצַל and יָהּ prolonged; Jah has reserved; Atsaljah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Azaliah.
H684: From an unused root probably meaning to be strong; strength (i.e. strong); Otsem, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ozem.
H685: A variation from צְעָדָה; properly, a step- chain; by analogy, a bracelet. In the KJV it is rendered: bracelet, chain.
H686: A primitive root; to store up. In the KJV it is rendered: (lay up in) store, + (make) treasure(-r).
H687: From אָצַר; treasure; Etser, an Idumaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Ezer.
H688: From קִדָּה; burning, i.e. a carbuncle or other fiery gem. In the KJV it is rendered: carbuncle.
H689: Probably from אָנַק; slender, i.e. the ibex. In the KJV it is rendered: wild goat.
H690: Probably for אֲרִי; lion; Ara, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ara.
H691: Probably for אֲרִיאֵל; a hero (collectively). In the KJV it is rendered: valiant one.
H692: From אֶרְאֵל; heroic; Areli (or an Arelite, collectively), an Israelite and his descendants. In the KJV it is rendered: Areli, Arelites.
H693: A primitive root; to lurk. In the KJV it is rendered: (lie in) ambush(-ment), lay (lie in) wait.
H694: From אָרַב; ambush; Arab, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Arab.
H695: From אָרַב; ambuscade. In the KJV it is rendered: den, lie in wait.
H696: The same as אָ֫רֶב. In the KJV it is rendered: wait.
H697: From רָבָה; a locust (from its rapid increase). In the KJV it is rendered: grasshopper, locust.
H698: Feminine of אֹ֫רֶב (only in the plural); ambuscades. In the KJV it is rendered: spoils.
H699: Feminine participle passive of אָרַב (as if for lurking); a lattice; (by implication) a window, dove-cot (because of the pigeon-holes), chimney (with its apertures for smoke), sluice (with openings for water). In the KJV it is rendered: chimney, window.
H700: Plural of אֲרֻבָּה; Arubboth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Aruboth.
H701: Patrial from אֲרָב; an Arbite or native of Arab. In the KJV it is rendered: Arbite.
H702: Masculine oarbaah; from רָבַע; four. In the KJV it is rendered: four.
H703: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַרְבַּע. In the KJV it is rendered: four.
H704: The same as אַרְבַּע; Arba, one of the Anakim. In the KJV it is rendered: Arba.
H705: Multiple of אַרְבַּע; forty. In the KJV it is rendered: -forty.
H706: Dual of אַרְבַּע; fourfold. In the KJV it is rendered: fourfold.
H707: A primitive root; to plait or weave. In the KJV it is rendered: weaver(-r).
H708: From אָרַג; a weaving; a braid; also a shuttle. In the KJV it is rendered: beam, weaver's shuttle.
H709: From the same as רְגָבִים; stony; Argob, a district of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Argob.
H710: A variation for אַרְגָּמָן; purple. In the KJV it is rendered: purple.
H711: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַרְגְּוָן. In the KJV it is rendered: purple.
H712: Perhaps from רָגַז (in the sense of being suspended), a box (as a pannier). In the KJV it is rendered: coffer.
H713: Of foreign origin; purple (the color or the dyed stuff). In the KJV it is rendered: purple.
H714: From an unused root probably meaning to wander; fugitive; Ard, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ard.
H715: From the same as אָרְדְּ; roaming; Ardon, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ardon.
H716: Patronymic from אָרְדְּ; an Ardite (collectively) or descendant of Ard. In the KJV it is rendered: Ardites.
H717: A primitive root; to pluck. In the KJV it is rendered: gather, pluck.
H718: (Aramaic) probably akin to אֲלוּ; lo!. In the KJV it is rendered: behold,lo.
H719: Probably from רוּד; a refuge for the roving; Arvad, an island-city of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Arvad.
H720: An orthographical variation of אַרְוַד; fugitive; Arod, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Arod.
H721: Patrial from אַרְוַד; an Arvadite or citizen of Arvad. In the KJV it is rendered: Arvadite.
H722: Patronymic from אַרְוָדִי; an Arodite or descendant of Arod. In the KJV it is rendered: Arodi, Arodites.
H723: Or rarayah; from אָרָה(in the sense of feeding); a herding-place for an animal. In the KJV it is rendered: stall.
H724: Or rarukah; feminine passive participle of 748 (in the sense of restoring to soundness); wholeness (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: health, made up, perfected.
H725: A variation of רוּמָה; height; Arumah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Arumah.
H726: A clerical error for אֲדֹמִי; an Edomite (as in the margin). In the KJV it is rendered: Syrian.
H727: Or laron; from אָרָה (in the sense of gathering); a box. In the KJV it is rendered: ark, chest, coffin.
H728: Or (by transposition) Owrnah; or Arniyah; all by orthographical variation for אָרְנָן; Aravnah (or Arnijah or Ornah), a Jebusite. In the KJV it is rendered: Araunah.
H729: A primitive root; to be firm; used only in the passive participle as a denominative from אָ֫רֶז; of cedar. In the KJV it is rendered: made of cedar.
H730: From אָרַז; a cedar tree (from the tenacity of its roots). In the KJV it is rendered: cedar (tree).
H731: Fem of אָ֫רֶז; cedar wainscoating. In the KJV it is rendered: cedar work.
H732: A primitive root; to travel. In the KJV it is rendered: go, wayfaring (man).
H733: From אָרַח; way faring; Arach, the name of three Israelites: Arah.
H734: From אָרַח; a well-trodden road (literally or figuratively); also a caravan. In the KJV it is rendered: manner, path, race, rank, traveller, troop, (by-, high-)way.
H735: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֹ֫רַח; a road. In the KJV it is rendered: way.
H736: Feminine active participle of אָרַח; a caravan. In the KJV it is rendered: (travelling) company.
H737: Feminine passive participle of אָרַח (in the sense of appointing); a ration of food. In the KJV it is rendered: allowance, diet, dinner, victuals.
H738: Or (prolonged) earyeh; from אָרָה (in the sense of violence); a lion. In the KJV it is rendered: (young) lion, + pierce (from the margin).
H739: Or (arilel; from אֲרִי and אֵל; lion of God; i.e. heroic. In the KJV it is rendered: lionlike men.
H740: The same as אֲרִיאֵל; Ariel, a symbolical name for Jerusalem, also the name of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ariel.
H741: Either by transposition for אֲרִיאֵל or, more probably, an orthographical variation for הַרְאֵל; the altar of the temple. In the KJV it is rendered: altar.
H742: Of Persian origin; Aridai, a son of Haman. In the KJV it is rendered: Aridai.
H743: Of Persian origin; Aridatha, a son of Haman. In the KJV it is rendered: Aridatha.
H744: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֲרִי. In the KJV it is rendered: lion.
H745: The same as אֲרִי; lion; Arjeh, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Arieh.
H746: Of foreign origin; Arjok, the name of two Babylonians. In the KJV it is rendered: Arioch.
H747: Of Persian origin; Arisai, a son of Haman. In the KJV it is rendered: Arisai.
H748: A primitive root; to be (causative, make) long (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: defer, draw out, lengthen, (be, become, make, pro-)long, + (out-, over-)live, tarry (long).
H749: (Aramaic) properly, corresponding to אָרַך, but used only in the sense of reaching to a given point; to suit. In the KJV it is rendered: be meet.
H750: From אָרַך; long. In the KJV it is rendered: long(-suffering, -winged), patient, slow (to anger).
H751: From אָרַך; length; Erek, a place in Babylon. In the KJV it is rendered: Erech.
H752: From אָרַך; long. In the KJV it is rendered: long.
H753: From אָרַך; length. In the KJV it is rendered: + forever, length, long.
H754: (Aramaic) or narkah (Aramaic); from אֲרִיך; length. In the KJV it is rendered: lengthening, prolonged.
H755: (Aramaic) from an unused root corresponding to רָכַב (in the sense of bending the knee); the knee. In the KJV it is rendered: knee.
H756: (Aramaic) patrial from אֶ֫רֶך; an Arkevite (collectively) or native of Erek. In the KJV it is rendered: Archevite.
H757: Patrial from another place (in Palestine) of similar name with אֶ֫רֶך; an Arkite or native of Erek. In the KJV it is rendered: Archi, Archite.
H758: From the same as אַרְמוֹן; the highland; Aram or Syria, and its inhabitants; also the name of the son of Shem, a grandson of Nahor, and of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Aram, Mesopotamia, Syria, Syrians.
H759: From an unused root (meaning to be elevated); a citadel (from its height). In the KJV it is rendered: castle, palace.
H760: From אֲרָם and צוֹבָה; Aram of Tsoba (or Coele-Syria). In the KJV it is rendered: Aram-zobah.
H761: Patrial from אֲרָם; an Aramite or Aramaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Syrian, Aramitess.
H762: Feminine of אֲרַמִּי; (only adverbial)in Aramean. In the KJV it is rendered: in the Syrian language (tongue), in Syriac.
H763: From אֲרָם and the dual of נָהָר; Aram of (the) two rivers (Euphrates and Tigris) or Mesopotamia. In the KJV it is rendered: Aham-naharaim, Mesopotamia.
H764: From אַרְמוֹן; palatial; Armoni, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Armoni.
H765: From רָנַן; stridulous; Aran, an Edomite. In the KJV it is rendered: Aran.
H766: From the same as אֲרָן (in the sense of strength); the ash tree (from its toughness). In the KJV it is rendered: ash.
H767: The same as אֹ֫רֶן; Oren, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Oren.
H768: Of uncertain derivation; the hare. In the KJV it is rendered: hare.
H769: Or Arnon; from רָנַן; a brawling stream; the Arnon, a river east of the Jordan, also its territory. In the KJV it is rendered: Arnon.
H770: Probably from the same as אַרְנוֹן; noisy; Arnan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Arnan.
H771: Probably from אֹ֫רֶן; strong; Ornan, a Jebusite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ornan.
H772: (Aramaic) corresponding to אָ֫רֶץ; the earth; by implication (figuratively) low. In the KJV it is rendered: earth, interior.
H773: (Aramaic) feminine of אַרְעָא; the bottom. In the KJV it is rendered: bottom.
H774: From רָפַד; spread out; Arpad, a place in Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Arpad, Arphad.
H775: Probably of foreign origin; Arpakshad, a son of Noah; also the region settled by him. In the KJV it is rendered: Arphaxad.
H776: From an unused root probably meaning to be firm; the earth (at large, or partitively a land). In the KJV it is rendered: X common, country, earth, field, ground, land, X natins, way, + wilderness, world.
H777: From אָ֫רֶץ; earthiness; Artsa, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Arza.
H778: (Aramaic) by transmutation for אַרְעָא; the earth. In the KJV it is rendered: earth.
H779: A primitive root; to execrate. In the KJV it is rendered: X bitterly curse.
H780: Of foreign origin; Ararat (or rather Armenia). In the KJV it is rendered: Ararat, Armenia.
H781: A primitive root; to engage for matrimony. In the KJV it is rendered: betroth, espouse.
H782: From אָרַשׂ (in the sense of desiring to possess); a longing for. In the KJV it is rendered: request.
H783: Or Artachshasht; or by permutation Artachshactu; of foreign origin; Artachshasta (or Artaxerxes), a title (rather than name) of several Persian kings. In the KJV it is rendered: Artaxerxes.
H784: A primitive word; fire (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: burning, fiery, fire, flaming, hot.
H785: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֵשׁ. In the KJV it is rendered: flame.
H786: Identical (in origin and formation) with אֵשׁ; entity, used only adverbially, there is or are. In the KJV it is rendered: are there, none can.
H787: (Aramaic) corresponding (by transposition and abbreviation) to אָשְׁוִיֹּת; a foundation. In the KJV it is rendered: foundation.
H788: Probably from the same as שֹׁ֫בֶל; flowing; Ashbel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashbel.
H789: Patronymic from אַשְׁבֵּל; an Ashbelite (collectively) or descendant of Ashbel. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashbelites.
H790: Probably from the same as שֶׁבְנָה; vigorous; Eshban, an Idumaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Eshban.
H791: From שָׁבַע; adjurer; Asbea, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashbea.
H792: From אּישׁ and בַּ֫עַל; man of Baal; Eshbaal (or Ishbosheth), a son of Saul. In the KJV it is rendered: Eshbaal.
H793: From an unused root meaning to pour; an outpouring. In the KJV it is rendered: stream.
H794: Feminine of אֶ֫שֶׁד; a ravine. In the KJV it is rendered: springs.
H795: From שָׁדַד; ravager; Ashdod, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ahdod.
H796: Patrial from אַשְׁדּוֹד; an Ashdodite (often collectively) or inhabitant of Asdod. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashdodites, of Ashdod.
H797: Feminine of אַשְׁדּוֹדִי; (only adverb) in the language of Ashdod. In the KJV it is rendered: in the speech of Ashdod.
H798: From the plural of אֲשֵׁדוֹת and פִּסְגָּה with the article interposed; ravines of the Pisgah; Ashdoth- Pisgah, a place east of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashdoth-pisgah.
H799: From אֵשׁ and דָּת; a fire-law. In the KJV it is rendered: fiery law.
H800: Feminine of אֵשׁ; fire. In the KJV it is rendered: fire.
H801: The same as מֵאֵשׁ, but used in a liturgical sense; properly, a burnt-offering; but occasionally of any sacrifice. In the KJV it is rendered: (offering, sacrifice), (made) by fire.
H802: Feminine of אּישׁ or אֱנוֹשׁ; irregular plural nashiym; a woman (used in the same wide sense as אֱנוֹשׁ). In the KJV it is rendered: (adulter)ess, each, every, female, X many, + none, one, + together, wife, woman.
H803: Feminine passive participle from an unused root meaning to found; foundation. In the KJV it is rendered: foundation.
H804: Or Ashshur; apparently from אָשַׁר (in the sense of successful); Ashshur, the second son of Shem; also his descendants and the country occupied by them (i.e. Assyria), its region and its empire. In the KJV it is rendered: Asshur, Assur, Assyria, Assyrians.
H805: Or Ashshuwriy; from a patrial word of the same form as אַשּׁוּר; an Ashurite (collectively) or inhabitant of Ashur, a district in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Asshurim, Ashurites.
H806: Probably from שָׁחַר; black; Ashchur, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashur.
H807: Of foreign origin; Ashima, a deity of Hamath. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashima.
H808: From the same as אֵשׁ (in the sense of pressing down firmly; compare אָשְׁוִיֹּת); a (ruined) foundation. In the KJV it is rendered: foundation.
H809: Feminine of אֲשִׁישֵׁי; something closely pressed together, i.e. a cake of raisins or other comfits. In the KJV it is rendered: flagon.
H810: From an unused root (probably meaning to bunch together); a testicle (as a lump). In the KJV it is rendered: stone.
H811: Or meshkol; probably prolonged from אָ֫שֶׁך; a bunch of grapes or other fruit. In the KJV it is rendered: cluster (of grapes).
H812: The same as אֶשְׁכּוֹל; Eshcol, the name of an Amorite, also of a valley in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Eshcol.
H813: Of foreign origin; Ashkenaz, a Japhethite, also his descendants. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashkenaz.
H814: For שָׂכָר; a gratuity. In the KJV it is rendered: gift, present.
H815: From a root of uncertain signification; a tamarisk tree; by extension, a grove of any kind. In the KJV it is rendered: grove, tree.
H816: Or mashem; a primitive root; to be guilty; by implication to be punished or perish. In the KJV it is rendered: X certainly, be(-come, made) desolate, destroy, X greatly, be(-come, found, hold) guilty, offend (acknowledge offence), trespass.
H817: From אָשַׁם; guilt; by implication, a fault; also a sin-offering. In the KJV it is rendered: guiltiness, (offering for) sin, trespass (offering).
H818: From אָשַׁם; guilty; hence, presenting a sin- offering. In the KJV it is rendered: one which is faulty, guilty.
H819: Feminine of אָשָׁם; guiltiness, a fault, the presentation of a sin-offering. In the KJV it is rendered: offend, sin, (cause of) trespass(-ing, offering).
H820: Probably from שָׁ֫מֶן; a fat-field. In the KJV it is rendered: desolate place.
H821: Or bashmuwrah; or -ashmoreth; (feminine) from שָׁמַר; a night watch. In the KJV it is rendered: watch.
H822: Apparently from an unused root (probably meaning to leave interstices); A latticed window. In the KJV it is rendered: casement, lattice.
H823: Probably a variation for יְשָׁנָה; Ashnah, the name of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashnah.
H824: From שָׁעַן; support; Eshan, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Eshean.
H825: From an unused root (probably meaning to lisp, i.e. practice enchantment); a conjurer. In the KJV it is rendered: astrologer.
H826: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַשָּׁפִים. In the KJV it is rendered: astrologer.
H827: Perhaps (feminine) from the same as אַשָּׁפִים (in the sense of covering); a quiver or arrow-case. In the KJV it is rendered: quiver.
H828: Of foreign origin; Ashpenaz, a Babylonian eunuch. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashpenaz.
H829: Of uncertain derivation; a measured portion. In the KJV it is rendered: good piece (of flesh).
H830: Or uashpowth; or (contraction) shphoth; plural of a noun of the same form as אַשְׁפָּה, from שָׁפָה (in the sense of scraping); a heap of rubbish or filth. In the KJV it is rendered: dung (hill).
H831: Probably from שָׁקַל in the sense of weighing-place (i.e. mart); Ashkelon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashkelon, Askalon.
H832: Patrial from אַשְׁקְלוֹן; Ashkelonite (collectively) or inhabitant of Ashkelon. In the KJV it is rendered: Eshkalonites.
H833: Or rasher; a primitive root; to be straight (used in the widest sense, especially to be level, right, happy); figuratively, to go forward, be honest, proper. In the KJV it is rendered: (call, be) bless(-ed, happy), go, guide, lead, relieve.
H834: A primitive relative pronoun (of every gender and number); who, which, what, that; also (as an adverb and a conjunction) when, where, how, because, in order that, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: X after, X alike, as (soon as), because, X every, for, + forasmuch, + from whence, + how(-soever), X if, (so) that ((thing) which, wherein), X though, + until, + whatsoever, when, where (+ -as, -in, -of, -on, -soever, -with), which, whilst, + whither(- soever), who(-m, -soever, -se).
H835: From אָשַׁר; happiness; only in masculine plural construction as interjection, how happy!. In the KJV it is rendered: blessed, happy.
H836: From אָשַׁר, happy; Asher, a son of Jacob, and the tribe descended from him, with its territory; also a place in Palestine:--Asher.
H837: From אָשַׁר; happiness. In the KJV it is rendered: happy.
H838: Or ashshur; from אָשַׁר in the sense of going; a step. In the KJV it is rendered: going, step.
H839: Contracted for תְּאַשּׁוּר; the cedar tree or some other light elastic wood. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashurite.
H840: By orthographical variation from אָשַׁר and אֵל; right of God; Asarel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Asareel.
H841: From the same as אֲשַׂרְאֵל; right toward God; Asarelah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Asarelah.
H842: Or masheyrah; from אָשַׁר; happy; Asherah (or Astarte) a Phoenician goddess; also an image of the same. In the KJV it is rendered: grove.
H843: Patronymic from אָשֵׁר; an Asherite (collectively) or descendant of Asher. In the KJV it is rendered: Asherites.
H844: An orthographical variation for אֲשַׂרְאֵל; Asriel, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashriel, Asriel.
H845: Patronymic from אַשְׂרִיאֵל; an Asrielite (collectively) or descendant of Asriel. In the KJV it is rendered: Asrielites.
H846: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to אָשַׁר; a wall (from its uprightness). In the KJV it is rendered: wall.
H847: Or Eshtafowl; probably from שָׁאַל; intreaty; Eshtaol, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Eshtaol.
H848: Patrial from אֶשְׁתָּאֹל; an Eshtaolite (collectively) or inhabitant of Eshtaol. In the KJV it is rendered: Eshtaulites.
H849: (Aramaic) from שְׁדַר (in a bad sense); rebellion. In the KJV it is rendered: sedition.
H850: Probably from the same as שׁוּנִי; restful; Eshton, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Eshton.
H851: Or Eshtmowam; or Eshtmoh; from שָׁמַע (in the sense of obedience); Eshtemoa or Eshtemoh, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Eshtemoa, Eshtemoh.
H852: (Aramaic) corresponding to אוֹת; a portent. In the KJV it is rendered: sign.
H853: Apparent contracted from אוֹת in the demonstrative sense of entity; properly, self (but generally used to point out more definitely the object of a verb or preposition, even or namely). In the KJV it is rendered: (as such unrepresented in English).
H854: Probably from אָנָה; properly, nearness (used only as a preposition or an adverb), near; hence, generally, with, by, at, among, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: against, among, before, by, for, from, in(-to), (out) of, with.
H855: Of uncertain derivation; a hoe or other digging implement. In the KJV it is rendered: coulter, plowshare.
H856: From אוֹת and בַּ֫עַל; with Baal; Ethbaal, a Phoenician king. In the KJV it is rendered: Ethbaal.
H857: Or matha; a primitive root (collateral to 225 contraction); to arrive. In the KJV it is rendered: (be-, things to) come (upon), bring.
H858: (Aramaic) or wathaw (Aramaic); corresponding to אָתָה. In the KJV it is rendered: (be-)come, bring.
H859: Or (shortened) aatta; or wath; feminine (irregular) sometimes nattiy; plural masculine attem; feminine atten; or oattenah; or fattennah; a primitive pronoun of the second person; thou and thee, or (plural) ye and you. In the KJV it is rendered: thee, thou, ye, you.
H860: Probably from the same as אֵיתָן (in the sense of patience); a female donkey (from its docility). In the KJV it is rendered: (she) ass.
H861: (Aramaic) probably from the corresponding to אֵשׁ; probably a fire-place, i.e. furnace. In the KJV it is rendered: furnace.
H862: Or mattiyq; from נָתַק in the sense of decreasing; a ledge or offset in a building. In the KJV it is rendered: gallery.
H863: Or Iythay; from אוֹת; near; Ittai or Ithai, the name of a Gittite and of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ithai, Ittai.
H864: Of Egyptian derivation; Etham, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Etham.
H865: Or tithmowl; or methmuwl; probably from אוֹת or אוֹת and מוֹאל; heretofore; definitely yesterday. In the KJV it is rendered: + before (that) time, + heretofore, of late (old), + times past, yester(day).
H866: From תָּנָה; a present (as the price of harlotry). In the KJV it is rendered: reward.
H867: Perhaps from אֶתְנָה; munificence; Ethni, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ethni.
H868: The same as אֶתְנָה; a gift (as the price of harlotry or idolatry). In the KJV it is rendered: hire, reward.
H869: The same as אֶתְנָן in the sense of אֶתְנִי; Ethnan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ethnan.
H870: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of אֲתָרִים; a place; (adverb) after. In the KJV it is rendered: after, place.
H871: Plural from an unused root (probably meaning to step); places; Atharim, a place near Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: spies.
H872: From בּוֹא; an entrance to a building. In the KJV it is rendered: entry.
H873: (Aramaic) from בְּאֵשׁ; wicked. In the KJV it is rendered: bad.
H874: A primitive root; to dig; by analogy, to engrave; figuratively, to explain. In the KJV it is rendered: declare, (make) plain(-ly).
H875: From בָּאַר; a pit; especially a well. In the KJV it is rendered: pit, well.
H876: The same as בְּאֵר; Beer, a place in the Desert, also one in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beer.
H877: From בָּאַר; a cistern. In the KJV it is rendered: cistern.
H878: From בְּאֵר; a well; Beera, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Beera.
H879: From בְּאֵר and the plural of אֵל; well of heroes; Beer-Elim, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Beer-elim.
H880: The same as בְּאֵרָא; Beerah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Beerah.
H881: Feminine plural of בְּאֵר; wells; Beeroth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beeroth.
H882: From בְּאֵר; fountained; Beeri, the name of a Hittite and of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Beeri.
H883: From בְּאֵר and חָי (with prefix) and רֹאֶה; well of a living (One) my Seer; Beer-Lachai-Roi, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Beer-lahai-roi.
H884: From בְּאֵר and שֶׁ֫בַע (in the sense of שָׁבַע); well of an oath; Beer-Sheba, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beer-shebah.
H885: From the feminine plural of בְּאֵר, and the plural contraction of בֵּן, and יַעֲקָן; wells of (the) sons of Jaakan; Beeroth-Bene-Jaakan, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Beeroth of the children of Jaakan.
H886: Patrial from בְּאֵרוֹת; a Beerothite or inhabitant of Beeroth. In the KJV it is rendered: Beerothite.
H887: A primitive root; to smell bad; figuratively, to be offensive morally. In the KJV it is rendered: (make to) be abhorred (had in abomination, loathsome, odious), (cause a, make to) stink(-ing savour), X utterly.
H888: (Aramaic) corresponding to בָּאַשׁ. In the KJV it is rendered: displease.
H889: From בֹּארוֹת; a stench. In the KJV it is rendered: stink.
H890: Feminine of בְּאֹשׁ; stink-weed or any other noxious or useless plant. In the KJV it is rendered: cockle.
H891: Plural of בְּאֹשׁ; poison-berries. In the KJV it is rendered: wild grapes.
H892: Feminine active participle of an unused root meaning to hollow out; something hollowed (as a gate), i.e. pupil of the eye. In the KJV it is rendered: apple (of the eye).
H893: Probably of foreign origin; Bebai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bebai.
H894: From בָּלַל; confusion; Babel (i.e. Babylon), including Babylonia and the Babylonian empire. In the KJV it is rendered: Babel, Babylon.
H895: (Aramaic) corresponding to בָּבֶל. In the KJV it is rendered: Babylon.
H896: (Aramaic) patrial from בָּבֶל; a Babylonian. In the KJV it is rendered: Babylonia.
H897: A Persian word; food. In the KJV it is rendered: spoil (from the margin for baz.
H898: A primitive root; to cover (with a garment); figuratively, to act covertly; by implication, to pillage. In the KJV it is rendered: deal deceitfully (treacherously, unfaithfully), offend, transgress(-or), (depart), treacherous (dealer, -ly, man), unfaithful(-ly, man), X very.
H899: From בָּגַד; a covering, i.e. clothing; also treachery or pillage. In the KJV it is rendered: apparel, cloth(-es, ing), garment, lap, rag, raiment, robe, X very (treacherously), vesture, wardrobe.
H900: Feminine plural active participle of בָּגַד; treacheries. In the KJV it is rendered: treacherous.
H901: From בָּגַד; treacherous. In the KJV it is rendered: treacherous.
H902: Probably of foreign origin; Bigvai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bigvai.
H903: Of Persian derivation; Bigtha, a eunuch of Xerxes. In the KJV it is rendered: Bigtha.
H904: Or Bigthanad; of similar derivation to בִּגְתָא; Bigthan or Bigthana, a eunuch of Xerxes. In the KJV it is rendered: Bigthan, Bigthana.
H905: From בָּדַד; properly, separation; by implication, a part of the body, branch of a tree, bar for carrying; figuratively, chief of a city; especially (with prepositional prefix) as an adverb, apart, only, besides. In the KJV it is rendered: alone, apart, bar, besides, branch, by self, of each alike, except, only, part, staff, strength.
H906: Perhaps from בָּדַד (in the sense of divided fibres); flaxen thread or yarn; hence, a linen garment. In the KJV it is rendered: linen.
H907: From בָּדָא; a brag or lie; also a liar. In the KJV it is rendered: liar, lie.
H908: A primitive root; (figuratively) to invent. In the KJV it is rendered: devise, feign.
H909: A primitive root; to divide, i.e. (reflex.) be solitary. In the KJV it is rendered: alone.
H910: From בָּדַד; separate; adverb, separately. In the KJV it is rendered: alone, desolate, only, solitary.
H911: From בָּדַד; separation; Bedad, an Edomite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bedad.
H912: Probably a shortened form עֹבַדְיָה; servant of Jehovah; Bedejah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bedeiah.
H913: From בָּדַל; alloy (because removed by smelting); by analogy, tin. In the KJV it is rendered: + plummet, tin.
H914: A primitive root; to divide (in variation senses literally or figuratively, separate, distinguish, differ, select, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: (make, put) difference, divide (asunder), (make) separate (self, -ation), sever (out), X utterly.
H915: From בָּדַל; a part. In the KJV it is rendered: piece.
H916: Probably from בָּדַל; something in pieces, i.e. bdellium, a (fragrant) gum (perhaps amber); others a pearl. In the KJV it is rendered: bdellium.
H917: Probably shortened for עַבְדּוֹן; servile; Bedan, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Bedan.
H918: A primitive root; to gap open; used only as a denominative from בֶּ֫דֶק; to mend a breach. In the KJV it is rendered: repair.
H919: From בָּדַק; a gap or leak (in a building or a ship). In the KJV it is rendered: breach, + calker.
H920: Probably from דָּקַר with a prepositional prefix; by stabbing, i.e. assassin; Bidkar, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bidkar.
H921: (Aramaic) corresponding (by transposition) to פָּרַד; to scatter. In the KJV it is rendered: scatter.
H922: From an unused root (meaning to be empty); a vacuity, i.e. (superficially) an undistinguishable ruin. In the KJV it is rendered: emptiness, void.
H923: From an unused root (probably meaning to glisten); white marble or perhaps alabaster. In the KJV it is rendered: red (marble).
H924: (Aramaic) from בְּהַל; a hurry; only adverb, hastily. In the KJV it is rendered: in haste.
H925: From an unused root (meaning to be bright); shining. In the KJV it is rendered: bright.
H926: A primitive root; to tremble inwardly (or palpitate), i.e. (figuratively) be (causative, make) (suddenly) alarmed or agitated; by implication to hasten anxiously. In the KJV it is rendered: be (make) affrighted (afraid, amazed, dismayed, rash), (be, get, make) haste(-n, -y, -ily), (give) speedy(-ily), thrust out, trouble, vex.
H927: (Aramaic) corresponding to בָּהַל; to terrify, hasten. In the KJV it is rendered: in haste, trouble.
H928: From בָּהַל; panic, destruction. In the KJV it is rendered: terror, trouble.
H929: From an unused root (probably meaning to be mute); properly, a dumb beast; especially any large quadruped or animal (often collective). In the KJV it is rendered: beast, cattle.
H930: In form a plural or בְּהֵמָה, but really a singular of Egyptian derivation; a water-ox, i.e. the hippopotamus or Nile- horse. In the KJV it is rendered: Behemoth.
H931: From an unused root apparently meaning to be thick; the thumb of the hand or great toe of the foot. In the KJV it is rendered: thumb, great toe.
H932: An orthographical variation of בֹּ֫הֶן; thumb, Bohan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bohan.
H933: From an unused root meaning to be pale; white scurf. In the KJV it is rendered: freckled spot.
H934: Feminine active participle of the same as בָּהִיר; a whitish spot on the skin. In the KJV it is rendered: bright spot.
H935: A primitive root; to go or come (in a wide variety of applications). In the KJV it is rendered: abide, apply, attain, X be, befall, + besiege, bring (forth, in, into, to pass), call, carry, X certainly, (cause, let, thing for) to come (against, in, out, upon, to pass), depart, X doubtless again, + eat, + employ, (cause to) enter (in, into, -tering, -trance, -try), be fallen, fetch, + follow, get, give, go (down, in, to war), grant, + have, X indeed, (in-)vade, lead, lift (up), mention, pull in, put, resort, run (down), send, set, X (well) stricken (in age), X surely, take (in), way.
H936: A primitive root; to disrespect. In the KJV it is rendered: contemn, despise, X utterly.
H937: From בּוּז; disrespect. In the KJV it is rendered: contempt(-uously), despised, shamed.
H938: The same as בּוּז; Buz, the name of a son of Nahor, and of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Buz.
H939: Feminine passive participle of בּוּז; something scorned; an object of contempt. In the KJV it is rendered: despised.
H940: Patronymic from בּוּז; a Buzite or descendant of Buz. In the KJV it is rendered: Buzite.
H941: The same as בּוּזִי; Buzi, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Buzi.
H942: Probably of Persian origin; Bavvai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bavai.
H943: A primitive root; to involve (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: be entangled, (perplexed).
H944: For יְבוּל; produce (of the earth, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: food, stock.
H945: The same as בוּל (in the sense of rain); Bul, the eighth Hebrew month. In the KJV it is rendered: Bul.
H946: From בִּין; discretion; Bunah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bunah.
H947: A primitive root; to trample (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: loath, tread (down, under (foot)), be polluted.
H948: From an unused root (of the same form) meaning to bleach, i.e. (intransitive) be white; probably cotton (of some sort). In the KJV it is rendered: fine (white) linen.
H949: From the same as בּוּץ; shining; Botsets, a rock near Michmash. In the KJV it is rendered: Bozez.
H950: Feminine passive participle of an unused root (meaning to be hollow); emptiness (as adjective). In the KJV it is rendered: empty.
H951: Properly, active participle from בָּקַר as denominative from בָּקָר; a cattle-tender. In the KJV it is rendered: herdman.
H952: A primitive root; to bore, i.e. (figuratively) examine. In the KJV it is rendered: declare.
H953: From בּוּר (in the sense of בֹּארוֹת); a pit hole (especially one used as a cistern or a prison). In the KJV it is rendered: cistern, dungeon, fountain, pit, well.
H954: A primitive root; properly, to pale, i.e. by implication to be ashamed; also (by implication) to be disappointed or delayed. In the KJV it is rendered: (be, make, bring to, cause, put to, with, a-)shamed(-d), be (put to) confounded(-fusion), become dry, delay, be long.
H955: Feminine participle passive of בּוּשׁ; shame. In the KJV it is rendered: shame.
H956: (Aramaic) apparent denominative from בַּיְתָא; to lodge over night. In the KJV it is rendered: pass the night.
H957: From בָּזַז; plunder. In the KJV it is rendered: booty, prey, spoil(-ed).
H958: A primitive root; probably to cleave. In the KJV it is rendered: spoil.
H959: A primitive root; to disesteem. In the KJV it is rendered: despise, disdain, contemn(-ptible), + think to scorn, vile person.
H960: From בָּזָה; scorned. In the KJV it is rendered: despise.
H961: Feminine of בָּז; booty. In the KJV it is rendered: prey, spoil.
H962: A primitive root; to plunder. In the KJV it is rendered: catch, gather, (take) for a prey, rob(-ber), spoil, take (away, spoil), X utterly.
H963: From בָּזָה. In the KJV it is rendered: disesteem:--contempt.
H964: From בָּזָה and יָהּ; contempts of Jah; Bizjothjah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Bizjothjah.
H965: From an unused root meaning to lighten; a flash of lightning. In the KJV it is rendered: flash of lightning.
H966: From בָּזָק; lightning; Bezek, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Bezek.
H967: A primitive root; to disperse. In the KJV it is rendered: scatter.
H968: Of Persian origin; Biztha, a eunuch of Xerxes. In the KJV it is rendered: Biztha.
H969: From בָּחַן; an assayer or metals. In the KJV it is rendered: tower.
H970: Or bachur; participle passive of בָּחַר; properly, selected, i.e. a youth (often collective). In the KJV it is rendered: (choice) young (man), chosen, X hole.
H971: Another form of בַּ֫חַן; a watch-tower of besiegers. In the KJV it is rendered: tower.
H972: From בָּחַר; select. In the KJV it is rendered: choose, chosen one, elect.
H973: A primitive root; to loath. In the KJV it is rendered: abhor, get hastily (from the margin for bahal).
H974: A primitive root; to test (especially metals); generally and figuratively, to investigate. In the KJV it is rendered: examine, prove, tempt, try (trial).
H975: From בָּחַן (in the sense of keeping a look-out); a watch-tower. In the KJV it is rendered: tower.
H976: From בָּחַן; trial. In the KJV it is rendered: tried.
H977: A primitive root; properly, to try, i.e. (by implication) select. In the KJV it is rendered: acceptable, appoint, choose (choice), excellent, join, be rather, require.
H978: Patrial from בַּחוּרִים (by transposition); a Bacharumite or inhabitant of Bachurim. In the KJV it is rendered: Baharumite.
H979: Or bchuwrowth; feminine plural of בָּחוּר; also (masculine plural) bchuriym; youth (collectively and abstractly). In the KJV it is rendered: young men, youth.
H980: Or Bachuwriym; masculine plural of בָּחוּר; young men; Bachurim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Bahurim.
H981: Or batah; a primitive root; to babble; hence, to vociferate angrily. In the KJV it is rendered: pronounce, speak (unadvisedly).
H982: A primitive root; properly, to hie for refuge (but not so precipitately as חָסָה); figuratively, to trust, be confident or sure. In the KJV it is rendered: be bold (confident, secure, sure), careless (one, woman), put confidence, (make to) hope, (put, make to) trust.
H983: From בָּטַח; properly, a place of refuge; abstract, safety, both the fact (security) and the feeling (trust); often (adverb with or without preposition) safely. In the KJV it is rendered: assurance, boldly, (without) care(- less), confidence, hope, safe(-ly, -ty), secure, surely.
H984: The same as בֶּ֫טַח; Betach, a place in Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Betah.
H985: Feminine of בֶּ֫טַח; trust. In the KJV it is rendered: confidence.
H986: From בָּטַח; trust. In the KJV it is rendered: confidence, hope.
H987: Feminine plural from בָּטַח; security. In the KJV it is rendered: secure.
H988: A primitive root; to desist from labor. In the KJV it is rendered: cease.
H989: (Aramaic) corresponding to בָּטֵל; to stop. In the KJV it is rendered: (cause, make to), cease, hinder.
H990: From an unused root probably meaning to be hollow; the belly, especially the womb; also the bosom or body of anything. In the KJV it is rendered: belly, body, + as they be born, + within, womb.
H991: The same as בָּ֫טֶן; Beten. a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beten.
H992: From בָּ֫טֶן; (only in plural) a pistachio-nut (from its form). In the KJV it is rendered: nut.
H993: Probably plural from בָּטְנִים; hollows: Betonim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Betonim.
H994: Perhaps from בָּעָה (in the sense of asking); properly, a request; used only adverbially (always with "my Lord"); Oh that!; with leave, or if it please. In the KJV it is rendered: alas, O, oh.
H995: A primitive root; to separate mentally (or distinguish), i.e.(generally) understand. H996: (sometimes in the plural masculine or feminine); properly, the constructive form of an otherwise unused noun from בִּין; a distinction; but used only as a prep, between (repeated before each noun, often with other particles); also as a conjunction, either...or. In the KJV it is rendered: among, asunder, at, between (-twixt.
H997: (Aramaic) corresponding to בֵּין. In the KJV it is rendered: among, between.
H998: From בִּין; understanding. In the KJV it is rendered: knowledge, meaning, X perfectly, understanding, wisdom.
H999: (Aramaic) corresponding to בִּינָה. In the KJV it is rendered: knowledge.
H1000: From the same as בּוּץ; an egg (from its whiteness). In the KJV it is rendered: egg.
H1001: (Aramaic) corresponding to בִּירָה; a palace. In the KJV it is rendered: palace.
H1002: Of foreign origin; a castle or palace. In the KJV it is rendered: palace.
H1003: From בִּירָה; a fortress. In the KJV it is rendered: castle.
H1004: Probably from בָּנָה abbreviated; a house (in the greatest variation of applications, especially family, etc.). H1005: (Aramaic) corresponding to בָּ֫יִת. In the KJV it is rendered: house.
H1006: The same as בָּ֫יִת; Bajith, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Bajith.
H1007: From בָּ֫יִת and אָ֫וֶן; house of vanity; Beth- Aven, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-aven.
H1008: From בָּ֫יִת and אֵל; house of God; Beth-El, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-el.
H1009: From בָּ֫יִת and אָ֫רֶב and אֵל; house of God's ambush; Beth-Arbel, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-Arbel.
H1010: From בָּ֫יִת and בַּ֫עַל and מָעוֹן; house of Baal of (the) habitation of (apparently by transposition); or (shorter) Beyth M own; house of habitation of (Baal); Beth- Baal-Meon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-baal-meon.
H1011: From בָּ֫יִת and בָּרָא; house of a creative one; Beth-Biri, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-birei.
H1012: Probably from בָּ֫יִת and עֲבָרָה; house of (the) ford; Beth-Barah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-barah.
H1013: From בָּ֫יִת and גָּדֵר; house of (the) wall; Beth-Gader, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-gader.
H1014: From בָּ֫יִת and the passive participle of גְּמוּל; house of (the) weaned; Beth-Gamul, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth- gamul.
H1015: From בָּ֫יִת and the dual of דְּבֵלִים; house of (the) two figcakes; Beth-Diblathajim, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-diblathaim.
H1016: From בָּ֫יִת and דָּגוֹן; house of Dagon; Beth-Dagon, the name of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-dagon.
H1017: Patrial from בֵּית־אֵל with the article interposed; a Beth-elite, or inhabitant of Bethel. In the KJV it is rendered: Bethelite.
H1018: From בָּ֫יִת and אֵ֫צֶל with the article interposed; house of the side; Beth-ha-Etsel, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth- ezel.
H1019: From בָּ֫יִת and הַגִּלְגָּל with the article interposed; house of Gilgal (or rolling); Beth-hag-Gilgal, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-gilgal.
H1020: From בָּ֫יִת and the plural of יַשִּׁ֫ימָ֫וֶת with the article interposed; house of the deserts; Beth-ha- Jeshimoth, a town East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-jeshimoth.
H1021: From בָּ֫יִת and כָּ֫רֶם with the article interposed; house of the vineyard; Beth-hak-Kerem, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-haccerem.
H1022: Patrial from בֵּית לָ֫חֶם with the article inserted; a Beth-lechemite, or native of Bethlechem. In the KJV it is rendered: Bethlehemite.
H1023: From בָּ֫יִת and מֶרְחָק with the article interposed; house of the breadth; Beth-ham-Merchak, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: place that was far off.
H1024: Or (shortened) Beyth Mar-kabowth; from בָּ֫יִת and the plural of מֶרְכָּבָה (with or without the article interposed); place of (the) chariots; Beth-ham-Markaboth or Beth-Markaboth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-marcaboth.
H1025: From בָּ֫יִת and עֵ֫מֶק with the article interposed; house of the valley; Beth-ha-Emek, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth- emek.
H1026: From בָּ֫יִת and עֲרָבָה with the article interposed; house of the Desert; Beth-ha-Arabah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-arabah.
H1027: From בָּ֫יִת and רוּם with the article interposed; house of the height; Beth-ha-Ram, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-aram.
H1028: Probably for בֵּית הָרָם; Beth-ha-Ram, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-haran.
H1029: From בָּ֫יִת and שִׁטִּים with the article interposed; house of the acacia; Beth-hash-Shittah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-shittah.
H1030: Patrial from בֵּית שָׁ֫מֶשׁ with the article inserted; a Beth-shimshite, or inhabitant of Bethshemesh. In the KJV it is rendered: Bethshemite.
H1031: From בָּ֫יִת and the same as חָגְלָה; house of a partridge; Beth-Choglah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-hoglah.
H1032: From בָּ֫יִת and חֹר; house of hollowness; Beth-Choron, the name of two adjoining places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth- horon.
H1033: From בָּ֫יִת and כָּר; house of pasture; Beth-Car, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-car.
H1034: From בָּ֫יִת and the plural of לָבִיא; house of lionesses; Beth-Lebaoth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-lebaoth.
H1035: From בָּ֫יִת and לָ֫חֶם; house of bread; Beth- Lechem, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-lehem.
H1036: From בָּ֫יִת and the feminine of עָפָר (with preposition interposed); house to (i.e. of) dust; Beth-le-Aphrah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: house of Aphrah.
H1037: Or Beyth Mil-loh; from בָּ֫יִת and מִלּוֹא; house of (the) rampart; Beth-Millo, the name of two citadels. In the KJV it is rendered: house of Millo.
H1038: From בָּ֫יִת and מַעֲכָה; house of Maakah; Beth-Maakah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-maachah.
H1039: From בָּ֫יִת and the feminine of נָמֵר; house of (the) leopard; Beth-Nimrah, a place east of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-Nimrah.
H1040: From בָּ֫יִת and עֲדָנִים; house of pleasure; Beth-Eden, a place in Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-eden.
H1041: From בָּ֫יִת and עַזְמָ֫וֶת; house of Azmaveth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-az-maveth.
H1042: From בָּ֫יִת and a plural from עָנָה; house of replies; Beth-Anoth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-anoth.
H1043: An orthographical variation for בֵּית עֲנוֹת; Beth-Anath, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-anath.
H1044: From בָּ֫יִת and a derivative of עָקַד; house of (the) binding (for sheep-shearing); Beth-Eked, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: shearing house.
H1045: : from בָּ֫יִת and עַשְׁתָּרוֹת; house of Ashtoreths; Beth-Ashtaroth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: house of Ashtaroth.
H1046: From בָּ֫יִת and פָּלִיט; house of escape; Beth- Palet, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-palet.
H1047: From בָּ֫יִת and פְּעוֹר; house of Peor; Beth- Peor, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-peor.
H1048: From בָּ֫יִת and a derivative from פּוּץ; house of dispersion; Beth-Patstsets, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-pazzez.
H1049: From בָּ֫יִת and צוּר; house of (the) rock; Beth-Tsur, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-zur.
H1050: From בָּ֫יִת and רְחוֹב; house of (the) street; Beth-Rechob, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-rehob.
H1051: From בָּ֫יִת and רָפָא; house of (the) giant; Beth-Rapha, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-rapha.
H1052: Or Beyth Shan; from בָּ֫יִת and שָׁאַן; house of ease; Beth-Shean or Beth-Shan, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth- shean, Beth-Shan.
H1053: From בָּ֫יִת and שָׁ֫מֶשׁ; house of (the) sun; Beth-Shemesh, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-shemesh.
H1054: From בָּ֫יִת and תַּפּ֫וּחַ; house of (the) apple; Beth-Tappuach, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Beth-tappuah.
H1055: Probably from בָּ֫יִת; a palace (i.e. large house). In the KJV it is rendered: palace.
H1056: From בָּכָה, weeping; Baca, a valley in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Baca.
H1057: The same as הַבָּכָא; the weeping tree (some gum- distilling tree, perhaps the balsam). In the KJV it is rendered: mulberry tree.
H1058: A primitive root; to weep; generally to bemoan. In the KJV it is rendered: X at all, bewail, complain, make lamentation, X more, mourn, X sore, X with tears, weep.
H1059: From בָּכָה; a weeping. In the KJV it is rendered: X sore.
H1060: From בָּכַר; firstborn; hence, chief. In the KJV it is rendered: eldest (son), firstborn(-ling).
H1061: From בָּכַר; the first-fruits of the crop. In the KJV it is rendered: first fruit (-ripe (figuratively)), hasty fruit.
H1062: Or (short) bkorah; feminine of בְּכוֹר; the firstling of man or beast; abstractly primogeniture. In the KJV it is rendered: birthright, firstborn(-ling).
H1063: Feminine of בִּכּוּרִים; the early fig. In the KJV it is rendered: firstripe (fruit).
H1064: Feminine of בְּכֹרָה; primogeniture; Bekorath, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bechorath.
H1065: From בָּכָה; a weeping; by analogy, a dripping. In the KJV it is rendered: overflowing, X sore, (continual) weeping, wept.
H1066: Plural active participle of בָּכָה; (with the article) the weepers; Bo-kim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Bochim.
H1067: Feminine from בָּכַר; the eldest daughter. In the KJV it is rendered: firstborn.
H1068: From בָּכָה; a weeping. In the KJV it is rendered: mourning.
H1069: A primitive root; properly, to burst the womb, i.e. (causatively) bear or make early fruit (of woman or tree); also (as denominative from בִּכּוּרִים) to give the birthright. In the KJV it is rendered: make firstborn, be firstling, bring forth first child (new fruit).
H1070: From בָּכַר (in the sense of youth); a young camel. In the KJV it is rendered: dromedary.
H1071: The same as בִּכְרֵי; Beker, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Becher.
H1072: Feminine of בִּכְרֵי; a young she-camel. In the KJV it is rendered: dromedary.
H1073: By orthographical variation for בִּכּוּרָה; a first- ripe fig. In the KJV it is rendered: firstripe.
H1074: From בָּכַר; first-born; Bokeru, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bocheru.
H1075: From בָּכַר; youth-ful; Bikri, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bichri.
H1076: Patronymically from בָּ֫כֶר; a Bakrite (collectively) or descendants of Beker. In the KJV it is rendered: Bachrites.
H1077: From בָּלָה; properly, a failure; by implication nothing; usually (adverb) not at all; also lest. In the KJV it is rendered: lest, neither, no, none (that.
H1078: By contraction for בַּ֫עַל; Bel, the Baal of the Babylonians. In the KJV it is rendered: Bel.
H1079: (Aramaic) from בְּלָא; properly, anxiety, i.e. (by implication) the heart (as its seat). In the KJV it is rendered: heart.
H1080: (Aramaic) corresponding to בָּלָה (but used only in a mental sense); to afflict. In the KJV it is rendered: wear out.
H1081: From בֵּל and אָדוֹן (contracted); Bel (is his) lord; Baladan, the name of a Babylonian prince. In the KJV it is rendered: Baladan.
H1082: A primitive root; to break off or loose (in a favorable or unfavorable sense), i.e. desist (from grief) or invade (with destruction). In the KJV it is rendered: comfort, (recover) strength(-en).
H1083: From בָּלַג; desistance; Bilgah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Bilgah.
H1084: From בָּלַג; desistant; Bilgai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bilgai.
H1085: Of uncertain derivation; Bildad, one of Job's friends. In the KJV it is rendered: Bildad.
H1086: A primitive root; to fail; by implication to wear out, decay (causatively, consume, spend). In the KJV it is rendered: consume, enjoy long, become (make, wax) old, spend, waste.
H1087: From בָּלָה; worn out. In the KJV it is rendered: old.
H1088: Feminine of בָּלִים; failure; Balah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Balah.
H1089: A primitive root (rather by transposition for בָּהַל); to palpitate; hence, (causatively) to terrify. In the KJV it is rendered: trouble.
H1090: From בָּלַהּ; timid; Bilhah, the name of one of Jacob's concubines; also of a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Bilhah.
H1091: From בָּלַהּ; alarm; hence, destruction. In the KJV it is rendered: terror, trouble.
H1092: From בָּלַהּ; timid; Bilhan, the name of an Edomite and of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bilhan.
H1093: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to בָּלָה; excise (on articles consumed). In the KJV it is rendered: tribute.
H1094: Or (fully) blowy; from בָּלָה; (only in plural construction) rags. In the KJV it is rendered: old.
H1095: Of foreign derivation; Belteshatstsar, the Babylonian name of Daniel. In the KJV it is rendered: Belteshazzar.
H1096: (Aramaic) corresponding to בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר. In the KJV it is rendered: Belteshazzar.
H1097: From בָּלָה; properly, failure, i.e. nothing or destruction; usually (with preposition) without, not yet, because not, as long as, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: corruption, ig(norantly), for lack of, where no.
H1098: From בָּלַל; mixed, i.e. (specifically) feed (for cattle). In the KJV it is rendered: corn, fodder, provender.
H1099: From בְּלִי and מָה; (as indef.) nothing whatever. In the KJV it is rendered: nothing.
H1100: From בְּלִי and יָעַל; without profit, worthlessness; by extension, destruction, wickedness (often in connection with אּישׁ, נָשִׁים, בֵּן, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: Belial, evil, naughty, ungodly (men), wicked.
H1101: A primitive root; to overflow (specifically with oil.); by implication, to mix; also (denominatively from בְּלִיל) to fodder. In the KJV it is rendered: anoint, confound, X fade, mingle, mix (self), give provender, temper.
H1102: A primitive root; to muzzle. In the KJV it is rendered: be held in.
H1103: A primitive root; to pinch sycamore figs (a process necessary to ripen them). In the KJV it is rendered: gatherer.
H1104: A primitive root; to make away with (specifically by swallowing); generally, to destroy. In the KJV it is rendered: cover, destroy, devour, eat up, be at end, spend up, swallow down (up).
H1105: From בָּלַע; a gulp; figuratively, destruction. In the KJV it is rendered: devouring, that which he hath swallowed up.
H1106: The same as בֶּ֫לַע; Bela, the name of a place, also of an Edomite and of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Bela.
H1107: Or balmadey; constructive plural from בַּל and עַד, not till, i.e. (as preposition or adverb) except, without, besides. In the KJV it is rendered: beside, not (in), save, without.
H1108: Patronymically from בָּ֫לַע: a Belaite (collectively) or descendants of Bela. In the KJV it is rendered: Belaites.
H1109: Probably from בַּל and עָם; not (of the) people, i.e. foreigner; Bilam, a Mesopotamian prophet; also a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Balaam, Bileam.
H1110: A primitive root; to annihilate. In the KJV it is rendered: (make) waste.
H1111: From בָּלַק; waster; Balak, a Moabitish king. In the KJV it is rendered: Balak.
H1112: Or Belshatstsar; of foreign origin (compare בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר); Belshatstsar, a Babylonian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Belshazzar.
H1113: (Aramaic) corresponding to NONE. In the KJV it is rendered: Belshazzar.
H1114: Of uncertain derivation; Bilshan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bilshan.
H1115: Constructive feminine of בָּלָה (equivalent to בְּלִי); properly, a failure of, i.e. (used only as a negative particle, usually with a prepositional prefix) not, except, without, unless, besides, because not, until, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: because un(satiable), beside, but, + continual, except, from, lest, neither, no more, none, not, nothing, save, that no, without.
H1116: From an unused root (meaning to be high); an elevation. In the KJV it is rendered: height, high place, wave.
H1117: The same as בָּמָה; Bamah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Bamah.
H1118: Probably from מָהַל with prepositional prefix; with pruning; Bimhal, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bimhal.
H1119: Prolongation for prepositional prefix; in, with, by, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: for, in into, through.
H1120: Plural of בָּמָה; heights; or (fully) Bamowth Bahal; from the same and בַּ֫עַל; heights of Baal; Bamoth or Bamoth-Baal, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Bamoth, Bamoth-baal.
H1121: From בָּנָה; a son (as a builder of the family name), in the widest sense (of literal and figurative relationship, including grandson, subject, nation, quality or condition, etc., (like אָב, אָח, etc.)). In the KJV it is rendered: + afflicted, age, (Ahoh-) (Ammon-) (Hachmon-) (Lev-)ite, (anoint-)ed one, appointed to, (+) arrow, (Assyr-) (Babylon-) (Egypt-) (Grec-)ian, one born, bough, branch, breed, + (young) bullock, + (young) calf, X came up in, child, colt, X common, X corn, daughter, X of first, + firstborn, foal, + very fruitful, + postage, X in, + kid, + lamb, (+) man, meet, + mighty, + nephew, old, (+) people, + rebel, + robber, X servant born, X soldier, son, + spark, + steward, + stranger, X surely, them of, + tumultuous one, + valiant(-est), whelp, worthy, young (one), youth.
H1122: The same as בֵּן; Ben, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ben.
H1123: (Aramaic) corresponding to בֵּן. In the KJV it is rendered: child, son, young.
H1124: (Aramaic) or bnah (Aramaic); corresponding to בָּנָה; to build. In the KJV it is rendered: build, make.
H1125: From בֵּן and אֲבִימֶ֫לֶך; (the) son of Abinadab; Ben-Abinadab, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: the son of Abinadab.
H1126: From בֵּן and אָ֫וֶן; son of my sorrow; Ben-Oni, the original name of Benjamin. In the KJV it is rendered: Ben-oni.
H1127: From בֵּן and גָּ֫בֶר; son of (the) hero; Ben- Geber, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: the son of Geber.
H1128: From בֵּן and a derivative of דָּקַר; son of piercing (or of a lance); Ben-Deker, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: the son of Dekar.
H1129: A primitive root; to build (literally and figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: (begin to) build(-er), obtain children, make, repair, set (up), X surely.
H1130: From בֵּן and הֲדָד; son of Hadad; Ben-Hadad, the name of several Syrian kings. In the KJV it is rendered: Ben-hadad.
H1131: From בָּנָה; built up; Binnui, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Binnui.
H1132: From בֵּן and זוֹחֵת; son of Zocheth; Ben- Zocheth, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ben-zoketh.
H1133: From בֵּן and חוּר; son of Chur; Ben-Chur, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: the son of Hur.
H1134: From בֵּן and חָ֫יִל; son of might; Ben-Chail, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ben-hail.
H1135: From בֵּן and חָנָן; son of Chanan; Ben- Chanan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ben-hanan.
H1136: From בֵּן and חָ֫סֶד; son of kindness; Ben- Chesed, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: the son of Hesed.
H1137: From בָּנָה; built; Bani, the name of five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Bani.
H1138: Or (fuller) Buwniy; from בָּנָה; built; Bunni or Buni, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bunni.
H1139: From the plural construction of בֵּן and בָּרָק; sons of lightning, Bene-berak, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Bene-barak.
H1140: Feminine from בָּנָה; a structure. In the KJV it is rendered: building.
H1141: Or (prolonged) Bnayahuw; from בָּנָה and יָהּ; Jah has built; Benajah, the name of twelve Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Benaiah.
H1142: From the plural of בֵּן and יַעֲקָן; sons of Yaakan; Bene-Jaakan, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Bene-jaakan.
H1143: Dual of בֵּין; a double interval, i.e. the space between two armies. In the KJV it is rendered: + champion.
H1144: From בֵּן and יָמִין; son of (the) right hand; Binjamin, youngest son of Jacob; also the tribe descended from him, and its territory. In the KJV it is rendered: Benjamin.
H1145: Sometimes (with the article inserted) Ben-ha-yminiy; with אּישׁ inserted (1 Sam. 9:1) Ben-miysh Ymiyniy; son of a man of Jemini; or shortened (1 Sam. 9:4; Esth. 2:5) Iysh Ymiyniy; a man of Jemini, or (1 Sam. 20:1) simply Yminiy; a Jeminite; (plural Bniy Ymiyniy; patron from בִּנְיָמִן; a Benjaminite, or descendent of Benjamin. In the KJV it is rendered: Benjamite, of Benjamin.
H1146: From בָּנָה; an edifice. In the KJV it is rendered: building.
H1147: (Aramaic) corresponding to בִּנְיָן. In the KJV it is rendered: building.
H1148: Probably from בֵּן with pron. suff.; our son; Beninu, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Beninu.
H1149: (Aramaic) of uncertain affinity; to be enraged. In the KJV it is rendered: be angry.
H1150: Or Bincah; of uncertain derivation; Bina or Binah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Binea, Bineah.
H1151: From בֵּן and עָם with pronomial suffix; son of my people; Ben-Ammi, a son of Lot. In the KJV it is rendered: Ben-ammi.
H1152: From סוֹד and יָהּ with prepositional prefix; in (the) counsel of Jehovah; Besodejah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Besodeiah.
H1153: From בּוּס; domineering; Besai, one of the Nethinim. In the KJV it is rendered: Besai.
H1154: From an unused root meaning to be sour; an immature grape. In the KJV it is rendered: unripe grape.
H1155: From the same as בֵּ֫סֶר. In the KJV it is rendered: sour grape.
H1156: (Aramaic) or b ah (Aramaic); corresponding to בָּעָה; to seek or ask. In the KJV it is rendered: ask, desire, make (petition), pray, request, seek.
H1157: From עַד with prepositional prefix; in up to or over against; generally at, beside, among, behind, for, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: about, at by (means of), for, over, through, up (-on), within.
H1158: A primitive root; to gush over, i.e. to swell; (figuratively) to desire earnestly; by implication to ask. In the KJV it is rendered: cause, inquire, seek up, swell out.
H1159: (Aramaic) from בְּעָא; a request. In the KJV it is rendered: petition.
H1160: From בָּעַר (in the sense of burning); a lamp; Beor, the name of the father of an Edomitish king; also of that of Balaam. In the KJV it is rendered: Beor.
H1161: Masculine plural from בָּעַת; alarms. In the KJV it is rendered: terrors.
H1162: From an unused root of uncertain meaning; Boaz, the ancestor of David; also the name of a pillar in front of the temple. In the KJV it is rendered: Boaz.
H1163: A primitive root; to trample down, i.e. (figuratively) despise. In the KJV it is rendered: kick.
H1164: From בָּעָה; a prayer. In the KJV it is rendered: grave.
H1165: From בָּעַר (in the sense of eating): cattle. In the KJV it is rendered: beast, cattle.
H1166: A primitive root; to be master; hence, (as denominative from בַּ֫עַל) to marry. In the KJV it is rendered: have dominion (over), be husband, marry(-ried, X wife).
H1167: From בָּעַל; a master; hence, a husband, or (figuratively) owner (often used with another noun in modifications of this latter sense). In the KJV it is rendered: + archer, + babbler, + bird, captain, chief man, + confederate, + have to do, + dreamer, those to whom it is due, + furious, those that are given to it, great, + hairy, he that hath it, have, + horseman, husband, lord, man, + married, master, person, + sworn, they of.
H1168: The same as בַּ֫עַל; Baal, a Phoenician deity. In the KJV it is rendered: Baal, (plural) Baalim.
H1169: (Aramaic) corresponding to בַּ֫עַל. In the KJV it is rendered: + chancellor.
H1170: From בַּ֫עַל and בְּרִית; Baal of (the) covenant; Baal-Berith, a special deity of the Shechemites. In the KJV it is rendered: Baal-berith.
H1171: From בַּ֫עַל and גָּד; Baal of Fortune; Baal-Gad, a place in Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Baal-gad.
H1172: Feminine of בַּ֫עַל; a mistress. In the KJV it is rendered: that hath, mistress.
H1173: The same as בַּעֲלַת; Baalah, the name of three places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Baalah.
H1174: From בַּ֫עַל and הָמוֹן; possessor of a multitude; Baal-Hamon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Baal-hamon.
H1175: Plural of בַּעֲלַת; mistresses; Bealoth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Bealoth, in Aloth (by mistake for a plural from `alah with prepositional prefix).
H1176: From בַּ֫עַל and זְבוּב; Baal of (the) Fly; Baal-Zebub, a special deity of the Ekronites. In the KJV it is rendered: Baal-zebub.
H1177: From בַּ֫עַל and חָנַן; possessor of grace; Baal-Chanan, the name of an Edomite, also of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Baal-hanan.
H1178: From בַּ֫עַל and a modification of חָצֵר; possessor of a village; Baal-Chatsor, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Baal-hazor.
H1179: From בַּ֫עַל and חֶרְמוֹן; possessor of Hermon; Baal-Chermon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Baal-hermon.
H1180: From בַּ֫עַל with pron. suff.; my master; Baali, a symbolical name for Jehovah. In the KJV it is rendered: Baali.
H1181: From the plural of בַּ֫עַל and the plural of בָּמָה; Baals of (the) heights; Baale-Bamoth, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: lords of the high places.
H1182: From בַּ֫עַל and יָדַע; Baal has known; Beeljada, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Beeliada.
H1183: From בַּ֫עַל and יָהּ; Jah (is) master; Bealjah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bealiah.
H1184: From the plural of בַּ֫עַל and יְהוּדָה; masters of Judah; Baale-Jehudah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Baale of Judah.
H1185: Probably from a derivative of עָלַס with prepositional prefix; in exultation; Baalis, an Ammonitish king. In the KJV it is rendered: Baalis.
H1186: From בַּ֫עַל and מָעוֹן; Baal of (the) habitation (of) (compare בֵּית בַּ֫עַל מְעוֹן); Baal-Meon, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Baal-meon.
H1187: From בַּ֫עַל and פְּעוֹר; Baal of Peor; Baal-Peor, a Moabitish deity. In the KJV it is rendered: Baal-peor.
H1188: From בַּ֫עַל and the plural of פָּ֫רֶץ; possessor of breaches; Baal-Peratsim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Baal- perazim.
H1189: From בַּ֫עַל and צָפוֹן (in the sense of cold) (according to others an Egyptian form of Typhon, the destroyer); Baal of winter; Baal-Tsephon, a place in Eqypt. In the KJV it is rendered: Baal-zephon.
H1190: From בַּ֫עַל and שָׁלִ֫שָׁה; Baal of Shalishah, Baal-Shalishah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Baal-shalisha.
H1191: A modification of בַּעֲלַת; mistressship; Baalath, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Baalath.
H1192: From בַּעֲלַת and בְּאֵר; mistress of a well; Baalath-Beer, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Baalath-beer.
H1193: From בַּ֫עַל and תָּמָר; possessor of (the) palm-tree; Baal-Tamar, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Baal-tamar.
H1194: Probably a contraction of בֵּית בַּ֫עַל מְעוֹן; Beon, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Beon.
H1195: The same as בַּעֲנָה; Banana, the name of four Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Baana, Baanah.
H1196: From a derivative of עָנָה with prepositional prefix; in affliction. In the KJV it is rendered: Baanah, the name of four Israelites:--Baanah.
H1197: A primitive root; to kindle, i.e. consume (by fire or by eating); also (as denominative from בָּ֫עַר) to be(-come) brutish. In the KJV it is rendered: be brutish, bring (put, take) away, burn, (cause to) eat (up), feed, heat, kindle, set ((on fire)), waste.
H1198: From בָּעַר; properly, foot (as consumed); i.e. (by exten.) of cattle brutishness; (concretely) stupid. In the KJV it is rendered: brutish (person), foolish.
H1199: From בָּ֫עַר; brutish: Baara, an Israelitish woman. In the KJV it is rendered: Baara.
H1200: From בָּעַר; a burning. In the KJV it is rendered: fire.
H1201: From an unused root meaning to stink; offensiveness; Basha, a king of Israel. In the KJV it is rendered: Baasha.
H1202: From עָשָׂה and יָהּ with a prepositional prefix; in (the) work of Jah; Baasejah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Baaseiah.
H1203: From עַשְׁתְּרוֹת (as singular of עַשְׁתָּרוֹת) with a prepositional prefix; with Ashtoreth; Beeshterah, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Beeshterah.
H1204: A primitive root; to fear. In the KJV it is rendered: affright, be (make) afraid, terrify, trouble.
H1205: From בָּעַת; fear. In the KJV it is rendered: trouble.
H1206: Probably the same as בּוּץ; mud (as whitish clay). In the KJV it is rendered: mire.
H1207: Intensive from בֹּץ; a swamp. In the KJV it is rendered: fen, mire(-ry place).
H1208: From בָּצַר; inaccessible, i.e. lofty. In the KJV it is rendered: vintage (by confusion with batsiyr).
H1209: Perhaps the same as בֵּסָי; Betsai, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Bezai.
H1210: From בָּצַר; clipped, i.e. the grape crop. In the KJV it is rendered: vintage.
H1211: From an unused root apparently meaning to peel; an onion. In the KJV it is rendered: onion.
H1212: Probably from צֵל and אֵל with a prepositional prefix; in (the) shadow (i.e. protection) of God; Betsalel, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Bezaleel.
H1213: Or Batsliyth; from the same as בְּצָלִים; a peeling; Batsluth or Batslith, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bazlith, Bazluth.
H1214: A primitive root to break off, i.e. (usually) plunder; figuratively, to finish, or (intransitively) stop. In the KJV it is rendered: (be) covet(- ous), cut (off), finish, fulfill, gain (greedily), get, be given to (covetousness), greedy, perform, be wounded.
H1215: From בָּצַע; plunder; by extension, gain (usually unjust). In the KJV it is rendered: covetousness, (dishonest) gain, lucre, profit.
H1216: A primitive root; perhaps to swell up, i.e. blister. In the KJV it is rendered: swell.
H1217: From בָּצֵק; dough (as swelling by fermentation). In the KJV it is rendered: dough, flour.
H1218: From בָּצֵק; a swell of ground; Botscath, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Bozcath, Boskath.
H1219: A primitive root; to clip off; specifically (as denominative from בָּצִיר) to gather grapes; also to be isolated (i.e. inaccessible by height or fortification). In the KJV it is rendered: cut off, (de-)fenced, fortify, (grape) gather(-er), mighty things, restrain, strong, wall (up), withhold.
H1220: From בָּצַר; strictly a clipping, i.e. gold (as dug out). In the KJV it is rendered: gold defence.
H1221: The same as בָּ֫צֶר, an inaccessible spot; Betser, a place in Palestine; also an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bezer.
H1222: Another form for בָּ֫צֶר; gold. In the KJV it is rendered: gold.
H1223: Feminine from בָּצַר; an enclosure, i.e. sheep fold. In the KJV it is rendered: Bozrah.
H1224: The same as בָּצְרָה; Botsrah, a place in Edom. In the KJV it is rendered: Bozrah.
H1225: Masculine intensive from בָּצַר; a fortress. In the KJV it is rendered: stronghold.
H1226: Feminine intensive from בָּצַר; restraint (of rain), i.e. drought. In the KJV it is rendered: dearth, drought.
H1227: The same as בַּקְבֻּק; Bakbuk, one of the Nethinim. In the KJV it is rendered: Bakbuk.
H1228: From בָּקַק; a bottle (from the gurgling in emptying). In the KJV it is rendered: bottle, cruse.
H1229: From בַּקְבֻּק and יָהּ; emptying (i.e. wasting) of Jah; Bakbukjah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bakbukiah.
H1230: Reduplicated from בָּקַר; searcher; Bakbakkar, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bakbakkar.
H1231: From בָּקַק; wasteful; Bukki, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Bukki.
H1232: From בָּקַק and יָהּ; wasting of Jah; Bukkijah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bukkiah.
H1233: From בָּקַע; a fissure. In the KJV it is rendered: breach, cleft.
H1234: A primitive root; to cleave; generally, to rend, break, rip or open. In the KJV it is rendered: make a breach, break forth (into, out, in pieces, through, up), be ready to burst, cleave (asunder), cut out, divide, hatch, rend (asunder), rip up, tear, win.
H1235: From בָּקַע; a section (half) of a shekel, i.e. a beka (a weight and a coin). In the KJV it is rendered: bekah, half a shekel.
H1236: (Aramaic) corresponding to בִּקְעָה. In the KJV it is rendered: plain.
H1237: From בָּקַע; properly, a split, i.e. a wide level valley between mountains. In the KJV it is rendered: plain, valley.
H1238: A primitive root; to pour out, i.e. to empty, figuratively, to depopulate; by analogy, to spread out (as a fruitful vine). In the KJV it is rendered: (make) empty (out), fail, X utterly, make void.
H1239: A primitive root; properly, to plough, or (generally) break forth, i.e. (figuratively) to inspect, admire, care for, consider. In the KJV it is rendered: (make) inquire (-ry), (make) search, seek out.
H1240: (Aramaic) corresponding to בָּקַר. In the KJV it is rendered: inquire, make search.
H1241: From בָּקַר; beef cattle or an animal of the ox family of either gender (as used for plowing); collectively, a herd. In the KJV it is rendered: beeve, bull (+ -ock), + calf, + cow, great (cattle), + heifer, herd, kine, ox.
H1242: From בָּקַר; properly, dawn (as the break of day); generally, morning. In the KJV it is rendered: (+) day, early, morning, morrow.
H1243: Intensive from בָּקַר; a looking after. In the KJV it is rendered: seek out.
H1244: From בָּקַר; properly, examination, i.e. (by implication) punishment. In the KJV it is rendered: scourged.
H1245: A primitive root; to search out (by any method, specifically in worship or prayer); by implication, to strive after. In the KJV it is rendered: ask, beg, beseech, desire, enquire, get, make inquisition, procure, (make) request, require, seek (for).
H1246: From בָּקַשׁ; a petition. In the KJV it is rendered: request.
H1247: (Aramaic) corresponding to בֵּן; a son, grandson, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: X old, son.
H1248: Borrowed (as a title) from בַּר; the heir (apparent to the throne). In the KJV it is rendered: son.
H1249: From בָּרַר (in its various senses); beloved; also pure, empty. In the KJV it is rendered: choice, clean, clear, pure.
H1250: Or bar; from בָּרַר (in the sense of winnowing); grain of any kind (even while standing in the field); by extens. the open country. In the KJV it is rendered: corn, wheat.
H1251: (Aramaic) corresponding to בָּר; a field. In the KJV it is rendered: field.
H1252: From בָּרַר; purify. In the KJV it is rendered: cleanness, pureness.
H1253: The same as בֹּר; vegetable lye (from its cleansing); used as a soap for washing, or a flux for metals. In the KJV it is rendered: X never so, purely.
H1254: A primitive root; (absolutely) to create; (qualified) to cut down (a wood), select, feed (as formative processes). In the KJV it is rendered: choose, create (creator), cut down, dispatch, do, make (fat).
H1255: A variation of NONE; Berodak-Baladan, a Babylonian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Berodach-baladan.
H1256: From בָּרָא and שְׁמוּאֵל; Jah has created; Berajah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Beraiah.
H1257: By reduplication from בָּר; a fowl (as fattened on grain). In the KJV it is rendered: fowl.
H1258: A primitive root, to hail. In the KJV it is rendered: hail.
H1260: From בָּרַד; hail; Bered, the name of a place south of Palestine, also of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bered.
H1261: From בָּרַד; spotted (as if with hail). In the KJV it is rendered: grisled.
H1262: A primitive root; to select; also (as denominative from בָּר) to feed; also (as equivalent to בָּרַר) to render clear (Eccl. 3:18). In the KJV it is rendered: choose, (cause to) eat, manifest, (give) meat.
H1263: Passive participle from בָּרַך; blessed; Baruk, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Baruch.
H1264: Probably of foreign origin; damask (stuff of variegated thread). In the KJV it is rendered: rich apparel.
H1265: Of uncertain derivation; a cypress (?) tree; hence, a lance or a musical instrument (as made of that wood). In the KJV it is rendered: fir (tree).
H1266: A variation of בְּרוֹשׁ; the cypress (or some elastic tree). In the KJV it is rendered: fir.
H1267: From בָּרָה; food. In the KJV it is rendered: meat.
H1268: Or Berothay; probably from בְּרוֹתִים; cypress or cypresslike; Berothah or Berothai, a place north of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Berothah, Berothai.
H1269: Probably feminine plural from an unused root (apparently mean to pierce); holes; Birzoth, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Birzavith (from the marg.
H1270: Perhaps from the root of בִּרְזוּת; iron (as cutting); by extension, an iron implement. In the KJV it is rendered: (ax) head, iron.
H1271: From בַּרְזֶל; iron-hearted; Barzillai, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Barzillai.
H1272: A primitive root; to bolt, i.e. figuratively, to flee suddenly. In the KJV it is rendered: chase (away); drive away, fain, flee (away), put to flight, make haste, reach, run away, shoot.
H1273: By transposition for בַּחֲרוּמִי; a Barchumite, or native of Bachurim. In the KJV it is rendered: Barhumite.
H1274: From בָּרָה; fat. In the KJV it is rendered: fat.
H1275: Probably by contraction from בְּאֵרִי; Beri, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Beri.
H1276: Of uncertain derivation; (only in the plural and with the article) the Berites, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Berites.
H1277: From בָּרָא (in the sense of בָּרָה); fatted or plump. In the KJV it is rendered: fat ((fleshed), -ter), fed, firm, plenteous, rank.
H1278: Feminine from בָּרָא; a creation, i.e. a novelty. In the KJV it is rendered: new thing.
H1279: Feminine from בָּרָה; food. In the KJV it is rendered: meat.
H1280: From בָּרַח; a bolt. In the KJV it is rendered: bar, fugitive.
H1281: Or (shortened) bariach; from בָּרַח; a fugitive, i.e. the serpent (as fleeing), and the constellation by that name. In the KJV it is rendered: crooked, noble, piercing.
H1282: The same as בָּרִ֫יחַ; Bariach, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Bariah.
H1283: Apparently from the feminine of רָע with a prepositional prefix; in trouble; Beriah, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Beriah.
H1284: Patronymically from בְּרִיעָה; a Beriite (collectively) or descendants of Beriah. In the KJV it is rendered: Beerites.
H1285: From בָּרָה (in the sense of cutting (like בָּרָא)); a compact (because made by passing between pieces of flesh). In the KJV it is rendered: confederacy, (con-)feder(-ate), covenant, league.
H1286: The same as בְּרִית; Berith, a Shechemitish deity. In the KJV it is rendered: Berith.
H1287: Feminine of בֹּר; vegetable alkali. In the KJV it is rendered: sope.
H1288: A primitive root; to kneel; by implication to bless God (as an act of adoration), and (vice-versa) man (as a benefit); also (by euphemism) to curse (God or the king, as treason). In the KJV it is rendered: X abundantly, X altogether, X at all, blaspheme, bless, congratulate, curse, X greatly, X indeed, kneel (down), praise, salute, X still, thank.
H1289: (Aramaic) corresponding to בָּרַך. In the KJV it is rendered: bless, kneel.
H1290: From בָּרַך; a knee. In the KJV it is rendered: knee.
H1291: (Aramaic) corresponding to בֶּ֫רֶך. In the KJV it is rendered: knee.
H1292: From בָּרַך and אֵל, God has blessed; Barakel, the father of one of Job's friends. In the KJV it is rendered: Barachel.
H1293: From בָּרַך; benediction; by implication prosperity. In the KJV it is rendered: blessing, liberal, pool, present.
H1294: The same as בְּרָכָה; Berakah, the name of an Israelite, and also of a valley in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Berachah.
H1295: From בָּרַך; a reservoir (at which camels kneel as a resting-place). In the KJV it is rendered: (fish-)pool.
H1296: Or Berekyahuw; from בֶּ֫רֶך and יָהּ; knee (i.e. blessing) of Jah; Berekjah, the name of six Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Berachiah, Berechiah.
H1297: (Aramaic) perhaps from רוּם with a prepositional prefix; properly, highly, i.e. surely; but used adversatively, however. In the KJV it is rendered: but, nevertheless, yet.
H1298: Of uncertain derivation; Bera, a Sodomitish king. In the KJV it is rendered: Bera.
H1299: A primitive root; to lighten (lightning). In the KJV it is rendered: cast forth.
H1300: From בָּרַק; lightning; by analogy, a gleam; concretely, a flashing sword. In the KJV it is rendered: bright, glitter(-ing sword), lightning.
H1301: The same as בָּרָק; Barak, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Barak.
H1302: Of uncertain derivation; Barkos, one of the Nethimim. In the KJV it is rendered: Barkos.
H1303: From בָּרָק; a thorn (perhaps as burning brightly). In the KJV it is rendered: brier.
H1304: Or barkath; from בָּרָק; a gem (as flashing), perhaps the emerald. In the KJV it is rendered: carbuncle.
H1305: A primitive root; to clarify (i.e. brighten), examine, select. In the KJV it is rendered: make bright, choice, chosen, cleanse (be clean), clearly, polished, (shew self) pure(-ify), purge (out).
H1306: Probably from רֶ֫שַׁע with a prepositional prefix; with wickedness; Birsha, a king of Gomorrah. In the KJV it is rendered: Birsha.
H1307: Patrial from בֵּרֹתַי; a Berothite, or inhabitant of Berothai. In the KJV it is rendered: Berothite.
