H1308: From בָּשַׂר; cheerful; Besor, a stream of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Besor.
H1309: Or (shortened) bsorah; feminine from בָּשַׂר; glad tidings; by implication, reward for good news. In the KJV it is rendered: reward for tidings.
H1310: A primitive root; properly, to boil up; hence, to be done in cooking; figuratively to ripen. In the KJV it is rendered: bake, boil, bring forth, roast, seethe, sod (be sodden).
H1311: From בָּשַׁל; boiled. In the KJV it is rendered: X at all, sodden.
H1312: Of foreign derivation; Bishlam, a Pers. In the KJV it is rendered: Bishlam.
H1313: From an unused root meaning to be fragrant; (compare סַמִּים) the balsam plant. In the KJV it is rendered: spice.
H1314: Or bosem; from the same as בָּשָׂם; fragrance; by implication, spicery; also the balsam plant. In the KJV it is rendered: smell, spice, sweet (odour).
H1315: Feminine of בְּשָׂמִים (the second form); fragrance; Bosmath, the name of a wife of Esau, and of a daughter of Solomon. In the KJV it is rendered: Bashemath, Basmath.
H1316: Of uncertain derivation; Bashan (often with the article), a region East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Bashan.
H1317: Feminine from בּוּשׁ; shamefulness. In the KJV it is rendered: shame.
H1318: A primitive root; to trample down. In the KJV it is rendered: tread.
H1319: A primitive root; properly, to be fresh, i.e. full (rosy, (figuratively) cheerful); to announce (glad news). In the KJV it is rendered: messenger, preach, publish, shew forth, (bear, bring, carry, preach, good, tell good) tidings.
H1320: From בָּשַׂר; flesh (from its freshness); by extension, body, person; also (by euphem.) the pudenda of a man. In the KJV it is rendered: body, (fat, lean) flesh(-ed), kin, (man-)kind, + nakedness, self, skin.
H1321: (Aramaic) corresponding to בָּשָׂר. In the KJV it is rendered: flesh.
H1322: From בּוּשׁ; shame (the feeling and the condition, as well as its cause); by implication (specifically) an idol. In the KJV it is rendered: ashamed, confusion, + greatly, (put to) shame(-ful thing).
H1323: From בָּנָה (as feminine of בֵּן); a daughter (used in the same wide sense as other terms of relationship, literally and figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: apple (of the eye), branch, company, daughter, X first, X old, + owl, town, village.
H1324: Probably from the same as בַּתּוֹת; a bath or Hebrew measure (as a means of division) of liquids. In the KJV it is rendered: bath.
H1325: (Aramaic) corresponding to בָּת. In the KJV it is rendered: bath.
H1326: Probably an orthographical variation for בַּתּוֹת; desolation. In the KJV it is rendered: waste.
H1327: Feminine from an unused root (meaning to break in pieces); desolation. In the KJV it is rendered: desolate.
H1328: Apparently from the same as בָּתָה and אֵל; destroyed of God; Bethuel, the name of a nephew of Abraham, and of a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Bethuel.
H1329: For בְּתוּאֵל; Bethul (i.e. Bethuel), a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Bethuel.
H1330: Feminine passive participle of an unused root meaning to separate; a virgin (from her privacy); sometimes (by continuation) a bride; also (figuratively) a city or state. In the KJV it is rendered: maid, virgin.
H1331: Masculine plural of the same as בְּתוּלָה; (collectively and abstractly) virginity; by implication and concretely, the tokens of it. In the KJV it is rendered: X maid, virginity.
H1332: From בַּת and יָהּ; daughter (i.e. worshipper) of Jah; Bithjah, an Egyptian woman. In the KJV it is rendered: Bithiah.
H1333: A primitive root; to cut in pieces. In the KJV it is rendered: thrust through.
H1334: A primitive root, to chop up. In the KJV it is rendered: divide.
H1335: From בָּתַר; a section. In the KJV it is rendered: part, piece.
H1336: The same as בֶּ֫תֶר; Bether, a (craggy) place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Bether.
H1337: From בַּת and a masculine plural from רָב; the daughter (i.e. city) of Rabbah. In the KJV it is rendered: Bath-rabbim.
H1338: From בָּתַר; (with the article) the craggy spot; Bithron, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Bithron.
H1339: From בַּת and שֶׁ֫בַע (in the sense of שָׁבַע); daughter of an oath; Bath-Sheba, the mother of Solomon. In the KJV it is rendered: Bath- sheba.
H1340: From בַּת and שׁ֫וֹעַ; daughter of wealth; Bath-shua, the same as בַּת־שֶׁ֫בַע. In the KJV it is rendered: Bath-shua.
H1341: For גֵּאֶה; haughty. In the KJV it is rendered: proud.
H1342: A primitive root; to mount up; hence, in general, to rise, (figuratively) be majestic. In the KJV it is rendered: gloriously, grow up, increase, be risen, triumph.
H1343: From גָּאָה; lofty; figuratively, arrogant. In the KJV it is rendered: proud.
H1344: Feminine from גָּאָה; arrogance. In the KJV it is rendered: pride.
H1345: From גָּאָה and אֵל; majesty of God; Geuel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Geuel.
H1346: From גָּאָה; arrogance or majesty; by implication, (concretely) ornament. In the KJV it is rendered: excellency, haughtiness, highness, pride, proudly, swelling.
H1347: From גָּאָה; the same as גַּאֲוָה. In the KJV it is rendered: arrogancy, excellency(-lent), majesty, pomp, pride, proud, swelling.
H1348: From גָּאָה; the same as גַּאֲוָה. In the KJV it is rendered: excellent things, lifting up, majesty, pride, proudly, raging.
H1349: From גָּאָה: haughty. In the KJV it is rendered: proud.
H1350: A primitive root, to redeem (according to the Oriental law of kinship), i.e. to be the next of kin (and as such to buy back a relative's property, marry his widow, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: X in any wise, X at all, avenger, deliver, (do, perform the part of near, next) kinsfolk(-man), purchase, ransom, redeem(-er), revenger.
H1351: A primitive root, (rather identified with גָּאַל, through the idea of freeing, i.e. repudiating); to soil or (figuratively) desecrate. In the KJV it is rendered: defile, pollute, stain.
H1352: From גָּאַל; profanation. In the KJV it is rendered: defile.
H1353: Feminine passive participle of גָּאַל; redemption (including the right and the object); by implication, relationship. In the KJV it is rendered: kindred, redeem, redemption, right.
H1354: From an unused root meaning to hollow or curve; the back (as rounded (compare גֵּו and גּוּף); by analogy, the top or rim, a boss, a vault, arch of eye, bulwarks, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: back, body, boss, eminent (higher) place, (eye)brows, nave, ring.
H1355: (Aramaic) corresponding to גָּב. In the KJV it is rendered: back.
H1356: From גּוּב; a log (as cut out); also well or cistern (as dug). In the KJV it is rendered: beam, ditch, pit.
H1357: Probably from גּוּב (compare גֹּבַי); a locust (from its cutting). In the KJV it is rendered: locust.
H1358: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to גּוּב; a pit (for wild animals) (as cut out). In the KJV it is rendered: den.
H1359: Or (fully) Gowb; from גּוּב; pit; Gob, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gob.
H1360: From an unused root meaning probably to collect; a reservoir; by analogy, a marsh. In the KJV it is rendered: marish, pit.
H1361: A primitive root; to soar, i.e. be lofty; figuratively, to be haughty. In the KJV it is rendered: exalt, be haughty, be (make) high(-er), lift up, mount up, be proud, raise up great height, upward.
H1362: From גָּבַהּ; lofty (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: high, proud.
H1363: From גָּבַהּ; elation, grandeur, arrogance. In the KJV it is rendered: excellency, haughty, height, high, loftiness, pride.
H1364: Or (fully) gabowahh; from גָּבַהּ; elevated (or elated), powerful, arrogant. In the KJV it is rendered: haughty, height, high(-er), lofty, proud, X exceeding proudly.
H1365: From גָּבַהּ; pride. In the KJV it is rendered: loftiness, lofty.
H1366: Or (shortened) gbul; from גָּבַל; properly, a cord (as twisted), i.e. (by implication) a boundary; by extens. the territory inclosed. In the KJV it is rendered: border, bound, coast, X great, landmark, limit, quarter, space.
H1367: Or (shortened) gbulah; feminine of גְּבוּל; a boundary, region. In the KJV it is rendered: border, bound, coast, landmark.
H1368: Or (shortened) gibbor; intensive from the same as גָּ֫בֶר; powerful; by implication, warrior, tyrant. In the KJV it is rendered: champion, chief, X excel, giant, man, mighty (man, one), strong (man), valiant man.
H1369: Feminine passive participle from the same as גִּבּוֹר; force (literally or figuratively); by implication, valor, victory. In the KJV it is rendered: force, mastery, might, mighty (act, power), power, strength.
H1370: (Aramaic) corresponding to גְּבוּרָה; power. In the KJV it is rendered: might.
H1371: From an unused root meaning to be high (in the forehead); bald in the forehead. In the KJV it is rendered: forehead bald.
H1372: From the same as גִּבֵּ֫חַ; baldness in the forehead; by analogy, a bare spot on the right side of cloth. In the KJV it is rendered: bald forehead, X without.
H1373: From the same as גָּב; collective. In the KJV it is rendered: Gabbai, an Israelite:--Gabbai.
H1374: Plural of גֵּבִים; cisterns; Gebim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gebim.
H1375: From an unused root (meaning to be convex); a goblet; by analogy, the calyx of a flower. In the KJV it is rendered: house, cup, pot.
H1376: From גָּבַר; a master. In the KJV it is rendered: lord.
H1377: Feminine of גְּבִיר; a mistress. In the KJV it is rendered: queen.
H1378: From an unused root (probably meaning to freeze); crystal (from its resemblance to ice). In the KJV it is rendered: pearl.
H1379: A primitive root; properly, to twist as a rope; only (as a denominative from גְּבוּל) to bound (as by a line). In the KJV it is rendered: be border, set (bounds about).
H1380: From גָּבַל (in the sense of a chain of hills); a mountain; Gebal, a place in Phoenicia. In the KJV it is rendered: Gebal.
H1381: The same as גְּבַל; Gebal, a region in Idumaea. In the KJV it is rendered: Gebal.
H1382: : patrial from גְּבַל; a Gebalite, or inhabitant of Gebal. In the KJV it is rendered: Giblites, stone-squarer.
H1383: From גָּבַל; a twisted chain or lace. In the KJV it is rendered: end.
H1384: From an unused root meaning to be arched or contracted; hunch-backed. In the KJV it is rendered: crookbackt.
H1385: Feminine from the same as גִּבֵּן; curdled milk. In the KJV it is rendered: cheese.
H1386: From the same as גִּבֵּן; a hump or peak of hills. In the KJV it is rendered: high.
H1387: From the same as גָּבִ֫יעַ, a hillock; Geba, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gaba, Geba, Gibeah.
H1388: By permutation for גִּבְעָה; a hill; Giba, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gibeah.
H1389: Feminine from the same as גָּ֫בַע; a hillock. In the KJV it is rendered: hill, little hill.
H1390: The same as גִּבְעָה; Gibah; the name of three places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gibeah, the hill.
H1391: From the same as גָּ֫בַע; hilly; Gibon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gibeon.
H1392: Prolonged from גָּבִ֫יעַ; the calyx of a flower. In the KJV it is rendered: bolled.
H1393: Patrial from גִּבְעוֹן; a Gibonite, or inhabitant of Gibon. In the KJV it is rendered: Gibeonite.
H1394: From the same as גָּבִ֫יעַ; hilliness; Gibath. In the KJV it is rendered: Gibeath.
H1395: Patrial from גִּבְעָה; a Gibathite, or inhabitant of Gibath. In the KJV it is rendered: Gibeathite.
H1396: A primitive root; to be strong; by implication, to prevail, act insolently. In the KJV it is rendered: exceed, confirm, be great, be mighty, prevail, put to more (strength), strengthen, be stronger, be valiant.
H1397: From גָּבַר; properly, a valiant man or warrior; generally, a person simply. In the KJV it is rendered: every one, man, X mighty.
H1398: The same as גָּ֫בֶר; Geber, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Geber.
H1399: From גָּבַר; the same as גָּ֫בֶר; a person. In the KJV it is rendered: man.
H1400: (Aramaic) corresponding to גְּבַר. In the KJV it is rendered: certain, man.
H1401: (Aramaic) intensive of גְּבַר; valiant, or warrior. In the KJV it is rendered: mighty.
H1402: Intensive of גְּבַר; Gibbar, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Gibbar.
H1403: From גָּ֫בֶר and אֵל; man of God; Gabriel, an archangel. In the KJV it is rendered: Garbriel.
H1404: Feminine of גְּבִיר; mistress. In the KJV it is rendered: lady, mistress.
H1405: Intensive from גִּבְעָה; a hilly spot; Gibbethon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gibbethon.
H1406: Probably by reduplication from גָּאָה; a roof; by analogy, the top of an altar. In the KJV it is rendered: roof (of the house), (house) top (of the house).
H1407: From גָּדַד (in the sense of cutting); coriander seed (from its furrows). In the KJV it is rendered: coriander.
H1408: A variation of גָּד; Fortune, a Babylonian deity. In the KJV it is rendered: that troop.
H1409: From גּוּד (in the sense of distributing); fortune. In the KJV it is rendered: troop.
H1410: From גּוּד; Gad, a son of Jacob, including his tribe and its territory; also a prophet. In the KJV it is rendered: Gad.
H1411: (Aramaic) corresponding to גִּזְבָּר; a treasurer. In the KJV it is rendered: treasurer.
H1412: By reduplication from גָּדַד (in the sense of cutting) cleft; Gudgodah, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Gudgodah.
H1413: A primitive root (compare גּוּד); to crowd; also to gash (as if by pressing into). In the KJV it is rendered: assemble (selves by troops), gather (selves together, self in troops), cut selves.
H1414: (Aramaic) corresponding to גָּדַד; to cut down. In the KJV it is rendered: hew down.
H1415: From an unused root (meaning to cut off); a border of a river (as cut into by the stream). In the KJV it is rendered: bank.
H1416: From גָּדַד; a crowd (especially of soldiers). In the KJV it is rendered: army, band (of men), company, troop (of robbers).
H1417: Or (feminine) gdudah; from גָּדַד; a furrow (as cut). In the KJV it is rendered: furrow.
H1418: Feminine participle passive of גָּדַד; an incision. In the KJV it is rendered: cutting.
H1419: Or (shortened) gadol; from גָּדַל; great (in any sense); hence, older; also insolent. In the KJV it is rendered: + aloud, elder(-est), + exceeding(-ly), + far, (man of) great (man, matter, thing,-er,-ness), high, long, loud, mighty, more, much, noble, proud thing, X sore, (X) very.
H1420: Or (shortened) gdullah; or (less accurately) gduwllah; feminine of גָּדוֹל; greatness; (concretely) mighty acts. In the KJV it is rendered: dignity, great things(-ness), majesty.
H1421: Or (shortened) gidduph; and (feminine) gidduphah; or gidduphah; from גְּדוּפָה; vilification. In the KJV it is rendered: reproach, reviling.
H1422: Feminine passive participle of גָּדַף; a revilement. In the KJV it is rendered: taunt.
H1423: From the same as גְּדוֹת; a young goat (from browsing). In the KJV it is rendered: kid.
H1424: From גָּד; fortunate; Gadi, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Gadi.
H1425: Patronymically from גָּד; a Gadite (collectively) or descendants of Gad. In the KJV it is rendered: Gadites, children of Gad.
H1426: Intensive for גָּדִי; Gaddi, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Gaddi.
H1427: From גָּד and אֵל; fortune of God; Gaddiel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Gaddiel.
H1428: Or gadyah; the same as גְּדוֹת; a river brink. In the KJV it is rendered: bank.
H1429: Feminine of גֶּ֫דִי; a young female goat. In the KJV it is rendered: kid.
H1430: From an unused root (meaning to heap up); a stack of sheaves; by analogy, a tomb. In the KJV it is rendered: shock (stack) (of corn), tomb.
H1431: A primitive root; properly, to twist (compare גְּדִלִים), i.e. to be (causatively make) large (in various senses, as in body, mind, estate or honor, also in pride). In the KJV it is rendered: advance, boast, bring up, exceed, excellent, be(-come, do, give, make, wax), great(-er, come to.
H1432: From גָּדַל; large (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: great, grew.
H1433: From גָּדַל; magnitude (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: greatness, stout(-ness).
H1434: From גָּדַל (in the sense of twisting); thread, i.e. a tassel or festoon. In the KJV it is rendered: fringe, wreath.
H1435: From גָּדַל; stout; Giddel, the name of one of the Nethinim, also of one of "Solomon's servants". In the KJV it is rendered: Giddel.
H1436: Or (prolonged) Gdalyahuw; from גָּדַל and יָהּ; Jah has become great; Gedaljah, the name of five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Gedaliah.
H1437: From גָּדַל; I have made great; Giddalti, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Giddalti.
H1438: A primitive root; to fell a tree; generally, to destroy anything. In the KJV it is rendered: cut (asunder, in sunder, down, off), hew down.
H1439: From גָּדַע; feller (i.e. warrior); Gidon, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Gideon.
H1440: From גָּדַע; a cutting (i.e. desolation); Gidom, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gidom.
H1441: From גָּדַע; warlike (compare גִּדְעוֹן); Gidoni, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Gideoni.
H1442: A primitive root; to hack (with words), i.e. revile. In the KJV it is rendered: blaspheme, reproach.
H1443: A primitive root; to wall in or around. In the KJV it is rendered: close up, fence up, hedge, inclose, make up (a wall), mason, repairer.
H1444: From גָּדַר; a circumvallation. In the KJV it is rendered: wall.
H1445: : the same as גֶּ֫דֶר; Geder, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Geder.
H1446: Or (fully) Gdowr; from גָּדַר; inclosure; Gedor, a place in Palestine; also the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Gedor.
H1447: From גָּדַר; a circumvallation; by implication, an inclosure. In the KJV it is rendered: fence, hedge, wall.
H1448: Feminine of גָּדֵר; enclosure (especially for flocks). In the KJV it is rendered: (sheep-) cote (fold) hedge, wall.
H1449: The same as גְּדֵרָה; (with the article) Gederah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gederah, hedges.
H1450: Plural of גְּדֵרָה; walls; Gederoth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gederoth.
H1451: Patrial from גֶּ֫דֶר; a Gederite, or inhabitant of Geder. In the KJV it is rendered: Gederite.
H1452: Patrial from גְּדֵרָה; a Gederathite, or inhabitant of Gederah. In the KJV it is rendered: Gederathite.
H1453: Dual of גְּדֵרָה; double wall; Gederothajim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gederothaim.
H1454: Probably a clerical error for זֶה; this. In the KJV it is rendered: this.
H1455: A primitive root; to remove (a bandage from a wound, i.e. heal it). In the KJV it is rendered: cure.
H1456: From גָּהָה; a cure. In the KJV it is rendered: medicine.
H1457: A primitive root; to prostrate oneself. In the KJV it is rendered: cast self down, stretch self.
H1458: Another form for גֵּו; the back. In the KJV it is rendered: back.
H1459: (Aramaic) corresponding to גֵּו; the middle. In the KJV it is rendered: midst, same, there- (where-) in.
H1460: From גָּאָה (corresponding to גָּב); the back; by analogy, the middle. In the KJV it is rendered: + among, back, body.
H1461: A primitive root; to dig. In the KJV it is rendered: husbandman.
H1462: From גּוּב; the locust (from its grubbing as a larvae). In the KJV it is rendered: grasshopper, X great.
H1463: Of uncertain derivation; Gog, the name of an Israelite, also of some nothern nation. In the KJV it is rendered: Gog.
H1464: A primitive root (akin to גָּדַד); to crowd upon, i.e. attack. In the KJV it is rendered: invade, overcome.
H1465: Feminine of גֵּו; the back, i.e. (by extensive) the person. In the KJV it is rendered: body.
H1466: The same as גֵּוָה; exaltation; (figuratively) arrogance. In the KJV it is rendered: lifting up, pride.
H1467: (Aramaic) corresponding to גֵּוָה. In the KJV it is rendered: pride.
H1468: A primitive root (compare גָּזַז); properly, to shear off; but used only in the (figuratively) sense of passing rapidly. In the KJV it is rendered: bring, cut off.
H1469: Or (shortened) gozal; from גָּזַל; a nestling (as being comparatively nude of feathers). In the KJV it is rendered: young (pigeon).
H1470: Probably from גּוּז; a quarry (as a place of cutting stones); Gozan, a province of Assyria. In the KJV it is rendered: Gozan.
H1471: Rarely (shortened) goy; apparently from the same root as גֵּוָה (in the sense of massing); a foreign nation; hence, a Gentile; also (figuratively) a troop of animals, or a flight of locusts. In the KJV it is rendered: Gentile, heathen, nation, people.
H1472: Prolonged for גֵּוָה; a body, whether alive or dead. In the KJV it is rendered: (dead) body, carcase, corpse.
H1473: Or (shortened) golah; active participle feminine of גָּלָה; exile; concretely and collectively exiles. In the KJV it is rendered: (carried away), captive(-ity), removing.
H1474: From גּוֹלָה; captive; Golan, a place east of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Golan.
H1475: Of uncertain derivation; a pit. In the KJV it is rendered: pit.
H1476: Probably from גָּנַן; protected; Guni, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Guni.
H1477: Patronymically from גּוּנִי; a Gunite (collectively with article prefix) or descendants of Guni. In the KJV it is rendered: Gunites.
H1478: A primitive root; to breathe out, i.e. (by implication) expire. In the KJV it is rendered: die, be dead, give up the ghost, perish.
H1479: A primitive root; properly, to hollow or arch, i.e. (figuratively) close; to shut. In the KJV it is rendered: shut.
H1480: From גּוּף; a corpse (as closed to sense). In the KJV it is rendered: body.
H1481: A primitive root; properly, to turn aside from the road (for a lodging or any other purpose), i.e. sojourn (as a guest); also to shrink, fear (as in a strange place); also to gather for hostility (as afraid). In the KJV it is rendered: abide, assemble, be afraid, dwell, fear, gather (together), inhabitant, remain, sojourn, stand in awe, (be) stranger, X surely.
H1482: Or (shortened) gur; perhaps from גּוּר; a cub (as still abiding in the lair), especially of the lion. In the KJV it is rendered: whelp, young one.
H1483: The same as גּוּר; Gur, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gur.
H1484: Or (feminine) gorah; a variation of גּוּר. In the KJV it is rendered: whelp.
H1485: From גּוּר and בַּ֫עַל; dwelling of Baal; Gur- Baal, a place in Arabia. In the KJV it is rendered: Gur-baal.
H1486: Or (shortened) goral; from an unused root meaning to be rough (as stone); properly, a pebble, i.e. a lot (small stones being used for that purpose); figuratively, a portion or destiny (as if determined by lot). In the KJV it is rendered: lot.
H1487: Or rather (by permutation) giysh; of uncertain derivation; a mass of earth. In the KJV it is rendered: clod.
H1488: From גָּזַז; a fleece (as shorn); also mown grass. In the KJV it is rendered: fleece, mowing, mown grass.
H1489: Of foreign derivation; treasurer. In the KJV it is rendered: treasurer.
H1490: (Aramaic) corresponding to גִּזְבָּר. In the KJV it is rendered: treasurer.
H1491: A primitive root (akin to גּוּז); to cut off, i.e. portion out. In the KJV it is rendered: take.
H1492: Feminine from גָּזַז; a fleece. In the KJV it is rendered: fleece.
H1493: Patrial from the unused name of a place apparently in Palestine; a Gizonite or inhabitant of Gizoh. In the KJV it is rendered: Gizonite.
H1494: A primitive root (akin to גּוּז); to cut off; specifically to shear a flock or shave the hair; figuratively to destroy an enemy. In the KJV it is rendered: cut off (down), poll, shave, ((sheep-)) shear(-er).
H1495: From גָּזַז; shearer; Gazez, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Gazez.
H1496: From גָּזָה; something cut, i.e. dressed stone. In the KJV it is rendered: hewed, hewn stone, wrought.
H1497: A primitive root; to pluck off; specifically to flay, strip or rob. In the KJV it is rendered: catch, consume, exercise (robbery), pluck (off), rob, spoil, take away (by force, violence), tear.
H1498: From גָּזַל; robbery, or (concretely) plunder. In the KJV it is rendered: robbery, thing taken away by violence.
H1499: From גָּזַל; plunder, i.e. violence. In the KJV it is rendered: violence, violent perverting.
H1500: Feminine of גָּזֵל and mean the same: -that (he had robbed) (which he took violently away), spoil, violence.
H1501: From an unused root meaning to devour; a kind of locust. In the KJV it is rendered: palmer-worm.
H1502: From the same as גָּזָם; devourer. In the KJV it is rendered: Gazzam, one of the Nethinim:--Gazzam.
H1503: From an unused root meaning to cut down (trees); the trunk or stump of a tree (as felled or as planted). In the KJV it is rendered: stem, stock.
H1504: A primitive root; to cut down or off; (figuratively) to destroy, divide, exclude, or decide. In the KJV it is rendered: cut down (off), decree, divide, snatch.
H1505: (Aramaic) corresponding to גָּזַר; to quarry; determine. In the KJV it is rendered: cut out, soothsayer.
H1506: From גָּזַר; something cut off; a portion. In the KJV it is rendered: part, piece.
H1507: The same as גְּזָרִים; Gezer, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gazer, Gezer.
H1508: Feminine of גְּזָרִים; the figure or person (as if cut out); also an inclosure (as separated). In the KJV it is rendered: polishing, separate place.
H1509: From גָּזַר; a desert (as separated). In the KJV it is rendered: not inhabited.
H1510: (Aramaic) from גְּזַר (as גָּזַר); a decree. In the KJV it is rendered: decree.
H1511: (in the m patrial from גָּ֫זֶר; a Gezerite (collectively) or inhabitants of Gezer; but better (as in the text) by transposition Girziy; patrial of גְּרִזִים; a Grizite (collectively) or member of a native tribe in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gezrites.
H1512: Probably from גִּ֫יחַ; the external abdomen, belly (as the source of the faetus (compare גִּיחוֹן)). In the KJV it is rendered: belly.
H1513: Or (feminine) gacheleth; from an unused root meaning to glow or kindle; an ember. In the KJV it is rendered: (burning) coal.
H1514: From an unused root meaning to burn; flame; Gacham, a son of Nahor. In the KJV it is rendered: Gaham.
H1515: From an unused root meaning to hide; lurker; Gachar, one of the Nethinim. In the KJV it is rendered: Gahar.
H1516: Or (shortened) gay; probably (by transmutation) from the same root as גֵּוָה (abbreviated); a gorge (from its lofty sides; hence, narrow, but not a gully or winter-torrent). In the KJV it is rendered: valley.
H1517: Probably from גּוּד; a thong (as compressing); by analogy, a tendon. In the KJV it is rendered: sinew.
H1518: Or (shortened) goach; a primitive root; to gush forth (as water), generally to issue. In the KJV it is rendered: break forth, labor to bring forth, come forth, draw up, take out.
H1519: (Aramaic) or (shortened) guwach (Aramaic); corresponding to גִּ֫יחַ; to rush forth. In the KJV it is rendered: strive.
H1520: From גִּ֫יחַ; a fountain; Giach, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Giah.
H1521: Or (shortened) Gichown; from גִּ֫יחַ; stream; Gichon, a river of Paradise; also a valley (or pool) near Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: Gihon.
H1522: Or Gechaziy; apparently from גָּיְא and חָזָה; valley of a visionary; Gechazi, the servant of Elisha. In the KJV it is rendered: Gehazi.
H1523: Or (by permutation) guwl; a primitive root; properly, to spin round (under the influence of any violent emotion), i.e. usually rejoice, or (as cringing) fear. In the KJV it is rendered: be glad, joy, be joyful, rejoice.
H1524: From גִּיל; a revolution (of time, i.e. an age); also joy. In the KJV it is rendered: X exceedingly, gladness, X greatly, joy, rejoice(-ing), sort.
H1525: Or giylath; feminine of גִּיל; joy. In the KJV it is rendered: joy, rejoicing.
H1526: Patrial from גִּלֹה; a Gilonite or inhabitant of Giloh. In the KJV it is rendered: Gilonite.
H1527: Of uncertain derivation; Ginath, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ginath.
H1528: (Aramaic) corresponding to גִּר; lime. In the KJV it is rendered: plaster.
H1529: From the same as גִּישׁ; lumpish; Geshan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Geshan.
H1530: From גָּלַל; something rolled, i.e. a heap of stone or dung (plural ruins), by analogy, a spring of water (plural waves). In the KJV it is rendered: billow, heap, spring, wave.
H1531: From גָּלַל; a cup for oil (as round). In the KJV it is rendered: bowl.
H1532: From an unused root meaning to shave; a barber. In the KJV it is rendered: barber.
H1533: From גָּל and בָּעָה; fountain of ebullition; Gilboa, a mountain of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gilboa.
H1534: By reduplication from גָּלַל; a wheel; by analogy, a whirlwind; also dust (as whirled). In the KJV it is rendered: heaven, rolling thing, wheel.
H1535: (Aramaic) corresponding to גַּלְגַּל; a wheel. In the KJV it is rendered: wheel.
H1536: A variation of גַּלְגַּל. In the KJV it is rendered: wheel.
H1537: The same as גִּלְגַּל (with the article as a properly, noun); Gilgal, the name of three places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gilgal.
H1538: By reduplication from גָּלַל; a skull (as round); by implication, a head (in enumeration of persons). In the KJV it is rendered: head, every man, poll, skull.
H1539: From an unused root probably meaning to polish; the (human) skin (as smooth). In the KJV it is rendered: skin.
H1540: A primitive root; to denude (especially in a disgraceful sense); by implication, to exile (captives being usually stripped); figuratively, to reveal. In the KJV it is rendered: + advertise, appear, bewray, bring, (carry, lead, go) captive (into captivity), depart, disclose, discover, exile, be gone, open, X plainly, publish, remove, reveal, X shamelessly, shew, X surely, tell, uncover.
H1541: (Aramaic) or glat (Aramaic); corresponding to גָּלָה. In the KJV it is rendered: bring over, carry away, reveal.
H1542: Or (fully) Giyloh; from גָּלָה; open; Giloh, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Giloh.
H1543: Feminine from גָּלַל; a fountain, bowl or globe (all as round). In the KJV it is rendered: bowl, pommel, spring.
H1544: Or (shortened) gillul; from גָּלַל; properly, a log (as round); by implication, an idol. In the KJV it is rendered: idol.
H1545: From גָּלַם; clothing (as wrapped). In the KJV it is rendered: clothes.
H1546: Feminine from גָּלָה; captivity; concretely, exiles (collectively). In the KJV it is rendered: (they that are carried away) captives(-ity).
H1547: (Aramaic) corresponding to גָּלוּת. In the KJV it is rendered: captivity.
H1548: A primitive root; properly, to be bald, i.e. (causatively) to shave; figuratively to lay waste. In the KJV it is rendered: poll, shave (off).
H1549: Or gilyown; from גָּלָה; a tablet for writing (as bare); by analogy, a mirror (as a plate). In the KJV it is rendered: glass, roll.
H1550: From גָּלַל; a valve of a folding door (as turning); also a ring (as round). In the KJV it is rendered: folding, ring.
H1551: Or (prolonged) Galiylah; the same as גְּלִילִים; a circle (with the article); Galil (as a special circuit) in the North of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Galilee.
H1552: Feminine of גְּלִילִים; a circuit or region. In the KJV it is rendered: border, coast, country.
H1553: Plural of גְּלִילָה; circles; Geliloth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Geliloth.
H1554: Plural of גָּל; springs; Gallim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gallim.
H1555: Perhaps from גָּלָה; exile; Goljath, a Philistine. In the KJV it is rendered: Goliath.
H1556: A primitive root; to roll (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: commit, remove, roll (away, down, together), run down, seek occasion, trust, wallow.
H1557: From גָּלַל; dung (as in balls). In the KJV it is rendered: dung.
H1558: From גָּלַל; a circumstance (as rolled around); only used adverbially, on account of. In the KJV it is rendered: because of, for (sake).
H1559: From גָּלַל, in the sense of גְּלָל; great; Galal, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Galal.
H1560: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to גָּלַל; weight or size (as if rolled). In the KJV it is rendered: great.
H1561: A variation of גָּלָל; dung (plural balls of dung). In the KJV it is rendered: dung.
H1562: From גֵּ֫לֶל; dungy; Gilalai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Gilalai.
H1563: A primitive root; to fold. In the KJV it is rendered: wrap together.
H1564: From גָּלַם; a wrapped (and unformed mass, i.e. as the embryo). In the KJV it is rendered: substance yet being unperfect.
H1565: Probably by prolonged from גָּלַם; sterile (as wrapped up too hard); figuratively, desolate. In the KJV it is rendered: desolate, solitary.
H1566: A primitive root; to be obstinate. In the KJV it is rendered: (inter-)meddle (with).
H1567: From גָּל and עֵד; heap of testimony; Galed, a memorial cairn East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Galeed.
H1568: Probably from גַּלְעֵד; Gilad, a region East of the Jordan; also the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Gilead, Gileadite.
H1569: Patronymically from גִּלְעָד; a Giladite or descendant of Gilad. In the KJV it is rendered: Gileadite.
H1570: A primitive root; probably to caper (as a goat). In the KJV it is rendered: appear.
H1571: By contraction from an unused root meaning to gather; properly, assemblage; used only adverbially also, even, yea, though; often repeated as correl. both...and. In the KJV it is rendered: again, alike, also, (so much) as (soon), both (so).
H1572: A primitive root (literally or figuratively) to absorb. In the KJV it is rendered: swallow, drink.
H1573: From גָּמָא; properly, an absorbent, i.e. the bulrush (from its porosity); specifically the papyrus. In the KJV it is rendered: (bul-)rush.
H1574: From an unused root apparently meaning to grasp; properly, a span. In the KJV it is rendered: cubit.
H1575: From the same as גֹּ֫מֶד; a warrior (as grasping weapons). In the KJV it is rendered: Gammadims.
H1576: From גָּמַל; treatment, i.e. an act (of good or ill); by implication, service or requital. In the KJV it is rendered: + as hast served, benefit, desert, deserving, that which he hath given, recompense, reward.
H1577: Passive participle of גָּמַל; rewarded; Gamul, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Gamul.
H1578: Feminine of גְּמוּל; meaning the same. In the KJV it is rendered: deed, recompense, such a reward.
H1579: Of uncertain derivation; Gimzo, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gimzo.
H1580: A primitive root; to treat a person (well or ill), i.e. benefit or requite; by implication (of toil), to ripen, i.e. (specifically) to wean. In the KJV it is rendered: bestow on, deal bountifully, do (good), recompense, requite, reward, ripen, + serve, mean, yield.
H1581: Apparently from גָּמַל (in the sense of labor or burden-bearing); a camel. In the KJV it is rendered: camel.
H1582: Probably from גָּמָל; camel-driver; Gemalli, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Gemalli.
H1583: From גָּמַל and אֵל; reward of God; Gamliel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Gamaliel.
H1584: A primitive root; to end (in the sense of completion or failure). In the KJV it is rendered: cease, come to an end, fail, perfect, perform.
H1585: (Aramaic) corresponding to גָּמַר. In the KJV it is rendered: perfect.
H1586: From גָּמַר; completion; Gomer, the name of a son of Japheth and of his descendants; also of a Hebrewess. In the KJV it is rendered: Gomer.
H1587: Or Gmaryahuw; from גָּמַר and יָהּ; Jah has perfected; Gemarjah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Gemariah.
H1588: From גָּנַן; a garden (as fenced). In the KJV it is rendered: garden.
H1589: A primitive root; to thieve (literally or figuratively); by implication, to deceive. In the KJV it is rendered: carry away, X indeed, secretly bring, steal (away), get by stealth.
H1590: From גָּנַב; a stealer. In the KJV it is rendered: thief.
H1591: From גָּנַב; stealing, i.e. (concretely) something stolen. In the KJV it is rendered: theft.
H1592: From גָּנַב; theft; Genubath, an Edomitish prince. In the KJV it is rendered: Genubath.
H1593: Feminine of גָּן; a garden. In the KJV it is rendered: garden.
H1594: Another form for גַּנָּה. In the KJV it is rendered: garden.
H1595: From an unused root meaning to store; treasure; by implication, a coffer. In the KJV it is rendered: chest, treasury.
H1596: (Aramaic) corresponding to גִּנְזֵי; treasure. In the KJV it is rendered: treasure.
H1597: Prolonged from גִּנְזֵי; a treasury. In the KJV it is rendered: treasury.
H1598: A primitive root; to hedge about, i.e. (generally) protect. In the KJV it is rendered: defend.
H1599: Or Ginnthow; from גָּנַן; gardener; Ginnethon or Ginnetho, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ginnetho, Ginnethon.
H1600: A primitive root; to bellow (as cattle). In the KJV it is rendered: low.
H1601: Feminine active participle of גָּעָה; lowing; Goah, a place near Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: Goath.
H1602: A primitive root; to detest; by implication, to reject. In the KJV it is rendered: abhor, fail, lothe, vilely cast away.
H1603: From גָּעַל; loathing; Gaal, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Gaal.
H1604: From גָּעַל; abhorrence. In the KJV it is rendered: loathing.
H1605: A primitive root; to chide. In the KJV it is rendered: corrupt, rebuke, reprove.
H1606: From גָּעַר; a chiding. In the KJV it is rendered: rebuke(-ing), reproof.
H1607: A primitive root to agitate violently. In the KJV it is rendered: move, shake, toss, trouble.
H1608: From גָּעַשׁ; a quaking; Gaash, a hill in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gaash.
H1609: Of uncertain derivation; Gatam, an Edomite. In the KJV it is rendered: Gatam.
H1610: From an unused root meaning to arch; the back; by extensive the body or self. In the KJV it is rendered: + highest places, himself.
H1611: (Aramaic) corresponding to גַּף; a wing. In the KJV it is rendered: wing.
H1612: From an unused root meaning to bend; a vine (as twining), especially the grape. In the KJV it is rendered: vine, tree.
H1613: From an unused root, probably meaning to house in; a kind of tree or wood (as used for building), apparently the cypress. In the KJV it is rendered: gopher.
H1614: Probably feminine of גֹּ֫פֶר; properly, cypress- resin; by analogy, sulphur (as equally inflammable). In the KJV it is rendered: brimstone.
H1615: Perhaps from כּוּר; lime (from being burned in a kiln). In the KJV it is rendered: chalk(-stone).
H1616: Or (fully) geyr (gare); from גּוּר; properly, a guest; by implication, a foreigner. In the KJV it is rendered: alien, sojourner, stranger.
H1617: Perhaps from גֵּרָה; a grain; Gera, the name of six Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Gera.
H1618: From an unused root meaning to scratch; scurf (from itching). In the KJV it is rendered: scab, scurvy.
H1619: From the same as גָּרָב; scabby; Gareb, the name of an Israelite, also of a hill near Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: Gareb.
H1620: By reduplication from גָּרַר; a berry (as if a pellet of rumination). In the KJV it is rendered: berry.
H1621: Feminine plural from גָּרַר; the throat (as used in rumination). In the KJV it is rendered: neck.
H1622: Patrial from an unused name (of uncertain derivation); a Girgashite, one of the native tribes of Canaan. In the KJV it is rendered: Girgashite, Girgasite.
H1623: A primitive root; to abrade. In the KJV it is rendered: scrape.
H1624: A primitive root; properly, to grate, i.e. (figuratively) to anger. In the KJV it is rendered: contend, meddle, stir up, strive.
H1625: From גָּרַר; the cud (as scraping the throat). In the KJV it is rendered: cud.
H1626: From גָּרַר (as in גֵּרָה); properly, (like גַּרְגְּרִים) a kernel (round as if scraped), i.e. a gerah or small weight (and coin). In the KJV it is rendered: gerah.
H1627: Or (shortened) garon; from גָּרַר; the throat (compare גַּרְגְּרוֹת) (as roughened by swallowing). In the KJV it is rendered: X aloud, mouth, neck, throat.
H1628: From גּוּר; a (temporary) residence. In the KJV it is rendered: habitation.
H1629: A primitive root; to cut off. In the KJV it is rendered: cut off.
H1630: Plural of an unused noun from גָּרַז (compare גִּרְזִי), cut up (i.e. rocky); Gerizim, a mountain of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gerizim.
H1631: From גָּרַז; an axe. In the KJV it is rendered: ax.
H1632: From the same as גּוֹרָל; harsh. In the KJV it is rendered: man of great (as in the margin which reads gadowl).
H1633: A primitive root; to be spare or skeleton-like; used only as a denominative from גָּ֫רֶם; (causative) to bone, i.e. denude (by extensive, craunch) the bones. In the KJV it is rendered: gnaw the bones, break.
H1634: From גָּרַם; a bone (as the skeleton of the body); hence, self, i.e. (figuratively) very. In the KJV it is rendered: bone, strong, top.
H1635: (Aramaic) corresponding to גָּ֫רֶם; a bone. In the KJV it is rendered: bone.
H1636: From גָּ֫רֶם; bony, i.e. strong. In the KJV it is rendered: Garmite.
H1637: From an unused root meaning to smooth; a threshing- floor (as made even); by analogy, any open area. In the KJV it is rendered: (barn, corn, threshing-)floor, (threshing-, void) place.
H1638: A primitive root; to crush; also (intransitively and figuratively) to dissolve. In the KJV it is rendered: break.
H1639: A primitive root; to scrape off; by implication, to shave, remove, lessen, withhold. In the KJV it is rendered: abate, clip, (di-)minish, do (take) away, keep back, restrain, make small, withdraw.
H1640: A primitive root; to bear off violently. In the KJV it is rendered: sweep away.
H1641: A primitive root; to drag off roughly; by implication, to bring up the cud (i.e. ruminate); by analogy, to saw. In the KJV it is rendered: catch, chew, X continuing, destroy, saw.
H1642: Probably from גָּרַר; a rolling country; Gerar, a Philistine city. In the KJV it is rendered: Gerar.
H1643: From an unused root meaning to husk; a kernel (collectively), i.e. grain. In the KJV it is rendered: beaten corn.
H1644: A primitive root; to drive out from a possession; especially to expatriate or divorce. In the KJV it is rendered: cast up (out), divorced (woman), drive away (forth, out), expel, X surely put away, trouble, thrust out.
H1645: From גָּרַשׁ; produce (as if expelled). In the KJV it is rendered: put forth.
H1646: Feminine passive participle of גָּרַשׁ; (abstractly) dispossession. In the KJV it is rendered: exaction.
H1647: For גֵּרְשׁוֹן; Gereshom, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Gershom.
H1648: Or Gershowm; from גָּרַשׁ; a refugee; Gereshon or Gereshom, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Gershon, Gershom.
H1649: Patronymically from גֵּרְשׁוֹן; a Gereshonite or descendant of Gereshon. In the KJV it is rendered: Gershonite, sons of Gershon.
H1650: From an unused root (meaning to join); bridge; Geshur, a district of Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Geshur, Geshurite.
H1651: Patrial from גְּשׁוּר; a Geshurite (also collectively) or inhabitants of Geshur. In the KJV it is rendered: Geshuri, Geshurites.
H1652: A primitive root; to shower violently. In the KJV it is rendered: (cause to) rain.
H1653: From גָּשַׁם; a shower. In the KJV it is rendered: rain, shower.
H1654: Or (prolonged) Gashmuw; the same as גֶּ֫שֶׁם; Geshem or Gashmu, an Arabian. In the KJV it is rendered: Geshem, Gashmu.
H1655: (Aramaic) apparently the same as גֶּ֫שֶׁם; used in a peculiar sense, the body (probably for the (figuratively) idea of a hard rain). In the KJV it is rendered: body.
H1656: From גָּשַׁם; equivalent to גֶּ֫שֶׁם. In the KJV it is rendered: rained upon.
H1657: Probably of Egyptian origin; Goshen, the residence of the Israelites in Egypt; also a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Goshen.
H1658: Of uncertain derivation; Gishpa, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Gispa.
H1659: A primitive root; apparently to feel about. In the KJV it is rendered: grope.
H1660: Probably from נָגַן (in the sense of treading out grapes); a wine-press (or vat for holding the grapes in pressing them). In the KJV it is rendered: (wine-)press (fat).
H1661: The same as גַּת; Gath, a Philistine city. In the KJV it is rendered: Gath.
H1662: Or (abridged) Gittah-Chepher; from גַּת and חָפַר with the article inserted; wine- press of (the) well; Gath-Chepher, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gath-kephr, Gittah-kephr.
H1663: Patrial from גַּת; a Gittite or inhabitant of Gath. In the KJV it is rendered: Gittite.
H1664: Dual of גַּת; double wine-press; Gittajim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gittaim.
H1665: Feminine of גִּתִּי; a Gittite harp. In the KJV it is rendered: Gittith.
H1666: Of uncertain derivation; Gether, a son of Aram, and the region settled by him. In the KJV it is rendered: Gether.
H1667: From גַּת and רִמּוֹן; wine-press of (the) pomegranate; Gath-Rimmon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gath-rimmon.
H1668: (Aramaic) corresponding to זֶה; this. In the KJV it is rendered: one.
H1669: A primitive root; to pine. In the KJV it is rendered: mourn, sorrow(-ful).
H1670: From דָּאַב; properly, pining; by analogy, fear. In the KJV it is rendered: sorrow.
H1671: From דָּאַב; pining. In the KJV it is rendered: sorrow.
H1672: A primitive root; be anxious. In the KJV it is rendered: be afraid (careful, sorry), sorrow, take thought.
H1673: Or (fully) Dowoeg; active participle of דָּאַג; anxious; Doeg, an Edomite. In the KJV it is rendered: Doeg.
H1674: From דָּאַג; anxiety. In the KJV it is rendered: care(-fulness), fear, heaviness, sorrow.
H1675: A primitive root; to dart, i.e. fly rapidly. In the KJV it is rendered: fly.
H1676: From דָּאַו; the kite (from its rapid flight). In the KJV it is rendered: vulture.
H1677: Or (fully) dowb; from דָּבַב; the bear (as slow). In the KJV it is rendered: bear.
H1678: (Aramaic) corresponding to דֹּב. In the KJV it is rendered: bear.
H1679: From an unused root (compare דָּבַב) (probably meaning to be sluggish, i.e. restful); quiet. In the KJV it is rendered: strength.
H1680: A primitive root (compare דֹּ֫בֶא); to move slowly, i.e. glide. In the KJV it is rendered: cause to speak.
H1681: From דָּבַב (in the sense of furtive motion); slander. In the KJV it is rendered: defaming, evil report, infamy, slander.
H1682: Or (shortened) dborah; from דָּבַר (in the sense of orderly motion); the bee (from its systematic instincts). In the KJV it is rendered: bee.
H1683: Or (shortened) Dborah; the same as דְּבוֹרִים; Deborah, the name of two Hebrewesses. In the KJV it is rendered: Deborah.
H1684: (Aramaic) corresponding to זָבַח; to sacrifice (an animal). In the KJV it is rendered: offer (sacrifice).
H1685: (Aramaic) from דְּבַח; a sacrifice. In the KJV it is rendered: sacrifice.
H1686: In the margin for the textual reading, cheryown; both (in the plural only and) of uncertain derivation; probably some cheap vegetable, perhaps a bulbous root. In the KJV it is rendered: dove's dung.
H1687: Or (shortened) dbir; from דָּבַר (apparently in the sense of oracle); the shrine or innermost part of the sanctuary. In the KJV it is rendered: oracle.
H1688: Or (shortened) Dbir (Josh. 13:26 (but see לֹא דְּבַר)); the same as דְּבִיר; Debir, the name of an Amoritish king and of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Debir.
H1689: Probably an orthographical error for רִבְלָה; Diblah, a place in Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Diblath.
H1690: From an unused root (akin to זָבַל) probably meaning to press together; a cake of pressed figs. In the KJV it is rendered: cake (lump) of figs.
H1691: Dual from the masculine of דְּבֵלִים; two cakes; Diblajim, a symbolic name. In the KJV it is rendered: Diblaim.
H1692: A primitive root; properly, to impinge, i.e. cling or adhere; figuratively, to catch by pursuit. In the KJV it is rendered: abide fast, cleave (fast together), follow close (hard after), be joined (together), keep (fast), overtake, pursue hard, stick, take.
H1693: (Aramaic) corresponding to דָּבַק; to stick to. In the KJV it is rendered: cleave.
H1694: From דָּבַק; a joint; by implication, solder. In the KJV it is rendered: joint, solder.
H1695: From דָּבַק; adhering. In the KJV it is rendered: cleave, joining, stick closer.
H1696: A primitive root; perhaps properly, to arrange; but used figuratively (of words), to speak; rarely (in a destructive sense) to subdue. In the KJV it is rendered: answer, appoint, bid, command, commune, declare, destroy, give, name, promise, pronounce, rehearse, say, speak, be spokesman, subdue, talk, teach, tell, think, use (entreaties), utter, X well, X work.
H1697: From דָּבַר; a word; by implication, a matter (as spoken of) or thing; adverbially, a cause. In the KJV it is rendered: act, advice, affair, answer, X any such (thing), because of, book, business, care, case, cause, certain rate, + chronicles, commandment, X commune(-ication), + concern(-ing), + confer, counsel, + dearth, decree, deed, X disease, due, duty, effect, + eloquent, errand, (evil favoured-)ness, + glory, + harm, hurt, + iniquity, + judgment, language, + lying, manner, matter, message, (no) thing, oracle, X ought, X parts, + pertaining, + please, portion, + power, promise, provision, purpose, question, rate, reason, report, request, X (as hast) said, sake, saying, sentence, + sign, + so, some (uncleanness), somewhat to say, + song, speech, X spoken, talk, task, + that, X there done, thing (concerning), thought, + thus, tidings, what(-soever), + wherewith, which, word, work.
H1698: From דָּבַר (in the sense of destroying); a pestilence. In the KJV it is rendered: murrain, pestilence, plague.
H1699: From דָּבַר (in its original sense); a pasture (from its arrangement of the flock). In the KJV it is rendered: fold, manner.
H1700: Feminine of דָּבָר; a reason, suit or style. In the KJV it is rendered: cause, end, estate, order, regard.
H1701: (Aramaic) corresponding to דִּבְרַת. In the KJV it is rendered: intent, sake.
H1702: Feminine active participle of דָּבַר in the sense of driving (compare דֹּ֫בֶר); a raft. In the KJV it is rendered: float.
H1703: Intensive from דָּבַר; a word. In the KJV it is rendered: word.
H1704: From דָּבָר; wordy; Dibri, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Dibri.
H1705: From דָּבָר (perhaps in the sense of דֹּ֫בֶר); Daberath, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Dabareh, Daberath.
H1706: From an unused root meaning to be gummy; honey (from its stickiness); by analogy, syrup. In the KJV it is rendered: honey((-comb)).
H1707: Intensive from the same as דְּבָשׁ; a sticky mass, i.e. the hump of a camel. In the KJV it is rendered: hunch (of a camel).
H1708: The same as דַּבֶּ֫שֶׁת; Dabbesheth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Dabbesheth.
H1709: Or (fully) dag (Nehemiah 13:16); from דָּגָו; a fish (as prolific); or perhaps rather from דָּאַג (as timid); but still better from דָּאַג (in the sense of squirming, i.e. moving by the vibratory action of the tail); a fish (often used collectively). In the KJV it is rendered: fish.
H1710: Feminine of דָּאג, and meaning the same. In the KJV it is rendered: fish.
H1711: A primitive root; to move rapidly; used only as a denominative from דָּאג; to spawn, i.e. become numerous. In the KJV it is rendered: grow.
H1712: From דָּאג; the fish-god; Dagon, a Philistine deity. In the KJV it is rendered: Dagon.
H1713: A primitive root; to flaunt, i.e. raise a flag; figuratively, to be conspicuous. In the KJV it is rendered: (set up, with) banners, chiefest.
H1714: From דָּגַל; a flag. In the KJV it is rendered: banner, standard.
H1715: From דָּגָו; properly, increase, i.e. grain. In the KJV it is rendered: corn ((floor)), wheat.
H1716: A primitive root, to brood over eggs or young. In the KJV it is rendered: gather, sit.
H1717: Apparently from the same as דּוֹד; the breast (as the seat of love, or from its shape). In the KJV it is rendered: breast, teat.
H1718: A doubtful root; to walk gently. In the KJV it is rendered: go (softly, with).
H1719: Or (prolonged) Ddaneh (Ezek. 25:13); of uncertain derivation; Dedan, the name of two Cushites and of their territory. In the KJV it is rendered: Dedan.
H1720: Plural of דְּדָן (as patrial); Dedanites, the descendants or inhabitants of Dedan. In the KJV it is rendered: Dedanim.
H1721: Or (by orthographical error) Rodaniym (1 Chron. 1:7); a plural of uncertain derivation; Dodanites, or descendants of a son of Javan. In the KJV it is rendered: Dodanim.
H1722: (Aramaic) corresponding to זָהָב; gold. In the KJV it is rendered: gold(- en).
H1723: (Aramaic) of uncertain derivation; Dahava, a people colonized in Samaria. In the KJV it is rendered: Dehavites.
H1724: A primitive root (compare דּ֫וּחַ); to be dumb, i.e. (figuratively) dumbfounded. In the KJV it is rendered: astonished.
H1725: A primitive root; to curvet or move irregularly. In the KJV it is rendered: pause.
H1726: By reduplication from דָּהַר; a gallop. In the KJV it is rendered: pransing.
H1727: A primitive root; to mope, i.e. (figuratively) pine. In the KJV it is rendered: sorrow.
H1728: An orthographical variation of דָּאג as a denominative (דַּיָּגִים); a fisherman. In the KJV it is rendered: fisher.
H1729: Feminine from the same as דַּוָּגִים; properly, fishery, i.e. a hook for fishing. In the KJV it is rendered: fish (hook).
H1730: Or (shortened) dod; from an unused root meaning properly, to boil, i.e. (figuratively) to love; by implication, a love- token, lover, friend; specifically an uncle. In the KJV it is rendered: (well-)beloved, father's brother, love, uncle.
H1731: From the same as דּוֹד; a pot (for boiling); also (by resemblance of shape) a basket. In the KJV it is rendered: basket, caldron, kettle, (seething) pot.
H1732: Rarely (fully); Daviyd; from the same as דּוֹד; loving; David, the youngest son of Jesse. In the KJV it is rendered: David.
H1733: Feminine of דּוֹד; an aunt. In the KJV it is rendered: aunt, father's sister, uncle's wife.
H1734: From דּוֹד; loving; Dodo, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Dodo.
H1735: From דּוֹד and יָהּ; love of Jah; Dodavah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Dodavah.
H1736: From דּוּד; a boiler or basket; also the mandrake (as an aphrodisiac). In the KJV it is rendered: basket, mandrake.
H1737: Formed like דּוּדָאּים; amatory; Dodai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Dodai.
H1738: A primitive root; to be sick (as if in menstruation). In the KJV it is rendered: infirmity.
H1739: From דָּוָה; sick (especially in menstruation). In the KJV it is rendered: faint, menstruous cloth, she that is sick, having sickness.
H1740: A primitive root; to thrust away; figuratively, to cleanse. In the KJV it is rendered: cast out, purge, wash.
H1741: From דָּוֶה; sickness; figuratively, loathing. In the KJV it is rendered: languishing, sorrowful.
H1742: From דָּוֶה; sick; figuratively, troubled. In the KJV it is rendered: faint.
H1743: A primitive root; to bruise in a mortar. In the KJV it is rendered: beat.
H1744: Of uncertain derivation; the hoopoe or else the grouse. In the KJV it is rendered: lapwing.
H1745: From an unused root meaning to be dumb (compare דָּמָה); silence; figuratively, death. In the KJV it is rendered: silence.
H1746: The same as דּוּמָה; Dumah, a tribe and region of Arabia. In the KJV it is rendered: Dumah.
H1747: From דָּמָה; stillness; adverbially, silently; abstractly quiet, trust. In the KJV it is rendered: silence, silent, waiteth.
H1748: From דָּמַם; still; adverbially, silently. In the KJV it is rendered: dumb, silent, quietly wait.
H1750: A primitive root; to leap. In the KJV it is rendered: be turned.
H1751: (Aramaic) corresponding to דָּקַק; to crumble. In the KJV it is rendered: be broken to pieces.
H1752: A primitive root; properly, to gyrate (or move in a circle), i.e. to remain. In the KJV it is rendered: dwell.
H1753: (Aramaic) corresponding to דּוּר; to reside. In the KJV it is rendered: dwell.
H1754: From דּוּר; a circle, ball or pile. In the KJV it is rendered: ball, turn, round about.
H1755: Or (shortened) dor; from דּוּר; properly, a revolution of time, i.e. an age or generation; also a dwelling. In the KJV it is rendered: age, X evermore, generation, (n-)ever, posterity.
H1756: Or (by permutation) Dorr (Josh. 17:11; 1 Kings 4:11); from דּוֹר; dwelling; Dor, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Dor.
H1757: (Aramaic) probably from דּוּר; circle or dwelling; Dura, a place in Babylonia. In the KJV it is rendered: Dura.
H1758: Or dowsh; or diysh; a primitive root; to trample or thresh. In the KJV it is rendered: break, tear, thresh, tread out (down), at grass (Jer.
H1759: (Aramaic) corresponding to דּוּשׁ; to trample. In the KJV it is rendered: tread down.
H1760: Or dachach (Jer. 23:12); a primitive root; to push down. In the KJV it is rendered: chase, drive away (on), overthrow, outcast, X sore, thrust, totter.
H1761: (Aramaic) from the equivalent of דָּחָה; probably a musical instrument (as being struck). In the KJV it is rendered: instrument of music.
H1762: From דָּחָה; a push, i.e. (by implication) a fall. In the KJV it is rendered: falling.
H1763: (Aramaic) corresponding to זָחַל; to slink, i.e. (by implication) to fear, or (causatively) be formidable. In the KJV it is rendered: make afraid, dreadful, fear, terrible.
H1764: Of uncertain derivation; millet. In the KJV it is rendered: millet.
H1765: A primitive root; to urge, i.e. hasten. In the KJV it is rendered: (be) haste(-ned), pressed on.
H1766: A primitive root; to press, i.e. oppress. In the KJV it is rendered: thrust, vex.
H1767: Of uncertain derivation; enough (as noun or adverb), used chiefly with preposition in phrases. In the KJV it is rendered: able, according to, after (ability), among, as (oft as), (more than) enough, from, in, since, (much as is) sufficient(-ly), too much, very, when.
H1768: (Aramaic) apparently for דָּא; that, used as relative conjunction, and especially (with a preposition) in adverbial phrases; also as preposition of. In the KJV it is rendered: X as, but, for(-asmuch +), + now, of, seeing, than, that, therefore, until, + what (-soever), when, which, whom, whose.
H1769: Or (shortened) Diybon; from דִּיב; pining. In the KJV it is rendered: Dibon, the name of three places in Palestine:--Dibon.
H1770: Denominative from דָּאג; to fish. In the KJV it is rendered: fish.
H1771: From דִּיג; a fisherman. In the KJV it is rendered: fisher.
H1772: Intensive from דָּאַו; a falcon (from its rapid flight). In the KJV it is rendered: vulture.
H1773: Of uncertain derivation; ink. In the KJV it is rendered: ink.
H1774: As if from דִּי and זָהָב; of gold; Dizahab, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Dizahab.
H1775: Perhaps for דִּיבוֹן; Dimon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Dimon.
H1776: Feminine of דִּימוֹן; Dimonah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Dimonah.
H1777: Or (Gen. 6:3) duwn; a primitive roy a straight course, i.e. sail direct. In the KJV it is rendered: (come) with a straight course.
H1778: (Aramaic) corresp. to דִּין; to judge. In the KJV it is rendered: judge.
H1779: From דִּין; judgement (the suit, justice, sentence or tribunal); by impl. also strife. In the KJV it is rendered: cause, judgement, plea, strife.
H1780: (Aramaic) corresp. to דִּין. In the KJV it is rendered: judgement.
H1781: From דִּין; a judge or advocate. In the KJV it is rendered: judge.
H1782: (Aramaic) corresp. to דַּיָּן. In the KJV it is rendered: judge.
H1783: Fem. of דִּין; justice; Dinah, the daughter of Jacob. In the KJV it is rendered: Dinah.
H1784: (Aramaic) partial from uncertain primitive; a Dinaite or inhabitant of some unknown Assyria province. In the KJV it is rendered: Dinaite.
H1785: From a root corresp. to דּוּק; a battering-tower. In the KJV it is rendered: fort.
H1786: From דּוּשׁ; threshing-time. In the KJV it is rendered: threshing.
H1787: (Diyshon, the same as דִּישֹׁן; Dishon, the name of two Edomites. In the KJV it is rendered: Dishon.
H1788: From דּוּשׁ; the leaper, i.e. an antelope. In the KJV it is rendered: pygarg.
H1789: Another form of דִּישׁוֹן Dishan, an Edomite. In the KJV it is rendered: Dishon.
H1790: From an unused root (compare דָּכָה); crushed, i.e. (fig.) injured. In the KJV it is rendered: afflicted, oppressed.
H1791: (Aramaic) or dak (Aramaic); prolonged from דָּא; this. In the KJV it is rendered: the same, this.
H1792: A primitive root (compare דָּכָה); to crumble; transitively, to bruise (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: beat to pieces, break (in pieces), bruise, contrite, crush, destroy, humble, oppress, smite.
H1793: From דָּכָא; crushed (literally powder, or figuratively, contrite). In the KJV it is rendered: contrite, destruction.
H1794: A primitive root (compare דָּך, דָּכָא); to collapse (phys. or mentally). In the KJV it is rendered: break (sore), contrite, crouch.
H1795: From דָּכָה like דַּכָּא; mutilated. In the KJV it is rendered: + wounded.
H1796: From דָּכָה; a dashing of surf. In the KJV it is rendered: wave.
H1797: (Aramaic) prolonged from דֵּך; this. In the KJV it is rendered: same, that, this.
H1798: (Aramaic) corresponding to זָכָר; properly, a male, i.e. of sheep. In the KJV it is rendered: ram.
H1799: (Aramaic) or dokran (Aramaic); corresponding to זִכָּרוֹן; a register. In the KJV it is rendered: record.
H1800: From דָּלַל; properly, dangling, i.e. (by implication) weak or thin. In the KJV it is rendered: lean, needy, poor (man), weaker.
H1801: A primitive root; to spring. In the KJV it is rendered: leap.
H1802: A primitive root (compare דָּלַל); properly, to dangle, i.e. to let down a bucket (for drawing out water); figuratively, to deliver. In the KJV it is rendered: draw (out), X enough, lift up.
H1803: From דָּלָה; properly, something dangling, i.e. a loose thread or hair; figuratively, indigent. In the KJV it is rendered: hair, pining sickness, poor(-est sort).
H1804: A primitive root; to roil water. In the KJV it is rendered: trouble.
H1805: Or doliy; from דָּלָה; a pail or jar (for drawing water). In the KJV it is rendered: bucket.
H1806: Or (prolonged) Dlayahhuw; from דָּלָה and יָהּ; Jah has delivered; Delajah, the name of five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Dalaiah, Delaiah.
H1807: From דָּלַל; languishing. In the KJV it is rendered: Delilah, a Philistine woman:--Delilah.
H1808: From דָּלָה; something dangling, i.e. a bough. In the KJV it is rendered: branch.
H1809: A primitive root (compare דָּלָה); to slacken or be feeble; figuratively, to be oppressed. In the KJV it is rendered: bring low, dry up, be emptied, be not equal, fail, be impoverished, be made thin.
H1810: Of uncertain derivation; Dilan, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Dilean.
H1811: A primitive root; to drip; by implication, to weep. In the KJV it is rendered: drop through, melt, pour out.
H1812: From דָּלַף; a dripping. In the KJV it is rendered: dropping.
H1813: From דָּלַף; dripping; Dalphon, a son of Haman. In the KJV it is rendered: Dalphon.
H1814: A primitive root; to flame (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: burning, chase, inflame, kindle, persecute(-or), pursue hotly.
H1815: (Aramaic) corresponding to דָּלַק. In the KJV it is rendered: burn.
H1816: : from דָּלַק; a burning fever. In the KJV it is rendered: inflammation.
H1817: From דָּלָה; something swinging, i.e. the valve of a door. In the KJV it is rendered: door (two-leaved), gate, leaf, lid.
