H1819: A primitive root; to compare; by implication, to resemble, liken, consider. In the KJV it is rendered: compare, devise, (be) like(-n), mean, think, use similitudes.
H1820: A primitive root; to be dumb or silent; hence, to fail or perish; trans. to destroy. In the KJV it is rendered: cease, be cut down (off), destroy, be brought to silence, be undone, X utterly.
H1821: (Aramaic) corresponding to דָּמָה; to resemble. In the KJV it is rendered: be like.
H1822: From דָּמָה; desolation; concretely, desolate. In the KJV it is rendered: destroy.
H1823: From דָּמָה; resemblance; concretely, model, shape; adverbially, like. In the KJV it is rendered: fashion, like (-ness, as), manner, similitude.
H1824: Or domiy; from דָּמָה; quiet. In the KJV it is rendered: cutting off, rest, silence.
H1825: From דָּמָה; resemblance. In the KJV it is rendered: X like.
H1826: A prim root (compare דָּהַם, דָּמָה); to be dumb; by implication, to be astonished, to stop; also to perish. In the KJV it is rendered: cease, be cut down (off), forbear, hold peace, quiet self, rest, be silent, keep (put to) silence, be (stand) still, tarry, wait.
H1827: Feminine from דָּמַם; quiet. In the KJV it is rendered: calm, silence, still.
H1828: Of uncertain derivation; manure. In the KJV it is rendered: dung.
H1829: Feminine from the same as דֹּ֫מֶן; a dung-heap; Dimnah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Dimnah.
H1830: A primitive root; to weep. In the KJV it is rendered: X sore, weep.
H1831: From דָּמַע; a tear; figuratively, juice. In the KJV it is rendered: liquor.
H1832: Feminine of דֶּ֫מַע; weeping. In the KJV it is rendered: tears.
H1833: By orthographical variation from NONE; damask (as a fabric of Damascus). In the KJV it is rendered: in Damascus.
H1834: Or Duwmeseq; or Darmeseq; of foreign origin; Damascus, a city of Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Damascus.
H1835: From דִּין; judge; Dan, one of the sons of Jacob; also the tribe descended from him, and its territory; likewise a place in Palestine colonized by them. In the KJV it is rendered: Dan.
H1836: (Aramaic) an orthographical variation of דֵּך; this. In the KJV it is rendered: (afore-)time, + after this manner, here (-after), one.
H1837: Of uncertain derivation; Dannah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Dannah.
H1838: Of uncertain derivation; Dinhabah, an Edomitish town. In the KJV it is rendered: Dinhaban.
H1839: Patronymically from דָּן; a Danite (often collectively) or descendants (or inhabitants) of Dan. In the KJV it is rendered: Danites, of Dan.
H1840: In Ezekiel it is: Daniel; from דָּן and אֵל; judge of God; Daniel or Danijel, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Daniel.
H1841: (Aramaic) corresponding to דָּנִיֵּאל; Danijel, the Heb. prophet. In the KJV it is rendered: Daniel.
H1842: From דָּן and (apparently) יַ֫עַן; judge of purpose; Dan-Jaan, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Dan-jaan.
H1843: From יָדַע; knowledge. In the KJV it is rendered: knowledge, opinion.
H1844: Feminine of דֵּעִי; knowledge. In the KJV it is rendered: knowledge.
H1845: From יָדַע and אֵל; known of God; Deuel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Deuel.
H1846: A primitive root; to be extinguished; figuratively, to expire or be dried up. In the KJV it is rendered: be extinct, consumed, put out, quenched.
H1847: From יָדַע; knowledge. In the KJV it is rendered: cunning, (ig-)norantly, know(-ledge), (un-)awares (wittingly).
H1848: From an unused root (meaning to push over); a stumbling-block. In the KJV it is rendered: slanderest.
H1849: A primitive root; to knock; by analogy, to press severely. In the KJV it is rendered: beat, knock, overdrive.
H1850: From דָּפַק; a knock; Dophkah, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Dophkah.
H1851: From דָּקַק; crushed, i.e. (by implication) small or thin. In the KJV it is rendered: dwarf, lean(-fleshed), very little thing, small, thin.
H1852: From דָּקַק; something crumbling, i.e. fine (as a thin cloth). In the KJV it is rendered: curtain.
H1853: Of foreign origin; Diklah, a region of Arabia. In the KJV it is rendered: Diklah.
H1854: A primitive root (compare הָדַך); to crush (or intransitively) crumble. In the KJV it is rendered: beat in pieces (small), bruise, make dust, (into) X powder, (be, very) small, stamp (small).
H1855: (Aramaic) corresponding to דָּקַק; to crumble or (trans.) crush. In the KJV it is rendered: break to pieces.
H1856: A primitive root; to stab; by analogy, to starve; figuratively, to revile. In the KJV it is rendered: pierce, strike (thrust) through, wound.
H1857: From דָּקַר; a stab; Deker, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Dekar.
H1858: Apparently from the same as דְּרוֹר; properly, a pearl (from its sheen as rapidly turned); by analogy, pearl-stone, i.e. mother-of-pearl or alabaster. In the KJV it is rendered: X white.
H1859: (Aramaic) corresponding to דּוֹר; an age. In the KJV it is rendered: generation.
H1860: Or dera)own; from an unused root (meaning to repulse); an object of aversion. In the KJV it is rendered: abhorring, contempt.
H1861: (also dor-bawn'); of uncertain derivation; a goad. In the KJV it is rendered: goad.
H1862: Apparently from דַּר and דֵּעִי; pearl of knowledge; Darda, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Darda.
H1863: Of uncertain derivation; a thorn. In the KJV it is rendered: thistle.
H1864: Of uncertain derivation; the south; poet. the south wind. In the KJV it is rendered: south.
H1865: From an unused root (meaning to move rapidly); freedom; hence, spontaneity of outflow, and so clear. In the KJV it is rendered: liberty, pure.
H1866: The same as דְּרוֹר, applied to a bird; the swift, a kind of swallow. In the KJV it is rendered: swallow.
H1867: Of Persian origin; Darejavesh, a title (rather than name) of several Persian kings. In the KJV it is rendered: Darius.
H1868: (Aramaic) corresponding to NONE. In the KJV it is rendered: Darius.
H1869: A primitive root; to tread; by implication, to walk; also to string a bow (by treading on it in bending). In the KJV it is rendered: archer, bend, come, draw, go (over), guide, lead (forth), thresh, tread (down), walk.
H1870: From דָּרַך; a road (as trodden); figuratively, a course of life or mode of action, often adverb. In the KJV it is rendered: along, away, because of, + by, conversation, custom, (east-)ward, journey, manner, passenger, through, toward, (high-) (path-)way(-side), whither(-soever).
H1871: Of Pers. origin; a "drachma," or coin. In the KJV it is rendered: dram.
H1872: (Aramaic) corresponding to זְר֫וֹעַ; an arm. In the KJV it is rendered: arm.
H1873: Probably a contraction from דַּרְדַּע; Dara, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Dara.
H1874: Of uncertain derivation; Darkon, one of "Solomon's servants". In the KJV it is rendered: Darkon.
H1875: A primitive root; properly, to tread or frequent; usually to follow (for pursuit or search); by implication, to seek or ask; specifically to worship. In the KJV it is rendered: ask, X at all, care for, X diligently, inquire, make inquisition, (necro-)mancer, question, require, search, seek (for, out), X surely.
H1876: A primitive root; to sprout. In the KJV it is rendered: bring forth, spring.
H1877: From דָּשָׁא; a sprout; by analogy, grass. In the KJV it is rendered: (tender) grass, green, (tender)herb.
H1878: A primitive root; to be fat; transitively, to fatten (or regard as fat); specifically to anoint; figuratively, to satisfy; denominatively (from דָּ֫שֶׁן) to remove (fat) ashes (of sacrifices). In the KJV it is rendered: accept, anoint, take away the (receive) ashes (from), make (wax) fat.
H1879: From דָּשֵׁן; fat; figuratively, rich, fertile. In the KJV it is rendered: fat.
H1880: From דָּשֵׁן; the fat; abstractly fatness, i.e. (figuratively) abundance; specifically the (fatty) ashes of sacrifices. In the KJV it is rendered: ashes, fatness.
H1881: Of uncertain (perhaps foreign) derivation: a royal edict or statute. In the KJV it is rendered: commandment, commission, decree, law, manner.
H1883: (Aramaic) corresponding to דֶּ֫שֶׁא. In the KJV it is rendered: tender grass.
H1884: (Aramaic) of Pers. origin; meaning one skilled in law; a judge. In the KJV it is rendered: counsellor.
H1885: Of uncertain derivation; Dathan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Dathan.
H1886: Or (Aramaic dual) Dothayin (Gen. 37:17); of uncertain derivation; Dothan, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Dothan.
H1887: A primitive particle; lo!. In the KJV it is rendered: behold, lo.
H1888: (Aramaic) or har (Aramaic); corresponding to הֵא. In the KJV it is rendered: even, lo.
H1889: From הֵא and אָח; aha!. In the KJV it is rendered: ah, aha, ha.
H1890: By reduplication from יָהַב; gift (in sacrifice), i.e. holocaust. In the KJV it is rendered: offering.
H1891: A primitive root; to be vain in act, word, or expectation; specifically to lead astray. In the KJV it is rendered: be (become, make) vain.
H1892: Or (rarely in the abs.) habel; from הָבַל; emptiness or vanity; figuratively, something transitory and unsatisfactory; often used as an adverb. In the KJV it is rendered: X altogether, vain, vanity.
H1893: The same as הָ֫בֶל; Hebel, the son of Adam. In the KJV it is rendered: Abel.
H1894: Only in plural, from an unused root meaning to be hard; ebony. In the KJV it is rendered: ebony.
H1895: A primitive root of uncertain (perhaps foreign) derivation; to be a horoscopist. In the KJV it is rendered: + (astro-)loger.
H1896: Or (by permutation) Hegay; probably of Persian origin; Hege or Hegai, a eunuch of Xerxes. In the KJV it is rendered: Hegai, Hege.
H1897: A primitive root (compare הֲגִיג); to murmur (in pleasure or anger); by implication, to ponder. In the KJV it is rendered: imagine, meditate, mourn, mutter, roar, X sore, speak, study, talk, utter.
H1898: A primitive root; to remove. In the KJV it is rendered: stay, stay away.
H1899: From הָגָה; a muttering (in sighing, thought, or as thunder). In the KJV it is rendered: mourning, sound, tale.
H1900: From הָגָה; musing. In the KJV it is rendered: meditation.
H1901: From an unused root akin to הָגָה; properly, a murmur, i.e. complaint. In the KJV it is rendered: meditation, musing.
H1902: Intensive from הָגָה; a murmuring sound, i.e. a musical notation (probably similar to the modern affettuoso to indicate solemnity of movement); by implication, a machination. In the KJV it is rendered: device, Higgaion, meditation, solemn sound.
H1903: Of uncertain derivation; perhaps suitable or turning. In the KJV it is rendered: directly.
H1904: Of uncertain (perhaps foreign) derivation; Hagar, the mother of Ishmael. In the KJV it is rendered: Hagar.
H1905: Or (prolonged) Hagris; perhaps patronymically from הָגָר; a Hagrite or member of a certain Arabian clan. In the KJV it is rendered: Hagarene, Hagarite, Haggeri.
H1906: For הֵידָד; a shout. In the KJV it is rendered: sounding again.
H1907: (Aramaic) probably of foreign origin; a vizier. In the KJV it is rendered: counsellor.
H1908: Probably of foreign origin (compare אֲדַד); Hadad, the name of an idol, and of several kings of Edom. In the KJV it is rendered: Hadad.
H1909: From הֲדָד and עֵ֫זֶר; Hadad (is his) help; Hadadezer, a Syrian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Hadadezer.
H1910: From הֲדָד and רִמּוֹן; Hadad-Rimmon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hadad-rimmon.
H1911: A primitive root (compare יָדָה); to stretch forth the hand. In the KJV it is rendered: put.
H1912: Of foreign origin; Hodu (i.e. Hindu-stan). In the KJV it is rendered: India.
H1913: Or Hadoram; probably of foreign derivation; Hadoram, a son of Joktan, and the tribe descended from him. In the KJV it is rendered: Hadoram.
H1914: Of uncertain derivation; Hiddai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hiddai.
H1915: A primitive root (compare דָּקַק); to crush with the foot. In the KJV it is rendered: tread down.
H1916: From an unused root meaning to stamp upon; a foot stool. In the KJV it is rendered: (foot-)stool.
H1917: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of הֲדֹם; something stamped to pieces, i.e. a bit. In the KJV it is rendered: piece.
H1918: Of uncertain derivation; the myrtle. In the KJV it is rendered: myrtle (tree).
H1919: Feminine of הֲדַס; Hadassah (or Esther). In the KJV it is rendered: Hadassah.
H1920: A prim root; to push away or down. In the KJV it is rendered: cast away (out), drive, expel, thrust (away).
H1921: A primitive root; to swell up (literally or figuratively, active or passive); by implication, to favor or honour, be high or proud. In the KJV it is rendered: countenance, crooked place, glorious, honour, put forth.
H1922: (Aramaic) corresponding to הָדַר; to magnify (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: glorify, honour.
H1923: (Aramaic) from הֲדַר; magnificence. In the KJV it is rendered: honour, majesty.
H1924: The same as הָדָר; Hadar, an Edomite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hadar.
H1925: From הָדַר; honour; used (figuratively) for the capital city (Jerusalem). In the KJV it is rendered: glory.
H1926: From הָדַר; magnificence, i.e. ornament or splendor. In the KJV it is rendered: beauty, comeliness, excellency, glorious, glory, goodly, honour, majesty.
H1927: Feminine of הָדָר; decoration. In the KJV it is rendered: beauty, honour.
H1928: From הֲדַר and עֵ֫זֶר; Hadar (i.e. Hadad, הֲדָד) is his help; Hadarezer (i.e. Hadadezer, הֲדַדְעָ֫זֶר), a Syrian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Hadarezer.
H1929: A shortened form of אֲהָהּ; ah! expressing grief. In the KJV it is rendered: woe worth.
H1930: By permutation from הָהּ; oh!. In the KJV it is rendered: alas.
H1931: Of which the feminine (beyond the Pentateuch) is hiyw; a primitive word, the third person pronoun singular, he (she or it); only expressed when emphatic or without a verb; also (intensively) self, or (especially with the article) the same; sometimes (as demonstrative) this or that; occasionally (instead of copula) as or are. In the KJV it is rendered: he, as for her, him(-self), it, the same, she (herself), such, that (.
H1932: (Aramaic) or (feminine) hiyo (Aramaic); corresponding to הוּא. In the KJV it is rendered: X are, it, this.
H1933: Or havah; a primitive root (compare אָוָה, הָיָה) supposed to mean properly, to breathe; to be (in the sense of existence). In the KJV it is rendered: be, X have.
H1934: (Aramaic) or havah (Aramaic); corresponding to הָוָה; to exist; used in a great variety of applications (especially in connection with other words). In the KJV it is rendered: be, become, + behold, + came (to pass), + cease, + cleave, + consider, + do, + give, + have, + judge, + keep, + labour, + mingle (self), + put, + see, + seek, + set, + slay, + take heed, tremble, + walk, + would.
H1935: From an unused root; grandeur (i.e. an imposing form and appearance). In the KJV it is rendered: beauty, comeliness, excellency, glorious, glory, goodly, honour, majesty.
H1936: The same as הוֹד; Hod, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hod.
H1937: A form of הוֹדַוְיָה; Hodevah (or Hodevjah), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hodevah.
H1938: From הוֹד and יָהּ; majesty of Jah; Hodavjah, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hodaviah.
H1939: A form of הוֹדַוְיָה; Hodajvah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hodaiah.
H1940: A form for the feminine of יְהוּדִי; a Jewess. In the KJV it is rendered: Hodiah.
H1941: A form of הוֹדַוְיָה; Hodijah, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hodijah.
H1942: From הָוָה (in the sense of eagerly coveting and rushing upon; by implication, of falling); desire; also ruin. In the KJV it is rendered: calamity, iniquity, mischief, mischievous (thing), naughtiness, naughty, noisome, perverse thing, substance, very wickedness.
H1943: Another form for הַוַּת; ruin. In the KJV it is rendered: mischief.
H1944: Of uncertain derivation; Hoham, a Canaanitish king. In the KJV it is rendered: Hoham.
H1945: A prolonged form of הוֹ (akin to אוֹי); oh!. In the KJV it is rendered: ah, alas, ho, O, woe.
H1946: (Aramaic) corresponding to הֲלַך; to go; causatively, to bring. In the KJV it is rendered: bring again, come, go (up).
H1947: Feminine active participle of הָלַל; folly. In the KJV it is rendered: madness.
H1948: From active participle of הָלַל; folly. In the KJV it is rendered: madness.
H1949: A primitive root (compare הָמַם); to make an uproar, or agitate greatly. In the KJV it is rendered: destroy, move, make a noise, put, ring again.
H1950: From הָמַם; raging; Homam, an Edomitish chieftain. In the KJV it is rendered: Homam.
H1951: A primitive root; properly, to be naught, i.e. (figuratively) to be (causatively, act) light. In the KJV it is rendered: be ready.
H1952: From the same as הוּן in the sense of אוֹן; wealth; by implication, enough. In the KJV it is rendered: enough, + for nought, riches, substance, wealth.
H1953: From יְהֹוָה and שָׁמַע; Jehovah has heard; Hoshama, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hoshama.
H1954: From יָשַׁע; deliverer; Hoshea, the name of five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hosea, Hoshea, Oshea.
H1955: From יָשַׁע and יָהּ; Jah has saved; Hoshajah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hoshaiah.
H1956: From יָתַר; he has caused to remain; Hothir, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hothir.
H1957: A primitive root (compare חָזָה); to dream. In the KJV it is rendered: sleep.
H1958: For נֶ֫הִי; lamentation. In the KJV it is rendered: woe.
H1959: From an unused root (meaning to shout); acclamation. In the KJV it is rendered: shout(-ing).
H1960: From the same as הֵידָד; properly, an acclaim, i.e. a choir of singers. In the KJV it is rendered: thanksgiving.
H1961: A primitive root (compare הָוָה); to exist, i.e. be or become, come to pass (always emphatic, and not a mere copula or auxiliary). In the KJV it is rendered: beacon, X altogether, be(-come), accomplished, committed, like), break, cause, come (to pass), do, faint, fall, + follow, happen, X have, last, pertain, quit (one-)self, require, X use.
H1962: Another form for הֹוָה; ruin. In the KJV it is rendered: calamity.
H1963: Another form for NONE; how?. In the KJV it is rendered: how.
H1964: Probably from יָכֹל (in the sense of capacity); a large public building, such as a palace or temple. In the KJV it is rendered: palace, temple.
H1965: (Aramaic) corresponding to הֵיכָל. In the KJV it is rendered: palace, temple.
H1966: From הָלַל (in the sense of brightness); the morning-star. In the KJV it is rendered: lucifer.
H1967: Another form for הוֹמָם; Hemam, an Idumaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Hemam.
H1968: Probably from אָמַן; faithful; Heman, the name of at least two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Heman.
H1969: Probably of Egyptian origin; a hin or liquid measure. In the KJV it is rendered: hin.
H1970: A primitive root; apparently to injure. In the KJV it is rendered: make self strange.
H1971: From נָכַר; respect, i.e. partiality. In the KJV it is rendered: shew.
H1972: Probably denominatively from הָלְאָה; to remove or be remote. In the KJV it is rendered: cast far off.
H1973: From the primitive form of the article (hal); to the distance, i.e. far away; also (of time) thus far. In the KJV it is rendered: back, beyond, (hence,-)forward, hitherto, thence,forth, yonder.
H1974: From הָלַל (in the sense of rejoicing); a celebration of thanksgiving for harvest. In the KJV it is rendered: merry, praise.
H1975: From הַלָּזֶה; this or that. In the KJV it is rendered: side, that, this.
H1976: From the article (see הָלְאָה) and זֶה; this very. In the KJV it is rendered: this.
H1977: Another form of הַלָּזֶה; that. In the KJV it is rendered: this.
H1978: From הָלַך; a walk, i.e. (by implication) a step. In the KJV it is rendered: step.
H1979: Feminine of הֲלִיכִים; a walking; by implication, a procession or march, a caravan. In the KJV it is rendered: company, going, walk, way.
H1980: Akin to יָלַך; a primitive root; to walk (in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: (all) along, apace, behave (self), come, (on) continually, be conversant, depart, + be eased, enter, exercise (self), + follow, forth, forward, get, go (about, abroad, along, away, forward, on, out, up and down), + greater, grow, be wont to haunt, lead, march, X more and more, move (self), needs, on, pass (away), be at the point, quite, run (along), + send, speedily, spread, still, surely, + tale-bearer, + travel(-ler), walk (abroad, on, to and fro, up and down, to places), wander, wax, (way-)faring man, X be weak, whirl.
H1981: (Aramaic) corresponding to הָלַך (compare הוּך); to walk. In the KJV it is rendered: walk.
H1982: From הָלַך; properly, a journey, i.e. (by implication) a wayfarer; also a flowing. In the KJV it is rendered: X dropped, traveller.
H1983: (Aramaic) from הֲלַך; properly, a journey, i.e. (by implication) toll on goods at a road. In the KJV it is rendered: custom.
H1984: A primitive root; to be clear (orig. of sound, but usually of color); to shine; hence, to make a show, to boast; and thus to be (clamorously) foolish; to rave; causatively, to celebrate; also to stultify. In the KJV it is rendered: (make) boast (self), celebrate, commend, (deal, make), fool(- ish, -ly), glory, give (light), be (make, feign self) mad (against), give in marriage, (sing, be worthy of) praise, rage, renowned, shine.
H1985: From הָלַל; praising (namely God); Hillel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hillel.
H1986: A primitive root; to strike down; by implication, to hammer, stamp, conquer, disband. In the KJV it is rendered: beat (down), break (down), overcome, smite (with the hammer).
H1987: From הָלַם; smiter; Helem, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Helem.
H1988: From the article (see הָלְאָה); hither. In the KJV it is rendered: here, hither(-(to)), thither.
H1989: From הָלַם; a hammer (or mallet). In the KJV it is rendered: hammer.
H1990: Of uncertain derivation; Ham, a region of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ham.
H1991: From הָמָה; abundance, i.e. wealth. In the KJV it is rendered: any of theirs.
H1992: Or (prolonged) hemmah; masculine plural from הֲלַך; they (only used when emphatic). In the KJV it is rendered: it, like, X (how, so) many (soever, more as) they (be), (the) same, X so, X such, their, them, these, they, those, which, who, whom, withal, ye.
H1993: A primitive root (compare הוּם); to make a loud sound like Engl. "hum"); by implication, to be in great commotion or tumult, to rage, war, moan, clamor. In the KJV it is rendered: clamorous, concourse, cry aloud, be disquieted, loud, mourn, be moved, make a noise, rage, roar, sound, be troubled, make in tumult, tumultuous, be in an uproar.
H1994: (Aramaic) or (prolonged) himmown (Aramaic); corresponding to הֵם; they. In the KJV it is rendered: X are, them, those.
H1995: Or hamon (Ezek. 5:7); from הָמָה; a noise, tumult, crowd; also disquietude, wealth. In the KJV it is rendered: abundance, company, many, multitude, multiply, noise, riches, rumbling, sounding, store, tumult.
H1996: From הָמוֹן and גּוֹג; the multitude of Gog; the fanciful name of an emblematic place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hamogog.
H1997: Feminine of הָמוֹן; multitude; hamonah, the same as הֲמוֹן גּוֹג. In the KJV it is rendered: Hamonah.
H1998: From הָמָה; sound. In the KJV it is rendered: noise.
H1999: Or (too fully) hamuwllah (Jer. 11:16); feminine passive participle of an unused root meaning to rush (as rain with a windy roar); a sound. In the KJV it is rendered: speech, tumult.
H2000: A primitive root (compare הוּם, הָמָה); properly, to put in commotion; by implication, to disturb, drive, destroy. In the KJV it is rendered: break, consume, crush, destroy, discomfit, trouble, vex.
H2001: Of foreign derivation; Haman, a Persian vizier. In the KJV it is rendered: Haman.
H2002: (Aramaic) but the text is hamuwnek; of foreign origin; a necklace. In the KJV it is rendered: chain.
H2003: From an unused root apparently meaning to crackle; a dry twig or brushwood. In the KJV it is rendered: melting.
H2004: Feminine plural from הוּא; they (only used when emphatic). In the KJV it is rendered: X in, such like, (with) them, thereby, therein, (more than) they, wherein, in which, whom, withal.
H2005: A primitive particle; lo!; also (as expressing surprise) if. In the KJV it is rendered: behold, if, lo, though.
H2006: (Aramaic) corresponding to הֵן: lo! also there(-fore), (un-)less, whether, but, if. In the KJV it is rendered: (that) if, or, whether.
H2007: Prolongation for הֵן; themselves (often used emphatic for the copula, also in indirect relation). In the KJV it is rendered: X in, X such (and such things), their, (into) them, thence, therein, these, they (had), on this side, whose, wherein.
H2008: From הֵן; hither or thither (but used both of place and time). In the KJV it is rendered: here, hither(-to), now, on this (that) side, + since, this (that) way, thitherward, + thus far, to.
H2009: Prolongation for הֵן; lo!. In the KJV it is rendered: behold, lo, see.
H2010: From נ֫וּחַ; permission of rest, i.e. quiet. In the KJV it is rendered: release.
H2011: Probably of foreign origin; Hinnom, apparently a Jebusite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hinnom.
H2012: Probably of foreign derivation; Hena, a place apparently in Mesopotamia. In the KJV it is rendered: Hena.
H2013: A primitive root; to hush. In the KJV it is rendered: hold peace (tongue), (keep) silence, be silent, still.
H2014: From פּוּג; relaxation. In the KJV it is rendered: intermission.
H2015: A primitive root; to turn about or over; by implication, to change, overturn, return, pervert. In the KJV it is rendered: X become, change, come, be converted, give, make (a bed), overthrow (-turn), perverse, retire, tumble, turn (again, aside, back, to the contrary, every way).
H2016: : or hephek; from הָפַך; a turn, i.e. the reverse. In the KJV it is rendered: contrary.
H2017: From הָפַך; an upset, i.e. (abstract) perversity. In the KJV it is rendered: turning of things upside down.
H2018: Feminine of הֵ֫פֶך; destruction. In the KJV it is rendered: overthrow.
H2019: By reduplication from הָפַך; very perverse. In the KJV it is rendered: froward.
H2020: From נָצַל; rescue. In the KJV it is rendered: deliverance.
H2021: From an unused root meaning apparently to be sharp or strong; a weapon of war. In the KJV it is rendered: chariot.
H2022: A shortened form of הָ֫רַר; a mountain or range of hills (sometimes used figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: hill (country), mount(-ain), X promotion.
H2023: Another form of הָר; mountain; Hor, the name of a peak in Idumaea and of one in Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Hor.
H2024: Perhaps from הָר; mountainousness; Hara, a region of Media. In the KJV it is rendered: Hara.
H2025: From הָר and אֵל; mount of God; figuratively, the altar of burnt-offering. In the KJV it is rendered: altar.
H2026: A primitive root; to smite with deadly intent. In the KJV it is rendered: destroy, out of hand, kill, murder(-er), put to (death), make (slaughter), slay(-er), X surely.
H2027: From הָרַג; slaughter. In the KJV it is rendered: be slain, slaughter.
H2028: Feminine of הֶ֫רֶג; slaughter. In the KJV it is rendered: slaughter.
H2029: A primitive root; to be (or become) pregnant, conceive (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: been, be with child, conceive, progenitor.
H2030: Or hariy (Hosea 14:1); from הָרָה; pregnant. In the KJV it is rendered: (be, woman) with child, conceive, X great.
H2031: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to הָרָה; a mental conception. In the KJV it is rendered: thought.
H2032: Or herayown; from הָרָה; pregnancy. In the KJV it is rendered: conception.
H2033: Another form for הָרָרִי; a Harorite or mountaineer. In the KJV it is rendered: Harorite.
H2034: From הָרַס; something demolished. In the KJV it is rendered: ruin.
H2035: From הָרַס; demolition. In the KJV it is rendered: destruction.
H2036: From an unused root (meaning to tower up); high; Horam, a Canaanitish king. In the KJV it is rendered: Horam.
H2037: Passive participle of the same as הֹרָם; high; Harum, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Harum.
H2038: From the same as הֹרָם; a castle (from its height). In the KJV it is rendered: palace.
H2039: Perhaps from הָר; mountaineer; Haran, the name of two men. In the KJV it is rendered: Haran.
H2040: A primitive root; to pull down or in pieces, break, & destroy. In the KJV it is rendered: beat down, break (down, through), destroy, overthrow, pluck down, pull down, ruin, throw down, X utterly.
H2041: From הָרַס; demolition. In the KJV it is rendered: destruction.
H2042: From an unused root meaning to loom up; a mountain. In the KJV it is rendered: hill, mount(-ain).
H2043: Or Harariy (2 Sam. 23:11); or Haarariy (2 Sam. 23:34, last clause); apparently from הָ֫רַר; a mountaineer. In the KJV it is rendered: Hararite.
H2044: Perhaps from the same as חָשֻׁם; wealthy; Hashem, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hashem.
H2045: From שָׁמַע; announcement. In the KJV it is rendered: to cause to hear.
H2046: From נָתַך; a melting. In the KJV it is rendered: is melted.
H2047: Probably of foreign origin; Hathak, a Persian eunuch. In the KJV it is rendered: Hatach.
H2048: A primitive root; to deride; by implication, to cheat. In the KJV it is rendered: deal deceitfully, deceive, mock.
H2049: From הָתַל (only in plural collectively); a derision. In the KJV it is rendered: mocker.
H2050: A primitive root; properly, to break in upon, i.e. to assail. In the KJV it is rendered: imagine mischief.
H2051: Perhaps for עֲדָנִים; Vedan (or Aden), a place in Arabia. In the KJV it is rendered: Dan also.
H2052: Of uncertain derivation; Vaheb, a place in Moab. In the KJV it is rendered: what he did.
H2053: Probably a hook (the name of the sixth Heb. letter). In the KJV it is rendered: hook.
H2054: Presumed to be from an unused root meaning to bear guilt; crime. In the KJV it is rendered: X strange.
H2055: Of foreign origin; Vajezatha, a son of Haman. In the KJV it is rendered: Vajezatha.
H2056: For יָ֫לֶד; a boy. In the KJV it is rendered: child.
H2057: Perhaps for עֲנָיָה; Vanjah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Vaniah.
H2058: Probably from יָסַף; additional; Vophsi, an & Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Vophsi.
H2059: Probably from יִשְׁמְרַי; weak; Vashni, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Vashni.
H2060: Of Persian origin; Vashti, the queen of Xerxes. In the KJV it is rendered: Vashti.
H2061: From an unused root meaning to be yellow; a wolf. In the KJV it is rendered: wolf.
H2062: The same as זְאֵב; Zeeb, a Midianitish prince. In the KJV it is rendered: Zeeb.
H2063: Irregular feminine of שֶׂה; this (often used adverb). In the KJV it is rendered: hereby (-in, -with), it, likewise, the one (other, same), she, so (much), such (deed), that, therefore, these, this (thing), thus.
H2064: A primitive root; to confer. In the KJV it is rendered: endure.
H2065: From זָבַד; a gift. In the KJV it is rendered: dowry.
H2066: From זָבַד; giver; Zabad, the name of seven Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Zabad.
H2067: From זֵ֫בֶד; giving; Zabdi, the name of four & Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Zabdi.
H2068: From זֵ֫בֶד and אֵל; gift of God: zabdiel, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Zabdiel.

H2070: From an unused root (meaning to flit); a fly (especially one of a stinging nature). In the KJV it is rendered: fly.
H2071: From זָבַד; given, Zabud, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zabud.

H2073: Or zbul; from זָבַל; a residence. In the KJV it is rendered: dwell in, dwelling, habitation.
H2074: Or Zbuluwn; or Zbuwlun; from זָבַל; habitation; Zebulon, a son of Jacob; also his territory and tribe. In the KJV it is rendered: Zebulun.
H2075: Patronymically from זְבוּלוּן; a Zebulonite or descendant of Zebulun. In the KJV it is rendered: Zebulonite.
H2076: A primitive root; to slaughter an animal (usually in sacrifice). In the KJV it is rendered: kill, offer, (do) sacrifice, slay.
H2077: From זָבַח; properly, a slaughter, i.e. the flesh of an animal; by implication, a sacrifice (the victim or the act). In the KJV it is rendered: offer(- ing), sacrifice.
H2078: The same as זֶ֫בַח; sacrifice; Zebach, a Midianitish prince. In the KJV it is rendered: Zebah.
H2079: Probably by orthographical error for זַכָּי; Zabbai (or Zaccai), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zabbai.
H2080: Feminine from זָבַד; giving; Zebidah, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Zebudah.
H2081: From an unused root (meaning to purchase); gainfulness; Zebina, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zebina.
H2082: A primitive root; apparently properly, to inclose, i.e. to reside. In the KJV it is rendered: dwell with.
H2083: The same as זְבֻל; dwelling; Zebul, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zebul.
H2084: (Aramaic) corresponding to the root of זְבִינָא; to acquire by purchase. In the KJV it is rendered: gain.
H2085: From an unused root probably meaning to inclose; the skin of a grape. In the KJV it is rendered: husk.
H2086: From זִיד; arrogant. In the KJV it is rendered: presumptuous, proud.
H2087: From זִיד; arrogance. In the KJV it is rendered: presumptuously, pride, proud (man).
H2088: A primitive word; the masculine demonstrative pronoun, this or that. In the KJV it is rendered: he, X hence, X here, it(-self), X now, X of him, the one.
H2089: (1 Samuel by permutation for שֶׂה; a sheep. In the KJV it is rendered: lamb.
H2090: For זֶה; this or that. In the KJV it is rendered: as well as another, it, this, that, thus and thus.
H2091: From an unused root meaning to shimmer; gold, figuratively, something gold-colored (i.e. yellow), as oil, a clear sky. In the KJV it is rendered: gold(-en), fair weather.
H2092: A primitive root; to be rancid, i.e. (transitively) to loathe. In the KJV it is rendered: abhor.
H2093: From זָהַם; loathing; Zaham, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zaham.
H2094: A primitive root; to gleam; figuratively, to enlighten (by caution). In the KJV it is rendered: admonish, shine, teach, (give) warn(-ing).
H2095: (Aramaic) corresponding to זָהַר; (passively) be admonished. In the KJV it is rendered: take heed.
H2096: From זָהַר; brilliancy. In the KJV it is rendered: brightness.
H2097: For זֶה; this or that. In the KJV it is rendered: that, this.
H2098: For זֶה; this or that. In the KJV it is rendered: that, this, X wherein, which, whom.
H2099: Probably from an unused root meaning to be prominent; properly, brightness (compare זִיו), i.e. (figuratively) the month of flowers; Ziv (corresponding to Ijar or May). In the KJV it is rendered: Zif.
H2100: A primitive root; to flow freely (as water), i.e. (specifically) to have a (sexual) flux; figuratively, to waste away; also to overflow. In the KJV it is rendered: flow, gush out, have a (running) issue, pine away, run.
H2101: From זוּב; a seminal or menstrual flux. In the KJV it is rendered: issue.
H2102: Or (by permutation) ziyd; a primitive root; to seethe; figuratively, to be insolent. In the KJV it is rendered: be proud, deal proudly, & presume, (come) presumptuously, sod.
H2103: (Aramaic) corresponding to זִיד; to be proud. In the KJV it is rendered: in pride.
H2104: Plural probably from the same as זִיז; prominent; Zuzites, an aboriginal tribe of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Zuzims.
H2105: Of uncertain origin; Zocheth, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zoheth.
H2106: Apparently from the same root as זִו (in the sense of prominence); an angle (as projecting), i.e. (by implication) a corner-column (or anta). In the KJV it is rendered: corner(stone).
H2107: A primitive root (compare זָלַל); probably to shake out, i.e. (by implication) to scatter profusely; figuratively, to treat lightly. In the KJV it is rendered: lavish, despise.
H2108: From זוּל; probably scattering, i.e. removal; used adverbially, except. In the KJV it is rendered: beside, but, only, save.
H2109: A primitive root; perhaps properly, to be plump, i.e. (transitively) to nourish. In the KJV it is rendered: feed.
H2110: (Aramaic) corresponding to זוּן. In the KJV it is rendered: feed.
H2111: A primitive root; properly, to shake off, i.e. (figuratively) to agitate (as with fear). In the KJV it is rendered: move, tremble, vex.
H2112: (Aramaic) corresponding to ז֫וּעַ; to shake (with fear). In the KJV it is rendered: tremble.
H2113: From ז֫וּעַ; agitation, fear. In the KJV it is rendered: be removed, trouble, vexation.

H2115: A primitive root (compare צוֹק); to press together, & tighten. In the KJV it is rendered: close, rush, thrust together.
H2116: From זוּר; trodden on. In the KJV it is rendered: that which is crushed.
H2117: Probably from the root of זִיז; prominent; Zaza, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zaza.
H2118: A primitive root; to shove or displace. In the KJV it is rendered: loose.
H2119: A primitive root; to crawl; by implication, to fear. In the KJV it is rendered: be afraid, serpent, worm.
H2120: Feminine active participle of זָחַל; crawling (i.e. serpent); Zocheleth, a boundary stone in. Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Zoheleth.
H2121: From זִיד; boiling of water, i.e. wave. In the KJV it is rendered: proud.
H2122: (Aramaic) corresponding to זִו; (figuratively) cheerfulness. In the KJV it is rendered: brightness, countenance.
H2123: From an unused root apparently meaning to be conspicuous; fulness of the breast; also a moving creature. In the KJV it is rendered: abundance, wild beast.
H2124: Apparently from the same as זִיז; prominence; Ziza, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ziza.
H2125: Another form for זִיזָא; Zizah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zizah.
H2126: From זוּן; well-fed; or perhaps an orthographical error for זִיזָא; Zina, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zina.
H2127: From ז֫וּעַ; agitation; Zia, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zia.
H2128: From the same as זָ֫פֶת; flowing; Ziph, the name of a place in Palestine; also of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ziph.
H2129: Feminine of זִיף; a flowing; Ziphah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ziphah.
H2130: Patrial from זִיף; a Ziphite or inhabitant of Ziph. In the KJV it is rendered: Ziphim, Ziphite.

H2134: From זָכַך; clear. In the KJV it is rendered: clean, pure.

H2170: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to זָמַר; instrumental music. In the KJV it is rendered: musick.
H2171: (Aramaic) from the same as זְמָרָא; an instrumental musician. In the KJV it is rendered: singer.
H2172: From זָמַר; a musical piece or song to be accompanied by an instrument. In the KJV it is rendered: melody, psalm.
H2173: From זָמַר; pruned (i.e. choice) fruit. In the KJV it is rendered: best fruit.
H2174: From זָמַר; musical; Zimri, the name of five Israelites, and of an Arabian tribe. In the KJV it is rendered: Zimri.
H2175: From זָמַר; musical; Zimran, a son of Abraham by Keturah. In the KJV it is rendered: Zimran.
H2176: From זָמַר; instrumental music; by implication, praise. In the KJV it is rendered: song.
H2177: From זוּן; properly, nourished (or fully developed), i.e. a form or sort. In the KJV it is rendered: divers kinds, X all manner of store.
H2178: (Aramaic) corresponding to NONE; sort. In the KJV it is rendered: kind.
H2179: A primitive root meaning to wag; used only as a denominative from זָנָב; to curtail, i.e. cut off the rear. In the KJV it is rendered: smite the hindmost.
H2180: From זָנַב (in the original sense of flapping); the tail (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: tail.
H2181: A primitive root (highly-fed and therefore wanton); to commit adultery (usually of the female, and less often of simple fornication, rarely of involuntary ravishment); figuratively, to commit idolatry (the Jewish people being regarded as the spouse of Jehovah). In the KJV it is rendered: (cause to) commit fornication, X continually, X great, (be an, play the) harlot, (cause to be, play the) whore, (commit, fall to) whoredom, (cause to) go a-whoring, whorish.
H2182: From זָנַח; rejected; Zanoach, the name of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Zanoah.
H2183: From זָנָה; adultery; figuratively, idolatry. In the KJV it is rendered: whoredom.
H2184: From זָנָה; adultery, i.e. (figuratively) infidelity, idolatry. In the KJV it is rendered: whoredom.
H2185: Regarded by some as if from זוּן or an unused root, and applied to military equipments; but evidently the feminine plural active participle of זָנָה; harlots. In the KJV it is rendered: armour.
H2186: A primitive root meaning to push aside, i.e. reject, forsake, fail. In the KJV it is rendered: cast away (off), remove far away (off).
H2187: A primitive root; properly, to draw together the feet (as an animal about to dart upon its prey), i.e. to spring forward. In the KJV it is rendered: leap.
H2188: From ז֫וּעַ (in the sense of יָ֫זַע); perspiration. In the KJV it is rendered: sweat.
H2189: By transposition for זְוָעָה; agitation, maltreatment. In the KJV it is rendered: X removed, trouble.
H2190: From ז֫וּעַ; disquiet; Zaavan, an Idumaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Zaavan.
H2191: From an unused root (akin (by permutation) to צָעַר), meaning to dwindle; small. In the KJV it is rendered: little.
H2192: (Aramaic) corresponding to זְעֵיר. In the KJV it is rendered: little.
H2193: A primitive root; to extinguish. In the KJV it is rendered: be extinct.
H2194: A primitive root; properly, to foam at the mouth, i.e. to be enraged. In the KJV it is rendered: abhor, abominable, (be) angry, defy, (have) indignation.
H2195: From זָעַם; strictly froth at the mouth, i.e. (figuratively) fury (especially of God's displeasure with sin). In the KJV it is rendered: angry, indignation, rage.
H2196: A primitive root; properly, to boil up, i.e. (figuratively) to be peevish or angry. In the KJV it is rendered: fret, sad, worse liking, be wroth.
H2197: From זָעַף; anger. In the KJV it is rendered: indignation, rage(-ing), wrath.
H2198: From זָעַף; angry. In the KJV it is rendered: displeased.
H2199: A primitive root; to shriek (from anguish or danger); by analogy, (as a herald) to announce or convene publicly. In the KJV it is rendered: assemble, call (together), (make a) cry (out), come with such a company, gather (together), cause to be proclaimed.
H2200: (Aramaic) corresponding to זָעַק; to make an outcry. In the KJV it is rendered: cry.
H2201: And (feminine) zoaqah; from זָעַק; a shriek or outcry. In the KJV it is rendered: cry(-ing).
H2202: From an unused root (meaning to be fragrant); Ziphron, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ziphron.
H2203: From an unused root (meaning to liquify); asphalt (from its tendency to soften in the sun). In the KJV it is rendered: pitch.
H2204: A primitive root; to be old. In the KJV it is rendered: aged man, be (wax) old (man).
H2205: From זָקֵן; old. In the KJV it is rendered: aged, ancient (man), elder(-est), old (man, men and.
H2206: From זָקֵן; the beard (as indicating age). In the KJV it is rendered: beard.
H2207: From זָקֵן; old age. In the KJV it is rendered: age.
H2208: Properly, passive participle of זָקֵן (used only in the plural as a noun); old age:-old age.
H2209: Feminine of זָקֵן; old age. In the KJV it is rendered: old (age).
H2210: A primitive root; to life, i.e. (figuratively) comfort. In the KJV it is rendered: raise (up).
H2211: (Aramaic) corresponding to זָקַף; to hang, i.e. impale. In the KJV it is rendered: set up.
H2212: A primitive root; to strain, (figuratively) extract, clarify. In the KJV it is rendered: fine, pour down, purge, purify, refine.
H2213: From זָרַר (in the sense of scattering); a chaplet (as spread around the top), i.e. (specifically) a border moulding. In the KJV it is rendered: crown.
H2214: From זוּר (in the sense of estrangement) (compare זָרָה); disgust. In the KJV it is rendered: loathsome.
H2215: A primitive root; to flow away. In the KJV it is rendered: wax warm.
H2216: From זָרַב and בָּבֶל; descended of (i.e. from) Babylon, i.e. born there; Zerubbabel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zerubbabel.
H2217: (Aramaic) corresponding to זְרֻבָּבֶל. In the KJV it is rendered: Zerubbabel.
H2218: From an unused root meaning to be exuberant in growth; lined with shrubbery; Zered, a brook East of the Dead Sea. In the KJV it is rendered: Zared, Zered.
H2219: A primitive root (compare זוּר); to toss about; by implication, to diffuse, winnow. In the KJV it is rendered: cast away, compass, disperse, fan, scatter (away), spread, strew, winnow.
H2220: Or (shortened) zroao; and (feminine) zrowpah; or zrowah; from זָרַע; the arm (as stretched out), or (of animals) the foreleg; figuratively, force. In the KJV it is rendered: arm, + help, mighty, power, shoulder, strength.
H2221: From זָרַע; something sown, i.e. a plant. In the KJV it is rendered: sowing, thing that is sown.
H2222: By reduplication from an unused root meaning to flow; a pouring rain. In the KJV it is rendered: water.
H2223: By reduplication from זוּר; properly, tightly girt, i.e. probably a racer, or some fleet animal (as being slender in the waist). In the KJV it is rendered: + greyhound.
H2224: A primitive root; properly, to irradiate (or shoot forth beams), i.e. to rise (as the sun); specifically, to appear (as a symptom of leprosy). In the KJV it is rendered: arise, rise (up), as soon as it is up.
H2225: From זָרַח; a rising of light. In the KJV it is rendered: rising.
H2226: The same as זֶ֫רַח; Zerach, the name of three Israelites, also of an Idumaean and an Ethiopian prince. In the KJV it is rendered: Zarah, Zerah.
H2227: Patronymically from זָ֫רַח; a Zarchite or descendant of Zerach. In the KJV it is rendered: Zarchite.
H2228: From זֶ֫רַח and יָהּ; Jah has risen: Zerachjah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Zerahiah.
H2229: A primitive root; to gush (as water). In the KJV it is rendered: carry away as with a flood, pour out.
H2230: From זָרַם; a gush of water. In the KJV it is rendered: flood, overflowing, shower, storm, tempest.
H2231: Feminine of זָ֫רֶם; a gushing of fluid (semen). In the KJV it is rendered: issue.
H2232: A primitive root; to sow; figuratively, to disseminate, plant, fructify. In the KJV it is rendered: bear, conceive seed, set with sow(-er), yield.
H2233: From זָרַע; seed; figuratively, fruit, plant, sowing-time, posterity. In the KJV it is rendered: X carnally, child, fruitful, seed(-time), sowing- time.
H2234: (Aramaic) corresponding to זָ֫רַע; posterity. In the KJV it is rendered: seed.
H2235: Or zeraSon; from זָרַע; something sown (only in the plural), i.e. a vegetable (as food). In the KJV it is rendered: pulse.
H2236: A primitive root; to sprinkle (fluid or solid particles). In the KJV it is rendered: be here and there, scatter, sprinkle, strew.
H2237: A primitive root (compare זוּר); perhaps to diffuse, i.e. (specifically) to sneeze. In the KJV it is rendered: sneeze.
H2238: Of Persian origin; Zeresh, Haman's wife. In the KJV it is rendered: Zeresh.
H2239: From זָרָה; the spread of the fingers, i.e. a span. In the KJV it is rendered: span.
H2240: Of uncertain derivation; Zattu, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zattu.
H2241: Apparently a variation for זֵיתָן; Zetham, an & Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zetham.
H2242: Of Persian origin; Zethar, a eunuch of Xerxes. In the KJV it is rendered: Zethar.
H2243: By contraction from חָבַב; properly, a cherisher, i.e. the bosom. In the KJV it is rendered: bosom.
H2244: A primitive root (compare חָבַב); to secrete. In the KJV it is rendered: X held, hide (self), do secretly.
H2245: A primitive root (compare חָבָא, חָבָה); properly, to hide (as in the bosom), i.e. to cherish (with affection). In the KJV it is rendered: love.
H2246: From חָבַב; cherished; Chobab, father-in-law of Moses. In the KJV it is rendered: Hobab.
H2247: A primitive root (compare חָבַב); to secrete. In the KJV it is rendered: hide (self).
H2248: (Aramaic) from חֲבַל; properly, overthrown, i.e. (morally) crime. In the KJV it is rendered: hurt.
H2249: From חָבַר; united; Chabor, a river of Assyria. In the KJV it is rendered: Habor.
H2250: Or chabburah; or chaburah; from חָבַר; properly, bound (with stripes), i.e. a weal (or black-and-blue mark itself). In the KJV it is rendered: blueness, bruise, hurt, stripe, wound.
H2251: A primitive root; to knock out or off. In the KJV it is rendered: beat (off, out), thresh.
H2252: Or Chabayah; from חָבָה and יָהּ; Jah has hidden; Chabajah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Habaiah.
H2253: From חָבָה; a concealment. In the KJV it is rendered: hiding.
H2254: A primitive root; to wind tightly (as a rope), i.e. to bind; specifically, by a pledge; figuratively, to pervert, destroy; also to writhe in pain (especially of parturition). In the KJV it is rendered: X at all, band, bring forth, (deal) corrupt(-ly), destroy, offend, lay & to (take a) pledge, spoil, travail, X very, withhold.
H2255: (Aramaic) corresponding to חָבַל; to ruin. In the KJV it is rendered: destroy, hurt.
H2256: Or chebel; from חָבַל; a rope (as twisted), especially a measuring line; by implication, a district or inheritance (as measured); or a noose (as of cords); figuratively, a company (as if tied together); also a throe (especially of parturition); also ruin. In the KJV it is rendered: band, coast, company, cord, country, destruction, line, lot, pain, pang, portion, region, rope, snare, sorrow, tackling.
H2257: (Aramaic) from חֲבַל; harm (personal or pecuniary). In the KJV it is rendered: damage, hurt.
H2258: Or (feminine) chabolah; from חָבַל; a pawn (as security for debt). In the KJV it is rendered: pledge.
H2259: Active participle from חָבַל (in the sense of handling ropes); a sailor. In the KJV it is rendered: pilot, shipmaster.
H2260: From חָבַל (in the sense of furnished with ropes); a mast. In the KJV it is rendered: mast.
H2261: Of uncertain derivation; probably meadow-saffron. In the KJV it is rendered: rose.
H2262: Of uncertain derivation; Chabatstsanjah, a Rechabite. In the KJV it is rendered: Habazaniah.
H2263: A primitive root; to clasp (the hands or in embrace). In the KJV it is rendered: embrace, fold.
H2264: From חָבַק; a clasping of the hands (in idleness). In the KJV it is rendered: fold.
H2265: By reduplication from חָבַק; embrace; Chabakkuk, the prophet. In the KJV it is rendered: Habakkuk.
H2266: A primitive root; to join (literally or figuratively); specifically (by means of spells) to fascinate. In the KJV it is rendered: charm(- er), be compact, couple (together), have fellowship with, heap up, join (self, together), league.
H2267: From חָבַר; a society; also a spell. In the KJV it is rendered: + charmer(- ing), company, enchantment, X wide.
H2268: The same as חָ֫בֶר; community; Cheber, the name of a Kenite and of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Heber.
H2269: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to חָבַר; an associate. In the KJV it is rendered: companion, fellow.
H2270: From חָבַר; an associate. In the KJV it is rendered: companion, fellow, knit together.
H2271: From חָבַר; a partner. In the KJV it is rendered: companion.
H2272: By reduplication from חָבַר; a streak (like a line), as on the tiger. In the KJV it is rendered: spot.
H2273: (Aramaic) feminine of חַבְרִין; an associate. In the KJV it is rendered: other.
H2274: Feminine of חָ֫בֶר; association. In the KJV it is rendered: company.
H2275: From חָ֫בֶר; seat of association; Chebron, a place in Palestine, also the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hebron.
H2276: Or Chebroniy; patronymically from חֶבְרוֹן; Chebronite (collectively), an inhabitant of Chebron. In the KJV it is rendered: Hebronites.
H2277: Patronymically from חָ֫בֶר; a Chebrite (collectively) or descendants of Cheber. In the KJV it is rendered: Heberites.
H2278: Feminine of חָבֵר; a consort. In the KJV it is rendered: companion.
H2279: Feminine active participle of חָבַר; a joint. In the KJV it is rendered: which coupleth, coupling.
H2280: A primitive root; to wrap firmly (especially a turban, compress, or saddle); figuratively, to stop, to rule. In the KJV it is rendered: bind (up), gird about, govern, healer, put, saddle, wrap about.
H2281: From an unused root probably meaning to cook (compare מַחֲבַת); something fried, probably a griddle-cake. In the KJV it is rendered: pan.
H2282: Or chag; from חָגַג; a festival, or a victim therefor. In the KJV it is rendered: (solemn) feast (day), sacrifice, solemnity.
H2283: From an unused root meaning to revolve (compare חָגַג); properly, vertigo, i.e. (figuratively) fear. In the KJV it is rendered: terror.
H2284: Of uncertain derivation; a locust. In the KJV it is rendered: locust.
H2285: The same as חָגָב; locust; Chagab, one of the Nethinim. In the KJV it is rendered: Hagab.
H2286: Or Chagabah; feminine of חָגָב; locust; Chagaba or Chagabah, one of the Nethinim. In the KJV it is rendered: Hagaba, Hagabah.
H2287: A primitive root (compare חָגָּא, חוּג); properly, to move in a circle, i.e. (specifically) to march in a sacred procession, to observe a festival; by implication, to be giddy. In the KJV it is rendered: celebrate, dance, (keep, hold) a (solemn) feast (holiday), reel to and fro.
H2288: From an unused root meaning to take refuge; a rift in rocks. In the KJV it is rendered: cleft.
H2289: From חָגַר; belted. In the KJV it is rendered: girded with.
H2290: Or chagor; and (feminine) chagowrah; or chagorah; from חָגַר; a belt (for the waist). In the KJV it is rendered: apron, armour, gird(-le).
H2291: From חָגַג; festive, Chaggi, an Israelite; also (patronymically) a Chaggite, or descendant of the same. In the KJV it is rendered: Haggi, Haggites.
H2292: From חָג; festive; Chaggai, a Heb. prophet. In the KJV it is rendered: Haggai.
H2293: From חָג and יָהּ; festival of Jah; Chaggijah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Haggiah.
H2294: Feminine of חַגִּי; festive; Chaggith, a wife of David. In the KJV it is rendered: Haggith.
H2295: Of uncertain derivation; probably a partridge; Choglah, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Hoglah.
H2296: A primitive root; to gird on (as a belt, armor, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: be able to put on, be afraid, appointed, gird, restrain, X on every side.
H2297: Abridged from אֶחָד; one. In the KJV it is rendered: one.
H2298: (Aramaic) corresponding to חַד; as card. one; as article single; as an ordinal, first; adverbially, at once. In the KJV it is rendered: a, first, one, together.
H2299: From חָדַד; sharp. In the KJV it is rendered: sharp.
H2300: A primitive root; to be (causatively, make) sharp or (figuratively) severe. In the KJV it is rendered: be fierce, sharpen.
H2301: From חָדַד; fierce; Chadad, an Ishmaelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hadad.
H2302: A primitive root; to rejoice. In the KJV it is rendered: make glad, be joined, rejoice.
H2303: From חָדַד; a point. In the KJV it is rendered: sharp.
H2304: From חָדָה; rejoicing. In the KJV it is rendered: gladness, joy.
H2305: (Aramaic) corresponding to חֶדְוָה. In the KJV it is rendered: joy.
H2306: (Aramaic) corresponding to חָזֶה; a breast. In the KJV it is rendered: breast.
H2307: From חָדַד; a peak; Chadid, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hadid.
H2308: A primitive root; properly, to be flabby, i.e. (by implication) desist; (figuratively) be lacking or idle. In the KJV it is rendered: cease, end, fall, forbear, forsake, leave (off), let alone, rest, be unoccupied, want.
H2309: From חָדַל; rest, i.e. the state of the dead. In the KJV it is rendered: world.
H2310: From חָדַל; vacant, i.e. ceasing or destitute. In the KJV it is rendered: he that forbeareth, frail, rejected.
H2311: From חָ֫דֶל; idle; Chadlai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hadlai.
H2312: From an unused root meaning to sting; a prickly plant. In the KJV it is rendered: brier, thorn.
H2313: Probably of foreign origin; the Chiddekel (or Tigris) river. In the KJV it is rendered: Hiddekel.
H2314: A primitive root; properly, to inclose (as a room), i.e. (by analogy,) to beset (as in a siege). In the KJV it is rendered: enter a privy chamber.
H2315: From חָדַר; an apartment (usually literal). In the KJV it is rendered: ((bed) inner)chamber, innermost(-ward) part, parlour, + south, X within.
H2316: Another form for חֶ֫דֶר; chamber; Chadar, an Ishmaelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hadar.
H2317: Of uncertain derivation; Chadrak, a Syrian deity. In the KJV it is rendered: Hadrach.
H2318: A primitive root; to be new; causatively, to rebuild. In the KJV it is rendered: renew, repair.
H2319: From חָדַשׁ; new. In the KJV it is rendered: fresh, new thing.
H2320: From חָדַשׁ; the new moon; by implication, a month. In the KJV it is rendered: month(-ly), new moon.
H2321: The same as חֹ֫דֶשׁ; Chodesh, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Hodesh.
H2322: Feminine of חָדָשׁ; new; Chadashah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hadashah.
H2323: (Aramaic) corresponding to חָדָשׁ; new. In the KJV it is rendered: new.
H2324: (Aramaic) corresponding to חָוָה; to show. In the KJV it is rendered: shew.
H2325: Also chayab; a primitive root; properly, perhaps to tie, i.e. (figuratively and reflexively) to owe, or (by implication) to forfeit. In the KJV it is rendered: make endanger.
H2326: From חוּב; debt. In the KJV it is rendered: debtor.
H2327: Feminine active participle of חָבָה; hiding place; Chobah, a place in Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Hobah.
H2328: A primitive root (compare חָגַג); to describe a circle. In the KJV it is rendered: compass.
H2329: From חוּג; a circle. In the KJV it is rendered: circle, circuit, compass.
H2330: A primitive root; properly, to tie a knot, i.e. (figuratively) to propound a riddle. In the KJV it is rendered: put forth.
H2331: A primitive root; (compare חֲוָא, חָיָה); properly, to live; by implication (intensively) to declare or show. In the KJV it is rendered: show.
H2332: Causatively from חָוָה; life-giver; Chavvah (or Eve), the first woman. In the KJV it is rendered: Eve.
H2333: Properly, the same as חַוָּה (life-giving, i.e. living-place); by implication, an encampment or village. In the KJV it is rendered: (small) town.
H2334: From the plural of חַוֹּת and a modification of יָעוּר; hamlets of Jair, a region of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: (Bashan-)Havoth-jair.
H2335: From חֹזֶה; visionary; Chozai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: the seers.
H2336: From an unused root apparently meaning to pierce; a thorn; by analogy, a ring for the nose. In the KJV it is rendered: bramble, thistle, thorn.
H2337: Perhaps the same as ח֫וֹחַ; a dell or crevice (as if pierced in the earth). In the KJV it is rendered: thicket.
H2338: (Aramaic) corresponding to the root of חוּט, perhaps as a denominative; to string together, i.e. (figuratively) to repair. In the KJV it is rendered: join.
H2339: From an unused root probably meaning to sew; a string; by implication, a measuring tape. In the KJV it is rendered: cord, fillet, line, thread.
H2340: Perhaps from חַוֹּת; a villager; a Chivvite, one of the aboriginal tribes of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hivite.
H2341: Probably from חוּל; circular; Chavilah, the name of two or three eastern regions; also perhaps of two men. In the KJV it is rendered: Havilah.
H2342: Or chiyl; a primitive root; properly, to twist or whirl (in a circular or spiral manner), i.e. (specifically) to dance, to writhe in pain (especially of parturition) or fear; figuratively, to wait, to pervert. In the KJV it is rendered: bear, (make to) bring forth, (make to) calve, dance, drive away, fall grievously (with pain), fear, form, great, grieve, (be) grievous, hope, look, make, be in pain, be much (sore) pained, rest, shake, shapen, (be) sorrow(-ful), stay, tarry, travail (with pain), tremble, trust, wait carefully (patiently), be wounded.
H2343: From חוּל; a circle; Chul, a son of Aram; also the region settled by him. In the KJV it is rendered: Hul.
H2344: From חוּל; sand (as round or whirling particles). In the KJV it is rendered: sand.

H2348: From an unused root meaning to cover; a cove (as a sheltered bay). In the KJV it is rendered: coast (of the sea), haven, shore, (sea-)side.
H2349: From the same as חוֹף; protection: Chupham, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hupham.
H2350: Patronymically from חוּפָם; a Chuphamite or descendant of Chupham. In the KJV it is rendered: Huphamites.

H2352: Or (shortened) chur; from an unused root probably meaning to bore; the crevice of a serpent; the cell of a prison. In the KJV it is rendered: hole.
H2353: From חָוַר; white linen. In the KJV it is rendered: white.
H2354: The same as חוּר or חֻר; Chur, the name of four Israelites and one Midianite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hur.
H2355: The same as חוּר; white linen. In the KJV it is rendered: network.
H2356: Or (shortened) chor; the same as חֻר; a cavity, socket, den. In the KJV it is rendered: cave, hole.
H2357: A primitive root; to blanch (as with shame). In the KJV it is rendered: wax pale.
H2358: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to חָוַר; white. In the KJV it is rendered: white.
H2359: Probably from חוּר; linen-worker; Churi, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Huri.
H2360: Probably an orthographical variation for חוּרִי; Churai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hurai.
H2361: Probably from חוּר; whiteness, i.e. noble; Churam, the name of an Israelite and two Syrians. In the KJV it is rendered: Huram.
H2362: Apparently from חָוַר (in the sense of חֻר); cavernous; Chavran, a region East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Hauran.

H2364: From חוּשׁ; haste; Chushah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hushah.
H2365: From חוּשׁ; hasty; Chushai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hushai.
H2366: Or Chushiym; or Chushim; plural from חוּשׁ; hasters; Chushim, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hushim.
H2367: Or Chusham; from חוּשׁ; hastily; Chusham, an Idumaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Husham.
H2368: Or chotham; from חָתַם; a signature-ring. In the KJV it is rendered: seal, signet.
H2369: The same as חוֹתָם; seal; Chotham, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hotham, Hothan.

H2371: Or Chazahoel; from חָזָה and אֵל; God has seen; Chazael, a king of Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazael.
H2372: A primitive root; to gaze at; mentally, to perceive, contemplate (with pleasure); specifically, to have a vision of. In the KJV it is rendered: behold, look, prophesy, provide, see.
H2373: From חָזָה; the breast (as most seen in front). In the KJV it is rendered: breast.
H2374: Active participle of חָזָה; a beholder in vision; also a compact (as looked upon with approval). In the KJV it is rendered: agreement, prophet, see that, seer, (star-)gazer.
H2375: From חָזָה; seer; Chazo, a nephew of Abraham. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazo.
H2376: (Aramaic) from חֲזָה; a sight. In the KJV it is rendered: look, vision.
H2377: From חָזָה; a sight (mentally), i.e. a dream, revelation, or oracle. In the KJV it is rendered: vision.
H2378: From חָזָה; a revelation. In the KJV it is rendered: vision.
H2379: (Aramaic) from חֲזָה; a view. In the KJV it is rendered: sight.
H2380: From חָזָה; a look; hence (figuratively) striking appearance, revelation, or (by implication) compact. In the KJV it is rendered: agreement, notable (one), vision.
H2381: From חָזָה and אֵל; seen of God; Chaziel, a Levite. In the KJV it is rendered: Haziel.
H2382: From חָזָה and יָהּ; Jah has seen; Chazajah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazaiah.
H2383: From חָזָה; vision; Chezjon, a Syrian. In the KJV it is rendered: Hezion.
H2384: From חָזָה; a revelation, expectation by dream. In the KJV it is rendered: vision.
H2385: From an unused root meaning to glare; a flash of lightning. In the KJV it is rendered: bright cloud, lightning.
H2386: From an unused root probably meaning to enclose; a hog (perhaps as penned). In the KJV it is rendered: boar, swine.
H2387: From the same as חֲזִיר; perhaps protected; Chezir, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hezir.

H2390: From חָזַק; powerful. In the KJV it is rendered: X wax louder, stronger.
H2391: From חָזַק; help. In the KJV it is rendered: strength.
H2392: From חָזַק; power. In the KJV it is rendered: strength.

H2395: From חָזַק; strong; Chizki, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hezeki.

H2399: From חָטָא; a crime or its penalty. In the KJV it is rendered: fault, X grievously, offence, (punishment of) sin.
H2400: Intensively from חָטָא; a criminal, or one accounted guilty. In the KJV it is rendered: offender, sinful, sinner.
H2401: Feminine of חֵטְא; an offence, or a sacrifice for it. In the KJV it is rendered: sin (offering).
H2402: (Aramaic) corresponding to חֲטָאָה; an offence, and the penalty or sacrifice for it. In the KJV it is rendered: sin (offering).

H2404: A primitive root; to chop or carve wood. In the KJV it is rendered: cut down, hew(-er), polish.
H2405: Feminine passive participle of חָטַב; properly, a carving; hence, a tapestry (as figured). In the KJV it is rendered: carved.
H2406: Of uncertain derivation; wheat, whether the grain or the plant. In the KJV it is rendered: wheat(-en).
H2407: From an unused root of uncertain signification; Chattush, the name of four or five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hattush.
H2408: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to חָטָא; an offence. In the KJV it is rendered: sin.
H2409: (Aramaic) from the same as חֲטֵי; an expiation. In the KJV it is rendered: sin offering.
H2410: From an unused root apparently meaning to dig out; explorer; Chatita, a temple porter. In the KJV it is rendered: Hatita.
H2411: From an unused root apparently meaning to wave; fluctuating; Chattil, one of "Solomon's servants". In the KJV it is rendered: Hattil.
H2412: From חָטַף; robber; Chatipha, one of the Nethinim. In the KJV it is rendered: Hatipha.
H2413: A primitive root; to stop. In the KJV it is rendered: refrain.
H2414: A primitive root; to clutch; hence, to seize as a prisoner. In the KJV it is rendered: catch.
H2415: From an unused root of uncertain signification; a twig. In the KJV it is rendered: rod.
H2416: From חָיָה; alive; hence, raw (flesh); fresh (plant, water, year), strong; also (as noun, especially in the feminine singular and masculine plural) life (or living thing), whether literally or figuratively. H2417: (Aramaic) from חֲיָא; alive; also (as noun in plural) life. In the KJV it is rendered: life, that liveth, living.
H2418: (Aramaic) or chayah (Aramaic); corresponding to חָיָה; to live. In the KJV it is rendered: live, keep alive.
H2419: From חָי and אֵל; living of God; Chiel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hiel.
H2420: From חוּד; a puzzle, hence, a trick, conundrum, sententious maxim. In the KJV it is rendered: dark saying (sentence, speech), hard question, proverb, riddle.
H2421: A primitive root (compare חָוָה, חָיָה); to live, whether literally or figuratively; causatively, to revive. H2422: From חָיָה; vigorous. In the KJV it is rendered: lively.
H2423: (Aramaic) from חֲיָא; an animal. In the KJV it is rendered: beast.
H2424: From חָיָה; life. In the KJV it is rendered: X living.
H2425: A primitive root (compare חָיָה); to live; causatively to revive. In the KJV it is rendered: live, save life.

H2427: And (feminine) chiylah; from חוּל; a throe (expectant of childbirth). In the KJV it is rendered: pain, pang, sorrow.
H2428: From חוּל; probably a force, whether of men, means or other resources; an army, wealth, virtue, valor, strength. H2429: (Aramaic) corresponding to חָ֫יִל; an army, or strength. In the KJV it is rendered: aloud, army, X most (mighty), power.
H2430: Feminine of חָ֫יִל; an intrenchment. In the KJV it is rendered: bulwark.
H2431: Or Cheleam; from חָ֫יִל; fortress; Chelam, a place East of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Helam.
H2432: From חָ֫יִל; fortress; Chilen, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hilen.
H2433: Another form for חֵן; beauty. In the KJV it is rendered: comely.
H2434: Another form for חוּץ; a wall. In the KJV it is rendered: wall.
H2435: From חַ֫יִץ; properly, the (outer) wall side; hence, exterior; figuratively, secular (as opposed to sacred). In the KJV it is rendered: outer, outward, utter, without.
H2436: Or cheq; and chowq; from an unused root, apparently meaning to inclose; the bosom (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: bosom, bottom, lap, midst, within.
H2437: From חָוַר in the sense of splendor; Chirah, an Adullamite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hirah.
H2438: Or Chiyrowm; another form of חוּרָם; Chiram or Chirom, the name of two Tyrians. In the KJV it is rendered: Hiram, Huram.
H2439: Another form of חוּשׁ; to hurry. In the KJV it is rendered: make haste.
H2440: From חִישׁ; properly, a hurry; hence (adverb) quickly. In the KJV it is rendered: soon.
H2441: Probably from חָנַך in the sense of tasting; properly, the palate or inside of the mouth; hence, the mouth itself (as the organ of speech, taste and kissing). In the KJV it is rendered: (roof of the) mouth, taste.
H2442: A primitive root (apparently akin to חָקָה through the idea of piercing); properly, to adhere to; hence, to await. In the KJV it is rendered: long, tarry, wait.
H2443: Probably from חָכָה; a hook (as adhering). In the KJV it is rendered: angle, hook.
H2444: From the same as חַכְלִיל; dark; Chakilah, a hill in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hachilah.
H2445: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to חָכַם; wise, i.e. a Magian. In the KJV it is rendered: wise.

H2448: From חַכְלִיל; flash (of the eyes); in a bad sense, blearedness. In the KJV it is rendered: redness.

H2451: From חָכַם; wisdom (in a good sense). In the KJV it is rendered: skilful, wisdom, wisely, wit.
H2452: (Aramaic) corresponding to חָכְמָה; wisdom. In the KJV it is rendered: wisdom.
H2453: From חָכַם; skilful; Chakmoni, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hachmoni, Hachmonite.
H2454: Or chakmowth; collateral forms of חָכְמָה; wisdom. In the KJV it is rendered: wisdom, every wise (woman).
H2455: From חָלַל; properly, exposed; hence, profane. In the KJV it is rendered: common, profane (place), unholy.
H2456: A primitive root (compare חָלָה); to be sick. In the KJV it is rendered: be diseased.
H2457: From חָלָא; properly, disease; hence, rust. In the KJV it is rendered: scum.
H2458: The same as חֶלְאַת; Chelah, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Helah.
H2459: Or cheleb; from an unused root meaning to be fat; fat, whether literally or figuratively; hence, the richest or choice part. In the KJV it is rendered: X best, fat(-ness), X finest, grease, marrow.
H2460: The same as חֵ֫לֶב; fatness; Cheleb, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Heleb.
H2461: From the same as חֵ֫לֶב; milk (as the richness of kine). In the KJV it is rendered: + cheese, milk, sucking.
H2462: Feminine of חֵ֫לֶב; fertility: Chelbah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Helbah.
H2463: From חֵ֫לֶב; fruitful; Chelbon, a place in Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Helbah.
H2464: From חֵ֫לֶב; galbanam, an odorous gum (as if fatty). In the KJV it is rendered: galbanum.
H2465: From an unused root apparently meaning to glide swiftly; life (as a fleeting portion of time); hence, the world (as transient). In the KJV it is rendered: age, short time, world.
H2466: The same as חֶ֫לֶד; Cheled, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Heled.
H2467: From the same as חֶ֫לֶד; a weasel (from its gliding motion). In the KJV it is rendered: weasel.
H2468: Feminine of חֹ֫לֶד; Chuldah, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Huldah.
H2469: From חֵ֫לֶד; worldliness; Cheldai, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Heldai.
H2470: A primitive root (compare חוּל, חָלָה, חָלַל); properly, to be rubbed or worn; hence (figuratively) to be weak, sick, afflicted; or (causatively) to grieve, make sick; also to stroke (in flattering), entreat. H2471: From חָלַל; a cake (as usually punctured). In the KJV it is rendered: cake.
H2472: Or (shortened) chalom; from חָלַם; a dream. In the KJV it is rendered: dream(-er).
H2473: Or (shortened) Cholon; probably from חוֹל; sandy; Cholon, the name of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Holon.
H2474: A window (as perforated). In the KJV it is rendered: window.
H2475: From חָלַף; properly, surviving; by implication (collectively) orphans. In the KJV it is rendered: X destruction.
H2476: Feminine passive participle of חָלַשׁ; defeat. In the KJV it is rendered: being overcome.
H2477: Probably of foreign origin; Chalach, a region of Assyria. In the KJV it is rendered: Halah.
H2478: By reduplication from חוּל; contorted; Chalchul, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Halhul.
H2479: Feminine from the same as חַלְחוּל; writhing (in childbirth); by implication, terror. In the KJV it is rendered: (great, much) pain.
H2480: A primitive root; to snatch at. In the KJV it is rendered: catch.
H2481: From חָלָה; a trinket (as polished). In the KJV it is rendered: jewel, ornament.
H2482: The same as חֲלִי; Chali, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hali.
H2483: From חָלָה; malady, anxiety, calamity. In the KJV it is rendered: disease, grief, (is) sick(-ness).
H2484: Feminine of חֲלִי; a trinket. In the KJV it is rendered: jewel.
H2485: From חָלַל; a flute (as perforated). In the KJV it is rendered: pipe.

H2487: From חָלַף; alternation. In the KJV it is rendered: change, course.
H2488: From חָ֫לֶץ; spoil. In the KJV it is rendered: armour.
H2489: Or chelkah; apparently from an unused root probably meaning to be dark or (figuratively) unhappy; a wretch, i.e. unfortunate. In the KJV it is rendered: poor.

H2493: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to חָלַם; a dream. In the KJV it is rendered: dream.
H2494: From חָלַם; a dream; Chelem, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Helem.
H2495: From חָלַם (in the sense of insipidity); probably purslain. In the KJV it is rendered: egg.
H2496: Probably from חָלַם (in the sense of hardness); flint. In the KJV it is rendered: flint(-y), rock.
H2497: From חָ֫יִל; strong; Chelon, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Helon.

H2499: (Aramaic) corresponding to חָלַף; to pass on (of time). In the KJV it is rendered: pass.
H2500: From חָלַף; properly, exchange; hence (as preposition) instead of. In the KJV it is rendered: X for.
H2501: The same as חֵ֫לֶף; change; Cheleph, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Heleph.

H2506: From חָלַק; properly, smoothness (of the tongue); also an allotment. In the KJV it is rendered: flattery, inheritance, part, X partake, portion.
H2507: The same as חֵ֫לֶק; portion; Chelek, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Helek.
H2508: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to חָלַק; a part. In the KJV it is rendered: portion.
H2509: From חָלַק; smooth (especially of tongue). In the KJV it is rendered: flattering, smooth.
H2510: The same as חָלָק; bare; Chalak, a mountain of Idumaea. In the KJV it is rendered: Halak.
H2511: From חָלַק; smooth. In the KJV it is rendered: smooth.
H2512: From חָלַק; smooth. In the KJV it is rendered: smooth.
H2513: Feminine of חֵ֫לֶק; properly, smoothness; figuratively, flattery; also an allotment. In the KJV it is rendered: field, flattering(-ry), ground, parcel, part, piece of land (ground), plat, portion, slippery place, smooth (thing).
H2514: Feminine from חָלַק; flattery. In the KJV it is rendered: flattery.
H2515: Feminine of חַלֻּקֵי; a distribution. In the KJV it is rendered: division.
H2516: Patronymically from חֵ֫לֶק; a Chelkite or descendant of Chelek. In the KJV it is rendered: Helkites.
H2517: From חָלַק; apportioned; Chelkai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Helkai.
H2518: Or Chilqiyahuw from חֵ֫לֶק and יָהּ; portion of Jah; Chilhijah, the name of eight Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hillkiah.
H2519: By reduplication from חָלַק; properly, something very smooth; i.e. a treacherous spot; figuratively, blandishment. In the KJV it is rendered: flattery, slippery.
H2520: A form of חֶלְקָה; smoothness; Chelkath, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Helkath.
H2521: From חֶלְקָת and the plural of צוּר, with the article inserted; smoothness of the rocks; Chelkath Hats-tsurim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Helkath-hazzurim.
H2522: A primitive root; to prostrate; by implication, to overthrow, decay. In the KJV it is rendered: discomfit, waste away, weaken.
H2523: From חָלַשׁ; frail. In the KJV it is rendered: weak.
H2524: From the same as חוֹמָה; a father-in-law (as in affinity). In the KJV it is rendered: father in law.
H2525: From חָמַם; hot. In the KJV it is rendered: hot, warm.
H2526: The same as חָם; hot (from the tropical habitat); Cham, a son of Noah; also (as a patronymic) his descendants or their country. In the KJV it is rendered: Ham.
H2527: From חָמַם; heat. In the KJV it is rendered: heat, to be hot (warm).
H2528: (Aramaic) or chamah (Aramaic); corresponding to חֵמָה; anger. In the KJV it is rendered: fury.
H2529: Or (shortened) chemah; from the same root as חוֹמָה; curdled milk or cheese. In the KJV it is rendered: butter.
H2530: A primitive root; to delight in. In the KJV it is rendered: beauty, greatly beloved, covet, delectable thing, (X great) delight, desire, goodly, lust, (be) pleasant (thing), precious (thing).
H2531: Om חָמַד; delight. In the KJV it is rendered: desirable, pleasant.
H2532: Feminine of חֶ֫מֶד; delight. In the KJV it is rendered: desire, goodly, pleasant, precious.
H2533: From חֶ֫מֶד; pleasant; Chemdan, an Idumaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Hemdan.
H2534: Or (Dan. 11:44) chemaC; from יָחַם; heat; figuratively, anger, poison (from its fever). In the KJV it is rendered: anger, bottles, hot displeasure, furious(-ly, -ry), heat, indignation, poison, rage, wrath(- ful).
H2535: From חָם; heat; by implication, the sun. In the KJV it is rendered: heat, sun.
H2536: From חַמָּה and אֵל; anger of God; Chammuel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hamuel.
H2537: Or Chamiytal; from חָם and טָל; father-in-law of dew; Chamutal or Chamital, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Hamutal.
H2538: From חָמַל; pitied; Chamul, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hamul.
H2539: Patronymically from חָמוּל: a Chamulite (collectively) or descendants of Chamul. In the KJV it is rendered: Hamulites.
H2540: From חָמַם; warm spring; Chammon, the name of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hammon.
H2541: From חָמֵץ; properly, violent; by implication, a robber. In the KJV it is rendered: oppressed.
H2542: From חָמַק; a wrapping, i.e. drawers. In the KJV it is rendered: joints.
H2543: Or (shortened) chamor; from חָמַר; a male ass (from its dun red). In the KJV it is rendered: (he)ass.
H2544: The same as חֲמוֹר; donkey; Chamor, a Canaanite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hamor.
H2545: Or (shortened) chamoth; feminine of חָם; a mother-in-law. In the KJV it is rendered: mother in law.
H2546: From an unused root probably meaning, to lie low; a lizard (as creeping). In the KJV it is rendered: snail.
H2547: Feminine of חֹ֫מֶט; low; Chumtah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Humtah.
H2548: From חָמֵץ; seasoned, i.e. salt provender. In the KJV it is rendered: clean.
H2549: Or chamishshiy; ord. from חָמֵשׁ; fifth; also a fifth. In the KJV it is rendered: fifth (part).
H2550: A primitive root; to commiserate; by implication, to spare. In the KJV it is rendered: have compassion, (have) pity, spare.
H2551: From חָמַל; commiseration. In the KJV it is rendered: merciful, pity.
H2552: A primitive root; to be hot (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: enflame self, get (have) heat, be (wax) hot, (be, wax) warm (self, at).
H2553: From חַמָּה; a sun-pillar. In the KJV it is rendered: idol, image.
H2554: A primitive root; to be violent; by implication, to maltreat. In the KJV it is rendered: make bare, shake off, violate, do violence, take away violently, wrong, imagine wrongfully.
