H2555: From חָמַס; violence; by implication, wrong; by meton. unjust gain. In the KJV it is rendered: cruel(-ty), damage, false, injustice, X oppressor, unrighteous, violence (against, done), violent (dealing), wrong.
H2556: A primitive root; to be pungent; i.e. in taste (sour, i.e. literally fermented, or figuratively, harsh), in color (dazzling). In the KJV it is rendered: cruel (man), dyed, be grieved, leavened.
H2557: From חָמֵץ; ferment, (figuratively) extortion. In the KJV it is rendered: leaven, leavened (bread).
H2558: From חָמֵץ; vinegar. In the KJV it is rendered: vinegar.
H2559: A primitive root; properly, to wrap; hence, to depart (i.e. turn about). In the KJV it is rendered: go about, withdraw self.
H2560: A primitive root; properly, to boil up; hence, to ferment (with scum); to glow (with redness); as denominative (from חֵמָר) to smear with pitch. In the KJV it is rendered: daub, befoul, be red, trouble.
H2561: From חָמַר; wine (as fermenting). In the KJV it is rendered: X pure, red wine.
H2562: (Aramaic) corresponding to חָ֫מֶר; wine. In the KJV it is rendered: wine.
H2563: From חָמַר; properly, a bubbling up, i.e. of water, a wave; of earth, mire or clay (cement); also a heap; hence, a chomer or dry measure. In the KJV it is rendered: clay, heap, homer, mire, motion.
H2564: From חָמַר; bitumen (as rising to the surface). In the KJV it is rendered: slime(-pit).
H2565: From חָמַר (compare חֹ֫מֶר); a heap. In the KJV it is rendered: heap.
H2566: From חָמַר; red; Chamran, an Idumaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Amran.
H2567: A denominative from חָמֵשׁ; to tax a fifth:--take up the fifth participle.
H2568: Masculine chamishshah; a primitive numeral; five. In the KJV it is rendered: fif(-teen), fifth, five (X apiece).
H2569: From חִמֵּשׁ; a fifth tax:--fifth participle.
H2570: From an unused root probably meaning, to be stout; the abdomen (as obese). In the KJV it is rendered: fifth (rib).
H2571: Passive participle of the same as חֹ֫מֶשׁ; staunch, i.e. able-bodied soldiers. In the KJV it is rendered: armed (men), harnessed.
H2572: Multiple of חָמֵשׁ; fifty. In the KJV it is rendered: fifty.
H2573: From the same as חוֹמָה; a skin bottle (as tied up). In the KJV it is rendered: bottle.
H2574: From the same as חוֹמָה; walled; Chamath, a place in Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Hamath, Hemath.
H2575: A variation for the first part of חַמֹּת דֹּאר; hot springs; Chammath, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hammath.
H2576: From the plural of חַמָּה and דֹּאר; hot springs of Dor; Chammath-Dor, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hamath-Dor.
H2577: Patrial from חֲמָת; a Chamathite or native of Chamath. In the KJV it is rendered: Hamathite.
H2578: From חֲמָת and צוֹבָה; Chamath of Tsobah; Chamath-Tsobah; probably the same as חֲמָת. In the KJV it is rendered: Hamath-Zobah.
H2579: From חֲמָת and רַבָּה; Chamath of Rabbah; Chamath-Rabbah, probably the same as חֲמָת.
H2580: From חָנַן; graciousness, i.e. subjective (kindness, favor) or objective (beauty). In the KJV it is rendered: favour, grace(-ious), pleasant, precious, (well-)favoured.
H2581: The same as חֵן; grace; Chen, a figurative name for an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hen.
H2582: Probably from חֵן and הֲדָד; favor of Hadad; Chenadad, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Henadad.
H2583: A primitive root (compare חָנַן); properly, to incline; by implication, to decline (of the slanting rays of evening); specifically, to pitch a tent; gen. to encamp (for abode or siege). In the KJV it is rendered: abide (in tents), camp, dwell, encamp, grow to an end, lie, pitch (tent), rest in tent.
H2584: From חָנַן; favored; Channah, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Hannah.
H2585: From חָנַך; initiated; Chanok, an antediluvian patriach. In the KJV it is rendered: Enoch.
H2586: From חָנַן; favored; Chanun, the name of an Ammonite and of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hanun.
H2587: From חָנַן; gracious. In the KJV it is rendered: gracious.
H2588: From חָנָה; properly, a vault or cell (with an arch); by implication, a prison. In the KJV it is rendered: cabin.
H2589: From חָנַן (in the sense of prayer); supplication. In the KJV it is rendered: be gracious, intreated.
H2590: A primitive root; to spice; by implication, to embalm; also to ripen. In the KJV it is rendered: embalm, put forth.
H2591: (Aramaic) corresponding to חִטִּים; wheat. In the KJV it is rendered: wheat.
H2592: From חָנַן and אֵל; favor of God; Channiel, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hanniel.
H2593: From חָנַך; initiated; i.e. practiced. In the KJV it is rendered: trained.
H2594: From חָנַן; graciousness. In the KJV it is rendered: favour.
H2595: From חָנָה; a lance (for thrusting, like pitching a tent). In the KJV it is rendered: javelin, spear.
H2596: A primitive root; properly, to narrow (compare חָנַק); figuratively, to initiate or discipline. In the KJV it is rendered: dedicate, train up.
H2597: (Aramaic) corresponding to חֲנֻכָּה; consecration. In the KJV it is rendered: dedication.
H2598: From חָנַך; initiation, i.e. consecration. In the KJV it is rendered: dedicating(-tion).
H2599: Patronymically from חֲנוֹך; a Chanokite (collectively) or descendants of Chanok. In the KJV it is rendered: Hanochites.
H2600: From חֵן; gratis, i.e. devoid of cost, reason or advantage. In the KJV it is rendered: without a cause (cost, wages), causeless, to cost nothing, free(-ly), innocent, for nothing (nought, in vain.
H2601: Probably by orthographical variation for חֲנַנְאֵל; Chanamel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hanameel.
H2602: Of uncertain derivation; perhaps the aphis or plantlouse. In the KJV it is rendered: frost.
H2603: A primitive root (compare חָנָה); properly, to bend or stoop in kindness to an inferior; to favor, bestow; causatively to implore (i.e. move to favor by petition). In the KJV it is rendered: beseech, X fair, (be, find, shew) favour(-able), be (deal, give, grant (gracious(-ly), intreat, (be) merciful, have (shew) mercy (on, upon), have pity upon, pray, make supplication, X very.
H2604: (Aramaic) corresponding to חָנַן; to favor or (causatively) to entreat. In the KJV it is rendered: shew mercy, make supplication.
H2605: From חָנַן; favor; Chanan, the name of seven Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Canan.
H2606: From חָנַן and אֵל; God has favored; Chananel, probably an Israelite, from whom a tower of Jerusalem was named. In the KJV it is rendered: Hananeel.
H2607: From חָנַן; gracious; Chanani, the name of six Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hanani.
H2608: Or Chananyahuw; from חָנַן and יָהּ; Jah has favored; Chananjah, the name of thirteen Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hananiah.
H2609: Of Egyptian derivation; Chanes, a place in Egypt. In the KJV it is rendered: Hanes.
H2610: A primitive root; to soil, especially in a moral sense. In the KJV it is rendered: corrupt, defile, X greatly, pollute, profane.
H2611: From חָנֵף; soiled (i.e. with sin), impious. In the KJV it is rendered: hypocrite(-ical).
H2612: From חָנֵף; moral filth, i.e. wickedness. In the KJV it is rendered: hypocrisy.
H2613: Feminine from חָנֵף; impiety. In the KJV it is rendered: profaneness.
H2614: A primitive root (compare חָנַך); to be narrow; by implication, to throttle, or (reflex.) to choke oneself to death (by a rope). In the KJV it is rendered: hang self, strangle.
H2615: Probably from חָנַן; favored; Channathon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hannathon.
H2616: A primitive root; properly, perhaps to bow (the neck only (compare חָנַן) in courtesy to an equal), i.e. to be kind; also (by euphem. (compare בָּרַך), but rarely) to reprove. In the KJV it is rendered: shew self merciful, put to shame.
H2617: From חָסַד; kindness; by implication (towards God) piety: rarely (by opposition) reproof, or (subject.) beauty. In the KJV it is rendered: favour, good deed(-liness, -ness), kindly, (loving-)kindness, merciful (kindness), mercy, pity, reproach, wicked thing.
H2618: The same as חָ֫סֶד: favor; Chesed, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hesed.
H2619: From חָ֫סֶד and יָהּ; Jah has favored: Chasadjah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hasadiah.
H2620: A primitive root; to flee for protection (compare בָּטַח); figuratively, to confide in. In the KJV it is rendered: have hope, make refuge, (put) trust.
H2621: From חָסָה; hopeful; Chosah, an Israelite; also a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hosah.
H2622: From חָסָה; confidence. In the KJV it is rendered: trust.
H2623: From חָסַד; properly, kind, i.e. (religiously) pious (a saint). In the KJV it is rendered: godly (man), good, holy (one), merciful, saint, (un-)godly.
H2624: Feminine of חָסִיד; the kind (maternal) bird, i.e. a stork. In the KJV it is rendered: X feather, stork.
H2625: From חָסַל; the ravager, i.e. a locust. In the KJV it is rendered: caterpillar.
H2626: From חָסַן; properly, firm, i.e. (by implication) mighty. In the KJV it is rendered: strong.
H2627: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to חָסֵר; deficient. In the KJV it is rendered: wanting.
H2628: A primitive root; to eat off. In the KJV it is rendered: consume.
H2629: A primitive root; to muzzle; by analogy, to stop the nose. In the KJV it is rendered: muzzle, stop.
H2630: A primitive root; properly, to (be) compact; by implication, to hoard. In the KJV it is rendered: lay up.
H2631: (Aramaic) corresponding to חָסַן; to hold in occupancy. In the KJV it is rendered: possess.
H2632: (Aramaic) from חֲסַן; strength. In the KJV it is rendered: power.
H2633: From חָסַן; wealth. In the KJV it is rendered: riches, strength, treasure.
H2634: From חָסַן; powerful. In the KJV it is rendered: strong.
H2635: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of מְחֻסְפָּס; a clod. In the KJV it is rendered: clay.
H2636: Reduplicated from an unused root meaning apparently to peel; a shred or scale. In the KJV it is rendered: round thing.
H2637: A primitive root; to lack; by implication, to fail, want, lessen. In the KJV it is rendered: be abated, bereave, decrease, (cause to) fail, (have) lack, make lower, want.
H2638: From חָסֵר; lacking; hence, without. In the KJV it is rendered: destitute, fail, lack, have need, void, want.
H2639: From חָסֵר; lack; hence, destitution. In the KJV it is rendered: poverty, want.
H2640: From חָסֵר; poverty. In the KJV it is rendered: in want of.
H2641: From חָסֵר; want. In the KJV it is rendered: Chasrah, an Israelite:--Hasrah.
H2642: From חָסֵר; deficiency. In the KJV it is rendered: wanting.
H2643: From חָפַף (in the moral sense of covered from soil); pure. In the KJV it is rendered: innocent.
H2644: An orthographical variation of חָפָה; properly, to cover, i.e. (in a sinister sense) to act covertly. In the KJV it is rendered: do secretly.
H2645: A primitive root (compare חָפָא, חָפַף); to cover; by implication, to veil, to encase, protect. In the KJV it is rendered: ceil, cover, overlay.
H2646: From חָפָה; a canopy. In the KJV it is rendered: chamber, closet, defence.
H2647: The same as חֻפָּה; Chuppah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Huppah.
H2648: A primitive root; properly, to start up suddenly, i.e. (by implication) to hasten away, to fear. In the KJV it is rendered: (make) haste (away), tremble.
H2649: From חֻלְדָּה; hasty flight. In the KJV it is rendered: haste.
H2650: Plural of חֻפָּה (compare חוּפָם); Chuppim, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Huppim.
H2651: From an unused root of uncertain signification; a fist (only in the dual). In the KJV it is rendered: fists, (both) hands, hand(-ful).
H2652: From חָפְנַ֫יִם; perhaps pugilist; Chophni, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hophni.
H2653: A primitive root (compare חָפָה, יָחֵף); to cover (in protection). In the KJV it is rendered: cover.
H2654: A primitive root; properly, to incline to; by implication (literally but rarely) to bend; figuratively, to be pleased with, desire. In the KJV it is rendered: X any at all, (have, take) delight, desire, favour, like, move, be (well) pleased, have pleasure, will, would.
H2655: From חָפֵץ; pleased with. In the KJV it is rendered: delight in, desire, favour, please, have pleasure, whosoever would, willing, wish.
H2656: From חָפֵץ; pleasure; hence (abstractly) desire; concretely, a valuable thing; hence (by extension) a matter (as something in mind). In the KJV it is rendered: acceptable, delight(-some), desire, things desired, matter, pleasant(-ure), purpose, willingly.
H2657: From חֵ֫פֶץ with suffixes; my delight (is) in her; Cheptsi-bah, a fanciful name for Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hephzi-bah.
H2658: A primitive root; properly, to pry into; by implication, to delve, to explore. In the KJV it is rendered: dig, paw, search out, seek.
H2659: A primitive root (perhaps rath. the same as חָפַר through the idea of detection): to blush; figuratively, to be ashamed, disappointed; causatively, to shame, reproach. In the KJV it is rendered: be ashamed, be confounded, be brought to confusion (unto shame), come (be put to) shame, bring reproach.
H2660: From חָפַר or חָפֵר; a pit of shame; Chepher, a place in Palestine; also the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hepher.
H2661: From חָפַר; a hole; only in connection with פֵּרוֹת, which ought rather to be joined as one word, thus chapharperah; by reduplication from חָפַר; a burrower, i.e. probably a rat. In the KJV it is rendered: + mole.
H2662: Patronymically from חֵ֫פֶר; a Chephrite (collectively) or descendants of Chepher. In the KJV it is rendered: Hepherites.
H2663: Dual of חֵ֫פֶר; double pit; Chapharajim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Haphraim.
H2664: A primitive root; to seek; causatively, to conceal oneself (i.e. let be sought), or mask. In the KJV it is rendered: change, (make) diligent (search), disquise self, hide, search (for, out).
H2665: From חָפַשׂ; something covert, i.e. a trick. In the KJV it is rendered: search.
H2666: A primitive root; to spread loose; figuratively, to manumit. In the KJV it is rendered: be free.
H2667: From חָפַשׁ; something spread loosely, i.e. a carpet. In the KJV it is rendered: precious.
H2668: From חָפַשׁ; liberty (from slavery). In the KJV it is rendered: freedom.
H2669: And chophshiyth; from חָפַשׁ; prostration by sickness (with בָּ֫יִת, a hospital). In the KJV it is rendered: several.
H2670: From חָפַשׁ; exempt (from bondage, tax or care). In the KJV it is rendered: free, liberty.
H2671: From חָצַץ; properly, a piercer, i.e. an arrow; by implication, a wound; figuratively, (of God) thunder-bolt; (by interchange for עֵץ) the shaft of a spear. In the KJV it is rendered: + archer, arrow, dart, shaft, staff, wound.
H2672: Or chatseb; a primitive root; to cut or carve (wood), stone or other material); by implication, to hew, split, square, quarry, engrave. In the KJV it is rendered: cut, dig, divide, grave, hew (out, -er), made, mason.
H2673: A primitive root (compare זֵד)); to cut or split in two; to halve:--divide, X live out half, reach to the midst, participle.
H2674: A collective form of חָצֵר; village; Chatsor, the name (thus simply) of two places in Palestine and of one in Arabia. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazor.
H2675: From חָצוֹר and a Aramaizing form of the feminine of חָדָשׁ (compare חֲדַת); new Chatsor, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazor, Hadattah (as if two places).
H2676: From חָצָה; the middle (of the night). In the KJV it is rendered: mid(-night).
H2677: From חָצָה; the half or middle. In the KJV it is rendered: half, middle, mid(-night), midst, part, two parts.
H2678: Or chetsiy; prolongation from חֵץ; an arrow. In the KJV it is rendered: arrow.
H2679: From חֵ֫צִי and the plural of מְנוּחָה, with the article interposed; midst of the resting- places; Chatsi-ham-Menuchoth, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: half of the Manahethites.
H2680: Patronymically from חֲצִי הַמְּנֻחוֹת; a Chatsi-ham-Menachtite or descendant of Chatsi-ham-Menuchoth. In the KJV it is rendered: half of the Manahethites.
H2681: A collateral form of חָצֵר; a court or abode. In the KJV it is rendered: court.
H2682: Perhaps originally the same as חָצִיר, from the greenness of a courtyard; grass; also a leek (collectively). In the KJV it is rendered: grass, hay, herb, leek.
H2683: From an unused root meaning to hold firmly; the bosom (as comprised between the arms). In the KJV it is rendered: bosom.
H2684: A collateral form of חֵ֫צֶן, and meaning the same. In the KJV it is rendered: arm, lap.
H2685: (Aramaic) a primitive root; properly, to shear or cut close; figuratively, to be severe. In the KJV it is rendered: hasty, be urgent.
H2686: A primitive root (compare חָצָה); properly, to chop into, pierce or sever; hence, to curtail, to distribute (into ranks); as denom. from חֵץ, to shoot an arrow. In the KJV it is rendered: archer, X bands, cut off in the midst.
H2687: From חָצָץ; properly, something cutting; hence, gravel (as grit); also (like חֵץ) an arrow. In the KJV it is rendered: arrow, gravel (stone).
H2688: Or Chatsatson Tamar; from חָצַץ and תָּמָר; division (i.e. perhaps row) of (the) palm-tree; Chatsetson-tamar, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazezon- tamar.
H2689: By reduplication from חָצַר; a trumpet (from its sundered or quavering note). In the KJV it is rendered: trumpet(-er).
H2690: A primitive root; properly, to surround with a stockade, and thus separate from the open country; but used only in the reduplicated form chatsotser; or (2 Chronicles 5:12) chatsorer; as dem. from NONE; to trumpet, i.e. blow on that instrument. In the KJV it is rendered: blow, sound, trumpeter.
H2691: (masculine and feminine); from חָצַר in its original sense; a yard (as inclosed by a fence); also a hamlet (as similarly surrounded with walls). In the KJV it is rendered: court, tower, village.
H2692: From חָצֵר and אַדָּר; (the) village of Addar; Chatsar-Addar, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazar-addar.
H2693: From חָצֵר and a feminine of גַּד; (the) village of (female) Fortune; Chatsar-Gaddah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazar-gaddah.
H2694: From חָצֵר and תִּיכוֹן with the article interposed; village of the middle; Chatsar-hat-Tikon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazar-hatticon.
H2695: By an orthographical variation for חֶצְרוֹן; enclosure; Chetsro, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hezro, Hezrai.
H2696: From חָצֵר; court-yard; Chetsron, the name of a place in Palestine; also of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hezron.
H2697: Patronymically from חֶצְרוֹן; a Chetsronite or (collectively) descendants of Chetsron. In the KJV it is rendered: Hezronites.
H2698: Feminine plural of חָצֵר; yards; Chatseroth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazeroth.
H2699: Plural masculine of חָצֵר; yards; Chatserim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazerim.
H2700: From חָצֵר and מָ֫וֶת; village of death; Chatsarmaveth, a place in Arabia. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazarmaveth.
H2701: From חָצֵר and סוּסָה; village of cavalry; Chatsar-Susah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazar-susah.
H2702: From חָצֵר and the plural of סוּס; village of horses; Chatsar-Susim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazar- susim.
H2703: From חָצֵר and a derivative of עַ֫יִן; village of springs; Chatsar-Enon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazar- enon.
H2704: From חָצֵר and the same as עֵינָן; village of springs; Chatsar-Enan, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazar-enan.
H2705: From חָצֵר and שׁוּעָל; village of (the) fox; Chatsar-Shual, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hazar-shual.
H2706: From חָקַק; an enactment; hence, an appointment (of time, space, quantity, labor or usage). In the KJV it is rendered: appointed, bound, commandment, convenient, custom, decree(-d), due, law, measure, X necessary, ordinance(- nary), portion, set time, statute, task.
H2707: A primitive root; to carve; by implication, to delineate; also to entrench. In the KJV it is rendered: carved work, portrayed, set a print.
H2708: Feminine of חֹק, and meaning substantially the same. In the KJV it is rendered: appointed, custom, manner, ordinance, site, statute.
H2709: From an unused root probably meaning to bend; crooked; Chakupha, one of the Nethinim. In the KJV it is rendered: Hakupha.
H2710: A primitive root; properly, to hack, i.e. engrave (Judges 5:14, to be a scribe simply); by implication, to enact (laws being cut in stone or metal tablets in primitive times) or (gen.) prescribe. In the KJV it is rendered: appoint, decree, governor, grave, lawgiver, note, pourtray, print, set.
H2711: From חָקַק; an enactment, a resolution. In the KJV it is rendered: decree, thought.
H2712: Or (fully) Chuwqoq; from חָקַק; appointed; Chukkok or Chukok, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hukkok, Hukok.
H2713: A primitive root; properly, to penetrate; hence, to examine intimately. In the KJV it is rendered: find out, (make) search (out), seek (out), sound, try.
H2714: From חָקַר; examination, enumeration, deliberation. In the KJV it is rendered: finding out, number, (un-)search(-able, -ed, out, -ing).
H2715: Or (fully) chowr; from חָרַר; properly, white or pure (from the cleansing or shining power of fire (compare חֹרִי); hence (figuratively) noble (in rank). In the KJV it is rendered: noble.
H2716: From an unused (and vulgar) root probably meaning to evacuate the bowels: excrement; -dung. Also chariy.
H2717: Or chareb; a primitive root; to parch (through drought) i.e. (by analogy,) to desolate, destroy, kill. In the KJV it is rendered: decay, (be) desolate, destroy(-er), (be) dry (up), slay, X surely, (lay, lie, make) waste.
H2718: (Aramaic) a root corresponding to חָרַב; to demolish. In the KJV it is rendered: destroy.
H2719: From חָרַב; drought; also a cutting instrument (from its destructive effect), as a knife, sword, or other sharp implement. In the KJV it is rendered: axe, dagger, knife, mattock, sword, tool.
H2720: From חָרַב; parched or ruined. In the KJV it is rendered: desolate, dry, waste.
H2721: A collaterally form of חָ֫רֶב; drought or desolation. In the KJV it is rendered: desolation, drought, dry, heat, X utterly, waste.
H2722: From חָרַב; desolate; Choreb, a (generic) name for the Sinaitic mountains. In the KJV it is rendered: Horeb.
H2723: Feminine of חֹ֫רֶב; properly, drought, i.e. (by implication) a desolation. In the KJV it is rendered: decayed place, desolate (place, -tion), destruction, (laid) waste (place).
H2724: Feminine of חָרֵב; a desert. In the KJV it is rendered: dry (ground, land).
H2725: From חָרַב; parching heat. In the KJV it is rendered: drought.
H2726: Or Charbownah; of Persian origin; Charbona or Charbonah, a eunuch of Xerxes. In the KJV it is rendered: Harbona, Harbonah.
H2727: A primitive root; properly, to leap suddenly, i.e. (by implication) to be dismayed. In the KJV it is rendered: be afraid.
H2728: From חָרַג; the leaping insect, i.e. a locust. In the KJV it is rendered: beetle.
H2729: A primitive root; to shudder with terror; hence, to fear; also to hasten (with anxiety). In the KJV it is rendered: be (make) afraid, be careful, discomfit, fray (away), quake, tremble.
H2730: From חָרַד; fearful; also reverential. In the KJV it is rendered: afraid, trembling.
H2731: Feminine of חָרֵד; fear, anxiety. In the KJV it is rendered: care, X exceedingly, fear, quaking, trembling.
H2732: The same as חֲרָדָה; Charadah, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Haradah.
H2733: Patrial from a derivative of חָרַד (compare עֵין חֲרֹד); a Charodite, or inhabitant of Charod. In the KJV it is rendered: Harodite.
H2734: A primitive root (compare חָרַר); to glow or grow warm; figuratively (usually) to blaze up, of anger, zeal, jealousy. In the KJV it is rendered: be angry, burn, be displeased, X earnestly, fret self, grieve, be (wax) hot, be incensed, kindle, X very, be wroth.
H2735: From חֹר and a collateral (masculine) form of גֻּדְגֹּ֫דָה, with the article interposed; hole of the cleft: Chor-hag-Gidgad, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Hor-hagidgad.
H2736: From חָרָה and יָהּ; fearing Jah; Charhajah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Harhaiah.
H2737: From an unused root meaning to perforate; properly, pierced, i.e. a bead of pearl, gems or jewels (as strung). In the KJV it is rendered: chain.
H2738: Or (shortened) charul; apparently, a passive participle of an unused root probably meaning to be prickly; properly, pointed, i.e. a bramble or other thorny weed: nettle.
H2739: From passive participle of חָרַם and אַף; snub-nosed; Charumaph, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Harumaph.
H2740: Or (shortened) charon; from חָרָה; a burning of anger. In the KJV it is rendered: sore displeasure, fierce(-ness), fury, (fierce) wrath(-ful).
H2741: A patrial from (probably) a collateral form of חָרִיף; a Charuphite or inhabitant of Charuph (or Chariph). In the KJV it is rendered: Haruphite.
H2742: Or charuts; passive participle of חָרַץ; properly, incised or (active) incisive; hence (as noun masculine or feminine) a trench (as dug), gold (as mined), a threshing-sledge (having sharp teeth); (figuratively) determination; also eager. In the KJV it is rendered: decision, diligent, (fine) gold, pointed things, sharp, threshing instrument, wall.
H2743: The same as חָרוּץ; earnest; Charuts, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Haruz.
H2744: A fuller form of חַרְחֻר; inflammation; Charchur, one of the Nethinim. In the KJV it is rendered: Harhur.
H2745: From the same as חָ֫רֶס; perhaps shining; Charchas, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Harhas.
H2747: From a primitive root meaning to engrave; a chisel or graver; also a style for writing. In the KJV it is rendered: graving tool, pen.
H2748: From the same as חֶ֫רֶט; a horoscopist (as drawing magical lines or circles). In the KJV it is rendered: magician.
H2749: (Aramaic) the same as חַרְטֹם. In the KJV it is rendered: magician.
H2750: From חָרָה; a burning (i.e. intense) anger. In the KJV it is rendered: fierce, X great, heat.
H2751: From the same as חוּר; white bread. In the KJV it is rendered: white.
H2752: From חֹר; cave-dweller or troglodyte; a Chorite or aboriginal Idumaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Horims, Horites.
H2753: Or Chowriy; the same as חֹרִי; Chori, the name of two men. In the KJV it is rendered: Hori.
H2754: Or charit; from the same as חֶ֫רֶט; properly, cut out (or hollow), i.e. (by implication) a pocket. In the KJV it is rendered: bag, crisping pin.
H2755: From the plural of חַרְאֵי and the plural of יוֹנִים; excrements of doves, or perhaps rather the plural of a single word charapyown; of similar or uncertain derivation, probably a kind of vegetable. In the KJV it is rendered: doves' dung.
H2756: From חָרַף; autumnal; Chariph, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hariph.
H2757: Or charits; from חָרַץ; properly, incisure or (passively) incised (compare חָרוּץ); hence, a threshing-sledge (with sharp teeth): also a slice (as cut). In the KJV it is rendered: + cheese, harrow.
H2758: From חָרַשׁ; ploughing or its season. In the KJV it is rendered: earing (time), ground.
H2759: From חָרַשׁ in the sense of silence; quiet, i.e. sultry (as feminine noun, the sirocco or hot east wind). In the KJV it is rendered: vehement.
H2760: A primitive root; to braid (i.e. to entangle or snare) or catch (game) in a net. In the KJV it is rendered: roast.
H2761: (Aramaic) a root probably allied to the equivalent of חָרַר; to scorch. In the KJV it is rendered: singe.
H2762: From חָרַך; properly, a net, i.e. (by analogy) lattice. In the KJV it is rendered: lattice.
H2763: A primitive root; to seclude; specifically (by a ban) to devote to religious uses (especially destruction); physical and reflexive, to be blunt as to the nose. In the KJV it is rendered: make accursed, consecrate, (utterly) destroy, devote, forfeit, have a flat nose, utterly (slay, make away).
H2764: Or (Zecheriah 14:11) cherem; from חָרַם; physical (as shutting in) a net (either literally or figuratively); usually a doomed object; abstr. extermination. In the KJV it is rendered: (ac-)curse(-d, -d thing), dedicated thing, things which should have been utterly destroyed, (appointed to) utter destruction, devoted (thing), net.
H2765: From חָרַם; devoted; Chorem, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Horem.
H2766: From חָרַם; snub-nosed; Charim, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Harim.
H2767: From חָרַם; devoted; Chormah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hormah.
H2768: From חָרַם; abrupt; Chermon, a mount of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hermon.
H2769: Plural of חֶרְמוֹן; Hermons, i.e. its peaks. In the KJV it is rendered: the Hermonites.
H2770: From חָרַם; a sickle (as cutting). In the KJV it is rendered: sickle.
H2771: From חָרַר; parched; Charan, the name of a man and also of a place. In the KJV it is rendered: Haran.
H2772: Patrial from חֹרוֹנָ֫יִם; a Choronite or inhabitant of Choronaim. In the KJV it is rendered: Horonite.
H2773: Dual of a derivative from חֹר; double cave-town; Choronajim, a place in Moab. In the KJV it is rendered: Horonaim.
H2774: Of uncertain derivation; Charnepher, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Harnepher.
H2775: From an unused root meaning to scrape; the itch; also (perhaps from the mediating idea of חַרְסוּת) the sun. In the KJV it is rendered: itch, sun.
H2776: The same as חָ֫רֶס; shining; Cheres, a mountain in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Heres.
H2777: From חָ֫רֶס (apparently in the sense of a red tile used for scraping); a potsherd, i.e. (by implication) a pottery; the name of a gate at Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: east.
H2778: A primitive root; to pull off, i.e. (by implication) to expose (as by stripping); specifically, to betroth (as if a surrender); figuratively, to carp at, i.e. defame; denominative (from חֹ֫רֶף) to spend the winter. In the KJV it is rendered: betroth, blaspheme, defy, jeopard, rail, reproach, upbraid.
H2779: From חָרַף; properly, the crop gathered, i.e. (by implication) the autumn (and winter) season; figuratively, ripeness of age. In the KJV it is rendered: cold, winter (-house), youth.
H2780: From חָרַף; reproachful; Chareph, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hareph.
H2781: From חָרַף; contumely, disgrace, the pudenda. In the KJV it is rendered: rebuke, reproach(-fully), shame.
H2782: A primitive root; properly, to point sharply, i.e. (literally) to wound; figuratively, to be alert, to decide. In the KJV it is rendered: bestir self, decide, decree, determine, maim, move.
H2783: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to חָרַץ in the sense of vigor; the loin (as the seat of strength). In the KJV it is rendered: loin.
H2784: Of uncertain derivation; a fetter; figuratively, a pain. In the KJV it is rendered: band.
H2785: From חָרַץ; a sour grape (as sharp in taste). In the KJV it is rendered: kernel.
H2786: A primitive root; to grate the teeth. In the KJV it is rendered: gnash.
H2787: A primitive root; to glow, i.e. literally (to melt, burn, dry up) or figuratively (to show or incite passion. In the KJV it is rendered: be angry, burn, dry, kindle.
H2788: From חָרַר; arid. In the KJV it is rendered: parched place.
H2789: A collateral form mediating between חָ֫רֶס and חֶ֫רֶשׁ; a piece of pottery. In the KJV it is rendered: earth(-en), (pot-)sherd, + stone.
H2790: A primitive root; to scratch, i.e. (by implication) to engrave, plough; hence (from the use of tools) to fabricate (of any material); figuratively, to devise (in a bad sense); hence (from the idea of secrecy) to be silent, to let alone; hence (by implication) to be deaf (as an accompaniment of dumbness). In the KJV it is rendered: X altogether, cease, conceal, be deaf, devise, ear, graven, imagine, leave off speaking, hold peace, plow(-er, man), be quiet, rest, practise secretly, keep silence, be silent, speak not a word, be still, hold tongue, worker.
H2791: From חָרַשׁ; magical craft; also silence. In the KJV it is rendered: cunning, secretly.
H2792: The same as חֶ֫רֶשׁ. In the KJV it is rendered: Cheresh, a Levite:--Heresh.
H2793: From חָרַשׁ; a forest (perhaps as furnishing the material for fabric). In the KJV it is rendered: bough, forest, shroud, wood.
H2794: Active participle of חָרַשׁ; a fabricator or mechanic. In the KJV it is rendered: artificer.
H2795: From חָרַשׁ; deaf (whether literally or spir.). In the KJV it is rendered: deaf.
H2796: From חָרַשׁ; a fabricator or any material. In the KJV it is rendered: artificer, (+) carpenter, craftsman, engraver, maker, + mason, skilful, (+) smith, worker, workman, such as wrought.
H2797: From חֶ֫רֶשׁ; magician; Charsha, one of the Nethinim. In the KJV it is rendered: Harsha.
H2798: Plural of חָרָשׁ; mechanics, the name of a valley in Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: Charashim, craftsmen.
H2799: From חָרַשׁ; mechanical work. In the KJV it is rendered: carving, cutting.
H2800: The same as חֲרֹ֫שֶׁת; Charosheth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Harosheth.
H2801: A primitive root; to engrave. In the KJV it is rendered: graven.
H2802: From חָרַת (but equivalent to חֹ֫רֶשׁ); forest; Chereth, a thicket in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hereth.
H2803: A primitive root; properly, to plait or interpenetrate, i.e. (literally) to weave or (gen.) to fabricate; figuratively, to plot or contrive (usually in a malicious sense); hence (from the mental effort) to think, regard, value, compute. In the KJV it is rendered: (make) account (of), conceive, consider, count, cunning (man, work, workman), devise, esteem, find out, forecast, hold, imagine, impute, invent, be like, mean, purpose, reckon(-ing be made), regard, think.
H2804: (Aramaic) corresponding to חָשַׁב; to regard. In the KJV it is rendered: repute.
H2805: From חָשַׁב; a belt or strap (as being interlaced). In the KJV it is rendered: curious girdle.
H2806: From חָשַׁב and דִּין; considerate judge; Chasbaddanah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hasbadana.
H2807: From חָשַׁב; estimation; Cashubah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hashubah.
H2808: From חָשַׁב; properly, contrivance; by implication, intelligence. In the KJV it is rendered: account, device, reason.
H2809: The same as חֶשְׁבּוֹן; Cheshbon, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Heshbon.
H2810: From חָשַׁב; a contrivance, i.e. actual (a warlike machine) or mental (a machination). In the KJV it is rendered: engine, invention.
H2811: Or Chashabyahuw; from חָשַׁב and יָהּ; Jah has regarded; Chashabjah, the name of nine Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hashabiah.
H2812: Feminine of חֶשְׁבּוֹן; inventiveness; Chashnah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hashabnah.
H2813: From חֶשְׁבּוֹן and יָהּ; thought of Jah; Chashabnejah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hashabniah.
H2814: A primitive root; to hush or keep quiet. In the KJV it is rendered: hold peace, keep silence, be silent, (be) still.
H2815: From חָשַׁב; intelligent; Chashshub, the name of two or three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hashub, Hasshub.
H2816: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to חָשַׁך; the dark. In the KJV it is rendered: darkness.
H2817: Or Chasuphao; from חָשַׂף; nakedness; Chasupha, one of the Nethinim. In the KJV it is rendered: Hashupha, Hasupha.
H2818: (Aramaic) a collateral root to one corresponding to חוּשׁ in the sense of readiness; to be necessary (from the idea of convenience) or (transitively) to need. In the KJV it is rendered: careful, have need of.
H2819: From a root corresponding to חֲשַׁח; necessity. In the KJV it is rendered: be needful.
H2820: A primitive root; to restrain or (reflex.) refrain; by implication, to refuse, spare, preserve; also (by interch. with חָשַׁך) to observe. In the KJV it is rendered: assuage, X darken, forbear, hinder, hold back, keep (back), punish, refrain, reserve, spare, withhold.
H2821: A primitive root; to be dark (as withholding light); transitively, to darken. In the KJV it is rendered: be black, be (make) dark, darken, cause darkness, be dim, hide.
H2822: From חָשַׁך; the dark; hence (literally) darkness; figuratively, misery, destruction, death, ignorance, sorrow, wickedness. In the KJV it is rendered: dark(-ness), night, obscurity.
H2824: From חָשַׁך; darkness. In the KJV it is rendered: dark.
H2825: Or chashekah; from חָשַׁך; darkness; figuratively, misery. In the KJV it is rendered: darkness.
H2826: A primitive root; to make (intrans. be) unsteady, i.e. weak. In the KJV it is rendered: feeble.
H2827: (Aramaic) a root corresponding to חָשַׁל; to weaken, i.e. crush. In the KJV it is rendered: subdue.
H2828: From the same as חַשְׁמַנִּים; enriched; Chashum, the name of two or three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hashum.
H2829: The same as חַשְׁמַנִּים; opulent; Cheshmon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Heshmon.
H2830: Of uncertain derivation; probably bronze or polished spectrum metal. In the KJV it is rendered: amber.
H2831: From an unused root (probably meaning firm or capacious in resources); apparently wealthy. In the KJV it is rendered: princes.
H2832: Feminine of חַשְׁמַנִּים; fertile; Chasmonah, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Hashmonah.
H2833: From an unused root probably meaning to contain or sparkle; perhaps a pocket (as holding the Urim and Thummim), or rich (as containing gems), used only of the gorget of the highpriest. In the KJV it is rendered: breastplate.
H2834: A primitive root; to strip off, i.e. generally to make naked (for exertion or in disgrace), to drain away or bail up (a liquid). In the KJV it is rendered: make bare, clean, discover, draw out, take, uncover.
H2835: From חָשַׂף; properly, drawn off, i.e. separated; hence, a small company (as divided from the rest). In the KJV it is rendered: little flock.
H2836: A primitive root; to cling, i.e. join, (figuratively) to love, delight in; elliptically (or by interchangeable for חָשַׂך) to deliver. In the KJV it is rendered: have a delight, (have a) desire, fillet, long, set (in) love.
H2837: From חָשַׁק; delight. In the KJV it is rendered: desire, pleasure.
H2838: Or chashuwq; past participle of חָשַׁק; attached, i.e. a fence-rail or rod connecting the posts or pillars. In the KJV it is rendered: fillet.
H2839: From חָשַׁק; conjoined, i.e. a wheel-spoke or rod connecting the hub with the rim. In the KJV it is rendered: felloe.
H2840: From an unused root meaning to bind together; combined, i.e. the nave or hub of a wheel (as holding the spokes together). In the KJV it is rendered: spoke.
H2841: From the same as חִשֻּׁרֵי; properly, a combination or gathering, i.e. of watery clouds. In the KJV it is rendered: dark.
H2842: By variation for קָשׁ; dry grass. In the KJV it is rendered: chaff.
H2843: Patronymically from חוּשָׁה; a Chushathite or descendant of Chushah. In the KJV it is rendered: Hushathite.
H2844: From חָתַת; concretely, crushed; also afraid; abstractly, terror. In the KJV it is rendered: broken, dismayed, dread, fear.
H2845: From חָתַת; terror; Cheth, an aboriginal Canaanite. In the KJV it is rendered: Heth.
H2846: A primitive root; to lay hold of; especially to pick up fire. In the KJV it is rendered: heap, take (away).
H2847: From חָתַת; fear. In the KJV it is rendered: terror.
H2848: From חָתַל; swathed, i.e. a bandage. In the KJV it is rendered: roller.
H2849: From חָת; terror. In the KJV it is rendered: fear.
H2850: Patronymically from חֵת; a Chittite, or descendant of Cheth. In the KJV it is rendered: Hittite, Hittities.
H2851: From חָתַת; fear. In the KJV it is rendered: terror.
H2852: A primitive root; properly, to cut off, i.e. (figuratively) to decree. In the KJV it is rendered: determine.
H2853: A primitive root; to swathe. In the KJV it is rendered: X at all, swaddle.
H2854: From חָתַל; a swathing cloth (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: swaddling band.
H2855: From חָתַל; enswathed; Chethlon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hethlon.
H2856: A primitive root; to close up; especially to seal. In the KJV it is rendered: make an end, mark, seal (up), stop.
H2857: (Aramaic) a root corresponding to חָתַם; to seal. In the KJV it is rendered: seal.
H2858: Feminine active participle of חָתַם; a seal. In the KJV it is rendered: signet.
H2859: A primitive root; to give (a daughter) away in marriage; hence (generally) to contract affinity by marriage. In the KJV it is rendered: join in affinity, father in law, make marriages, mother in law, son in law.
H2860: From חָתַן; a relative by marriage (especially through the bride); figuratively, a circumcised child (as a species of religious espousal). In the KJV it is rendered: bridegroom, husband, son in law.
H2861: From חָתַן; a wedding. In the KJV it is rendered: espousal.
H2862: A primitive root; to clutch. In the KJV it is rendered: take away.
H2863: From חָתַף; properly, rapine; figuratively, robbery. In the KJV it is rendered: prey.
H2864: A primitive root; to force a passage, as by burglary; figuratively, with oars. In the KJV it is rendered: dig (through), row.
H2865: A primitive root; properly, to prostrate; hence, to break down, either (literally) by violence, or (figuratively) by confusion and fear. In the KJV it is rendered: abolish, affright, be (make) afraid, amaze, beat down, discourage, (cause to) dismay, go down, scare, terrify.
H2866: From חָתַת; dismay. In the KJV it is rendered: casting down.
H2867: The same as חֲתַת; Chathath, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: cathath.
H2868: (Aramaic) a primitive root; to rejoice. In the KJV it is rendered: be glad.
H2869: (Aramaic) from טְאֵב; the same as טוֹב; good. In the KJV it is rendered: fine, good.
H2870: From טוֹב and אֵל; pleasing (to) God; Tabeel, the name of a Syrian and of a Persian. In the KJV it is rendered: Tabeal, Tabeel.
H2871: Passive participle of טָבַל; properly, dyed, i.e. a turban (probably as of colored stuff). In the KJV it is rendered: dyed attire.
H2872: From an unused root meaning to pile up; properly, accumulated; i.e. (by implication) a summit. In the KJV it is rendered: middle, midst.
H2873: A primitive root; to slaughter (animals or men). In the KJV it is rendered: kill, (make) slaughter, slay.
H2874: From טָבַח; properly, something slaughtered; hence, a beast (or meat, as butchered); abstr. butchery (or concretely, a place of slaughter). In the KJV it is rendered: X beast, slaughter, X slay, X sore.
H2875: The same as טָ֫בַח; massacre; Tebach, the name of a Mesopotamian and of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Tebah.
H2876: From טָבַח; properly, a butcher; hence, a lifeguardsman (because he was acting as an executioner); also a cook (usually slaughtering the animal for food). In the KJV it is rendered: cook, guard.
H2877: (Aramaic) the same as טַבָּח; a lifeguardsman. In the KJV it is rendered: guard.
H2878: Feminine of טָ֫בַח and meaning the same. In the KJV it is rendered: flesh, slaughter.
H2879: Feminine of טַבָּח; a female cook. In the KJV it is rendered: cook.
H2880: From טִבְחָה; slaughter; Tibchath, a place in Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Tibhath.
H2881: A primitive root; to dip, to immerse. In the KJV it is rendered: dip, plunge.
H2882: From טָבַל and יָהּ; Jah has dipped; Tebaljah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Tebaliah.
H2883: A primitive root; to sink. In the KJV it is rendered: drown, fasten, settle, sink.
H2884: Plural of טַבַּ֫עַת; rings; Tabbaoth, one of the Nethinim. In the KJV it is rendered: Tabaoth.
H2885: From טָבַע; properly, a seal (as sunk into the wax), i.e. signet (for sealing); hence (generally) a ring of any kind. In the KJV it is rendered: ring.
H2886: From טוֹב and רִמּוֹן; pleasing (to) Rimmon; Tabrimmon, a Syrian. In the KJV it is rendered: Tabrimmon.
H2887: Probably of foreign derivation; Tebeth, the tenth Heb. month. In the KJV it is rendered: Tebeth.
H2888: Of uncertain derivation; Tabbath, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Tabbath.
H2889: Or tahor; from טָהֵר; pure (in a physical, chemical, ceremonial or moral sense). In the KJV it is rendered: clean, fair, pure(-ness).
H2890: From טָהֵר; purity. In the KJV it is rendered: pureness.
H2891: A primitive root; properly, to be bright; i.e. (by implication) to be pure (physical sound, clear, unadulterated; Levitically, uncontaminated; morally, innocent or holy). In the KJV it is rendered: be (make, make self, pronounce) clean, cleanse (self), purge, purify(-ier, self).
H2892: From טָהֵר; literally brightness; ceremonially purification. In the KJV it is rendered: clearness, glory, purifying.
H2893: Feminine of טֹ֫הַר; ceremonial purification; moral purity. In the KJV it is rendered: X is cleansed, cleansing, purification(-fying).
H2894: A primitive root; to sweep away. In the KJV it is rendered: sweep.
H2895: A primitive root, to be (transitively, do or make) good (or well) in the widest sense. In the KJV it is rendered: be (do) better, cheer, be (do, seem) good, (make) goodly, X please, (be, do, go, play) well.
H2896: From טוֹב; good (as an adjective) in the widest sense; used likewise as a noun, both in the masculine and the feminine, the singular and the plural (good, a good or good thing, a good man or woman; the good, goods or good things, good men or women), also as an adverb (well). In the KJV it is rendered: beautiful, best, better, bountiful, cheerful, at ease, X fair (word), (be in) favour, fine, glad, good (deed, -lier, -liest, -ly, -ness, -s), graciously, joyful, kindly, kindness, liketh (best), loving, merry, X most, pleasant, + pleaseth, pleasure, precious, prosperity, ready, sweet, wealth, welfare, (be) well ((-favoured)).
H2897: The same as טוֹב; good; Tob, a region apparently East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Tob.
H2898: From טוֹב; good (as a noun), in the widest sense, especially goodness (superlative concretely, the best), beauty, gladness, welfare. In the KJV it is rendered: fair, gladness, good(-ness, thing, -s), joy, go well with.
H2899: From טוֹב and אֲדֹנִיָּה; pleasing (to) Adonijah; Tob-Adonijah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Tob-adonijah.
H2900: Or Towbiyahuw; from טוֹב and יָהּ; goodness of Jehovah; Tobijah, the name of three Israelites and of one Samaritan. In the KJV it is rendered: Tobiah, Tobijah.
H2901: A primitive root; to spin. In the KJV it is rendered: spin.
H2902: A primitive root; to smear, especially with lime. In the KJV it is rendered: daub, overlay, plaister, smut.
H2903: From an unusued root meaning to go around or bind; a fillet for the forehead. In the KJV it is rendered: frontlet.
H2904: A primitive root; to pitch over or reel; hence (transitively) to cast down or out. In the KJV it is rendered: carry away, (utterly) cast (down, forth, out), send out.
H2905: From an unused root meaning to range in a regular manner; a row; hence, a wall. In the KJV it is rendered: row.
H2906: (Aramaic) corresponding to צוּר; a rock or hill. In the KJV it is rendered: mountain.
H2907: A primitive root; to pounce as a bird of prey. In the KJV it is rendered: haste.
H2908: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to טָוָה; hunger (as twisting). In the KJV it is rendered: fasting.
H2909: A primitive root; to stretch a bow, as an archer. In the KJV it is rendered: (bow-)shot.
H2910: From טָחָה (or ט֫וּחַ) in the sense of overlaying; (in the plural only) the kidneys (as being covered); hence (figuratively) the inmost thought. In the KJV it is rendered: inward parts.
H2911: From טָחַן; a hand mill; hence, a millstone. In the KJV it is rendered: to grind.
H2912: A primitive root; to grind meal; hence, to be a concubine (that being their employment). In the KJV it is rendered: grind(-er).
H2913: From טָחַן; a hand mill; hence (figuratively) chewing. In the KJV it is rendered: grinding.
H2914: From an unused root meaning to burn; a boil or ulcer (from the inflammation), especially a tumor in the anus or pudenda (the piles). In the KJV it is rendered: emerod.
H2915: From (the equiv. of) ט֫וּחַ; mortar or plaster. In the KJV it is rendered: daubing.
H2916: From an unused root meaning apparently to be sticky (rath. perb. a demon. from טוּא, through the idea of dirt to be swept away); mud or clay; figuratively, calamity. In the KJV it is rendered: clay, dirt, mire.
H2917: (Aramaic) perhaps, by interchange, for a word corresponding to טִיט; clay. In the KJV it is rendered: miry.
H2918: Feminine of (an equivalent to) טוּר; a wall; hence, a fortress or a hamlet. In the KJV it is rendered: (goodly) castle, habitation, palace, row.
H2919: From טָלַל; dew (as covering vegetation). In the KJV it is rendered: dew.
H2920: (Aramaic) the same as טָל. In the KJV it is rendered: dew.
H2921: A primitive root; properly, to cover with pieces; i.e. (by implication) to spot or variegate (as tapestry). In the KJV it is rendered: clouted, with divers colours, spotted.
H2922: Apparently from טָלָא in the (orig.) sense of covering (for protection); a lamb (compare טָלֶה). In the KJV it is rendered: lamb.
H2923: From the plural of טְלָאּים; lambs; Telaim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Telaim.
H2924: By variation for טְלָאּים; a lamb. In the KJV it is rendered: lamb.
H2925: From טוּל; overthrow or rejection. In the KJV it is rendered: captivity.
H2926: A primitive root; properly, to strew over, i.e. (by implication) to cover in or plate (with beams). In the KJV it is rendered: cover.
H2927: (Aramaic) corresponding to טָלַל; to cover with shade. In the KJV it is rendered: have a shadow.
H2928: From an unused root meaning to break up or treat violently; oppression; Telem, the name of a place in Idumaea, also of a temple doorkeeper. In the KJV it is rendered: Telem.
H2929: From the same as NONE; oppressive; Talmon, a temple doorkeeper. In the KJV it is rendered: Talmon.
H2930: A primitive root; to be foul, especially in a ceremial or moral sense (contaminated). In the KJV it is rendered: defile (self), pollute (self), be (make, make self, pronounce) unclean, X utterly.
H2931: From טָמֵא; foul in a relig. sense. In the KJV it is rendered: defiled, + infamous, polluted(-tion), unclean.
H2932: From טָמֵא; religious impurity. In the KJV it is rendered: filthiness, unclean(-ness).
H2933: A collateral form of טָמֵא; to be impure in a religious sense. In the KJV it is rendered: be defiled, be reputed vile.
H2934: A primitive root; to hide (by covering over). In the KJV it is rendered: hide, lay privily, in secret.
H2935: From an unused root probably meaning to weave; a basket (of interlaced osiers). In the KJV it is rendered: basket.
H2936: A primitive root; to soil. In the KJV it is rendered: defile.
H2937: A primitive root; to wander;,causatively to lead astray. In the KJV it is rendered: seduce.
H2938: A primitive root; to taste; figuratively, to perceive. In the KJV it is rendered: X but, perceive, taste.
H2939: (Aramaic) corresponding to טָעַם; to taste; causatively to feed. In the KJV it is rendered: make to eat, feed.
H2940: From טָעַם; properly, a taste, i.e. (figuratively) perception; by implication, intelligence; transitively, a mandate. In the KJV it is rendered: advice, behaviour, decree, discretion, judgment, reason, taste, understanding.
H2941: (Aramaic) from טְעַם; properly, a taste, i.e. (as in טָ֫עַם) a judicial sentence. In the KJV it is rendered: account, X to be commanded, commandment, matter.
H2942: (Aramaic) from טְעַם, and equivalent to טַ֫עַם; properly, flavor; figuratively, judgment (both subjective and objective); hence, account (both subj. and obj.). In the KJV it is rendered: + chancellor, + command, commandment, decree, + regard, taste, wisdom.
H2943: A primitive root; to load a beast. In the KJV it is rendered: lade.
H2944: A primitive root; to stab. In the KJV it is rendered: thrust through.
H2945: From טָפַף (perhaps referring to the tripping gait of children); a family (mostly used collectively in the singular). In the KJV it is rendered: (little) children (ones), families.
H2946: A primitive root; to flatten out or extend (as a tent); figuratively, to nurse a child (as promotive of growth); or perhaps a denom. from טֶ֫פַח, from dandling on the palms. In the KJV it is rendered: span, swaddle.
H2947: From טָפַח; a spread of the hand, i.e. a palm- breadth (not "span" of the fingers); architecturally, a corbel (as a supporting palm). In the KJV it is rendered: coping, hand-breadth.
H2948: From טָפַח (the same as טֶ֫פַח). In the KJV it is rendered: hand-breadth (broad).
H2949: From טָפַח; nursing. In the KJV it is rendered: span long.
H2950: A primitive root; properly, to stick on as a patch; figuratively, to impute falsely. In the KJV it is rendered: forge(-r), sew up.
H2951: Of foreign derivation; a military governor. In the KJV it is rendered: captain.
H2952: A primitive root; apparently to trip (with short steps) coquettishly. In the KJV it is rendered: mince.
H2953: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to צָפַר, and meaning the same as צִפֹּ֫רֶן; a finger-nail; also a hoof or claw. In the KJV it is rendered: nail.
H2954: A primitive root; properly, apparently to be thick; figuratively, to be stupid. In the KJV it is rendered: be fat.
H2955: Probably from נָטַף; a dropping (of ointment); Taphath, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Taphath.
H2956: A primitive root; to drive on; figuratively, to follow close. In the KJV it is rendered: continual.
H2957: (Aramaic) corresponding to טָרַד; to expel. In the KJV it is rendered: drive.
H2958: A variation of טֶ֫רֶם; not yet. In the KJV it is rendered: before.
H2959: A primitive root; to overburden. In the KJV it is rendered: weary.
H2960: From טָרַח; a burden. In the KJV it is rendered: cumbrance, trouble.
H2961: From an unused root apparently meaning to be moist; properly, dripping; hence, fresh (i.e. recently made such). In the KJV it is rendered: new, putrefying.
H2962: From an unused root apparently meaning to interrupt or suspend; properly, non-occurrence; used adverbially, not yet or before. In the KJV it is rendered: before, ere, not yet.
H2963: A primitive root; to pluck off or pull to pieces; causatively to supply with food (as in morsels). In the KJV it is rendered: catch, X without doubt, feed, ravin, rend in pieces, X surely, tear (in pieces).
H2964: From טָרַף; something torn, i.e. a fragment, e.g. a fresh leaf, prey, food. In the KJV it is rendered: leaf, meat, prey, spoil.
H2965: From טָרַף; recently torn off, i.e. fresh. In the KJV it is rendered: pluckt off.
H2966: Feminine (collectively) of טָ֫רֶף; prey, i.e. flocks devoured by animals. In the KJV it is rendered: ravin, (that which was) torn (of beasts, in pieces).
H2967: (Aramaic) from a name of foreign derivation; a Tarpelite (collectively) or inhabitants of Tarpel, a place in Assyria. In the KJV it is rendered: Tarpelites.
H2968: A primitive root; to desire. In the KJV it is rendered: long.
H2969: A primitive root; to be suitable. In the KJV it is rendered: appertain.
H2970: Or Ya.azanyahuw; from הֶאֱזִין and יָהּ; heard of Jah; Jaazanjah, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jaazaniah.
H2971: From אוֹר; enlightener; Jair, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jair.
H2972: Patronymically from יָאּיר; a Jairite or descendant of Jair. In the KJV it is rendered: Jairite.
H2973: A primitive root; properly, to be slack, i.e. (figuratively) to be foolish. In the KJV it is rendered: dote, be (become, do) foolish(-ly).
H2974: A primitive root (probably rather the same as יָאַל through the idea of mental weakness); properly, to yield, especially assent; hence (pos.) to undertake as an act of volition. In the KJV it is rendered: assay, begin, be content, please, take upon, X willingly, would.
H2975: Of Egyptian origin; a channel, e.g. a fosse, canal, shaft; specifically the Nile, as the one river of Egypt, including its collateral trenches; also the Tigris, as the main river of Assyria. In the KJV it is rendered: brook, flood, river, stream.
H2976: A primitive root; to desist, i.e. (figuratively) to despond. In the KJV it is rendered: (cause to) despair, one that is desperate, be no hope.
H2977: From the same root as אָשְׁוִיֹּת and יָהּ; founded of Jah; Joshijah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Josiah.
H2978: From אָתָה; an entry. In the KJV it is rendered: entrance.
H2979: From the same as אֲתָרִים; stepping; Jeatherai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jeaterai.
H2980: A primitive root; to bawl. In the KJV it is rendered: cry out.
H2981: From יָבַל; produce, i.e. a crop or (figuratively) wealth. In the KJV it is rendered: fruit, increase.
H2982: From בּוּס; trodden, i.e. threshing-place; Jebus, the aboriginal name of Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: Jebus.
H2983: Patrial from יְבוּס; a Jebusite or inhabitant of Jebus. In the KJV it is rendered: Jebusite(-s).
H2984: From בָּחַר; choice; Jibchar, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ibhar.
H2985: From בִּין; intelligent; Jabin, the name of two Canaanitish kings. In the KJV it is rendered: Jabin.
H2986: A primitive root; properly, to flow; causatively, to bring (especially with pomp). In the KJV it is rendered: bring (forth), carry, lead (forth).
H2987: (Aramaic) corresponding to יָבַל; to bring. In the KJV it is rendered: bring, carry.
H2988: From יָבַל; a stream. In the KJV it is rendered: (water-)course, stream.
H2989: The same as יִבְלֵי; Jabal, an antediluvian. In the KJV it is rendered: Jabal.
H2990: From יָבַל; having running sores. In the KJV it is rendered: wen.
H2991: From בָּלַע and עָם; devouring people; Jibleam, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ibleam.
H2992: A primitive root of doubtful meaning; used only as a denominative from יָבָם; to marry a (deceased) brother's widow. In the KJV it is rendered: perform the duty of a husband's brother, marry.
H2993: From (the orig. of) יָבַם; a brother-in-law. In the KJV it is rendered: husband's brother.
H2994: Feminine participle of יָבַם; a sister-in-law. In the KJV it is rendered: brother's wife, sister in law.
H2995: From בָּנָה and אֵל: built of God; Jabneel, the name of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Jabneel.
H2996: From בָּנָה; a building; Jabneh, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Jabneh.
H2997: From בָּנָה and יָהּ; built of Jah; Jibnejah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ibneiah.
H2998: From בָּנָה and יָהּ; building of Jah; Jibnijah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ibnijah.
H2999: Probably from בָּקַק; pouring forth; Jabbok, a river east of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Jabbok.
H3000: From בָּרַך and יָהּ: blessed of Jah; Jeberekjah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jeberechiah.
H3001: A primitive root; to be ashamed, confused or disappointed; also (as failing) to dry up (as water) or wither (as herbage). In the KJV it is rendered: be ashamed, clean, be confounded, (make) dry (up), (do) shame(-fully), X utterly, wither (away).
H3002: From יָבֵשׁ; dry. In the KJV it is rendered: dried (away), dry.
H3003: The same as יָבֵשׁ (also Yabeysh; often with the addition of גִּלְעָד, i.e. Jabesh of Gilad); Jobesh, the name of an Israelite and of a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Jobesh ((-Gilead)).
H3004: From יָבֵשׁ; dry ground. In the KJV it is rendered: dry (ground, land).
H3005: From the same as בְּשָׂמִים; fragrant; Jibsam, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jibsam.
H3006: A variation of יַבָּשָׁה; dry ground. In the KJV it is rendered: dry land.
H3007: (Aramaic) corresponding to יַבָּ֫שֶׁת; dry land. In the KJV it is rendered: earth.
H3008: From גָּאַל; avenger; Jigal, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Igal, Igeal.
H3009: A primitive root; to dig or plow. In the KJV it is rendered: husbandman.
H3010: From יָגַב; a plowed field. In the KJV it is rendered: field.
H3011: Feminine from גָּבַהּ; hillock; Jogbehah, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Jogbehah.
H3012: From גָּדַל and יָהּ; magnified of Jah; Jigdaljah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Igdaliah.
H3013: A primitive root; to grieve. In the KJV it is rendered: afflict, cause grief, grieve, sorrowful, vex.
H3014: A primitive root (probably rather the same as יָגָה through the common idea of dissatisfaction); to push away; -be removed.
H3015: From יָגָה; affliction. In the KJV it is rendered: grief, sorrow.
H3016: From יָגֹר; fearful. In the KJV it is rendered: afraid, fearest.
H3017: Probably from גּוּר; a lodging; Jagur, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Jagur.
H3018: From יָגַע; toil; hence, a work, produce, property (as the result of labor). In the KJV it is rendered: labour, work.
H3019: From יָגַע; tired. In the KJV it is rendered: weary.
H3020: From גָּלָה; exiled; Jogli, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jogli.
H3021: A primitive root; properly, to gasp; hence, to be exhausted, to tire, to toil. In the KJV it is rendered: faint, (make to) labour, (be) weary.
H3022: From יָגַע; earnings (as the product of toil); -that which he laboured for.
H3023: From יָגַע; tired; hence (transitive) tiresome. In the KJV it is rendered: full of labour, weary.
H3024: Feminine of יְגִיעֵי; fatigue. In the KJV it is rendered: weariness.
H3025: A primitive root; to fear. In the KJV it is rendered: be afraid, fear.
H3026: (Aramaic) from a word derived from an unused root (meaning to gather) and a derivation of a root corresponding to שָׂהֲדִי; heap of the testimony; Jegar-Sahadutha, a cairn East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Jegar-Sahadutha.
H3027: A primitive word; a hand (the open one (indicating power, means, direction, etc.), in distinction from כָּף, the closed one); used (as noun, adverb, etc.) in a great variety of applications, both literally and figuratively, both proximate and remote (as follows). In the KJV it is rendered: (+ be) able, X about, + armholes, at, axletree, because of, beside, border, X bounty, + broad, (broken-)handed, X by, charge, coast, + consecrate, + creditor, custody, debt, dominion, X enough, + fellowship, force, X from, hand(-staves, -y work), X he, himself, X in, labour, + large, ledge, (left-)handed, means, X mine, ministry, near, X of, X order, ordinance, X our, parts, pain, power, X presumptuously, service, side, sore, state, stay, draw with strength, stroke, + swear, terror, X thee, X by them, X themselves, X thine own, X thou, through, X throwing, + thumb, times, X to, X under, X us, X wait on, (way-)side, where, + wide, X with (him, me, you), work, + yield, X yourselves.
H3028: (Aramaic) corresponding to יָד. In the KJV it is rendered: hand, power.
H3029: (Aramaic) corresponding to יָדָה; to praise. In the KJV it is rendered: (give) thank(-s).
H3030: Of uncertain derivation; Jidalah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Idalah.
H3031: From the same as דְּבָשׁ; perhaps honeyed; Jidbash, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Idbash.
H3032: A primitive root; properly, to handle (compare יָדָה), i.e. to throw, e.g. lots. In the KJV it is rendered: cast.
H3033: From יְדִיד; properly, affection; concretely, a darling object. In the KJV it is rendered: dearly beloved.
H3034: A primitive root; used only as denominative from יָד; literally, to use (i.e. hold out) the hand; physically, to throw (a stone, an arrow) at or away; especially to revere or worship (with extended hands); intensively, to bemoan (by wringing the hands). In the KJV it is rendered: cast (out), (make) confess(-ion), praise, shoot, (give) thank(-ful, -s, -sgiving).
H3035: From יָדָה; praised; Jiddo, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Iddo.
H3036: From יָדָה; thankful; Jadon, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jadon.
H3037: From יָדַע; knowing; Jaddua, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jaddua.
H3038: Or Yduthuwn; or Ydiythuwn; probably from יָדָה; laudatory; Jeduthun, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jeduthun.
H3039: From the same as דּוֹד; loved. In the KJV it is rendered: amiable, (well-)beloved, loves.
H3040: Feminine of יְדִיד; beloved; Jedidah, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Jedidah.
H3041: From יְדִיד and יָהּ; beloved of Jah; Jedidejah, a name of Solomon. In the KJV it is rendered: Jedidiah.
H3042: From יָדָה and יָהּ; praised of Jah; Jedajah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jedaiah.
H3043: From יָדַע and אֵל; knowing God; Jediael, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jediael.
H3044: From דָּלַף; tearful; Jidlaph, a Mesopotamian. In the KJV it is rendered: Jidlaph.
H3045: A primitive root; to know (properly, to ascertain by seeing); used in a great variety of senses, figuratively, literally, euphemistically and inferentially (including observation, care, recognition; and causatively, instruction, designation, punishment, etc.) (as follow). In the KJV it is rendered: acknowledge, acquaintance(-ted with), advise, answer, appoint, assuredly, be aware, (un-)awares, can(-not), certainly, comprehend, consider, X could they, cunning, declare, be diligent, (can, cause to) discern, discover, endued with, familiar friend, famous, feel, can have, be (ig-)norant, instruct, kinsfolk, kinsman, (cause to let, make) know, (come to give, have, take) knowledge, have (knowledge), (be, make, make to be, make self) known, + be learned, + lie by man, mark, perceive, privy to, X prognosticator, regard, have respect, skilful, shew, can (man of) skill, be sure, of a surety, teach, (can) tell, understand, have (understanding), X will be, wist, wit, wot.
H3046: (Aramaic) corresponding to יָדַע. In the KJV it is rendered: certify, know, make known, teach.
H3047: From יָדַע; knowing; Jada, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jada.
H3048: From יָדַע and יָהּ; Jah has known; Jedajah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jedaiah.
H3049: From יָדַע; properly, a knowing one; specifically, a conjurer; (by impl) a ghost. In the KJV it is rendered: wizard.
H3050: Contraction for יְהֹוָה, and meaning the same; Jah, the sacred name. In the KJV it is rendered: Jah, the Lord, most vehement.
H3051: A primitive root; to give (whether literal or figurative); generally, to put; imperatively (reflexive) come. In the KJV it is rendered: ascribe, bring, come on, give, go, set, take.
H3052: (Aramaic) corresponding to יָהַב; -deliver, give, lay, + prolong, pay, yield.
H3053: From יָהַב; properly, what is given (by Providence), i.e. a lot. In the KJV it is rendered: burden.
H3054: Denominative from a form corresponding to יְהוּד; to Judaize, i.e. become Jewish. In the KJV it is rendered: become Jews.
H3055: A briefer form of one corresponding to יְהוּד; Jehud, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehud.
H3056: Perhaps from a form corresponding to יְהוּד; Judaistic; Jehdai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehdai.
H3057: Feminine of יְהוּדִי; Jehudijah, a Jewess: -Jehudijah.
H3058: From יְהֹוָה and הוּא; Jehovah (is) He; Jehu, the name of five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehu.
H3059: From יְהֹוָה and אָחַז; Jehovah-seized; Jehoachaz, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehoahaz.
H3060: From יְהֹוָה and (perhaps) אֵשׁ; Jehovah-fired; Jehoash, the name of two Israelite kings. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehoash.
H3061: (Aramaic) contracted from a form corresponding to יְהוּדָה; properly, Judah, hence, Judaea. In the KJV it is rendered: Jewry, Judah, Judea.
H3062: (Aramaic) patrial from יְהוּד; a Jehudaite (or Judaite), i.e. Jew. In the KJV it is rendered: Jew.
H3063: From יָדָה; celebrated; Jehudah (or Judah), the name of five Israelites; also of the tribe descended from the first, and of its territory. In the KJV it is rendered: Judah.
H3064: Patronymically from יְהוּדָה; a Jehudite (i.e. Judaite or Jew), or descendant of Jehudah (i.e. Judah). In the KJV it is rendered: Jew.
H3065: The same as יְהוּדִי; Jehudi, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehudi.
H3066: Feminine of יְהוּדִי; the Jewish (used adverbially) language. In the KJV it is rendered: in the Jews' language.
H3067: The same as יְהוּדִית; Jewess; Jehudith, a Canaanitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Judith.
H3068: From הָיָה; (the) self-Existent or Eternal; Jehovah, Jewish national name of God. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehovah, the Lord.
H3069: A variation of יְהֹוָה (used after אֲדֹנָי, and pronounced by Jews as אֱלֹהִים, in order to prevent the repetition of the same sound, since they elsewhere pronounce יְהֹוָה as אֲדֹנָי). In the KJV it is rendered: God.
H3070: From יְהֹוָה and רָאָה; Jehovah will see (to it); Jehovah-Jireh, a symbolical name for Mount Moriah. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehovah- jireh.
H3071: From יְהֹוָה and נֵס with the prononimal suffix; Jehovah (is) my banner; Jehovah-Nissi, a symbolical name of an altar in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehovah-nissi.
H3072: From יְהֹוָה and צֶ֫דֶק with pronominal suffix; Jehovah (is) our right; Jehovah-Tsidkenu, a symbolical epithet of the Messiah and of Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: the Lord our righteousness.
H3073: From יְהֹוָה and שָׁלוֹם; Jehovah (is) peace; Jehovah-Shalom, a symbolical name of an altar in Palestine: -Jehovah-shalom.
H3074: From יְהֹוָה and שָׁם with directive enclitic; Jehovah (is) thither; Jehovah-Shammah, a symbolic title of Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehovah-shammah.
H3075: From יְהֹוָה and זָבַד; Jehovah-endowed; Jehozabad, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehozabad.
H3076: From יְהֹוָה and חָנַן; Jehovah-favored; Jehochanan, the name of eight Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehohanan, Johanan.
H3077: From יְהֹוָה and יָדַע; Jehovah-known; Jehojada, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehoiada.
H3078: From יְהֹוָה and כּוּן; Jehovah will establish; Jehojakin, a Jewish king. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehoiachin.
H3079: From יְהֹוָה abbreviated and קוּם; Jehovah will raise; Jehojakim, a Jewish king. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehoiakim.
H3080: From יְהֹוָה and רִיב; Jehovah will contend; Jehojarib, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehoiarib.
H3081: From יָכֹל; potent; Jehukal, an Israelite: -Jehucal. Compare יוּכַל.
H3082: From יְהֹוָה and נָדַב; Jehovah-largessed; Jehonadab, the name of an Israelite and of an Arab. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehonadab, Jonadab.
H3083: From יְהֹוָה and נָתַן; Jehovah-given; Jehonathan, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jonathan.
H3084: A fuller form of יוֹסֵף; Jehoseph (i.e. Joseph), a son of Jacob. In the KJV it is rendered: Joseph.
H3085: From יְהֹוָה and עָדָה; Jehovah-adorned; Jehoaddah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehoada.
H3086: Or Yhowaddan; from יְהֹוָה and עָדַן; Jehovah-pleased; Jehoaddin or Jehoaddan, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehoaddan.
H3087: From יְהֹוָה and צָדַק; Jehovah-righted; Jehotsadak, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehozadek, Josedech.
H3088: From יְהֹוָה and רוּם; Jehovah-raised; Jehoram, the name of a Syrian and of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehoram, Joram.
H3089: From יְהֹוָה and שָׁבַע; Jehovah-sworn; Jehosheba, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehosheba.
H3090: A form of יְהוֹשֶׁ֫בַע; Jehoshabath, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehoshabeath.
H3091: Or Yhowshua; from יְהֹוָה and יָשַׁע; Jehovah-saved; Jehoshua (i.e. Joshua), the Jewish leader. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehoshua, Jehoshuah, Joshua.
H3092: From יְהֹוָה and שָׁפַט; Jehovah-judged; Jehoshaphat, the name of six Israelites; also of a valley near Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehoshaphat.
H3093: Probably from the same as הָר; elated; hence, arrogant. In the KJV it is rendered: haughty, proud.
H3094: From הָלַל and אֵל; praising God; Jehallelel, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehalellel, Jehalelel.
H3095: From הָלַם (in the sense of hardness); a precious stone, probably onyx. In the KJV it is rendered: diamond.
H3096: Or Yahtsah; or (feminine) Yahtsah; from an unused root meaning to stamp; perhaps threshing-floor; Jahats or Jahtsah, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Jahaz, Jahazah, Jahzah.
H3097: From יְהֹוָה and אָב; Jehovah-fathered; Joab, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Joab.
H3098: From יְהֹוָה and אָח; Jehovah-brothered; Joach, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Joah.
H3099: A form of יְהוֹאָחָז; Joachaz, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehoahaz, Joahaz.
H3100: From יְהֹוָה and אֵל; Jehovah (is his) God; Joel, the name of twelve Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Joel.
H3101: Or Yoash (2 Chron. 24:1); a form of יְהוֹאָשׁ; Joash, the name of six Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Joash.
H3102: Perhaps a form of יוֹבָב, but more probably by erroneous transcription for יָשׁוּב; Job, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Job.
H3103: From יָבַב; howler; Jobab, the name of two Israelites and of three foreigners. In the KJV it is rendered: Jobab.
H3104: Or yobel; apparently from יָבַל; the blast of a horn (from its continuous sound); specifically, the signal of the silver trumpets; hence, the instrument itself and the festival thus introduced. In the KJV it is rendered: jubile, ram's horn, trumpet.
H3105: From יָבַל; a stream. In the KJV it is rendered: river.
H3106: From יָבַל; stream; Jubal, an antediluvian. In the KJV it is rendered: Jubal.
H3107: A form of יְהוֹזָבָד; Jozabad, the name of ten Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Josabad, Jozabad.
H3108: From יְהֹוָה and זָכַר; Jehovah-remembered; Jozacar, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jozachar.
H3109: Probably from יְהֹוָה and a variation of חָיָה; Jehovah-revived; Jocha, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Joha.
H3110: A form of יְהוֹחָנָן; Jochanan, the name of nine Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Johanan.
H3111: A form of יְהוֹיָדָע; Jojada, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehoiada, Joiada.
H3112: A form of יְהוֹיָכִין; Jojakin, an Israelite king. In the KJV it is rendered: Jehoiachin.
H3113: A form of יְהוֹיָקִים; Jojakim, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Joiakim.
H3114: A form of יְהוֹיָרִיב; Jojarib, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Joiarib.
H3115: From יְהֹוָה contracted and כָּבַד; Jehovah-gloried; Jokebed, the mother of Moses. In the KJV it is rendered: Jochebed.
H3116: A form of יְהוּכַל; Jukal, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jucal.
H3117: From an unused root meaning to be hot; a day (as the warm hours), whether literal (from sunrise to sunset, or from one sunset to the next), or figurative (a space of time defined by an associated term), (often used adverb). In the KJV it is rendered: age, + always, + chronicals, continually(-ance), daily, ((birth-), each, to) day, (now a, two) days (agone), + elder, X end, + evening, + (for) ever(-lasting, -more), X full, life, as (so) long as (.
H3118: (Aramaic) corresponding to יוֹם; a day. In the KJV it is rendered: day (by day), time.
H3119: From יוֹם; daily. In the KJV it is rendered: daily, (by, in the) day(-time).
H3120: Probably from the same as יָ֫יִן; effervescing (i.e. hot and active); Javan, the name of a son of Joktan, and of the race (Ionians, i.e. Greeks) descended from him, with their territory; also of a place in Arabia. In the KJV it is rendered: Javan.
H3121: From the same as יָ֫יִן; properly, dregs (as effervescing); hence, mud. In the KJV it is rendered: mire, miry.
H3122: A form of יְהוֹנָדָב; Jonadab, the name of an Israelite and of a Rechabite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jonadab.
H3123: Probably from the same as יָ֫יִן; a dove (apparently from the warmth of their mating). In the KJV it is rendered: dove, pigeon.
H3124: The same as יוֹנִים; Jonah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jonah.
H3125: Patronymically from יָוֵן; a Jevanite, or descendant of Javan. In the KJV it is rendered: Grecian.
H3126: Active participle of יָנַק; a sucker; hence, a twig (of a tree felled and sprouting). In the KJV it is rendered: tender plant.
H3127: Feminine of יוֹנֵק; a sprout. In the KJV it is rendered: (tender) branch, young twig.
H3128: From יוֹנִים and אֵ֫לֶם and the plural of רָחוֹק; dove of (the) silence (i.e. dumb Israel) of (i.e. among) distances (i.e. strangers); the title of a ditty (used for a name of its melody). In the KJV it is rendered: Jonath-elem-rechokim.
H3129: A form of יְהוֹנָתָן; Jonathan, the name of ten Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jonathan.
H3130: Future of יָסַף; let him add (or perhaps simply active participle adding); Joseph, the name of seven Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Joseph.
H3131: From active participle of יָסַף and יָהּ; Jah (is) adding; Josiphjah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Josiphiah.
H3132: Perhaps feminine active participle of יָעַל; furthermore; Joelah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Joelah.
H3133: Apparently the active participle of יָעַד; appointer; Joed, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Joed.
H3134: From יְהֹוָה and עֵ֫זֶר; Jehovah (is his) help; Joezer, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Joezer.
H3135: From יְהֹוָה and עוּשׁ; Jehovah-hastened; Joash, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Joash.
H3136: A form of יְהוֹצָדָק; Jotsadak, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jozadak.
H3137: A form of יוֹיָקִים; Jokim, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jokim.
H3138: Active participle of יָרָה; sprinkling; hence, a sprinkling (or autumnal showers). In the KJV it is rendered: first rain, former (rain).
H3139: From יָרָה; rainy; Jorah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jorah.
H3140: From יָרָה; rainy; Jorai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jorai.
H3141: A form of יְהוֹרָם; Joram, the name of three Israelites and one Syrian. In the KJV it is rendered: Joram.
H3142: From שׁוּב and חָ֫סֶד; kindness will be returned; Jushab-Chesed, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jushab-hesed.
H3143: From יָשַׁב and יָהּ; Jehovah will cause to dwell; Josibjah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Josibiah.
H3144: Probably a form of יוֹשַׁוְיָה; Joshah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Joshah.
H3145: From יְהֹוָה and שָׁוָה; Jehovah-set; Joshavjah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Joshaviah.
H3146: A form of יְהוֹשָׁפָט; Joshaphat, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Joshaphat.
H3147: From יְהֹוָה and תָּם־; Jehovah (is) perfect; Jotham, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jotham.
H3148: Active participle of יָתַר; properly, redundant; hence, over and above, as adjective, noun, adverb or conjunction (as follows). In the KJV it is rendered: better, more(-over), over, profit.
H3149: From an unused root (meaning to sprinkle) and אֵל; sprinkled of God; Jezavel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jeziel (from the margin).
H3150: From the same as the first part of יְזוּאֵל and יָהּ; sprinkled of Jah; Jizzijah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jeziah.
H3151: From the same as זִיז; he will make prominent; Jaziz, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jaziz.
H3152: Perhaps from an unused root (meaning to draw up); he will draw out; Jizliah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jezliah.
H3153: Or Yzanyahuw; probably for יַאֲזַנְיָה; Jezanjah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jezaniah.
H3154: From an unused root mean to ooze; sweat, i.e. (by implication) a sweating dress. In the KJV it is rendered: any thing that causeth sweat.
H3155: A variation for אֶזְרָחִי; a Jizrach (i.e. Ezrachite or Zarchite) or descendant of Zerach. In the KJV it is rendered: Izrahite.
H3156: From זָרַח and יָהּ; Jah will shine; Jizrachjah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Izrahiah, Jezrahiah.
H3157: From זָרַע and אֵל; God will sow; Jizreel, the name of two places in Palestine and of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jezreel.
H3158: Patronymically from יִזְרְעֶאל; a Jizreelite or native of Jizreel. In the KJV it is rendered: Jezreelite.
