H3458: From שָׁמַע and אֵל; God will hear; Jishmael, the name of Abraham's oldest son, and of five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ishmael.
H3459: Patronymically from יִשְׁמָעֵאל; a Jishmaelite or descendant of Jishmael. In the KJV it is rendered: Ishmaelite.
H3460: Or Yishmacyahuw; from שָׁמַע and יָהּ; Jah will hear; Jishmajah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ishmaiah.
H3461: From שָׁמַר; preservative; Jishmerai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ishmerai.
H3462: A primitive root; properly, to be slack or languid, i.e. (by implication) sleep (figuratively, to die); also to grow old, stale or inveterate: -old (store), remain long, (make to) sleep.
H3463: From יָשֵׁן; sleepy. In the KJV it is rendered: asleep, (one out of) sleep(-eth, -ing), slept.
H3464: The same as יָשֵׁן; Jashen, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jashen.
H3465: From יָשֵׁן; old. In the KJV it is rendered: old.
H3466: Feminine of יָשָׁן; Jeshanah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Jeshanah.
H3467: A primitive root; properly, to be open, wide or free, i.e. (by implication) to be safe; causatively, to free or succor. In the KJV it is rendered: X at all, avenging, defend, deliver(-er), help, preserve, rescue, be safe, bring (having) salvation, save(-iour), get victory.
H3468: Or yeshai; from יָשַׁע; liberty, deliverance, prosperity. In the KJV it is rendered: safety, salvation, saving.
H3469: From יָשַׁע; saving; Jishi, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ishi.
H3470: Or Yshayahuw; from יָשַׁע and יָהּ; Jah has saved; Jeshajah, the name of seven Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Isaiah, Jesaiah, Jeshaiah.
H3471: From an unused root meaning to polish; a gem supposed to be jasper (from the resemblance in name). In the KJV it is rendered: jasper.
H3472: Perhaps from שָׁפָה; he will scratch; Jishpah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ispah.
H3473: Probably from the same as שָׁפָן; he will hide; Jishpan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ishpan.
H3474: A primitive root; to be straight or even; figuratively, to be (causatively, to make) right, pleasant, prosperous. In the KJV it is rendered: direct, fit, seem good (meet), + please (will), be (esteem, go) right (on), bring (look, make, take the) straight (way), be upright(-ly).
H3475: From יָשַׁר; the right; Jesher, an Israelite: -Jesher.
H3476: From יָשַׁר; the right. In the KJV it is rendered: equity, meet, right, upright(-ness).
H3477: From יָשַׁר; straight (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: convenient, equity, Jasher, just, meet(-est), + pleased well right(-eous), straight, (most) upright(-ly, -ness).
H3478: From שָׂרָה and אֵל; he will rule as God; Jisrael, a symbolical name of Jacob; also (typically) of his posterity. In the KJV it is rendered: Israel.
H3479: (Aramaic) corresponding to יִשְׂרָאֵל. In the KJV it is rendered: Israel.
H3480: By variation from יָשָׁר and אֵל with directive enclitic; right towards God; Jesarelah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jesharelah.
H3481: Patronymically from יִשְׂרָאֵל; a Jisreelite or descendant of Jisrael. In the KJV it is rendered: of Israel, Israelite.
H3482: Feminine of יִשְׂרְאֵלִי; a Jisreelitess or female descendant of Jisrael. In the KJV it is rendered: Israelitish.
H3483: Feminine or יָשָׁר; rectitude. In the KJV it is rendered: uprightness.
H3484: From יָשַׁר; upright; Jeshurun, a symbol. name for Israel. In the KJV it is rendered: Jeshurun.
H3485: (strictly yis-saws-kawr'); from נָשָׂא and שָׂכָר; he will bring a reward; Jissaskar, a son of Jacob. In the KJV it is rendered: Issachar.
H3486: From an unused root meaning to blanch; gray-haired, i.e. an aged man. In the KJV it is rendered: stoop for age.
H3487: (Aramaic) corresponding to אוֹת; a sign of the object of a verb: + whom.
H3488: (Aramaic) corresponding to יָשַׁב; to sit or dwell: -dwell, (be) set, sit.
H3489: From an unused root meaning to pin through or fast; a peg. In the KJV it is rendered: nail, paddle, pin, stake.
H3490: From an unused root meaning to be lonely; a bereaved person. In the KJV it is rendered: fatherless (child), orphan.
H3491: Passive participle of יָתַר; properly, what is left, i.e. (by implication) a gleaning. In the KJV it is rendered: range.
H3492: From יָתַר; redundant; Jattir, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Jattir.
H3493: (Aramaic) corresponding to יַתִּיר; preeminent; as an adverb, very. In the KJV it is rendered: exceeding(-ly), excellent.
H3494: Probably from תָּלָה; it will hang, i.e. be high; Jithlah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Jethlah.
H3495: From the same as יָתוֹם; orphanage; Jithmah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ithmah.
H3496: From an unused root meaning to endure, and אֵל; continued of God; Jathniel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jathniel.
H3497: From the same as תַּנִּין; extensive; Jithnan, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ithnan.
H3498: A primitive root; to jut over or exceed; by implication, to excel; (intransitively) to remain or be left; causatively, to leave, cause to abound, preserve. In the KJV it is rendered: excel, leave (a remnant), left behind, too much, make plenteous, preserve, (be, let) remain(-der, -ing, - nant), reserve, residue, rest.
H3499: From יָתַר; properly, an overhanging, i.e. (by implication) an excess, superiority, remainder; also a small rope (as hanging free). In the KJV it is rendered: + abundant, cord, exceeding, excellancy(-ent), what they leave, that hath left, plentifully, remnant, residue, rest, string, with.
H3500: The same as יֶ֫תֶר; Jether, the name of five or six Israelites and of one Midianite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jether, Jethro.
H3501: By variation for יִתְרָה; Jithra, an Israelite (or Ishmaelite). In the KJV it is rendered: Ithra.
H3502: Feminine of יֶ֫תֶר; properly, excellence, i.e. (by implication) wealth. In the KJV it is rendered: abundance, riches.
H3503: From יֶ֫תֶר with pron. suffix; his excellence; Jethro, Moses' father-in-law. In the KJV it is rendered: Jethro.
H3504: From יָתַר; preeminence, gain. In the KJV it is rendered: better, excellency(-leth), profit(-able).
H3505: Patronymically from יֶ֫תֶר; a Jithrite or descendant of Jether. In the KJV it is rendered: Ithrite.
H3506: From יָתַר; excellent; Jithran, the name of an Edomite and of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ithran.
H3507: From יֶ֫תֶר and עָם; excellence of people; Jithream, a son of David. In the KJV it is rendered: Ithream.
H3508: Feminine active participle of יָתַר; the lobe or flap of the liver (as if redundant or outhanging). In the KJV it is rendered: caul.
H3509: Of uncertain derivation; Jetheth, an Edomite: -Jetheth.
H3510: A primitive root; properly, to feel pain; by implication, to grieve; figuratively, to spoil. In the KJV it is rendered: grieving, mar, have pain, make sad (sore), (be) sorrowful.
H3511: From כָּאַב; suffering (physical or mental), adversity. In the KJV it is rendered: grief, pain, sorrow.
H3512: A primitive root; to despond: causatively, to deject. In the KJV it is rendered: broken, be grieved, make sad.
H3513: Or kabed; a primitive root; to be heavy, i.e. in a bad sense (burdensome, severe, dull) or in a good sense (numerous, rich, honorable; causatively, to make weighty (in the same two senses). In the KJV it is rendered: abounding with, more grievously afflict, boast, be chargeable, X be dim, glorify, be (make) glorious (things), glory, (very) great, be grievous, harden, be (make) heavy, be heavier, lay heavily, (bring to, come to, do, get, be had in) honour (self), (be) honourable (man), lade, X more be laid, make self many, nobles, prevail, promote (to honour), be rich, be (go) sore, stop.
H3514: From כָּבַד; weight, multitude, vehemence: -grievousness, heavy, great number.
H3515: From כָּבַד; heavy; figuratively in a good sense (numerous) or in a bad sense (severe, difficult, stupid). In the KJV it is rendered: (so) great, grievous, hard(-ened), (too) heavy(-ier), laden, much, slow, sore, thick.
H3516: The same as כָּבֵד; the liver (as the heaviest of the viscera). In the KJV it is rendered: liver.
H3517: Feminine of כָּבֵד; difficulty. In the KJV it is rendered: X heavily.
H3518: A primitive root; to expire or (causatively) to extinguish (fire, light, anger). In the KJV it is rendered: go (put) out, quench.
H3519: Rarely kabod; from כָּבַד; properly, weight, but only figuratively in a good sense, splendor or copiousness. In the KJV it is rendered: glorious(-ly), glory, honour(-able).
H3520: Irreg. feminine passive participle of כָּבַד; weightiness, i.e. magnificence, wealth. In the KJV it is rendered: carriage, all glorious, stately.
H3521: From the same as כֶּ֫בֶל in the sense of limitation; sterile; Cabul, the name of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Cabul.
H3522: From an unused root meaning to heap up; hilly; Cabon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Cabbon.
H3523: From כָּבַר in the original sense of plaiting; a matrass (of intertwined materials). In the KJV it is rendered: pillow.
H3524: From כָּבַר; vast, whether in extent (figuratively, of power, mighty; of time, aged), or in number, many. In the KJV it is rendered: + feeble, mighty, most, much, strong, valiant.
H3525: From an unused root meaning to twine or braid together; a fetter. In the KJV it is rendered: fetter.
H3526: A primitive root; to trample; hence, to wash (properly, by stamping with the feet), whether literal (including the fulling process) or figurative. In the KJV it is rendered: fuller, wash(-ing).
H3527: A primitive root; properly, to plait together, i.e. (figuratively) to augment (especially in number or quantity, to accumulate). In the KJV it is rendered: in abundance, multiply.
H3528: From כָּבַר; properly, extent of time, i.e. a great while; hence, long ago, formerly, hitherto. In the KJV it is rendered: already, (seeing that which), now.
H3529: The same as כְּבָר; length; Kebar, a river of Mesopotamia. In the KJV it is rendered: Chebar.
H3530: Feminine of כְּבָר; properly, length, i.e. a measure (of uncertain dimension). In the KJV it is rendered: X little.
H3531: From כָּבַר in its original sense; a sieve (as netted). In the KJV it is rendered: sieve.
H3532: From an unused root meaning to dominate; a ram (just old enough to butt). In the KJV it is rendered: lamb, sheep.
H3533: A primitive root; to tread down; hence, negatively, to disregard; positively, to conquer, subjugate, violate. In the KJV it is rendered: bring into bondage, force, keep under, subdue, bring into subjection.
H3534: From כָּבַשׁ; a footstool (as trodden upon): -footstool.
H3535: Or kabsah; feminine of כֶּ֫בֶשׂ; a ewe. In the KJV it is rendered: (ewe) lamb.
H3536: From כָּבַשׁ; a smelting furnace (as reducing metals). In the KJV it is rendered: furnace.
H3537: From an unused root meaning to deepen; properly, a pail; but generally of earthenware; a jar for domestic purposes. In the KJV it is rendered: barrel, pitcher.
H3538: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to כָּזַב; false: -lying.
H3539: From the same as כַּד in the sense of striking fire from a metal forged; a sparkling gem, probably the ruby. In the KJV it is rendered: agate.
H3540: Of foreign origin; Kedorlaomer, an early Persian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Chedorlaomer.
H3541: From the prefix k and הוּא; properly, like this, i.e. by implication, (of manner) thus (or so); also (of place) here (or hither); or (of time) now. In the KJV it is rendered: also, here, + hitherto, like, on the other side, so (and much), such, on that manner, (on) this (manner, side, way, way and that way), + mean while, yonder.
H3542: (Aramaic) corresponding to כֹּה. In the KJV it is rendered: hitherto.
H3543: A primitive root; to be weak, i.e. (figuratively) to despond (causatively, rebuke), or (of light, the eye) to grow dull. In the KJV it is rendered: darken, be dim, fail, faint, restrain, X utterly.
H3544: From כָּהָה; feeble, obscure. In the KJV it is rendered: somewhat dark, darkish, wax dim, heaviness, smoking.
H3545: Feminine of כֵּהָה; properly, a weakening; figuratively, alleviation, i.e. cure. In the KJV it is rendered: healing.
H3546: (Aramaic) a root corresponding to יָכֹל and כּוּל; to be able. In the KJV it is rendered: be able, could.
H3547: A primitive root, apparently meaning to mediate in religious services; but used only as denominative from כֹּהֵן; to officiate as a priest; figuratively, to put on regalia. In the KJV it is rendered: deck, be (do the office of a, execute the, minister in the) priest('s office).
H3548: Active participle of כָּהַן; literally, one officiating, a priest; also (by courtesy) an acting priest (although a layman). In the KJV it is rendered: chief ruler, X own, priest, prince, principal officer.
H3549: (Aramaic) corresponding to כֹּהֵן. In the KJV it is rendered: priest.
H3550: From כָּהַן; priesthood. In the KJV it is rendered: priesthood, priest's office.
H3551: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to לַ֫הַג in the sense of piercing; a window (as a perforation). In the KJV it is rendered: window.
H3552: Of foreign derivation; Kub, a country near Egypt. In the KJV it is rendered: Chub.
H3553: From an unused root meaning to be high or rounded; a helmet (as arched). In the KJV it is rendered: helmet.
H3554: A primitive root; properly, to prick or penetrate; hence, to blister (as smarting or eating into). In the KJV it is rendered: burn.
H3555: From כָּוָה; a branding. In the KJV it is rendered: burning.
H3556: Probably from the same as כַּבּוֹן (in the sense of rolling) or כָּוָה (in the sense of blazing); a star (as round or as shining); figuratively, a prince. In the KJV it is rendered: star((-gazer)).
H3557: A primitive root; properly, to keep in; hence, to measure; figuratively, to maintain (in various senses). In the KJV it is rendered: (be able to, can) abide, bear, comprehend, contain, feed, forbearing, guide, hold(-ing in), nourish(-er), be present, make provision, receive, sustain, provide sustenance (victuals).
H3558: From an unused root meaning to store away; a jewel (probably gold beads). In the KJV it is rendered: tablet.
H3559: A primitive root; properly, to be erect (i.e. stand perpendicular); hence (causatively) to set up, in a great variety of applications, whether literal (establish, fix, prepare, apply), or figurative (appoint, render sure, proper or prosperous). In the KJV it is rendered: certain(-ty), confirm, direct, faithfulness, fashion, fasten, firm, be fitted, be fixed, frame, be meet, ordain, order, perfect, (make) preparation, prepare (self), provide, make provision, (be, make) ready, right, set (aright, fast, forth), be stable, (e-)stablish, stand, tarry, X very deed.
H3560: Probably from כּוּן; established; Kun, a place in Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Chun.
H3561: From כּוּן; something prepared, i.e. a sacrificial wafer. In the KJV it is rendered: cake.
H3562: From כּוּן and יָהּ; Jah has sustained; Conanjah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Conaniah, Cononiah.
H3563: From an unused root meaning to hold together; a cup (as a container), often figuratively, a lot (as if a potion); also some unclean bird, probably an owl (perhaps from the cup-like cavity of its eye). In the KJV it is rendered: cup, (small) owl.
H3564: From an unused root meaning properly, to dig through; a pot or furnace (as if excavated). In the KJV it is rendered: furnace.
H3565: From כּוּר and עָשָׁן; furnace of smoke; Cor-Ashan, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Chor-ashan.
H3566: Or (Ezra 1:1 (last time),2) Koresh; from the Persians; Koresh (or Cyrus), the Persian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Cyrus.
H3567: (Aramaic) corresponding to כּ֫וֹרֶשׁ. In the KJV it is rendered: Cyrus.
H3568: Probably of foreign origin; Cush (or Ethiopia), the name of a son of Ham, and of his territory; also of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Chush, Cush, Ethiopia.
H3569: Patronymically from כּוּשׁ; a Cushite, or descendant of Cush. In the KJV it is rendered: Cushi, Cushite, Ethiopian(-s).
H3570: The same as כּוּשִׁי; Cushi, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Cushi.
H3571: Feminine of כּוּשִׁי; a Cushite woman: -Ethiopian.
H3572: Perhaps from כּוּשׁ; Cushan, a region of Arabia: -Cushan.
H3573: Apparently from כּוּשָׁן and the dual of רִשְׁעָה; Cushan of double wickedness; Cushan-Rishathajim, a Mesopotamian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Chushan-rishathayim.
H3574: From כָּשֵׁר; prosperity; in plural freedom: -X chain.
H3575: Or (feminine) Kuwthah; of foreign origin; Cuth or Cuthah, a province of Assyria. In the KJV it is rendered: Cuth.
H3576: A primitive root; to lie (i.e. deceive), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: fail, (be found a, make a) liar, lie, lying, be in vain.
H3577: From כָּזַב; falsehood; literally (untruth) or figuratively (idol). In the KJV it is rendered: deceitful, false, leasing, + liar, lie, lying.
H3578: From כָּזַב; fallacious; Cozeba, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Choseba.
H3579: From כָּזַב; false; Cozbi, a Midianitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Cozbi.
H3580: From כָּזַב; falsified; Kezib, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Chezib.
H3581: Or (Dan. 11:6) kowach; from an unused root meaning to be firm; vigor, literally (force, in a good or a bad sense) or figuratively (capacity, means, produce); also (from its hardiness) a large lizard: -ability, able, chameleon, force, fruits, might, power(-ful), strength, substance, wealth.
H3582: A primitive root; to secrete, by act or word; hence (intensively) to destroy. In the KJV it is rendered: conceal, cut down (off), desolate, hide.
H3583: A primitive root; to paint (with stibium): -paint.
H3584: A primitive root; to be untrue, in word (to lie, feign, disown) or deed (to disappoint, fail, cringe). In the KJV it is rendered: deceive, deny, dissemble, fail, deal falsely, be found liars, (be-)lie, lying, submit selves.
H3585: From כָּחַשׁ; literally, a failure of flesh, i.e. emaciation; figuratively, hypocrisy. In the KJV it is rendered: leanness, lies, lying.
H3586: From כָּחַשׁ; faithless. In the KJV it is rendered: lying.
H3587: From כָּוָה; a brand or scar. In the KJV it is rendered: burning.
H3588: A primitive particle (the full form of the prepositional prefix) indicating causal relations of all kinds, antecedent or consequent; (by implication) very widely used as a relative conjunction or adverb (as below); often largely modified by other particles annexed. In the KJV it is rendered: and, + (forasmuch, inasmuch, where-)as, assured(-ly), + but, certainly, doubtless, + else, even, + except, for, how, (because, in, so, than) that, + nevertheless, now, rightly, seeing, since, surely, then, therefore, + (al-)though, + till, truly, + until, when, whether, while, whom, yea, yet.
H3589: From a primitive root meaning to strike: a crushing; figuratively, calamity. In the KJV it is rendered: destruction.
H3590: From the same as כִּיד (compare כַּדְכֹּד); properly, something struck off, i.e. a spark (as struck). In the KJV it is rendered: spark.
H3591: From the same as כִּיד; properly, something to strike with, i.e. a dart (perhaps smaller that חֲנִית). In the KJV it is rendered: lance, shield, spear, target.
H3592: The same as כִּידוֹן; Kidon, a place in Palestine: -Chidon.
H3593: Of uncertain derivation; perhaps tumult. In the KJV it is rendered: battle.
H3594: From כּוּן; properly, a statue, i.e. idol; but used (by euphemism) for some heathen deity (perhaps corresponding to Priapus or Baal-peor). In the KJV it is rendered: Chiun.
H3595: Or kiyor; from the same as כּוּר; properly, something round (as excavated or bored), i.e. a chafing-dish for coals or a caldron for cooking; hence (from similarity of form) a washbowl; also (for the same reason) a pulpit or platform. In the KJV it is rendered: hearth, laver, pan, scaffold.
H3596: Or kelay; from כּוּל in the sense of withholding; niggardly. In the KJV it is rendered: churl.
H3597: From an unused root meaning to clap or strike with noise; a club or sledge-hammer. In the KJV it is rendered: hammer.
H3598: From the same as כּוּמָז; a cluster of stars, i.e. the Pleiades. In the KJV it is rendered: Pleiades, seven stars.
H3599: A form for כּוֹס; a cup; also a bag for money or weights. In the KJV it is rendered: bag, cup, purse.
H3600: A form for כּוּר (only in the dual); a cooking range (consisting of two parallel stones, across which the boiler is set): -ranges for pots.
H3601: From כָּשֵׁר; literally, a director, i.e. the spindle or shank of a distaff (פֶּ֫לֶך), by which it is twirled. In the KJV it is rendered: spindle.
H3602: From כֹּה; just so, referring to the previous or following context. In the KJV it is rendered: after that (this) manner, this matter, (even) so, in such a case, thus.
H3603: From כָּרַר; a circle, i.e. (by implication) a circumjacent tract or region, expec. the Ghor or valley of the Jordan; also a (round) loaf; also a talent (or large (round) coin). In the KJV it is rendered: loaf, morsel, piece, plain, talent.
H3604: (Aramaic) corresponding to כִּכָּר; a talent. In the KJV it is rendered: talent.
H3605: Or (Jer. 33:8) kowl; from כָּלַל; properly, the whole; hence, all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense). In the KJV it is rendered: (in) all (manner, (ye)), altogether, any (manner), enough, every (one, place, thing), howsoever, as many as, (no-)thing, ought, whatsoever, (the) whole, whoso(-ever).
H3606: (Aramaic) corresponding to כֹּל. In the KJV it is rendered: all, any, + (forasmuch) as, + be-(for this) cause, every, + no (manner, -ne), + there (where)-fore, + though, what (where, who)-soever, (the) whole.
H3607: A primitive root; to restrict, by act (hold back or in) or word (prohibit). In the KJV it is rendered: finish, forbid, keep (back), refrain, restrain, retain, shut up, be stayed, withhold.
H3608: From כָּלָא; a prison. In the KJV it is rendered: prison.
H3609: Apparently from כָּלָא and אָב; restraint of (his) father; Kilab, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Chileab.
H3610: Dual of כֶּ֫לֶא in the original sense of separation; two heterogeneities. In the KJV it is rendered: divers seeds (-e kinds), mingled (seed).
H3611: From an unused root means. to yelp, or else to attack; a dog; hence (by euphemism) a male prostitute. In the KJV it is rendered: dog.
H3612: Perhaps a form of כָּ֫לֶב, or else from the same root in the sense of forcible; Caleb, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Caleb.
H3613: From כָּלֵב and אֶפְרָת; Caleb- Ephrathah, a place in Egypt (if the text is correct). In the KJV it is rendered: Caleb-ephrathah.
H3614: Probably by erroneous transcription for Kalebiy; patronymically from כָּלֵב; a Calebite or descendant of Caleb. In the KJV it is rendered: of the house of Caleb.
H3615: A primitive root; to end, whether intransitive (to cease, be finished, perish) or transitived (to complete, prepare, consume). In the KJV it is rendered: accomplish, cease, consume (away), determine, destroy (utterly), be (when.
H3616: From כָּלָה; pining. In the KJV it is rendered: fail.
H3617: From כָּלָה; a completion; adverb, completely; also destruction. In the KJV it is rendered: altogether, (be, utterly) consume(-d), consummation(-ption), was determined, (full, utter) end, riddance.
H3618: From כָּלַל; a bride (as if perfect); hence, a son's wife. In the KJV it is rendered: bride, daughter-in-law, spouse.
H3619: From the same as כָּ֫לֶב; a bird-trap (as furnished with a clap-stick or treadle to spring it); hence, a basket (as resembling a wicker cage). In the KJV it is rendered: basket, cage.
H3620: The same as כְּלוּב; Kelub, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Chelub.
H3621: A form of כָּלֵב; Kelubai, an Israelite: -Chelubai.
H3622: From כָּלָה; completed; Keluhai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Chelluh.
H3623: Denominative passive participle from כַּלָּה; bridehood (only in the plural). In the KJV it is rendered: espousal.
H3624: From an unused root meaning to be complete; maturity. In the KJV it is rendered: full (old) age.
H3625: The same as כָּ֫לַח; Kelach, a place in Assyria: -Calah.
H3626: From כֹּל and חֹזֶה; every seer; Col- Chozeh, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Col-hozeh.
H3627: From כָּלָה; something prepared, i.e. any apparatus (as an implement, utensil, dress, vessel or weapon). In the KJV it is rendered: armour ((-bearer)), artillery, bag, carriage, + furnish, furniture, instrument, jewel, that is made of, X one from another, that which pertaineth, pot, + psaltery, sack, stuff, thing, tool, vessel, ware, weapon, + whatsoever.
H3628: Or kluw1; from כָּלָא (compare כֶּ֫לֶא); a prison. In the KJV it is rendered: prison.
H3629: Feminine of כְּלִי (only in the plural); a kidney (as an essential organ); figuratively, the mind (as the interior self). In the KJV it is rendered: kidneys, reins.
H3630: A form of כִּלָּיוֹן; Kiljon, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Chilion.
H3632: From כָּלַל; complete; as noun, the whole (specifically, a sacrifice entirely consumed); as adverb, fully. In the KJV it is rendered: all, every whit, flame, perfect(-ion), utterly, whole burnt offering (sacrifice), wholly.
H3633: From כּוּל; sustenance; Calcol, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Calcol, Chalcol.
H3634: A primitive root; to complete. In the KJV it is rendered: (make) perfect.
H3635: (Aramaic) corresponding to כָּלַל; to complete. In the KJV it is rendered: finish, make (set) up.
H3636: From כָּלַל; complete; Kelal, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Chelal.
H3637: A primitive root; properly, to wound; but only figuratively, to taunt or insult. In the KJV it is rendered: be (make) ashamed, blush, be confounded, be put to confusion, hurt, reproach, (do, put to) shame.
H3638: Of foreign derivation; Kilmad, a place apparently in the Assyrian empire. In the KJV it is rendered: Chilmad.
H3639: From כָּלָם; disgrace. In the KJV it is rendered: confusion, dishonour, reproach, shame.
H3640: From כְּלִמָּה; disgrace. In the KJV it is rendered: shame.
H3641: Or Kalneh; also Kalnow; of foreign derivation; Calneh or Calno, a place in the Assyrian empire. In the KJV it is rendered: Calneh, Calno.
H3642: A primitive root; to pine after. In the KJV it is rendered: long.
H3643: From כָּמַהּ; pining; Kimham, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Chimham.
H3644: Or kamow; a form of the prefix "k-", but used separately (compare כֵּן); as, thus, so. In the KJV it is rendered: according to, (such) as (it were, well as), in comparison of, like (as, to, unto), thus, when, worth.
H3645: Or (Jer. 48:7) Kmiysh; from an unused root meaning to subdue; the powerful; Kemosh, the god of the Moabites. In the KJV it is rendered: Chemosh.
H3646: From an unused root meaning to store up or preserve; "cummin" (from its use as a condiment). In the KJV it is rendered: cummin.
H3647: A primitive root; to store away, i.e. (figuratively) in the memory. In the KJV it is rendered: lay up in store.
H3648: A primitive root; properly, to intertwine or contract, i.e. (by implication) to shrivel (as with heat); figuratively, to be deeply affected with passion (love or pity). In the KJV it is rendered: be black, be kindled, yearn.
H3649: From כָּמַר; properly, an ascetic (as if shrunk with self-maceration), i.e. an idolatrous priest (only in plural). In the KJV it is rendered: Chemarims (idolatrous) priests.
H3650: Redupl. from כָּמַר; obscuration (as if from shrinkage of light, i.e. an eclipse (only in plural). In the KJV it is rendered: blackness.
H3651: From כּוּן; properly, set upright; hence (figuratively as adjective) just; but usually (as adverb or conjunction) rightly or so (in various applications to manner, time and relation; often with other particles). In the KJV it is rendered: + after that (this, -ward, -wards), as.
H3652: (Aramaic) corresponding to כֵּן; so. In the KJV it is rendered: thus.
H3653: The same as כֵּן, used as a noun; a stand, i.e. pedestal or station. In the KJV it is rendered: base, estate, foot, office, place, well.
H3654: From כָּנַן in the sense of fastening; a gnat (from infixing its sting; used only in plural (and irreg. in Exod. 8:17,18; Heb. 13:14)). In the KJV it is rendered: lice, X manner.
H3655: A primitive root; to address by an additional name; hence, to eulogize. In the KJV it is rendered: give flattering titles, surname (himself).
H3656: For כַּלְנוֹ; Canneh, a place in Assyria. In the KJV it is rendered: Canneh.
H3657: From כָּנַן; a plant (as set). In the KJV it is rendered: X vineyard.
H3658: From a unused root meaning to twang; a harp: -harp.
H3659: For יְכָנְיָה; Conjah, an Israelite king. In the KJV it is rendered: Coniah.
H3660: (Aramaic) corresponding to NONE; so or thus. In the KJV it is rendered: so, (in) this manner (sort), thus.
H3661: A primitive root; to set out, i.e. plant. In the KJV it is rendered: X vineyard.
H3662: From כָּנַן; planted; Kenani, an Israelite: -Chenani.
H3663: Or Knanyahuw; from כָּנַן and יָהּ; Jah has planted; Kenanjah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Chenaniah.
H3664: A primitive root; to collect; hence, to enfold: -gather (together), heap up, wrap self.
H3665: A primitive root; properly, to bend the knee; hence, to humiliate, vanquish. In the KJV it is rendered: bring down (low), into subjection, under, humble (self), subdue.
H3666: From כָּנַע in the sense of folding (compare כָּנַס); a package. In the KJV it is rendered: wares.
H3667: From כָּנַע; humiliated; Kenaan, a son a Ham; also the country inhabited by him. In the KJV it is rendered: Canaan, merchant, traffick.
H3668: Feminine of כְּנַ֫עַן; Kenaanah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Chenaanah.
H3669: Patrial from כְּנַ֫עַן; a Kenaanite or inhabitant of Kenaan; by implication, a pedlar (the Canaanites standing for their neighbors the Ishmaelites, who conducted mercantile caravans). In the KJV it is rendered: Canaanite, merchant, trafficker.
H3670: A primitive root; properly, to project laterally, i.e. probably (reflexive) to withdraw. In the KJV it is rendered: be removed.
H3671: From כָּנַף; an edge or extremity; specifically (of a bird or army) a wing, (of a garment or bed-clothing) a flap, (of the earth) a quarter, (of a building) a pinnacle. In the KJV it is rendered: + bird, border, corner, end, feather(-ed), X flying, + (one an-)other, overspreading, X quarters, skirt, X sort, uttermost part, wing((-ed)).
H3672: Or Kinnereth; respectively plural and singular feminine from the same as כִּנּוֹר; perhaps harp-shaped; Kinneroth or Kinnereth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Chinnereth, Chinneroth, Cinneroth.
H3673: (Aramaic) corresponding to כָּנַס; to assemble. In the KJV it is rendered: gather together.
H3674: From כָּנָה; a colleague (as having the same title). In the KJV it is rendered: companion.
H3675: (Aramaic) corresponding to כְּנָוֹת. In the KJV it is rendered: companion.
H3676: Apparently a contraction for כִּסֵּא, but probably by erroneous transcription for נֵס. In the KJV it is rendered: sworn.
H3677: Or keceh; apparently from כָּסָה; properly, fulness or the full moon, i.e. its festival. In the KJV it is rendered: (time) appointed.
H3678: Or kicceh; from כָּסָה; properly, covered, i.e. a throne (as canopied). In the KJV it is rendered: seat, stool, throne.
H3679: For כַּשְׂדִּי. In the KJV it is rendered: Chaldean.
H3680: A primitive root; properly, to plump, i.e. fill up hollows; by implication, to cover (for clothing or secrecy). In the KJV it is rendered: clad self, close, clothe, conceal, cover (self), (flee to) hide, overwhelm.
H3681: Passive participle of כָּסָה; properly, covered, i.e. (as noun) a covering. In the KJV it is rendered: covering.
H3682: From כָּסָה; a cover (garment); figuratively, a veiling. In the KJV it is rendered: covering, raiment, vesture.
H3683: A primitive root; to cut off. In the KJV it is rendered: cut down (up).
H3684: From כָּסַל; properly, fat, i.e. (figuratively) stupid or silly. In the KJV it is rendered: fool(-ish).
H3685: The same as כְּסִיל; any notable constellation; specifically Orion (as if a burly one). In the KJV it is rendered: constellation, Orion.
H3686: The same as כְּסִיל; Kesil, a place in Palestine: -Chesil.
H3687: From כְּסִיל; silliness. In the KJV it is rendered: foolish.
H3688: A primitive root; properly, to be fat, i.e. (figuratively) silly. In the KJV it is rendered: be foolish.
H3689: From כָּסַל; properly, fatness, i.e. by implication (literally) the loin (as the seat of the leaf fat) or (generally) the viscera; also (figuratively) silliness or (in a good sense) trust. In the KJV it is rendered: confidence, flank, folly, hope, loin.
H3690: Feminine of כָּ֫סֶל; in a good sense, trust; in a bad one, silliness. In the KJV it is rendered: confidence, folly.
H3691: Probably of foreign origin; Kisleu, the 9th Heb. month. In the KJV it is rendered: Chisleu.
H3692: From כָּסַל; hopeful; Kislon, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Chislon.
H3693: From כָּסַל; fertile; Kesalon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Chesalon.
H3694: Feminine plural of passive participle of כָּסַל; fattened; Kesulloth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Chesulloth.
H3695: A plural probably of foreign derivation; Casluchim, a people cognate to the Egyptians. In the KJV it is rendered: Casluhim.
H3696: From the feminine plural of כָּ֫סֶל and תָּבוֹר; flanks of Tabor; Kisloth-Tabor, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Chisloth- tabor.
H3697: A primitive root; to shear. In the KJV it is rendered: X only, poll.
H3698: From כָּסַם; spelt (from its bristliness as if just shorn). In the KJV it is rendered: fitches, rie.
H3699: A primitive root; to estimate. In the KJV it is rendered: make count.
H3700: A primitive root; properly, to become pale, i.e. (by implication) to pine after; also to fear. In the KJV it is rendered: (have) desire, be greedy, long, sore.
H3701: From כָּסַף; silver (from its pale color); by implication, money. In the KJV it is rendered: money, price, silver(-ling).
H3702: (Aramaic) corresponding to כָּ֫סֶפ. In the KJV it is rendered: money, silver.
H3703: Perhaps from כָּ֫סֶפ; silvery; Casiphja, a place in Bab. In the KJV it is rendered: Casiphia.
H3704: From כָּסָה; a cushion or pillow (as covering a seat or bed). In the KJV it is rendered: pillow.
H3705: (Aramaic) probably from כֵּן; now. In the KJV it is rendered: now.
H3706: (Aramaic) or kaeth (Aramaic); feminine of כְּעַן; thus (only in the formula "and so forth"). In the KJV it is rendered: at such a time.
H3707: A primitive root; to trouble; by implication, to grieve, rage, be indignant. In the KJV it is rendered: be angry, be grieved, take indignation, provoke (to anger, unto wrath), have sorrow, vex, be wroth.
H3708: Or (in Job) kaoas; from כָּעַס; vexation: -anger, angry, grief, indignation, provocation, provoking, X sore, sorrow, spite, wrath.
H3709: From כָּפַף; the hollow hand or palm (so of the paw of an animal, of the sole, and even of the bowl of a dish or sling, the handle of a bolt, the leaves of a palm-tree); figuratively, power. In the KJV it is rendered: branch, + foot, hand((-ful), -dle, (-led)), hollow, middle, palm, paw, power, sole, spoon.
H3710: From כָּפַף; a hollow rock. In the KJV it is rendered: rock.
H3711: A primitive root; properly, to bend, i.e. (figuratively) to tame or subdue. In the KJV it is rendered: pacify.
H3712: Feminine of כָּף; a leaf of a palm-tree. In the KJV it is rendered: branch.
H3713: From כָּפַר; properly, a cover, i.e. (by implication) a tankard (or covered goblet); also white frost (as covering the ground). In the KJV it is rendered: bason, hoar(-y) frost.
H3714: From an unused root meaning to connect; a girder. In the KJV it is rendered: beam.
H3715: From כָּפַר; a village (as covered in by walls); also a young lion (perhaps as covered with a mane). In the KJV it is rendered: (young) lion, village.
H3716: Feminine of כְּפִיר; the village (always with the art.); Kephirah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Chephirah.
H3717: A primitive root; to fold together; figuratively, to repeat. In the KJV it is rendered: double.
H3718: From כָּפַל; a duplicate. In the KJV it is rendered: double.
H3719: A primitive root; to bend. In the KJV it is rendered: bend.
H3720: From כָּפַן; hunger (as making to stoop with emptiness and pain). In the KJV it is rendered: famine.
H3721: A primitive root; to curve. In the KJV it is rendered: bow down (self).
H3722: A primitive root; to cover (specifically with bitumen); figuratively, to expiate or condone, to placate or cancel. In the KJV it is rendered: appease, make (an atonement, cleanse, disannul, forgive, be merciful, pacify, pardon, purge (away), put off, (make) reconcile(-liation).
H3723: From כָּפַר; a village (as protected by walls): -village. Compare כְּפִיר.
H3724: From כָּפַר; properly, a cover, i.e. (literally) a village (as covered in); (specifically) bitumen (as used for coating), and the henna plant (as used for dyeing); figuratively, a redemption-price. In the KJV it is rendered: bribe, camphire, pitch, ransom, satisfaction, sum of money, village.
H3726: From כְּפַר and עַמּוֹנִי, with the article interposed; village of the Ammonite; Kefar-ha-Ammoni, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Chefar-haamonai.
H3727: From כָּפַר; a lid (used only of the cover of the sacred Ark). In the KJV it is rendered: mercy seat.
H3728: A primitive root; to tread down; figuratively, to humiliate. In the KJV it is rendered: cover.
H3729: (Aramaic) a root of uncertain correspondence; to fetter. In the KJV it is rendered: bind.
H3730: Or (Am. 9:1) kaphtowr; probably from an unused root meaning to encircle; a chaplet; but used only in an architectonic sense, i.e. the capital of a column, or a wreath-like button or disk on the candelabrum: knop, (upper) lintel.
H3731: Or (Am. 9:7) Kaphtowr; apparently the same as כַּפְתֹּר; Caphtor (i.e. a wreath-shaped island), the original seat of the Philistines. In the KJV it is rendered: Caphtor.
H3732: Patrial from כַּפְתּוֹר; a Caphtorite (collectively) or native of Caphtor. In the KJV it is rendered: Caphthorim, Caphtorim(-s).
H3733: From כָּרַר in the sense of plumpness; a ram (as full-grown and fat), including a battering-ram (as butting); hence, a meadow (as for sheep); also a pad or camel's saddle (as puffed out). In the KJV it is rendered: captain, furniture, lamb, (large) pasture, ram.
H3734: From the same as כּוּר; properly, a deep round vessel, i.e. (specifically) a cor or measure for things dry. In the KJV it is rendered: cor, measure.
H3735: (Aramaic) probably corresponding to כָּרָה in the sense of piercing (figuratively); to grieve. In the KJV it is rendered: be grieved.
H3736: From the same as כֶּ֫בֶל; to gird or clothe: -clothed.
H3737: (Aramaic) from a verb corresponding to that of מְכֻרְבָּל; a mantle. In the KJV it is rendered: hat.
H3738: A primitive root; properly, to dig; figuratively, to plot; generally, to bore or open. In the KJV it is rendered: dig, X make (a banquet), open.
H3739: Usually assigned as a primitive root, but probably only a special application of כָּרָה (through the common idea of planning implied in a bargain); to purchase. In the KJV it is rendered: buy, prepare.
H3740: From כָּרָה; a purchase. In the KJV it is rendered: provision.
H3741: Feminine of כָּר; a meadow. In the KJV it is rendered: cottage.
H3742: Of uncertain derivation; a cherub or imaginary figure. In the KJV it is rendered: cherub, (plural) cherubims.
H3743: The same as כְּרוּב; Kerub, a place in Bab.: -Cherub.
H3744: (Aramaic) from כְּרַז; a herald. In the KJV it is rendered: herald.
H3745: (Aramaic) probably of Greek origin; to proclaim. In the KJV it is rendered: make a proclamation.
H3746: Perhaps an abridged plural of כָּר in the sense of leader (of the flock); a life-guardsman. In the KJV it is rendered: captains, Cherethites (from the margin).
H3747: From כָּרַת; a cut; Kerith, a brook of Palestine: -Cherith.
H3748: From כָּרַת; a cutting (of the matrimonial bond), i.e. divorce. In the KJV it is rendered: divorce(-ment).
H3749: Expanded from the same as כַּבּוֹן; a rim or top margin. In the KJV it is rendered: compass.
H3750: Probably of foreign origin; the crocus. In the KJV it is rendered: saffron.
H3751: Of foreign derivation; Karkemish, a place in Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Carchemish.
H3752: Of Persian origin; Karkas, a eunuch of Xerxes: -Carcas.
H3753: From כָּרַר; a dromedary (from its rapid motion as if dancing). In the KJV it is rendered: swift beast.
H3754: From an unused root of uncertain meaning; a garden or vineyard. In the KJV it is rendered: vines, (increase of the) vineyard(-s), vintage.
H3755: Active participle of an imaginary denominative from כָּ֫רֶם; a vinedresser. In the KJV it is rendered: vine dresser (as one or two words).
H3756: From כָּ֫רֶם; gardener; Karmi, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Carmi.
H3757: Patronymically from כַּרְמִי; a Karmite or descendant of Karmi. In the KJV it is rendered: Carmites.
H3758: Probably of foreign origin; carmine, a deep red: -crimson.
H3759: From כָּ֫רֶם; a planted field (garden, orchard, vineyard or park); by implication, garden produce. In the KJV it is rendered: full (green) ears (of corn), fruitful field (place), plentiful (field).
H3760: The same as כַּרְמֶל; Karmel, the name of a hill and of a town in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Carmel, fruitful (plentiful) field, (place).
H3761: Patron from כַּרְמֶל; a Karmelite or inhabitant of Karmel (the town). In the KJV it is rendered: Carmelite.
H3762: Feminine of כַּרְמְלִי; a Karmelitess or female inhabitant of Karmel. In the KJV it is rendered: Carmelitess.
H3763: Of uncertain derivation; Keran, an aboriginal Idumaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Cheran.
H3764: (Aramaic) corresponding to כִּסֵּא; a throne. In the KJV it is rendered: throne.
H3765: From כָּסַם; to lay waste. In the KJV it is rendered: waste.
H3766: A primitive root; to bend the knee; by implication, to sink, to prostrate. In the KJV it is rendered: bow (down, self), bring down (low), cast down, couch, fall, feeble, kneeling, sink, smite (stoop) down, subdue, X very.
H3767: From כָּרַע; the leg (from the knee to the ankle) of men or locusts (only in the dual). In the KJV it is rendered: leg.
H3768: Of foreign origin; byssus or fine vegetable wool: -green.
H3769: A primitive root; to dance (i.e. whirl): -dance(-ing).
H3770: By variation from קָרַס; the paunch or belly (as swelling out). In the KJV it is rendered: belly.
H3771: Of foreign origin; Karshena, a courtier of Xerxes. In the KJV it is rendered: Carshena.
H3772: A primitive root; to cut (off, down or asunder); by implication, to destroy or consume; specifically, to covenant (i.e. make an alliance or bargain, originally by cutting flesh and passing between the pieces). In the KJV it is rendered: be chewed, be con-(feder-)ate, covenant, cut (down, off), destroy, fail, feller, be freed, hew (down), make a league ((covenant)), X lose, perish, X utterly, X want.
H3773: Passive participle feminine of כָּרַת; something cut, i.e. a hewn timber. In the KJV it is rendered: beam.
H3774: Probably from כָּרַת in the sense of executioner; a Kerethite or life-guardsman (compare טַבָּח) (only collectively in the singular as plural). In the KJV it is rendered: Cherethims, Cherethites.
H3775: Apparently by transposition for כֶּ֫בֶשׂ; a young sheep. In the KJV it is rendered: lamb.
H3776: Feminine of כֶּ֫שֶׂב; a young ewe. In the KJV it is rendered: lamb.
H3777: From an unused root of uncertain meaning; Kesed, a relative of Abraham. In the KJV it is rendered: Onesed.
H3778: Or (occasionally with enclitic) Kasdiymah; towards the Kasdites. In the KJV it is rendered: into Chaldea), patronymically from Kesed (only in the plural); a Kasdite, or descendant of Kesed; by implication, a Chaldaean (as if so descended); also an astrologer (as if proverbial of that people:--Chaldeans, Chaldees, inhabitants of Chaldea.
H3779: (Aramaic) corresponding to כַּשְׂדִּי; a Chaldaean or inhabitant of Chaldaea; by implication, a Magian or professional astrologer. In the KJV it is rendered: Chaldean.
H3780: A primitive root; to grow fat (i.e. be covered with flesh). In the KJV it is rendered: be covered.
H3781: From כָּשַׁל; properly, a feller, i.e. an axe: -ax.
H3782: A primitive root; to totter or waver (through weakness of the legs, especially the ankle); by implication, to falter, stumble, faint or fall. In the KJV it is rendered: bereave (from the margin), cast down, be decayed, (cause to) fail, (cause, make to) fall (down, -ing), feeble, be (the) ruin(-ed, of), (be) overthrown, (cause to) stumble, X utterly, be weak.
H3783: From כָּשַׁל; properly, a tottering, i.e. ruin. In the KJV it is rendered: fall.
H3784: A primitive root; properly, to whisper a spell, i.e. to inchant or practise magic. In the KJV it is rendered: sorcerer, (use) witch(-craft).
H3785: From כָּשַׁף; magic. In the KJV it is rendered: sorcery, witchcraft.
H3786: From כָּשַׁף; a magician. In the KJV it is rendered: sorcerer.
H3787: A primitive root properly, to be straight or right; by implication, to be acceptable; also to succeed or prosper. In the KJV it is rendered: direct, be right, prosper.
H3788: From כָּשֵׁר; success, advantage. In the KJV it is rendered: equity, good, right.
H3789: A primitive root; to grave, by implication, to write (describe, inscribe, prescribe, subscribe). In the KJV it is rendered: describe, record, prescribe, subscribe, write(-ing, -ten).
H3790: (Aramaic) corresponding to כָּתַב. In the KJV it is rendered: write(-ten).
H3791: From כָּתַב; something written, i.e. a writing, record or book. In the KJV it is rendered: register, scripture, writing.
H3792: (Aramaic) corresponding to כְּתָב. In the KJV it is rendered: prescribing, writing(-ten).
H3793: From כָּתַב; a letter or other mark branded on the skin. In the KJV it is rendered: X any (mark).
H3794: Or Kittiyiy; patrial from an unused name denoting Cyprus (only in the plural); a Kittite or Cypriote; hence, an islander in general, i.e. the Greeks or Romans on the shores opposite Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Chittim, Kittim.
H3796: From an unused root meaning to compact; a wall (as gathering inmates). In the KJV it is rendered: wall.
H3797: (Aramaic) corresponding to כֹּ֫תֶל. In the KJV it is rendered: wall.
H3798: From כֹּ֫תֶל and אּישׁ; wall of a man; Kithlish, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Kithlish.
H3799: A primitive root; properly, to carve or engrave, i.e. (by implication) to inscribe indelibly. In the KJV it is rendered: mark.
H3800: From כָּתַם; properly, something carved out, i.e. ore; hence, gold (pure as originally mined). In the KJV it is rendered: ((most) fine, pure) gold(-en wedge).
H3801: Or kuttoneth; from an unused root meaning to cover (compare כָּתֵף); a shirt. In the KJV it is rendered: coat, garment, robe.
H3802: From an unused root meaning to clothe; the shoulder (proper, i.e. upper end of the arm; as being the spot where the garments hang); figuratively, side-piece or lateral projection of anything. In the KJV it is rendered: arm, corner, shoulder(-piece), side, undersetter.
H3803: A primitive root; to enclose; hence (in a friendly sense) to crown, (in a hostile one) to besiege; also to wait (as restraining oneself). In the KJV it is rendered: beset round, compass about, be crowned inclose round, suffer.
H3804: From כָּתַר; properly, a circlet, i.e. a diadem: -crown.
H3805: Feminine active participle of כָּתַר; the capital of a column. In the KJV it is rendered: chapiter.
H3806: A primitive root; to butt or pound. In the KJV it is rendered: bray.
H3807: A primitive root; to bruise or violently strike. In the KJV it is rendered: beat (down, to pieces), break in pieces, crushed, destroy, discomfit, smite, stamp.
H3808: Or lowi; or loh (Deut. 3:11); a primitive particle; not (the simple or abs. negation); by implication, no; often used with other particles (as follows). In the KJV it is rendered: X before, + or else, ere, + except, ig(-norant), much, less, nay, neither, never, no((-ne), -r, (-thing)), (X as though.
H3809: (Aramaic) or lah (Aramaic) (Dan. 4:32); corresponding to לֹא. In the KJV it is rendered: or even, neither, no(-ne, -r), ((can-))not, as nothing, without.
H3810: Or Low Dbar (2 Samuel 9:4,5); or Lidbir (Joshua 13:26); (probably rather Lodbar); from לֹא and דֹּ֫בֶר; pastureless; Lo-Debar, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Debir, Lo-debar.
H3811: A primitive root; to tire; (figuratively) to be (or make) disgusted. In the KJV it is rendered: faint, grieve, lothe, (be, make) weary (selves).
H3812: From לָאָה; weary; Leah, a wife of Jacob. In the KJV it is rendered: Leah.
H3813: A primitive root; to muffle. In the KJV it is rendered: cover.
H3814: From לָאַט (or perhaps for active participle of לוּט); properly, muffled, i.e. silently. In the KJV it is rendered: softly.
H3815: From the prepositional prefix and אֵל; (belonging) to God; Lael an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Lael.
H3816: Or l owm; from an unused root meaning to gather; a community. In the KJV it is rendered: nation, people.
H3817: Plural of לְאֹם; communities; Leum mim, an Arabian. In the KJV it is rendered: Leummim.
H3818: From לֹא and עָם with pronominal suffix; not my people; Lo-Ammi, the symbolic name of a son of Hosea. In the KJV it is rendered: Lo-ammi.
H3819: From לֹא and רָחַם; not pitied; Lo- Ruchamah, the symbol. name of a son of Hosea. In the KJV it is rendered: Lo-ruhamah.
H3820: A form of לֵבָב; the heart; also used (figuratively) very widely for the feelings, the will and even the intellect; likewise for the centre of anything. In the KJV it is rendered: + care for, comfortably, consent, X considered, courag(-eous), friend(-ly), ((broken-), (hard-), (merry-), (stiff-), (stout-), double) heart((-ed)), X heed, X I, kindly, midst, mind(-ed), X regard((-ed)), X themselves, X unawares, understanding, X well, willingly, wisdom.
H3821: (Aramaic) corresponding to לֵב. In the KJV it is rendered: heart.
H3822: Plural of לָבִיא; lionesses; Lebaoth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Lebaoth.
H3823: A primitive root; properly, to be enclosed (as if with fat); by implication (as denominative from לֵבָב) to unheart, i.e. (in a good sense) transport (with love), or (in a bad sense) stultify; also (as denominative from לְבִבוֹת) to make cakes. In the KJV it is rendered: make cakes, ravish, be wise.
H3824: From לָבַב; the heart (as the most interior organ); used also like לֵב. In the KJV it is rendered: + bethink themselves, breast, comfortably, courage, ((faint), (tender-)heart((-ed)), midst, mind, X unawares, understanding.
H3825: (Aramaic) corresponding to לֵבָב. In the KJV it is rendered: heart.
H3826: Feminine of לֵב; the heart. In the KJV it is rendered: heart.
H3827: For לֶהָבָה; flame. In the KJV it is rendered: flame.
H3828: Or lbonah; from לָבָן; frankincense (from its whiteness or perhaps that of its smoke): -(frank-)incense.
H3829: The same as לְבוֹנָה; Lebonah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Lebonah.
H3830: Or lbush; from לָבַשׁ; a garment (literally or figuratively); by implication (euphem.) a wife. In the KJV it is rendered: apparel, clothed with, clothing, garment, raiment, vestment, vesture.
H3831: (Aramaic) corresponding to לְבוּשׁ. In the KJV it is rendered: garment.
H3832: A primitive root; to overthrow; intransposed, to fall. In the KJV it is rendered: fall.
H3833: Or (Ezek. 19:2) lbiyao; irreg. masculine plural lbaviym; irreg. feminine plural lbaeowth; from an unused root men. to roar; a lion (properly, a lioness as the fiercer (although not a roarer; compare אֲרִי)). In the KJV it is rendered: (great, old, stout) lion, lioness, young (lion).
H3834: Or rather lbibah; from לָבַב in its original sense of fatness (or perhaps of folding); a cake (either as fried or turned). In the KJV it is rendered: cake.
H3835: A primitive root; to be (or become) white; also (as denominative from לְבֵנִים) to make bricks. In the KJV it is rendered: make brick, be (made, make) white(-r).
H3836: Or (Gen. 49:12) laben; from לָבַן; white. In the KJV it is rendered: white.
H3837: The same as לָבָן; Laban, a Mesopotamian; also a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Laban.
H3838: Or Lbanah; the same as לְבָנָה; Lebana or Lebanah, one of the Nethinim. In the KJV it is rendered: Lebana, Lebanah.
H3839: From לָבַן; some sort of whitish tree, perhaps the storax. In the KJV it is rendered: poplar.
H3840: From לָבַן; properly, whiteness, i.e. (by implication) transparency. In the KJV it is rendered: paved.
H3841: The same as לִבְנֶה; Libnah, a place in the Desert and one in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Libnah.
H3842: From לָבַן; properly, (the) white, i.e. the moon. In the KJV it is rendered: moon.
H3843: From לָבַן; a brick (from the whiteness of the clay). In the KJV it is rendered: (altar of) brick, tile.
H3844: From לְבַב; (the) white mountain (from its snow); Lebanon, a mountain range in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Lebanon.
H3845: From לָבַן; white; Libni, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Libni.
H3846: Patronymically from לִבְנִי; a Libnite or descendants of Libni (collectively). In the KJV it is rendered: Libnites.
H3847: Or labesh; a primitive root; properly, wrap around, i.e. (by implication) to put on a garment or clothe (oneself, or another), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: (in) apparel, arm, array (self), clothe (self), come upon, put (on, upon), wear.
H3848: (Aramaic) corresponding to לָבַשׁ. In the KJV it is rendered: clothe.
H3849: From an unused root apparently meaning to deepen or hollow (like כַּד); a log or measure for liquids. In the KJV it is rendered: log (of oil).
H3850: From an unused root of uncertain signification; Lod, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Lod.
H3851: From an usused root meaning to gleam; a flash; figuratively, a sharply polished blade or point of a weapon. In the KJV it is rendered: blade, bright, flame, glittering.
H3852: Or lahebeth; feminine of לַ֫הַב, and meaning the same. In the KJV it is rendered: flame(-ming), head (of a spear).
H3853: Plural of לַ֫הַב; flames; Lehabim, a son of Mizrain, and his descendants. In the KJV it is rendered: Lehabim.
H3854: From an unused root meaning to be eager; intense mental application. In the KJV it is rendered: study.
H3855: From an unused root meaning to glow (compare לַ֫הַב) or else to be earnest (compare לַ֫הַג); Lahad, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Lahad.
H3856: A primitive root meaning properly, to burn, i.e. (by implication) to be rabid (figuratively, insane); also (from the exhaustion of frenzy) to languish. In the KJV it is rendered: faint, mad.
H3857: A primitive root; properly, to lick, i.e. (by implication) to blaze. In the KJV it is rendered: burn (up), set on fire, flaming, kindle.
H3858: From לָהַט; a blaze; also (from the idea of enwrapping) magic (as covert). In the KJV it is rendered: flaming, enchantment.
H3859: A primitive root; properly, to burn in, i.e. (figuratively) to rankle. In the KJV it is rendered: wound.
H3860: From the prepositional prefix meaning to or for and הֵן; popularly for if; hence, therefore. In the KJV it is rendered: for them (by mistake for prepositional suffix).
H3861: (Aramaic) corresponding to לָהֵן; therefore; also except. In the KJV it is rendered: but, except, save, therefore, wherefore.
H3862: Probably from an unused root meaning to gather; an assembly. In the KJV it is rendered: company.
H3863: Or lu; or luw; a conditional particle; if; by implication (interj. as a wish) would that!. In the KJV it is rendered: if (haply), peradventure, I pray thee, though, I would, would God (that).
H3864: Or Lubbiy (Dan. 11:43); partrial from a name probably derived from an unused root meaning to thirst, i.e. a dry region; apparently a Libyan or inhabitant of interior Africa (only in plural): -Lubim(-s), Libyans.
H3865: Probably of foreign derivation; Lud, the name of two nations. In the KJV it is rendered: Lud, Lydia.
H3866: Or Luwdiyiy; patrial from לוּד; a Ludite or inhabitants of Lud (only in plural). In the KJV it is rendered: Ludim.
H3867: A primitive root; properly, to twine, i.e. (by implication) to unite, to remain; also to borrow (as a form of obligation) or (caus.) to lend. In the KJV it is rendered: abide with, borrow(-er), cleave, join (self), lend(-er).
H3868: A primitive root; to turn aside (compare לָוָה, לוּט and לוּן), i.e. (literally) to depart, (figuratively) be perverse. In the KJV it is rendered: depart, froward, perverse(-ness).
H3869: Probably of foreign origin; some kind of nut-tree, perhaps the almond. In the KJV it is rendered: hazel.
H3870: Probably from לוּז (as growing there); Luz, the name of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Luz.
H3871: Or luach; from a primitive root; probably meaning to glisten; a tablet (as polished), of stone, wood or metal. In the KJV it is rendered: board, plate, table.
H3872: Or Luchowth (Jer. 48:5); from the same as ל֫וּחַ; floored; Luchith, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Luhith.
H3873: Active participle of לָחַשׁ; (the) enchanter; Lochesh, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Hallohesh, Haloshesh (includ.
H3874: A primitive root; to wrap up. In the KJV it is rendered: cast, wrap.
H3875: From לוּט; a veil. In the KJV it is rendered: covering.
H3876: The same as לוֹט; Lot, Abraham's nephew. In the KJV it is rendered: Lot.
H3877: From לוֹט; covering; Lotan, an Idumaean: -Lotan.
H3878: From לָוָה; attached; Levi, a son of Jacob. In the KJV it is rendered: Levi.
H3879: (Aramaic) corresponding to לִוְיַת. In the KJV it is rendered: Levite.
H3880: From לָוָה; something attached, i.e. a wreath: -ornament.
H3881: Or Leviy; patronymically from לֵוִי; a Levite or descendant of Levi. In the KJV it is rendered: Leviite.
H3882: From לָוָה; a wreathed animal, i.e. a serpent (especially the crocodile or some other large sea- monster); figuratively, the constellation of the dragon; also as a symbol of Bab. In the KJV it is rendered: leviathan, mourning.
H3883: From an unused root meaning to fold back; a spiral step. In the KJV it is rendered: winding stair.
H3884: Or luwley; from לוּא and לֹא; if not. In the KJV it is rendered: except, had not, if (.
H3885: Or liyn; a primitive root; to stop (usually over night); by implication, to stay permanently; hence (in a bad sense) to be obstinate (especially in words, to complain). In the KJV it is rendered: abide (all night), continue, dwell, endure, grudge, be left, lie all night, (cause to) lodge (all night, in, -ing, this night), (make to) murmur, remain, tarry (all night, that night).
H3886: A primitive root; to gulp; figuratively, to be rash. In the KJV it is rendered: swallow down (up).
H3887: A primitive root; properly, to make mouths at, i.e. to scoff; hence (from the effort to pronounce a foreign language) to interpret, or (generally) intercede. In the KJV it is rendered: ambassador, have in derision, interpreter, make a mock, mocker, scorn(-er, -ful), teacher.
H3888: A primitive root; to knead. In the KJV it is rendered: knead.
H3889: From לוּשׁ; kneading; Lush, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Laish (from the margin).
H3890: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to לָוָה; properly, adhesion, i.e. (as preposition) with. In the KJV it is rendered: X thee.
H3891: From לוּז; perverseness. In the KJV it is rendered: perverse.
H3892: From an unused root meaning to be new; fresh, i.e. unused or undried. In the KJV it is rendered: green, moist.
H3893: From the same as לָח; freshness, i.e. vigor: -natural force.
H3894: Or lachum; passive participle of לָחַם; properly, eaten, i.e. food; also flesh, i.e. body. In the KJV it is rendered: while.
H3895: From an unused root meaning to be soft; the cheek (from its fleshiness); hence, the jaw-bone. In the KJV it is rendered: cheek (bone), jaw (bone).
H3896: A form of לֶ֫חִי; Lechi, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Lehi.
H3897: A primitive root; to lick. In the KJV it is rendered: lick (up).
H3898: A primitive root; to feed on; figuratively, to consume; by implication, to battle (as destruction). In the KJV it is rendered: devour, eat, X ever, fight(-ing), overcome, prevail, (make) war(-ring).
H3899: From לָחַם; food (for man or beast), especially bread, or grain (for making it). In the KJV it is rendered: ((shew-))bread, X eat, food, fruit, loaf, meat, victuals.
H3900: (Aramaic) corresponding to לָ֫חֶם. In the KJV it is rendered: feast.
H3901: From לָחַם, battle. In the KJV it is rendered: war.
H3902: From לָ֫חֶם; foodful; Lachmi, an Israelite; or rather probably a brief form (or perhaps erroneous transcription) for בֵּית הַלַּחְמִי. In the KJV it is rendered: Lahmi.
H3903: Probably by erroneous transcription for Lachmam; from לָ֫חֶם; food-like; Lachmam or Lachmas, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Lahmam.
H3904: (Aramaic) from an unused root of uncertain meaning; a concubine. In the KJV it is rendered: concubine.
H3905: A primitive root; properly, to press, i.e. (figuratively) to distress. In the KJV it is rendered: afflict, crush, force, hold fast, oppress(-or), thrust self.
H3906: From לָחַץ; distress. In the KJV it is rendered: affliction, oppression.
H3907: A primitive root; to whisper; by implication, to mumble a spell (as a magician). In the KJV it is rendered: charmer, whisper (together).
H3908: From לָחַשׁ; properly, a whisper, i.e. by implication, (in a good sense) a private prayer, (in a bad one) an incantation; concretely, an amulet. In the KJV it is rendered: charmed, earring, enchantment, orator, prayer.
H3909: A form of לָאט or else participle from לוּט; properly, covered, i.e. secret; by implication, incantation; also secrecy or (adverb) covertly: -enchantment, privily, secretly, softly.
H3910: Probably from לוּט; a gum (from its sticky nature), probably ladanum. In the KJV it is rendered: myrrh.
H3911: From an unused root meaning to hide; a kind of lizard (from its covert habits). In the KJV it is rendered: lizard.
H3912: Masculine plural of passive participle of לָטַשׁ; hammered (i.e. oppressed) ones; Letushim, an Arabian tribe. In the KJV it is rendered: Letushim.
H3913: A primitive root; properly, to hammer out (an edge), i.e. to sharpen. In the KJV it is rendered: instructer, sharp(-en), whet.
H3914: A form of לִוְיַת; a wreath. In the KJV it is rendered: addition.
H3915: Or (Isa. 21:11) leyl; also laylah; from the same as לוּלִים; properly, a twist (away of the light), i.e. night; figuratively, adversity. In the KJV it is rendered: ((mid-))night (season).
H3916: (Aramaic) corresponding to לָאֵל. In the KJV it is rendered: night.
H3917: From לַיְלָה; a night spectre. In the KJV it is rendered: screech owl.
H3918: From לוּשׁ in the sense of crushing; a lion (from his destructive blows). In the KJV it is rendered: (old)lion.
H3919: The same as לַ֫יִשׁ; Laish, the name of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Laish.
H3920: A primitive root; to catch (in a net, trap or pit); generally, to capture or occupy; also to choose (by lot); figuratively, to cohere. In the KJV it is rendered: X at all, catch (self), be frozen, be holden, stick together, take.
H3921: From לָכַד; something to capture with, i.e. a noose. In the KJV it is rendered: being taken.
H3922: From יָלַך; a journey; Lekah, a place in Palestine: -Lecah.
H3923: From an unused root of uncertain meaning; Lakish, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Lachish.
H3924: From the same as לוּלִים; a loop. In the KJV it is rendered: loop.
H3925: A primitive root; properly, to goad, i.e. (by implication) to teach (the rod being an Oriental incentive):(un-) accustomed, X diligently, expert, instruct, learn, skilful, teach(-er, - ing).
H3926: A prol. and separable form of the prepositional prefix; to or for. In the KJV it is rendered: at, for, to, upon.
H3927: Or Lmow el; from לְמוֹ and אֵל; (belonging) to God; Lemuel or Lemoel, a symbolic name of Solomon: -Lemuel.
H3928: Or limmud; from לָמַד; instructed: -accustomed, disciple, learned, taught, used.
H3929: From an unused root of uncertain meaning; Lemek, the name of two antediluvian patriarchs. In the KJV it is rendered: Lamech.
H3930: From לָעַע; the gullet. In the KJV it is rendered: throat.
H3931: A primitive root; to deride. In the KJV it is rendered: mock.
H3932: A primitive root; to deride; by implication (as if imitating a foreigner) to speak unintelligibly. In the KJV it is rendered: have in derision, laugh (to scorn), mock (on), stammering.
H3933: From לָעַג; derision, scoffing. In the KJV it is rendered: derision, scorn (-ing).
H3934: From לָעַג; a buffoon; also a foreigner. In the KJV it is rendered: mocker, stammering.
H3935: From an unused root of uncertain meaning; Ladah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Laadah.
H3936: From the same as לַעְדָּה; Ladan, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Laadan.
H3937: A primitive root; to speak in a foreign tongue: -strange language.
H3938: A primitive root; to swallow greedily; causatively, to feed. In the KJV it is rendered: feed.
H3939: From an unused root supposed to mean to curse; wormwood (regarded as poisonous, and therefore accursed). In the KJV it is rendered: hemlock, wormwood.
H3940: Or lappid; from an unused root probably meaning to shine; a flambeau, lamp or flame. In the KJV it is rendered: (fire-)brand, (burning) lamp, lightning, torch.
H3941: Feminine plural of לַפִּיד; Lappidoth, the husband of Deborah. In the KJV it is rendered: Lappidoth.
H3942: From the prepositional prefix (to or for) and פָּנִים; anterior. In the KJV it is rendered: before.
H3943: A primitive root; properly, to bend, i.e. (by implication) to clasp; also (reflexively) to turn around or aside. In the KJV it is rendered: take hold, turn aside (self).
H3944: From לִיץ; derision. In the KJV it is rendered: scornful(-ning).
H3945: A primitive root; to deride. In the KJV it is rendered: scorn.
H3946: From an unused root thought to mean to stop up by a barricade; perhaps fortification; Lakkum, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Lakum.

H3949: From לָקַח; learned; Likchi, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Likhi.
H3950: A primitive root; properly, to pick up, i.e. (generally) to gather; specifically, to glean. In the KJV it is rendered: gather (up), glean.
H3951: From לָקַט; the gleaning. In the KJV it is rendered: gleaning.
H3952: A primitive root; to lick or lap. In the KJV it is rendered: lap, lick.
H3953: A primitive root; to gather the after crop. In the KJV it is rendered: gather.
H3954: From לָקַשׁ; the after crop. In the KJV it is rendered: latter growth.
H3955: From an unused root of uncertain meaning; apparently juice, i.e. (figuratively) vigor; also a sweet or fat cake. In the KJV it is rendered: fresh, moisture.
H3956: Or lashon; also (in plural) feminine lshonah; from לָשַׁן; the tongue (of man or animals), used literally (as the instrument of licking, eating, or speech), and figuratively (speech, an ingot, a fork of flame, a cove of water). H3957: From an unused root of uncertain meaning; a room in a building (whether for storage, eating, or lodging). In the KJV it is rendered: chamber, parlour.
H3958: From an unused root of uncertain meaning; a gem, perhaps the jacinth. In the KJV it is rendered: ligure.
H3959: The same as לֶ֫שֶׁם; Leshem, a place in Palestine: -Leshem.
H3960: A primitive root; properly, to lick; but used only as a denominative from לָשׁוֹן; to wag the tongue, i.e. to calumniate. In the KJV it is rendered: accuse, slander.
H3961: (Aramaic) corresponding to לָשׁוֹן; speech, i.e. a nation. In the KJV it is rendered: language.
H3962: From an unused root thought to mean to break through; a boiling spring; Lesha, a place probably East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Lasha.
H3963: From an unused root of uncertain meaning; a measure for things dry. In the KJV it is rendered: half homer.
H3964: (Aramaic) corresponding to מָה; (as indef.) that. In the KJV it is rendered: + what.
H3965: From אָבַס; a granary. In the KJV it is rendered: storehouse.
H3966: From the same as אוּד; properly, vehemence, i.e. (with or without preposition) vehemently; by implication, wholly, speedily, etc. (often with other words as an intensive or superlative; especially when repeated). In the KJV it is rendered: diligently, especially, exceeding(-ly), far, fast, good, great(-ly), X louder and louder, might(-ily, -y), (so) much, quickly, (so) sore, utterly, very (+ much, sore), well.
H3967: Or metyah; properly, a primitive numeral; a hundred; also as a multiplicative and a fraction. In the KJV it is rendered: hundred((-fold), -th), + sixscore.
H3968: The same as NONE; Meah, a tower in Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: Meah.
H3969: (Aramaic) corresponding to NONE. In the KJV it is rendered: hundred.
H3970: From אָוָה; a desire. In the KJV it is rendered: desire.
H3971: Usually muwm; as if passive participle from an unused root probably meaning to stain; a blemish (physically or morally). In the KJV it is rendered: blemish, blot, spot.
H3972: Apparently a form of מְאוּם; properly, a speck or point, i.e. (by implication) something; with negative, nothing. In the KJV it is rendered: fault, + no(-ught), ought, somewhat, any ((no-))thing.
H3973: From מָאַס; refuse. In the KJV it is rendered: refuse.
H3974: Or maor; also (in plural) feminine mpowrah; or morah; from אוֹר; properly, a luminous body or luminary, i.e. (abstractly) light (as an element): figuratively, brightness, i.e.cheerfulness; specifically, a chandelier. In the KJV it is rendered: bright, light.
H3975: Feminine passive participle of אוֹר; something lighted, i.e. an aperture; by implication, a crevice or hole (of a serpent). In the KJV it is rendered: den.
H3976: From אָזַן; (only in the dual) a pair of scales: -balances.
H3977: (Aramaic) corresponding to מֹאזְנָ֫יִם. In the KJV it is rendered: balances.
H3978: From אָכַל; an eatable (includ. provender, flesh and fruit). In the KJV it is rendered: food, fruit, ((bake-)) meat(-s), victual.
H3979: From אָכַל; something to eat with,- i.e. a knife. In the KJV it is rendered: knife.
H3980: From אָכַל; something eaten (by fire), i.e. fuel. In the KJV it is rendered: fuel.
H3981: From אָמַץ; strength, i.e. (plural) resources. In the KJV it is rendered: force.
H3982: From אָמַר; something (authoritatively) said, i.e. an edict. In the KJV it is rendered: commandment, decree.
H3983: (Aramaic) corresponding to מַאֲמַר. In the KJV it is rendered: appointment, word.
H3984: (Aramaic) probably from a root corresponding to אָנָה in the sense of an inclosure by sides; a utensil. In the KJV it is rendered: vessel.
H3985: A primitive root; to refuse. In the KJV it is rendered: refuse, X utterly.
H3986: From מָאֵן; unwilling. In the KJV it is rendered: refuse.
H3987: From מָאֵן; refractory. In the KJV it is rendered: refuse.
H3988: A primitive root; to spurn; also (intransitively) to disappear. In the KJV it is rendered: abhor, cast away (off), contemn, despise, disdain, (become) loathe(some), melt away, refuse, reject, reprobate, X utterly, vile person.
H3989: From אָפָה; something baked, i.e. a batch: -baken.
H3990: From the same as אָפֵל; something opaque: -darkness.
H3992: A primitive root; to be bitter or (causatively) to embitter, i.e. be painful. In the KJV it is rendered: fretting, picking.
H3993: From אָרַב; an ambuscade. In the KJV it is rendered: lie in ambush, ambushment, lurking place, lying in wait.
H3994: From אָרַר; an execration. In the KJV it is rendered: curse.
H3995: From בָּדַל; a separation, i.e. (concretely) a separate place. In the KJV it is rendered: separate.

H3997: Feminine of מָבוֹא; a haven. In the KJV it is rendered: entry.
H3998: From בּוּך; perplexity. In the KJV it is rendered: perplexity.
H3999: From יָבַל in the sense of flowing; a deluge: -flood.
H4000: From בִּין; instructing. In the KJV it is rendered: taught.
H4001: From בּוּס; a trampling. In the KJV it is rendered: treading (trodden) down (under foot).
H4002: From נָבַע; a fountain. In the KJV it is rendered: fountain, spring.
H4003: From the same as בּוּקָה; emptiness. In the KJV it is rendered: void.
H4004: From בָּחַר; select, i.e. well fortified. In the KJV it is rendered: choice.
H4005: From בָּחַר; select, i.e. best. In the KJV it is rendered: choice(-st), chosen.
H4006: The same as מִבְחָר; Mibchar, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Mibhar.
H4007: Or mebbat; from נָבַט; something expected, i.e. (abstractly) expectation. In the KJV it is rendered: expectation.
H4008: From בָּטָא; a rash utterance (hasty vow). In the KJV it is rendered: (that which.
H4009: From בָּטַח; properly, a refuge, i.e. (objective) security, or (subjective) assurance. In the KJV it is rendered: confidence, hope, sure, trust.
H4010: From בָּלַג; desistance (or rather desolation). In the KJV it is rendered: comfort self.
H4011: From בָּנָה; a building. In the KJV it is rendered: frame.
H4012: From בָּנָה; built up; Mebunnai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Mebunnai.
H4013: Also (in plural) feminine (Dan. 11:15) mibtsarah; from בָּצַר; a fortification, castle, or fortified city; figuratively, a defender. In the KJV it is rendered: (de-, most) fenced, fortress, (most) strong (hold).
H4014: The same as מִבְצָר; Mibtsar, an Idumaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Mibzar.
H4015: From בָּרַח; a refugee. In the KJV it is rendered: fugitive.
H4016: From בּוּשׁ; (plural) the (male) pudenda. In the KJV it is rendered: secrets.
H4017: From the same as בְּשָׂמִים; fragrant; Mibsam, the name of an Ishmaelite and of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Mibsam.
H4018: From בָּשַׁל; a cooking hearth. In the KJV it is rendered: boiling-place.
H4019: From the same as גָּבִישׁ; stiffening; Magbish, an Israelite, or a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Magbish.
H4020: From גָּבַל; a border. In the KJV it is rendered: end.
H4021: From the same as גִּבְעָה; a cap (as hemispherical). In the KJV it is rendered: bonnet.
H4022: From an unused root probably meaning to be eminent; properly, a distinguished thing; hence something valuable, as a product or fruit. In the KJV it is rendered: pleasant, precious fruit (thing).
H4023: (Zech. 12 or Mgiddow; from גָּדַד; rendezvous; Megiddon or Megiddo, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Megiddo, Megiddon.
H4024: Or Migdol; probably of Egyptian origin; Migdol, a place in Egypt. In the KJV it is rendered: Migdol, tower.
H4025: From מֶ֫גֶד and אֵל; preciousness of God; Magdiel, an Idumaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Magdiel.
H4026: Also (in plural) feminine migdalah; from גָּדַל; a tower (from its size or height); by analogy, a rostrum; figuratively, a (pyramidal) bed of flowers. In the KJV it is rendered: castle, flower, tower.
H4027: From מִגְדָּל and אֵל; tower of God; Migdal-El, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Migdal-el.
H4028: From מִגְדָּל and גַּד; tower of Fortune; Migdal-Gad, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Migdal-gad.
H4029: From מִגְדָּל and עֵ֫דֶר; tower of a flock; Migdal-Eder, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Migdal-eder, tower of the flock.
H4030: From the same as מֶ֫גֶד; preciousness, i.e. a gem. In the KJV it is rendered: precious thing, present.
H4031: From גּוֹג; Magog, a son of Japheth; also a barbarous northern region. In the KJV it is rendered: Magog.
H4032: Or (Lam. 2:22) maguwr; from גּוּר in the sense of fearing; a fright (objective or subjective). In the KJV it is rendered: fear, terror.
H4033: Or magur; from גּוּר in the sense of lodging; a temporary abode; by extension, a permanent residence. In the KJV it is rendered: dwelling, pilgrimage, where sojourn, be a stranger.
H4034: Feminine of מָגוֹר; affright. In the KJV it is rendered: fear.
H4035: Feminine of מָגוֹר or of מָגוּר; a fright; also a granary. In the KJV it is rendered: barn, fear.
H4036: From מָגוֹר and סָבִיב with the preposition inserted; affright from around; Magor-mis-Sabib, a symbolic name of Pashur. In the KJV it is rendered: Magor-missabib.
H4037: From גָּזַר; a cutting implement, i.e. a blade. In the KJV it is rendered: axe.
H4038: From an unused root meaning to reap; a sickle. In the KJV it is rendered: sickle.
H4039: From גָּלַל; a roll. In the KJV it is rendered: roll, volume.
H4040: (Aramaic) corresponding to מְגִלָּה. In the KJV it is rendered: roll.
H4041: From the same as גַּם; properly, accumulation, i.e. impulse or direction. In the KJV it is rendered: sup up.
H4042: A denominative from מָגֵן; properly, to shield; encompass with; figuratively, to rescue, to hand safely over (i.e. surrender). In the KJV it is rendered: deliver.
H4043: Also (in plural) feminine mginnah; from גָּנַן; a shield (i.e. the small one or buckler); figuratively, a protector; also the scaly hide of the crocodile. In the KJV it is rendered: X armed, buckler, defence, ruler, + scale, shield.
H4044: From מָגַן; a covering (in a bad sense), i.e. blindness or obduracy. In the KJV it is rendered: sorrow.
H4045: From גָּעַר; reproof (i.e. curse). In the KJV it is rendered: rebuke.
H4046: From נָגַף; a pestilence; by analogy, defeat. In the KJV it is rendered: (X be) plague(-d), slaughter, stroke.

H4049: (Aramaic) corresponding to מָגַר; to overthrow. In the KJV it is rendered: destroy.
H4050: From גָּרַר; a saw. In the KJV it is rendered: axe, saw.
H4051: From מָגַר; precipice; Migron, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Migron.
H4052: From גָּרַע; a ledge or offset. In the KJV it is rendered: narrowed rest.
H4053: From גָּרַף; something thrown off (by the spade), i.e. a clod. In the KJV it is rendered: clod.
H4054: Also (in plural) feminine (Ezek. 27:28) migrashah; from גָּרַשׁ; a suburb (i.e. open country whither flocks are driven from pasture); hence, the area around a building, or the margin of the sea. In the KJV it is rendered: cast out, suburb.

H4056: (Aramaic) from דְּבַח; a sacrificial altar. In the KJV it is rendered: altar.

H4059: From נָדַד; flight. In the KJV it is rendered: be gone.
H4060: Feminine of מִדּוֹ; properly, extension, i.e. height or breadth; also a measure (including its standard); hence a portion (as measured) or a vestment; specifically, tribute (as measured). In the KJV it is rendered: garment, measure(-ing, meteyard, piece, size, (great) stature, tribute, wide.
H4061: (Aramaic) or mindah (Aramaic); corresponding to מִדָּה; tribute in money. In the KJV it is rendered: toll, tribute.
H4062: Perhaps from the equivalent of דְּהַב; goldmaking, i.e. exactness. In the KJV it is rendered: golden city.
H4063: From an unused root meaning to stretch; properly, extent, i.e. measure; by implication, a dress (as measured). In the KJV it is rendered: garment.
H4064: From דָּוָה; sickness. In the KJV it is rendered: disease.
H4065: From נָדַח; seduction. In the KJV it is rendered: cause of banishment.
H4066: From דִּין; a contest or quarrel. In the KJV it is rendered: brawling, contention(-ous), discord, strife.
H4067: From the same as מַדְוֵי; extensiveness, i.e. height. In the KJV it is rendered: stature.
H4068: The same as מָדוֹן; Madon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Madon.

H4070: (Aramaic) or mdor (Aramaic); or mdar (Aramaic); from דּוּר; a dwelling. In the KJV it is rendered: dwelling.
H4071: Or mdurah; from דּוּר in the sense of accumulation; a pile of fuel. In the KJV it is rendered: pile (for fire).
H4072: From דָּחָה; overthrow. In the KJV it is rendered: ruin.
H4073: From דָּחַף; a push, i.e. ruin. In the KJV it is rendered: overthrow.

H4076: (Aramaic) corresponding to NONE. In the KJV it is rendered: Mede(-s).
H4077: (Aramaic) corresponding to NONE. In the KJV it is rendered: Median.
H4078: From מָה and דָּי; what (is) enough, i.e. sufficiently. In the KJV it is rendered: sufficiently.
H4079: A variation for מָדוֹן. In the KJV it is rendered: brawling, contention(-ous).
