H4903: (Aramaic) corresponding to מִשְׁכָּב; a bed. In the KJV it is rendered: bed.
H4904: From שָׁכַב; a bed (figuratively, a bier); abstractly, sleep; by euphemism, carnal intercourse. In the KJV it is rendered: bed((-chamber)), couch, lieth (lying) with.
H4905: From שָׂכַל; instructive, i.e. a didactic poem. In the KJV it is rendered: Maschil.
H4906: From the same as שֶׂ֫כוּ; a figure (carved on stone, the wall, or any object); figuratively, imagination. In the KJV it is rendered: conceit, image(-ry), picture, X wish.
H4907: (Aramaic) corresponding to מִשְׁכָּן; residence. In the KJV it is rendered: habitation.
H4908: From שָׁכַן; a residence (including a shepherd's hut, the lair of animals, figuratively, the grave; also the Temple); specifically, the Tabernacle (properly, its wooden walls). In the KJV it is rendered: dwelleth, dwelling (place), habitation, tabernacle, tent.
H4909: From שָׂכַר; wages or a reward. In the KJV it is rendered: reward, wages.
H4910: A primitive root; to rule. In the KJV it is rendered: (have, make to have) dominion, governor, X indeed, reign, (bear, cause to, have) rule(-ing, -r), have power.
H4911: Denominative from מָשָׁל; to liken, i.e. (transitively) to use figurative language (an allegory, adage, song or the like); intransitively, to resemble. In the KJV it is rendered: be(-come) like, compare, use (as a) proverb, speak (in proverbs), utter.
H4912: Apparently from מָשַׁל in some original sense of superiority in mental action; properly, a pithy maxim, usually of metaphorical nature; hence, a simile (as an adage, poem, discourse). In the KJV it is rendered: byword, like, parable, proverb.
H4913: For מִשְׁאָל; Mashal, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Mashal.
H4914: From מָשַׁל; a satire. In the KJV it is rendered: byword.
H4915: (1) from מָשַׁל; empire; (2) from מָשַׁל; a parallel. In the KJV it is rendered: dominion, like.
H4916: Or mishloach; also mishlach; from שָׁלַח; a sending out, i.e. (abstractly) presentation (favorable), or seizure (unfavorable); also (concretely) a place of dismissal, or a business to be discharged. In the KJV it is rendered: to lay, to put, sending (forth), to set.
H4917: Feminine of מִשְׁלַח; a mission, i.e. (abstractly) and favorable) release, or (concretely and unfavorable) an army. In the KJV it is rendered: discharge, sending.
H4918: From שָׁלַם; allied; Meshullam, the name of seventeen Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Meshullam.
H4919: Plural from שָׁלַם; reconciliations. In the KJV it is rendered: Meshillemoth, an Israelite:--Meshillemoth.
H4920: Or Mshelemyahuw; from שָׁלַם and יָהּ; ally of Jah; Meshelemjah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Meshelemiah.
H4921: From שָׁלַם; reconciliation; Meshillemith, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Meshillemith.
H4922: Feminine of מְשֻׁלָּם; Meshullemeth, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Meshullemeth.
H4923: From שָׁמֵם; a waste or amazement. In the KJV it is rendered: astonishment, desolate.
H4924: From שָׁמַן; fat, i.e. (literally and abstractly) fatness; but usually (figuratively and concretely) a rich dish, a fertile field, a robust man. In the KJV it is rendered: fat (one, -ness, -test, -test place).
H4925: From שָׁמַן; fatness; Mashmannah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Mishmannah.
H4926: From שָׁמַע; a report. In the KJV it is rendered: hearing.
H4927: The same as מִשְׁמַע; Mishma, the name of a son of Ishmael, and of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Mishma.
H4928: Feminineal sense of superiority in mental action; properly, a pithy maxim, usually of metaphorical nature; hence, a simile (as a adae, compare, use (as a) proverb, speak (in proverbs), utter.
H4929: From שָׁמַר; a guard (the man, the post or the prison); a deposit (fig.); also (as observed) a usage (abstr.), or an example (concr.). In the KJV it is rendered: diligence, guard, office, prison, ward, watch.
H4930: For מַסְמְרִים fem.; a peg. In the KJV it is rendered: nail.
H4931: Fem. of מִשְׁמָר; watch, i.e. the act (custody), or (concr.) the sentry, the post; obj. preservation, or (concr.) safe; fig. observance, i.e. (abstr.) duty or (obj.) a usage or party. In the KJV it is rendered: charge, keep, or to be kept, office, ordinace, safeguard, ward, watch.
H4932: From שָׁנָה; properly, a repetition, i.e. a duplicate (copy of a document), or a double (in amount); by implication, a second (in order, rank, age, quality or location). In the KJV it is rendered: college, copy, double, fatlings, next, second (order), twice as much.
H4933: From שָׁסַס; plunder. In the KJV it is rendered: booty, spoil.
H4934: From the same as שֹׁ֫עַל; a hollow, i.e. a narrow passage. In the KJV it is rendered: path.
H4935: Probably from שָׁעָה; inspection. In the KJV it is rendered: to supple.
H4936: Apparently from שָׁעָה; inspection; Misham, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Misham.
H4937: Or mishtan; from שָׁעַן; a support (concretely), i.e. (figuratively) a protector or sustenance. In the KJV it is rendered: stay.
H4938: Or mishteneth; feminine of מַשְׁעֵן; support (abstractly), i.e. (figuratively) sustenance or (concretely) a walking-stick. In the KJV it is rendered: staff.
H4939: From סָפַח; slaughter. In the KJV it is rendered: oppression.
H4940: From שָׁפָה (compare שִׁפְחָה); a family, i.e. circle of relatives; figuratively, a class (of persons), a species (of animals) or sort (of things); by extens. a tribe or people. In the KJV it is rendered: family, kind(-red).
H4941: From שָׁפַט; properly, a verdict (favorable or unfavorable) pronounced judicially, especially a sentence or formal decree (human or (participant's) divine law, individual or collective), including the act, the place, the suit, the crime, and the penalty; abstractly, justice, including a participant's right or privilege (statutory or customary), or even a style. In the KJV it is rendered: + adversary, ceremony, charge, X crime, custom, desert, determination, discretion, disposing, due, fashion, form, to be judged, judgment, just(-ice, -ly), (manner of) law(-ful), manner, measure, (due) order, ordinance, right, sentence, usest, X worthy, + wrong.
H4942: From שָׁפָה; a stall for cattle (only dual). In the KJV it is rendered: burden, sheepfold.
H4943: From an unused root meaning to hold; possession. In the KJV it is rendered: + steward.
H4944: From שָׁקַק; a traversing, i.e. rapid motion. In the KJV it is rendered: running to and fro.
H4945: From שָׁקָה; properly, causing to drink, i.e. a butler; by implication (intransitively), drink (itself); figuratively, a well-watered region. In the KJV it is rendered: butler(-ship), cupbearer, drink(-ing), fat pasture, watered.
H4946: From שָׁקַל; weight. In the KJV it is rendered: weight.
H4947: From שָׁקַף in its original sense of overhanging; a lintel. In the KJV it is rendered: lintel.
H4948: From שָׁקַל; weight (numerically estimated); hence, weighing (the act). In the KJV it is rendered: (full) weight.
H4949: Or mishqoleth; feminine of מִשְׁקָל or מַשְׁקוֹף; a weight, i.e. a plummet (with line attached). In the KJV it is rendered: plummet.
H4950: From שָׁקַע; a settling place (of water), i.e. a pond. In the KJV it is rendered: deep.
H4951: From שָׂרָה; empire. In the KJV it is rendered: government.
H4952: From שָׁרָה in the sense of loosening; maceration, i.e. steeped juice. In the KJV it is rendered: liquor.
H4953: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to שָׁרַק; a (musical) pipe (from its whistling sound). In the KJV it is rendered: flute.
H4954: Patrial from an unused noun from an unused root; probably meaning to stretch out; extension; a Mishraite, or inhabitant (collectively) of Mishra. In the KJV it is rendered: Mishraites.
H4955: From שָׂרַף; combustion, i.e. cremation (of a corpse), or calcination (of lime). In the KJV it is rendered: burning.
H4956: From the plural of מִשְׂרְפוֹת and מָ֫יִם; burnings of water; Misrephoth-Majim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Misrephoth-mayim.
H4957: A form for שֹׂרֵק used denominatively; vineyard; Masrekah, a place in Idumaea. In the KJV it is rendered: Masrekah.
H4958: Apparently from an unused root meaning to perforate, i.e. hollow out; a pan. In the KJV it is rendered: pan.
H4959: A primitive root; to feel of; by implication, to grope. In the KJV it is rendered: feel, grope, search.
H4960: From שָׁתָה; drink, by implication, drinking (the act); also (by implication) a banquet or (generally) feast. In the KJV it is rendered: banquet, drank, drink, feast((-ed), -ing).
H4961: (Aramaic) corresponding to מִשְׁתֶּה; a banquet. In the KJV it is rendered: banquet.
H4962: From the same as מָתַי; properly, an adult (as of full length); by implication, a man (only in the plural). In the KJV it is rendered: + few, X friends, men, persons, X small.
H4963: Denominative from תֶּ֫בֶן; straw in the heap. In the KJV it is rendered: straw.
H4964: From an unused root meaning to curb; a bit. In the KJV it is rendered: bit, bridle.
H4965: From מֶ֫תֶג and אַמָּה with the art. interposed; bit of the metropolis; Metheg-ha-Ammah, an epithet of Gath. In the KJV it is rendered: Metheg-ammah.
H4966: Or mathuwq; from מָתַק; sweet. In the KJV it is rendered: sweet(-er, -ness).
H4967: From מְתִים and אֵל, with the relative interposed; man who (is) of God; Methusael, an antediluvian patriarch. In the KJV it is rendered: Methusael.
H4968: From מְתִים and שָׁ֫לַח; man of a dart; Methushelach, an antediluvian patriarch. In the KJV it is rendered: Methuselah.
H4969: A primitive root; to stretch out. In the KJV it is rendered: spread out.
H4970: From an unused root meaning to extend; properly, extent (of time); but used only adverbially (especially with other particle prefixes), when (either relative or interrogative). In the KJV it is rendered: long, when.
H4971: Or mathkuneth; from תָּכַן in the transferred sense of measuring; proportion (in size, number or ingredients). In the KJV it is rendered: composition, measure, state, tale.
H4972: From מָה and תְּלָאָה; what a trouble!. In the KJV it is rendered: what a weariness.
H4973: Contr. from יָלַע; properly, a biter, i.e. a tooth. In the KJV it is rendered: cheek (jaw) tooth, jaw.
H4974: From תָּמַם; wholesomeness; also (adverb) completely. In the KJV it is rendered: men (by reading math), soundness.
H4975: From an unused root meaning to be slender; properly, the waist or small of the back; only in plural the loins. In the KJV it is rendered: + greyhound, loins, side.
H4976: From נָתַן; a present. In the KJV it is rendered: gift, to give, reward.
H4977: The same as מַתָּן; Mattan, the name of a priest of Baal, and of an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Mattan.
H4978: (Aramaic) corresponding to מַתָּנָה. In the KJV it is rendered: gift.
H4979: Feminine of מַתָּן; a present; specifically (in a good sense), a sacrificial offering, (in a bad sense) a bribe. In the KJV it is rendered: gift.
H4980: The same as מַתָּנָה; Mattanah, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Mattanah.
H4981: Probably patrial from an unused noun meaning slenderness; a Mithnite, or inhabitant of Methen. In the KJV it is rendered: Mithnite.
H4982: From מַתָּן; liberal; Mattenai, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Mattenai.
H4983: Or Mattanyahuw; from מַתָּן and יָהּ; gift of Jah; Mattanjah, the name of ten Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Mattaniah.
H4984: From נָשָׂא; (used as abstractly) supreme exaltation. In the KJV it is rendered: exalted.
H4985: A primitive root; to suck, by implication, to relish, or (intransitively) be sweet. In the KJV it is rendered: be (made, X take) sweet.
H4986: From מָתַק; figuratively, pleasantness (of discourse). In the KJV it is rendered: sweetness.
H4987: From מָתַק; sweetness. In the KJV it is rendered: sweetness.
H4988: From מָתַק; a dainty, i.e. (generally) food. In the KJV it is rendered: feed sweetly.
H4989: Feminine of מֹ֫תֶק; sweetness; Mithkah, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Mithcah.
H4990: Of Persian origin; Mithredath, the name of two Persians. In the KJV it is rendered: Mithredath.
H4991: Feminine of מַתָּן abbreviated form; a present. In the KJV it is rendered: gift.
H4992: For מַתִּתְיָה; gift of Jah; Mattattah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Mattathah.
H4993: Or Mattithyahuw; from מַתָּ֫נֶת and יָהּ; gift of Jah; Mattithjah, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Mattithiah.
H4994: A primitive particle of incitement and entreaty, which may usually be rendered: "I pray," "now," or "then"; added mostly to verbs (in the Imperative or Future), or to interjections, occasionally to an adverb or conjunction. In the KJV it is rendered: I beseech (pray) thee (you), go to, now, oh.
H4995: Apparently from נוּא in the sense of harshness from refusal; properly, tough, i.e. uncooked (flesh). In the KJV it is rendered: raw.
H4996: Of Egyptian origin; No (i.e. Thebes), the capital of Upper Egypt. In the KJV it is rendered: No.
H4997: Or noywd; also (feminine) no)dah; from an unused root of uncertain signification; a (skin or leather) bag (for fluids). In the KJV it is rendered: bottle.
H4998: A primitive root; properly, to be at home, i.e. (by implication) to be pleasant (or suitable), i.e. beautiful. In the KJV it is rendered: be beautiful, become, be comely.
H4999: From נָאָה; a home; figuratively, a pasture. In the KJV it is rendered: habitation, house, pasture, pleasant place.
H5000: From נָאָה or נָוֶה; suitable, or beautiful. In the KJV it is rendered: becometh, comely, seemly.
H5001: A primitive root; properly, to whisper, i.e. (by implication) to utter as a oracle. In the KJV it is rendered: say.
H5002: From נָאַם; an oracle. In the KJV it is rendered: (hath) said, saith.
H5003: A primitive root; to commit adultery; figuratively, to apostatize. In the KJV it is rendered: adulterer(-ess), commit(-ing) adultery, woman that breaketh wedlock.
H5004: From נָאַף; adultery. In the KJV it is rendered: adultery.
H5005: From נָאַף; adultery. In the KJV it is rendered: adultery.
H5006: A primitive root; to scorn; or (Ecclesiastes 12:5) by interchange for נוּץ, to bloom. In the KJV it is rendered: abhor, (give occasion to) blaspheme, contemn, despise, flourish, X great, provoke.
H5007: Or nematsah; from נָאַץ; scorn. In the KJV it is rendered: blasphemy.
H5008: A primitive root; to groan. In the KJV it is rendered: groan.
H5009: From נָאַק; a groan. In the KJV it is rendered: groaning.
H5010: A primitive root; to reject. In the KJV it is rendered: abhor, make void.
H5011: The same as נִיב; fruit; Nob, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Nob.
H5012: A primitive root; to prophesy, i.e. speak (or sing) by inspiration (in prediction or simple discourse). In the KJV it is rendered: prophesy(-ing), make self a prophet.
H5013: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָבָא. In the KJV it is rendered: prophesy.
H5014: A primitive root; to pierce; to be hollow, or (figuratively) foolish. In the KJV it is rendered: hollow, vain.
H5015: Probably of foreign derivation; Nebo, the name of a Babylonian deity, also of a mountain in Moab, and of a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Nebo.
H5016: From נָבָא; a prediction (spoken or written). In the KJV it is rendered: prophecy.
H5017: (Aramaic) corresponding to נְבוּאָה; inspired teaching. In the KJV it is rendered: prophesying.
H5018: Of foreign origin; Nebuzaradan, a Babylonian general. In the KJV it is rendered: Nebuzaradan.
H5019: Or Nbukadneotstsar (2 Kings 24:1, 10); or Nbuwkadnetstsar (Esther 2:6; Daniel 1:18); or Nbuwkadreotstsar; or Nbuwkadreltstsowr (Ezra 2:1; Jeremiah 49:28); or foreign derivation; Nebukadnetstsar (or -retstsar, or -retstsor), king of Babylon. In the KJV it is rendered: Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadrezzar.
H5020: (Aramaic) corresponding to נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר. In the KJV it is rendered: Nebuchadnezzar.
H5021: Of foreign derivation; Nebushazban, Nebuchadnezzar's chief eunuch. In the KJV it is rendered: Nebushazban.
H5022: Feminine plural from the same as נֹב; fruits; Naboth, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Naboth.
H5023: (Aramaic) of uncertain derivation; a largess. In the KJV it is rendered: reward.
H5024: A primitive root; to bark (as a dog). In the KJV it is rendered: bark.
H5025: From נָבַח; a bark; Nobach, the name of an Israelite, and of a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Nobah.
H5026: Of foreign origin; Nibchaz, a deity of the Avites. In the KJV it is rendered: Nibhaz.
H5027: A primitive root; to scan, i.e. look intently at; by implication, to regard with pleasure, favor or care. In the KJV it is rendered: (cause to) behold, consider, look (down), regard, have respect, see.
H5028: From נָבַט; regard; Nebat, the father of Jeroboam I. In the KJV it is rendered: Nebat.
H5029: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָבִיא; a prophet. In the KJV it is rendered: prophet.
H5030: From נָבָא; a prophet or (generally) inspired man. In the KJV it is rendered: prophecy, that prophesy, prophet.
H5031: Feminine of נָבִיא; a prophetess or (generally) inspired woman; by implication, a poetess; by association a prophet's wife. In the KJV it is rendered: prophetess.
H5032: Or Nbayoth; feminine plural from נוּב; fruitfulnesses; Nebajoth, a son of Ismael, and the country settled by him. In the KJV it is rendered: Nebaioth, Nebajoth.
H5033: From an unused root meaning to burst forth; a fountain. In the KJV it is rendered: spring.
H5034: A primitive root; to wilt; generally, to fall away, fail, faint; figuratively, to be foolish or (morally) wicked; causatively, to despise, disgrace. In the KJV it is rendered: disgrace, dishounour, lightly esteem, fade (away, - ing), fall (down, -ling, off), do foolishly, come to nought, X surely, make vile, wither.
H5035: Or nebel; from נָבֵל; a skin-bag for liquids (from collapsing when empty); hence, a vase (as similar in shape when full); also a lyre (as having a body of like form). In the KJV it is rendered: bottle, pitcher, psaltery, vessel, viol.
H5036: From נָבֵל; stupid; wicked (especially impious). In the KJV it is rendered: fool(-ish, -ish man, -ish woman), vile person.
H5037: The same as נָבָל; dolt; Nabal, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Nabal.
H5038: From נָבֵל; a flabby thing, i.e. a carcase or carrion (human or bestial, often collectively); figuratively, an idol. In the KJV it is rendered: (dead) body, (dead) carcase, dead of itself, which died, (beast) that (which) dieth of itself.
H5039: Feminine of נָבָל; foolishness, i.e. (morally) wickedness; concretely, a crime; by extension, punishment. In the KJV it is rendered: folly, vile, villany.
H5040: From נָבָל; properly, disgrace, i.e. the (female) pudenda. In the KJV it is rendered: lewdness.
H5041: Apparently from נָבָל and לָט; foolish secrecy; Neballat, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Neballat.
H5042: A primitive root; to gush forth; figuratively, to utter (good or bad words); specifically, to emit (a foul odor). In the KJV it is rendered: belch out, flowing, pour out, send forth, utter (abundantly).
H5043: (Aramaic) from an unused root meaning to shine; a light; plural (collectively) a chandelier. In the KJV it is rendered: candlestick.
H5044: Of uncertain derivation; Nibshan, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Nibshan.
H5045: From an unused root meaning to be parched; the south (from its drought); specifically, the Negeb or southern district of Judah, occasionally, Egypt (as south to Palestine). In the KJV it is rendered: south (country, side, -ward).
H5046: A primitive root; properly, to front, i.e. stand boldly out opposite; by implication (causatively), to manifest; figuratively, to announce (always by word of mouth to one present); specifically, to expose, predict, explain, praise. In the KJV it is rendered: bewray, X certainly, certify, declare(-ing), denounce, expound, X fully, messenger, plainly, profess, rehearse, report, shew (forth), speak, X surely, tell, utter.
H5047: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָגַד; to flow (through the idea of clearing the way). In the KJV it is rendered: issue.
H5048: From נָגַד; a front, i.e. part opposite; specifically a counterpart, or mate; usually (adverbial, especially with preposition) over against or before. In the KJV it is rendered: about, (over) against, X aloof, X far (off), X from, over, presence, X other side, sight, X to view.
H5049: (Aramaic) corresponding to נֶ֫גֶד; opposite. In the KJV it is rendered: toward.
H5050: A primitive root; to glitter; causatively, to illuminate. In the KJV it is rendered: (en-)lighten, (cause to) shine.
H5051: From נָגַהּ; brilliancy (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: bright(-ness), light, (clear) shining.
H5052: The same as נֹ֫גַהּ; Nogah, a son of David. In the KJV it is rendered: Nogah.
H5053: (Aramaic) corresponding to נֹ֫גַהּ; dawn. In the KJV it is rendered: morning.
H5054: Feminine of נֹ֫גַהּ; splendor. In the KJV it is rendered: brightness.
H5055: A primitive root; to but with the horns; figuratively, to war against. In the KJV it is rendered: gore, push (down, -ing).
H5056: From נָגַח; butting, i.e. vicious. In the KJV it is rendered: used (wont) to push.
H5057: Or nagid; from נָגַד; a commander (as occupying the front), civil, military or religious; generally (abstractly, plural), honorable themes. In the KJV it is rendered: captain, chief, excellent thing, (chief) governor, leader, noble, prince, (chief) ruler.
H5058: Or ngiynath (Psa. 61:title); from נָגַן; properly, instrumental music; by implication, a stringed instrument; by extension, a poem set to music; specifically, an epigram. In the KJV it is rendered: stringed instrument, musick, Neginoth (plural), song.
H5059: A primitive root; properly, to thrum, i.e. beat a tune with the fingers; expec. to play on a stringed instrument; hence (generally), to make music. In the KJV it is rendered: player on instruments, sing to the stringed instruments, melody, ministrel, play(-er, -ing).
H5060: A primitive root; properly, to touch, i.e. lay the hand upon (for any purpose; euphem., to lie with a woman); by implication, to reach (figuratively, to arrive, acquire); violently, to strike (punish, defeat, destroy, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: beat, (X be able to) bring (down), cast, come (nigh), draw near (nigh), get up, happen, join, near, plague, reach (up), smite, strike, touch.
H5061: From נָגַע; a blow (figuratively, infliction); also (by implication) a spot (concretely, a leprous person or dress). In the KJV it is rendered: plague, sore, stricken, stripe, stroke, wound.
H5062: A primitive root; to push, gore, defeat, stub (the toe), inflict (a disease). In the KJV it is rendered: beat, dash, hurt, plague, slay, smite (down), strike, stumble, X surely, put to the worse.
H5063: From נָגַף; a trip (of the foot); figuratively, an infliction (of disease). In the KJV it is rendered: plague, stumbling.
H5064: A primitive root; to flow; figuratively, to stretch out; causatively, to pour out or down; figuratively, to deliver over. In the KJV it is rendered: fall, flow away, pour down (out), run, shed, spilt, trickle down.
H5065: A primitive root; to drive (an animal, a workman, a debtor, an army); by implication, to tax, harass, tyrannize. In the KJV it is rendered: distress, driver, exact(-or), oppress(-or), X raiser of taxes, taskmaster.
H5066: A primitive root; to be or come (causatively, bring) near (for any purpose); euphemistically, to lie with a woman; as an enemy, to attack; relig. to worship; causatively, to present; figuratively, to adduce an argument; by reversal, to stand back. In the KJV it is rendered: (make to) approach (nigh), bring (forth, hither, near), (cause to) come (hither, near, nigh), give place, go hard (up), (be, draw, go) near (nigh), offer, overtake, present, put, stand.
H5067: From נוּד in the sense of piling up; a mound, i.e. wave. In the KJV it is rendered: heap.
H5068: A primitive root; to impel; hence, to volunteer (as a soldier), to present spontaneously. In the KJV it is rendered: offer freely, be (give, make, offer self) willing(-ly).
H5069: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָדַב; be (or give) liberal(-ly). In the KJV it is rendered: (be minded of.
H5070: From נָדַב; liberal; Nadab, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Nadab.
H5071: From נָדַב; properly (abstractly) spontaneity, or (adjectively) spontaneous; also (concretely) a spontaneous or (by inference, in plural) abundant gift. In the KJV it is rendered: free(-will) offering, freely, plentiful, voluntary(-ily, offering), willing(-ly), offering).
H5072: From נָדַב and יָהּ; largess of Jah; Nedabjah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Nedabiah.
H5073: (Aramaic) from a root meaning to stick; a layer (of building materials). In the KJV it is rendered: row.
H5074: A primitive root; properly, to wave to and fro (rarely to flap up and down); figuratively, to rove, flee, or (causatively) to drive away. In the KJV it is rendered: chase (away), X could not, depart, flee (X apace, away), (re-)move, thrust away, wander (abroad, -er, -ing).
H5075: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָדַד; to depart. In the KJV it is rendered: go from.
H5076: Passive participle of נָדַד; properly, tossed; abstractly, a rolling (on the bed). In the KJV it is rendered: tossing to and fro.
H5077: Or nada (2 Kings 17:21); a primitive root; properly, to toss; figuratively, to exclude, i.e. banish, postpone, prohibit. In the KJV it is rendered: cast out, drive, put far away.
H5078: From נָדָה in the sense of freely flinging money; a bounty (for prostitution). In the KJV it is rendered: gifts.
H5079: From נָדַד; properly, rejection; by implication, impurity, especially personal (menstruation) or moral (idolatry, incest). In the KJV it is rendered: X far, filthiness, X flowers, menstruous (woman), put apart, X removed (woman), separation, set apart, unclean(-ness, thing, with filthiness).
H5080: A primitive root; to push off; used in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively (to expel, mislead, strike, inflict, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: banish, bring, cast down (out), chase, compel, draw away, drive (away, out, quite), fetch a stroke, force, go away, outcast, thrust away (out), withdraw.
H5081: From נָדַב; properly, voluntary, i.e. generous; hence, magnanimous; as noun, a grandee (sometimes a tyrant). In the KJV it is rendered: free, liberal (things), noble, prince, willing ((hearted)).
H5082: Feminine of נָדִיב; properly, nobility, i.e. reputation. In the KJV it is rendered: soul.
H5083: Probably from an unused root meaning to give; a present (for prostitution). In the KJV it is rendered: gift.
H5084: Of uncertain derivation; a sheath (of a sword). In the KJV it is rendered: sheath.
H5085: (Aramaic) from the same as נָדָן; a sheath; figuratively, the body (as the receptacle of the soul). In the KJV it is rendered: body.
H5086: A primitive root; to shove asunder, i.e. disperse. In the KJV it is rendered: drive (away, to and fro), thrust down, shaken, tossed to and fro.
H5087: A primitive root; to promise (pos., to do or give something to God). In the KJV it is rendered: (make a) vow.
H5088: Or neder; from נָדַר; a promise (to God); also (concretely) a thing promised. In the KJV it is rendered: vow((-ed)).
H5089: From an unused root meaning to lament; lamentation. In the KJV it is rendered: wailing.
H5090: A primitive root; to drive forth (a person, an animal or chariot), i.e. lead, carry away; reflexively, to proceed (i.e. impel or guide oneself); also (from the panting induced by effort), to sigh. In the KJV it is rendered: acquaint, bring (away), carry away, drive (away), lead (away, forth), (be) guide, lead (away, forth).
H5091: A primitive root; to groan, i.e. bewail; hence (through the idea of crying aloud), to assemble (as if on proclamation). In the KJV it is rendered: lament, wail.
H5092: From נָהָה; an elegy. In the KJV it is rendered: lamentation, wailing.
H5093: Feminine of נֶ֫הִי; lamentation. In the KJV it is rendered: doleful.
H5094: (Aramaic) or nehiyruw (Aramaic); from the same as נְהָרָה; illumination, i.e. (figuratively) wisdom. In the KJV it is rendered: light.
H5095: A primitive root; properly, to run with a sparkle, i.e. flow; hence (transitively), to conduct, and (by inference) to protect, sustain. In the KJV it is rendered: carry, feed, guide, lead (gently, on).
H5096: Or Nahalol; the same as נַהֲלֹלִים; Nahalal or Nahalol, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Nahalal, Nahallal, Nahalol.
H5097: From נָהַל; pasture. In the KJV it is rendered: bush.
H5098: A primitive root; to growl. In the KJV it is rendered: mourn, roar(-ing).
H5099: From נָהַם; a snarl. In the KJV it is rendered: roaring.
H5100: Feminine of נַ֫הַם; snarling. In the KJV it is rendered: disquietness, roaring.
H5101: A primitive root; to bray (as an ass), scream (from hunger. In the KJV it is rendered: bray.
H5102: A primitive root; to sparkle, i.e. (figuratively) be cheerful; hence (from the sheen of a running stream) to flow, i.e. (figuratively) assemble. In the KJV it is rendered: flow (together), be lightened.
H5103: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to נָהַר; a river, especially the Euphrates. In the KJV it is rendered: river, stream.
H5104: From נָהַר; a stream (including the sea; expec. the Nile, Euphrates, etc.); figuratively, prosperity. In the KJV it is rendered: flood, river.
H5105: From נָהַר in its original sense; daylight. In the KJV it is rendered: light.
H5106: A primitive root; to refuse, forbid, dissuade, or neutralize. In the KJV it is rendered: break, disallow, discourage, make of none effect.
H5107: A primitive root; to germinate, i.e. (figuratively) to (causatively, make) flourish; also (of words), to utter. In the KJV it is rendered: bring forth (fruit), make cheerful, increase.
H5108: Or neyb; from נוּב; produce, literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: fruit.
H5109: From נִיב; fruitful; Nobai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Nebai (from the margin).
H5110: A primitive root; to nod, i.e. waver; figuratively, to wander, flee, disappear; also (from shaking the head in sympathy), to console, deplore, or (from tossing the head in scorn) taunt. In the KJV it is rendered: bemoan, flee, get, mourn, make to move, take pity, remove, shake, skip for joy, be sorry, vagabond, way, wandering.
H5111: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָוֶה; to flee. In the KJV it is rendered: get away.
H5112: (only defect. nod); from נוּד; exile. In the KJV it is rendered: wandering.
H5113: The same as נֹדִי; vagrancy; Nod, the land of Cain. In the KJV it is rendered: Nod.
H5114: From נָדַב; noble; Nodab, an Arab tribe. In the KJV it is rendered: Nodab.
H5115: A primitive root; to rest (as at home); causatively (through the implied idea of beauty (compare נָוֶה)), to celebrate (with praises). In the KJV it is rendered: keept at home, prepare an habitation.
H5116: Or (feminine) navah; from נָוָה; (adjectively) at home; hence (by implication of satisfaction) lovely; also (noun) a home, of God (temple), men (residence), flocks (pasture), or wild animals (den). In the KJV it is rendered: comely, dwelling (place), fold, habitation, pleasant place, sheepcote, stable, tarried.
H5117: A primitive root; to rest, i.e. settle down; used in a great variety of applications, literal and figurative, intransitive, transitive and causative (to dwell, stay, let fall, place, let alone, withdraw, give comfort, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: cease, be confederate, lay, let down, (be) quiet, remain, (cause to, be at, give, have, make to) rest, set down.
H5118: Or nowach; from נ֫וּחַ; quiet. In the KJV it is rendered: rest(-ed, -ing place).
H5119: Feminine of נ֫וּחַ; quietude; Nochah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Nohah.
H5120: To quake. In the KJV it is rendered: be moved.
H5121: From נָוָה; residence; Navith, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Naioth (from the margin).
H5122: (Aramaic) or nvaliy (Aramaic); from an unused root probably meaning to be foul; a sink. In the KJV it is rendered: dunghill.
H5123: A primitive root; to slumber (from drowsiness). In the KJV it is rendered: sleep, slumber.
H5124: From נוּם; sleepiness. In the KJV it is rendered: drowsiness.
H5125: A primitive root; to resprout, i.e. propagate by shoots; figuratively, to be perpetual. In the KJV it is rendered: be continued.
H5126: Or Nown (1 Chron. 7:27); from נוּן; perpetuity, Nun or Non, the father of Joshua. In the KJV it is rendered: Non, Nun.
H5127: A primitive root; to flit, i.e. vanish away (subside, escape; causatively, chase, impel, deliver). In the KJV it is rendered: X abate, away, be displayed, (make to) flee (away, -ing), put to flight, X hide, lift up a standard.
H5128: A primitive root; to waver, in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively (as subjoined). In the KJV it is rendered: continually, fugitive, X make, to (go) up and down, be gone away, (be) move(-able, -d), be promoted, reel, remove, scatter, set, shake, sift, stagger, to and fro, be vagabond, wag, (make) wander (up and down).
H5129: From יָעַד and יָהּ; convened of Jah; Noadjah, the name of an Israelite, and a false prophetess. In the KJV it is rendered: Noadiah.
H5130: A primitive root; to quiver (i.e. vibrate up and down, or rock to and fro); used in a great variety of applications (including sprinkling, beckoning, rubbing, bastinadoing, sawing, waving, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: lift up, move, offer, perfume, send, shake, sift, strike, wave.
H5131: From נוּף; elevation. In the KJV it is rendered: situation.
H5132: A primitive root; properly, to flash; hence, to blossom (from the brilliancy of color); also, to fly away (from the quickness of motion). In the KJV it is rendered: flee away, bud (forth).
H5133: Or notsah; feminine active participle of נָצָה in the sense of flying; a pinion (or wing feather); often (collectively) plumage. In the KJV it is rendered: feather(-s), ostrich.
H5134: A primitive root; to suckle. In the KJV it is rendered: nurse.
H5135: (Aramaic) from an unused root (corresponding to that of נֵר) meaning to shine; fire. In the KJV it is rendered: fiery, fire.
H5136: A primitive root; to be sick, i.e. (figuratively) distressed. In the KJV it is rendered: be full of heaviness.
H5137: A primitive root; to spirt, i.e. besprinkle (especially in expiation). In the KJV it is rendered: sprinkle.
H5138: From זִיד; something boiled, i.e. soup. In the KJV it is rendered: pottage.
H5139: Or nazir; from נָזַר; separate, i.e. consecrated (as prince, a Nazirite); hence (figuratively from the latter) an unpruned vine (like an unshorn Nazirite). In the KJV it is rendered: Nazarite (by a false alliteration with Nazareth), separate(-d), vine undressed.
H5140: A primitive root; to drip, or shed by trickling. In the KJV it is rendered: distil, drop, flood, (cause to) flow(-ing), gush out, melt, pour (down), running water, stream.
H5141: From an unused root of uncertain meaning; a nose-ring. In the KJV it is rendered: earring, jewel.
H5142: (Aramaic) corresponding to the root of נֵ֫זֶק; to suffer (causatively, inflict) loss. In the KJV it is rendered: have (en-)damage, hurt(-ful).
H5143: From an unused root meaning to injure; loss. In the KJV it is rendered: damage.
H5144: A primitive root; to hold aloof, i.e. (intransitivey) abstain (from food and drink, from impurity, and even from divine worship (i.e. apostatize)); specifically, to set apart (to sacred purposes), i.e. devote. In the KJV it is rendered: consecrate, separate(-ing, self).
H5145: Or nezer; from נָזַר; properly, something set apart, i.e. (abstractly) dedication (of a priet or Nazirite); hence (concretely) unshorn locks; also (by implication) a chaplet (especially of royalty). In the KJV it is rendered: consecration, crown, hair, separation.
H5146: The same as נ֫וּחַ; rest; Noach, the patriarch of the flood. In the KJV it is rendered: Noah.
H5147: From חָבָה; occult; Nachbi, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Nakbi.
H5148: A primitive root; to guide; by implication, to transport (into exile, or as colonists). In the KJV it is rendered: bestow, bring, govern, guide, lead (forth), put, straiten.
H5149: From נָחַם; comforted; Nechum, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Nehum.
H5150: Or nichum; from נָחַם; properly, consoled; abstractly, solace. In the KJV it is rendered: comfort(-able), repenting.
H5151: From נָחַם; comfortable; Nachum, an Israelite prophet. In the KJV it is rendered: Nahum.
H5152: From the same as נַ֫חַר; snorer; Nochor, the name of the grandfather and a brother of Abraham. In the KJV it is rendered: Nahor.
H5153: Apparently passive participle of נָחַשׁ (perhaps in the sense of ringing, i.e. bell-metal; or from the red color of the throat of a serpent (נָחָשׁ, as denominative) when hissing); coppery, i.e. (figuratively) hard. In the KJV it is rendered: of brass.
H5154: Or nchushah; feminine of נָחוּשׁ; copper. In the KJV it is rendered: brass, steel.
H5155: Probably denominative from חָלִיל; a flute. In the KJV it is rendered: (plural) Nehiloth.
H5156: From the same as נַ֫חַר; a nostril. In the KJV it is rendered: (dual) nostrils.
H5157: A primitive root; to inherit (as a (figurative) mode of descent), or (generally) to occupy; causatively, to bequeath, or (generally) distribute, instate. In the KJV it is rendered: divide, have ((inheritance)), take as a heritage, (cause to, give to, make to) inherit, (distribute for, divide (for, for an, by), give for, have, leave for, take (for)) inheritance, (have in, cause to, be made to) possess(-ion).
H5158: Or (feminine) nachlah (Psalm 124:4); or nachalah (Ezekiel 47:19; 48:28); from נָחַל in its original sense; a stream, especially a winter torrent; (by implication) a (narrow) valley (in which a brook runs); also a shaft (of a mine). In the KJV it is rendered: brook, flood, river, stream, valley.
H5159: From נָחַל (in its usual sense); properly, something inherited, i.e. (abstractly) occupancy, or (concretely) an heirloom; generally an estate, patrimony or portion. In the KJV it is rendered: heritage, to inherit, inheritance, possession.
H5160: From נַ֫חַל and אֵל; valley of God; Nachaliel, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Nahaliel.
H5161: Apparently a patronymic from an unused name (apparently passive participle of חָלַם); dreamed; a Nechelamite, or descendant of Nechlam. In the KJV it is rendered: Nehelamite.
H5162: A primitive root; properly, to sigh, i.e. breathe strongly; by implication, to be sorry, i.e. (in a favorable sense) to pity, console or (reflexively) rue; or (unfavorably) to avenge (oneself). In the KJV it is rendered: comfort (self), ease (one's self), repent(-er,-ing, self).
H5163: From נָחַם; consolation; Nacham, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Naham.
H5164: From נָחַם; ruefulness, i.e. desistance. In the KJV it is rendered: repentance.
H5165: From נָחַם; consolation. In the KJV it is rendered: comfort.
H5166: From נָחַם and יָהּ; consolation of Jah; Nechemjah, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Nehemiah.
H5167: From נָחַם; consolatory; Nachamani, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Nahamani.
H5168: For אֲנַ֫חְנוּ; we. In the KJV it is rendered: we.
H5169: A primitive root; to be urgent. In the KJV it is rendered: require haste.
H5170: And (feminine) nacharah; from an unused root meaning to snort or snore; a snorting. In the KJV it is rendered: nostrils, snorting.
H5171: Or Nachray; from the same as נַ֫חַר; snorer; Nacharai or Nachrai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Naharai, Nahari.
H5172: A primitive root; properly, to hiss, i.e. whisper a (magic) spell; generally, to prognosticate. In the KJV it is rendered: X certainly, divine, enchanter, (use) X enchantment, learn by experience, X indeed, diligently observe.
H5173: From נָחַשׁ; an incantation or augury. In the KJV it is rendered: enchantment.
H5174: (Aramaic) corresponding to נְחוּשָׁה; copper. In the KJV it is rendered: brass.
H5175: From נָחַשׁ; a snake (from its hiss). In the KJV it is rendered: serpent.
H5176: The same as נָחָשׁ; Nachash, the name of two persons apparently non-Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Nahash.
H5177: From נָחַשׁ; enchanter; Nachshon, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Naashon, Nahshon.
H5178: For נְחוּשָׁה; copper, hence, something made of that metal, i.e. coin, a fetter; figuratively, base (as compared with gold or silver). In the KJV it is rendered: brasen, brass, chain, copper, fetter (of brass), filthiness, steel.
H5179: From נְחֹ֫שֶׁת; copper; Nechushta, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Nehushta.
H5180: From נְחֹ֫שֶׁת; something made of copper, i.e. the copper serpent of the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Nehushtan.
H5181: A primitive root; to sink, i.e. descend; causatively, to press or lead down. In the KJV it is rendered: be broken, (cause to) come down, enter, go down, press sore, settle, stick fast.
H5182: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָחַת; to descend; causatively, to bring away, deposit, depose. In the KJV it is rendered: carry, come down, depose, lay up, place.
H5183: From נְחַת; a descent, i.e. imposition, unfavorable (punishment) or favorable (food); also (intransitively; perhaps from נ֫וּחַ), restfulness. In the KJV it is rendered: lighting down, quiet(-ness), to rest, be set on.
H5184: The same as נָ֫חַת; quiet; Nachath, the name of an Edomite and of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Nahath.
H5185: From נָחַת; descending. In the KJV it is rendered: come down.
H5186: A primitive root; to stretch or spread out; by implication, to bend away (including moral deflection); used in a great variety of application (as follows). In the KJV it is rendered: + afternoon, apply, bow (down, - ing), carry aside, decline, deliver, extend, go down, be gone, incline, intend, lay, let down, offer, outstretched, overthrown, pervert, pitch, prolong, put away, shew, spread (out), stretch (forth, out), take (aside), turn (aside, away), wrest, cause to yield.
H5187: From נָטַל; laden. In the KJV it is rendered: that bear.
H5188: From נָטַף; a pendant for the ears (especially of pearls). In the KJV it is rendered: chain, collar.
H5189: From נָטַשׁ; a tendril (as an offshoot). In the KJV it is rendered: battlement, branch, plant.
H5190: A prim root; to lift; by implication, to impose. In the KJV it is rendered: bear, offer, take up.
H5191: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָטַל; to raise. In the KJV it is rendered: take up.
H5192: : from נָטַל; a burden. In the KJV it is rendered: weighty.
H5193: A primitive root; properly, to strike in, i.e. fix; specifically, to plant (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: fastened, plant(- er).
H5194: From נָטַע; a plant; collectively, a plantation; abstractly, a planting. In the KJV it is rendered: plant.
H5195: From נָטַע; a plant. In the KJV it is rendered: plant.
H5196: Plural of נָ֫טַע; Netaim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: plants.
H5197: A primitive root; to ooze, i.e. distil gradually; by implication, to fall in drops; figuratively, to speak by inspiration. In the KJV it is rendered: drop(-ping), prophesy(-et).
H5198: From נָטַף; a drop; specifically, an aromatic gum (probably stacte). In the KJV it is rendered: drop, stacte.
H5199: From נָטַף; distillation; Netophah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Netophah.
H5200: Patronymic from נְטֹפָה; a Netophathite, or inhabitant of Netophah. In the KJV it is rendered: Netophathite.
H5201: A primitive root; to guard; figuratively, to cherish (anger). In the KJV it is rendered: bear grudge, keep(-er), reserve.
H5202: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָטַר; to retain. In the KJV it is rendered: keep.
H5203: A primitive root; properly, to pound, i.e. smite; by implication (as if beating out, and thus expanding) to disperse; also, to thrust off, down, out or upon (inclusively, reject, let alone, permit, remit, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: cast off, drawn, let fall, forsake, join (battle), leave (off), lie still, loose, spread (self) abroad, stretch out, suffer.
H5204: A doubtful word; apparently from נָהָה; lamentation. In the KJV it is rendered: wailing.
H5205: From נוּד; motion (of the lips in speech). In the KJV it is rendered: moving.
H5206: Feminine of נִיד; removal, i.e. exile. In the KJV it is rendered: removed.
H5207: Or niychoach; from נ֫וּחַ; properly, restful, i.e. pleasant; abstractly, delight. In the KJV it is rendered: sweet (odour).
H5208: (Aramaic) or (shorter) niychoach (Aramaic); corresponding to נִיח֫וֹחַ; pleasure. In the KJV it is rendered: sweet odour (savour).
H5209: From נוּן; progeny. In the KJV it is rendered: son.
H5210: Of foreign origin; Nineveh, the capital of Assyria. In the KJV it is rendered: Nineveh.
H5211: From נוּס; fugitive. In the KJV it is rendered: that fleeth.
H5212: Probably of foreign origin; Nisan, the first month of the Jewish sacred year. In the KJV it is rendered: Nisan.
H5213: From נָצַץ; a spark. In the KJV it is rendered: spark.
H5214: A root probably identical with that of נֵר, through the idea of the gleam of a fresh furrow; to till the soil. In the KJV it is rendered: break up.
H5215: Or nir; from נִיר; properly, plowing, i.e. (concretely) freshly plowed land. In the KJV it is rendered: fallow ground, plowing, tillage.
H5216: Or nir; also neyr; or ner; or (feminine) nerah; from a primitive root (see נִיר; נוּר) properly, meaning to glisten; a lamp (i.e. the burner) or light (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: candle, lamp, light.
H5217: A primitive root; to smite, i.e. drive away. In the KJV it is rendered: be viler.
H5218: Or nakat; from נָכָא; smitten, i.e. (figuratively) afflicted. In the KJV it is rendered: broken, stricken, wounded.
H5219: From נְכָאּים; properly, a smiting, i.e. (concretely) an aromatic gum (perhaps styrax) (as powdered). In the KJV it is rendered: spicery(-ces).
H5220: From an unused root meaning to propagate; offspring. In the KJV it is rendered: nephew, son's son.
H5221: A primitive root; to strike (lightly or severely, literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: beat, cast forth, clap, give (wounds), X go forward, X indeed, kill, make (slaughter), murderer, punish, slaughter, slay(-er, -ing), smite(-r, -ing), strike, be stricken, (give) stripes, X surely, wound.
H5222: From נָכָה; a smiter, i.e. (figuratively) traducer. In the KJV it is rendered: abject.
H5223: Smitten, i.e. (literally) maimed, or (figuratively) dejected. In the KJV it is rendered: contrite, lame.
H5224: Probably of Egyptian origin; Neko, an Egyptian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Necho.
H5225: From כּוּן; prepared; Nakon, probably an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Nachon.
H5226: From an unused root meaning to be straightforward; properly, the fore part; used adverbially, opposite. In the KJV it is rendered: before, over against.
H5227: From the same as נֵ֫כַח; properly, the front part; used adverbially (especially with preposition), opposite, in front of, forward, in behalf of. In the KJV it is rendered: (over) against, before, direct(-ly), for, right (on).
H5228: From the same as נֵ֫כַח; straightforward, i.e. (figuratively), equitable, correct, or (abstractly), integrity. In the KJV it is rendered: plain, right, uprightness.
H5229: Feminine of נָכֹ֫חַ; properly, straightforwardness, i.e. (figuratively) integrity, or (concretely) a truth. In the KJV it is rendered: equity, right (thing), uprightness.
H5230: A prim root; to defraud, i.e. act treacherously. In the KJV it is rendered: beguile, conspire, deceiver, deal subtilly.
H5231: From נָכַל; deceit. In the KJV it is rendered: wile.
H5232: (Aramaic) corresponding to נְכָסִים. In the KJV it is rendered: goods.
H5233: From an unused root meaning to accumulate; treasure. In the KJV it is rendered: riches, wealth.
H5234: A primitive root; properly, to scrutinize, i.e. look intently at; hence (with recognition implied), to acknowledge, be acquainted with, care for, respect, revere, or (with suspicion implied), to disregard, ignore, be strange toward, reject, resign, dissimulate (as if ignorant or disowning). In the KJV it is rendered: acknowledge, X could, deliver, discern, dissemble, estrange, feign self to be another, know, take knowledge (notice), perceive, regard, (have) respect, behave (make) self strange(-ly).
H5235: Or noker; from נָכַר; something strange, i.e. unexpected calamity. In the KJV it is rendered: strange.
H5236: ' from נָכַר; foreign, or (concretely) a foreigner, or (abstractly) heathendom. In the KJV it is rendered: alien, strange (+ -er).
H5237: From נֹ֫כֶר (second form); strange, in a variety of degrees and applications (foreign, non-relative, adulterous, different, wonderful). In the KJV it is rendered: alien, foreigner, outlandish, strange(-r, woman).
H5238: Probably for נְכֹאת; spicery, i.e. (generally) valuables. In the KJV it is rendered: precious things.
H5239: Apparently a primitive root; to complete. In the KJV it is rendered: make an end.
H5240: From בָּזָה, despised. In the KJV it is rendered: vile.
H5241: Apparently for יְמוּאֵל; Nemuel, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Nemuel.
H5242: From נְמוּאֵל; a Nemuelite, or descendant of Nemuel. In the KJV it is rendered: Nemuelite.
H5243: A primitive root; to become clipped or (specifically) circumcised. In the KJV it is rendered: (branch to) be cut down (off), circumcise.
H5244: Feminine from נָמַל; an ant (probably from its almost bisected form). In the KJV it is rendered: ant.
H5245: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָמֵר. In the KJV it is rendered: leopard.
H5246: From an unused root meaning properly, to filtrate, i.e. be limpid (comp נִמְרָה and נִמְרִים); and thus to spot or stain as if by dripping; a leopard (from its stripes). In the KJV it is rendered: leopard.
H5247: From the same as נָמֵר; clear water; Nimrah, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Nimrah.
H5248: Or Nimrod; probably of foreign origin; Nimrod, a son of Cush. In the KJV it is rendered: Nimrod.
H5249: Plural of a masculine corresponding to נִמְרָה; clear waters; Nimrim, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Nimrim.
H5250: Probably from מָשָׁה; extricated; Nimshi, the (grand-)father of Jehu. In the KJV it is rendered: Nimshi.
H5251: From נָסַס; a flag; also a sail; by implication, a flagstaff; generally a signal; figuratively, a token. In the KJV it is rendered: banner, pole, sail, (en-)sign, standard.
H5252: Feminine participle passive of סָבַב; properly, an environment, i.e. circumstance or turn of affairs. In the KJV it is rendered: cause.
H5253: A primitive root; to retreat. In the KJV it is rendered: departing away, remove, take (hold), turn away.
H5254: A primitive root; to test; by implication, to attempt. In the KJV it is rendered: adventure, assay, prove, tempt, try.
H5255: A primitive root; to tear away. In the KJV it is rendered: destroy, pluck, root.
H5256: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָסַח. In the KJV it is rendered: pull down.
H5257: From נָסַך; properly, something poured out, i.e. a libation; also a molten image; by implication, a prince (as anointed). In the KJV it is rendered: drink offering, duke, prince(-ipal).
H5258: A primitive root; to pour out, especially a libation, or to cast (metal); by analogy, to anoint a king. In the KJV it is rendered: cover, melt, offer, (cause to) pour (out), set (up).
H5259: A primitive root (probably identical with נָסַך through the idea of fusion); to interweave, i.e. (figuratively) to overspread. In the KJV it is rendered: that is spread.
H5260: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָסַך; to pour out a libation. In the KJV it is rendered: offer.
H5261: (Aramaic) corresponding to נֶ֫סֶך; a libation. In the KJV it is rendered: drink offering.
H5262: Or necek; from נָסַך; a libation; also a cast idol. In the KJV it is rendered: cover, drink offering, molten image.
H5263: A primitive root; to wane, i.e. be sick. In the KJV it is rendered: faint.
H5264: A primitive root; to gleam from afar, i.e. to be conspicuous as a signal; or rather perhaps a denominative from נֵס (and identical with נָסַס, through the idea of a flag as fluttering in the wind); to raise a beacon. In the KJV it is rendered: lift up as an ensign.
H5265: A primitive root; properly, to pull up, especially the tent-pins, i.e. start on a journey. In the KJV it is rendered: cause to blow, bring, get, (make to) go (away, forth, forward, onward, out), (take) journey, march, remove, set aside (forward), X still, be on his (go their) way.
H5266: A primitive root; to go up. In the KJV it is rendered: ascend.
H5267: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָסַק. In the KJV it is rendered: take up.
H5268: Of foreign origin; Nisrok, a Babylonian idol. In the KJV it is rendered: Nisroch.
H5269: From נ֫וּעַ; motion; Neah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Neah.
H5270: From נ֫וּעַ; movement; Noah, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Noah.
H5271: Or naur; and (feminine) nturah; properly, passive participle from נַ֫עַר as denominative; (only in plural collectively or emphatic form) youth, the state (juvenility) or the persons (young people). In the KJV it is rendered: childhood, youth.
H5272: From נ֫וּעַ and אֵל; moved of God; Neiel, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Neiel.
H5273: From נָעֵם; delightful (objective or subjective, literal or figurative). In the KJV it is rendered: pleasant(-ure), sweet.
H5274: A primitive root; properly, to fasten up, i.e. with a bar or cord; hence (denominative from נָ֫עַל), to sandal, i.e. furnish with slippers. In the KJV it is rendered: bolt, inclose, lock, shoe, shut up.
H5275: Or (feminine) na`alah; from נָעַל; properly, a sandal tongue; by extens. a sandal or slipper (sometimes as a symbol of occupancy, a refusal to marry, or of something valueless). In the KJV it is rendered: dryshod, (pair of) shoe((-latchet), -s).
H5276: A primitive root; to be agreeable (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: pass in beauty, be delight, be pleasant, be sweet.
H5277: From נָעֵם; pleasure; Naam, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Naam.
H5278: From נָעֵם; agreeableness, i.e. delight, suitableness, splendor or grace. In the KJV it is rendered: beauty, pleasant(-ness).
H5279: Feminine of נָ֫עַם; pleasantness; Naamah, the name of an antediluvian woman, of an Ammonitess, and of a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Naamah.
H5280: Patronymic from נַעֲמָן; a Naamanite, or descendant of Naaman (collectively). In the KJV it is rendered: Naamites.
H5281: From נֹ֫עַם; pleasant; Noomi, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Naomi.
H5282: From נָעֵם; pleasantness (plural as concrete). In the KJV it is rendered: pleasant.
H5283: The same as נַעֲמָנִים; Naaman, the name of an Israelite and of a Damascene. In the KJV it is rendered: Naaman.
H5284: Patrial from a place corresponding in name (but not identical) with נַעֲמָה; a Naamathite, or inhabitant of Naamah. In the KJV it is rendered: Naamathite.
H5285: From an unused root meaning to prick; probably a brier; by implication, a thicket of thorny bushes. In the KJV it is rendered: thorn.
H5286: A primitive root; to growl. In the KJV it is rendered: yell.
H5287: A primitive root (probably identical with נָעַר, through the idea of the rustling of mane, which usually accompanies the lion's roar); to tumble about. In the KJV it is rendered: shake (off, out, self), overthrow, toss up and down.
H5288: From נָעַר; (concretely) a boy (as active), from the age of infancy to adolescence; by implication, a servant; also (by interch. of sex), a girl (of similar latitude in age). In the KJV it is rendered: babe, boy, child, damsel (from the margin), lad, servant, young (man).
H5289: From נָעַר in its derivative sense of tossing about; a wanderer. In the KJV it is rendered: young one.
H5290: From נָעַר; (abstractly) boyhood (compare נַ֫עַר). In the KJV it is rendered: child, youth.
H5291: Feminine of נַ֫עַר; a girl (from infancy to adolescence). In the KJV it is rendered: damsel, maid(-en), young (woman).
H5292: The same as נַעֲרָה; Naarah, the name of an Israelitess, and of a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Naarah, Naarath.
H5293: From נַ֫עַר; youthful; Naarai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Naarai.
H5294: From נַ֫עַר and יָהּ; servant of Jah; Nearjah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Neariah.
H5295: From נַ֫עַר; juvenile; Naaran, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Naaran.
H5296: From נָעַר; something shaken out, i.e. tow (as the refuse of flax). In the KJV it is rendered: tow.
H5297: A variation of מֹף; Noph, the capital of Upper Egypt. In the KJV it is rendered: Noph.
H5298: From an unused root probably meaning to spring forth; a sprout; Nepheg, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Nepheg.
H5299: From נוּף in the sense of lifting; a height; also a sieve. In the KJV it is rendered: border, coast, region, sieve.
H5300: For נְפִיסִים; Nephushesim, a Temple- servant. In the KJV it is rendered: Nephisesim (from the margin).
H5301: A primitive root; to puff, in various applications (literally, to inflate, blow hard, scatter, kindle, expire; figuratively, to disesteem). In the KJV it is rendered: blow, breath, give up, cause to lose (life), seething, snuff.
H5302: From נָפַח; a gust; Nophach, a place in Moab. In the KJV it is rendered: Nophah.
H5303: Or nphil; from נָפַל; properly, a feller, i.e. a bully or tyrant. In the KJV it is rendered: giant.
H5304: Plural from an unused root meaning to scatter; expansions; Nephisim, a Temple-servant. In the KJV it is rendered: Nephusim (from the margin).
H5305: From נָפַשׁ; refreshed; Naphish, a son of Ishmael, and his posterity. In the KJV it is rendered: Naphish.
H5306: From an unused root meaning to glisten; shining; a gem, probably the garnet. In the KJV it is rendered: emerald.
H5307: A primitive root; to fall, in a great variety of applications (intransitive or causative, literal or figurative). In the KJV it is rendered: be accepted, cast (down, self, (lots), out), cease, die, divide (by lot), (let) fail, (cause to, let, make, ready to) fall (away, down, -en, -ing), fell(-ing), fugitive, have (inheritance), inferior, be judged (by mistake for palal), lay (along), (cause to) lie down, light (down), be (X hast) lost, lying, overthrow, overwhelm, perish, present(-ed, -ing), (make to) rot, slay, smite out, X surely, throw down.
H5308: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָפַל. In the KJV it is rendered: fall (down), have occasion.
H5309: Or nephel; from נָפַל; something fallen, i.e. an abortion. In the KJV it is rendered: untimely birth.
H5310: A primitive root; to dash to pieces, or scatter. In the KJV it is rendered: be beaten in sunder, break (in pieces), broken, dash (in pieces), cause to be discharged, dispersed, be overspread, scatter.
H5311: From נָפַץ; a storm (as dispersing). In the KJV it is rendered: scattering.
H5312: (Aramaic) a primitive root; to issue; causatively, to bring out. In the KJV it is rendered: come (go, take) forth (out).
H5313: (Aramaic) from נְפַק; an outgo, i.e. expense. In the KJV it is rendered: expense.
H5314: A primitive root; to breathe; passively, to be breathed upon, i.e. (figuratively) refreshed (as if by a current of air). In the KJV it is rendered: (be) refresh selves (-ed).
H5315: From נָפַשׁ; properly, a breathing creature, i.e. animal of (abstractly) vitality; used very widely in a literal, accommodated or figurative sense (bodily or mental). In the KJV it is rendered: any, appetite, beast, body, breath, creature, X dead(-ly), desire, X (dis-)contented, X fish, ghost, + greedy, he, heart(-y), (hath, X jeopardy of) life (X in jeopardy), lust, man, me, mind, mortally, one, own, person, pleasure, (her-, him-, my-, thy-)self, them (your)-selves, + slay, soul, + tablet, they, thing, (X she) will, X would have it.
H5316: For נָ֫פַת; a height. In the KJV it is rendered: country.
H5317: From נוּף in the sense of shaking to pieces; a dripping i.e. of honey (from the comb). In the KJV it is rendered: honeycomb.
H5318: From פָּתַח; opened, i.e. a spring; Nephtoach, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Neptoah.
H5319: From פָּתַל; properly, wrestled; but ued (in the plural) transitively, a struggle. In the KJV it is rendered: wrestling.
H5320: Plural of foreign origin, Naphtuchim, an Egyptian tribe. In the KJV it is rendered: Naptuhim.
H5321: From פָּתַל; my wrestling; Naphtali, a son of Jacob, with the tribe descended from him, and its territory. In the KJV it is rendered: Naphtali.
H5322: From נָצַץ; a flower (from its brilliancy); also a hawk (from it flashing speed); --blossom, hawk.
H5323: A primitive root; to go away; --flee.
H5324: A prim root; to station, in various applications (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: appointed, deputy, erect, establish, X Huzzah (by mistake for a proper name), lay, officer, pillar, present, rear up, set (over, up), settle, sharpen, establish, (make to) stand(-ing, still, up, upright), best state.
H5325: Passive participle of נָצַב; fixed, i.e. a handle. In the KJV it is rendered: haft.
H5326: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to נָצַב; fixedness, i.e. firmness. In the KJV it is rendered: strength.
H5327: A primitive root; properly, to go forth, i.e. (by implication) to be expelled, and (consequently) desolate; causatively, to lay waste; also (specifically), to quarrel. In the KJV it is rendered: be laid waste, runinous, strive (together).
H5329: A primitive root; properly, to glitter from afar, i.e. to be eminent (as a superintendent, especially of the Temple services and its music); also (as denominative from נֵ֫צַח), to be permanent. In the KJV it is rendered: excel, chief musician (singer), oversee(-r), set forward.
H5330: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָצַח; to become chief. In the KJV it is rendered: be preferred.
H5331: Or netsach; from נָצַח; properly, a goal, i.e. the bright object at a distance travelled towards; hence (figuratively), splendor, or (subjectively) truthfulness, or (objectively) confidence; but usually (adverbially), continually (i.e. to the most distant point of view); --alway(-s), constantly, end, (+ n-)ever(more), perpetual, strength, victory.
H5332: Probably identical with נֵ֫צַח, through the idea of brilliancy of color; juice of the grape (as blood red). In the KJV it is rendered: blood, strength.
H5333: Or ntsib; from נָצַב; something stationary, i.e. a prefect, a military post, a statue. In the KJV it is rendered: garrison, officer, pillar.
H5334: The same as נְצִיב; station; Netsib, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Nezib.
H5335: From נָצַח; conspicuous; Netsiach, a Temple- servant. In the KJV it is rendered: Neziah.
H5336: From נָצַר; properly, conservative; but used passively, delivered. In the KJV it is rendered: preserved.
H5337: A primitive root; to snatch away, whether in a good or a bad sense:- X at all, defend, deliver (self), escape, X without fail, part, pluck, preserve, recover, rescue, rid, save, spoil, strip, X surely, take (out).
H5338: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָצַל; to extricate. In the KJV it is rendered: deliver, rescue.
H5339: From נֵץ; a blossom. In the KJV it is rendered: flower.
H5340: A primitive root; to glare, i.e. be bright- colored. In the KJV it is rendered: sparkle.
H5341: A primitive root; to guard, in a good sense (to protect, maintain, obey, etc.) or a bad one (to conceal, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: besieged, hidden thing, keep(-er, -ing), monument, observe, preserve(-r), subtil, watcher(-man).
H5342: From נָצַר in the sense of greenness as a striking color; a shoot; figuratively, a descendant. In the KJV it is rendered: branch.
H5343: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to נָקָה; clean. In the KJV it is rendered: pure.
H5344: A primitive root; to puncture, literally (to perforate, with more or less violence) or figuratively (to specify, designate, libel). In the KJV it is rendered: appoint, blaspheme, bore, curse, express, with holes, name, pierce, strike through.
H5345: A bezel (for a gem). In the KJV it is rendered: pipe.
H5346: The same as נֶ֫קֶב; dell; Nekeb, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Nekeb.
H5347: From נָקַב; female (from the sexual form). In the KJV it is rendered: female.
H5348: From an unused root meaning to mark (by puncturing or branding); spotted. In the KJV it is rendered: speckled.
H5349: Active participle from the same as נָקֹד; a spotter (of sheep or cattle), i.e. the owner or tender (who thus marks them). In the KJV it is rendered: herdman, sheepmaster.
H5350: From the same as נָקֹד; a crumb (as broken to spots); also a biscuit (as pricked). In the KJV it is rendered: cracknel, mouldy.
H5351: Feminine of נָקֹד; a boss. In the KJV it is rendered: stud.
H5352: A primitive root; to be (or make) clean (literally or figuratively); by implication (in an adverse sense) to be bare, i.e. extirpated. In the KJV it is rendered: acquit X at all, X altogether, be blameless, cleanse, (be) clear(-ing), cut off, be desolate, be free, be (hold) guiltless, be (hold) innocent, X by no means, be quit, be (leave) unpunished, X utterly, X wholly.
H5353: Feminine of נָקֹד (in the figurative sense of marked); distinction; Nekoda, a Temple-servant. In the KJV it is rendered: Nekoda.
H5354: A primitive root; to loathe. In the KJV it is rendered: weary.
H5355: Or naqiyi (Joel 4:19; Jonah 1:14); from נָקָה; innocent. In the KJV it is rendered: blameless, clean, clear, exempted, free, guiltless, innocent, quit.
H5356: Or niqqayon; from נָקָה; clearness (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: cleanness, innocency.
H5357: From an unused root meaning to bore; a cleft. In the KJV it is rendered: hole.
H5358: A primitive root; to grudge, i.e. avenge or punish. In the KJV it is rendered: avenge(-r, self), punish, revenge (self), X surely, take vengeance.
H5359: From נָקַם; revenge. In the KJV it is rendered: + avenged, quarrel, vengeance.
H5360: Feminine of נָקָם; avengement, whether the act of the passion. In the KJV it is rendered: + avenge, revenge(-ing), vengeance.
H5361: A primitive root; to feel aversion. In the KJV it is rendered: be alienated.
H5362: A primitive root; to strike with more or less violence (beat, fell, corrode); by implication (of attack) to knock together, i.e. surround or circulate. In the KJV it is rendered: compass (about, -ing), cut down, destroy, go round (about), inclose, round.
H5363: From נָקַף; a threshing (of olives). In the KJV it is rendered: shaking.
H5364: From נָקַף; probably a rope (as encircling). In the KJV it is rendered: rent.
H5365: A primitive root; to bore (penetrate, quarry). In the KJV it is rendered: dig, pick out, pierce, put (thrust) out.
H5366: From נָקַר, a fissure. In the KJV it is rendered: cleft, clift.
H5367: A primitive root; to entrap (with a noose), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: catch (lay a) snare.
H5368: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָקַשׁ; but used in the sense of נָקַף; to knock. In the KJV it is rendered: smote.
H5369: The same as נֵר; lamp; Ner, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ner.
H5370: Of foreign origin; Nergal, a Cuthite deity. In the KJV it is rendered: Nergal.
H5371: From NONE and שַׂר־אֶ֫צֶר; Nergal-Sharetser, the name of two Babylonians. In the KJV it is rendered: Nergal-sharezer.
H5372: From an unused root meaning to roll to pieces; a slanderer. In the KJV it is rendered: talebearer, whisperer.
H5373: Of foreign origin; nard, an aromatic. In the KJV it is rendered: spikenard.
H5374: Or Neriyahuw; from נֵר and יָהּ; light of Jah; Nerijah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Neriah.
H5375: Or nacah (Psalm 4 : 6 (7)); a primitive root; to lift, in a great variety of applications, literal and figurative, absol. and rel. (as follows). In the KJV it is rendered: accept, advance, arise, (able to, (armor), suffer to) bear(-er, up), bring (forth), burn, carry (away), cast, contain, desire, ease, exact, exalt (self), extol, fetch, forgive, furnish, further, give, go on, help, high, hold up, honorable (+ man), lade, lay, lift (self) up, lofty, marry, magnify, X needs, obtain, pardon, raise (up), receive, regard, respect, set (up), spare, stir up, + swear, take (away, up), X utterly, wear, yield.
H5376: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָשָׂא. In the KJV it is rendered: carry away, make insurrection, take.
H5377: A primitive root; to lead astray, i.e. (mentally) to delude, or (morally) to seduce. In the KJV it is rendered: beguile, deceive, X greatly, X utterly.
H5378: A primitive root (perhaps identical with נָשָׁא, through the idea of imposition); to lend on interest; by implication, to dun for debt. In the KJV it is rendered: X debt, exact, giver of usury.
H5379: Passive participle feminine of נָשָׂא; something taken, i.e. a present. In the KJV it is rendered: gift.
H5380: A primitive root; to blow; by implication, to disperse. In the KJV it is rendered: (cause to) blow, drive away.
H5381: A primitive root; to reach (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: ability, be able, attain (unto), (be able to, can) get, lay at, put, reach, remove, wax rich, X surely, (over-)take (hold of, on, upon).
H5382: A primitive root; to forget; figuratively, to neglect; causatively, to remit, remove. In the KJV it is rendered: forget, deprive, exact.
H5383: A primitive root (rather identical with נָשָׁה, in the sense of נָשָׁא); to lend or (by reciprocity) borrow on security or interest. In the KJV it is rendered: creditor, exact, extortioner, lend, usurer, lend on (taker on) usury.
H5384: From נָשָׁה, in the sense of failure; rheumatic or crippled (from the incident to Jacob). In the KJV it is rendered: which shrank.
H5385: Or rather nsutah; feminine. passive participle of נָשָׂא; something borne, i.e. a load. In the KJV it is rendered: carriage.
H5386: From נָשָׁה; a debt. In the KJV it is rendered: debt.
H5387: Or nasi8; from נָשָׂא; properly, an exalted one, i.e. a king or sheik; also a rising mist. In the KJV it is rendered: captain, chief, cloud, governor, prince, ruler, vapour.
H5389: (Aramaic) irregular plural feminine of אֱנָשׁ. In the KJV it is rendered: women.
H5390: From נָשַׁק; a kiss. In the KJV it is rendered: kiss.
H5391: A primitive root; to strike with a sting (as a serpent); figuratively, to oppress with interest on a loan. In the KJV it is rendered: bite, lend upon usury.
H5392: From נָשַׁך; interest on a debt. In the KJV it is rendered: usury.
H5393: For לִשְׁכָּה; a cell. In the KJV it is rendered: chamber.
H5394: A primitive root; to pluck off, i.e. divest, eject or drop. In the KJV it is rendered: cast (out), drive, loose, put off (out), slip.
H5395: A primitive root; properly, to blow away, i.e. destroy. In the KJV it is rendered: destroy.
H5396: (Aramaic) corresponding to נְשָׁמָה; vital breath. In the KJV it is rendered: breath.
H5397: From נָשַׁם; a puff, i.e. wind, angry or vital breath, divine inspiration, intellect. or (concretely) an animal. In the KJV it is rendered: blast, (that) breath(-eth), inspiration, soul, spirit.
H5398: A primitive root; to breeze, i.e. blow up fresh (as the wind). In the KJV it is rendered: blow.
H5399: From נָשַׁף; properly, a breeze, i.e. (by implication) dusk (when the evening breeze prevails). In the KJV it is rendered: dark, dawning of the day (morning), night, twilight.
H5400: A primitive root; to catch fire. In the KJV it is rendered: burn, kindle.
H5401: A primitive root (identical with נָשַׂק, through the idea of fastening up; compare חָזַק, חָשַׁק); to kiss, literally or figuratively (touch); also (as a mode of attachment), to equip with weapons. In the KJV it is rendered: armed (men), rule, kiss, that touched.
H5402: Or nesheq; from נָשַׁק; military equipment, i.e. (collectively) arms (offensive or defensive), or (concretely) an arsenal. In the KJV it is rendered: armed men, armour(-y), battle, harness, weapon.
H5403: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָ֫שֶׁר; an eagle. In the KJV it is rendered: eagle.
H5404: From an unused root meaning to lacerate; the eagle (or other large bird of prey). In the KJV it is rendered: eagle.
H5405: A primitive root; properly, to eliminate, i.e. (intransitively) to dry up. In the KJV it is rendered: fail.
H5406: Probably of Persian origin; an epistle. In the KJV it is rendered: letter.
H5407: (Aramaic) corresponding to NONE. In the KJV it is rendered: letter.
H5408: A primitive root; to dismember. In the KJV it is rendered: cut (in pieces), divide, hew in pieces.
H5409: From נָתַח; a fragment. In the KJV it is rendered: part, piece.
H5410: Or (feminine) nthiybah; or nthibah (Jeremiah 6:16); from an unused root meaning to tramp; a (beaten) track. In the KJV it is rendered: path((-way)), X travel(-ler), way.
H5411: Or Nathuwn (Ezra 8:17) (the proper form as passive participle), from נָתַן; one given, i.e. (in the plural only) the Nethinim, or Temple-servants (as given to that duty). In the KJV it is rendered: Nethinims.
H5412: (Aramaic) corresponding to נְתִינִים. In the KJV it is rendered: Nethinims.
H5413: A primitive root; to flow forth (literally or figuratively); by implication, to liquify. In the KJV it is rendered: drop, gather (together), melt, pour (forth, out).
H5414: A primitive root; to give, used with greatest latitude of application (put, make, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: add, apply, appoint, ascribe, assign, X avenge, X be ((healed)), bestow, bring (forth, hither), cast, cause, charge, come, commit, consider, count, + cry, deliver (up), direct, distribute, do, X doubtless, X without fail, fasten, frame, X get, give (forth, over, up), grant, hang (up), X have, X indeed, lay (unto charge, up), (give) leave, lend, let (out), + lie, lift up, make, + O that, occupy, offer, ordain, pay, perform, place, pour, print, X pull, put (forth), recompense, render, requite, restore, send (out), set (forth), shew, shoot forth (up), + sing, + slander, strike, (sub-)mit, suffer, X surely, X take, thrust, trade, turn, utter, + weep, + willingly, + withdraw, + would (to) God, yield.
H5415: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָתַן; give. In the KJV it is rendered: bestow, give pay.
H5416: From נָתַן; given; Nathan, the name of five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Nathan.
H5417: From נָתַן and אֵל; given of God; Nethanel, the name of ten Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Nethaneel.
H5418: Or Nthanyahuw; from נָתַן and יָהּ; given of Jah; Nethanjah, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Nethaniah.
H5419: From נָתַן and מֶ֫לֶך; given of (the) king; Nethan-Melek, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Nathan-melech.
H5420: A primitive root; to tear up. In the KJV it is rendered: mar.
H5421: For נָתַץ; to tear out. In the KJV it is rendered: break.
H5422: A primitive root; to tear down. In the KJV it is rendered: beat down, break down (out), cast down, destroy, overthrow, pull down, throw down.
H5423: A primitive root; to tear off. In the KJV it is rendered: break (off), burst, draw (away), lift up, pluck (away, off), pull (out), root out.
H5424: From נָתַק; scurf. In the KJV it is rendered: (dry) scall.
H5425: A primitive root; to jump, i.e. be violently agitated; causatively, to terrify, shake off, untie. In the KJV it is rendered: drive asunder, leap, (let) loose, X make, move, undo.
H5426: (Aramaic) corresponding to נָתַר. In the KJV it is rendered: shake off.
H5427: From נָתַר; mineral potash (so called from effervescing with acid). In the KJV it is rendered: nitre.
H5428: A primitive root; to tear away. In the KJV it is rendered: destroy, forsake, pluck (out, up, by the roots), pull up, root out (up), X utterly.
H5429: From an unused root meaning to define; a seah, or certain measure (as determinative) for grain. In the KJV it is rendered: measure.
H5430: From סָאַן; perhaps a military boot (as a protection from mud. In the KJV it is rendered: battle.
H5431: A primitive root; to be miry; used only as denominative from סְאוֹן; to shoe, i.e. (active participle) a soldier shod. In the KJV it is rendered: warrior.
H5432: For סְאָה־; measurement, i.e. moderation. In the KJV it is rendered: measure.
H5433: A primitive root; to quaff to satiety, i.e. become tipsy. In the KJV it is rendered: drunkard, fill self, Sabean, (wine-)bibber.
H5434: Of foreign origin; Seba, a son of Cush, and the country settled by him. In the KJV it is rendered: Seba.
H5435: From סָבָא; potation, concretely (wine), or abstractly (carousal). In the KJV it is rendered: drink, drunken, wine.
H5436: Patrial from סְבָא; a Sebaite, or inhabitant of Seba. In the KJV it is rendered: Sabean.
H5437: A primitive root; to revolve, surround, or border; used in various applications, literally and figuratively (as follows). In the KJV it is rendered: bring, cast, fetch, lead, make, walk, X whirl, X round about, be about on every side, apply, avoid, beset (about), besiege, bring again, carry (about), change, cause to come about, X circuit, (fetch a) compass (about, round), drive, environ, X on every side, beset (close, come, compass, go, stand) round about, inclose, remove, return, set, sit down, turn (self) (about, aside, away, back).
H5438: From סָבַב; a (providential) turn (of affairs). In the KJV it is rendered: cause.
H5439: Or (feminine) cbiybah; from סָבַב; (as noun) a circle, neighbour, or environs; but chiefly (as adverb, with or without preposition) around. In the KJV it is rendered: (place, round) about, circuit, compass, on every side.
H5440: A primitive root; to entwine. In the KJV it is rendered: fold together, wrap.
H5441: From סָבַך; a copse. In the KJV it is rendered: thicket.
H5442: From סָבַך, a copse. In the KJV it is rendered: thick(-et).
H5443: (Aramaic) or sabbka: (Aramaic); from a root corresponding to סָבַך; a lyre. In the KJV it is rendered: sackbut.
H5444: From סָבַך; copse-like; Sibbecai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Sibbecai, Sibbechai.
H5445: A primitive root; to carry (literally or figuratively), or (reflexively) be burdensome; specifically, to be gravid. In the KJV it is rendered: bear, be a burden, carry, strong to labour.
H5446: (Aramaic) corresponding to סָבַל; to erect. In the KJV it is rendered: strongly laid.
H5447: From סָבַל; a load (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: burden, charge.
H5448: (only in the form cubbal; from סָבַל; a load (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: burden.
H5449: From סָבַל; a porter. In the KJV it is rendered: (to bear, bearer of) burden(-s).
H5450: From סֵ֫בֶל; porterage. In the KJV it is rendered: burden.
H5451: For שִׁבֳּלִים; an ear of grain. In the KJV it is rendered: Sibboleth.
H5452: (Aramaic) a primitive root; to bear in mind, i.e. hope. In the KJV it is rendered: think.
H5453: Dual from a root corresponding to סְבַר; double hope; Sibrajim, a place in Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Sibraim.
H5454: Or Cabtah; probably of foreign derivation; Sabta or Sabtah, the name of a son of Cush, and the country occupied by his posterity. In the KJV it is rendered: Sabta, Sabtah.
H5455: Probably of foreign derivation; Sabteca, the name of a son of Cush, and the region settled by him. In the KJV it is rendered: Sabtecha, Sabtechah.
H5456: A primitive root; to prostrate oneself (in homage). In the KJV it is rendered: fall down.
H5457: (Aramaic) corresponding to סָגַד. In the KJV it is rendered: worship.
H5458: From סָגַר; properly, shut up, i.e. the breast (as inclosing the heart); also gold (as generally shut up safely). In the KJV it is rendered: caul, gold.
H5459: Feminine passive participle of an unused root meaning to shut up; wealth (as closely shut up). In the KJV it is rendered: jewel, peculiar (treasure), proper good, special.
H5460: (Aramaic) corresponding to סְגָנִים. In the KJV it is rendered: governor.
H5461: From an unused root meaning to superintend; a prefect of a province. In the KJV it is rendered: prince, ruler.
H5462: A primitive root; to shut up; figuratively, to surrender. In the KJV it is rendered: close up, deliver (up), give over (up), inclose, X pure, repair, shut (in, self, out, up, up together), stop, X straitly.
