H5463: (Aramaic) corresponding to סָגַר. In the KJV it is rendered: shut up.
H5464: Probably from סָגַר in the sense of sweeping away; a pouring rain. In the KJV it is rendered: very rainy.
H5465: From an unused root meaning to estop; the stocks. In the KJV it is rendered: stocks.
H5466: From an unused root meaning to envelop; a wrapper, i.e. shirt. In the KJV it is rendered: fine linen, sheet.
H5467: From an unused root meaning to scorch; burnt (i.e. volcanic or bituminous) district; Sedom, a place near the Dead Sea. In the KJV it is rendered: Sodom.
H5468: From an unused root meaning to arrange; order. In the KJV it is rendered: order.
H5469: From an unused root meaning to be round; roundness. In the KJV it is rendered: round.
H5470: From the same as סַ֫הַר; a dungeon (as surrounded by walls). In the KJV it is rendered: prison.
H5471: Of foreign derivation; So, an Egyptian king. In the KJV it is rendered: So.
H5472: A primitive root; properly, to flinch, i.e. (by implication) to go back, literally (to retreat) or figuratively (to apostatize). In the KJV it is rendered: backslider, drive, go back, turn (away, back).
H5473: A primitive root (probably rather identical with סוּג through the idea of shrinking from a hedge; compare שׂוּג); to hem in, i.e. bind. In the KJV it is rendered: set about.
H5474: From סָגַר; an inclosure, i.e. cage (for an animal). In the KJV it is rendered: ward.
H5475: From יָסַד; a session, i.e. company of persons (in close deliberation); by implication, intimacy, consultation, a secret. In the KJV it is rendered: assembly, consel, inward, secret (counsel).
H5476: From סוֹד; a confidant; Sodi, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Sodi.
H5477: From an unused root meaning to wipe away; sweeping; Suach, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Suah.
H5478: From the same as ס֫וּחַ; something swept away, i.e. filth. In the KJV it is rendered: torn.
H5479: From סוּט; roving; Sotai, one of the Nethinim. In the KJV it is rendered: Sotai.
H5480: A primitive root; properly, to smear over (with oil), i.e. anoint. In the KJV it is rendered: anoint (self), X at all.
H5481: (Aramaic) or cuwmponyah (Aramaic); or ciyphonya: (Dan. 3:10) (Aramaic); of Greek origin; a bagpipe (with a double pipe). In the KJV it is rendered: dulcimer.
H5482: (rather to be written Cvenah; for Cven; i.e to Seven); of Egyptian derivation; Seven, a place in Upper Egypt. In the KJV it is rendered: Syene.
H5483: Or cuc; from an unused root meaning to skip (properly, for joy); a horse (as leaping); also a swallow (from its rapid flight). In the KJV it is rendered: crane, horse((-back, -hoof)).
H5484: Feminine of סוּס; a mare. In the KJV it is rendered: company of horses.
H5485: From סוּס; horse-like; Susi, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Susi.
H5486: A primitive root; to snatch away, i.e. terminate. In the KJV it is rendered: consume, have an end, perish, X be utterly.
H5487: (Aramaic) corresponding to סוּף; to come to an end. In the KJV it is rendered: consume, fulfill.
H5488: Probably of Egyptian origin; a reed, especially the papyrus. In the KJV it is rendered: flag, Red (sea), weed.
H5489: For סוּף (by ellipsis of יָם); the Reed (Sea). In the KJV it is rendered: Red Sea.
H5490: From סוּף; a termination:--conclusion, end, hinder participle.
H5491: (Aramaic) corresponding to סוֹף. In the KJV it is rendered: end.
H5492: From סוּף; a hurricane. In the KJV it is rendered: Red Sea, storm, tempest, whirlwind, Red sea.
H5493: Or suwr (Hosea 9:12); a primitive root; to turn off (literal or figurative). In the KJV it is rendered: be(-head), bring, call back, decline, depart, eschew, get (you), go (aside), X grievous, lay away (by), leave undone, be past, pluck away, put (away, down), rebel, remove (to and fro), revolt, X be sour, take (away, off), turn (aside, away, in), withdraw, be without.
H5494: Probably passive participle of סוּר; turned off, i.e. deteriorated. In the KJV it is rendered: degenerate.
H5495: The same as סוּר; Sur, a gate of the temple. In the KJV it is rendered: Sur.
H5496: Perhaps denominative from שָׁ֫יִת; properly, to prick, i.e. (figuratively) stimulate; by implication, to seduce. In the KJV it is rendered: entice, move, persuade, provoke, remove, set on, stir up, take away.
H5497: Probably from the same root as מַסְוֶה; covering, i.e. clothing. In the KJV it is rendered: clothes.
H5498: A primitive root; to trail along. In the KJV it is rendered: draw (out), tear.
H5499: From סָחַב; a rag. In the KJV it is rendered: cast clout.
H5500: A primitive root; to sweep away. In the KJV it is rendered: scrape.
H5501: From סָחָה; refuse (as swept off). In the KJV it is rendered: offscouring.
H5502: A primitive root; to scrape off. In the KJV it is rendered: sweep (away).
H5503: A primitive root; to travel round (specifically as a pedlar); intensively, to palpitate. In the KJV it is rendered: go about, merchant(-man), occupy with, pant, trade, traffick.
H5504: From סָחַר; profit (from trade). In the KJV it is rendered: merchandise.
H5505: From סָחַר; an emporium; abstractly, profit (from trade). In the KJV it is rendered: mart, merchandise.
H5506: From סָחַר: traffic. In the KJV it is rendered: merchandise.
H5507: Properly, active participle feminine of סָחַר; something surrounding the person, i.e. a shield. In the KJV it is rendered: buckler.
H5508: Similar to סֹחֵרָה; probably a (black) tile (or tessara) for laying borders with. In the KJV it is rendered: black marble.
H5509: Or cuwg (Ezek. 22:18); from סוּג in the sense of refuse; scoria. In the KJV it is rendered: dross.
H5510: Probably of Persian origin; Sivan, the third Heb. month. In the KJV it is rendered: Sivan.
H5511: Or Ciychon; from the same as ס֫וּחַ; tempestuous; Sichon, an Amoritish king. In the KJV it is rendered: Sihon.
H5512: Of uncertain derivation; Sin the name of an Egyptian town and (probably) desert adjoining. In the KJV it is rendered: Sin.
H5513: From an otherwise unknown name of a man; a Sinite, or descendant of one of the sons of Canaan. In the KJV it is rendered: Sinite.
H5514: Of uncertain derivation; Sinai, mountain of Arabia. In the KJV it is rendered: Sinai.
H5515: Plural of an otherwise unknown name; Sinim, a distant Oriental region. In the KJV it is rendered: Sinim.
H5516: Of uncertain derivation; Sisera, the name of a Canaanitish king and of one of the Nethinim. In the KJV it is rendered: Sisera.
H5517: Or Ciyeahai; from an unused root meaning to converse; congregation; Sia or Siaha, one of the Nethinim. In the KJV it is rendered: Sia, Siaha.
H5518: Or (feminine) ciyrah; or cirah (Jeremiah 52:18); from a primitive root meaning to boil up; a pot; also a thorn (as springing up rapidly); by implication, a hook. In the KJV it is rendered: caldron, fishhook, pan, ((wash-))pot, thorn.
H5519: From סָכַך; properly, a thicket of men, i.e. a crowd. In the KJV it is rendered: multitude.
H5520: From סָכַך; a hut (as of entwined boughs); also a lair. In the KJV it is rendered: covert, den, pavilion, tabernacle.
H5521: Fem of סֹך; a hut or lair. In the KJV it is rendered: booth, cottage, covert, pavilion, tabernacle, tent.
H5522: Feminine of סָך; an (idolatrous) booth. In the KJV it is rendered: tabernacle.
H5523: Or Cukkoth; plural of סֻכָּה; booths; Succoth, the name of a place in Egypt and of three in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Succoth.
H5524: From סֻכּוֹת and the (irreg.) plural of בַּת; booths of (the) daughters; brothels, i.e. idoalatrous tents for impure purpose. In the KJV it is rendered: Succoth-benoth.
H5525: Patrial from an unknown name (perhaps סֹך); a Sukkite, or inhabitant of some place near Egypt (i.e. hut-dwellers). In the KJV it is rendered: Sukkiims.
H5526: Or sakak (Exod. 33:22); a primitive root; properly, to entwine as a screen; by implication, to fence in, cover over, (figuratively) protect. In the KJV it is rendered: cover, defence, defend, hedge in, join together, set, shut up.
H5527: From סָכַך; inclosure; Secacah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Secacah.
H5528: For כָּסַל; to be silly. In the KJV it is rendered: do (make, play the, turn into) fool(-ish, -ishly, -ishness).
H5529: From סָכַל; silliness; concretely and collectively, dolts. In the KJV it is rendered: folly.
H5530: From סָכַל; silly. In the KJV it is rendered: fool(-ish), sottish.
H5531: Or sikluwth (Eccl. 1:17); from סָכַל; silliness. In the KJV it is rendered: folly, foolishness.
H5532: A primitive root; to be familiar with; by implication, to minister to, be serviceable to, be customary. In the KJV it is rendered: acquaint (self), be advantage, X ever, (be, (un-))profit(-able), treasurer, be wont.
H5533: Probably a denominative from שַׂכִּין; properly, to cut, i.e. damage; also to grow (causatively, make) poor. In the KJV it is rendered: endanger, impoverish.
H5534: A primitive root; to shut up; by implication, to surrender. In the KJV it is rendered: stop, give over.
H5535: A primitive root to be silent; by implication, to observe quietly. In the KJV it is rendered: take heed.
H5536: From סָלַל; properly, a willow twig (as pendulous), i.e. an osier; but only as woven into a basket. In the KJV it is rendered: basket.
H5537: A primitive root; to suspend in a balance, i.e. weigh. In the KJV it is rendered: compare.
H5538: From סָלַל; an embankment; Silla, a place in Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: Silla.
H5539: A primitive root; probably to leap (with joy), i.e. exult. In the KJV it is rendered: harden self.
H5540: From סָלַד; exultation; Seled, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Seled.
H5541: A primitive root; to hang up, i.e. weigh, or (figuratively) contemn. In the KJV it is rendered: tread down (under foot), value.
H5542: From סָלָה; suspension (of music), i.e. pause. In the KJV it is rendered: Selah.
H5543: Or Calluw; or Caluw; or Callay; from סָלָה; weighed; Sallu or Sallai, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Sallai, Sallu, Salu.
H5544: Or callown; from סָלָה; a prickle (as if pendulous); brier, thorn.
H5545: A primitive root; to forgive. In the KJV it is rendered: forgive, pardon, spare.
H5546: From סָלַח; placable: ready to forgive.
H5547: From סָלַח; pardon. In the KJV it is rendered: forgiveness, pardon.
H5548: From an unused root. meaning to walk; walking; Salcah, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Salcah, Salchah.
H5549: A primitive root; to mound up (especially a turnpike); figurative, to exalt; reflexively, to oppose (as by a dam). In the KJV it is rendered: cast up, exalt (self), extol, make plain, raise up.
H5550: Or cowllah; active participle feminine of סָלַל, but used passively; a military mound, i.e. rampart of besiegers. In the KJV it is rendered: bank, mount.
H5551: From סָלַל; a stair-case. In the KJV it is rendered: ladder.
H5552: From סָלָה; a twig (as pendulous). In the KJV it is rendered: basket.
H5553: From an unused root meaning to be lofty; a craggy rock, literally or figuratively (a fortress). In the KJV it is rendered: (ragged) rock, stone(-ny), strong hold.
H5554: The same as סָ֫לַע; Sela, the rock-city of Idumaea. In the KJV it is rendered: rock, Sela(-h).
H5555: From סָ֫לַע and the plural of מַחֲלֹ֫קֶת with the article interposed; rock of the divisions; Sela- ham-Machlekoth, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Sela-hammalekoth.
H5556: Apparently from the same as סָ֫לַע in the sense of crushing as with a rock, i.e. consuming; a kind of locust (from its destructiveness). In the KJV it is rendered: bald locust.
H5557: A primitive root; properly, to wrench, i.e. (figuratively) to subvert. In the KJV it is rendered: overthrow, pervert.
H5558: From סָלַף; distortion, i.e. (figuratively) viciousness. In the KJV it is rendered: perverseness.
H5559: (Aramaic) a primitive root; to ascend. In the KJV it is rendered: come (up).
H5560: From an unused root meaning to strip; flour (as chipped off). In the KJV it is rendered: (fine) flour, meal.
H5561: From an unused root meaning to smell sweet; an aroma. In the KJV it is rendered: sweet (spice).
H5562: Of foreign origin; Samgar-Nebo, a Babylonian general. In the KJV it is rendered: Samgar-nebo.
H5563: Of uncertain derivation; a vine blossom; used also adverbially, abloom. In the KJV it is rendered: tender grape.
H5564: A primitive root; to prop (literally or figuratively); reflexively, to lean upon or take hold of (in a favorable or unfavorable sense). In the KJV it is rendered: bear up, establish, (up-)hold, lay, lean, lie hard, put, rest self, set self, stand fast, stay (self), sustain.
H5565: From סָמַך and יָהּ; supported of Jah; Semakjah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Semachiah.
H5566: Or cemel; from an unused root meaning to resemble; a likeness. In the KJV it is rendered: figure, idol, image.
H5567: A primitive root; to designate. In the KJV it is rendered: appointed.
H5568: A primitive root; to be erect, i.e. bristle as hair. In the KJV it is rendered: stand up, tremble.
H5569: From סָמַר; bristling, i.e. shaggy. In the KJV it is rendered: rough.
H5570: From an unused root meaning to prick; thorny; Senaah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Senaah, Hassenaah (with the article).
H5571: Of foreign origin; Sanballat, a Persian satrap of Samaria. In the KJV it is rendered: Sanballat.
H5572: From an unused root meaning to prick; a bramble. In the KJV it is rendered: bush.
H5573: The same s סְנֶה; thorn; Seneh, a crag in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Seneh.
H5574: Or Cnu.ah from the same as סְנָאָה; pointed; (used with the article as a proper name) Senuah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Hasenuah (including the art), Senuah.
H5575: Of uncertain derivation; (in plural) blindness. In the KJV it is rendered: blindness.
H5576: Of foreign origin; Sancherib, an Assyrian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Sennacherib.
H5577: From an unused root meaning to be pointed; a twig (as tapering). In the KJV it is rendered: bough.
H5578: Feminine of a form of סַנְסִן; a bough; Sansannah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Sansannah.
H5579: Of uncertain derivation; a fin (collectively). In the KJV it is rendered: fins.
H5580: From the same as סוּס; a moth (from the agility of the fly). In the KJV it is rendered: moth.
H5581: Of uncertain derivation; Sismai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Sisamai.
H5582: A primitive root; to suport (mostly figurative). In the KJV it is rendered: comfort, establish, hold up, refresh self, strengthen, be upholden.
H5583: (Aramaic) corresponding to סָעַד; to aid. In the KJV it is rendered: helping.
H5584: A primitive root; to rush. In the KJV it is rendered: storm.
H5585: From סָעַף; a fissure (of rocks); also a bough (as subdivided). In the KJV it is rendered: (outmost) branch, clift, top.
H5586: A primitive root; properly, to divide up; but used only as denominative from סְעִיף, to disbranch (a tree). In the KJV it is rendered: top.
H5587: Or samiph; from סָעַף; divided (in mind), i.e. (abstractly) a sentiment. In the KJV it is rendered: opinion.
H5588: From סָעַף; divided (in mind), i.e. (concretely) a skeptic. In the KJV it is rendered: thought.
H5589: Feminine of סְעִיף; a twig. In the KJV it is rendered: bough, branch.
H5590: A primitive root; to rush upon; by implication, to toss (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative). In the KJV it is rendered: be (toss with) tempest(-uous), be sore, troubled, come out as a (drive with the, scatter with a) whirlwind.
H5591: Or (feminine) ctarah; from סָעַר; a hurricane. In the KJV it is rendered: storm(-y), tempest, whirlwind.
H5592: From סָפַף, in its original sense of containing; a vestibule (as a limit); also a dish (for holding blood or wine). In the KJV it is rendered: bason, bowl, cup, door (post), gate, post, threshold.
H5593: The same as סַף; Saph, a Philistine. In the KJV it is rendered: Saph.
H5594: A primitive root; properly, to tear the hair and beat the breasts (as Orientals do in grief); generally to lament; by implication, to wail. In the KJV it is rendered: lament, mourn(-er), wail.
H5595: A primitive root; properly, to scrape (literally, to shave; but usually figuratively) together (i.e. to accumulate or increase) or away (i.e. to scatter, remove, or ruin; intransitively, to perish). In the KJV it is rendered: add, augment, consume, destroy, heap, join, perish, put.
H5596: Or saphach (Isaiah 3:17); a primitive root; properly, to scrape out, but in certain peculiar senses (of removal or association). In the KJV it is rendered: abiding, gather together, cleave, smite with the scab.
H5597: From סָפַח; the mange (as making the hair fall off). In the KJV it is rendered: scab.
H5598: From סַף; bason-like; Sippai, a Philistine. In the KJV it is rendered: Sippai.
H5599: From סָפַח; something (spontaneously) falling off, i.e. a self-sown crop; figuratively, a freshet. In the KJV it is rendered: (such) things as (which) grow (of themselves), which groweth of its own accord (itself).
H5600: From סָפַן; a (sea-going) vessel (as ceiled with a deck). In the KJV it is rendered: ship.
H5601: From סָפַר; a gem (perhaps used for scratching other substances), probably the sapphire. In the KJV it is rendered: sapphire.
H5602: From an unused root meaning to depress; a basin (as deepened out). In the KJV it is rendered: bowl, dish.
H5603: A primitive root; to hide by covering; specifically, to roof (passive participle as noun, a roof) or wainscot; figuratively, to reserve. In the KJV it is rendered: cieled, cover, seated.
H5604: From סָפַן; a wainscot. In the KJV it is rendered: cieling.
H5605: A primitive root; properly, to snatch away, i.e. terminate; but used only as denominative from סַף (in the sense of a vestibule), to wait at the threshold. In the KJV it is rendered: be a doorkeeper.
H5606: Or saphaq (1 Kings 20:10; Job 27:23; Isaiah 2:6); a primitive root; to clap the hands (in token of compact, derision, grief, indignation, or punishment); by implication of satisfaction, to be enough; by implication of excess, to vomit. In the KJV it is rendered: clap, smite, strike, suffice, wallow.
H5607: Or sepheq (Job 20:22; 36:18); from סָפַק; chastisement; also satiety. In the KJV it is rendered: stroke, sufficiency.
H5608: A primitive root; properly, to score with a mark as a tally or record, i.e. (by implication) to inscribe, and also to enumerate; intensively, to recount, i.e. celebrate. In the KJV it is rendered: commune, (ac-)count; declare, number, + penknife, reckon, scribe, shew forth, speak, talk, tell (out), writer.
H5609: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to סָפַר; a book. In the KJV it is rendered: book, roll.
H5610: From סָפַר; a census. In the KJV it is rendered: numbering.
H5611: The same as סְפָר; Sephar, a place in Arabia. In the KJV it is rendered: Sephar.
H5612: Or (feminine) ciphrah (Psa. 56:8 (9)); from סָפַר; properly, writing (the art or a document); by implication, a book. In the KJV it is rendered: bill, book, evidence, X learn(-ed) (-ing), letter, register, scroll.
H5613: (Aramaic) from the same as סְפַר; a scribe (secular or sacred). In the KJV it is rendered: scribe.
H5614: Of foreign derivation; Sepharad, a region of Assyria. In the KJV it is rendered: Sepharad.
H5615: From סָפַר; a numeration. In the KJV it is rendered: number.
H5616: Patrial from NONE; a Sepharvite or inhabitant of Sepharvain. In the KJV it is rendered: Sepharvite.
H5618: Feminine active participle of סָפַר; a scribe (properly, female); Sophereth, a temple servant. In the KJV it is rendered: Sophereth.
H5619: A primitive root; properly, to be weighty; but used only in the sense of lapidation or its contrary (as if a delapidation). In the KJV it is rendered: (cast, gather out, throw) stone(-s), X surely.
H5620: Contracted from סָרַר; peevish. In the KJV it is rendered: heavy, sad.
H5621: From an unused root meaning to sting; a thistle. In the KJV it is rendered: brier.
H5622: (Aramaic) of uncertain derivation; a cloak. In the KJV it is rendered: coat.
H5623: Of foreign derivation; Sargon, an Assyrian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Sargon.
H5624: From a primitive root meaning to tremble; trembling; Sered, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Sered.
H5625: Patron from סֶ֫רֶד; a Seredite (collectively) or descendants of Sered. In the KJV it is rendered: Sardites.
H5626: From סוּר; departure; Sirah, a cistern so-called. In the KJV it is rendered: Sirah.
H5627: From סוּר; apostasy, crime; figuratively, remission. In the KJV it is rendered: X continual, rebellion, revolt((-ed)), turn away, wrong.
H5628: A primitive root; to extend (even to excess). In the KJV it is rendered: exceeding, hand, spread, stretch self, banish.
H5629: From סָרַח; a redundancy. In the KJV it is rendered: remnant.
H5630: For שִׁרְיוֹן; a coat of mail. In the KJV it is rendered: brigandine.
H5631: Or caric; from an unused root meaning to castrate; a eunuch; by implication, valet (especially of the female apartments), and thus, a minister of state. In the KJV it is rendered: chamberlain, eunuch, officer.
H5632: (Aramaic) of foreign origin; an emir. In the KJV it is rendered: president.
H5633: From an unused root of uncertain meaning; an axle; figuratively, a peer. In the KJV it is rendered: lord, plate.
H5634: For סְעַפּוֹת; a twig. In the KJV it is rendered: bough.
H5635: A primitive root; to cremate, i.e. to be (near) of kin (such being privileged to kindle the pyre). In the KJV it is rendered: burn.
H5636: From סָרַף; a nettle (as stinging like a burn). In the KJV it is rendered: brier.
H5637: A primitive root; to turn away, i.e. (morally) be refractory. In the KJV it is rendered: X away, backsliding, rebellious, revolter(-ing), slide back, stubborn, withdrew.
H5638: From an unused root meaning to hide; winter (as the dark season). In the KJV it is rendered: winter.
H5639: From סָתַר; hidden; Sethur, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Sethur.
H5640: Or satham (Numbers 24:15); a primitive root; to stop up; by implication, to repair; figuratively, to keep secret. In the KJV it is rendered: closed up, hidden, secret, shut out (up), stop.
H5641: A primitive root; to hide (by covering), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: be absent, keep close, conceal, hide (self), (keep) secret, X surely.
H5642: (Aramaic) corresponding to סָתַר; to conceal; figuratively, to demolish. In the KJV it is rendered: destroy, secret thing.
H5643: Or (feminine) cithrah (Deut. 32:38),; from סָתַר; a cover (in a good or a bad, a literal or a figurative sense). In the KJV it is rendered: backbiting, covering, covert, X disguise(-th), hiding place, privily, protection, secret(-ly, place).
H5644: From סָ֫תֶר; protective; Sithri, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zithri.
H5645: (masculine and feminine); from עוּב; properly, an envelope, i.e. darkness (or density, 2 Chron. 4:17); specifically, a (scud) cloud; also a copse. In the KJV it is rendered: clay, (thick) cloud, X thick, thicket.
H5646: Or sob; from an unused root meaning to cover; properly, equivalent to עָב; but used only as an architectural term, an architrave (as shading the pillars). In the KJV it is rendered: thick (beam, plant).
H5647: A primitive root; to work (in any sense); by implication, to serve, till, (causatively) enslave, etc.:--X be, keep in bondage, be bondmen, bond-service, compel, do, dress, ear, execute, + husbandman, keep, labour(-ing man, bring to pass, (cause to, make to) serve(-ing, self), (be, become) servant(-s), do (use) service, till(-er), transgress (from margin), (set a) work, be wrought, worshipper.
H5648: (Aramaic) corresponding to עָבַד; to do, make, prepare, keep, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: X cut, do, execute, go on, make, move, work.
H5649: (Aramaic) from עֲבַד; a servant. In the KJV it is rendered: servant.
H5650: From עָבַד; a servant. In the KJV it is rendered: X bondage, bondman, (bond-)servant, (man-)servant.
H5651: The same as עָ֫בֶד; Ebed, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ebed.
H5652: From עָבַד; a deed. In the KJV it is rendered: work.
H5653: From עָבַד; work; Abda, the name of two Israelites:--Abda.
H5654: From the active participle of עָבַד and אֱדוֹם; worker of Edom; Obed-Edom, the name of five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Obed-edom.
H5655: From עָבַד and אֵל; serving God; Abdeel, an Israelite: Abdeel. Compare עַבְדִּיאֵל.
H5656: Or mabowdah; from עָבַד; work of any kind. In the KJV it is rendered: act, bondage, + bondservant, effect, labour, ministering(-try), office, service(-ile, -itude), tillage, use, work, X wrought.
H5657: Passive participle of עָבַד; something wrought, i.e. (concretely) service. In the KJV it is rendered: household, store of servants.
H5658: From עָבַד; servitude; Abdon, the name of a place in Palestine and of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Abdon.
H5659: From עָבַד; servitude. In the KJV it is rendered: bondage.
H5660: From עָבַד; serviceable; Abdi, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Abdi.
H5661: From עָ֫בֶד and אֵל; servant of God; Abdiel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Abdiel.
H5662: Or Obadyahuw; active participle of עָבַד and יָהּ; serving Jah; Obadjah, the name of thirteen Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Obadiah.
H5663: From עָ֫בֶד and מֶ֫לֶך; servant of a king; Ebed-Melek, a eunuch of Zedekeah. In the KJV it is rendered: Ebed-melech.
H5664: The same as עֲבֵד נְגוֹ; Abed-Nego, the Babylonian name of one of Daniel's companions. In the KJV it is rendered: Abed-nego.
H5665: (Aramaic) of foreign origin; Abed-Nego, the name of Azariah. In the KJV it is rendered: Abed-nego.
H5666: A primitive root; to be dense. In the KJV it is rendered: be (grow) thick(-er).
H5667: Or rabot; from עָבַט; a pawn. In the KJV it is rendered: pledge.
H5668: Or rabur; passive participle of עָבַר; properly, crossed, i.e. (abstractly) transit; used only adverbially, on account of, in order that. In the KJV it is rendered: because of, for (.
H5669: The same as עֲבוּר; passed, i.e. kept over; used only of stored grain. In the KJV it is rendered: old corn.
H5670: A primitive root; to pawn; causatively, to lend (on security); figuratively, to entangle. In the KJV it is rendered: borrow, break (ranks), fetch (a pledge), lend, X surely.
H5671: From עָבַט; something pledged, i.e. (collectively) pawned goods. In the KJV it is rendered: thick clay (by a false etym.
H5672: Or mobiy; from עָבָה; density, i.e. depth or width. In the KJV it is rendered: thick(-ness).
H5673: (Aramaic) from עֲבַד; labor or business. In the KJV it is rendered: affairs, service, work.
H5674: A primitive root; to cross over; used very widely of any transition (literal or figurative; transitive, intransitive, intensive, causative); specifically, to cover (in copulation). In the KJV it is rendered: alienate, alter, X at all, beyond, bring (over, through), carry over, (over-)come (on, over), conduct (over), convey over, current, deliver, do away, enter, escape, fail, gender, get over, (make) go (away, beyond, by, forth, his way, in, on, over, through), have away (more), lay, meddle, overrun, make partition, (cause to, give, make to, over) pass(-age, along, away, beyond, by, -enger, on, out, over, through), (cause to, make) + proclaim(-amation), perish, provoke to anger, put away, rage, + raiser of taxes, remove, send over, set apart, + shave, cause to (make) sound, X speedily, X sweet smelling, take (away), (make to) transgress(-or), translate, turn away, (way-)faring man, be wrath.
H5675: (Aramaic) corresponding to עֵ֫בֶר. In the KJV it is rendered: beyond, this side.
H5676: From עָבַר; properly, a region across; but used only adverbially (with or without a preposition) on the opposite side (especially of the Jordan; ususally meaning the east). In the KJV it is rendered: X against, beyond, by, X from, over, passage, quarter, (other, this) side, straight.
H5677: The same as עֵ֫בֶר; Eber, the name of two patriarchs and four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Eber, Heber.
H5678: Feminine of עֵ֫בֶר; an outburst of passion. In the KJV it is rendered: anger, rage, wrath.
H5679: From עָבַר; a crossing-place. In the KJV it is rendered: ferry, plain (from the margin).
H5680: Patronymic from עֵ֫בֶר; an Eberite (i.e. Hebrew) or descendant of Eber. In the KJV it is rendered: Hebrew(-ess, woman).
H5681: The same as עִבְרִי; Ibri, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ibri.
H5682: Plural of עֵ֫בֶר; regions beyond; Abarim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Abarim, passages.
H5683: From עֵ֫בֶר; transitional; Ebron, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Hebron.
H5684: Feminine of עֶבְרֹן; Ebronah, place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Ebronah.
H5685: A primitive root; to dry up. In the KJV it is rendered: be rotten.
H5686: A primitive root; to interlace, i.e. (figuratively) to pervert. In the KJV it is rendered: wrap up.
H5687: Or rabowth; from עָבַת; intwined, i.e. dense. In the KJV it is rendered: thick.
H5688: Or rabowth; or (feminine) tabothah; the same as עָבֹת; something intwined, i.e. a string, wreath or foliage. In the KJV it is rendered: band, cord, rope, thick bough (branch), wreathen (chain).
H5689: A primitive root; to breathe after, i.e. to love (sensually). In the KJV it is rendered: dote, lover.
H5690: From עָגַב; love (concretely), i.e. amative words. In the KJV it is rendered: much love, very lovely.
H5691: From עָגַב; love (abstractly), i.e. amorousness. In the KJV it is rendered: inordinate love.
H5692: From עוּג; an ash-cake (as round). In the KJV it is rendered: cake (upon the hearth).
H5693: Passive part (but with active sense) of an unused root meaning to twitter: probably the swallow. In the KJV it is rendered: swallow.
H5694: From the same as עָגֹל; something round, i.e. a ring (for the ears). In the KJV it is rendered: earring.
H5695: From the same as עָגֹל; a (male) calf (as frisking round), especially one nearly grown (i.e. a steer). In the KJV it is rendered: bullock, calf.
H5696: Or magowl; from an unused root meaning to revolve, circular. In the KJV it is rendered: round.
H5697: Feminine of עֵ֫גֶל; a (female) calf, especially one nearly grown (i.e. a heifer). In the KJV it is rendered: calf, cow, heifer.
H5698: The same as עֶגְלָה; Eglah, a wife of David. In the KJV it is rendered: Eglah.
H5699: From the same as עָגֹל; something revolving, i.e. a wheeled vehicle:--cart, chariot, wagon.
H5700: From עֵ֫גֶל; vituline; Eglon, the name of a place in Palestine and of a Moabitish king. In the KJV it is rendered: Eglon.
H5701: A primitive root; to be sad. In the KJV it is rendered: grieve.
H5702: A primitive root; to debar, i.e. from marriage. In the KJV it is rendered: stay.
H5703: From עָדָה; properly, a (peremptory) terminus, i.e. (by implication) duration, in the sense of advance or perpetuity (substantially as a noun, either with or without a preposition). In the KJV it is rendered: eternity, ever(- lasting, -more), old, perpetually, + world without end.
H5704: Properly, the same as עַד (used as a preposition, adverb or conjunction; especially with a preposition); as far (or long, or much) as, whether of space (even unto) or time (during, while, until) or degree (equally with). In the KJV it is rendered: against, and, as, at, before, by (that), even (to), for(-asmuch as), (hither-)to, + how long, into, as long (much) as, (so) that, till, toward, until, when, while, (+ as) yet.
H5705: (Aramaic) corresponding to עַד; X and, at, for, (hither-)to, on till, (un-)to, until, within.
H5706: The same as עַד in the sense of the aim of an attack; booty. In the KJV it is rendered: prey.
H5707: Contracted from עוּד; concretely, a witness; abstractly, testimony; specifically, a recorder, i.e. prince. In the KJV it is rendered: witness.
H5708: From an unused root meaning to set a period (compare עָדָה, עוּד); the menstrual flux (as periodical); by implication (in plural) soiling. In the KJV it is rendered: filthy.
H5709: (Aramaic) or adah (Aramaic); corresponding to עָדָה. In the KJV it is rendered: alter, depart, pass (away), remove, take (away).
H5710: A primitive root; to advance, i.e. pass on or continue; causatively, to remove; specifically, to bedeck (i.e. bring an ornament upon). In the KJV it is rendered: adorn, deck (self), pass by, take away.
H5711: From עָדָה; ornament; Adah, the name of two women. In the KJV it is rendered: Adah.
H5712: Feminine of עֵד in the original sense of fixture; a stated assemblage (specifically, a concourse, or generally, a family or crowd). In the KJV it is rendered: assembly, company, congregation, multitude, people, swarm.
H5713: Feminine of עֵד in its techn. sense; testimony. In the KJV it is rendered: testimony, witness.
H5714: Or Iddowo; or Iddiy; from עָדָה; timely; Iddo (or Iddi), the name of five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Iddo.
H5715: Feminine of עֵד; testimony. In the KJV it is rendered: testimony, witness.
H5716: From עָדָה in the sense of trappings; finery; generally an outfit; specifically, a headstall. In the KJV it is rendered: X excellent, mouth, ornament.
H5717: From עֶ֫דִי and אֵל; ornament of God; Adiel, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Adiel.
H5718: Or Adayahuw; from עָדָה and יָהּ; Jah has adorned; Adajah, the name of eight Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Adaiah.
H5719: From עָדַן; voluptuous. In the KJV it is rendered: given to pleasures.
H5720: The same as עֲדִינָה; Adin, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Adin.
H5721: From עֲדִינָה; effeminacy; Adina, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Adina.
H5722: Probably from עֲדִינָה in the original sense of slender (i.e. a spear); his spear. In the KJV it is rendered: Adino.
H5723: Dual of a feminine of עַד; double prey; Adithajim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Adithaim.
H5724: Probably from an unused root of uncertain meaning; Adlai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Adlai.
H5725: Probably from the passive participle of the same as עַדְלָי; Adullam, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Adullam.
H5726: Patrial from עֲדֻלָּם; an Adullamite or native of Adullam. In the KJV it is rendered: Adullamite.
H5727: A primitive root; to be soft or pleasant; figuratively and reflexively, to live voluptuously. In the KJV it is rendered: delight self.
H5728: Or radennah; from עַד and הֵן; till now. In the KJV it is rendered: yet.
H5729: From עָדַן; pleasure; Eden, a place in Mesopotamia. In the KJV it is rendered: Eden.
H5730: Or (feminine) aednah; from עָדַן; pleasure. In the KJV it is rendered: delicate, delight, pleasure.
H5731: The same as עֲדָנִים (masculine); Eden, the region of Adam's home. In the KJV it is rendered: Eden.
H5732: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of עִדִּים; a set time; technically, a year. In the KJV it is rendered: time.
H5733: From עָדַן; pleasure; Adna, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Adna.
H5734: From עָדַן; pleasure; Adnah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Adnah.
H5735: From עֵדָה; festival; Adadah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Adadah.
H5736: A primitive root; to be (causatively, have) redundant. In the KJV it is rendered: be more, odd number, be (have) over (and above), overplus, remain.
H5737: A primitive root; to arrange, as a battle, a vineyard (to hoe); hence, to muster and so to miss (or find wanting). In the KJV it is rendered: dig, fail, keep (rank), lack.
H5738: From עָדַר; an arrangement (i.e. drove); Eder, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ader.
H5739: From עָדַר; an arrangement, i.e. muster (of animals). In the KJV it is rendered: drove, flock, herd.
H5740: The same as עֵ֫דֶר; Eder, the name of an Israelite and of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Edar, Eder.
H5741: From עֵ֫דֶר and אֵל; flock of God; Adriel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Adriel.
H5742: From an unused root of uncertain meaning; a lentil. In the KJV it is rendered: lentile.
H5743: A primitive root; to be dense or dark, i.e. to becloud. In the KJV it is rendered: cover with a cloud.
H5744: Active participle of עָבַד; serving; Obed, the name of five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Obed.
H5745: Of foreign derivation; Obal, a son of Joktan. In the KJV it is rendered: Obal.
H5746: A primitive root; properly, to gyrate; but used only as a denominative from עֻגָה, to bake (round cakes on the hearth). In the KJV it is rendered: bake.
H5747: Probably from עוּג; round; Og, a king of Bashan. In the KJV it is rendered: Og.
H5748: Or buggab; from עָגַב in the original sense of breathing; a reed-instrument of music. In the KJV it is rendered: organ.
H5749: A primitive root; to duplicate or repeat; by implication, to protest, testify (as by reiteration); intensively, to encompass, restore (as a sort of reduplication). In the KJV it is rendered: admonish, charge, earnestly, lift up, protest, call (take) to record, relieve, rob, solemnly, stand upright, testify, give warning, (bear, call to, give, take to) witness.
H5750: Or rod; from עוּד; properly, iteration or continuance; used only adverbially (with or without preposition), again, repeatedly, still, more. In the KJV it is rendered: again, X all life long, at all, besides, but, else, further(-more), henceforth, (any) longer, (any) more(-over), X once, since, (be) still, when, (good, the) while (having being), (as, because, whether, while) yet (within).
H5751: (Aramaic) corresponding to עוֹד. In the KJV it is rendered: while.
H5752: Or Oded; from עוּד; reiteration; Oded, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Oded.
H5753: A primitive root; to crook, literally or figuratively (as follows). In the KJV it is rendered: do amiss, bow down, make crooked, commit iniquity, pervert, (do) perverse(-ly), trouble, X turn, do wickedly, do wrong.
H5754: Intensive from עָוָה abbreviated; overthrow. In the KJV it is rendered: X overturn.
H5755: Or Avvae (2 Kings 17:24); for עַוָּה; Ivvah or Avva, a region of Assyria. In the KJV it is rendered: Ava, Ivah.
H5756: A primitive root; to be strong; causatively, to stregthen, i.e. (figuratively) to save (by flight). In the KJV it is rendered: gather (self, self to flee), retire.
H5757: Patrial from עַוָּא; an Avvite or native of Avvah (only plural). In the KJV it is rendered: Avims, Avites.
H5758: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to עָוָה; perverseness. In the KJV it is rendered: iniquity.
H5759: From עוּל; a babe. In the KJV it is rendered: young child, little one.
H5760: From עָוַל; perverse (morally). In the KJV it is rendered: ungodly.
H5761: Plural of עַוִּים; Avvim (as inhabited by Avvites), a place in Palestine (with the article prefix). In the KJV it is rendered: Avim.
H5762: Or (perhaps Ayowth, as if plural of עַי) Ayuwth; from עָוָה; ruin; Avvith (or Avvoth), a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Avith.
H5763: A primitive root; to suckle, i.e. give milk. In the KJV it is rendered: milch, (ewe great) with young.
H5764: From עוּל; a babe. In the KJV it is rendered: sucking child, infant.
H5765: A primitive root; to distort (morally). In the KJV it is rendered: deal unjustly, unrighteous.
H5766: Or lavel; and (feminine) lavlah; or owlah; or .olah; from עָוַל; (moral) evil. In the KJV it is rendered: iniquity, perverseness, unjust(-ly), unrighteousness(-ly); wicked(-ness).
H5767: Intensive from עָוַל; evil (morally). In the KJV it is rendered: unjust, unrighteous, wicked.
H5768: Or lolal; from עוּל; a suckling. In the KJV it is rendered: babe, (young) child, infant, little one.
H5769: Or lolam; from עָלַם; properly, concealed, i.e. the vanishing point; generally, time out of mind (past or future), i.e. (practically) eternity; frequentatively, adverbial (especially with prepositional prefix) always. In the KJV it is rendered: alway(-s), ancient (time), any more, continuance, eternal, (for, (n-))ever(-lasting, -more, of old), lasting, long (time), (of) old (time), perpetual, at any time, (beginning of the) world (+ without end).
H5770: Denominative from עַ֫יִן; to watch (with jealosy). In the KJV it is rendered: eye.
H5771: Or oavown (2 Kings 7:9; Psalm 51:5 (7)); from עָוָה; perversity, i.e. (moral) evil. In the KJV it is rendered: fault, iniquity, mischeif, punishment (of iniquity), sin.
H5772: From an unused root apparently meaning to dwell together; sexual (cohabitation). In the KJV it is rendered: duty of marriage.
H5773: From עָוָה; perversity. In the KJV it is rendered: X perverse.
H5774: A primitive root; to cover (with wings or obscurity); hence (as denominative from עוֹף) to fly; also (by implication of dimness) to faint (from the darkness of swooning). In the KJV it is rendered: brandish, be (wax) faint, flee away, fly (away), X set, shine forth, weary.
H5775: From עוּף; a bird (as covered with feathers, or rather as covering with wings), often collectively. In the KJV it is rendered: bird, that flieth, flying, fowl.
H5776: (Aramaic) corresponding to עוֹף. In the KJV it is rendered: fowl.
H5777: Or mophereth; feminine participle active of עָפַר; lead (from its dusty color). In the KJV it is rendered: lead.
H5778: From עוֹף; birdlike; Ephai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ephai (from margin).
H5779: A primitive root; to consult. In the KJV it is rendered: take advice ((counsel) together).
H5780: Apparently from עוּץ; consultation; Uts, a son of Aram, also a Seirite, and the regions settled by them. In the KJV it is rendered: Uz.
H5781: A primitive root; to pack. In the KJV it is rendered: be pressed.
H5782: A primitive root (rather identical with עוּר through the idea of opening the eyes); to wake (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: (a-)wake(-n, up), lift up (self), X master, raise (up), stir up (self).
H5783: A primitive root; to (be) bare. In the KJV it is rendered: be made naked.
H5784: (Aramaic) chaff (as the naked husk). In the KJV it is rendered: chaff.
H5785: From עוּר; skin (as naked); by implication, hide, leather. In the KJV it is rendered: hide, leather, skin.
H5786: A primitive root (rather denominatively from עוֹר through the idea of a film over the eyes); to blind. In the KJV it is rendered: blind, put out.
H5787: Intensive from עָוַר; blind (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: blind (men, people).
H5788: And (feminine) avvereth; from עִוְרוֹת; blindness. In the KJV it is rendered: blind(-ness).
H5789: A primitive root; to hasten. In the KJV it is rendered: assemble self.
H5790: For עוּשׁ; to hasten, i.e. succor. In the KJV it is rendered: speak in season.
H5791: A primitive root; to wrest. In the KJV it is rendered: bow self, (make) crooked.
H5792: From עָוַת; oppression. In the KJV it is rendered: wrong.
H5793: From עוּת; succoring; Uthai, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Uthai.
H5794: From עָזַז; strong, vehement, harsh. In the KJV it is rendered: fierce, + greedy, mighty, power, roughly, strong.
H5795: From עָזַז; a she-goat (as strong), but masculine in plural (which also is used ellipt. for goat's hair). In the KJV it is rendered: (she) goat, kid.
H5796: (Aramaic) corresponding to עֵז. In the KJV it is rendered: goat.
H5797: Or (fully) rowz; from עָזַז; strength in various applications (force, security, majesty, praise). In the KJV it is rendered: boldness, loud, might, power, strength, strong.
H5798: Or (Uzzah; feminine of עֹז; strength; Uzza or Uzzah, the name of five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Uzza, Uzzah.
H5799: From עֵז and אָזַל; goat of departure; the scapegoat. In the KJV it is rendered: scapegoat.
H5800: A primitive root; to loosen, i.e. relinquish, permit, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: commit self, fail, forsake, fortify, help, leave (destitute, off), refuse, X surely.
H5801: From עָזַב in the sense of letting go (for a price, i.e. selling); trade, i.e. the place (mart) or the payment (revenue). In the KJV it is rendered: fair, ware.
H5802: From עָז and the root of בּוּקָה; stern depopulator; Azbuk, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Azbuk.
H5803: From עָז and גָּד; stern troop; Azgad, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Azgad.
H5804: Feminine of עָז; strong; Azzah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Azzah, Gaza.
H5805: Feminine passive participle of עָזַב; desertion (of inhabitants). In the KJV it is rendered: forsaking.
H5806: The same as עֲזוּבָה; Azubah, the name of two Israelitesses. In the KJV it is rendered: Azubah.
H5807: From עָזַז; forcibleness. In the KJV it is rendered: might, strength.
H5808: From עָזַז; forcible; collectively and concretely, an army. In the KJV it is rendered: power, strong.
H5809: Or Azzur; from עָזַר; helpful; Azzur, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Azur, Azzur.
H5810: A primitive root; to be stout (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: harden, impudent, prevail, strengthen (self), be strong.
H5811: From עָזַז; strong; Azaz, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Azaz.
H5812: From עָזַז and יָהּ; Jah has strengthened; Azazjah, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Azaziah.
H5813: From עָזַז; forceful; Uzzi, the name of six Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Uzzi.
H5814: Perhaps for עֻזִּיָּה; Uzzija, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Uzzia.
H5815: From עוּז and אֵל; strengthened of God; Aziel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Aziel.
H5816: From עֹז and אֵל; strength of God; Uzziel, the name of six Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Uzziel.
H5817: Patronymically from עֻזִּיאֵל; an Uzzielite (collectively) or descendants of Uzziel. In the KJV it is rendered: Uzzielites.
H5818: Or Uzziyahuw; from עֹז and יָהּ; strength of Jah; Uzzijah, the name of five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Uzziah.
H5819: From עוּז; strengthfulness; Aziza, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Aziza.
H5820: From עָז and מָ֫וֶת; strong one of death; Azmaveth, the name of three Israelites and of a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Azmaveth.
H5821: From עָז; strong one; Azzan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Azzan.
H5822: Probably feminine of עֹז; probably the sea-eagle (from its strength). In the KJV it is rendered: ospray.
H5823: A primitive root; to grub over. In the KJV it is rendered: fence about.
H5824: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to עָזַק; a signet-ring (as engraved). In the KJV it is rendered: signet.
H5825: From עָזַק; tilled; Azekah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Azekah.
H5826: A primitive root; to surround, i.e. protect or aid. In the KJV it is rendered: help, succour.
H5827: From עָזַר; help; Ezer, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ezer.
H5828: From עָזַר; aid. In the KJV it is rendered: help.
H5829: The same as עֵ֫זֶר; Ezer, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ezer.
H5830: A variation of עֶזְרָה; Ezra, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ezra.
H5831: (Aramaic) corresponding to עֶזְרָא; Ezra, an Israelite --Ezra.
H5832: From עָזַר and אֵל; God has helped; Azarel, the name of five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Azarael, Azareel.
H5833: Or mezrath (Psa. 60:11 (13); 108:12 (13)); feminine of עֵ֫זֶר; aid. In the KJV it is rendered: help(-ed, -er).
H5834: The same as עֶזְרָה; Ezrah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ezrah.
H5835: From עָזַר in its original meaning of surrounding; an inclosure; also a border. In the KJV it is rendered: court, settle.
H5836: From עֵ֫זֶר; helpful; Ezri, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ezri.
H5837: From עֵ֫זֶר and אֵל; help of God; Azriel, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Azriel.
H5838: Or Azaryahuw; from עָזַר and יָהּ; Jah has helped; Azarjah, the name of nineteen Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Azariah.
H5839: (Aramaic) corresponding to עֲזַרְיָה; Azarjah, one of Daniel's companions. In the KJV it is rendered: Azariah.
H5840: From עֵ֫זֶר and active participle of קוּם; help of an enemy; Azrikam, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Azrikam.
H5841: Patrial from עַזָּה; an Azzathite or inhabitant of Azzah. In the KJV it is rendered: Gazathite, Gazite.
H5842: From עִיט (contracted) in the sense of swooping, i.e. side-long stroke; a stylus or marking stick. In the KJV it is rendered: pen.
H5843: (Aramaic) from יְעַט; prudence. In the KJV it is rendered: counsel.
H5844: A primitive root; to wrap, i.e. cover, veil, cloth, or roll. In the KJV it is rendered: array self, be clad, (put a) cover (-ing, self), fill, put on, X surely, turn aside.
H5845: From an unused root meaning apparently to contain; a receptacle (for milk, i.e. pail; figuratively, breast). In the KJV it is rendered: breast.
H5846: From an unused root meaning to sneeze; sneezing. In the KJV it is rendered: sneezing.
H5847: Of uncertain derivation; a bat. In the KJV it is rendered: bat.
H5848: A primitive root; to shroud, i.e. clothe (whether transitive or reflex.); hence (from the idea of darkness) to languish. In the KJV it is rendered: cover (over), fail, faint, feebler, hide self, be overwhelmed, swoon.
H5849: A primitive root; to encircle (for attack or protection); especially to crown (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: compass, crown.
H5850: From עָטַר; a crown. In the KJV it is rendered: crown.
H5851: The same as עֲטָרָה; Atarah, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Atarah.
H5852: Or Ataroth; plural of עֲטָרָה; Ataroth, the name (thus simply) of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ataroth.
H5853: From the same as עֲטָרוֹת and אַדָּר; crowns of Addar; Atroth-Addar, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ataroth-adar(-addar).
H5854: From the same as עֲטָרוֹת and בָּ֫יִת and יוֹאָב; crowns of the house of Joab; Atroth-beth-Joab, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ataroth the house of Joab.
H5855: From the same as עֲטָרוֹת and a name otherwise unused (being from the same as שָׂפַן) meaning hidden; crowns of Shophan; Atroth-Shophan, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Atroth, Shophan (as if two places).
H5856: From עָוָה; a ruin (as if overturned). In the KJV it is rendered: heap.
H5857: Or (feminine) Aya( (Neh. 11:31); or Ayath (Isaiah 10:28); for עִי; Ai, Aja or Ajath, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ai, Aija, Aijath, Hai.
H5858: Perhaps from an unused root probably meaning to be bald; bare; Ebal, a mountain of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ebal.
H5859: From עִי; ruin; Ijon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ijon.
H5860: A primitive root; to swoop down upon (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: fly, rail.
H5861: From עִיט; a hawk or other bird of prey. In the KJV it is rendered: bird, fowl, ravenous (bird).
H5862: From עָ֫יִט; hawk-ground; Etam, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Etam.
H5863: From the plural of עִי and the plural of the active participle of עָבַר with the article interposed; ruins of the passers; Ije-ha-Abarim, a place near Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ije-abarim.
H5864: Plural of עִי; ruins; Ijim, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Iim.
H5865: For עוֹלָם. In the KJV it is rendered: ever.
H5866: From עָלָה; elevated; Ilai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ilai.
H5867: Or Owlam (Ezra 10:2; Jeremiah 49:36); probably from עָלַם; hidden, i.e. distant; Elam, a son of Shem and his descendants, with their country; also of six Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Elam.
H5868: Of doubtful origin and authenticity; probably meaning strength. In the KJV it is rendered: mighty.
H5869: Probably a primitive word; an eye (literally or figuratively); by analogy, a fountain (as the eye of the landscape). In the KJV it is rendered: affliction, outward appearance, + before, + think best, colour, conceit, + be content, countenance, + displease, eye((-brow), (-d), -sight), face, + favour, fountain, furrow (from the margin), X him, + humble, knowledge, look, (+ well), X me, open(-ly), + (not) please, presence, + regard, resemblance, sight, X thee, X them, + think, X us, well, X you(-rselves).
H5870: (Aramaic) corresponding to עַ֫יִן; an eye. In the KJV it is rendered: eye.
H5871: The same as עַ֫יִן; fountain; Ajin, the name (thus simply) of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ain.
H5872: From עַ֫יִן and גֶּ֫דִי; fountain of a kid; En-Gedi, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: En-gedi.
H5873: From עַ֫יִן and the plural of גָּן; fountain of gardens; En-Gannim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: En-gannim.
H5874: Or Eyn-Dor; from עַ֫יִן and דּוֹר; fountain of dwelling; En-Dor, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: En-dor.
H5875: From עַ֫יִן and the active participle of קָרָא; fountain of One calling; En-hak-Kore, a place near Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: En-hakhore.
H5876: From עַ֫יִן and the feminine of a derivative from חָדַד; fountain of sharpness; En-Chaddah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: En-haddah.
H5877: From עַ֫יִן and the same as חָצוֹר; fountain of a village; En-Chatsor, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: En-hazor.
H5878: From עַ֫יִן and a derivative of חָרַד; fountain of trembling; En-Charod, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: well of Harod.
H5879: Or Eynam; dual of עַ֫יִן; double fountain; Enajim or Enam, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Enaim, openly (Genesis 38:21).
H5880: From עַ֫יִן and מִשְׁפָּט; fountain of judgment; En-Mishpat, a place near Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: En-mishpat.
H5881: From עַ֫יִן; having eyes; Enan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Enan.
H5882: עַ֫יִן and the dual of עֵ֫גֶל; fountain of two calves; En-Eglajim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: En-eglaim.
H5883: From עַ֫יִן and the active participle of רָגַל; fountain of a traveller; En-Rogel, a place near Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: En-rogel.
H5884: From עַ֫יִן and רִמּוֹן; fountain of a pomegranate; En-Rimmon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: En-rimmon.
H5885: From עַ֫יִן and שָׁ֫מֶשׁ; fountain of the sun; En-Shemesh, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: En-shemesh.
H5886: From עַ֫יִן and the plural of תַּנִּים; fountain of jackals; En-Tannim, a pool near Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: dragon well.
H5887: From עַ֫יִן and תַּפּ֫וּחַ; fountain of an apple-tree; En-Tappuach, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: En-tappuah.
H5888: A primitive root; to languish. In the KJV it is rendered: be wearied.
H5889: From עִיף; languid. In the KJV it is rendered: faint, thirsty, weary.
H5890: Feminine from עוּף; obscurity (as if from covering). In the KJV it is rendered: darkness.
H5891: The same as עֵיפָה; Ephah, the name of a son of Midian, and of the region settled by him; also of an Israelite and of an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Ephah.
H5892: Or (in the plural) par; or ayar (Judges 10:4); from עוּר a city (a place guarded by waking or a watch) in the widest sense (even of a mere encampment or post). In the KJV it is rendered: Ai (from margin), city, court (from margin), town.
H5893: The same as עִיר; Ir, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ir.
H5894: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to עוּר; a watcher, i.e. an angel (as guardian). In the KJV it is rendered: watcher.
H5895: From עוּר in the sense of raising (i.e. bearing a burden); properly, a young ass (as just broken to a load); hence an ass-colt. In the KJV it is rendered: (ass) colt, foal, young ass.
H5896: From עוּר; wakefulness; Ira, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ira.
H5897: From the same as עֲרָד; fugitive; Irad, an antediluvian. In the KJV it is rendered: Irad.
H5898: From עִיר and מֶ֫לַח with the article of substance interp.; city of (the) salt; Ir-ham-Melach, a place near Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: the city of salt.
H5899: From עִיר and the plural of תָּמָר with the article interpolated; city of the palmtrees; Ir-hat-Temarim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: the city of palmtrees.
H5900: From עִיר; a citizen; Iru, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Iru.
H5901: From עִיר; urbane; Iri, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Iri.
H5902: From עִיר; city-wise; Iram, an Idumaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Iram.
H5903: Or merom; from עָרֹם; nudity. In the KJV it is rendered: naked(- ness).
H5904: From עִיר and נָחָשׁ; city of a serpent; Ir-Nachash, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ir-nahash.
H5905: From עִיר and שָׁ֫מֶשׁ; city of the sun; Ir-Shemesh, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ir-shemesh.
H5906: Or Ash; from עוּשׁ; the constellation of the Great Bear (perhaps from its migration through the heavens). In the KJV it is rendered: Arcturus.
H5907: Probably for עַכְבָּר; Akbor, the name of an Idumaean and of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Achbor.
H5908: Probably from an unused root in the literal sense of entangling; a spider (as weaving a network). In the KJV it is rendered: spider.
H5909: Probably from the same as עַכָּבִישׁ in the secondary sense of attacking; a mouse (as nibbling). In the KJV it is rendered: mouse.
H5910: Apparently from an unused root meaning to hem in; Akko (from its situation on a bay). In the KJV it is rendered: Accho.
H5911: From עָכַר; troubled; Akor, the name of a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Achor.
H5912: From an unused root meaning to trouble; troublesome; Akan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Achan.
H5913: A primitive root; properly, to tie, specifically, with fetters; but used only as denominative from עֲכָסִים; to put on anklets. In the KJV it is rendered: make a tinkling ornament.
H5914: From עָכַס; a fetter; hence, an anklet. In the KJV it is rendered: stocks, tinkling ornament.
H5915: Feminine of עֲכָסִים; anklet; Aksah, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Achsah.
H5916: A primitive root; properly, to roil water; figuratively, to disturb or affict. In the KJV it is rendered: trouble, stir.
H5917: From עָכַר; troublesome; Akar, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Achar.
H5918: From עָכַר; muddler; Okran, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ocran.
H5919: Probably from an unused root meaning to coil; an asp (from lurking coiled up). In the KJV it is rendered: adder.
H5920: From עָלָה; properly, the top; specifically, the highest (i.e. God); also (adverb) aloft, to Jehovah. In the KJV it is rendered: above, high, most High.
H5921: Properly, the same as עָל used as a preposition (in the singular or plural often with prefix, or as conjunction with a particle following); above, over, upon, or against (yet always in this last relation with a downward aspect) in a great variety of applications (as follow). In the KJV it is rendered: above, according to(-ly), after, (as) against, among, and, X as, at, because of, beside (the rest of), between, beyond the time, X both and, by (reason of), X had the charge of, concerning for, in (that), (forth, out) of, (from) (off), (up-)on, over, than, through(-out), to, touching, X with.
H5922: (Aramaic) corresponding to עַל. In the KJV it is rendered: about, against, concerning, for, (there-)fore, from, in, X more, of, (there-, up-)on, (in-)to, + why with.
H5923: Or mowl; from עָלַל; a yoke (as imposed on the neck), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: yoke.
H5924: (Aramaic) from עַל; above. In the KJV it is rendered: over.
H5925: Feminine of עֹל; burden; Ulla, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ulla.
H5926: From an unused root meaning to stutter; stuttering. In the KJV it is rendered: stammerer.
H5927: A primitive root; to ascend, intransitively (be high) or actively (mount); used in a great variety of senses, primary and secondary, literal and figurative (as follow). In the KJV it is rendered: arise (up), (cause to) ascend up, at once, break (the day) (up), bring (up), (cause to) burn, carry up, cast up, + shew, climb (up), (cause to, make to) come (up), cut off, dawn, depart, exalt, excel, fall, fetch up, get up, (make to) go (away, up); grow (over) increase, lay, leap, levy, lift (self) up, light, (make) up, X mention, mount up, offer, make to pay, + perfect, prefer, put (on), raise, recover, restore, (make to) rise (up), scale, set (up), shoot forth (up), (begin to) spring (up), stir up, take away (up), work.
H5928: (Aramaic) corresponding to עֹלָה; a holocaust. In the KJV it is rendered: burnt offering.
H5929: From עָלָה; a leaf (as coming up on a tree); collectively, foliage. In the KJV it is rendered: branch, leaf.
H5930: Or mowlah; feminine active participle of עָלָה; a step or (collectively, stairs, as ascending); usually a holocaust (as going up in smoke). In the KJV it is rendered: ascent, burnt offering (sacrifice), go up to.
H5931: (Aramaic) feminine from a root corresponding to עָלָה; a pretext (as arising artificially). In the KJV it is rendered: occasion.
H5932: For עָ֫וֶל; moral perverseness. In the KJV it is rendered: iniquity.
H5933: Or Alyah; the same as עַלְוָה; Alvah or Aljah, an Idumaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Aliah, Alvah.
H5934: Passive participle of עָלַם in the denominative sense of עָ֫לֶם; (only in plural as abstract) adolescence; figuratively, vigor. In the KJV it is rendered: youth.
H5935: Or Alyan; from עָלָה; lofty; Alvan or Aljan, an Idumaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Alian, Alvan.
H5936: Feminine passive participle of an unused root meaning to suck; the leech. In the KJV it is rendered: horse-leech.
H5937: A primitive root; to jump for joy, i.e. exult. In the KJV it is rendered: be joyful, rejoice, triumph.
H5938: From עָלַז; exultant. In the KJV it is rendered: that rejoiceth.
H5939: Feminine from an unused root meaning to cover; dusk. In the KJV it is rendered: dark, twilight.
H5940: From עָלָה; a pestle (as lifted). In the KJV it is rendered: pestle.
H5941: From עָלָה; lofty; Eli, an Israelite high-priest. In the KJV it is rendered: Eli.
H5942: From עָלָה; high; i.e. comparative. In the KJV it is rendered: upper.
H5943: (Aramaic) corresponding to עִלִּית; supreme (i.e. God). In the KJV it is rendered: (most) high.
H5944: Feminine from עָלָה; something lofty, i.e. a stair-way; also a second-story room (or even one on the roof); figuratively, the sky. In the KJV it is rendered: ascent, (upper) chamber, going up, loft, parlour.
H5945: From עָלָה; an elevation, i.e. (adj.) lofty (compar.); as title, the Supreme. In the KJV it is rendered: (Most, on) high(-er, -est), upper(-most).
H5946: (Aramaic) corresponding to עֶלְיוֹן; the Supreme. In the KJV it is rendered: Most high.
H5948: From עָלַל in the sense of completing; probably a crucible (as working over the metal). In the KJV it is rendered: furnace.
H5949: Or malilah; from עָלַל in the sense of effecting; an exploit (of God), or a performance (of man, often in a bad sense); by implication, an opportunity. In the KJV it is rendered: act(-ion), deed, doing, invention, occasion, work.
H5950: For עֲלִילָה; (miraculous) execution. In the KJV it is rendered: work.
H5951: From עָלַץ; exultation. In the KJV it is rendered: rejoicing.
H5952: From עָלָה; a second-story room. In the KJV it is rendered: chamber.
H5953: A primitive root; to effect thoroughly; specifically, to glean (also figuratively); by implication (in a bad sense) to overdo, i.e. maltreat, be saucy to, pain, impose (also literal). In the KJV it is rendered: abuse, affect, X child, defile, do, glean, mock, practise, thoroughly, work (wonderfully).
H5954: (Aramaic) corresponding to עָלַל (in the sense of thrusting oneself in), to enter; causatively, to introduce. In the KJV it is rendered: bring in, come in, go in.
H5955: Feminine active participle of עָלַל; only in plural gleanings; by extens. gleaning-time. In the KJV it is rendered: (gleaning) (of the) grapes, grapegleanings.
H5956: A primitive root; to veil from sight, i.e. conceal (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: X any ways, blind, dissembler, hide (self), secret (thing).
H5957: (Aramaic) corresponding to עוֹלָם; remote time, i.e. the future or past indefinitely; often adverb, forever. In the KJV it is rendered: for ((n-))ever (lasting), old.
H5958: From עָלַם; properly, something kept out of sight (compare עַלְמָה), i.e. a lad. In the KJV it is rendered: young man, stripling.
H5959: Feminine of עָ֫לֶם; a lass (as veiled or private). In the KJV it is rendered: damsel, maid, virgin.
H5960: From עָלַם; hidden; Almon, a place in Palestine See also עַלְמֹן דִּבְלָתָ֫יְמָה.
H5961: Plural of עַלְמָה; properly, girls, i.e. the soprano or female voice, perhaps falsetto. In the KJV it is rendered: Alamoth.
H5962: (Aramaic) patrial from a name corresponding to עֵילָם contracted; an Elamite or inhabitant of Elam. In the KJV it is rendered: Elamite.
H5963: From the same as עַלְמוֹן and the dual of דְּבֵלִים (compare בֵּית דִּבְלָתַ֫יִם) with enclitic of direction; Almon towards Diblathajim; Almon-Diblathajemah, a place in Moab. In the KJV it is rendered: Almon-dilathaim.
H5964: From עָלַם; a covering; Alemeth, the name of a place in Palestine and of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Alameth, Alemeth.
H5965: A primitive root; to leap for joy, i.e. exult, wave joyously. In the KJV it is rendered: X peacock, rejoice, solace self.
H5966: A prim root; to sip up. In the KJV it is rendered: suck up.
H5967: (Aramaic) corresponding to צְלָעֹת; a rib. In the KJV it is rendered: rib.
H5968: A primitive root; to veil or cover; figuratively, to be languid. In the KJV it is rendered: faint, overlaid, wrap self.
H5969: From עָלַף; an envelope, i.e. (figuratively) mourning. In the KJV it is rendered: fainted.
H5970: A primitive root; to jump for joy, i.e. exult. In the KJV it is rendered: be joyful, rejoice, triumph.
H5971: From עָמַם; a people (as a congregated unit); specifically, a tribe (as those of Israel); hence (collectively) troops or attendants; figuratively, a flock. In the KJV it is rendered: folk, men, nation, people.
H5972: (Aramaic) corresponding to עָם. In the KJV it is rendered: people.
H5973: From עָמַם; adverb or preposition, with (i.e. in conjunction with), in varied applications; specifically, equally with; often with prepositional prefix (and then usually unrepresented in English). In the KJV it is rendered: accompanying, against, and, as (X long as), before, beside, by (reason of), for all, from (among, between), in, like, more than, of, (un-)to, with(-al).
H5974: (Aramaic) corresponding to עִם. In the KJV it is rendered: by, from, like, to(-ward), with.
H5975: A primitive root; to stand, in various relations (literal and figurative, intransitive and transitive). In the KJV it is rendered: abide (behind), appoint, arise, cease, confirm, continue, dwell, be employed, endure, establish, leave, make, ordain, be (over), place, (be) present (self), raise up, remain, repair, + serve, set (forth, over, -tle, up), (make to, make to be at a, with-)stand (by, fast, firm, still, up), (be at a) stay (up), tarry.
H5976: For מָעַד; to shake. In the KJV it is rendered: be at a stand.
H5977: From עָמַד; a spot (as being fixed). In the KJV it is rendered: place, (+ where) stood, upright.
H5978: Prol. for עִם; along with. In the KJV it is rendered: against, by, from, + me, + mine, of, + that I take, unto, upon, with(-in.
H5979: From עָמַד; a station, i.e. domicile. In the KJV it is rendered: standing.
H5980: From עָמַם; conjunction, i.e. society; mostly adverb or preposition (with prepositional prefix), near, beside, along with. In the KJV it is rendered: (over) against, at, beside, hard by, in points.
H5981: The same as עֻמַּת; association; Ummah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ummah.
H5982: Or ammud; from עָמַד; a column (as standing); also a stand, i.e. platform. In the KJV it is rendered: X apiece, pillar.
H5983: From עָם; tribal, i.e. inbred; Ammon, a son of Lot; also his posterity and their country. In the KJV it is rendered: Ammon, Ammonites.
H5984: Patronymically from עַמּוֹן; an Ammonite or (the adjective) Ammonitish. In the KJV it is rendered: Ammonite(-s).
H5985: Feminine of עַמּוֹנִי; an Ammonitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Ammonite(-ss).
H5986: From עָמַס; burdensome; Amos, an Israelite prophet. In the KJV it is rendered: Amos.
H5987: From עָמַק; deep; Amok, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Amok.
H5988: From עָם and אֵל; people of God; Ammiel, the name of three or four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ammiel.
H5989: From עָם and הוֹד; people of splendor; Ammihud, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Ammihud.
H5990: From עָם and זָבַד; people of endowment; Ammizabad, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ammizabad.
H5991: From עָם and חוּר; people of nobility; Ammichur, a Syrian prince. In the KJV it is rendered: Ammihud (from the margin).
H5992: From עָם and נָדַב; people of liberality; Amminadab, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Amminadab.
H5993: From עָם and נָדִיב; my people (is) liberal; Ammi-Nadib, probably an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Amminadib.
H5994: (Aramaic) corresponding to עִמְקֵי; profound, i.e. unsearchable, deep.
H5995: From עָמַר; a bunch of grain. In the KJV it is rendered: handful, sheaf.
H5996: From עָם and שַׁדָּי; people of (the) Almighty; Ammishaddai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ammishaddai.
H5997: From a primitive root meaning to associate; companionship; hence (concretely) a comrade or kindred man. In the KJV it is rendered: another, fellow, neighbour.
H5998: A primitive root; to toil, i.e. work severely and with irksomeness. In the KJV it is rendered: (take) labour (in).
H5999: From עָמַל; toil, i.e. wearing effort; hence, worry, wheth. of body or mind. In the KJV it is rendered: grievance(-vousness), iniquity, labour, mischief, miserable(-sery), pain(-ful), perverseness, sorrow, toil, travail, trouble, wearisome, wickedness.
H6000: The same as עָמָל; Amal, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Amal.
H6001: From עָמַל; toiling; concretely, a laborer; figuratively, sorrowful. In the KJV it is rendered: that laboureth, that is a misery, had taken (labour), wicked, workman.
H6002: Probably of foreign origin; Amalek, a descendant of Esau; also his posterity and their country. In the KJV it is rendered: Amalek.
H6003: Patronymically from עֲמָלֵק; an Amalekite (or collectively the Amalekites) or descendants of Amalek. In the KJV it is rendered: Amalekite(-s).
H6004: A primitive root; to associate; by implication, to overshadow (by huddling together). In the KJV it is rendered: become dim, hide.
H6005: From עִם and אֵל with a pronominal suffix inserted; with us (is) God; Immanuel, a type name of Isaiah's son. In the KJV it is rendered: Immanuel.
H6006: Or mamas; a primitive root; to load, i.e. impose a burden (or figuratively, infliction). In the KJV it is rendered: be borne, (heavy) burden (self), lade, load, put.
H6007: From עָמַס and יָהּ; Jah has loaded; Amasjah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Amasiah.
H6008: From עָם and עַד; people of time; Amad, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Amad.
H6009: A primitive root; to be (causatively, make) deep (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: (be, have, make, seek) deep(-ly), depth, be profound.
H6010: From עָמַק; a vale (i.e. broad depression). In the KJV it is rendered: dale, vale, valley (often used as a part of proper names).
H6011: From עָמַק; depth. In the KJV it is rendered: depth.
H6012: From עָמַק; deep (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: deeper, depth, strange.
H6013: From עָמַק; deep (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: (X exceeding) deep (thing).
H6014: A primitive root; properly, apparently to heap; figuratively, to chastise (as if piling blows); specifically (as denominative from עֹ֫מֶר) to gather grain. In the KJV it is rendered: bind sheaves, make merchandise of.
H6015: (Aramaic) corresponding to צָ֫מֶר; wool. In the KJV it is rendered: wool.
H6016: From עָמַר; properly, a heap, i.e. a sheaf; also an omer, as a dry measure. In the KJV it is rendered: omer, sheaf.
H6017: From עָמַר; a (ruined) heap; Amorah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Gomorrah.
H6018: From עָמַר; heaping; Omri, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Omri.
H6019: Probably from עָם and רוּם; high people; Amram, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Amram.
H6020: From עַמְרָם; an Amramite or descendant of Amram. In the KJV it is rendered: Amramite.
H6021: From עָמַס; burden; Amasa, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Amasa.
H6022: From עָמַס; burdensome; Amasai, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Amasai.
H6023: Probably from עָמַס; burdensome; Amashsay, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Amashai.
H6024: From the same as עֲנָבִים; fruit; Anab, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Anab.
H6025: From an unused root probably meaning to bear fruit; a grape. In the KJV it is rendered: (ripe) grape, wine.
H6026: A primitive root; to be soft or pliable, i.e. (figuratively) effeminate or luxurious. In the KJV it is rendered: delicate(-ness), (have) delight (self), sport self.
H6027: From עָנַג; luxury. In the KJV it is rendered: delight, pleasant.
H6028: From עָנַג; luxurious. In the KJV it is rendered: delicate.
H6029: A primitive root; to lace fast. In the KJV it is rendered: bind, tie.
H6030: A primitive root; properly, to eye or (generally) to heed, i.e. pay attention; by implication, to respond; by extens. to begin to speak; specifically to sing, shout, testify, announce. In the KJV it is rendered: give account, afflict (by mistake for `anah), (cause to, give) answer, bring low (by mistake for `anah), cry, hear, Leannoth, lift up, say, X scholar, (give a) shout, sing (together by course), speak, testify, utter, (bear) witness.
H6031: A primitive root (possibly rather ident. with עָנָה through the idea of looking down or browbeating); to depress literally or figuratively, transitive or intransitive (in various applications, as follows). In the KJV it is rendered: abase self, afflict(-ion, self), answer (by mistake for `anah), chasten self, deal hardly with, defile, exercise, force, gentleness, humble (self), hurt, ravish, sing (by mistake for `anah), speak (by mistake for `anah), submit self, weaken, X in any wise.
H6032: (Aramaic) corresponding to עָנָה. In the KJV it is rendered: answer, speak.
H6033: (Aramaic) corresponding to עָנָה. In the KJV it is rendered: poor.
H6034: Probably from עָנָה; an answer; Anah, the name of two Edomites and one Edomitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Anah.
H6035: Or (by intermixture with עָנִי) Aanayv; from עָנָה; depressed (figuratively), in mind (gentle) or circumstances (needy, especially saintly). In the KJV it is rendered: humble, lowly, meek, poor.
H6036: Passive participle from the same as עֲנָבִים; borne (as fruit); Anub, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Anub.
H6037: Feminine of עָנָו; mildness (royal); also (concretely) oppressed. In the KJV it is rendered: gentleness, meekness.
H6038: From עָנָו; condescension, human and subjective (modesty), or divine and objective (clemency). In the KJV it is rendered: gentleness, humility, meekness.
H6039: From עָנָה; affliction. In the KJV it is rendered: affliction.
H6040: From עָנָה; depression, i.e. misery. In the KJV it is rendered: afflicted(-ion), trouble.
H6041: From עָנָה; depressed, in mind or circumstances (practically the same as עָנָו, although the margin constantly disputes this, making עָנָו subjective and עָנִי objective). In the KJV it is rendered: afflicted, humble, lowly, needy, poor.
H6042: From עָנָה; afflicted; Unni, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Unni.
H6043: From עָנָה; Jah has answered; Anajah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Anaiah.
H6044: For plural of עַ֫יִן; fountains; Anim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Anim.
H6045: From עָנָה; ado, i.e. (generally) employment or (specifically) an affair. In the KJV it is rendered: business, travail.
H6046: From the dual of עַ֫יִן; two fountains; Anem, a place in Palestine: Anem.
H6047: As if plural of some Egyptian word; Anamim, a son of Mizraim and his descendants, with their country. In the KJV it is rendered: Anamim.
H6048: Of foreign origin; Anammelek, an Assyrian deity. In the KJV it is rendered: Anammelech.
H6049: A primitive root; to cover; used only as a denominative from עָנָן, to cloud over; figuratively, to act covertly, i.e. practise magic. In the KJV it is rendered: X bring, enchanter, Meonemin, observe(-r of) times, soothsayer, sorcerer.
H6050: (Aramaic) corresponding to עָנָן. In the KJV it is rendered: cloud.
H6051: From עָנַן; a cloud (as covering the sky), i.e. the nimbus or thunder-cloud. In the KJV it is rendered: cloud(-y).
H6052: The same as עָנָן; cloud; Anan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Anan.
H6053: Feminine of עָנָן; cloudiness. In the KJV it is rendered: cloud.
H6054: From עָנָן; cloudy; Anani, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Anani.
H6055: From עָנַן and יָהּ; Jah has covered; Ananjah, the name of an Israelite and of a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ananiah.
H6056: (Aramaic) or deneph (Aramaic); corresponding to עָנָף. In the KJV it is rendered: bough, branch.
H6057: From an unused root meaning to cover; a twig (as covering the limbs). In the KJV it is rendered: bough, branch.
H6058: From the same as עָנָף; branching. In the KJV it is rendered: full of branches.
H6059: A primitive root; properly, to choke; used only as denominative from עֲנָק, to collar, i.e. adorn with a necklace; figuratively, to fit out with supplies. In the KJV it is rendered: compass about as a chain, furnish, liberally.
H6060: From עָנַק; a necklace (as if strangling). In the KJV it is rendered: chain.
H6061: The same as עֲנָק; Anak, a Canaanite. In the KJV it is rendered: Anak.
H6062: Patronymically from עֲנָק; an Anakite or descendant of Anak. In the KJV it is rendered: Anakim.
H6063: Probably for נַ֫עַר; Aner, a Amorite, also a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Aner.
H6064: A primitive root; properly, to urge; by implication, to inflict a penalty, specifically, to fine. In the KJV it is rendered: amerce, condemn, punish, X surely.
H6065: (Aramaic) corresponding to עֹ֫נֶשׁ; a mulct. In the KJV it is rendered: confiscation.
H6066: From עָנַשׁ; a fine. In the KJV it is rendered: punishment, tribute.
H6067: From עָנָה; answer; Anath, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Anath.
H6068: Plural of עֲנָת; Anathoth, the name of two Israelites, also of a place in Pal. In the KJV it is rendered: Anathoth.
H6069: Or Annthowthiy; patrial from עֲנָתוֹת; a Antothite or inhabitant of Anathoth. In the KJV it is rendered: of Anathoth, Anethothite, Anetothite, Antothite.
H6070: From the same as עֲנָתוֹת and יָהּ; answers of Jah; Anthothijah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Antothijah.
H6071: From עָסַס; must or fresh grape-juice (as just trodden out). In the KJV it is rendered: juice, new (sweet) wine.
H6072: A primitive root; to squeeze out juice; figuratively, to trample. In the KJV it is rendered: tread down.
H6073: From an unused root meaning to cover; a bough (as covering the tree). In the KJV it is rendered: branch.
H6074: (Aramaic) corresponding to עֳפָאּים; a twig; bough, i.e. (collectively) foliage. In the KJV it is rendered: leaves.
H6075: A primitive root; to swell; figuratively, be elated. In the KJV it is rendered: be lifted up, presume.
H6076: From עָפַל; a tumor; also a mound, i.e. fortress. In the KJV it is rendered: emerod, fort, strong hold, tower.
H6077: The same as עֹ֫פֶל; Ophel, a ridge in Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: Ophel.
H6078: From an unused noun (denoting a place in Palestine; from an unused root of uncertain meaning); an Ophnite (collectively) or inhabitants of Ophen. In the KJV it is rendered: Ophni.
H6079: From עוּף; an eyelash (as fluttering); figuratively, morning ray. In the KJV it is rendered: dawning, eye-lid.
