H6080: : a primitive root: meaning either to be gray or perhaps rather to pulverize; used only as denominative from עָפָר, to be dust. In the KJV it is rendered: cast (dust).
H6081: Probably a variation of עֹ֫פֶר; gazelle; Epher, the name of an Arabian and of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Epher.
H6082: From עָפַר; a fawn (from the dusty color). In the KJV it is rendered: young roe (hart).
H6083: From עָפַר; dust (as powdered or gray); hence, clay, earth, mud. In the KJV it is rendered: ashes, dust, earth, ground, morter, powder, rubbish.
H6084: Feminine of עֹ֫פֶר; female fawn; Ophrah, the name of an Israelite and of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ophrah.
H6085: From the same as עֵ֫פֶר; fawn-like; Ephron, the name of a Canaanite and of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ephron, Ephrain (from the margin).
H6086: From עָצָה; a tree (from its firmness); hence, wood (plural sticks). In the KJV it is rendered: + carpenter, gallows, helve, + pine, plank, staff, stalk, stick, stock, timber, tree, wood.
H6087: A primitive root; properly, to carve, i.e. fabricate or fashion; hence (in a bad sense) to worry, pain or anger. In the KJV it is rendered: displease, grieve, hurt, make, be sorry, vex, worship, wrest.
H6088: (Aramaic) corresponding to עָצַב; to afflict. In the KJV it is rendered: lamentable.
H6089: From עָצַב; an earthen vessel; usually (painful) toil; also a pang (whether of body or mind): grievous, idol, labor, sorrow.
H6090: A variation of עֶ֫צֶב; an idol (as fashioned); also pain (bodily or mental). In the KJV it is rendered: idol, sorrow, X wicked.
H6091: From עָצַב; an (idolatrous) image. In the KJV it is rendered: idol, image.
H6092: From עָצַב; a (hired) workman. In the KJV it is rendered: labour.
H6093: From עָצַב; worrisomeness, i.e. labor or pain. In the KJV it is rendered: sorrow, toil.
H6094: From עָצַב; a idol; also, a pain or wound. In the KJV it is rendered: sorrow, wound.
H6095: A primitive root; properly, to fasten (or make firm), i.e. to close (the eyes). In the KJV it is rendered: shut.
H6096: From עָצָה; the spine (as giving firmness to the body). In the KJV it is rendered: backbone.
H6097: Feminine of עֵץ; timber. In the KJV it is rendered: trees.
H6098: From יָעַץ; advice; by implication, plan; also prudence. In the KJV it is rendered: advice, advisement, counsel(l-(or)), purpose.
H6099: Or matsum; passive participle of עָצַם; powerful (specifically, a paw); by implication, numerous. In the KJV it is rendered: + feeble, great, mighty, must, strong.
H6100: Or shorter `Etsyon, from עָצֶה and גָּ֫בֶר; backbone-like of a man; Etsjon-Geber, a place on the Red Sea. In the KJV it is rendered: Ezion-geber.
H6101: A primitive root; to lean idly, i.e. to be indolent or slack. In the KJV it is rendered: be slothful.
H6102: From עָצַל; indolent. In the KJV it is rendered: slothful, sluggard.
H6103: Feminine of עָצֵל; (as abstractly) indolence. In the KJV it is rendered: slothfulness.
H6104: Rom עָצַל; indolence. In the KJV it is rendered: idleness.
H6105: A primitive root; to bind fast, i.e. close (the eyes); intransitively, to be (causatively, make) powerful or numerous; denominatively (from עָ֫צֶם) to crunch the bones. In the KJV it is rendered: break the bones, close, be great, be increased, be (wax) mighty(-ier), be more, shut, be(-come, make) strong(-er).
H6106: From עָצַם; a bone (as strong); by extension, the body; figuratively, the substance, i.e. (as pron.) selfsame. In the KJV it is rendered: body, bone, X life, (self-)same, strength, X very.
H6107: The same as עָ֫צֶם; bone; Etsem, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Azem, Ezem.
H6108: From עָצַם; power; hence, body. In the KJV it is rendered: might, strong, substance.
H6109: Feminine of עֹ֫צֶם; powerfulness; by extension, numerousness. In the KJV it is rendered: abundance, strength.
H6110: Feminine of עָצוּם; a bulwark, i.e. (figuratively) argument. In the KJV it is rendered: strong.
H6111: Or Atsmon; from עָ֫צֶם; bone-like; Atsmon, a place near Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Azmon.
H6112: From an unused root meaning to be sharp or strong; a spear. In the KJV it is rendered: Eznite (from the margin).
H6113: A primitive root; to inclose; by analogy, to hold back; also to maintain, rule, assemble. In the KJV it is rendered: X be able, close up, detain, fast, keep (self close, still), prevail, recover, refrain, X reign, restrain, retain, shut (up), slack, stay, stop, withhold (self).
H6114: From עָצַר; restraint. In the KJV it is rendered: + magistrate.
H6115: From עָצַר; closure; also constraint. In the KJV it is rendered: X barren, oppression, X prison.
H6116: Or matsereth; from עָצַר; an assembly, especially on a festival or holiday. In the KJV it is rendered: (solemn) assembly (meeting).
H6117: A primitive root; properly, to swell out or up; used only as denominative from עִקְּבֵי, to seize by the heel; figuratively, to circumvent (as if tripping up the heels); also to restrain (as if holding by the heel). In the KJV it is rendered: take by the heel, stay, supplant, X utterly.
H6118: From עָקַב in the sense of עִקְּבֵי; a heel, i.e. (figuratively) the last of anything (used adverbially, for ever); also result, i.e. compensation; and so (adverb with preposition or relatively) on account of. In the KJV it is rendered: X because, by, end, for, if, reward.
H6119: Or (feminine) hiqqbah; from עָקַב; a heel (as protuberant); hence, a track; figuratively, the rear (of an army). In the KJV it is rendered: heel, (horse-)hoof, last, lier in wait (by mistake for `aqeb), (foot-)step.
H6120: From עָקַב in its denominative sense; a lier in wait. In the KJV it is rendered: heel (by mistake for `aqeb).
H6121: From עָקַב; in the original sense, a knoll (as swelling up); in the denominative sense (transitive) fraudulent or (intransitive) tracked. In the KJV it is rendered: crooked, deceitful, polluted.
H6122: Feminine of an unused form from עָקַב meaning a trick; trickery. In the KJV it is rendered: subtilty.
H6123: A primitive root; to tie with thongs. In the KJV it is rendered: bind.
H6124: From עָקַד; striped (with bands). In the KJV it is rendered: ring straked.
H6125: From עוּק; constraint. In the KJV it is rendered: oppression.
H6126: From עָקַב; insidious; Akkub, the name of five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Akkub.
H6127: A primitive root; to wrest. In the KJV it is rendered: wrong.
H6128: From עָקַל; winding. In the KJV it is rendered: by(-way), crooked way.
H6129: From עָקַל; tortuous. In the KJV it is rendered: crooked.
H6130: From an unused root meaning to twist; tortuous; Akan, an Idummaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Akan.
H6131: A primitive root; to pluck up (especially by the roots); specifically, to hamstring; figuratively, to exterminate. In the KJV it is rendered: dig down, hough, pluck up, root up.
H6132: (Aramaic) corresponding to עָקַר. In the KJV it is rendered: pluck up by the roots.
H6133: From עָקַר. figuratively, a transplanted person, i.e. naturalized citizen. In the KJV it is rendered: stock.
H6134: The same as עֵ֫קֶר; Eker, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Eker.
H6135: From עָקַר; sterile (as if extirpated in the generative organs). In the KJV it is rendered: (X male or female) barren (woman).
H6136: (Aramaic) from עֲקַר; a stock. In the KJV it is rendered: stump.
H6137: Of uncertain derivation; a scorpion; figuratively, a scourge or knotted whip. In the KJV it is rendered: scorpion.
H6138: From עָקַר; eradication; Ekron, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ekron.
H6139: Or Eqroniy; patrial from עֶקְרוֹן; an Ekronite or inhabitant of Ekron. In the KJV it is rendered: Ekronite.
H6140: A primitive root; to knot or distort; figuratively, to pervert (act or declare perverse). In the KJV it is rendered: make crooked, (prove, that is) perverse(-rt).
H6141: From עָקַשׁ; distorted; hence, false. In the KJV it is rendered: crooked, froward, perverse.
H6142: The same as עִקֵּשׁ; perverse; Ikkesh, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ikkesh.
H6143: From עִקֵּשׁ; perversity. In the KJV it is rendered: X froward.
H6144: The same as עִיר; a city; Ar, a place in Moab. In the KJV it is rendered: Ar.
H6145: From עוּר; a foe (as watchful for mischief). In the KJV it is rendered: enemy.
H6146: (Aramaic) corresponding to עָר. In the KJV it is rendered: enemy.
H6147: From עוּר; watchful; Er, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Er.
H6148: A primitive root; to braid, i.e. intermix; technically, to traffic (as if by barter); also or give to be security (as a kind of exchange). In the KJV it is rendered: engage, (inter-)meddle (with), mingle (self), mortgage, occupy, give pledges, be(-come, put in) surety, undertake.
H6149: A primitive root (identical with עָרַב through the idea of close association); to be agreeable. In the KJV it is rendered: be pleasant(-ing), take pleasure in, be sweet.
H6150: A primitive root (identical with עָרַב through the idea of covering with a texture); to grow dusky at sundown. In the KJV it is rendered: be darkened, (toward) evening.
H6151: (Aramaic) corresponding to עָרַב; to commingle. In the KJV it is rendered: mingle (self), mix.
H6152: Or Arab; from עָרַב in the figurative sense of sterility; Arab (i.e. Arabia), a country East of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Arabia.
H6153: From עָרַב; dusk. In the KJV it is rendered: + day, even(-ing, tide), night.
H6154: Or mereb (1 Kings 10:15), (with the article prefix); from עָרַב; the web (or transverse threads of cloth); also a mixture, (or mongrel race). In the KJV it is rendered: Arabia, mingled people, mixed (multitude), woof.
H6155: From עָרַב; a willow (from the use of osiers as wattles). In the KJV it is rendered: willow.
H6156: From עָרֵב; pleasant. In the KJV it is rendered: sweet.
H6157: From עָרַב; a mosquito (from its swarming). In the KJV it is rendered: divers sorts of flies, swarm.
H6158: Or mowreb; from עָרַב; a raven (from its dusky hue). In the KJV it is rendered: raven.
H6159: Or Owreb; the same as עֹרֵב; Oreb, the name of a Midianite and of the cliff near the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Oreb.
H6160: From עָרַב (in the sense of sterility); a desert; especially (with the article prefix) the (generally) sterile valley of the Jordan and its continuation to the Red Sea. In the KJV it is rendered: Arabah, champaign, desert, evening, heaven, plain, wilderness.
H6161: Feminine passive participle of עֲנַמֶּ֫לֶך in the sense of a bargain or exchange; something given as security, i.e. (literally) a token (of safety) or (metaphorically) a bondsman. In the KJV it is rendered: pledge, surety.
H6162: From עָרַב (in the sense of exchange); a pawn (given as security). In the KJV it is rendered: pledge.
H6163: Or Arbiy; patrial from עֲרָב; an Arabian or inhabitant of Arab (i.e. Arabia). In the KJV it is rendered: Arabian.
H6164: Patrial from בֵּית הָעֲרָבָה; an Arbathite or inhabitant of (Beth-)Arabah. In the KJV it is rendered: Arbahite.
H6165: A primitive root; to long for. In the KJV it is rendered: cry, pant.
H6166: From an unused root meaning to sequester itself; fugitive; Arad, the name of a place near Palestine, also of a Canaanite and an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Arad.
H6167: (Aramaic) corresponding to עָרוֹד; an onager. In the KJV it is rendered: wild ass.
H6168: A primitive root; to be (causatively, make) bare; hence, to empty, pour out, demolish. In the KJV it is rendered: leave destitute, discover, empty, make naked, pour (out), rase, spread self, uncover.
H6169: Feminine from עָרָה; a naked (i.e. level) plot. In the KJV it is rendered: paper reed.
H6170: Or iarugah; feminine passive participle of עָרַג; something piled up (as if (figuratively) raised by mental aspiration), i.e. a paterre. In the KJV it is rendered: bed, furrow.
H6171: From the same as עֲרָד; an onager (from his lonesome habits). In the KJV it is rendered: wild ass.
H6172: From עָרָה; nudity, literally (especially the pudenda) or figuratively (disgrace, blemish). In the KJV it is rendered: nakedness, shame, unclean(-ness).
H6173: (Aramaic) corresponding to עֶרְוָה; nakedness, i.e. (figuratively) impoverishment. In the KJV it is rendered: dishonor.
H6174: Or marom; from עָרֹם (in its original sense); nude, either partially or totally. In the KJV it is rendered: naked.
H6175: Passive participle of עָרֹם; cunning (usually in a bad sense). In the KJV it is rendered: crafty, prudent, subtil.
H6176: Or sarear; from עָרַר reduplicated; a juniper (from its nudity of situation). In the KJV it is rendered: health.
H6177: Or `Aro`er; or `Ar`owr; the same as עֲרוֹעֵר; nudity of situation; Aroer, the name of three places in or near Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Aroer.
H6178: Passive participle of עָרַץ; feared, i.e. (concretely) a horrible place or chasm. In the KJV it is rendered: cliffs.
H6179: From עוּר; watchful; Eri, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Eri.
H6180: Patronymically of עֵרִי; a Erite (collectively) or descendants of Eri. In the KJV it is rendered: Erites.
H6181: For עֶרְוָה; nudity. In the KJV it is rendered: bare, naked, X quite.
H6182: From an unused root meaning to comminute; meal. In the KJV it is rendered: dough.
H6183: From עָרַף; the sky (as dropping at the horizon). In the KJV it is rendered: heaven.
H6184: From עָרַץ; fearful, i.e. powerful or tyrannical. In the KJV it is rendered: mighty, oppressor, in great power, strong, terrible, violent.
H6185: From עָרַר; bare, i.e. destitute (of children). In the KJV it is rendered: childless.
H6186: A primitive root; to set in a row, i.e. arrange, put in order (in a very wide variety of applications). In the KJV it is rendered: put (set) (the battle, self) in array, compare, direct, equal, esteem, estimate, expert (in war), furnish, handle, join (battle), ordain, (lay, put, reckon up, set) (in) order, prepare, tax, value.
H6187: From עָרַך; a pile, equipment, estimate. In the KJV it is rendered: equal, estimation, (things that are set in) order, price, proportion, X set at, suit, taxation, X valuest.
H6188: A primitive root; properly, to strip; but used as denominative from עָרֵל; to expose or remove the prepuce, whether literal (to go naked) or figurative (to refrain from using). In the KJV it is rendered: count uncircumcised, foreskin to be uncovered.
H6189: Rom עָרֵל; properly, exposed, i.e. projecting loose (as to the prepuce); used only technically, uncircumcised (i.e. still having the prepuce uncurtailed). In the KJV it is rendered: uncircumcised (person).
H6190: Feminine of עָרֵל; the prepuce. In the KJV it is rendered: foreskin, + uncircumcised.
H6191: A primitive root; properly, to be (or make) bare; but used only in the derivative sense (through the idea perhaps of smoothness) to be cunning (usually in a bad sense). In the KJV it is rendered: X very, beware, take crafty (counsel), be prudent, deal subtilly.
H6192: A primitive root; to pile up. In the KJV it is rendered: gather together.
H6193: From עָרֹם; a stratagem. In the KJV it is rendered: craftiness.
H6194: (Jer. 50:26) or (feminine) aremah; from עָרַם; a heap; specifically, a sheaf. In the KJV it is rendered: heap (of corn), sheaf.
H6195: Feminine of עֹ֫רֶם; trickery; or (in a good sense) discretion. In the KJV it is rendered: guile, prudence, subtilty, wilily, wisdom.
H6196: Probably from עָרֹם; the plane tree (from its smooth and shed bark). In the KJV it is rendered: chestnut tree.
H6197: Probably from עוּר; watchful; Eran, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Eran.
H6198: Patronymically from עֵרָן; an Eranite or descendant (collectively) of Eran. In the KJV it is rendered: Eranites.
H6199: From עָרַר; naked, i.e. (figuratively) poor. In the KJV it is rendered: destitute.
H6200: Patronymically from עַרְעוֹר; an Aroerite or inhabitant of Aroer. In the KJV it is rendered: Aroerite.
H6201: A primitive root; to droop; hence, to drip. In the KJV it is rendered: drop (down).
H6202: A primitive root (identical with עָרַף through the idea of sloping); properly, to bend downward; but used only as a denominative from עֹ֫רֶף, to break the neck; hence (figuratively) to destroy. In the KJV it is rendered: that is beheaded, break down, break (cut off, strike off) neck.
H6203: From עָרַף; the nape or back of the neck (as declining); hence, the back generally (whether literal or figurative). In the KJV it is rendered: back ((stiff-)neck((-ed).
H6204: Feminine of עֹ֫רֶף; mane; Orpah, a Moabites. In the KJV it is rendered: Orpah.
H6205: Probably from עָרַף; gloom (as of a lowering sky). In the KJV it is rendered: (gross, thick) dark (cloud, -ness).
H6206: A primitive root; to awe or (intransitive) to dread; hence, to harass. In the KJV it is rendered: be affrighted (afraid, dread, feared, terrified), break, dread, fear, oppress, prevail, shake terribly.
H6207: A primitive root; to gnaw, i.e. (figuratively) eat (by hyberbole); also (participle) a pain. In the KJV it is rendered: fleeing, sinew.
H6208: Patrial from an unused name meaning a tush; an Arkite or inhabitant of Erek. In the KJV it is rendered: Arkite.
H6209: A primitive root; to bare; figuratively, to demolish. In the KJV it is rendered: make bare, break, raise up (perhaps by clerical error for raze), X utterly.
H6210: From an unused root meaning perhaps to arch; a couch (properly, with a canopy). In the KJV it is rendered: bed(-stead), couch.
H6211: From עָשֵׁשׁ; a moth. In the KJV it is rendered: moth.
H6212: From an unused root meaning to glisten (or be green); grass (or any tender shoot). In the KJV it is rendered: grass, herb.
H6213: A primitive root; to do or make, in the broadest sense and widest application (as follows). In the KJV it is rendered: accomplish, advance, appoint, apt, be at, become, bear, bestow, bring forth, bruise, be busy, X certainly, have the charge of, commit, deal (with), deck, + displease, do, (ready) dress(-ed), (put in) execute(-ion), exercise, fashion, + feast, (fight-)ing man, + finish, fit, fly, follow, fulfill, furnish, gather, get, go about, govern, grant, great, + hinder, hold ((a feast)), X indeed, + be industrious, + journey, keep, labour, maintain, make, be meet, observe, be occupied, offer, + officer, pare, bring (come) to pass, perform, pracise, prepare, procure, provide, put, requite, X sacrifice, serve, set, shew, X sin, spend, X surely, take, X thoroughly, trim, X very, + vex, be (warr-)ior, work(-man), yield, use.
H6214: From עָשָׂה and אֵל; God has made; Asahel, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Asahel.
H6215: Apparently a form of the passive participle of עָשָׂה in the original sense of handling; rough (i.e. sensibly felt); Esav, a son of Isaac, including his posterity. In the KJV it is rendered: Esau.
H6216: From עָשַׁק; oppressive (as noun, a tyrant). In the KJV it is rendered: oppressor.
H6217: Or mashuq; passive participle of עָשַׁק; used in plural masculine as abstractly, tyranny. In the KJV it is rendered: oppressed(-ion).
H6218: Or masor; from עָ֫שֶׂר; ten; by abbrev. ten strings, and so a decachord. In the KJV it is rendered: (instrument of) ten (strings, -th).
H6219: From עָשַׁת; shining, i.e. polished. In the KJV it is rendered: bright.
H6220: For עָשׁוֹת; bright; Ashvath, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashvath.
H6221: From עָשָׂה and אֵל; made of God; Asiel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Asiel.
H6222: From עָשָׂה and יָהּ; Jah has made; Asajah, the name of three or four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Asaiah.
H6223: From עָשַׁר; rich, whether literal or figurative (noble). In the KJV it is rendered: rich (man).
H6224: From עָ֫שֶׂר; tenth; by abbreviation, tenth month or (feminine) part. In the KJV it is rendered: tenth (part).
H6225: A primitive root; to smoke, whether literal or figurative. In the KJV it is rendered: be angry (be on a) smoke.
H6226: From עָשַׁן; smoky. In the KJV it is rendered: smoking.
H6227: From עָשַׁן; smoke, literally or figuratively (vapor, dust, anger). In the KJV it is rendered: smoke(-ing).
H6228: The same as עָשָׁן; Ashan, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashan.
H6229: A primitive root (identical with עָשַׁק); to press upon, i.e. quarrel; --strive with.
H6230: From עָשַׂק; strife. In the KJV it is rendered: Esek.
H6231: A primitive root (compare עָשַׂק); to press upon, i.e. oppress, defraud, violate, overflow. In the KJV it is rendered: get deceitfully, deceive, defraud, drink up, (use) oppress((-ion)), -or), do violence (wrong).
H6232: From עָשַׁק; oppression; Eshek, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Eshek.
H6233: From עָשַׁק; injury, fraud, (subjectively) distress, (concretely) unjust gain. In the KJV it is rendered: cruelly, extortion, oppression, thing (deceitfully gotten).
H6234: Feminine of עֹ֫שֶׁק; anguish. In the KJV it is rendered: oppressed.
H6235: Masculine of term aasarah; from עָשַׂר; ten (as an accumulation to the extent of the digits). In the KJV it is rendered: ten, (fif-, seven-)teen.
H6236: (Aramaic) masculine aasrah (Aramaic); corresponding to עָ֫שֶׂר; ten. In the KJV it is rendered: ten, + twelve.
H6237: A primitive root (ident. with עָשַׁר); to accumulate; but used only as denominative from עָ֫שֶׂר; to tithe, i.e. to take or give a tenth. In the KJV it is rendered: X surely, give (take) the tenth, (have, take) tithe(-ing, -s), X truly.
H6238: A primitive root; properly, to accumulate; chiefly (specifically) to grow (causatively, make) rich. In the KJV it is rendered: be(-come, en-, make, make self, wax) rich, make (1 Kings 22:48 marg).
H6239: From עָשַׁר; wealth. In the KJV it is rendered: X far (richer), riches.
H6240: For עָ֫שֶׂר; ten (only in combination), i.e. -teen; also (ordinal) -teenth. In the KJV it is rendered: (eigh-, fif-, four-, nine-, seven-, six-, thir-)teen(-th), + eleven(-th), + sixscore thousand, + twelve(-th).
H6241: Or oissaron; from עָ֫שֶׂר; (fractional) a tenth part. In the KJV it is rendered: tenth deal.
H6242: From עָ֫שֶׂר; twenty; also (ordinal) twentieth. In the KJV it is rendered: (six-)score, twenty(-ieth).
H6243: (Aramaic) corresponding to עֶשְׂרִים. In the KJV it is rendered: twenty.
H6244: A primitive root; probably to shrink, i.e. fail. In the KJV it is rendered: be consumed.
H6245: A primitive root; probably to be sleek, i.e. glossy; hence (through the idea of polishing) to excogitate (as if forming in the mind). In the KJV it is rendered: shine, think.
H6246: (Aramaic) corresponding to עָשַׁת; to purpose. In the KJV it is rendered: think.
H6247: From עָשַׁת; a fabric. In the KJV it is rendered: bright.
H6248: From עָשַׁת; cogitation. In the KJV it is rendered: thought.
H6249: Apparently masculine plural construction of עֶ֫שֶׁת in the sense of an afterthought (used only in connection with עָשָׂר in lieu of אֶחָד) eleven or (ordinal) eleventh. In the KJV it is rendered: + eleven(-th).
H6250: From עָשַׁת; thinking. In the KJV it is rendered: thought.
H6251: Probably from עָשַׁר; increase. In the KJV it is rendered: flock.
H6252: Or Ashtaroth; plural of עַשְׁתְּרוֹת; Ashtaroth, the name of a Sidonian deity, and of a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Asharoth, Astaroth.
H6253: Probably for עַשְׁתְּרוֹת; Ashtoreth, the Phoenician goddess of love (and increase). In the KJV it is rendered: Ashtoreth.
H6254: Patrial from עַשְׁתָּרוֹת; an Ashterathite or inhabitant of Ashtaroth. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashterathite.
H6255: From עַשְׁתָּרוֹת and the dual of קָ֫רֶן; Ashtaroth of (the) double horns (a symbol of the deity); Ashteroth-Karnaim, a place East of the Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Ashtoreth Karnaim.
H6256: From עַד; time, especially (adverb with preposition) now, when, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: + after, (al-)ways, X certain, + continually, + evening, long, (due) season, so (long) as, (even-, evening-, noon-)tide, ((meal-)), what) time, when.
H6257: A primitive root; to prepare. In the KJV it is rendered: make fit, be ready to become.
H6258: From עֵת; at this time, whether adverb, conjunction or expletive. In the KJV it is rendered: henceforth, now, straightway, this time, whereas.
H6259: Passive participle of עָתַד; prepared. In the KJV it is rendered: ready.
H6260: Or sattud; from עָתַד; prepared, i.e. full grown; spoken only (in plural) of he-goats, or (figuratively) leaders of the people. In the KJV it is rendered: chief one, (he) goat, ram.
H6261: From עֵת; timely. In the KJV it is rendered: fit.
H6262: For עִתִּי; Attai, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Attai.
H6263: (Aramaic) corresponding to עָתִיד; prepared. In the KJV it is rendered: ready.
H6264: From עָתַד; prepared; by implication, skilful; feminine plural the future; also treasure. In the KJV it is rendered: things that shall come, ready, treasures.
H6265: From עוּת and יָהּ; Jah has helped; Athajah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Athaiah.
H6266: From עָתַק; properly, antique, i.e. venerable or splendid. In the KJV it is rendered: durable.
H6267: From עָתַק; removed, i.e. weaned; also antique. In the KJV it is rendered: ancient, drawn.
H6268: (Aramaic) corresponding to עַתִּיקִים; venerable. In the KJV it is rendered: ancient.
H6269: From an unused root meaning to sojourn; lodging; Athak, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Athach.
H6270: From an unused root meaning to compress; constringent; Athlai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Athlai.
H6271: Or Athalyahuw; from the same as עַתְלָי and יָהּ; Jah has constrained; Athaljah, the name of an Israelitess and two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Athaliah.
H6272: A primitive root; probably to glow, i.e. (figuratively) be desolated. In the KJV it is rendered: be darkened.
H6273: From an unused root meaning to force; forcible; Othni, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Othni.
H6274: From the same as עָתְנִי and אֵל; force of God; Othniel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Othniel.
H6275: A primitive root; to remove (intransitive or transitive) figuratively, to grow old; specifically, to transcribe. In the KJV it is rendered: copy out, leave off, become (wax) old, remove.
H6276: From עָתַק; antique, i.e. valued. In the KJV it is rendered: durable.
H6277: From עָתַק in the sense of license; impudent. In the KJV it is rendered: arrogancy, grievous (hard) things, stiff.
H6278: From עֵת and קַיָּם; time of a judge; Eth-Katsin, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ittah-kazin (by including directive enclitic).
H6279: A primitive root (rather denominative from עֶ֫תֶר); to burn incense in worship, i.e. intercede (reciprocally, listen to prayer). In the KJV it is rendered: intreat, (make) pray(-er).
H6280: A primitive root; to be (causatively, make) abundant. In the KJV it is rendered: deceitful, multiply.
H6281: From עָתַר; abundance; Ether, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ether.
H6282: From עָתַר; incense (as increasing to a volume of smoke); hence (from עָתַר) a worshipper. In the KJV it is rendered: suppliant, thick.
H6283: From עָתַר; copiousness. In the KJV it is rendered: abundance.
H6284: A primitive root; to puff, i.e. blow away. In the KJV it is rendered: scatter into corners.
H6285: Feminine of NONE; properly, mouth in a figurative sense, i.e. direction, region, extremity. In the KJV it is rendered: corner, end, quarter, side.
H6286: A primitive root; to gleam, i.e. (causatively) embellish; figuratively, to boast; also to explain (i.e. make clear) oneself; denominative from פֻּארָה, to shake a tree. In the KJV it is rendered: beautify, boast self, go over the boughs, glorify (self), glory, vaunt self.
H6287: From פָּאַר; an embellishment, i.e. fancy head-dress. In the KJV it is rendered: beauty, bonnet, goodly, ornament, tire.
H6288: Or pora'h; or pu'rah; from פָּאַר; properly, ornamentation, i.e. (plural) foliage (including the limbs) as bright green. In the KJV it is rendered: bough, branch, sprig.
H6289: From פָּאַר; properly, illuminated, i.e. a glow; as noun, a flush (of anxiety). In the KJV it is rendered: blackness.
H6290: From פָּאַר; ornamental; Paran, a desert of Arabia. In the KJV it is rendered: Paran.
H6291: From an unused root meaning to be torpid, i.e. crude; an unripe fig. In the KJV it is rendered: green fig.
H6292: Or piggul; from an unused root meaning to stink; properly, fetid, i.e. (figuratively) unclean (ceremonially). In the KJV it is rendered: abominable(-tion, thing).
H6293: A primitive root; to impinge, by accident or violence, or (figuratively) by importunity. In the KJV it is rendered: come (betwixt), cause to entreat, fall (upon), make intercession, intercessor, intreat, lay, light (upon), meet (together), pray, reach, run.
H6294: From פָּגַע; impact (casual). In the KJV it is rendered: chance, occurent.
H6295: From פֶּ֫גַע and אֵל; accident of God; Pagiel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Pagiel.
H6296: A primitive root; to relax, i.e. become exhausted. In the KJV it is rendered: be faint.
H6297: From פָּגַר; a carcase (as limp), whether of man or beast; figuratively, an idolatrous image. In the KJV it is rendered: carcase, corpse, dead body.
H6298: A primitive root; to come in contact with, whether by accident or violence; figuratively, to concur. In the KJV it is rendered: meet (with, together).
H6299: A primitive root; to sever, i.e. ransom; gener. to release, preserve. In the KJV it is rendered: X at all, deliver, X by any means, ransom, (that are to be, let be) redeem(-ed), rescue, X surely.
H6300: From פָּדָה and אֵל; God has ransomed; Pedahel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Pedahel.
H6301: From פָּדָה and צוּר; a rock (i.e. God) has ransomed; Pedahtsur, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Pedahzur.
H6302: Passive participle of פָּדָה. ransomed (and so occurring under פָּדָה); as abstractly (in plural masculine) a ransom. In the KJV it is rendered: (that are) to be (that were) redeemed.
H6303: From פָּדָה; ransom; Padon, one of the Nethinim. -- Padon.
H6304: Or pduth; from קֵ֫דְמָה; distinction; also deliverance. In the KJV it is rendered: division, redeem, redemption.
H6305: Or Pdayahuw; from פָּדָה and יָהּ; Jah has ransomed; Pedajah, the name of six Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Pedaiah.
H6306: Or pidyom; also pidyown; or pidyon; from פָּדָה; a ransom; --ransom, that were redeemed, redemption.
H6307: From an unused root meaning to extend; a plateau; or Paddan Aram; from the same and אֲרָם; the table-land of Aram; Paddan or Paddan-Aram, a region of Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Padan, Padan-aram.
H6308: A primitive root; to retrieve. In the KJV it is rendered: deliver.
H6309: From an unused root meaning to be greasy; suet. In the KJV it is rendered: fat.
H6310: From פָּאָה; the mouth (as the means of blowing), whether literal or figurative (particularly speech); specifically edge, portion or side; adverbially (with preposition) according to. In the KJV it is rendered: accord(-ing as, -ing to), after, appointment, assent, collar, command(-ment), X eat, edge, end, entry, + file, hole, X in, mind, mouth, part, portion, X (should) say(-ing), sentence, skirt, sound, speech, X spoken, talk, tenor, X to, + two-edged, wish, word.
H6311: Or po6 (Job 38:11); or pow; probably from a primitive inseparable particle "p" (of demonstrative force) and הוּא; this place (French ici), i.e. here or hence. In the KJV it is rendered: here, hither, the one (other, this, that) side.
H6312: Or Puvvah; from פָּאָה; a blast; Puah or Puvvah, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Phuvah, Pua, Puah.
H6313: A primitive root; to be sluggish. In the KJV it is rendered: cease, be feeble, faint, be slacked.
H6314: From פּוּג; intermission. In the KJV it is rendered: rest.
H6315: A primitive root; to puff, i.e. blow with the breath or air; hence, to fan (as a breeze), to utter, to kindle (a fire), to scoff. In the KJV it is rendered: blow (upon), break, puff, bring into a snare, speak, utter.
H6316: Of foreign origin; Put, a son of Ham, also the name of his descendants or their region, and of a Persian tribe. In the KJV it is rendered: Phut, Put.
H6317: From an unused root (probably meaning to disparage) and אֵל; contempt of God; Putiel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Putiel.
H6318: Of Egyptian derivation: Potiphar, an Egyptian. In the KJV it is rendered: Potiphar.
H6319: Of Egyptian derivation; Poti-Phera, an Egyptian. In the KJV it is rendered: Poti-pherah.
H6320: From an unused root meaning to paint; dye (specifically, stibium for the eyes). In the KJV it is rendered: fair colours, glistering, paint(-ed) (-ing).
H6321: From an unused root meaning to be thick; a bean (as plump). In the KJV it is rendered: beans.
H6322: Of foreign origin; Pul, the name of an Assyrian king and of an Ethiopian tribe. In the KJV it is rendered: Pul.
H6323: A primitive root meaning to turn, i.e. be perplexed. In the KJV it is rendered: be distracted.
H6324: Patronymically from an unused name meaning a turn; a Punite (collectively) or descendants of an unknown Pun. In the KJV it is rendered: Punites.
H6325: From פּוּן; perplexity; Punon, a place in the Desert. In the KJV it is rendered: Punon.
H6326: From an unused root meaning to glitter; brilliancy; Puah, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Puah.
H6327: A primitive root; to dash in pieces, literally or figuratively (especially to disperse). In the KJV it is rendered: break (dash, shake) in (to) pieces, cast (abroad), disperse (selves), drive, retire, scatter (abroad), spread abroad.
H6328: A primitive root; to waver. In the KJV it is rendered: stumble, move.
H6329: A primitive root (identical with פִּיק through the idea of dropping out; compare נְפַק); to issue, i.e. furnish; causatively, to secure; figuratively, to succeed. In the KJV it is rendered: afford, draw out, further, get, obtain.
H6330: From פִּיק; a stumbling-block. In the KJV it is rendered: grief.
H6331: A primitive root; to crush. In the KJV it is rendered: break, bring to nought, X utterly take.
H6332: Also (plural) Puwriym; or Puriym; from פּוּר; a lot (as by means of a broken piece). In the KJV it is rendered: Pur, Purim.
H6333: From פּוּר; a wine-press (as crushing the grapes). In the KJV it is rendered: winepress.
H6334: Of Persian origin; Poratha, a son of Haman. In the KJV it is rendered: Poratha.
H6335: A primitive root; to spread; figuratively, act proudly. In the KJV it is rendered: grow up, be grown fat, spread selves, be scattered.
H6336: Patronymically from an unused name meaning a hinge; a Puthite (collectively) or descendants of an unknown Puth. In the KJV it is rendered: Puhites (as if from Puw'ah).
H6337: From פָּזַז; pure (gold); hence, gold itself (as refined). In the KJV it is rendered: fine (pure) gold.
H6338: A primitive root; to refine (gold). In the KJV it is rendered: best (gold).
H6339: A primitive root (identical with פָּזַז); to solidify (as if by refining); also to spring (as if separating the limbs). In the KJV it is rendered: leap, be made strong.
H6340: A primitive root; to scatter, whether in enmity or bounty. In the KJV it is rendered: disperse, scatter (abroad).
H6341: From פָּחַח; a (metallic) sheet (as pounded thin); also a spring net (as spread out like a lamina). In the KJV it is rendered: gin, (thin) plate, snare.
H6342: A primitive root; to be startled (by a sudden alarm); hence, to fear in general. In the KJV it is rendered: be afraid, stand in awe, (be in) fear, make to shake.
H6343: From פָּחַד; a (sudden) alarm (properly, the object feared, by implication, the feeling). In the KJV it is rendered: dread(-ful), fear, (thing) great (fear, -ly feared), terror.
H6344: The same as פַּ֫חַד; a testicle (as a cause of shame akin to fear). In the KJV it is rendered: stone.
H6345: Feminine of פַּ֫חַד; alarm (i.e. awe). In the KJV it is rendered: fear.
H6346: Of foreign origin; a prefect (of a city or small district). In the KJV it is rendered: captain, deputy, governor.
H6347: (Aramaic) corresponding to פַּח. In the KJV it is rendered: captain, governor.
H6348: A primitive root; to bubble up or froth (as boiling water), i.e. (figuratively) to be unimportant. In the KJV it is rendered: light.
H6349: From פָּחַז; ebullition, i.e. froth (figuratively, lust). In the KJV it is rendered: unstable.
H6350: From פָּחַז; frivolity. In the KJV it is rendered: lightness.
H6351: A primitive root; to batter out; but used only as denominative from פָּח, to spread a net. In the KJV it is rendered: be snared.
H6352: Perhaps from an unused root probably meaning to be black; a coal, whether charred or live. In the KJV it is rendered: coals.
H6353: (Aramaic) from an unused root probably meaning to fashion; a potter. In the KJV it is rendered: potter.
H6354: Probably from an unused root apparently meaning to dig; a pit, especially for catching animals. In the KJV it is rendered: hole, pit, snare.
H6355: From פַּ֫חַת and מוֹאָב; pit of Moab; Pachath-Moab, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Pahath-moab.
H6356: From the same as פַּ֫חַת; a hole (by mildew in a garment). In the KJV it is rendered: fret inward.
H6357: Of foreign derivation; a gem, probably the topaz. In the KJV it is rendered: topaz.
H6358: Passive participle of פָּטַר; opened, i.e. (as noun) a bud. In the KJV it is rendered: open.
H6359: From פָּטַר; open, i.e. unoccupied. In the KJV it is rendered: free.
H6360: Intensively from an unused root meaning to pound; a hammer. In the KJV it is rendered: hammer.
H6361: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of פַּטִּישׁ; a gown (as if hammered out wide). In the KJV it is rendered: hose.
H6362: A primitive root; to cleave or burst through, i.e. (causatively) to emit, whether literal or figurative (gape). In the KJV it is rendered: dismiss, free, let (shoot) out, slip away.
H6363: Or pitrah; from פָּטַר; a fissure, i.e. (concretely) firstling (as opening the matrix). In the KJV it is rendered: firstling, openeth, such as open.
H6364: Of Egyptian origin; Pi-Beseth, a place in Egypt. In the KJV it is rendered: Pi-beseth.
H6365: From an unused root probably meaning to pierce; (figuratively) misfortune. In the KJV it is rendered: destruction, ruin.
H6366: Or piyah; feminine of פֶּה; an edge. In the KJV it is rendered: (two-)edge(-d).
H6367: From פֶּה and the feminine plural of a noun (from the same root as חֹר), with the article interpolated; mouth of the gorges; Pi-ha-Chiroth, a place in Egypt. In the KJV it is rendered: Pi-hahiroth.
H6368: From פּ֫וּחַ; a powder (as easily puffed away), i.e. ashes or dust. In the KJV it is rendered: ashes.
H6369: Apparently from פֶּה and כֹּל; mouth of all; Picol, a Philistine. In the KJV it is rendered: Phichol.
H6370: Or pilegesh; of uncertain derivation; a concubine; also (masculine) a paramour. In the KJV it is rendered: concubine, paramour.
H6371: Probably from an unused root meaning to be plump; obesity. In the KJV it is rendered: collops.
H6372: Apparently from פֶּה and a variation of נָחָשׁ; mouth of a serpent; Pinechas, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Phinehas.
H6373: Probably the same as פּוּנֹן; Pinon, an Idumaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Pinon.
H6374: For פֵּיוֹת; an edge or tooth. In the KJV it is rendered: tooth, X two-edged.
H6375: From פּוּק; a tottering. In the KJV it is rendered: smite together.
H6376: From פּוּשׁ; dispersive; Pishon, a river of Eden. In the KJV it is rendered: Pison.
H6377: Probably from the same as פּוֹת; expansive; Pithon, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Pithon.
H6378: From פָּכָה; a flask (from which a liquid may flow). In the KJV it is rendered: box, vial.
H6379: A primitive root; to pour. In the KJV it is rendered: run out.
H6380: From the active participle (of the same form as the first word) feminine of an unused root (meaning to entrap) and plural of צֶ֫בִי; trap of gazelles; Pokereth-Tsebajim, one of the "servants of Solomon". In the KJV it is rendered: Pochereth of Zebaim.
H6381: A primitive root; properly, perhaps to separate, i.e. distinguish (literally or figuratively); by implication, to be (causatively, make) great, difficult, wonderful. In the KJV it is rendered: accomplish, (arise.
H6382: From פָּלָא; a miracle. In the KJV it is rendered: marvellous thing, wonder(-ful, -fully).
H6383: Or paliy1; from פָּלָא; remarkable. In the KJV it is rendered: secret, wonderful.
H6384: Patronymically from פַּלּוּא; a Palluite (collectively) or descendants of Pallu. In the KJV it is rendered: Palluites.
H6385: A primitive root; to split (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: divide.
H6386: (Aramaic) corresponding to פָּלַג. In the KJV it is rendered: divided.
H6387: (Aramaic) from פְּלַג; a half. In the KJV it is rendered: dividing.
H6388: From פָּלַג; a rill (i.e. small channel of water, as in irrigation). In the KJV it is rendered: river, stream.
H6389: The same as פֶּ֫לֶג; earthquake; Peleg, a son of Shem. In the KJV it is rendered: Peleg.
H6390: From פָּלַג; a runlet, i.e. gully. In the KJV it is rendered: division, river.
H6391: From פָּלַג; a section. In the KJV it is rendered: division.
H6392: (Aramaic) corresponding to פְּלֻגּוֹת. In the KJV it is rendered: division.
H6393: From an unused root meaning to divide; a cleaver, i.e. iron armature (of a chariot). In the KJV it is rendered: torch.
H6394: Of uncertain derivation; Pildash, a relative of Abraham. In the KJV it is rendered: Pildash.
H6395: A primitive root; to distinguish (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: put a difference, show marvellous, separate, set apart, sever, make wonderfully.
H6396: From פָּלָה; distinguished; Pallu, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Pallu, Phallu.
H6397: Patronymically from an unused name (from פָּלָה) meaning separate; a Pelonite or inhabitant of an unknown Palon. In the KJV it is rendered: Pelonite.
H6398: A primitive root; to slice, i.e. break open or pierce. In the KJV it is rendered: bring forth, cleave, cut, shred, strike through.
H6399: (Aramaic) corresponding to פָּלַח; to serve or worship. In the KJV it is rendered: minister, serve.
H6400: From פָּלַח; a slice. In the KJV it is rendered: piece.
H6401: From פֶּ֫לַח; slicing; Pilcha, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Pilcha.
H6402: (Aramaic) from פְּלַח; worship. In the KJV it is rendered: service.
H6403: A primitive root; to slip out, i.e. escape; causatively, to deliver. In the KJV it is rendered: calve, carry away safe, deliver, (cause to) escape.
H6404: From פָּלַט; escape; Pelet, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Pelet.
H6405: From פָּלַט; escape. In the KJV it is rendered: deliverance, escape.
H6406: From פָּלַט; delivered; Palti, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Palti, Phalti.
H6407: Patronymically from פַּלְטִי; a Paltite or descendant of Palti. In the KJV it is rendered: Paltite.
H6408: For פַּלְטִי; Piltai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Piltai.
H6409: From the same as פָּ֫לֶט and אֵל; deliverance of God; Paltiel, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Paltiel, Phaltiel.
H6410: Or Platyahuw; from פָּלַט and יָהּ; Jah has delivered; Pelatjah, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Pelatiah.
H6411: Or Pla.yah; from פָּלָא and יָהּ; Jah has distinguished; Pelajah, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Pelaiah.
H6412: Or paleyt; or palet; from פָּלַט; a refugee. In the KJV it is rendered: (that have) escape(-d, -th), fugitive.
H6413: Or pletah; feminine of פָּלִיט; deliverance; concretely, an escaped portion. In the KJV it is rendered: deliverance, (that is) escape(-d), remnant.
H6414: From פָּלַל; a magistrate. In the KJV it is rendered: judge.
H6415: Feminine of פְּלִילִים; justice. In the KJV it is rendered: judgment.
H6416: From פְּלִילִים; judicial. In the KJV it is rendered: judge.
H6417: Feminine of פְּלִילִי; judicature. In the KJV it is rendered: judgment.
H6418: From an unused root meaning to be round; a circuit (i.e. district); also a spindle (as whirled); hence, a crutch:--(di-)staff, participle.
H6419: A primitive root; to judge (officially or mentally); by extension, to intercede, pray. In the KJV it is rendered: intreat, judge(-ment), (make) pray(-er, -ing), make supplication.
H6420: From פָּלַל; judge; Palal, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Palal.
H6421: From פָּלַל and יָהּ; Jah has judged; Pelaljah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Pelaliah.
H6422: Probably for פְּלֹנִי; a certain one, i.e. so-and-so. In the KJV it is rendered: certain.
H6423: From פָּלָה; such a one, i.e. a specified peccrson. In the KJV it is rendered: such.
H6424: A primitive root; properly, to roll flat, i.e. prepare (a road); also to revolve, i.e. weigh (mentally). In the KJV it is rendered: make, ponder, weigh.
H6425: From פָּלַס; a balance. In the KJV it is rendered: scales, weight.
H6426: A primitive root; properly, perhaps to rend, i.e. (by implication) to quiver. In the KJV it is rendered: tremble.
H6427: From פָּלַץ; affright. In the KJV it is rendered: fearfulness, horror, trembling.
H6428: A primitive root; to roll (in dust). In the KJV it is rendered: roll (wallow) self.
H6429: From פָּלַשׁ; rolling, i.e. migratory; Pelesheth, a region of Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Palestina, Palestine, Philistia, Philistines.
H6430: Patrial from פְּלָ֫שֶׁת; a Pelishtite or inhabitant of Pelesheth. In the KJV it is rendered: Philistine.
H6431: From an unused root meaning to flee; swiftness; Peleth, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Peleth.
H6432: From the same form as פֶּ֫לֶת; a courier (collectively) or official messenger. In the KJV it is rendered: Pelethites.
H6433: (Aramaic) probably for פֶּה; the mouth (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: mouth.
H6434: From an unused root meaning to turn; an angle (of a street or wall). In the KJV it is rendered: corner.
H6435: From פָּנָה; properly, removal; used only (in the construction) adverb as conjunction, lest. In the KJV it is rendered: (lest) (peradventure), that.
H6436: Of uncertain derivation; probably pastry. In the KJV it is rendered: Pannag.
H6437: A primitive root; to turn; by implication, to face, i.e. appear, look, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: appear, at (even-)tide, behold, cast out, come on, X corner, dawning, empty, go away, lie, look, mark, pass away, prepare, regard, (have) respect (to), (re-)turn (aside, away, back, face, self), X right (early).
H6438: Feminine of פֵּן; an angle; by implication, a pinnacle; figuratively, a chieftain. In the KJV it is rendered: bulwark, chief, corner, stay, tower.
H6439: Or (more properly,) Pniylel; from פָּנָה and אֵל; face of God; Penuel or Peniel, a place East of Jordan; also (as Penuel) the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Peniel, Penuel.
H6440: Plural (but always as singular) of an unused noun paneh from פָּנָה; the face (as the part that turns); used in a great variety of applications (literally and figuratively); also (with prepositional prefix) as a preposition (before, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: + accept, a-(be-)fore(-time), against, anger, X as (long as), at, + battle, + because (of), + beseech, countenance, edge, + employ, endure, + enquire, face, favour, fear of, for, forefront(-part), form(-er time, -ward), from, front, heaviness, X him(-self), + honourable, + impudent, + in, it, look(-eth) (- s), X me, + meet, X more than, mouth, of, off, (of) old (time), X on, open, + out of, over against, the partial, person, + please, presence, propect, was purposed, by reason of, + regard, right forth, + serve, X shewbread, sight, state, straight, + street, X thee, X them(-selves), through (+ - out), till, time(-s) past, (un-)to(-ward), + upon, upside (+ down), with(- in, + -stand), X ye, X you.
H6441: From פָּנִים with directive enclitic; faceward, i.e. indoors. In the KJV it is rendered: (with-)in(-ner part, -ward).
H6442: From פָּנִים; interior. In the KJV it is rendered: (with-)in(-ner, - ward).
H6443: Or paniy; from the same as פֵּן; probably a pearl (as round). In the KJV it is rendered: ruby.
H6444: Probably feminine from פְּנִינִים contr.; Peninnah, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Peninnah.
H6445: A primitive root; to enervate. In the KJV it is rendered: bring up.
H6446: From פָּסַס; properly, the palm (of the hand) or sole (of the foot) (compare פַּס); by implication (plural) a long and sleeved tunic (perhaps simply a wide one; from the original sense of the root, i.e. of many breadths). In the KJV it is rendered: (divers) colours.
H6447: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to פָּסַס; the palm (of the hand, as being spread out):--participle.
H6448: A primitive root; to cut up, i.e. (figuratively) contemplate. In the KJV it is rendered: consider.
H6449: From פָּסַג; a cleft; Pisgah, a mt. East of Jordan. In the KJV it is rendered: Pisgah.
H6450: From פַּסִּים and the plural of דָּם; palm (i.e. dell) of bloodshed; Pas-Dammim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Pas-dammim.
H6451: From פָּסַס; expansion, i.e. abundance. In the KJV it is rendered: handful.
H6452: A primitive root; to hop, i.e. (figuratively) skip over (or spare); by implication, to hesitate; also (literally) to limp, to dance. In the KJV it is rendered: halt, become lame, leap, pass over.
H6453: From פָּסַח; a pretermission, i.e. exemption; used only techically of the Jewish Passover (the festival or the victim). In the KJV it is rendered: passover (offering).
H6454: From פָּסַח; limping; Paseach, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Paseah, Phaseah.
H6455: From פָּסַח; lame. In the KJV it is rendered: lame.
H6456: From פָּסַל; an idol. In the KJV it is rendered: carved (graven) image, quarry.
H6457: From an unused root meaning to divide; divider; Pasak, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Pasach.
H6458: A primitive root; to carve, whether wood or stone. In the KJV it is rendered: grave, hew.
H6459: From פָּסַל; an idol. In the KJV it is rendered: carved (graven) image.
H6460: (Aramaic) or pcanteriyn (Aramaic); a transliteration of the Gr. psalterion; a lyre. In the KJV it is rendered: psaltery.
H6461: A primitive root; probably to disperse, i.e. (intransitive) disappear. In the KJV it is rendered: cease.
H6462: Perhaps from פָּסַס; dispersion; Pispah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Pispah.
H6463: A primitive root; to scream. In the KJV it is rendered: cry.
H6464: Or Pamiy; from פָּעָה; screaming; Pau or Pai, a place in Edom. In the KJV it is rendered: Pai, Pau.
H6465: From פָּעַר; a gap; Peor, a mountain East of Jordan; also (for בַּ֫עַל פְּעוֹר) a deity worshipped there. In the KJV it is rendered: Peor.
H6466: A primitive root; to do or make (systematically and habitually), especially to practise. In the KJV it is rendered: commit, (evil-) do(-er), make(-r), ordain, work(-er).
H6467: From פָּעַל; an act or work (concretely). In the KJV it is rendered: act, deed, do, getting, maker, work.
H6468: Feminine passive participle of פָּעַל; (abstractly) work. In the KJV it is rendered: labour, reward, wages, work.
H6469: From פְּעֻלַּת; laborious; Peullethai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Peulthai.
H6470: A primitive root; to tap, i.e. beat regularly; hence (generally) to impel or agitate. In the KJV it is rendered: move, trouble.
H6471: Or (feminine) pa`amah; from פָּעַם; a stroke, literally or figuratively (in various applications, as follow). In the KJV it is rendered: anvil, corner, foot(-step), going, (hundred-)fold, X now, (this) + once, order, rank, step, + thrice, ((often-)), second, this, two) time(-s), twice, wheel.
H6472: From פָּ֫עַם; a bell (as struck). In the KJV it is rendered: bell.
H6473: A primitive root; to yawn, i.e. open wide (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: gape, open (wide).
H6474: From פָּעַר; yawning; Paarai, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Paarai.
H6475: A primitive root; to rend, i.e. open (especially the mouth). In the KJV it is rendered: deliver, gape, open, rid, utter.
H6476: A primitive root; to break out (in joyful sound). In the KJV it is rendered: break (forth, forth into joy), make a loud noise.
H6477: From פָּצַר; bluntness. In the KJV it is rendered: + file.
H6478: A primitive root; to peel. In the KJV it is rendered: pill.
H6479: From פָּצַל; a peeling. In the KJV it is rendered: strake.
H6480: A primitive root; to rend (by earthquake). In the KJV it is rendered: break.
H6481: A primitive root; to split, i.e. wound. In the KJV it is rendered: wound.
H6482: From פָּצַע; a wound. In the KJV it is rendered: wound(-ing).
H6483: From an unused root meaning to dissever; dispersive; Pitstsets, a priest. In the KJV it is rendered: Apses (including the article).
H6484: A primitive root; to peck at, i.e. (figuratively) stun or dull. In the KJV it is rendered: press, urge, stubbornness.
H6485: A primitive root; to visit (with friendly or hostile intent); by analogy, to oversee, muster, charge, care for, miss, deposit, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: appoint, X at all, avenge, bestow, (appoint to have the, give a) charge, commit, count, deliver to keep, be empty, enjoin, go see, hurt, do judgment, lack, lay up, look, make, X by any means, miss, number, officer, (make) overseer, have (the) oversight, punish, reckon, (call to) remember(-brance), set (over), sum, X surely, visit, want.
H6486: Feminine passive participle of פָּקַד; visitation (in many senses, chiefly official). In the KJV it is rendered: account, (that have the) charge, custody, that which.
H6487: From פָּקַד; a deposit. In the KJV it is rendered: that which was delivered (to keep), store.
H6488: From פָּקִיד; supervision. In the KJV it is rendered: ward.
H6489: From פָּקַד; punishment; Pekod, a symbolic name for Bab. In the KJV it is rendered: Pekod.
H6490: Or piqqud; from פָּקַד; properly, appointed, i.e. a mandate (of God; plural only, collectively, for the Law). In the KJV it is rendered: commandment, precept, statute.
H6491: A primitive root; to open (the senses, especially the eyes); figuratively, to be observant. In the KJV it is rendered: open.
H6492: From פָּקַח; watch; Pekach, an Israelite king. In the KJV it is rendered: Pekah.
H6493: From פָּקַח; clear-sighted; figuratively, intelligent. In the KJV it is rendered: seeing, wise.
H6494: From פָּקַח and יָהּ; Jah has observed; Pekachjah, an Israelite king. In the KJV it is rendered: Pekahiah.
H6495: From פָּקַח redoubled; opening (of a dungeon), i.e. jail-delivery (figuratively, salvation for sin). In the KJV it is rendered: opening of the prison.
H6496: From פָּקַד; a superintendent (civil, military or religious). In the KJV it is rendered: which had the charge, governor, office, overseer, (that) was set.
H6497: From an unused root meaning to burst; only used as an architectural term of an ornament similar to פַּקֻּעֹת, a semi-globe. In the KJV it is rendered: knop.
H6498: From the same as פְּקָעִים; the wild cucumber (from splitting open to shed its seeds). In the KJV it is rendered: gourd.
H6499: Or par; from פָּרַר; a bullock (apparently as breaking forth in wild strength, or perhaps as dividing the hoof). In the KJV it is rendered: (+ young) bull(-ock), calf, ox.
H6500: A primitive root; to bear fruit. In the KJV it is rendered: be fruitful.
H6501: Or pereh (Jeremiah 2:24); from פָּרָא in the secondary sense of running wild; the onager. In the KJV it is rendered: wild (ass).
H6502: From פֶּ֫רֶא; wildly; Piram, a Canaanite. In the KJV it is rendered: Piram.
H6503: Or Parvar; of foreign origin; Parbar or Parvar, a quarter of Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: Parbar, suburb.
H6504: A primitive root; to break through, i.e. spread or separate (oneself). In the KJV it is rendered: disperse, divide, be out of joint, part, scatter (abroad), separate (self), sever self, stretch, sunder.
H6505: From פָּרַד; a mule (perhaps from his lonely habits). In the KJV it is rendered: mule.
H6506: Feminine of פֶּ֫רֶד; a she-mule. In the KJV it is rendered: mule.
H6507: Feminine passive participle of פָּרַד; something separated, i.e. a kernel. In the KJV it is rendered: seed.
H6508: Of foreign origin; a park. In the KJV it is rendered: forest, orchard.
H6509: A primitive root; to bear fruit (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: bear, bring forth (fruit), (be, cause to be, make) fruitful, grow, increase.
H6510: Feminine of פָּר; a heifer. In the KJV it is rendered: cow, heifer, kine.
H6511: The same as פָּרָה; Parah, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Parah.
H6512: From פּוּר; a hole (as broken, i.e. dug). In the KJV it is rendered: + mole.
H6513: For פֻּארָה; foliage; Purah, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Phurah.
H6514: Or Priyda; from פָּרַד; dispersion; Peruda or Perida, one of "Solomon's servants". In the KJV it is rendered: Perida, Peruda.
H6515: Passive participle of פָּרַח; blossomed; Paruach, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Paruah.
H6516: Of foreign origin; Parvajim, an Oriental region. In the KJV it is rendered: Parvaim.
H6517: Passive participle of פָּרַר in the sense of spreading out (compare פָּרַח); a skillet (as flat or deep). In the KJV it is rendered: pan, pot.
H6518: From an unused root meaning to separate, i.e. decide; a chieftain. In the KJV it is rendered: village.
H6519: From the same as פְּרָזִים; an open country. In the KJV it is rendered: (unwalled) town (without walls), unwalled village.
H6520: From the same as פְּרָזִים; magistracy, i.e. leadership (also concretely, chieftains). In the KJV it is rendered: village.
H6521: Or prowziy; from פְּרָזוֹת; a rustic. In the KJV it is rendered: village.
H6522: For פְּרָזִי; inhabitant of the open country; a Perizzite, one of the Canaanitish tribes. In the KJV it is rendered: Perizzite.
H6523: (Aramaic) corresponding to בַּרְזֶל; iron. In the KJV it is rendered: iron.
H6524: A primitive root; to break forth as a bud, i.e. bloom; generally, to spread; specifically, to fly (as extending the wings); figuratively, to flourish. In the KJV it is rendered: X abroad, X abundantly, blossom, break forth (out), bud, flourish, make fly, grow, spread, spring (up).
H6525: From פָּרַח; a calyx (natural or artificial); generally, bloom. In the KJV it is rendered: blossom, bud, flower.
H6526: From פָּרַח; progeny, i.e. a brood. In the KJV it is rendered: youth.
H6527: A primitive root; to scatter words, i.e. prate (or hum). In the KJV it is rendered: chant.
H6528: From פָּרַט; a stray or single berry. In the KJV it is rendered: grape.
H6529: From פָּרָה; fruit (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: bough, ((first-)) fruit((-ful)), reward.
H6530: From פָּרַץ; violent, i.e. a tyrant. In the KJV it is rendered: destroyer, ravenous, robber.
H6531: From an unused root meaning to break apart; fracture, i.e. severity. In the KJV it is rendered: cruelty, rigour.
H6532: Feminine active participle of the same as פָּ֫רֶך; a separatrix, i.e. (the sacred) screen. In the KJV it is rendered: vail.
H6533: A primitive root; to tear. In the KJV it is rendered: rend.
H6534: Of Persian origin; Parmashta, a son of Haman. In the KJV it is rendered: Parmasta.
H6535: Of uncertain derivation; Parnak, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Parnach.
H6536: A primitive root; to break in pieces, i.e. (usually without violence) to split, distribute. In the KJV it is rendered: deal, divide, have hoofs, part, tear.
H6537: (Aramaic) corresponding to פָּרַס; to split up. In the KJV it is rendered: divide, (U-)pharsin.
H6538: From פָּרַס; a claw; also a kind of eagle. In the KJV it is rendered: claw, ossifrage.
H6539: Of foreign origin; Paras (i.e. Persia), an Eastern country, including its inhabitants. In the KJV it is rendered: Persia, Persians.
H6540: (Aramaic) corresponding to פָּרָס. In the KJV it is rendered: Persia, Persians.
H6541: Feminine of פֶּ֫רֶס; a claw or split hoof. In the KJV it is rendered: claw, (cloven-)footed, hoof.
H6542: Patrial from פָּרָס; a Parsite (i.e. Persian), or inhabitant of Peres. In the KJV it is rendered: Persian.
H6543: (Aramaic) corresponding to פָּרְסִי. In the KJV it is rendered: Persian.
H6544: A primitive root; to loosen; by implication, to expose, dismiss; figuratively, absolve, begin. In the KJV it is rendered: avenge, avoid, bare, go back, let, (make) naked, set at nought, perish, refuse, uncover.
H6545: From פָּרַע; the hair (as dishevelled). In the KJV it is rendered: locks.
H6546: Feminine of פֶּ֫רַע (in the sense of beginning); leadership (plural concretely, leaders). In the KJV it is rendered: + avenging, revenge.
H6547: Of Egyptian derivation; Paroh, a general title of Egyptian kings. In the KJV it is rendered: Pharaoh.
H6548: Of Egyptian derivation; Paroh- Chophra, an Egyptian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Pharaoh-hophra.
H6549: Or Parpoh Nkow; of Egyptian derivation; Paroh-Nekoh (or -Neko), an Egyptian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Pharaoh-necho, Pharaoh-nechoh.
H6550: Probably from פָּרַע and עָשׁ; a flea (as the isolated insect). In the KJV it is rendered: flea.
H6551: The same as פַּרְעֹשׁ; Parosh, the name of our Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Parosh, Pharosh.
H6552: From פְּרָעוֹת; chieftaincy; Pirathon, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Pirathon.
H6553: Or Pirathoniy; patrial from פִּרְעָתוֹן; a Pirathonite or inhabitant of Pirathon. In the KJV it is rendered: Pirathonite.
H6554: Probably from פָּרַר in the sense of rushing; rapid; Parpar, a river of Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Pharpar.
H6555: A primitive root; to break out (in many applications, direct and indirect, literal and figurative). In the KJV it is rendered: X abroad, (make a) breach, break (away, down, -er, forth, in, up), burst out, come (spread) abroad, compel, disperse, grow, increase, open, press, scatter, urge.
H6556: From פָּרַץ; a break (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: breach, breaking forth (in), X forth, gap.
H6557: The same as פָּ֫רֶץ; Perets, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Perez, Pharez.
H6558: Patronymically from פָּ֫רֶץ; a Partsite (collectively) or descendants of Perets. In the KJV it is rendered: Pharzites.
H6559: Plural of פָּ֫רֶץ; breaks; Peratsim, a mountain in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Perazim.
H6560: From פָּ֫רֶץ and עֻזָּה; break of Uzza; Perets-Uzza, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Perez-uzza.
H6561: A primitive root; to break off or crunch; figuratively, to deliver. In the KJV it is rendered: break (off), deliver, redeem, rend (in pieces), tear in pieces.
H6562: (Aramaic) corresponding to פָּרַק; to discontinue. In the KJV it is rendered: break off.
H6563: From פָּרַק; rapine; also a fork (in roads). In the KJV it is rendered: crossway, robbery.
H6564: From פָּרַק; soup (as full of crumbed meat). In the KJV it is rendered: broth.
H6565: A primitive root; to break up (usually figuratively, i.e. to violate, frustrate. In the KJV it is rendered: X any ways, break (asunder), cast off, cause to cease, X clean, defeat, disannul, disappoint, dissolve, divide, make of none effect, fail, frustrate, bring (come) to nought, X utterly, make void.
H6566: A primitive root; to break apart, disperse, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: break, chop in pieces, lay open, scatter, spread (abroad, forth, selves, out), stretch (forth, out).
H6567: A primitive root; to separate, literally (to disperse) or figuratively (to specify); also (by implication) to wound. In the KJV it is rendered: scatter, declare, distinctly, shew, sting.
H6568: (Aramaic) corresponding to פָּרַשׁ; to specify. In the KJV it is rendered: distinctly.
H6569: From פָּרַשׁ; excrement (as eliminated). In the KJV it is rendered: dung.
H6570: The same as פֶּ֫רֶשׁ; Peresh, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Peresh.
H6571: From פָּרַשׁ; a steed (as stretched out to a vehicle, not single nor for mounting (compare סוּס)); also (by implication) a driver (in a chariot), i.e. (collectively) cavalry. In the KJV it is rendered: horseman.
H6572: Or pathshegen; of foreign origin; a transcript. In the KJV it is rendered: copy.
H6573: (Aramaic) corresponding to פַּרְשֶׁ֫גֶן. In the KJV it is rendered: copy.
H6574: Perhaps by compounding פָּרַשׁ and פָּרַד (in the sense of straddling) (compare פַּרְשֵׁז); the crotch (or anus). In the KJV it is rendered: dirt.
H6575: From פָּרַשׁ; exposition. In the KJV it is rendered: declaration, sum.
H6576: A root apparently formed by compounding פָּרַשׁ and that of פְּרָזִים (compare פַּרְשְׁדֹ֫נָה); to expand. In the KJV it is rendered: spread.
H6577: Of Persian origin; Parshandatha, a son of Haman. In the KJV it is rendered: Parshandatha.
H6578: From an unused root meaning to break forth; rushing; Perath (i.e. Euphrates), a river of the East. In the KJV it is rendered: Euphrates.
H6579: Of Persian origin; a grandee. In the KJV it is rendered: (most) noble, prince.
H6580: Probably from an unused root meaning to disintegrate; stupidity (as a result of grossness or of degeneracy). In the KJV it is rendered: extremity.
H6581: A primitive root; to spread. In the KJV it is rendered: spread.
H6582: A primitive root; to tear in pieces. In the KJV it is rendered: pull in pieces.
H6583: Probably from פָּשַׁח; liberation; Pashchur, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Pashur.
H6584: A primitive root; to spread out (i.e. deploy in hostile array); by analogy, to strip (i.e. unclothe, plunder, flay, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: fall upon, flay, invade, make an invasion, pull off, put off, make a road, run upon, rush, set, spoil, spread selves (abroad), strip (off, self).
H6585: A primitive root; to stride (from spreading the legs), i.e. rush upon. In the KJV it is rendered: go.
H6586: A primitive root (identical with פָּשַׂע through the idea of expansion); to break away (from just authority), i.e. trespass, apostatize, quarrel. In the KJV it is rendered: offend, rebel, revolt, transgress(-ion, -or).
H6587: From פָּשַׂע; a stride. In the KJV it is rendered: step.
H6588: From פָּשַׁע; a revolt (national, moral or religious). In the KJV it is rendered: rebellion, sin, transgression, trespass.
H6589: A primitive root; to dispart (the feet or lips), i.e. become licentious. In the KJV it is rendered: open (wide).
H6590: (Aramaic) corresponding to פָּתַר; to interpret. In the KJV it is rendered: make (interpretations), interpreting.
H6591: (Aramaic) from פְּשַׁר; an interpretation. In the KJV it is rendered: interpretation.
H6592: Corresponding to פְּשַׁר. In the KJV it is rendered: interpretation.
H6593: From the same as פַּשׁ as in the sense of comminuting; linen (i.e. the thread, as carded). In the KJV it is rendered: flax, linen.
H6594: Feminine of פִּשְׁתִּי; flax; by implication, a wick. In the KJV it is rendered: flax, tow.
H6595: From פָּתַת; a bit. In the KJV it is rendered: meat, morsel, piece.
H6596: Or pothah (Ezek. 13:19); from an unused root meaning to open; a hole, i.e. hinge or the female pudenda:--hinge, secret participle.
H6597: Or pith.om; from פֶּ֫תַע; instantly. In the KJV it is rendered: straightway, sudden(-ly).
H6598: Of Persian origin; a dainty. In the KJV it is rendered: portion (provision) of meat.
H6599: Of Persian origin; a (judicial) sentence. In the KJV it is rendered: decree, sentence.
H6600: (Aramaic) corresponding to פִּתְגָם; a word, answer, letter or decree. In the KJV it is rendered: answer, letter, matter, word.
H6601: A primitive root; to open, i.e. be (causatively, make) roomy; usually figuratively (in a mental or moral sense) to be (causatively, make) simple or (in a sinister way) delude. In the KJV it is rendered: allure, deceive, enlarge, entice, flatter, persuade, silly (one).
H6602: From פָּתָה and אֵל; enlarged of God; Pethuel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Pethuel.
H6603: Or pittuach; passive participle of פָּתַח; sculpture (in low or high relief or even intaglio). In the KJV it is rendered: carved (work) (are, en-)grave(-ing, -n).
H6604: Of foreign origin; Pethor, a place in Mesopotamia. In the KJV it is rendered: Pethor.
H6605: A primitive root; to open wide (literally or figuratively); specifically, to loosen, begin, plough, carve. In the KJV it is rendered: appear, break forth, draw (out), let go free, (en-)grave(-n), loose (self), (be, be set) open(-ing), put off, ungird, unstop, have vent.
H6606: (Aramaic) corresponding to פָּתַח; to open. In the KJV it is rendered: open.
H6607: From פָּתַח; an opening (literally), i.e. door (gate) or entrance way. In the KJV it is rendered: door, entering (in), entrance (-ry), gate, opening, place.
H6608: From פָּתַח; opening (figuratively) i.e. disclosure. In the KJV it is rendered: entrance.
H6609: From פָּתַח; something opened, i.e. a drawn sword. In the KJV it is rendered: drawn sword.
H6610: From פָּתַח; opening (the act). In the KJV it is rendered: open(-ing).
H6611: From פָּתַח and יָהּ; Jah has opened; Pethachjah, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Pethakiah.
H6612: Or pethiy; or pthaeiy; from פָּתָה; silly (i.e. seducible). In the KJV it is rendered: foolish, simple(-icity, one).
H6613: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to פָּתָה; open, i.e. (as noun) width. In the KJV it is rendered: breadth.
H6614: Of uncertain derivation; probably a figured mantle for holidays. In the KJV it is rendered: stomacher.
H6615: From פֶּ֫תִי; silliness (i.e. seducibility). In the KJV it is rendered: simple.
H6616: From פָּתַל; twine. In the KJV it is rendered: bound, bracelet, lace, line, ribband, thread, wire.
H6617: A primitive root; to twine, i.e. (literally) to struggle or (figuratively) be (morally) tortuous. In the KJV it is rendered: (shew self) froward, shew self unsavoury, wrestle.
H6618: From פָּתַל; tortuous (i.e. crafty). In the KJV it is rendered: crooked.
H6619: Of Egyptian derivation; Pithom, a place in Egypt. In the KJV it is rendered: Pithom.
H6620: From an unused root meaning to twist; an asp (from its contortions). In the KJV it is rendered: adder.
H6621: From an unused root meaning to open (the eyes); a wink, i.e. moment (compare פִּתְאוֹם) (used only (with or without preposition) adverbially, quickly or unexpectedly). In the KJV it is rendered: at an instant, suddenly, X very.
H6622: A primitive root; to open up, i.e. (figuratively) interpret (a dream). In the KJV it is rendered: interpret(-ation, -er).
H6623: Or pithron; from פָּתַר; interpretation (of a dream). In the KJV it is rendered: interpretation.
H6624: Of Egyptian derivation; Pathros, a part of Egypt. In the KJV it is rendered: Pathros.
H6625: Patrial from NONE; a Pathrusite, or inhabitant of Pathros. In the KJV it is rendered: Pathrusim.
H6626: A primitive root; to open, i.e. break:--participle.
H6627: From יָצָא; issue, i.e. (human) excrement. In the KJV it is rendered: that (which) cometh from (out).
H6628: From an unused root meaning to be slender; the lotus tree. In the KJV it is rendered: shady tree.
H6629: Or tsaown (Psalm 144:13); from an unused root meaning to migrate; a collective name for a flock (of sheep or goats); also figuratively (of men). In the KJV it is rendered: (small) cattle, flock (+ -s), lamb (+ -s), sheep((-cote, -fold, -shearer, -herds)).
H6630: From the same as צֹאן used denominatively; sheep pasture; Zaanan, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Zaanan.
H6631: From יָצָא; issue, i.e. produce, children. In the KJV it is rendered: that which cometh forth (out), offspring.
H6632: From an unused root meaning to establish; a palanquin or canopy (as a fixture); also a species of lizard (probably as clinging fast). In the KJV it is rendered: covered, litter, tortoise.
H6633: A primitive root; to mass (an army or servants). In the KJV it is rendered: assemble, fight, perform, muster, wait upon, war.
H6634: (Aramaic) corresponding to פִּתְרוֹן in the figurative sense of summoning one's wishes; to please. In the KJV it is rendered: will, would.
H6635: Or (feminine) tsbadah; from צָבָא; a mass of persons (or figuratively, things), especially reg. organized for war (an army); by implication, a campaign, literally or figuratively (specifically, hardship, worship). In the KJV it is rendered: appointed time, (+) army, (+) battle, company, host, service, soldiers, waiting upon, war(-fare).
H6636: Or (more correctly) Tsbiyiym; or Tsbiyim; plural of צֶ֫בִי; gazelles; Tseboim or Tsebijim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Zeboiim, Zeboim.
H6637: Feminine active participle of the same as צָב; the canopier (with the article); Tsobebah, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Zobebah.
H6638: A primitive root; to amass, i.e. grow turgid; specifically, to array an army against. In the KJV it is rendered: fight swell.
H6639: From צָבָה; turgid. In the KJV it is rendered: swell.
H6640: (Aramaic) from צְבָא; properly, will; concretely, an affair (as a matter of determination). In the KJV it is rendered: purpose.
H6641: Passive participle of the same as צֶ֫בַע; dyed (in stripes), i.e. the hyena. In the KJV it is rendered: speckled.
H6642: A primitive root; to grasp, i.e. hand out. In the KJV it is rendered: reach.
H6643: From צָבָה in the sense of prominence; splendor (as conspicuous); also a gazelle (as beautiful). In the KJV it is rendered: beautiful(-ty), glorious (-ry), goodly, pleasant, roe(-buck).
H6644: For צִבְיָה; Tsibja, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zibia.
H6645: For צְבִיָּה; Tsibjah, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Zibiah.
H6646: Feminine of צֶ֫בִי; a female gazelle. In the KJV it is rendered: roe.
H6647: (Aramaic) a root corresponding to that of צֶ֫בַע; to dip. In the KJV it is rendered: wet.
H6648: From an unused root meaning to dip (into coloring fluid); a dye. In the KJV it is rendered: divers, colours.
H6649: From the same as צֶ֫בַע; variegated; Tsibon, an Idumaean. In the KJV it is rendered: Zibeon.
H6650: Plural of צָב֫וּעַ; hyenas; Tseboim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Zeboim.
H6651: A primitive root; to aggregate. In the KJV it is rendered: gather (together), heap (up), lay up.
H6652: From פַּרְעֹשׁ; a pile. In the KJV it is rendered: heap.
H6653: From an unused root apparently meaning to grip; a lock of stalks. In the KJV it is rendered: handful.
H6654: Contr. from an unused root meaning to sidle off; a side; figuratively, an adversary. In the KJV it is rendered: (be-)side.
H6655: (Aramaic) corresponding to צַד; used adverbially (with preposition) at or upon the side of. In the KJV it is rendered: against, concerning.
H6656: (Aramaic) from an unused root corresponding to צָדָה in the sense of intentness; a (sinister) design. In the KJV it is rendered: true.
H6657: From the same as צַד; a siding; Tsedad, a place near Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Zedad.
H6658: A primitive root; to chase; by implication, to desolate. In the KJV it is rendered: destroy, hunt, lie in wait.
H6659: From צָדַק; just; Tsadok, the name of eight or nine Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Zadok.
H6660: From צָדָה; design (compare הַצְדָּא). In the KJV it is rendered: lying in wait.
H6661: Plural of צַד; sides; Tsiddim (with the article), a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ziddim.
H6662: From צָדַק; just. In the KJV it is rendered: just, lawful, righteous (man).
H6663: A primitive root; to be (causatively, make) right (in a moral or forensic sense). In the KJV it is rendered: cleanse, clear self, (be, do) just(-ice, -ify, -ify self), (be turn to) righteous(-ness).
H6664: From צָדַק; the right (natural, moral or legal); also (abstractly) equity or (figuratively) prosperity. In the KJV it is rendered: X even, (X that which is altogether) just(-ice), ((un-))right(-eous) (cause, -ly, - ness).
H6665: (Aramaic) corresponding to צְדָקָה; beneficence. In the KJV it is rendered: righteousness.
H6666: From צָדַק; rightness (abstractly), subjectively (rectitude), objectively (justice), morally (virtue) or figuratively (prosperity). In the KJV it is rendered: justice, moderately, right(-eous) (act, -ly, -ness).
H6667: Or Tsidqiyahuw; from צֶ֫דֶק and יָהּ; right of Jah; Tsidkijah, the name of six Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Zedekiah, Zidkijah.
H6668: A primitive root; to glitter, i.e. be golden in color. In the KJV it is rendered: X fine.
H6669: From צָהַב; golden in color. In the KJV it is rendered: yellow.
H6670: A prim root; to gleam, i.e. (figuratively) be cheerful; by transf. to sound clear (of various animal or human expressions). In the KJV it is rendered: bellow, cry aloud (out), lift up, neigh, rejoice, make to shine, shout.
H6671: A primitive root; to glisten; used only as denominative from יִצְהָר, to press out oil. In the KJV it is rendered: make oil.
H6672: From צָהַר; a light (i.e. window): dual double light, i.e. noon. In the KJV it is rendered: midday, noon(-day, -tide), window.
H6673: Or tsav; from צָוָה; an injunction. In the KJV it is rendered: commandment, precept.
H6674: Or tsov; from an unused root meaning to issue; soiled (as if excrementitious). In the KJV it is rendered: filthy.
H6675: Or tsovah : feminine of צוֹאּים; excrement; generally, dirt; figuratively, pollution. In the KJV it is rendered: dung, filth(-iness).
H6676: (Aramaic) corresponding to צַוָּר. In the KJV it is rendered: neck.
H6677: Or tsavvar (Nehemiah 3:5); or tsavvaron (Song of Solomon 4:9); or (feminine) tsavva.rah (Micah 2:3); intensively from צוּר in the sense of binding; the back of the neck (as that on which burdens are bound). In the KJV it is rendered: neck.
H6678: Or Tsowbah; or Tsobah; from an unused root meaning to station; a station; Zoba or Zobah, a region of Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Zoba, Zobah.
H6679: A primitive root; to lie alongside (i.e. in wait); by implication, to catch an animal (figuratively, men); (denominative from צָ֫יִד) to victual (for a journey). In the KJV it is rendered: chase, hunt, sore, take (provision).
H6680: A primitive root; (intensively) to constitute, enjoin. In the KJV it is rendered: appoint, (for-)bid, (give a) charge, (give a, give in, send with) command(-er, -ment), send a messenger, put, (set) in order.
H6681: A primitive root; to screech (exultingly). In the KJV it is rendered: shout.
H6682: From צָוַח; a screech (of anguish). In the KJV it is rendered: cry(-ing).
H6683: From an unused root meaning to sink: an abyss (of the sea). In the KJV it is rendered: deep.
H6684: A primitive root; to cover over (the mouth), i.e. to fast. In the KJV it is rendered: X at all, fast.
H6685: Or tsom; from from צוּם; a fast. In the KJV it is rendered: fast(-ing).
H6686: From צָעַר; small; Tsuar, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zuar.
H6687: A primitive root; to overflow. In the KJV it is rendered: (make to over-)flow, swim.
H6688: From צוּף; comb of honey (from dripping). In the KJV it is rendered: honeycomb.
H6689: Or Tsowphay; or Tsiyph; from צוּף; honey-comb; Tsuph or Tsophai or Tsiph, the name of an Israelite and of a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Zophai, Zuph.
H6690: From an unused root meaning to expand, breadth; Tsophach, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zophah.
H6691: From צָפַר; departing; Tsophar, a friend of Job. In the KJV it is rendered: Zophar.
H6692: A primitive root; to twinkle, i.e. glance; by analogy, to blossom (figuratively, flourish). In the KJV it is rendered: bloom, blossom, flourish, shew self.
H6693: A primitive root; to compress, i.e. (figuratively) oppress, distress. In the KJV it is rendered: constrain, distress, lie sore, (op-)press(-or), straiten.
H6694: A primitive root (identical with צוּק through the idea of narrowness (of orifice)); to pour out, i.e. (figuratively) smelt, utter. In the KJV it is rendered: be molten, pour.
H6695: Or (feminine) tsuwqah; from צוּק; a strait, i.e. (figuratively) distress. In the KJV it is rendered: anguish, X troublous.
H6696: A primitive root; to cramp, i.e. confine (in many applications, literally and figuratively, formative or hostile). In the KJV it is rendered: adversary, assault, beset, besiege, bind (up), cast, distress, fashion, fortify, inclose, lay siege, put up in bags.
H6697: Or tsur; from צוּר; properly, a cliff (or sharp rock, as compressed); generally, a rock or boulder; figuratively, a refuge; also an edge (as precipitous). In the KJV it is rendered: edge, X (mighty) God (one), rock, X sharp, stone, X strength, X strong.
