G2086: From a compound of ἕτερος and ζυγός; to yoke up differently, i.e. (figuratively) to associate discordantly. In the KJV it is rendered: unequally yoke together with.
G2087: Of uncertain affinity; (an-, the) other or different. In the KJV it is rendered: altered, else, next (day), one, (an-)other, some, strange.
G2088: Adverb from ἕτερος; differently. In the KJV it is rendered: otherwise.
G2089: Perhaps akin to ἔτος; "yet," still (of time or degree). In the KJV it is rendered: after that, also, ever, (any) further, (t-)henceforth (more), hereafter, (any) longer, (any) more(-one), now, still, yet.
G2090: From ἕτοιμος; to prepare. In the KJV it is rendered: prepare, provide, make ready.
G2091: From ἑτοιμάζω; preparation. In the KJV it is rendered: preparation.
G2092: From an old noun heteos (fitness); adjusted, i.e. ready. In the KJV it is rendered: prepared, (made) ready(-iness, to our hand).
G2093: Adverb from ἕτοιμος; in readiness. In the KJV it is rendered: ready.
G2094: Apparently a primary word; a year. In the KJV it is rendered: year.
G2095: Neuter of a primary eus (good); (adverbially) well. In the KJV it is rendered: good, well (done).
G2096: Of Hebrew origin (חַוָּה); Eua (or Eva, i.e. Chavvah), the first woman. In the KJV it is rendered: Eve.
G2097: From εὖ and ἄγγελος; to announce good news ("evangelize") especially the gospel. In the KJV it is rendered: declare, bring (declare, show) glad (good) tidings, preach (the gospel).
G2098: From the same as εὐαγγελίζω; a good message, i.e. the gospel. In the KJV it is rendered: gospel.
G2099: From εὐαγγελίζω; a preacher of the gospel. In the KJV it is rendered: evangelist.
G2100: From εὐάρεστος; to gratify entirely. In the KJV it is rendered: please (well).
G2101: From εὖ and ἀρεστός; fully agreeable. In the KJV it is rendered: acceptable(-ted), wellpleasing.
G2102: Adverb from εὐάρεστος; quite agreeably. In the KJV it is rendered: acceptably, + please well.
G2103: From εὖ and βούλομαι; good-willer; Eubulus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Eubulus.
G2104: From εὖ and γίνομαι; well born, i.e. (literally) high in rank, or (figuratively) generous. In the KJV it is rendered: more noble, nobleman.
G2105: Feminine from εὖ and the alternate of Ζεύς (as the god of the weather); a clear sky, i.e. fine weather. In the KJV it is rendered: fair weather.
G2106: From εὖ and δοκέω; to think well of, i.e. approve (an act); specially, to approbate (a person or thing). In the KJV it is rendered: think good, (be well) please(-d), be the good (have, take) pleasure, be willing.
G2107: From a presumed compound of εὖ and the base of δοκέω; satisfaction, i.e. (subjectively) delight, or (objectively) kindness, wish, purpose. In the KJV it is rendered: desire, good pleasure (will), X seem good.
G2108: From εὐεργέτης; beneficence (genitive case or specially). In the KJV it is rendered: benefit, good deed done.
G2109: From εὐεργέτης; to be philanthropic. In the KJV it is rendered: do good.
G2110: From εὖ and the base of ἔργον; a worker of good, i.e. (specially) a philanthropist. In the KJV it is rendered: benefactor.
G2111: From εὖ and a derivative of τίθημι; well placed, i.e. (figuratively) appropriate. In the KJV it is rendered: fit, meet.
G2112: Adverb from εὐθύς; directly, i.e. at once or soon. In the KJV it is rendered: anon, as soon as, forthwith, immediately, shortly, straightway.
G2113: From εὐθύς and δρόμος; to lay a straight course, i.e. sail direct. In the KJV it is rendered: (come) with a straight course.
G2114: From εὔθυμος; to cheer up, i.e. (intransitively) be cheerful; neuter comparative (adverbially) more cheerfully. In the KJV it is rendered: be of good cheer (merry).
G2115: From εὖ and θυμός; in fine spirits, i.e. cheerful. In the KJV it is rendered: of good cheer, the more cheerfully.
G2116: From εὐθύς; to straighten (level); technically, to steer. In the KJV it is rendered: governor, make straight.
G2117: Perhaps from εὖ and τίθημι; straight, i.e. (literally) level, or (figuratively) true; adverbially (of time) at once. In the KJV it is rendered: anon, by and by, forthwith, immediately, straightway.
G2118: From εὐθύς; rectitude. In the KJV it is rendered: righteousness.
G2119: From εὔκαιρος; to have good time, i.e. opportunity or leisure. In the KJV it is rendered: have leisure (convenient time), spend time.
G2120: From εὔκαιρος; a favorable occasion. In the KJV it is rendered: opportunity.
G2121: From εὖ and καιρός; well-timed, i.e. opportune. In the KJV it is rendered: convenient, in time of need.
G2122: Adverb from εὔκαιρος; opportunely. In the KJV it is rendered: conveniently, in season.
G2123: Comparative of a compound of εὖ and κόπος; better for toil, i.e. more facile. In the KJV it is rendered: easier.
G2124: From εὐλαβής; properly, caution, i.e. (religiously) reverence (piety); by implication, dread (concretely). In the KJV it is rendered: fear(-ed).
G2125: Middle voice from εὐλαβής; to be circumspect, i.e. (by implication) to be apprehensive; religiously, to reverence. In the KJV it is rendered: (moved with) fear.
G2126: From εὖ and λαμβάνω; taking well (carefully), i.e. circumspect (religiously, pious). In the KJV it is rendered: devout.
G2127: From a compound of εὖ and λόγος; to speak well of, i.e. (religiously) to bless (thank or invoke a benediction upon, prosper). In the KJV it is rendered: bless, praise.
G2128: From εὐλογέω; adorable. In the KJV it is rendered: blessed.
G2129: From the same as εὐλογέω; fine speaking, i.e. elegance of language; commendation ("eulogy"), i.e. (reverentially) adoration; religiously, benediction; by implication, consecration; by extension, benefit or largess. In the KJV it is rendered: blessing (a matter of) bounty (X -tifully), fair speech.
G2130: From εὖ and a presumed derivative of μεταδίδωμι; good at imparting, i.e. liberal. In the KJV it is rendered: ready to distribute.
G2131: From εὖ and νίκη; victorious; Eunice, a Jewess. In the KJV it is rendered: Eunice.
G2132: From a compound of εὖ and νοῦς; to be well- minded, i.e. reconcile. In the KJV it is rendered: agree.
G2133: From the same as εὐνοέω; kindness; euphemistically, conjugal duty. In the KJV it is rendered: benevolence, good will.
G2134: From εὐνοῦχος; to castrate (figuratively, live unmarried). In the KJV it is rendered: make…eunuch.
G2135: From eune (a bed) and ἔχω; a castrated person (such being employed in Oriental bed-chambers); by extension an impotent or unmarried man; by implication, a chamberlain (state-officer). In the KJV it is rendered: eunuch.
G2136: From the same as εὐοδόω; fine travelling; Euodia, a Christian woman. In the KJV it is rendered: Euodias.
G2137: From a compound of εὖ and ὁδός; to help on the road, i.e. (passively) succeed in reaching; figuratively, to succeed in business affairs. In the KJV it is rendered: (have a) prosper(-ous journey).
G2138: From εὖ and πείθω; good for persuasion, i.e. (intransitively) complaint. In the KJV it is rendered: easy to be intreated.
G2139: From εὖ and a derivative of a presumed compound of περί and ἵστημι; well standing around, i.e. (a competitor) thwarting (a racer) in every direction (figuratively, of sin in genitive case). In the KJV it is rendered: which doth so easily beset.
G2140: From a compound of εὖ and ποιέω; well-doing, i.e. beneficence. In the KJV it is rendered: to do good.
G2141: From a compound of ἑτοιμάζω and the base of πορεία; (intransitively) to be good for passing through, i.e. (figuratively) have pecuniary means. In the KJV it is rendered: ability.
G2142: From the same as εὐπορέω; pecuniary resources. In the KJV it is rendered: wealth.
G2143: From a compound of εὖ and πρέπω; good suitableness, i.e. gracefulness. In the KJV it is rendered: grace.
G2144: From εὖ and a derivative of προσδέχομαι; well-received, i.e. approved, favorable. In the KJV it is rendered: acceptable(-ted).
G2145: From εὖ and the same as προσεδρεύω; sitting well towards, i.e. (figuratively) assiduous (neuter, diligent service). In the KJV it is rendered: X attend upon.
G2146: From a compound of εὖ and πρόσωπον; to be of good countenance, i.e. (figuratively) to make a display. In the KJV it is rendered: make a fair show.
G2147: A prolonged form of a primary heuro, which (together with another cognate form) heureo is used for it in all the tenses except the present and imperfect; to find (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: find, get, obtain, perceive, see.
G2148: From Euros (the east wind) and κλύδων; a storm from the East (or southeast), i.e. (in modern phrase) a Levanter. In the KJV it is rendered: Euroklydon.
G2149: From eurus (wide) and χώρα; spacious. In the KJV it is rendered: broad.
G2150: From εὐσεβής; piety; specially, the gospel scheme. In the KJV it is rendered: godliness, holiness.
G2151: From εὐσεβής; to be pious, i.e. (towards God) to worship, or (towards parents) to respect (support). In the KJV it is rendered: show piety, worship.
G2152: From εὖ and σέβομαι; well-reverent, i.e. pious. In the KJV it is rendered: devout, godly.
G2153: Adverb from εὐσεβής; piously. In the KJV it is rendered: godly.
G2154: From εὖ and the base of σημαίνω; well indicated, i.e. (figuratively) significant. In the KJV it is rendered: easy to be understood.
G2155: From εὖ and σπλάγχνον; well compassioned, i.e. sympathetic. In the KJV it is rendered: pitiful, tender-hearted.
G2156: Adverb from εὐσχήμων; decorously. In the KJV it is rendered: decently, honestly.
G2157: From εὐσχήμων; decorousness. In the KJV it is rendered: comeliness.
G2158: From εὖ and σχῆμα; well-formed, i.e. (figuratively) decorous, noble (in rank). In the KJV it is rendered: comely, honourable.
G2159: Adverb from a compound of εὖ and a derivative of teino (to stretch); in a well-strung manner, i.e. (figuratively) intensely (in a good sense, cogently; in a bad one, fiercely). In the KJV it is rendered: mightily, vehemently.
G2160: From a compound of εὖ and a derivative of the base of τροπή (meaning well-turned, i.e. ready at repartee, jocose); witticism, i.e. (in a vulgar sense) ribaldry. In the KJV it is rendered: jesting.
G2161: From εὖ and a derivative of τυγχάνω; well- fated, i.e. fortunate; Eutychus, a young man. In the KJV it is rendered: Eutychus.
G2162: From εὔφημος; good language ("euphemy"), i.e. praise (repute). In the KJV it is rendered: good report.
G2163: From εὖ and φήμη; well spoken of, i.e. reputable. In the KJV it is rendered: of good report.
G2164: From εὖ and φορέω; to bear well, i.e. be fertile. In the KJV it is rendered: bring forth abundantly.
G2165: From εὖ and φρήν; to put (middle voice or passively, be) in a good frame of mind, i.e. rejoice. In the KJV it is rendered: fare, make glad, be (make) merry, rejoice.
G2166: Of foreign origin (compare פְּרָת); Euphrates, a river of Asia. In the KJV it is rendered: Euphrates.
G2167: From the same as εὐφραίνω; joyfulness. In the KJV it is rendered: gladness, joy.
G2168: From εὐχάριστος; to be grateful, i.e. (actively) to express gratitude (towards); specially, to say grace at a meal. In the KJV it is rendered: (give) thank(-ful, -s).
G2169: From εὐχάριστος; gratitude; actively, grateful language (to God, as an act of worship). In the KJV it is rendered: thankfulness, (giving of) thanks(-giving).
G2170: From εὖ and a derivative of χαρίζομαι; well favored, i.e. (by implication) grateful. In the KJV it is rendered: thankful.
G2171: From εὔχομαι; properly, a wish, expressed as a petition to God, or in votive obligation. In the KJV it is rendered: prayer, vow.
G2172: Middle voice of a primary verb; to wish; by implication, to pray to God. In the KJV it is rendered: pray, will, wish.
G2173: From εὖ and χρηστός; easily used, i.e. useful. In the KJV it is rendered: profitable, meet for use.
G2174: From a compound of εὖ and ψυχή; to be in good spirits, i.e. feel encouraged. In the KJV it is rendered: be of good comfort.
G2175: From a compound of εὖ and a derivative of ὄζω; good-scentedness, i.e. fragrance. In the KJV it is rendered: sweet savour (smell, -smelling).
G2176: From εὖ and ὄνομα; properly, well-named (good-omened), i.e. the left (which was the lucky side among the pagan Greeks); neuter as adverbial, at the left hand. In the KJV it is rendered: (on the) left.
G2177: From ἐπί and ἅλλομαι; to spring upon. In the KJV it is rendered: leap on.
G2178: From ἐπί and ἅπαξ; upon one occasion (only). In the KJV it is rendered: (at) once (for all).
G2179: From Ἔφεσος; Ephesine, or situated at Ephesus. In the KJV it is rendered: of Ephesus.
G2180: From Ἔφεσος; an Ephesian or inhabitant of Ephesus. In the KJV it is rendered: Ephesian, of Ephesus.
G2181: Probably of foreign origin; Ephesus, a city of Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Ephesus.
G2182: From a compound of ἐπί and εὑρίσκω; a discoverer, i.e. contriver. In the KJV it is rendered: inventor.
G2183: From ἐφήμερος; diurnality, i.e. (specially) the quotidian rotation or class of the Jewish priests' service at the Temple, as distributed by families. In the KJV it is rendered: course.
G2184: From ἐπί and ἡμέρα; for a day ("ephemeral"), i.e. diurnal. In the KJV it is rendered: daily.
G2185: From ἐπί and a cognate of ἥκω; to arrive upon, i.e. extend to. In the KJV it is rendered: reach.
G2186: From ἐπί and ἵστημι; to stand upon, i.e. be present (in various applications, friendly or otherwise, usually literal); --assault, come (in, to, unto, upon), be at hand (instant), present, stand (before, by, over).
G2187: Of Hebrew origin (אֶפְרַ֫יִם or better עֶפְרוֹן); Ephraim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ephraim.
G2188: Of Chaldee origin (פְּתַח); be opened!. In the KJV it is rendered: Ephphatha.
G2189: Feminine of ἐχθρός; hostility; by implication, a reason for opposition. In the KJV it is rendered: enmity, hatred.
G2190: From a primary echtho (to hate); hateful (passively, odious, or actively, hostile); usually as a noun, an adversary (especially Satan). In the KJV it is rendered: enemy, foe.
G2191: Of uncertain origin; an adder or other poisonous snake (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: viper.
G2192: Including an alternate form scheo (used in certain tenses only) a primary verb; to hold (used in very various applications, literally or figuratively, direct or remote; such as possession; ability, contiuity, relation, or condition). In the KJV it is rendered: be (able, X hold, possessed with), accompany, + begin to amend, can(+ -not), X conceive, count, diseased, do + eat, + enjoy, + fear, following, have, hold, keep, + lack, + go to law, lie, + must needs, + of necessity, + need, next, + recover, + reign, + rest, + return, X sick, take for, + tremble, + uncircumcised, use.
G2193: Of uncertain affinity; a conjunction, preposition and adverb of continuance, until (of time and place). In the KJV it is rendered: even (until, unto), (as) far (as), how long, (un-)til(-l), (hither-, un-, up) to, while(-s).
G2194: Of Hebrew origin (זְבוּלוּן); Zabulon (i.e. Zebulon), a region of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Zabulon.
G2195: Of Hebrew origin (compare זַכָּי); Zacchæus, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zacchæus.
G2196: Of Hebrew origin (זָ֫רַח); Zara, (i.e. Zerach), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zara.
G2197: Of Hebrew origin (זְכַרְיָה); Zacharias (i.e. Zechariah), the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Zacharias.
G2198: A primary verb; to live (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: life(-time), (a-)live(-ly), quick.
G2199: Of Hebrew origin (compare זַבְדִּי); Zebedæus, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zebedee.
G2200: From ζέω; boiled, i.e. (by implication) calid (figuratively, fervent). In the KJV it is rendered: hot.
G2201: From the same as ζυγός; a couple, i.e. a team (of oxen yoked together) or brace (of birds tied together). In the KJV it is rendered: yoke, pair.
G2202: Feminine of a derivative (at the second stage) from the same as ζυγός; a fastening (tiller-rope). In the KJV it is rendered: band.
G2203: Of uncertain affinity; in the oblique cases there is used instead of it a (probably cognate) name Dis, which is otherwise obsolete; Zeus or Dis (among the Latins, Jupiter or Jove), the supreme deity of the Greeks. In the KJV it is rendered: Jupiter.
G2204: A primary verb; to be hot (boil, of liquids; or glow, of solids), i.e. (figuratively) be fervid (earnest). In the KJV it is rendered: be fervent.
G2205: From ζέω; properly, heat, i.e. (figuratively) "zeal" (in a favorable sense, ardor; in an unfavorable one, jealousy, as of a husband (figuratively, of God), or an enemy, malice). In the KJV it is rendered: emulation, envy(-ing), fervent mind, indignation, jealousy, zeal.
G2206: From ζῆλος; to have warmth of feeling for or against. In the KJV it is rendered: affect, covet (earnestly), (have) desire, (move with) envy, be jealous over, (be) zealous(-ly affect).
G2207: From ζηλόω; a "zealot". In the KJV it is rendered: zealous.
G2208: The same as ζηλωτής; a Zealot, i.e. (specially) partisan for Jewish political independence. In the KJV it is rendered: Zelotes.
G2209: Probably akin to the base of δαμάζω (through the idea of violence); detriment. In the KJV it is rendered: damage, loss.
G2210: From ζημία; to injure, i.e. (reflexively or passively) to experience detriment. In the KJV it is rendered: be cast away, receive damage, lose, suffer loss.
G2211: Probably contracted from a poetic form of Ζεύς and δῶρον; Jove-given; Zenas, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Zenas.
G2212: Of uncertain affinity; to seek (literally or figuratively); specially, (by Hebraism) to worship (God), or (in a bad sense) to plot (against life). In the KJV it is rendered: be (go) about, desire, endeavour, enquire (for), require, (X will) seek (after, for, means).
G2213: From ζητέω; a search (properly concretely), i.e. (in words) a debate. In the KJV it is rendered: question.
G2214: From ζητέω; a searching (properly, the act), i.e. a dispute or its theme. In the KJV it is rendered: question.
G2215: Of uncertain origin; darnel or false grain. In the KJV it is rendered: tares.
G2216: Of Hebrew origin (זְרֻבָּבֶל); Zorobabel (i.e. Zerubbabel), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Zorobabel.
G2217: Akin to the base of νέφος; gloom (as shrouding like a cloud). In the KJV it is rendered: blackness, darkness, mist.
G2218: From the root of zeugnumi (to join, especially by a "yoke"); a coupling, i.e. (figuratively) servitude (a law or obligation); also (literally) the beam of the balance (as connecting the scales). In the KJV it is rendered: pair of balances, yoke.
G2219: Probably from ζέω; ferment (as if boiling up). In the KJV it is rendered: leaven.
G2220: From ζύμη; to cause to ferment. In the KJV it is rendered: leaven.
G2221: From the same as ζῶον and ἀγρεύω; to take alive (make a prisoner of war), i.e. (figuratively) to capture or ensnare. In the KJV it is rendered: take captive, catch.
G2222: From ζάω; life (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: life(-time).
G2223: Probably akin to the base of ζυγός; a belt; by implication, a pocket. In the KJV it is rendered: girdle, purse.
G2224: From ζώνη; to bind about (especially with a belt). In the KJV it is rendered: gird.
G2225: From the same as ζῶον and a derivative of γίνομαι; to engender alive, i.e. (by analogy) to rescue (passively, be saved) from death. In the KJV it is rendered: live, preserve.
G2226: Neuter of a derivative of ζάω; a live thing, i.e. an animal. In the KJV it is rendered: beast.
G2227: From the same as ζῶον and ποιέω; to (re-)vitalize (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: make alive, give life, quicken.
G2228: A primary particle of distinction between two connected terms; disjunctive, or; comparative, than. In the KJV it is rendered: and, but (either), (n-)either, except it be, (n-)or (else), rather, save, than, that, what, yea.
G2229: An adverb of confirmation; perhaps intensive of ἤ; used only (in the New Testament) before μέν; assuredly. In the KJV it is rendered: surely.
G2230: From ἡγεμών; to act as ruler. In the KJV it is rendered: be governor.
G2231: From ἡγεμών; government, i.e. (in time) official term. In the KJV it is rendered: reign.
G2232: From ἡγέομαι; a leader, i.e. chief person (or figuratively, place) of a province. In the KJV it is rendered: governor, prince, ruler.
G2233: Middle voice of a (presumed) strengthened form of ἄγω; to lead, i.e. command (with official authority); figuratively, to deem, i.e. consider. In the KJV it is rendered: account, (be) chief, count, esteem, governor, judge, have the rule over, suppose, think.
G2234: Adverb from a derivative of the base of ἡδονή; sweetly, i.e. (figuratively) with pleasure. In the KJV it is rendered: gladly.
G2235: Apparently from ἤ (or possibly ἦ) and δή; even now. In the KJV it is rendered: already, (even) now (already), by this time.
G2236: Neuter plural of the superlative of the same as ἡδέως; with great pleasure. In the KJV it is rendered: most (very) gladly.
G2237: From handano (to please); sensual delight; by implication, desire. In the KJV it is rendered: lust, pleasure.
G2238: Neuter of the compound of the same as ἡδέως and ὀσμή; a sweet-scented plant, i.e. mint. In the KJV it is rendered: mint.
G2239: A strengthened form of ἔθος; usage, i.e. (plural) moral habits. In the KJV it is rendered: manners.
G2240: A primary verb; to arrive, i.e. be present (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: come.
G2241: Of Hebrew origin (אֵל with pronominal suffix); my God. In the KJV it is rendered: Eli.
G2242: Of Hebrew origin (עֵלִי); Heli (i.e. Eli), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Heli.
G2243: Of Hebrew origin (אֵלִיָּה); Helias (i.e. Elijah), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Elias.
G2244: From the same as ἡλίκος; maturity (in years or size). In the KJV it is rendered: age, stature.
G2245: From helix (a comrade, i.e. one of the same age); as big as, i.e. (interjectively) how much. In the KJV it is rendered: how (what) great.
G2246: From hele (a ray; perhaps akin to the alternate of αἱρέομαι); the sun; by implication, light. In the KJV it is rendered: + east, sun.
G2247: Of uncertain affinity; a stud, i.e. spike. In the KJV it is rendered: nail.
G2248: Accusative case plural of ἐγώ; us. In the KJV it is rendered: our, us, we.
G2249: Nominative plural of ἐγώ; we (only used when emphatic). In the KJV it is rendered: us, we (ourselves).
G2250: Feminine (with ὥρα implied) of a derivative of hemai (to sit; akin to the base of ἑδραῖος) meaning tame, i.e. gentle; day, i.e. (literally) the time space between dawn and dark, or the whole 24 hours (but several days were usually reckoned by the Jews as inclusive of the parts of both extremes); figuratively, a period (always defined more or less clearly by the context). In the KJV it is rendered: age, + alway, (mid-)day (by day, (-ly)), + for ever, judgment, (day) time, while, years.
G2251: From θνητός; our. In the KJV it is rendered: our, your (by a different reading).
G2252: A prolonged form of ἦν; I was. In the KJV it is rendered: be, was.
G2253: From a presumed compound of the base of ἥμισυ and θνήσκω; half dead, i.e. entirely exhausted. In the KJV it is rendered: half dead.
G2254: Dative case plural of ἐγώ; to (or for, with, by) us. In the KJV it is rendered: our, (for) us, we.
G2255: Neuter of a derivative from an inseparable prefix akin to ἅμα (through the idea of partition involved in connection) and meaning semi-; (as noun) half. In the KJV it is rendered: half.
G2256: From the base of ἥμισυ and ὥρα; a half-hour. In the KJV it is rendered: half an hour.
G2257: Genitive case plural of ἐγώ; of (or from) us. In the KJV it is rendered: our (company), us, we.
G2258: Imperfect of εἰμί; I (thou, etc.) was (wast or were). In the KJV it is rendered: + agree, be, X have (+ charge of), hold, use, was(-t), were.
G2259: Of uncertain affinity; at which time. In the KJV it is rendered: when.
G2260: From ἤ and περ; than at all (or than perhaps, than indeed). In the KJV it is rendered: than.
G2261: Probably from ἔπος; properly, affable, i.e. mild or kind. In the KJV it is rendered: gentle.
G2262: Of Hebrew origin (עֵר); Er, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Er.
G2263: Perhaps by transposition from ἔρημος (through the idea of stillness); tranquil. In the KJV it is rendered: quiet.
G2264: Compound of heros (a "hero") and εἶδος; heroic; Herod, the name of four Jewish kings. In the KJV it is rendered: Herod.
G2265: Plural of a derivative of Ἡρώδης; Herodians, i.e. partisans of Herod. In the KJV it is rendered: Herodians.
G2266: From Ἡρώδης; Herodias, a woman of the Heodian family. In the KJV it is rendered: Herodias.
G2267: From Ἡρώδης; Herodion, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Herodion.
G2268: Of Hebrew origin (יְשַׁעְיָה); Hesaias (i.e. Jeshajah), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Esaias.
G2269: Of Hebrew origin (עֵשָׂו); Esau, an Edomite. In the KJV it is rendered: Esau.
G2270: From the same as ἡσύχιος; to keep still (intransitively), i.e. refrain from labor, meddlesomeness or speech. In the KJV it is rendered: cease, hold peace, be quiet, rest.
G2271: Feminine of ἡσύχιος; (as noun) stillness, i.e. desistance from bustle or language. In the KJV it is rendered: quietness, silence.
G2272: A prolonged form of a compound probably of a derivative of the base of ἑδραῖος and perhaps ἔχω; properly, keeping one's seat (sedentary), i.e. (by implication) still (undisturbed, undisturbing). In the KJV it is rendered: peaceable, quiet.
G2273: From ἤ and τοί; either indeed. In the KJV it is rendered: whether.
G2274: From the same as ἥττον; to make worse, i.e. vanquish (literally or figuratively); by implication, to rate lower. In the KJV it is rendered: be inferior, overcome.
G2275: From ἡττάω; a deterioration, i.e. (objectively) failure or (subjectively) loss. In the KJV it is rendered: diminishing, fault.
G2276: Neuter of comparative of heka (slightly) used for that of κακός; worse (as noun); by implication, less (as adverb). In the KJV it is rendered: less, worse.
G2277: Third person singular imperative of εἰμί; let him (or it) be. In the KJV it is rendered: let … be.
G2278: From ἦχος; to make a loud noise, i.e. reverberate. In the KJV it is rendered: roar, sound.
G2279: Of uncertain affinity; a loud or confused noise ("echo"), i.e. roar; figuratively, a rumor. In the KJV it is rendered: fame, sound.
G2280: Of uncertain origin; Thaddæus, one of the Apostles. In the KJV it is rendered: Thaddæus.
G2281: Probably prolonged from ἅλς; the sea (genitive case or specially). In the KJV it is rendered: sea.
G2282: Probably akin to thallo (to warm); to brood, i.e. (figuratively) to foster. In the KJV it is rendered: cherish.
G2283: Of Hebrew origin (תָּמָר); Thamar (i.e. Tamar), an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Thamar.
G2284: From θάμβος; to stupefy (with surprise), i.e. astound. In the KJV it is rendered: amaze, astonish.
G2285: Akin to an obsolete tapho (to dumbfound); stupefaction (by surprise), i.e. astonishment. In the KJV it is rendered: X amazed, + astonished, wonder.
G2286: From θάνατος; fatal, i.e. poisonous. In the KJV it is rendered: deadly.
G2287: From (the feminine form of) θάνατος and φέρω; death-bearing, i.e. fatal. In the KJV it is rendered: deadly.
G2288: From θνήσκω; (properly, an adjective used as a noun) death (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: X deadly, (be…) death.
G2289: From θάνατος to kill (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: become dead, (cause to be) put to death, kill, mortify.
G2290: A primary verb; to celebrate funeral rites, i.e. inter. In the KJV it is rendered: bury.
G2291: Of Hebrew origin (תָּ֫רַח); Thara (i.e. Terach), the father of Abraham. In the KJV it is rendered: Thara.
G2292: Another form for θαρσέω; to exercise courage. In the KJV it is rendered: be bold, X boldly, have confidence, be confident.
G2293: From θάρσος; to have courage. In the KJV it is rendered: be of good cheer (comfort).
G2294: Akin (by transposition) to thrasos (daring); boldness (subjectively). In the KJV it is rendered: courage.
G2295: Apparently from a form of θεάομαι; wonder (properly concrete; but by implication, abstract). In the KJV it is rendered: admiration.
G2296: From θαῦμα; to wonder; by implication, to admire. In the KJV it is rendered: admire, have in admiration, marvel, wonder.
G2297: From θαῦμα; wondrous, i.e. (neuter as noun) a miracle. In the KJV it is rendered: wonderful thing.
G2298: From θαυμάζω; wondered at, i.e. (by implication) wonderful. In the KJV it is rendered: marvel(-lous).
G2299: Feminine of θεός; a female deity. In the KJV it is rendered: goddess.
G2300: A prolonged form of a primary verb; to look closely at, i.e. (by implication) perceive (literally or figuratively); by extension to visit. In the KJV it is rendered: behold, look (upon), see.
G2301: From θέατρον; to expose as a spectacle. In the KJV it is rendered: make a gazing stock.
G2302: From θεάομαι; a place for public show ("theatre"), i.e. general audience-room; by implication, a show itself (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: spectacle, theatre.
G2303: Probably neuter of θεῖος (in its original sense of flashing); sulphur. In the KJV it is rendered: brimstone.
G2304: From θεός; godlike (neuter as noun, divinity). In the KJV it is rendered: divine, godhead.
G2305: From θεῖος; divinity (abstractly). In the KJV it is rendered: godhead.
G2306: From θεῖον and εἶδος; sulphur-like, i.e. sulphurous. In the KJV it is rendered: brimstone.
G2307: From the prolonged form of θέλω; a determination (properly, the thing), i.e. (actively) choice (specially, purpose, decree; abstractly, volition) or (passively) inclination. In the KJV it is rendered: desire, pleasure, will.
G2308: From θέλω; determination (properly, the act), i.e. option. In the KJV it is rendered: will.
G2309: Or ethelo, in certain tenses theleo, and etheleo, which are otherwise obsolete apparently strengthened from the alternate form of αἱρέομαι; to determine (as an active option from subjective impulse; whereas βούλομαι properly denotes rather a passive acquiescence in objective considerations), i.e. choose or prefer (literally or figuratively); by implication, to wish, i.e. be inclined to (sometimes adverbially, gladly); impersonally for the future tense, to be about to; by Hebraism, to delight in. In the KJV it is rendered: desire, be disposed (forward), intend, list, love, mean, please, have rather, (be) will (have, -ling, - ling(-ly)).
G2310: From a derivative of τίθημι; something put down, i.e. a substruction (of a building, etc.), (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: foundation.
G2311: From θεμέλιος; to lay a basis for, i.e. (literally) erect, or (figuratively) consolidate. In the KJV it is rendered: (lay the) found(- ation), ground, settle.
G2312: From θεός and διδάσκω; divinely instructed. In the KJV it is rendered: taught of God.
G2313: From θεομάχος; to resist deity. In the KJV it is rendered: fight against God.
G2314: From θεός and μάχομαι; an opponent of deity. In the KJV it is rendered: to fight against God.
G2315: From θεός and a presumed derivative of πνέω; divinely breathed in. In the KJV it is rendered: given by inspiration of God.
G2316: Of uncertain affinity; a deity, especially (with ὁ) the supreme Divinity; figuratively, a magistrate; by Hebraism, very. In the KJV it is rendered: X exceeding, God, god(-ly, -ward).
G2317: From θεοσεβής; devoutness, i.e. piety. In the KJV it is rendered: godliness.
G2318: From θεός and σέβομαι; reverent of God, i.e. pious. In the KJV it is rendered: worshipper of God.
G2319: From θεός and the base of στυγνητός; hateful to God, i.e. impious. In the KJV it is rendered: hater of God.
G2320: From θεός; divinity (abstractly). In the KJV it is rendered: godhead.
G2321: From θεός and φίλος; friend of God; Theophilus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Theophilus.
G2322: From θεραπεύω; attendance (specially, medical, i.e. cure); figuratively and collectively, domestics. In the KJV it is rendered: healing, household.
G2323: From the same as θεράπων; to wait upon menially, i.e. (figuratively) to adore (God), or (specially) to relieve (of disease). In the KJV it is rendered: cure, heal, worship.
G2324: Apparently a participle from an otherwise obsolete derivative of the base of θέρος; a menial attendant (as if cherishing). In the KJV it is rendered: servant.
G2325: From θέρος (in the sense of the crop); to harvest. In the KJV it is rendered: reap.
G2326: From θερίζω; reaping, i.e. the crop. In the KJV it is rendered: harvest.
G2327: From θερίζω; a harvester. In the KJV it is rendered: reaper.
G2328: From θέρμη; to heat (oneself). In the KJV it is rendered: (be) warm(-ed, self).
G2329: From the base of θέρος; warmth. In the KJV it is rendered: heat.
G2330: From a primary thero (to heat); properly, heat, i.e. summer. In the KJV it is rendered: summer.
G2331: From Θεσσαλονίκη; a Thessalonican, i.e. inhabitant of Thessalonice. In the KJV it is rendered: Thessalonian.
G2332: From Thessalos (a Thessalian) and νίκη; Thessalonice, a place in Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Thessalonica.
G2333: Of uncertain origin; Theudas, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Theudas.
G2334: From a derivative of θεάομαι (perhaps by addition of ὁράω); to be a spectator of, i.e. discern, (literally, figuratively (experience) or intensively (acknowledge)). In the KJV it is rendered: behold, consider, look on, perceive, see.
G2335: From the same as θεωρέω; spectatorship, i.e. (concretely) a spectacle. In the KJV it is rendered: sight.
G2336: From τίθημι; a receptacle, i.e. scabbard. In the KJV it is rendered: sheath.
G2337: From thele (the nipple); to suckle, (by implication) to suck. In the KJV it is rendered: (give) suck(-ling).
G2338: From the same as θηλάζω; female. In the KJV it is rendered: female, woman.
G2339: From ther (a wild animal, as game); hunting, i.e. (figuratively) destruction. In the KJV it is rendered: trap.
G2340: From θήρα; to hunt (an animal), i.e. (figuratively) to carp at. In the KJV it is rendered: catch.
G2341: From a compound of θηρίον and μάχομαι; to be a beast-fighter (in the gladiatorial show), i.e. (figuratively) to encounter (furious men). In the KJV it is rendered: fight with wild beasts.
G2342: Diminutive from the same as θήρα; a dangerous animal. In the KJV it is rendered: (venomous, wild) beast.
G2343: From θησαυρός; to amass or reserve (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: lay up (treasure), (keep) in store, (heap) treasure (together, up).
G2344: From τίθημι; a deposit, i.e. wealth (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: treasure.
G2345: A prolonged form of an obsolete primary thigo (to finger); to manipulate, i.e. have to do with; by implication, to injure. In the KJV it is rendered: handle, touch.
G2346: Akin to the base of τρίβος; to crowd (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: afflict, narrow, throng, suffer tribulation, trouble.
G2347: From θλίβω; pressure (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: afflicted(-tion), anguish, burdened, persecution, tribulation, trouble.
G2348: A strengthened form of a simpler primary thano than'-o (which is used for it only in certain tenses); to die (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: be dead, die.
G2349: From θνήσκω; liable to die. In the KJV it is rendered: mortal(-ity).
G2350: From θόρυβος; to be in tumult, i.e. disturb, clamor. In the KJV it is rendered: make ado (a noise), trouble self, set on an uproar.
G2351: From the base of θροέω; a disturbance. In the KJV it is rendered: tumult, uproar.
G2352: A primary verb; to crush. In the KJV it is rendered: bruise.
G2353: From τρέφω; stock (as raised on a farm). In the KJV it is rendered: cattle.
G2354: From θρῆνος; to bewail. In the KJV it is rendered: lament, mourn.
G2355: From the base of θροέω; wailing. In the KJV it is rendered: lamentation.
G2356: From a derivative of θρησκός; ceremonial observance. In the KJV it is rendered: religion, worshipping.
G2357: Probably from the base of θροέω; ceremonious in worship (as demonstrative), i.e. pious. In the KJV it is rendered: religious.
G2358: From a prolonged compound of the base of θροέω; and a derivative of ἅπτομαι (meaning a noisy iambus, sung in honor of Bacchus); to make an acclamatory procession, i.e. (figuratively) to conquer or (by Hebraism) to give victory. In the KJV it is rendered: (cause) to triumph (over).
G2359: Genitive case trichos, etc.; of uncertain derivation; hair. In the KJV it is rendered: hair.
G2360: From threomai to wail; to clamor, i.e. (by implication) to frighten. In the KJV it is rendered: trouble.
G2361: Perhaps from τρέφω (in the sense of thickening); a clot. In the KJV it is rendered: great drop.
G2362: From thrao (to sit); a stately seat ("throne"); by implication, power or (concretely) a potentate. In the KJV it is rendered: seat, throne.
G2363: Of uncertain derivation; Thyatira, a place in Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Thyatira.
G2364: Apparently a primary word (compare "daughter"); a female child, or (by Hebraism) descendant (or inhabitant). In the KJV it is rendered: daughter.
G2365: From θυγάτηρ; a daughterling. In the KJV it is rendered: little (young) daughter.
G2366: From θύω (in the sense of blowing) a storm. In the KJV it is rendered: tempest.
G2367: From a derivative of θύω (in the sense of blowing; denoting a certain fragrant tree); made of citron-wood. In the KJV it is rendered: thyine.
G2368: From θυμιάω; an aroma, i.e. fragrant powder burnt in religious service; by implication, the burning itself. In the KJV it is rendered: incense, odour.
G2369: From a derivative of θυμιάω; a place of fumigation, i.e. the alter of incense (in the Temple). In the KJV it is rendered: censer.
G2370: From a derivative of θύω (in the sense of smoking); to fumigate, i.e. offer aromatic fumes. In the KJV it is rendered: burn incense.
G2371: From a presumed compound of θυμός and μάχομαι; to be in a furious fight, i.e. (figuratively) to be exasperated. In the KJV it is rendered: be highly displeased.
G2372: From θύω; passion (as if breathing hard). In the KJV it is rendered: fierceness, indignation, wrath.
G2373: From θυμός; to put in a passion, i.e. enrage. In the KJV it is rendered: be wroth.
G2374: Apparently a primary word (compare "door"); a portal or entrance (the opening or the closure, literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: door, gate.
G2375: From θύρα; a large shield (as door-shaped). In the KJV it is rendered: shield.
G2376: From θύρα; an aperture, i.e. window. In the KJV it is rendered: window.
G2377: From θύρα and ouros (a watcher); a gate- warden. In the KJV it is rendered: that kept the door, porter.
G2378: From θύω; sacrifice (the act or the victim, literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: sacrifice.
G2379: From a derivative of θυσία; a place of sacrifice, i.e. an altar (special or genitive case, literal or figurative). In the KJV it is rendered: altar.
G2380: A primary verb; properly, to rush (breathe hard, blow, smoke), i.e. (by implication) to sacrifice (properly, by fire, but genitive case); by extension to immolate (slaughter for any purpose). In the KJV it is rendered: kill, (do) sacrifice, slay.
G2381: Of Chaldee origin (compare תְאוֹמִים); the twin; Thomas, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Thomas.
G2382: Of uncertain affinity; the chest ("thorax"), i.e. (by implication) a corslet. In the KJV it is rendered: breast-plate.
G2383: Of Hebrew origin (יָאּיר); Jairus (i.e. Jair), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jairus.
G2384: Of Hebrew origin (יַעֲקֹב); Jacob (i.e. Ja`akob), the progenitor of the Israelites; also an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jacob.
G2385: The same as Ἰακώβ Græcized; Jacobus, the name of three Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: James.
G2386: From ἰάομαι; a cure (the effect). In the KJV it is rendered: healing.
G2387: Of Egyptian origin; Jambres, an Egyptian. In the KJV it is rendered: Jambres.
G2388: Probably of Hebrew origin (compare יָנָה); Janna, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Janna.
G2389: Of Egyptian origin; Jannes, an Egyptian. In the KJV it is rendered: Jannes.
G2390: Middle voice of apparently a primary verb; to cure (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: heal, make whole.
G2391: Of Hebrew origin (יָ֫רֶד); Jared (i.e. Jered), an antediluvian. In the KJV it is rendered: Jared.
G2392: From ἰάομαι; curing (the act). In the KJV it is rendered: cure, heal(-ing).
G2393: Probably of foreign origin (see יָשְׁפֵה); "jasper", a gem. In the KJV it is rendered: jasper.
G2394: Future active participle masculine of ἰάομαι; about to cure; Jason, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Jason.
G2395: From ἰάομαι; a physician. In the KJV it is rendered: physician.
G2396: Second person singular imperative active of εἴδω; used as an interjection to denote surprise; lo!. In the KJV it is rendered: behold, lo, see.
G2397: From εἴδω; a sight (comparative figuratively "idea"), i.e. aspect. In the KJV it is rendered: countenance.
G2398: Of uncertain affinity; pertaining to self, i.e. one's own; by implication, private or separate. In the KJV it is rendered: X his acquaintance, when they were alone, apart, aside, due, his (own, proper, several), home, (her, our, thine, your) own (business), private(-ly), proper, severally, their (own).
G2399: From ἴδιος; a private person, i.e. (by implication) an ignoramus (compare "idiot"). In the KJV it is rendered: ignorant, rude, unlearned.
G2400: Second person singular imperative middle voice of εἴδω; used as imperative lo!; --behold, lo, see.
G2401: Of Hebrew origin (אֱדוֹם); Idumæa (i.e. Edom), a region East (and South) of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Idumæa.
G2402: A strengthened form of a primary idos (sweat); perspiration. In the KJV it is rendered: sweat.
G2403: Of Hebrew origin (אּיזָ֫בֶל); Jezabel (i.e. Jezebel), a Tyrian woman (used as a synonym of a termagant or false teacher). In the KJV it is rendered: Jezabel.
G2404: From ἱερός and πόλις; holy city; Hierapolis, a place in Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Hierapolis.
G2405: From ἱερατεύω; priestliness, i.e. the sacerdotal function. In the KJV it is rendered: office of the priesthood, priest's office.
G2406: From ἱερατεύω; the priestly fraternity, i.e. sacerdotal order (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: priesthood.
G2407: Prolongation from ἱερεύς; to be a priest, i.e. perform his functions. In the KJV it is rendered: execute the priest's office.
G2408: Of Hebrew origin (יִרְמְיָה); Hieremias (i.e. Jermijah), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jeremiah.
G2409: From ἱερός; a priest (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: (high) priest.
G2410: Of Hebrew origin (יְרֵחוֹ); Jericho, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Jericho.
G2411: Neuter of ἱερός; a sacred place, i.e. the entire precincts (whereas ναός denotes the central sanctuary itself) of the Temple (at Jerusalem or elsewhere). In the KJV it is rendered: temple.
G2412: From ἱερός and the same as πρέπω; reverent. In the KJV it is rendered: as becometh holiness.
G2413: Of uncertain affinity; sacred. In the KJV it is rendered: holy.
G2414: Of Hebrew origin (יְרוּשָׁלַ֫םִ); Hierosolyma (i.e. Jerushalaim), the capitol of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Jerusalem.
G2415: From Ἱεροσόλυμα; a Hierosolymite, i.e. inhabitant of Hierosolyma. In the KJV it is rendered: of Jerusalem.
G2416: From ἱερόσυλος; to be a temple-robber (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: commit sacrilege.
G2417: From ἱερόν and συλάω; a temple-despoiler. In the KJV it is rendered: robber of churches.
G2418: From a compound of ἱερόν and the base of ἔργον; to be a temple-worker, i.e. officiate as a priest (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: minister.
G2419: Of Hebrew origin (יְרוּשָׁלַ֫םִ); Hierusalem (i.e. Jerushalem), the capitol of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Jerusalem.
G2420: From ἱερός; sacredness, i.e. (by implication) the priestly office. In the KJV it is rendered: priesthood.
G2421: Of Hebrew origin (יִשַׁי); Jessæ (i.e. Jishai), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jesse.
G2422: Of Hebrew origin (יִפְתָּח); Jephthaë (i.e. Jiphtach), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jephthah.
G2423: Of Hebrew origin (יְכָנְיָה); Jechonias (i.e. Jekonjah), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jechonias.
G2424: Of Hebrew origin (יְהוֹשׁ֫וּעַ); Jesus (i.e. Jehoshua), the name of our Lord and two (three) other Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jesus.
G2425: From hiko (hikano or hikneomai, akin to ἥκω) (to arrive); competent (as if coming in season), i.e. ample (in amount) or fit (in character). In the KJV it is rendered: able, + content, enough, good, great, large, long (while), many, meet, much, security, sore, sufficient, worthy.
G2426: From ἱκανός; ability. In the KJV it is rendered: sufficiency.
G2427: From ἱκανός; to enable, i.e. qualify. In the KJV it is rendered: make able (meet).
G2428: From a derivative of the base of ἱκανός (through the idea of approaching for a favor); intreaty. In the KJV it is rendered: supplication.
G2429: Of uncertain affinity; dampness. In the KJV it is rendered: moisture.
G2430: Perhaps from εἰκών; image-like; Iconium, a place in Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Iconium.
G2431: From the same as ἵλεως; propitious or merry ("hilarious"), i.e. prompt or willing. In the KJV it is rendered: cheerful.
G2432: From ἱλαρός; alacrity. In the KJV it is rendered: cheerfulness.
G2433: Middle voice from the same as ἵλεως; to conciliate, i.e. (transitively) to atone for (sin), or (intransitively) be propitious. In the KJV it is rendered: be merciful, make reconciliation for.
G2434: Atonement, i.e. (concretely) an expiator. In the KJV it is rendered: propitiation.
G2435: Neuter of a derivative of ἱλάσκομαι; an expiatory (place or thing), i.e. (concretely) an atoning victim, or (specially) the lid of the Ark (in the Temple). In the KJV it is rendered: mercyseat, propitiation.
G2436: Perhaps from the alternate form of αἱρέομαι; cheerful (as attractive), i.e. propitious; adverbially (by Hebraism) God be gracious!, i.e. (in averting some calamity) far be it. In the KJV it is rendered: be it far, merciful.
G2437: Neuter of an adjective from a name of uncertain derivation; (the) Illyrican (shore), i.e. (as a name itself) Illyricum, a region of Europe. In the KJV it is rendered: Illyricum.
G2438: Perhaps from the same as ἅμα; a strap, i.e. (specially) the tie (of a sandal) or the lash (of a scourge). In the KJV it is rendered: latchet, thong.
G2439: From ἱμάτιον; to dress. In the KJV it is rendered: clothe.
G2440: Neuter of a presumed derivative of ennumi (to put on); a dress (inner or outer). In the KJV it is rendered: apparel, cloke, clothes, garment, raiment, robe, vesture.
G2441: From ἱματίζω; clothing. In the KJV it is rendered: apparel (X -led), array, raiment, vesture.
G2442: Middle voice from himeros (a yearning; of uncertain affinity); to long for. In the KJV it is rendered: be affectionately desirous.
G2443: Probably from the same as the former part of ἑαυτοῦ (through the demonstrative idea; compare ὁ); in order that (denoting the purpose or the result). In the KJV it is rendered: albeit, because, to the intent (that), lest, so as, (so) that, (for) to.
G2444: From ἵνα and τίς; for what reason ?, i.e. why?. In the KJV it is rendered: wherefore, why.
G2445: Of Hebrew origin (יָפוֹ); Joppe (i.e. Japho), a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Joppa.
G2446: Of Hebrew origin (יַרְדֵּן); the Jordanes (i.e. Jarden), a river of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Jordan.
G2447: Perhaps from eimi (to go) or hiemi (to send); rust (as if emitted by metals); also venom (as emitted by serpents). In the KJV it is rendered: poison, rust.
G2448: Of Hebrew origin (יְהוּדָה or perhaps יֻטָּה); Judah (i.e. Jehudah or Juttah), a part of (or place in) Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Judah.
G2449: Feminine of Ἰουδαῖος (with γῆ implied); the Judæan land (i.e. Judæa), a region of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Judæa.
G2450: From Ἰουδαῖος; to become a Judæan, i.e. "Judaize". In the KJV it is rendered: live as the Jews.
G2451: From Ἰουδαῖος; Judaïc, i.e. resembling a Judæan. In the KJV it is rendered: Jewish.
G2452: Adverb from Ἰουδαϊκός; Judaïcally or in a manner resembling a Judæan. In the KJV it is rendered: as do the Jews.
G2453: From Ἰουδά (in the sense of Ἰούδας as a country); Judæan, i.e. belonging to Jehudah. In the KJV it is rendered: Jew(-ess), of Judæa.
G2454: From Ἰουδαΐζω; "Judaism", i.e. the Jewish faith and usages. In the KJV it is rendered: Jews' religion.
G2455: Of Hebrew origin (יְהוּדָה); Judas (i.e. Jehudah), the name of ten Israelites; also of the posterity of one of them and its region. In the KJV it is rendered: Juda(-h, -s); Jude.
G2456: Feminine of the same as Ἰούλιος; Julia, a Christian woman. In the KJV it is rendered: Julia.
G2457: Of Latin origin; Julius, a centurion. In the KJV it is rendered: Julius.
G2458: Of Latin origin; Junias, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Junias.
G2459: Of Latin origin ("just"); Justus, the name of three Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Justus.
G2460: From ἵππος; an equestrian, i.e. member of a cavalry corps. In the KJV it is rendered: horseman.
G2461: Neuter of a derivative of ἵππος; the cavalry force. In the KJV it is rendered: horse(-men).
G2462: Of uncertain affinity; a horse. In the KJV it is rendered: horse.
G2463: Perhaps from ἐρέω (as a symbol of the female messenger of the pagan deities); a rainbow ("iris"). In the KJV it is rendered: rainbow.
G2464: Of Hebrew origin (יִצְחָק); Isaac (i.e. Jitschak), the son of Abraham. In the KJV it is rendered: Isaac.
G2465: From ἴσος and ἄγγελος; like an angel, i.e. angelic. In the KJV it is rendered: equal unto the angels.
G2466: Of Hebrew origin (יִשָּׂשָׂכָר); Isachar (i.e. Jissaskar), a son of Jacob (figuratively, his descendant). In the KJV it is rendered: Issachar.
G2467: Assumed by some as the base of certain irregular forms of εἴδω; to know. In the KJV it is rendered: know.
G2468: Second person imperative present of εἰμί; be thou. In the KJV it is rendered: + agree, be, X give thyself wholly to.
G2469: Of Hebrew origin (probably אּישׁ and קִרְיָא); inhabitant of Kerioth; Iscariotes (i.e. Keriothite), an epithet of Judas the traitor. In the KJV it is rendered: Iscariot.
G2470: Probably from εἴδω (through the idea of seeming); similar (in amount and kind). In the KJV it is rendered: + agree, as much, equal, like.
G2471: Likeness (in condition or proportion); by implication, equity. In the KJV it is rendered: equal(-ity).
G2472: From ἴσος and τιμή; of equal value or honor. In the KJV it is rendered: like precious.
G2473: From ἴσος and ψυχή; of similar spirit. In the KJV it is rendered: likeminded.
G2474: Of Hebrew origin (יִשְׂרָאֵל); Israel (i.e. Jisrael), the adopted name of Jacob, including his descendants (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: Israel.
G2475: From Ἰσραήλ; an "Israelite", i.e. descendant of Israel (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: Israelite.
G2476: A prolonged form of a primary stao stah'-o (of the same meaning, and used for it in certain tenses); to stand (transitively or intransitively), used in various applications (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: abide, appoint, bring, continue, covenant, establish, hold up, lay, present, set (up), stanch, stand (by, forth, still, up).
G2477: From a derivative of εἴδω; to be knowing (learned), i.e. (by implication) to visit for information (interview). In the KJV it is rendered: see.
G2478: From ἰσχύς; forcible (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: boisterous, mighty(-ier), powerful, strong(-er, man), valiant.
G2479: From a derivative of is (force; compare eschon, a form of ἔχω); forcefulness (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: ability, might(-ily), power, strength.
G2480: From ἰσχύς; to have (or exercise) force (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: be able, avail, can do(-not), could, be good, might, prevail, be of strength, be whole, + much work.
G2481: Adverb from ἴσος; likely, i.e. perhaps. In the KJV it is rendered: it may be.
G2482: Probably of foreign origin; Italia, a region of Europe. In the KJV it is rendered: Italy.
G2483: From Ἰταλία; Italic, i.e. belonging to Italia. In the KJV it is rendered: Italian.
G2484: Of Hebrew origin (יְטוּר); Ituræa (i.e. Jetur), a region of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ituræa.
G2485: Diminutive from ἰχθύς; a petty fish. In the KJV it is rendered: little (small) fish.
G2486: Of uncertain affinity; a fish. In the KJV it is rendered: fish.
G2487: From ikneomai (to arrive; compare ἥκω); a track (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: step.
G2488: Of Hebrew origin (יוֹתָם); Joatham (i.e. Jotham), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Joatham.
G2489: Feminine of the same as Ἰωάννης; Joanna, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Joanna.
G2490: A form of Ἰωάννης; Joannas, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Joannas.
G2491: Of Hebrew origin (יוֹחָנָן); Joannes (i.e. Jochanan), the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: John.
G2492: Of Hebrew origin (אּיּוֹב); Job (i.e. Ijob), a patriarch. In the KJV it is rendered: Job.
G2493: Of Hebrew origin (יוֹאֵל); Joel, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Joel.
G2494: Probably for Ἰωάννης or Ἰωνᾶς; Jonan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jonan.
G2495: Of Hebrew origin (יוֹנָה); Jonas (i.e. Jonah), the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Jonas.
G2496: Of Hebrew origin (יוֹרָם); Joram, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Joram.
G2497: Perhaps for Ἰωράμ; Jorim, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jorim.
G2498: Of Hebrew origin (יְהוֹשָׁפָט); Josaphat (i.e. Jehoshaphat), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Josaphat.
G2499: Genitive case of Ἰωσῆς; Jose, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Jose.
G2500: Perhaps for Ἰωσήφ; Joses, the name of two Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Joses.
G2501: Of Hebrew origin (יוֹסֵף); Joseph, the name of seven Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Joseph.
G2502: Of Hebrew origin (יֹאשִׁיָּה); Josias (i.e. Joshiah), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Josias.
G2503: Of Hebrew origin (the tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet); "iota", the name of the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, put (figuratively) for a very small part of anything. In the KJV it is rendered: jot.
G2504: From καί and ἐγώ; so also the dative case kamoi kam-oy', and accusative case kame kam-eh' and (or also, even, etc.) I, (to) me. In the KJV it is rendered: (and, even, even so, so) I (also, in like wise), both me, me also.
G2505: From κατά and the neuter plural of ὅς; according to which things, i.e. just as. In the KJV it is rendered: as.
G2506: From καθαιρέω; demolition; figuratively, extinction. In the KJV it is rendered: destruction, pulling down.
G2507: From κατά and αἱρέομαι (including its alternate); to lower (or with violence) demolish (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: cast (pull, put, take) down, destroy.
G2508: From καθαρός; to cleanse, i.e. (specially) to prune; figuratively, to expiate. In the KJV it is rendered: purge.
G2509: From καθά and περ; exactly as. In the KJV it is rendered: (even, as well) as.
G2510: From κατά and ἅπτομαι; to seize upon. In the KJV it is rendered: fasten on.
G2511: From καθαρός; to cleanse (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: (make) clean(-se), purge, purify.
G2512: From καθαρίζω; a washing off, i.e. (ceremonially) ablution, (morally) expiation. In the KJV it is rendered: cleansing, + purge, purification(-fying).
G2513: Of uncertain affinity; clean (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: clean, clear, pure.
G2514: From καθαρός; cleanness (ceremonially). In the KJV it is rendered: purification.
G2515: From κατά and the same as ἑδραῖος; a bench (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: seat.
G2516: From κατά and the base of ἑδραῖος; to sit down. In the KJV it is rendered: sit.
G2517: From κατά and ἑξῆς; thereafter, i.e. consecutively; as a noun (by ellipsis of noun) a subsequent person or time. In the KJV it is rendered: after(-ward), by (in) order.
G2518: From κατά and heudo (to sleep); to lie down to rest, i.e. (by implication) to fall asleep (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: (be a-)sleep.
G2519: From a compound of κατά and ἡγέομαι; a guide, i.e. (figuratively) a teacher. In the KJV it is rendered: master.
G2520: From κατά and ἥκω; to reach to, i.e. (neuter of present active participle, figuratively as adjective) becoming. In the KJV it is rendered: convenient, fit.
G2521: From κατά; and hemai (to sit; akin to the base of ἑδραῖος); to sit down; figuratively, to remain, reside. In the KJV it is rendered: dwell, sit (by, down).
G2522: From κατά and ἡμέρα; quotidian. In the KJV it is rendered: daily.
G2523: Another (active) form for καθέζομαι; to seat down, i.e. set (figuratively, appoint); intransitively, to sit (down); figuratively, to settle (hover, dwell). In the KJV it is rendered: continue, set, sit (down), tarry.
G2524: From κατά; and hiemi (to send); to lower. In the KJV it is rendered: let down.
G2525: From κατά and ἵστημι; to place down (permanently), i.e. (figuratively) to designate, constitute, convoy. In the KJV it is rendered: appoint, be, conduct, make, ordain, set.
G2526: From κατά and ὅς; according to which thing, i.e. precisely as, in proportion as. In the KJV it is rendered: according to that, (inasmuch) as.
G2527: From κατά and ὅλος; on the whole, i.e. entirely. In the KJV it is rendered: at all.
G2528: From κατά; and ὁπλίζω; to equip fully with armor. In the KJV it is rendered: arm.
G2529: From κατά and ὁράω; to behold fully, i.e. (figuratively) distinctly apprehend. In the KJV it is rendered: clearly see.
G2530: From κατά; and ὅς and τὶς; according to which certain thing, i.e. as far (or inasmuch) as. In the KJV it is rendered: (according, forasmuch) as, because (that).
G2531: From κατά and ὡς; just (or inasmuch) as, that. In the KJV it is rendered: according to, (according, even) as, how, when.
G2532: Apparently, a primary particle, having a copulative and sometimes also a cumulative force; and, also, even, so then, too, etc.; often used in connection (or composition) with other particles or small words. In the KJV it is rendered: and, also, both, but, even, for, if, or, so, that, then, therefore, when, yet.
G2533: Of Chaldee origin; the dell; Caiaphas (i.e. Cajepha), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Caiaphas.
G2534: From καί and γέ; and at least (or even, indeed). In the KJV it is rendered: and, at least.
G2535: Of Hebrew origin (קָ֫יִן); Cain, (i.e. Cajin), the son of Adam. In the KJV it is rendered: Cain.
G2536: Of Hebrew origin (קֵינָן); Cainan (i.e. Kenan), the name of two patriarchs. In the KJV it is rendered: Cainan.
G2537: Of uncertain affinity; new (especially in freshness; while νέος is properly so with respect to age. In the KJV it is rendered: new.
G2538: From καινός; renewal (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: newness.
G2539: From καί and περ; and indeed, i.e. nevertheless or notwithstanding. In the KJV it is rendered: and yet, although.
G2540: Of uncertain affinity; an occasion, i.e. set or proper time. In the KJV it is rendered: X always, opportunity, (convenient, due) season, (due, short, while) time, a while.
G2541: Of Latin origin; Cæsar, a title of the Roman emperor. In the KJV it is rendered: Cæsar.
G2542: From Καῖσαρ; Cæsaria, the name of two places in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Cæsarea.
G2543: From καί and τοί; and yet, i.e. nevertheless. In the KJV it is rendered: although.
G2544: From καίτοι and γέ; and yet indeed, i.e. although really. In the KJV it is rendered: nevertheless, though.
G2545: Apparently a primary verb; to set on fire, i.e. kindle or (by implication) consume. In the KJV it is rendered: burn, light.
G2546: From καί and ἐκεῖ; likewise in that place. In the KJV it is rendered: and there, there (thither) also.
G2547: From καί and ἐκεῖθεν; likewise from that place (or time). In the KJV it is rendered: and afterward (from) (thence), thence also.
G2548: From καί and ἐκεῖνος; likewise that (or those). In the KJV it is rendered: and him (other, them), even he, him also, them (also), (and) they.
G2549: From κακός; badness, i.e. (subjectively) depravity, or (actively) malignity, or (passively) trouble. In the KJV it is rendered: evil, malice(-iousness), naughtiness, wickedness.
G2550: From a compound of κακός and ἦθος; bad character, i.e. (specially) mischievousness. In the KJV it is rendered: malignity.
G2551: From a compound of κακός and λόγος; to revile. In the KJV it is rendered: curse, speak evil of.
G2552: From a compound of ἡμιώριον and πάθος; hardship. In the KJV it is rendered: suffering affliction.
G2553: From the same as κακοπάθεια; to undergo hardship. In the KJV it is rendered: be afflicted, endure afflictions (hardness), suffer trouble.
G2554: From κακοποιός; to be a bad-doer, i.e. (objectively) to injure, or (genitive) to sin. In the KJV it is rendered: do(ing) evil.
G2555: From κακός and ποιέω; a bad-doer; (specially), a criminal. In the KJV it is rendered: evil-doer, malefactor.
G2556: Apparently a primary word; worthless (intrinsically, such; whereas πονηρός properly refers to effects), i.e. (subjectively) depraved, or (objectively) injurious. In the KJV it is rendered: bad, evil, harm, ill, noisome, wicked.
G2557: From κακός and the base of ἔργον; a wrong-doer, i.e. criminal. In the KJV it is rendered: evil-doer, malefactor.
G2558: From a presumed compound of κακός and ἔχω; to maltreat. In the KJV it is rendered: which suffer adversity, torment.
G2559: From κακός; to injure; figuratively, to exasperate. In the KJV it is rendered: make evil affected, entreat evil, harm, hurt, vex.
G2560: From κακός; badly (physically or morally). In the KJV it is rendered: amiss, diseased, evil, grievously, miserably, sick, sore.
G2561: From κακόω; maltreatment. In the KJV it is rendered: affliction.
G2562: Feminine of κάλαμος; a stalk of grain, i.e. (collectively) stubble. In the KJV it is rendered: stubble.
G2563: Of uncertain affinity; a reed (the plant or its stem, or that of a similar plant); by implication, a pen. In the KJV it is rendered: pen, reed.
G2564: Akin to the base of κελεύω; to "call" (properly, aloud, but used in a variety of applications, directly or otherwise). In the KJV it is rendered: bid, call (forth), (whose, whose sur-)name (was (called)).
G2565: From the base of καλλίον and ἐλαία; a cultivated olive tree, i.e. a domesticated or improved one. In the KJV it is rendered: good olive tree.
G2566: Neuter of the (irregular) comparative of καλός; (adverbially) better than many. In the KJV it is rendered: very well.
G2567: From καλός and διδάσκαλος; a teacher of the right. In the KJV it is rendered: teacher of good things.
G2568: Plural of καλός and λιμήν; Good Harbors, i.e. Fairhaven, a bay of Crete. In the KJV it is rendered: fair havens.
G2569: From καλός and ποιέω; to do well, i.e. live virtuously. In the KJV it is rendered: well doing.
G2570: Of uncertain affinity; properly, beautiful, but chiefly (figuratively) good (literally or morally), i.e. valuable or virtuous (for appearance or use, and thus distinguished from ἀγαθός, which is properly intrinsic). In the KJV it is rendered: X better, fair, good(-ly), honest, meet, well, worthy.
G2571: From καλύπτω; a cover, i.e. veil. In the KJV it is rendered: vail.
G2572: Akin to κλέπτω and κρύπτω; to cover up (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: cover, hide.
G2573: Adverb from καλός; well (usually morally). In the KJV it is rendered: (in a) good (place), honestly, + recover, (full) well.
G2574: Of Hebrew origin (גָּמָל); a "camel". In the KJV it is rendered: camel.
G2575: Probably from καίω; a furnace. In the KJV it is rendered: furnace.
G2576: From a compound of κατά and the base of μυστήριον; to shut down, i.e. close the eyes. In the KJV it is rendered: close.
G2577: Apparently a primary verb; properly, to toil, i.e. (by implication) to tire (figuratively, faint, sicken). In the KJV it is rendered: faint, sick, be wearied.
G2578: Apparently a primary verb; to bend. In the KJV it is rendered: bow.
G2579: From καί and ἐάν; and (or even) if. In the KJV it is rendered: and (also) if (so much as), if but, at the least, though, yet.
G2580: Of Hebrew origin (compare קָנָה); Cana, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Cana.
G2581: Of Chaldee origin (compare קַנָּא); zealous; Cananites, an epithet. In the KJV it is rendered: Canaanite (by mistake for a derivative from Chanaan).
G2582: Of foreign origin; Candacè, an Egyptian queen. In the KJV it is rendered: Candace.
G2583: From kane (a straight reed, i.e. rod); a rule ("canon"), i.e. (figuratively) a standard (of faith and practice); by implication, a boundary, i.e. (figuratively) a sphere (of activity). In the KJV it is rendered: line, rule.
G2584: Of Hebrew origin (probably כְּפַר and נַחוּם); Capernaum (i.e. Caphanachum), a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Capernaum.
G2585: From kapelos (a huckster); to retail, i.e. (by implication) to adulterate (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: corrupt.
G2586: Of uncertain affinity; smoke. In the KJV it is rendered: smoke.
G2587: Of foreign origin; Cappadocia, a region of Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Cappadocia.
G2588: Prolonged from a primary kar (Latin cor, "heart"); the heart, i.e. (figuratively) the thoughts or feelings (mind); also (by analogy) the middle. In the KJV it is rendered: (+ broken-)heart(-ed).
G2589: From καρδία and γινώσκω; a heart-knower. In the KJV it is rendered: which knowest the hearts.
G2590: Probably from the base of ἁρπάζω; fruit (as plucked), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: fruit.
G2591: Perhaps for καρπός; Carpus, probably a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Carpus.
G2592: From καρποφόρος; to be fertile (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: be (bear, bring forth) fruit(-ful).
G2593: From καρπός and φέρω; fruitbearing (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: fruitful.
G2594: From a derivative of κράτος (transposed); to be strong, i.e. (figuratively) steadfast (patient). In the KJV it is rendered: endure.
G2595: From karpho (to wither); a dry twig or straw. In the KJV it is rendered: mote.
G2596: A primary particle; (prepositionally) down (in place or time), in varied relations (according to the case (genitive, dative or accusative) with which it is joined). In the KJV it is rendered: about, according as (to), after, against, (when they were) X alone, among, and, X apart, (even, like) as (concerning, pertaining to touching), X aside, at, before, beyond, by, to the charge of, (charita-)bly, concerning, + covered, (dai-)ly, down, every, (+ far more) exceeding, X more excellent, for, from … to, godly, in(-asmuch, divers, every, -to, respect of), … by, after the manner of, + by any means, beyond (out of) measure, X mightily, more, X natural, of (up-)on (X part), out (of every), over against, (+ your) X own, + particularly, so, through(-oughout, -oughout every), thus, (un-)to(-gether, -ward), X uttermost, where(-by), with.
G2597: From κατά and the base of βάσις; to descend (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: come (get, go, step) down, fall (down).
G2598: From κατά and βάλλω; to throw down. In the KJV it is rendered: cast down, lay.
G2599: From κατά and βαρέω; to impose upon. In the KJV it is rendered: burden.
G2600: From καταβαίνω; a declivity. In the KJV it is rendered: descent.
G2601: From κατά and a derivative of the base of βάσις; to cause to go down, i.e. precipitate. In the KJV it is rendered: bring (thrust) down.
G2602: From καταβάλλω; a deposition, i.e. founding; figuratively, conception. In the KJV it is rendered: conceive, foundation.
G2603: From κατά and βραβεύω (in its original sense); to award the price against, i.e. (figuratively) to defraud (of salvation). In the KJV it is rendered: beguile of reward.
G2604: From καταγγέλλω; a proclaimer. In the KJV it is rendered: setter forth.
G2605: From κατά and the base of ἄγγελος; to proclaim, promulgate. In the KJV it is rendered: declare, preach, shew, speak of, teach.
G2606: To laugh down, i.e. deride. In the KJV it is rendered: laugh to scorn.
G2607: From κατά and γινώσκω; to note against, i.e. find fault with. In the KJV it is rendered: blame, condemn.
G2608: From κατά and the base of ῥήγνυμι; to rend in pieces, i.e. crack apart. In the KJV it is rendered: break.
G2609: From κατά and ἄγω; to lead down; specially, to moor a vessel. In the KJV it is rendered: bring (down, forth), (bring to) land, touch.
G2610: From κατά and ἀγωνίζομαι; to struggle against, i.e. (by implication) to overcome. In the KJV it is rendered: subdue.
G2611: From κατά and δέω; to tie down, i.e. bandage (a wound). In the KJV it is rendered: bind up.
G2612: From κατά intensive and δῆλος; manifest. In the KJV it is rendered: far more evident.
G2613: From κατά and a derivative of δίκη; to adjudge against, i.e. pronounce guilty. In the KJV it is rendered: condemn.
G2614: From κατά and διώκω; to hunt down, i.e. search for. In the KJV it is rendered: follow after.
G2615: From κατά and δουλόω; to enslave utterly. In the KJV it is rendered: bring into bondage.
G2616: From κατά and a derivative of δυνάστης; to exercise dominion against, i.e. oppress. In the KJV it is rendered: oppress.
G2617: From κατά and αἰσχύνομαι; to shame down, i.e. disgrace or (by implication) put to the blush. In the KJV it is rendered: confound, dishonour, (be a-, make a-)shame(-d).
G2618: From κατά and καίω; to burn down (to the ground), i.e. consume wholly. In the KJV it is rendered: burn (up, utterly).
G2619: From κατά and καλύπτω; to cover wholly, i.e. veil. In the KJV it is rendered: cover, hide.
G2620: From κατά and καυχάομαι; to exult against (i.e. over). In the KJV it is rendered: boast (against), glory, rejoice against.
G2621: From κατά and κεῖμαι; to lie down, i.e. (by implication) be sick; specially, to recline at a meal. In the KJV it is rendered: keep, lie, sit at meat (down).
G2622: From κατά and κλάω; to break down, i.e. divide. In the KJV it is rendered: break.
G2623: From κατά and κλείω; to shut down (in a dungeon), i.e. incarcerate. In the KJV it is rendered: shut up.
G2624: From κατά and a derivative of a compound of κλῆρος and δίδωμι; to be a giver of lots to each, i.e. (by implication) to apportion an estate. In the KJV it is rendered: divide by lot.
G2625: From κατά and κλίνω; to recline down, i.e. (specially) to take a place at table. In the KJV it is rendered: (make) sit down (at meat).
G2626: From κατά and the base of κλύδων; to dash (wash) down, i.e. (by implication) to deluge. In the KJV it is rendered: overflow.
G2627: From κατακλύζω; an inundation. In the KJV it is rendered: flood.
G2628: From κατά and ἀκολουθέω; to accompany closely. In the KJV it is rendered: follow (after).
G2629: From κατά and κόπτω; to chop down, i.e. mangle. In the KJV it is rendered: cut.
G2630: From κατά and a derivative of κρημνός; to precipitate down. In the KJV it is rendered: cast down headlong.
G2631: From κατακρίνω; an adverse sentence (the verdict). In the KJV it is rendered: condemnation.
G2632: From κατά and κρίνω; to judge against, i.e. sentence. In the KJV it is rendered: condemn, damn.
G2633: From κατακρίνω; sentencing adversely (the act). In the KJV it is rendered: condemn(-ation).
G2634: From κατά and κυριεύω; to lord against, i.e. control, subjugate. In the KJV it is rendered: exercise dominion over (lordship), be lord over, overcome.
G2635: From κατάλαλος; to be a traducer, i.e. to slander. In the KJV it is rendered: speak against (evil of).
G2636: From κατάλαλος; defamation. In the KJV it is rendered: backbiting, evil speaking.
G2637: From κατά and the base of λαλέω; talkative against, i.e. a slanderer. In the KJV it is rendered: backbiter.
G2638: From κατά and λαμβάνω; to take eagerly, i.e. seize, possess, etc. (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: apprehend, attain, come upon, comprehend, find, obtain, perceive, (over-)take.
G2639: From κατά and λέγω (in its original meaning); to lay down, i.e. (figuratively) to enrol. In the KJV it is rendered: take into the number.
G2640: From καταλείπω; a remainder, i.e. (by implication) a few. In the KJV it is rendered: remnant.
G2641: From κατά and λείπω; to leave down, i.e. behind; by implication, to abandon, have remaining. In the KJV it is rendered: forsake, leave, reserve.
G2642: From κατά and λιθάζω; to stone down, i.e. to death. In the KJV it is rendered: stone.
G2643: From καταλλάσσω; exchange (figuratively, adjustment), i.e. restoration to (the divine) favor. In the KJV it is rendered: atonement, reconciliation(-ing).
G2644: From κατά and ἀλλάσσω; to change mutually, i.e. (figuratively) to compound a difference. In the KJV it is rendered: reconcile.
G2645: From κατά and λοιποί; left down (behind), i.e remaining (plural the rest). In the KJV it is rendered: residue.
G2646: From καταλύω; properly, a dissolution (breaking up of a journey), i.e. (by implication) a lodging-place. In the KJV it is rendered: guestchamber, inn.
G2647: From κατά and λύω; to loosen down (disintegrate), i.e. (by implication) to demolish (literally or figuratively); specially (compare κατάλυμα) to halt for the night. In the KJV it is rendered: destroy, dissolve, be guest, lodge, come to nought, overthrow, throw down.
G2648: From κατά and μανθάνω; to learn thoroughly, i.e. (by implication) to note carefully. In the KJV it is rendered: consider.
G2649: From κατά and μαρτυρέω; to testify against. In the KJV it is rendered: witness against.
G2650: From κατά and μένω; to stay fully, i.e. reside. In the KJV it is rendered: abide.
G2651: From κατά and accusative case plural feminine of μόνος (with χώρα implied); according to sole places, i.e. (adverbially) separately. In the KJV it is rendered: alone.
G2652: From κατά (intensive) and ἀνάθεμα; an imprecation. In the KJV it is rendered: curse.
G2653: From κατά (intensive) and ἀναθεματίζω; to imprecate. In the KJV it is rendered: curse.
G2654: From κατά and ἀναλίσκω; to consume utterly. In the KJV it is rendered: consume.
G2655: From κατά and narkao (to be numb); to grow utterly torpid, i.e. (by implication) slothful (figuratively, expensive). In the KJV it is rendered: be burdensome (chargeable).
G2656: From κατά and νεύω; to nod down (towards), i.e. (by analogy) to make signs to. In the KJV it is rendered: beckon.
G2657: From κατά and νοιέω; to observe fully. In the KJV it is rendered: behold, consider, discover, perceive.
G2658: From κατά and a derivative of ἀντί; to meet against, i.e. arrive at (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: attain, come.
G2659: From κατανύσσω; a prickling (sensation, as of the limbs asleep), i.e. (by implication, (perhaps by some confusion with νεύω or even with νύξ)) stupor (lethargy). In the KJV it is rendered: slumber.
G2660: From κατά and νύσσω; to pierce thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively) to agitate violently ("sting to the quick"). In the KJV it is rendered: prick.
G2661: From κατά and ἀξιόω; to deem entirely deserving. In the KJV it is rendered: (ac-)count worthy.
G2662: From κατά and πατέω; to trample down; figuratively, to reject with disdain. In the KJV it is rendered: trample, tread (down, underfoot).
G2663: From καταπαύω; reposing down, i.e. (by Hebraism) abode. In the KJV it is rendered: rest.
G2664: From κατά and παύω; to settle down, i.e. (literally) to colonize, or (figuratively) to (cause to) desist. In the KJV it is rendered: cease, (give) rest(-rain).
G2665: From a compound of κατά and a congener of πέτομαι; something spread thoroughly, i.e. (specially) the door screen (to the Most Holy Place) in the Jewish Temple. In the KJV it is rendered: vail.
G2666: From κατά and πίνω; to drink down, i.e. gulp entire (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: devour, drown, swallow (up).
G2667: From κατά and πίπτω; to fall down. In the KJV it is rendered: fall (down).
G2668: From κατά and πλέω; to sail down upon a place, i.e. to land at. In the KJV it is rendered: arrive.
G2669: From κατά and a derivative of πόνος; to labor down, i.e. wear with toil (figuratively, harass). In the KJV it is rendered: oppress, vex.
G2670: From κατά and a derivative of the same as Πόντος; to plunge down, i.e. submerge. In the KJV it is rendered: drown, sink.
G2671: From κατά (intensive) and ἀρά; imprecation, execration. In the KJV it is rendered: curse(-d, ing).
G2672: Middle voice from κατάρα; to execrate; by analogy, to doom. In the KJV it is rendered: curse.
G2673: From κατά and ἀργέω; to be (render) entirely idle (useless), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: abolish, cease, cumber, deliver, destroy, do away, become (make) of no (none, without) effect, fail, loose, bring (come) to nought, put away (down), vanish away, make void.
G2674: From κατά and ἀριθμέω; to reckon among. In the KJV it is rendered: number with.
G2675: From κατά and a derivative of ἄρτιος; to complete thoroughly, i.e. repair (literally or figuratively) or adjust. In the KJV it is rendered: fit, frame, mend, (make) perfect(-ly join together), prepare, restore.
G2676: From καταρτίζω; thorough equipment (subjectively). In the KJV it is rendered: perfection.
G2677: From καταρτίζω; complete furnishing (objectively). In the KJV it is rendered: perfecting.
G2678: From κατά and σείω; to sway downward, i.e. make a signal. In the KJV it is rendered: beckon.
G2679: From κατά and σκάπτω; to undermine, i.e. (by implication) destroy. In the KJV it is rendered: dig down, ruin.
G2680: From κατά and a derivative of σκεῦος; to prepare thoroughly (properly, by external equipment; whereas ἑτοιμάζω refers rather to internal fitness); by implication, to construct, create. In the KJV it is rendered: build, make, ordain, prepare.
G2681: From κατά and σκηνόω; to camp down, i.e. haunt; figuratively, to remain. In the KJV it is rendered: lodge, rest.
G2682: From κατασκηνόω; an encamping, i.e. (figuratively) a perch. In the KJV it is rendered: nest.
G2683: From κατά and a derivative of σκιά; to overshade, i.e. cover. In the KJV it is rendered: shadow.
G2684: From κατάσκοπος; to be a sentinel, i.e. to inspect insidiously. In the KJV it is rendered: spy out.
G2685: From κατά (intensive) and σκοπός (in the sense of a watcher); a reconnoiterer. In the KJV it is rendered: spy.
G2686: Middle voice from κατά and σοφίζω; to be crafty against, i.e. circumvent. In the KJV it is rendered: deal subtilly with.
G2687: From κατά and στέλλω; to put down, i.e. quell. In the KJV it is rendered: appease, quiet.
G2688: From καθίστημι; properly, a position or condition, i.e. (subjectively) demeanor. In the KJV it is rendered: behaviour.
G2689: From καταστέλλω; a deposit, i.e. (specially) costume. In the KJV it is rendered: apparel.
G2690: From κατά and στρέφω; to turn upside down, i.e. upset. In the KJV it is rendered: overthrow.
G2691: From κατά and στρηνιάω; to become voluptuous against. In the KJV it is rendered: begin to wax wanton against.
G2692: From καταστρέφω; an overturn ("catastrophe"), i.e. demolition; figuratively, apostasy. In the KJV it is rendered: overthrow, subverting.
G2693: From κατά and στρώννυμι; to strew down, i.e. (by implication) to prostrate (slay). In the KJV it is rendered: overthrow.
G2694: From κατά and σύρω; to drag down, i.e. arrest judicially. In the KJV it is rendered: hale.
G2695: From κατά and σφάζω; to kill down, i.e. slaughter. In the KJV it is rendered: slay.
G2696: From κατά and σφραγίζω; to seal closely. In the KJV it is rendered: seal.
