G3340: From μετά and νοιέω; to think differently or afterwards, i.e. reconsider (morally, feel compunction). In the KJV it is rendered: repent.
G3341: From μετανοέω; (subjectively) compunction (for guilt, including reformation); by implication, reversal (of (another's) decision). In the KJV it is rendered: repentance.
G3342: From μετά and a form of σύν; betwixt (of place or person); (of time) as adjective, intervening, or (by implication) adjoining. In the KJV it is rendered: between, mean while, next.
G3343: From μετά and πέμπω; to send from elsewhere, i.e. (middle voice) to summon or invite. In the KJV it is rendered: call (send) for.
G3344: From μετά and στρέφω; to turn across, i.e. transmute or (figuratively) corrupt. In the KJV it is rendered: pervert, turn.
G3345: From μετά and a derivative of σχῆμα; to transfigure or disguise; figuratively, to apply (by accommodation). In the KJV it is rendered: transfer, transform (self).
G3346: From μετά and τίθημι; to transfer, i.e. (literally) transport, (by implication) exchange, (reflexively) change sides, or (figuratively) pervert. In the KJV it is rendered: carry over, change, remove, translate, turn.
G3347: From μετά and ἔπειτα; thereafter. In the KJV it is rendered: afterward.
G3348: From μετά and ἔχω; to share or participate; by implication, belong to, eat (or drink). In the KJV it is rendered: be partaker, pertain, take part, use.
G3349: From a compound of μετά and a collateral form of αἴρω or perhaps rather ἀήρ (compare "meteor"); to raise in mid-air, i.e. (figuratively) suspend (passively, fluctuate or be anxious). In the KJV it is rendered: be of doubtful mind.
G3350: From a derivative of a compound of μετά and οἶκος; a change of abode, i.e. (specially), expatriation. In the KJV it is rendered: X brought, carried(-ying) away (in-)to.
G3351: From the same as μετοικεσία; to transfer as a settler or captive, i.e colonize or exile. In the KJV it is rendered: carry away, remove into.
G3352: From μετέχω; participation, i.e. intercourse. In the KJV it is rendered: fellowship.
G3353: From μετέχω; participant, i.e. (as noun) a sharer; by implication, an associate. In the KJV it is rendered: fellow, partaker, partner.
G3354: From μέτρον; to measure (i.e. ascertain in size by a fixed standard); by implication, to admeasure (i.e. allot by rule); figuratively, to estimate. In the KJV it is rendered: measure, mete.
G3355: From μετρέω; a measurer, i.e. (specially), a certain standard measure of capacity for liquids. In the KJV it is rendered: firkin.
G3356: From a compound of the base of μετρίως and πάθος; to be moderate in passion, i.e. gentle (to treat indulgently). In the KJV it is rendered: have compassion.
G3357: Adverb from a derivative of μέτρον; moderately, i.e. slightly. In the KJV it is rendered: a little.
G3358: An apparently primary word; a measure ("metre"), literally or figuratively; by implication, a limited portion (degree). In the KJV it is rendered: measure.
G3359: From μετά and ops (the face); the forehead (as opposite the countenance). In the KJV it is rendered: forehead.
G3360: Or mechris from μῆκος; as far as, i.e. up to a certain point (as a preposition, of extent (denoting the terminus, whereas ἄχρι refers especially to the space of time or place intervening) or conjunction). In the KJV it is rendered: till, (un-)to, until.
G3361: A primary particle of qualified negation (whereas οὐ expresses an absolute denial); (adverb) not, (conjunction) lest; also (as an interrogative implying a negative answer (whereas οὐ expects an affirmative one)) whether. In the KJV it is rendered: any but (that), X forbear, + God forbid, + lack, lest, neither, never, no (X wise in), none, nor, (can-)not, nothing, that not, un(-taken), without.
G3362: I.e. ἐάν and μή; if not, i.e. unless. In the KJV it is rendered: X before, but, except, if, no, (if, + whosoever) not.
G3363: I.e. ἵνα and μή; in order (or so) that not. In the KJV it is rendered: albeit not, lest, that, no(-t, (-thing)).
G3364: I.e. οὐ and μή; a double negative strengthening the denial; not at all. In the KJV it is rendered: any more, at all, by any (no) means, neither, never, no (at all), in no case (wise), nor ever, not (at all, in any wise).
G3365: Adverb from a compound of μή and amos (somebody); by no means. In the KJV it is rendered: not so.
G3366: From μή and δέ; but not, not even; in a continued negation, nor. In the KJV it is rendered: neither, nor (yet), (no) not (once, so much as).
G3367: Including the irregular feminine medemia, and the neuter meden from μή and εἷς; not even one (man, woman, thing). In the KJV it is rendered: any (man, thing), no (man), none, not (at all, any man, a whit), nothing, + without delay.
G3368: From μηδέ and ποτέ; not even ever. In the KJV it is rendered: never.
G3369: From μηδέ and -πω; not even yet. In the KJV it is rendered: not yet.
G3370: Of foreign origin (compare NONE); a Median, or inhabitant of Media. In the KJV it is rendered: Mede.
G3371: From μή and ἔτι; no further. In the KJV it is rendered: any longer, (not) henceforth, hereafter, no henceforward (longer, more, soon), not any more.
G3372: Probably akin to μέγας; length (literally or figuratively) length.
G3373: From μῆκος; to lengthen, i.e. (middle voice) to enlarge. In the KJV it is rendered: grow up.
G3374: From melon (a sheep); a sheep-skin. In the KJV it is rendered: sheepskin.
G3375: A stronger form of μέν; a particle of affirmation (only with ἦ); assuredly. In the KJV it is rendered: + surely.
G3376: A primary word; a month. In the KJV it is rendered: month.
G3377: Probably from the same base as μασσάομαι and μνάομαι (i.e. mao, to strive); to disclose (through the idea of mental effort and thus calling to mind), i.e. report, declare, intimate. In the KJV it is rendered: shew, tell.
G3378: I.e. μή and οὐ; as interrogative and negative, is it not that?. In the KJV it is rendered: neither (followed by no), + never, not.
G3379: Or me pote from μή and ποτέ; not ever; also if (or lest) ever (or perhaps). In the KJV it is rendered: if peradventure, lest (at any time, haply), not at all, whether or not.
G3380: From μή and -πω; not yet. In the KJV it is rendered: not yet.
G3381: Or me pos from μή and -πώς; lest somehow. In the KJV it is rendered: lest (by any means, by some means, haply, perhaps).
G3382: Perhaps a primary word; a thigh. In the KJV it is rendered: thigh.
G3383: From μή and τέ; not too, i.e. (in continued negation) neither or nor; also, not even. In the KJV it is rendered: neither, (n-)or, so as much.
G3384: Apparently a primary word; a "mother" (literally or figuratively, immediate or remote). In the KJV it is rendered: mother.
G3385: From μή and the neuter of τὶς; whether at all. In the KJV it is rendered: not (the particle usually not expressed, except by the form of the question).
G3386: From μήτι and γέ; not at all then, i.e. not to say (the rather still). In the KJV it is rendered: how much more.
G3387: Or me tis from μή and τὶς; whether any. In the KJV it is rendered: any (sometimes unexpressed except by the simple interrogative form of the sentence).
G3388: From μήτηρ; the matrix. In the KJV it is rendered: womb.
G3389: From μήτηρ and the base of ἅλων; a mother-thresher, i.e. matricide. In the KJV it is rendered: murderer of mothers.
G3390: From μήτηρ and πόλις; a mother city, i.e. "metropolis". In the KJV it is rendered: chiefest city.
G3391: Irregular feminine of εἷς; one or first. In the KJV it is rendered: a (certain), + agree, first, one, X other.
G3392: Perhaps a primary verb; to sully or taint, i.e. contaminate (ceremonially or morally). In the KJV it is rendered: defile.
G3393: From μιαίνω ("miasma"); (morally) foulness (properly, the effect). In the KJV it is rendered: pollution.
G3394: From μιαίνω; (morally) contamination (properly, the act). In the KJV it is rendered: uncleanness.
G3395: From μίγνυμι; a compound. In the KJV it is rendered: mixture.
G3396: A primary verb; to mix. In the KJV it is rendered: mingle.
G3397: Masculine or neuter singular of μικρός (as noun); a small space of time or degree. In the KJV it is rendered: a (little) (while).
G3398: Including the comparative mikroteros apparently a primary word; small (in size, quantity, number or (figuratively) dignity). In the KJV it is rendered: least, less, little, small.
G3399: Of uncertain origin; Miletus, a city of Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Miletus.
G3400: Of Latin origin; a thousand paces, i.e. a "mile". In the KJV it is rendered: mile.
G3401: Middle voice from mimos (a "mimic"); to imitate. In the KJV it is rendered: follow.
G3402: From μιμέομαι; an imitator. In the KJV it is rendered: follower.
G3403: A prolonged form of μνάομαι (from which some of the tenses are borrowed); to remind, i.e. (middle voice) to recall to mind. In the KJV it is rendered: be mindful, remember.
G3404: From a primary misos (hatred); to detest (especially to persecute); by extension, to love less. In the KJV it is rendered: hate(-ful).
G3405: From μισθαποδότης; requital (good or bad). In the KJV it is rendered: recompence of reward.
G3406: From μισθόω and ἀποδίδωμι; a renumerator. In the KJV it is rendered: rewarder.
G3407: From μισθός; a wage-earner. In the KJV it is rendered: hired servant.
G3408: Apparently a primary word; pay for service (literally or figuratively), good or bad. In the KJV it is rendered: hire, reward, wages.
G3409: From μισθός; to let out for wages, i.e. (middle voice) to hire. In the KJV it is rendered: hire.
G3410: From μισθόω; a rented building. In the KJV it is rendered: hired house.
G3411: From μισθόω; a wage-worker (good or bad). In the KJV it is rendered: hired servant, hireling.
G3412: For mutilene (abounding in shellfish); Mitylene (or Mytilene), a town on the island of Lesbos. In the KJV it is rendered: Mitylene.
G3413: Of Hebrew origin (מִיכָאֵל); Michael, an archangel. In the KJV it is rendered: Michael.
G3414: Of Latin origin; a mna (i.e. mina), a certain weight. In the KJV it is rendered: pound.
G3415: Middle voice of a derivative of μένω or perhaps of the base of μασσάομαι (through the idea of fixture in the mind or of mental grasp); to bear in mind, i.e. recollect; by implication, to reward or punish. In the KJV it is rendered: be mindful, remember, come (have) in remembrance.
G3416: Of uncertain origin; Mnason, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Mnason.
G3417: From μνάομαι or μιμνήσκω; recollection; by implication, recital. In the KJV it is rendered: mention, remembrance.
G3418: From μνάομαι; a memorial, i.e. sepulchral monument (burial-place). In the KJV it is rendered: grave, sepulchre, tomb.
G3419: From μνήμη; a remembrance, i.e. cenotaph (place of interment). In the KJV it is rendered: grave, sepulchre, tomb.
G3420: From μιμνήσκω; memory. In the KJV it is rendered: remembrance.
G3421: From a derivative of μνήμη; to exercise memory, i.e. recollect; by implication, to punish; also to rehearse. In the KJV it is rendered: make mention; be mindful, remember.
G3422: From μνημονεύω; a reminder (memorandum), i.e. record. In the KJV it is rendered: memorial.
G3423: From a derivative of μνάομαι; to give a souvenir (engagement present), i.e. betroth. In the KJV it is rendered: espouse.
G3424: From μόγις and λαλέω; hardly talking, i.e. dumb (tongue-tied). In the KJV it is rendered: having an impediment in his speech.
G3425: Adverb from a primary mogos (toil); with difficulty. In the KJV it is rendered: hardly.
G3426: Of Latin origin; a modius, i.e. certain measure for things dry (the quantity or the utensil). In the KJV it is rendered: bushel.
G3427: The simpler form of ἐμοί; to me. In the KJV it is rendered: I, me, mine, my.
G3428: A prolonged form of the feminine of μοιχός; an adulteress (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: adulteress(-ous, -y).
G3429: From μοιχός; (middle voice) to commit adultery. In the KJV it is rendered: commit adultery.
G3430: From μοιχεύω; adultery. In the KJV it is rendered: adultery.
G3431: From μοιχός; to commit adultery. In the KJV it is rendered: commit adultery.
G3432: Perhaps a primary word; a (male) paramour; figuratively, apostate. In the KJV it is rendered: adulterer.
G3433: Probably by variation for μόγις; with difficulty. In the KJV it is rendered: hardly, scarce(-ly), + with much work.
G3434: Of Hebrew origin (מֹ֫לֶך); Moloch (i.e. Molek), an idol. In the KJV it is rendered: Moloch.
G3435: Probably from μέλας; to soil (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: defile.
G3436: From μολύνω; a stain; i.e. (figuratively) immorality. In the KJV it is rendered: filthiness.
G3437: From μέμφομαι; blame, i.e. (by implication), a fault. In the KJV it is rendered: quarrel.
G3438: From μένω; a staying, i.e. residence (the act or the place). In the KJV it is rendered: abode, mansion.
G3439: From μόνος and γίνομαι; only-born, i.e. sole. In the KJV it is rendered: only (begotten, child).
G3440: Neuter of μόνος as adverb; merely. In the KJV it is rendered: alone, but, only.
G3441: Probably from μένω; remaining, i.e. sole or single; by implication, mere. In the KJV it is rendered: alone, only, by themselves.
G3442: From μόνος and ὀφθαλμός; one-eyed. In the KJV it is rendered: with one eye.
G3443: From μόνος; to isolate, i.e. bereave. In the KJV it is rendered: be desolate.
G3444: Perhaps from the base of μέρος (through the idea of adjustment of parts); shape; figuratively, nature. In the KJV it is rendered: form.
G3445: From the same as μορφή; to fashion (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: form.
G3446: From μορφόω; formation, i.e. (by implication), appearance (semblance or (concretely) formula). In the KJV it is rendered: form.
G3447: From μόσχος and ποιέω; to fabricate the image of a bullock. In the KJV it is rendered: make a calf.
G3448: Probably strengthened for oschos (a shoot); a young bullock. In the KJV it is rendered: calf.
G3449: From the base of μόγις; toil, i.e. (by implication) sadness. In the KJV it is rendered: painfulness, travail.
G3450: The simpler form of ἐμοῦ; of me. In the KJV it is rendered: I, me, mine (own), my.
G3451: From Mousa (a Muse); "musical", i.e. (as noun) a minstrel. In the KJV it is rendered: musician.
G3452: Perhaps a primary word; the marrow. In the KJV it is rendered: marrow.
G3453: From the base of μυστήριον; to initiate, i.e. (by implication) to teach. In the KJV it is rendered: instruct.
G3454: Perhaps from the same as μυέω (through the idea of tuition); a tale, i.e. fiction ("myth"). In the KJV it is rendered: fable.
G3455: From a presumed derivative of muzo ( to "moo"); to bellow (roar). In the KJV it is rendered: roar.
G3456: From a derivative of the base of μυκάομαι (meaning snout, as that whence lowing proceeds); to make mouths at, i.e. ridicule. In the KJV it is rendered: mock.
G3457: From μύλος; belonging to a mill. In the KJV it is rendered: mill(-stone).
G3458: Probably ultimately from the base of μόλις (through the idea of hardship); a "mill", i.e. (by implication), a grinder (millstone). In the KJV it is rendered: millstone.
G3459: From μύλος; a mill-house. In the KJV it is rendered: mill.
G3460: Of uncertain derivation; Myra, a place in Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Myra.
G3461: From μύριοι; a ten-thousand; by extension, a "myriad" or indefinite number. In the KJV it is rendered: ten thousand.
G3462: From μύρον; to apply (perfumed) unguent to. In the KJV it is rendered: anoint.
G3463: Plural of an apparently primary word (properly, meaning very many); ten thousand; by extension, innumerably many. In the KJV it is rendered: ten thousand.
G3464: Probably of foreign origin (compare מֹר, σμύρνα); "myrrh", i.e. (by implication) perfumed oil. In the KJV it is rendered: ointment.
G3465: Of uncertain origin; Mysia, a region of Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Mysia.
G3466: From a derivative of muo (to shut the mouth); a secret or "mystery" (through the idea of silence imposed by initiation into religious rites). In the KJV it is rendered: mystery.
G3467: From a compound of the base of μυστήριον and ops (the face; from ὀπτάνομαι); to shut the eyes, i.e. blink (see indistinctly). In the KJV it is rendered: cannot see far off.
G3468: From molos ("moil"; probably akin to the base of μόλις) and probably ops (the face; from ὀπτάνομαι); a mole ("black eye") or blow-mark. In the KJV it is rendered: stripe.
G3469: From μῶμος; to carp at, i.e. censure (discredit). In the KJV it is rendered: blame.
G3470: Perhaps from μέμφομαι; a flaw or blot, i.e. (figuratively) disgraceful person. In the KJV it is rendered: blemish.
G3471: From μωρός; to become insipid; figuratively, to make (passively, act) as a simpleton. In the KJV it is rendered: become fool, make foolish, lose savour.
G3472: From μωρός; silliness, i.e. absurdity. In the KJV it is rendered: foolishness.
G3473: From a compound of μωρός and λέγω; silly talk, i.e. buffoonery. In the KJV it is rendered: foolish talking.
G3474: Probably from the base of μυστήριον; dull or stupid (as if shut up), i.e. heedless, (morally) blockhead, (apparently) absurd. In the KJV it is rendered: fool(-ish, X -ishness).
G3475: Or Moses, or Mouses of Hebrew origin; (מֹשֶׁה); Moseus, Moses, or Mouses (i.e. Mosheh), the Hebrew lawgiver. In the KJV it is rendered: Moses.
G3476: Of Hebrew origin (נַחְשׁוֹן); Naasson (i.e. Nachshon), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Naasson.
G3477: Probably of Hebrew origin (compare נֹ֫גַהּ); Nangæ (i.e. perhaps Nogach), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Nagge.
G3478: Or Nazaret; of uncertain derivation; Nazareth or Nazaret, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Nazareth.
G3479: From Ναζαρέθ; a Nazarene, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth. In the KJV it is rendered: of Nazareth.
G3480: From Ναζαρέθ; a Nazoræan, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth; by extension, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Nazarene, of Nazareth.
G3481: Of Hebrew origin (נָתָן); Nathan, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Nathan.
G3482: Of Hebrew origin (נְתַנְאֵל); Nathanaël (i.e. Nathanel), an Israelite and Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Nathanael.
G3483: A primary particle of strong affirmation; yes. In the KJV it is rendered: even so, surely, truth, verily, yea, yes.
G3484: Probably of Hebrew origin (compare נְאוֹת); Nain, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Nain.
G3485: From a primary naio (to dwell); a fane, shrine, temple. In the KJV it is rendered: shrine, temple.
G3486: Of Hebrew origin (נַחוּם); Naum (i.e. Nachum), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Naum.
G3487: Of foreign origin (compare נֵרְדְּ); "nard". In the KJV it is rendered: (spike-)nard.
G3488: A flower of the same name, from narke (stupefaction, as a "narcotic"); Narcissus, a Roman. In the KJV it is rendered: Narcissus.
G3489: From a compound of ναῦς and ἄγω; to be shipwrecked (stranded, "navigate"), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: make (suffer) shipwreck.
G3490: From ναῦς and κλῆρος ("clerk"); a captain. In the KJV it is rendered: owner of a ship.
G3491: From nao or neo (to float); a boat (of any size). In the KJV it is rendered: ship.
G3492: From ναῦς; a boatman, i.e. seaman. In the KJV it is rendered: sailor, shipman.
G3493: Of Hebrew origin (נָחוֹר); Nachor, the grandfather of Abraham. In the KJV it is rendered: Nachor.
G3494: From a derivative of νέος; a youth (up to about forty years). In the KJV it is rendered: young man.
G3495: From the same as νεανίας; a youth (under forty). In the KJV it is rendered: young man.
G3496: From νέος and πόλις; new town; Neapolis, a place in Macedonia. In the KJV it is rendered: Neapolis.
G3497: Of Hebrew origin (נַעֲמָן); Neeman (i.e. Naaman), a Syrian. In the KJV it is rendered: Naaman.
G3498: From an apparently primary nekus (a corpse); dead (literally or figuratively; also as noun). In the KJV it is rendered: dead.
G3499: From νεκρός; to deaden, i.e. (figuratively) to subdue. In the KJV it is rendered: be dead, mortify.
G3500: From νεκρόω; decease; figuratively, impotency. In the KJV it is rendered: deadness, dying.
G3501: Including the comparative neoteros neh-o'-ter-os; a primary word; "new", i.e. (of persons) youthful, or (of things) fresh; figuratively, regenerate. In the KJV it is rendered: new, young.
G3502: From νέος; a youngling (nestling). In the KJV it is rendered: young.
G3503: From νέος; newness, i.e. youthfulness. In the KJV it is rendered: youth.
G3504: From νέος and a derivative of φύω; newly planted, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert ("neophyte"). In the KJV it is rendered: novice.
G3505: Of Latin origin; Neron (i.e. Nero), a Roman emperor. In the KJV it is rendered: Nero.
G3506: Apparently a primary verb; to "nod", i.e. (by analogy), signal. In the KJV it is rendered: beckon.
G3507: From νέφος; properly, cloudiness, i.e. (concretely) a cloud. In the KJV it is rendered: cloud.
G3508: Of Hebrew origin (נַפְתָּלִי); Nephthaleim (i.e. Naphthali), a tribe in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Nephthalim.
G3509: Apparently a primary word; a cloud. In the KJV it is rendered: cloud.
G3510: Of uncertain affinity; a kidney (plural), i.e. (figuratively) the inmost mind. In the KJV it is rendered: reins.
G3511: From a form of ναός and koreo (to sweep); a temple-servant, i.e. (by implication) a votary. In the KJV it is rendered: worshipper.
G3512: From the comparative of νέος; appertaining to younger persons, i.e. juvenile. In the KJV it is rendered: youthful.
G3513: Probably an intensive form of ναί; a particle of attestation (accompanied by the object invoked or appealed to in confirmation); as sure as. In the KJV it is rendered: I protest by.
G3514: From neo (of like meaning); to spin. In the KJV it is rendered: spin.
G3515: From νήπιος; to act as a babe, i.e. (figuratively) innocently. In the KJV it is rendered: be a child.
G3516: From an obsolete particle ne- (implying negation) and ἔπος; not speaking, i.e. an infant (minor); figuratively, a simple-minded person, an immature Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: babe, child (+ -ish).
G3517: Apparently from a derivative of the base of ναῦς (meaning wet); Nereus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Nereus.
G3518: Of Hebrew origin (נֵרִיָּה); Neri (i.e. Nerijah), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Neri.
G3519: Diminutive of νῆσος; an islet. In the KJV it is rendered: island.
G3520: Probably from the base of ναῦς; an island. In the KJV it is rendered: island, isle.
G3521: From νηστεύω; abstinence (from lack of food, or voluntary and religious); specially, the fast of the Day of Atonement. In the KJV it is rendered: fast(-ing).
G3522: From νῆστις; to abstain from food (religiously). In the KJV it is rendered: fast.
G3523: From the inseparable negative particle ne- (not) and ἐσθίω; not eating, i.e. abstinent from food (religiously). In the KJV it is rendered: fasting.
G3524: Or nephalios from νήφω; sober, i.e. (figuratively) circumspect. In the KJV it is rendered: sober.
G3525: Of uncertain affinity; to abstain from wine (keep sober), i.e. (figuratively) be discreet. In the KJV it is rendered: be sober, watch.
G3526: Of Latin origin; black; Niger, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Niger.
G3527: Probably from νικάω; victorious; Nicanor, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Nicanor.
G3528: From νίκη; to subdue (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: conquer, overcome, prevail, get the victory.
G3529: Apparently a primary word; conquest (abstractly), i.e. (figuratively) the means of success. In the KJV it is rendered: victory.
G3530: From νῖκος and δῆμος; victorious among his people; Nicodemus, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Nicodemus.
G3531: From Νικόλαος; a Nicolaite, i.e. adherent of Nicolaus. In the KJV it is rendered: Nicolaitane.
G3532: From νῖκος and Λαοδικεύς; victorious over the people; Nicolaus, a heretic. In the KJV it is rendered: Nicolaus.
G3533: From νῖκος and πόλις; victorious city; Nicopolis, a place in Macedonia. In the KJV it is rendered: Nicopolis.
G3534: From νίκη; a conquest (concretely), i.e. (by implication) triumph. In the KJV it is rendered: victory.
G3535: Of Hebrew origin (NONE); Ninevi (i.e. Nineveh), the capital of Assyria. In the KJV it is rendered: Nineve.
G3536: From Νινευΐ; a Ninevite, i.e. inhabitant of Nineveh. In the KJV it is rendered: of Nineve, Ninevite.
G3537: From νίπτω; a ewer. In the KJV it is rendered: bason.
G3538: To cleanse (especially the hands or the feet or the face); ceremonially, to perform ablution. In the KJV it is rendered: wash.
G3539: From νοῦς; to exercise the mind (observe), i.e. (figuratively) to comprehend, heed. In the KJV it is rendered: consider, perceive, think, understand.
G3540: From νοιέω; a perception, i.e. purpose, or (by implication) the intellect, disposition, itself. In the KJV it is rendered: device, mind, thought.
G3541: Of uncertain affinity; a spurious or illegitimate son. In the KJV it is rendered: bastard.
G3542: Feminine from the same as νόμος; pasture, i.e. (the act) feeding (figuratively, spreading of a gangrene), or (the food) pasturage. In the KJV it is rendered: X eat, pasture.
G3543: From νόμος; properly, to do by law (usage), i.e. to accustom (passively, be usual); by extension, to deem or regard. In the KJV it is rendered: suppose, thing, be wont.
G3544: From νόμος; according (or pertaining) to law, i.e. legal (ceremonially); as noun, an expert in the (Mosaic) law. In the KJV it is rendered: about the law, lawyer.
G3545: Adverb from a derivative of νόμος; legitimately (specially, agreeably to the rules of the lists). In the KJV it is rendered: lawfully.
G3546: From νομίζω; what is reckoned as of value (after the Latin numisma), i.e. current coin. In the KJV it is rendered: money.
G3547: From νόμος and διδάσκαλος; an expounder of the (Jewish) law, i.e. a Rabbi. In the KJV it is rendered: doctor (teacher) of the law.
G3548: From νομοθέτης; legislation (specially, the institution of the Mosaic code). In the KJV it is rendered: giving of the law.
G3549: From νομοθέτης; to legislate, i.e. (passively) to have (the Mosaic) enactments injoined, be sanctioned (by them). In the KJV it is rendered: establish, receive the law.
G3550: From νόμος and a derivative of τίθημι; a legislator. In the KJV it is rendered: lawgiver.
G3551: From a primary nemo (to parcel out, especially food or grazing to animals); law (through the idea of prescriptive usage), genitive case (regulation), specially, (of Moses (including the volume); also of the Gospel), or figuratively (a principle). In the KJV it is rendered: law.
G3552: From νόσος; to be sick, i.e. (by implication, of a diseased appetite) to hanker after (figuratively, to harp upon). In the KJV it is rendered: dote.
G3553: From νοσέω; an ailment. In the KJV it is rendered: disease.
G3554: Of uncertain affinity; a malady (rarely figuratively, of moral disability). In the KJV it is rendered: disease, infirmity, sickness.
G3555: From νεοσσός; a brood (of chickens). In the KJV it is rendered: brood.
G3556: Diminutive of νεοσσός; a birdling. In the KJV it is rendered: chicken.
G3557: Middle voice from nosphi (apart or clandestinely); to sequestrate for oneself, i.e. embezzle. In the KJV it is rendered: keep back, purloin.
G3558: Of uncertain affinity; the south(-west) wind; by extension, the southern quarter itself. In the KJV it is rendered: south (wind).
G3559: From νοῦς and a derivative of τίθημι; calling attention to, i.e. (by implication) mild rebuke or warning. In the KJV it is rendered: admonition.
G3560: From the same as νουθεσία; to put in mind, i.e. (by implication) to caution or reprove gently. In the KJV it is rendered: admonish, warn.
G3561: Feminine of a compound of νέος and μήν (as noun by implication, of ἡμέρα); the festival of new moon. In the KJV it is rendered: new moon.
G3562: Adverb from a comparative of the accusative case of νοῦς and ἔχω; in a mind-having way, i.e. prudently. In the KJV it is rendered: discreetly.
G3563: Probably from the base of γινώσκω; the intellect, i.e. mind (divine or human; in thought, feeling, or will); by implication, meaning. In the KJV it is rendered: mind, understanding.
G3564: Probably contracted for a compound of νύμφη and δῶρον; nymph-given (i.e. -born); Nymphas, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Nymphas.
G3565: From a primary but obsolete verb nupto (to veil as a bride; compare Latin "nupto," to marry); a young married woman (as veiled), including a betrothed girl; by implication, a son's wife. In the KJV it is rendered: bride, daughter in law.
G3566: From νύμφη; a bride-groom (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: bridegroom.
G3567: From νύμφη; the bridal room. In the KJV it is rendered: bridechamber.
G3568: A primary particle of present time; "now" (as adverb of date, a transition or emphasis); also as noun or adjective present or immediate. In the KJV it is rendered: henceforth, + hereafter, of late, soon, present, this (time).
G3569: Or ta nun from neuter plural of ὁ and νῦν; the things now, i.e. (adverbially) at present. In the KJV it is rendered: (but) now.
G3570: A prolonged form of νῦν for emphasis; just now. In the KJV it is rendered: now.
G3571: A primary word; "night" (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: (mid-)night.
G3572: Apparently a primary word; to prick ("nudge"). In the KJV it is rendered: pierce.
G3573: From a presumed derivative of νεύω; to nod, i.e. (by implication) to fall asleep; figuratively, to delay. In the KJV it is rendered: slumber.
G3574: From νύξ and ἡμέρα; a day-and-night, i.e. full day of twenty-four hours. In the KJV it is rendered: night and day.
G3575: Of Hebrew origin (נֹ֫חַ); Noë, (i.e. Noäch), a patriarch. In the KJV it is rendered: Noe.
G3576: From a derivative of νόθος; sluggish, i.e. (literally) lazy, or (figuratively) stupid. In the KJV it is rendered: dull, slothful.
G3577: Of uncertain affinity; the back. In the KJV it is rendered: back.
G3578: From ξένος; hospitality, i.e. (by implication) a place of entertainment. In the KJV it is rendered: lodging.
G3579: From ξένος; to be a host (passively, a guest); by implication, be (make, appear) strange. In the KJV it is rendered: entertain, lodge, (think it) strange.
G3580: From a compound of ξένος and δέχομαι; to be hospitable. In the KJV it is rendered: lodge strangers.
G3581: Apparently a primary word; foreign (literally, alien, or figuratively, novel); by implication, a guest or (vice-versa) entertainer. In the KJV it is rendered: host, strange(-r).
G3582: As if from xeo (properly, to smooth; by implication, (of friction) to boil or heat); a vessel (as fashioned or for cooking) (or perhaps by corruption from the Latin sextarius, the sixth of a modius, i.e. about a pint), i.e. (specially), a measure for liquids or solids, (by analogy, a pitcher). In the KJV it is rendered: pot.
G3583: From ξηρός; to desiccate; by implication, to shrivel, to mature. In the KJV it is rendered: dry up, pine away, be ripe, wither (away).
G3584: From the base of ξέστης (through the idea of scorching); arid; by implication, shrunken, earth (as opposed to water). In the KJV it is rendered: dry land, withered.
G3585: From ξύλον; wooden. In the KJV it is rendered: of wood.
G3586: From another form of the base of ξέστης; timber (as fuel or material); by implication, a stick, club or tree or other wooden article or substance. In the KJV it is rendered: staff, stocks, tree, wood.
G3587: From a derivative of the same as ξύλον (meaning a razor); to shave or "shear" the hair. In the KJV it is rendered: shave.
G3588: Including the feminine he, and the neuter to in all their inflections; the definite article; the (sometimes to be supplied, at others omitted, in English idiom). In the KJV it is rendered: the, this, that, one, he, she, it, etc.
G3589: From ὄγδοος; ten times eight. In the KJV it is rendered: fourscore.
G3590: From ὀκτώ; the eighth. In the KJV it is rendered: eighth.
G3591: Probably from the same as ἀγκάλη; a mass (as bending or bulging by its load), i.e. burden (hindrance). In the KJV it is rendered: weight.
G3592: Including the feminine hede, and the neuter tode from ὁ and δέ; the same, i.e. this or that one (plural these or those); often used as a personal pronoun. In the KJV it is rendered: he, she, such, these, thus.
G3593: From ὁδός; to travel. In the KJV it is rendered: journey.
G3594: From ὁδηγός; to show the way (literally or figuratively (teach)). In the KJV it is rendered: guide, lead.
G3595: From ὁδός and ἡγέομαι; a conductor (literally or figuratively (teacher)). In the KJV it is rendered: guide, leader.
G3596: From a compound of ὁδός and πορεύομαι; to be a wayfarer, i.e. travel. In the KJV it is rendered: go on a journey.
G3597: From the same as ὁδοιπορέω; travel. In the KJV it is rendered: journey(-ing).
G3598: Apparently a primary word; a road; by implication, a progress (the route, act or distance); figuratively, a mode or means. In the KJV it is rendered: journey, (high-)way.
G3599: Perhaps from the base of ἐσθίω; a "tooth". In the KJV it is rendered: tooth.
G3600: From ὀδύνη; to grieve. In the KJV it is rendered: sorrow, torment.
G3601: From δύνω; grief (as dejecting). In the KJV it is rendered: sorrow.
G3602: From a derivative of the base of δύνω; moaning, i.e. lamentation. In the KJV it is rendered: mourning.
G3603: From the neuter of ὅς and the third person singular present indicative of εἰμί; which is. In the KJV it is rendered: called, which is (make), that is (to say).
G3604: Of Hebrew origin (עֻזִּיָּה); Ozias (i.e. Uzzijah), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Ozias.
G3605: A primary verb (in a strengthened form); to scent (usually an ill "odor"). In the KJV it is rendered: stink.
G3606: From ὅς with the directive enclitic of source; from which place or source or cause (adverb or conjunction). In the KJV it is rendered: from thence, (from) whence, where(-by, -fore, -upon).
G3607: Of uncertain affinity; a linen cloth, i.e. (especially) a sail. In the KJV it is rendered: sheet.
G3608: Neuter of a presumed derivative of ὀθόνη; a linen bandage. In the KJV it is rendered: linen clothes.
G3609: From οἶκος; domestic, i.e. (as noun), a relative, adherent. In the KJV it is rendered: (those) of the (his own) house(-hold).
G3610: From οἰκέω; a fellow resident, i.e. menial domestic. In the KJV it is rendered: (household) servant.
G3611: From οἶκος; to occupy a house, i.e. reside (figuratively, inhabit, remain, inhere); by implication, to cohabit. In the KJV it is rendered: dwell.
G3612: From οἰκέω; a tenement, i.e. (specially), a jail. In the KJV it is rendered: prison.
G3613: Neuter of a presumed derivative of οἰκέω (equivalent to οἴκημα); a residence (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: habitation, house.
G3614: From οἶκος; properly, residence (abstractly), but usually (concretely) an abode (literally or figuratively); by implication, a family (especially domestics). In the KJV it is rendered: home, house(-hold).
G3615: From οἰκία; familiar, i.e. (as noun) relatives. In the KJV it is rendered: they (them) of (his own) household.
G3616: From οἰκοδεσπότης; to be the head of (i.e. rule) a family. In the KJV it is rendered: guide the house.
G3617: From οἶκος and δεσπότης; the head of a family. In the KJV it is rendered: goodman (of the house), householder, master of the house.
G3618: From the same as οἰκοδομή; to be a house-builder, i.e. construct or (figuratively) confirm. In the KJV it is rendered: (be in) build(-er, -ing, up), edify, embolden.
G3619: Feminine (abstract) of a compound of οἶκος and the base of δῶμα; architecture, i.e. (concretely) a structure; figuratively, confirmation. In the KJV it is rendered: building, edify(-ication, -ing).
G3620: From the same as οἰκοδομή; confirmation. In the KJV it is rendered: edifying.
G3621: From οἰκονόμος; to manage (a house, i.e. an estate). In the KJV it is rendered: be steward.
G3622: From οἰκονόμος; administration (of a household or estate); specially, a (religious) "economy". In the KJV it is rendered: dispensation, stewardship.
G3623: From οἶκος and the base of νόμος; a house-distributor (i.e. manager), or overseer, i.e. an employee in that capacity; by extension, a fiscal agent (treasurer); figuratively, a preacher (of the Gospel). In the KJV it is rendered: chamberlain, governor, steward.
G3624: Of uncertain affinity; a dwelling (more or less extensive, literal or figurative); by implication, a family (more or less related, literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: home, house(-hold), temple.
G3625: Feminine participle present passive of οἰκέω (as noun, by implication, of γῆ); land, i.e. the (terrene part of the) globe; specially, the Roman empire. In the KJV it is rendered: earth, world.
G3626: From οἶκος and ouros (a guard; be "ware"); a stayer at home, i.e. domestically inclined (a "good housekeeper"). In the KJV it is rendered: keeper at home.
G3627: Also (in certain tenses) prolonged oiktereo from oiktos (pity); to exercise pity. In the KJV it is rendered: have compassion on.
G3628: From οἰκτείρω; pity. In the KJV it is rendered: mercy.
G3629: From οἰκτείρω; compassionate. In the KJV it is rendered: merciful, of tender mercy.
G3630: From οἶνος and a derivative of the alternate of πίνω; a tippler. In the KJV it is rendered: winebibber.
G3631: A primary word (or perhaps of Hebrew origin (יָ֫יִן)); "wine" (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: wine.
G3632: From οἶνος and a form of the base of φλύαρος; an overflow (or surplus) of wine, i.e. vinolency (drunkenness). In the KJV it is rendered: excess of wine.
G3633: Or (shorter) oimai middle voice apparently from οἷος; to make like (oneself), i.e. imagine (be of the opinion). In the KJV it is rendered: suppose, think.
G3634: Probably akin to ὁ, ὅς, and ὅσος; such or what sort of (as a correlation or exclamation); especially the neuter (adverbially) with negative, not so. In the KJV it is rendered: so (as), such as, what (manner of), which.
G3635: From oknos (hesitation); to be slow (figuratively, loath). In the KJV it is rendered: delay.
G3636: From ὀκνέω; tardy, i.e. indolent; (figuratively) irksome. In the KJV it is rendered: grievous, slothful.
G3637: From ὀκτώ and ἡμέρα; an eight-day old person or act. In the KJV it is rendered: the eighth day.
G3638: A primary numeral; "eight". In the KJV it is rendered: eight.
G3639: From a primary ollumi (to destroy; a prolonged form); ruin, i.e. death, punishment. In the KJV it is rendered: destruction.
G3640: From ὀλίγος and πίστις; incredulous, i.e. lacking confidence (in Christ). In the KJV it is rendered: of little faith.
G3641: Of uncertain affinity; puny (in extent, degree, number, duration or value); especially neuter (adverbially) somewhat. In the KJV it is rendered: + almost, brief(-ly), few, (a) little, + long, a season, short, small, a while.
G3642: From ὀλίγος and ψυχή; little-spirited, i.e. faint-hearted. In the KJV it is rendered: feebleminded.
G3643: From a compound of ὀλίγος and ora ("care"); to have little regard for, i.e. to disesteem. In the KJV it is rendered: despise.
G3644: From ὀλοθρεύω; a ruiner, i.e. (specially), a venomous serpent. In the KJV it is rendered: destroyer.
G3645: From ὄλεθρος; to spoil, i.e. slay. In the KJV it is rendered: destroy.
G3646: From a derivative of a compound of ὅλος and a derivative of καίω; a wholly-consumed sacrifice ("holocaust"). In the KJV it is rendered: (whole) burnt offering.
G3647: From ὁλόκληρος; integrity, i.e. physical wholeness. In the KJV it is rendered: perfect soundness.
G3648: From ὅλος and κλῆρος; complete in every part, i.e. perfectly sound (in body). In the KJV it is rendered: entire, whole.
G3649: A reduplicated primary verb; to "howl" or "halloo", i.e. shriek. In the KJV it is rendered: howl.
G3650: A primary word; "whole" or "all", i.e. complete (in extent, amount, time or degree), especially (neuter) as noun or adverb. In the KJV it is rendered: all, altogether, every whit, + throughout, whole.
G3651: From ὅλος and τέλος; complete to the end, i.e. absolutely perfect. In the KJV it is rendered: wholly.
G3652: Probably a contraction from Olumpiodoros (Olympian-bestowed, i.e. heaven-descended); Olympas, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Olympas.
G3653: Of uncertain derivation; an unripe (because out of season) fig. In the KJV it is rendered: untimely fig.
G3654: Adverb from ὅλος; completely, i.e. altogether; (by analogy), everywhere; (negatively) not by any means. In the KJV it is rendered: at all, commonly, utterly.
G3655: Of uncertain affinity; a thunder storm. In the KJV it is rendered: shower.
G3656: From ὅμιλος; to be in company with, i.e. (by implication) to converse. In the KJV it is rendered: commune, talk.
G3657: From ὅμιλος; companionship ("homily"), i.e. (by implication) intercourse. In the KJV it is rendered: communication.
G3658: From the base of ὁμοῦ and a derivative of the alternate of αἱρέομαι (meaning a crowd); association together, i.e. a multitude. In the KJV it is rendered: company.
G3659: From ὀπτάνομαι; a sight, i.e. (by implication) the eye. In the KJV it is rendered: eye.
G3660: A prolonged form of a primary, but obsolete omo, for which another prolonged form omoo is used in certain tenses; to swear, i.e. take (or declare on) oath. In the KJV it is rendered: swear.
G3661: Adverb from a compound of the base of ὁμοῦ and θυμός; unanimously. In the KJV it is rendered: with one accord (mind).
G3662: From ὅμοιος; to resemble. In the KJV it is rendered: agree.
G3663: From ὅμοιος and the alternate of πάσχω; similarly affected. In the KJV it is rendered: of (subject to) like passions.
G3664: From the base of ὁμοῦ; similar (in appearance or character). In the KJV it is rendered: like, + manner.
G3665: From ὅμοιος; resemblance. In the KJV it is rendered: like as, similitude.
G3666: From ὅμοιος; to assimilate, i.e. compare; passively, to become similar. In the KJV it is rendered: be (make) like, (in the) liken(-ess), resemble.
G3667: From ὁμοιόω; a form; abstractly, resemblance. In the KJV it is rendered: made like to, likeness, shape, similitude.
G3668: Adverb from ὅμοιος; similarly. In the KJV it is rendered: likewise, so.
G3669: From ὁμοιόω; assimilation, i.e. resemblance. In the KJV it is rendered: similitude.
G3670: From a compound of the base of ὁμοῦ and λόγος; to assent, i.e. covenant, acknowledge. In the KJV it is rendered: con- (pro-)fess, confession is made, give thanks, promise.
G3671: From the same as ὁμολογέω; acknowledgment. In the KJV it is rendered: con- (pro-)fession, professed.
G3672: Adverb of present passive participle of ὁμολογέω; confessedly. In the KJV it is rendered: without controversy.
G3673: From the base of ὁμοῦ and τέχνη; a fellow-artificer. In the KJV it is rendered: of the same craft.
G3674: Genitive case of homos (the same; akin to ἅμα) as adverb; at the same place or time. In the KJV it is rendered: together.
G3675: From the base of ὁμοῦ and φρήν; like-minded, i.e. harmonious. In the KJV it is rendered: of one mind.
G3676: Adverb from the base of ὁμοῦ; at the same time, i.e. (conjunctionally) notwithstanding, yet still. In the KJV it is rendered: and even, nevertheless, though but.
G3677: Of uncertain derivation; a dream. In the KJV it is rendered: dream.
G3678: Neuter of a presumed derivative of ὄνος; a little ass. In the KJV it is rendered: young ass.
G3679: From ὄνειδος; to defame, i.e. rail at, chide, taunt. In the KJV it is rendered: cast in teeth, (suffer) reproach, revile, upbraid.
G3680: From ὀνειδίζω; contumely. In the KJV it is rendered: reproach.
G3681: Probably akin to the base of ὄνομα; notoriety, i.e. a taunt (disgrace). In the KJV it is rendered: reproach.
G3682: From ὀνίνημι; profitable; Onesimus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Onesimus.
G3683: From a derivative of ὀνίνημι and φόρος; profit-bearer; Onesiphorus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Onespiphorus.
G3684: From ὄνος; belonging to a ass, i.e. large (so as to be turned by a ass). In the KJV it is rendered: millstone.
G3685: A prolonged form of an apparently primary verb (onomai, to slur); for which another prolonged form (onao) is used as an alternate in some tenses (unless indeed it be identical with the base of ὄνομα through the idea of notoriety); to gratify, i.e. (middle voice) to derive pleasure or advantage from. In the KJV it is rendered: have joy.
G3686: From a presumed derivative of the base of γινώσκω (compare ὀνίνημι); a "name" (literally or figuratively) (authority, character). In the KJV it is rendered: called, (+ sur-)name(-d).
G3687: From ὄνομα; to name, i.e. assign an appellation; by extension, to utter, mention, profess. In the KJV it is rendered: call, name.
G3688: Apparently a primary word; a donkey. In the KJV it is rendered: an ass.
G3689: Adverb of the oblique cases of ὤν; really. In the KJV it is rendered: certainly, clean, indeed, of a truth, verily.
G3690: From ὀξύς; vinegar, i.e. sour wine. In the KJV it is rendered: vinegar.
G3691: Probably akin to the base of ἀκμήν ("acid"); keen; by analogy, rapid. In the KJV it is rendered: sharp, swift.
G3692: Probably from ὀπτάνομαι; a hole (as if for light), i.e. cavern; by analogy, a spring (of water). In the KJV it is rendered: cave, place.
G3693: From opis (regard; from ὀπτάνομαι) with enclitic of source; from the rear (as a secure aspect), i.e. at the back (adverb and preposition of place or time). In the KJV it is rendered: after, backside, behind.
G3694: From the same as ὄπισθεν with enclitic of direction; to the back, i.e. aback (as adverb or preposition of time or place; or as noun). In the KJV it is rendered: after, back(-ward), (+ get) behind, + follow.
G3695: From ὅπλον; to equip (with weapons (middle voice and figuratively)). In the KJV it is rendered: arm self.
G3696: Probably from a primary hepo (to be busy about); an implement or utensil or tool (literally or figuratively, especially, offensive for war). In the KJV it is rendered: armour, instrument, weapon.
G3697: From ὅς and ποῖος; of what kind that, i.e. how (as) great (excellent) (specially, as an indefinite correlative to the definite antecedent τοιοῦτος of quality). In the KJV it is rendered: what manner (sort) of, such as whatsoever.
G3698: From ὅς and ποτέ; what(-ever) then, i.e. (of time) as soon as. In the KJV it is rendered: when.
G3699: From ὅς and πού; what(-ever) where, i.e. at whichever spot. In the KJV it is rendered: in what place, where(-as, -soever), whither (+ soever).
G3700: A (middle voice) prolonged form of the primary (middle voice) optomai; which is used for it in certain tenses; and both as alternate of ὁράω; to gaze (i.e. with wide-open eyes, as at something remarkable; and thus differing from βλέπω, which denotes simply voluntary observation; and from εἴδω, which expresses merely mechanical, passive or casual vision; while θεάομαι, and still more emphatically its intensive θεωρέω, signifies an earnest but more continued inspection; and σκοπέω a watching from a distance). In the KJV it is rendered: appear, look, see, shew self.
G3701: From a presumed derivative of ὀπτάνομαι; visuality, i.e. (concretely) an apparition. In the KJV it is rendered: vision.
G3702: From an obsolete verb akin to hepso (to "steep"); cooked, i.e. roasted. In the KJV it is rendered: broiled.
G3703: Apparently from the base of ὀψέ and ὥρα; properly, even-tide of the (summer) season (dog-days), i.e. (by implication) ripe fruit. In the KJV it is rendered: fruit.
G3704: From ὅς and πῶς; what(-ever) how, i.e. in the manner that (as adverb or conjunction of coincidence, intentional or actual). In the KJV it is rendered: because, how, (so) that, to, when.
G3705: From ὁράω; something gazed at, i.e. a spectacle (especially supernatural). In the KJV it is rendered: sight, vision.
G3706: From ὁράω; the act of gazing, i.e. (externally) an aspect or (internally) an inspired appearance. In the KJV it is rendered: sight, vision.
G3707: From ὁράω; gazed at, i.e. (by implication) capable of being seen. In the KJV it is rendered: visible.
G3708: Properly, to stare at (compare ὀπτάνομαι), i.e. (by implication) to discern clearly (physically or mentally); by extension, to attend to; by Hebraism, to experience; passively, to appear. In the KJV it is rendered: behold, perceive, see, take heed.
G3709: From ὀρέγομαι; properly, desire (as a reaching forth or excitement of the mind), i.e. (by analogy), violent passion (ire, or (justifiable) abhorrence); by implication punishment. In the KJV it is rendered: anger, indignation, vengeance, wrath.
G3710: From ὀργή; to provoke or enrage, i.e. (passively) become exasperated. In the KJV it is rendered: be angry (wroth).
G3711: From ὀργή; irascible. In the KJV it is rendered: soon angry.
G3712: From ὀρέγομαι; a stretch of the arms, i.e. a fathom. In the KJV it is rendered: fathom.
G3713: Middle voice of apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary (compare ὄρος); to stretch oneself, i.e. reach out after (long for). In the KJV it is rendered: covet after, desire.
G3714: From ὄρος; mountainous, i.e. (feminine by implication, of χώρα) the Highlands (of Judæa). In the KJV it is rendered: hill country.
G3715: From ὀρέγομαι; excitement of the mind, i.e. longing after. In the KJV it is rendered: lust.
G3716: From a compound of ὀρθός and πούς; to be straight-footed, i.e. (figuratively) to go directly forward. In the KJV it is rendered: walk uprightly.
G3717: Probably from the base of ὄρος; right (as rising), i.e. (perpendicularly) erect (figuratively, honest), or (horizontally) level or direct. In the KJV it is rendered: straight, upright.
G3718: From a compound of ὀρθός and the base of τομώτερος, to make a straight cut, i.e. (figuratively) to dissect (expound) correctly (the divine message). In the KJV it is rendered: rightly divide.
G3719: From ὄρθρος; to use the dawn, i.e. (by implication) to repair betimes. In the KJV it is rendered: come early in the morning.
G3720: From ὄρθρος; relating to the dawn, i.e. matutinal (as an epithet of Venus, especially brilliant in the early day). In the KJV it is rendered: morning.
G3721: From ὄρθρος; in the dawn, i.e. up at day-break. In the KJV it is rendered: early.
G3722: From the same as ὄρος; dawn (as sun-rise, rising of light); by extension, morn. In the KJV it is rendered: early in the morning.
G3723: Adverb from ὀρθός; in a straight manner, i.e. (figuratively) correctly (also morally). In the KJV it is rendered: plain, right(-ly).
G3724: From ὅριον; to mark out or bound ("horizon"), i.e. (figuratively) to appoint, decree, specify. In the KJV it is rendered: declare, determine, limit, ordain.
G3725: Neuter of a derivative of an apparently primary horos (a bound or limit); a boundary-line, i.e. (by implication) a frontier (region). In the KJV it is rendered: border, coast.
G3726: From ὅρκος; to put on oath, i.e. make swear; by analogy, to solemnly enjoin. In the KJV it is rendered: adjure, charge.
G3727: From herkos (a fence; perhaps akin to ὅριον); a limit, i.e. (sacred) restraint (specially, an oath). In the KJV it is rendered: oath.
G3728: From a compound of ὅρκος and a derivative of ὀμνύω; asseveration on oath. In the KJV it is rendered: oath.
G3729: From ὁρμή; to start, spur or urge on, i.e. (reflexively) to dash or plunge. In the KJV it is rendered: run (violently), rush.
G3730: Of uncertain affinity; a violent impulse, i.e. onset. In the KJV it is rendered: assault.
G3731: From ὁρμή; an attack, i.e. (abstractly) precipitancy. In the KJV it is rendered: violence.
G3732: Neuter of a presumed derivative of ὄρνις; a birdling. In the KJV it is rendered: bird, fowl.
G3733: Probably from a prolonged form of the base of ὄρος; a bird (as rising in the air), i.e. (specially), a hen (or female domestic fowl). In the KJV it is rendered: hen.
G3734: From a compound of the base of ὅριον and a derivative of τίθημι; a limit-placing, i.e. (concretely) boundary-line. In the KJV it is rendered: bound.
G3735: Probably from an obsolete oro (to rise or "rear"; perhaps akin to αἴρω; compare ὄρνις); a mountain (as lifting itself above the plain). In the KJV it is rendered: hill, mount(-ain).
G3736: Apparently a primary verb; to "burrow" in the ground, i.e. dig. In the KJV it is rendered: dig.
G3737: Of uncertain affinity; bereaved ("orphan"), i.e. parentless. In the KJV it is rendered: comfortless, fatherless.
G3738: Middle voice from orchos (a row or ring); to dance (from the ranklike or regular motion). In the KJV it is rendered: dance.
G3739: Including feminine he, and neuter ho probably a primary word (or perhaps a form of the article ὁ); the relatively (sometimes demonstrative) pronoun, who, which, what, that. In the KJV it is rendered: one, (an-, the) other, some, that, what, which, who(-m, -se), etc.
G3740: Multiple adverb from ὅς; how (i.e. with ἄν, so) many times as. In the KJV it is rendered: as oft(-en) as.
G3741: Of uncertain affinity; properly, right (by intrinsic or divine character; thus distinguished from δίκαιος, which refers rather to human statutes and relations; from ἱερός, which denotes formal consecration; and from ἅγιος, which relates to purity from defilement), i.e. hallowed (pious, sacred, sure). In the KJV it is rendered: holy, mercy, shalt be.
G3742: From ὅσιος; piety. In the KJV it is rendered: holiness.
G3743: Adverb from ὅσιος; piously. In the KJV it is rendered: holily.
G3744: From ὄζω; fragrance (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: odour, savour.
G3745: By reduplication from ὅς; as (much, great, long, etc.) as. In the KJV it is rendered: all (that), as (long, many, much) (as), how great (many, much), (in-)asmuch as, so many as, that (ever), the more, those things, what (great, -soever), wheresoever, wherewithsoever, which, X while, who(-soever).
G3746: From ὅς and περ; who especially. In the KJV it is rendered: whomsoever.
G3747: Or contracted ostoun of uncertain affinity; a bone. In the KJV it is rendered: bone.
G3748: Including the feminine hetis, and the neuter hoti from ὅς and τὶς; which some, i.e. any that; also (definite) which same. In the KJV it is rendered: X and (they), (such) as, (they) that, in that they, what(-soever), whereas ye, (they) which, who(-soever).
G3749: From ostrakon ("oyster") (a tile, i.e. terra cotta); earthen-ware, i.e. clayey; by implication, frail. In the KJV it is rendered: of earth, earthen.
G3750: From a derivative of ὄζω; smell (the sense). In the KJV it is rendered: smelling.
G3751: Of uncertain affinity; the loin (externally), i.e. the hip; internally (by extension) procreative power. In the KJV it is rendered: loin.
G3752: From ὅτε and ἄν; whenever (implying hypothesis or more or less uncertainty); also causatively (conjunctionally) inasmuch as. In the KJV it is rendered: as long (soon) as, that, + till, when(-soever), while.
G3753: From ὅς and τέ; at which (thing) too, i.e. when. In the KJV it is rendered: after (that), as soon as, that, when, while.
G3754: Neuter of ὅστις as conjunction; demonstrative, that (sometimes redundant); causative, because. In the KJV it is rendered: as concerning that, as though, because (that), for (that), how (that), (in) that, though, why.
G3755: For the genitive case of ὅστις (as adverb); during which same time, i.e. whilst. In the KJV it is rendered: whiles.
G3756: Also (before a vowel) ouk, and (before an aspirate) ouch a primary word; the absolute negative (compare μή) adverb; no or not. In the KJV it is rendered: + long, nay, neither, never, no (X man), none, (can-)not, + nothing, + special, un(-worthy), when, + without, + yet but.
G3757: Genitive case of ὅς as adverb; at which place, i.e. where. In the KJV it is rendered: where(-in), whither(-soever).
G3758: A primary exclamation of surprise; "ah". In the KJV it is rendered: ah.
G3759: A primary exclamation of grief; "woe". In the KJV it is rendered: alas, woe.
G3760: Adverb from (the feminine) of οὐδείς; by no means. In the KJV it is rendered: not.
G3761: From οὐ and δέ; not however, i.e. neither, nor, not even. In the KJV it is rendered: neither (indeed), never, no (more, nor, not), nor (yet), (also, even, then) not (even, so much as), + nothing, so much as.
G3762: Including feminine oudemia, and neuter ouden from οὐδέ and εἷς; not even one (man, woman or thing), i.e. none, nobody, nothing. In the KJV it is rendered: any (man), aught, man, neither any (thing), never (man), no (man), none (+ of these things), not (any, at all, -thing), nought.
G3763: From οὐδέ and ποτέ; not even at any time, i.e. never at all. In the KJV it is rendered: neither at any time, never, nothing at any time.
G3764: From οὐδέ and -πω; not even yet. In the KJV it is rendered: as yet not, never before (yet), (not) yet.
G3765: Also (separately) ouk eti from οὐ and ἔτι; not yet, no longer. In the KJV it is rendered: after that (not), (not) any more, henceforth (hereafter) not, no longer (more), not as yet (now), now no more (not), yet (not).
G3766: From οὐ and οὖν; is it not therefore that, i.e. (affirmatively) hence or so. In the KJV it is rendered: then.
G3767: Apparently a primary word; (adverbially) certainly, or (conjunctionally) accordingly. In the KJV it is rendered: and (so, truly), but, now (then), so (likewise then), then, therefore, verily, wherefore.
G3768: From οὐ and -πω; not yet. In the KJV it is rendered: hitherto not, (no…) as yet, not yet.
G3769: Apparently a primary word; a tail. In the KJV it is rendered: tail.
G3770: From οὐρανός; celestial, i.e. belonging to or coming from the sky. In the KJV it is rendered: heavenly.
G3771: From οὐρανός and the enclitic of source; from the sky. In the KJV it is rendered: from heaven.
G3772: Perhaps from the same as ὄρος (through the idea of elevation); the sky; by extension, heaven (as the abode of God); by implication, happiness, power, eternity; specially, the Gospel (Christianity). In the KJV it is rendered: air, heaven(-ly), sky.
G3773: Of Latin origin; Urbanus (of the city, "urbane"), a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Urbanus.
G3774: Of Hebrew origin (אוּרִיָּה); Urias (i.e. Urijah), a Hittite. In the KJV it is rendered: Urias.
G3775: Apparently a primary word; the ear (physically or mentally). In the KJV it is rendered: ear.
G3776: From the feminine of ὤν; substance, i.e. property (possessions). In the KJV it is rendered: goods, substance.
G3777: From οὐ and τέ; not too, i.e. neither or nor; by analogy, not even. In the KJV it is rendered: neither, none, nor (yet), (no, yet) not, nothing.
G3778: Including nominative masculine plural houtoi, nominative feminine singular haute, and nominative feminine plural hautai from the article ὁ and αὐτός; the he (she or it), i.e. this or that (often with article repeated). In the KJV it is rendered: he (it was that), hereof, it, she, such as, the same, these, they, this (man, same, woman), which, who.
G3779: Or (before a vowel houtos adverb from οὗτος; in this way (referring to what precedes or follows). In the KJV it is rendered: after that, after (in) this manner, as, even (so), for all that, like(-wise), no more, on this fashion(-wise), so (in like manner), thus, what.
G3780: Intensive of οὐ; not indeed. In the KJV it is rendered: nay, not.
G3781: From ὀφείλω; an ower, i.e. person indebted; figuratively, a delinquent; morally, a transgressor (against God). In the KJV it is rendered: debtor, which owed, sinner.
G3782: From ὀφείλω; indebtedness, i.e. (concretely) a sum owed; figuratively, obligation, i.e. (conjugal) duty. In the KJV it is rendered: debt, due.
G3783: From (the alternate of) ὀφείλω; something owed, i.e. (figuratively) a due; morally, a fault. In the KJV it is rendered: debt.
G3784: Or (in certain tenses), its prolonged form opheileo probably from the base of ὄφελος (through the idea of accruing); to owe (pecuniarily); figuratively, to be under obligation (ought, must, should); morally, to fail in duty. In the KJV it is rendered: behove, be bound, (be) debt(-or), (be) due(-ty), be guilty (indebted), (must) need(-s), ought, owe, should.
G3785: First person singular of a past tense of ὀφείλω; I ought (wish), i.e. (interjection) oh that!. In the KJV it is rendered: would (to God).
G3786: From ophello (to heap up, i.e. accumulate or benefit); gain. In the KJV it is rendered: advantageth, profit.
G3787: From ὀφθαλμός and δουλεία; sight-labor, i.e. that needs watching (remissness). In the KJV it is rendered: eye-service.
G3788: From ὀπτάνομαι; the eye (literally or figuratively); by implication, vision; figuratively, envy (from the jealous side-glance). In the KJV it is rendered: eye, sight.
G3789: Probably from ὀπτάνομαι (through the idea of sharpness of vision); a snake, figuratively, (as a type of sly cunning) an artful malicious person, especially Satan. In the KJV it is rendered: serpent.
G3790: Perhaps from ὀπτάνομαι (through the idea of the shading or proximity to the organ of vision); the eye-"brow" or forehead, i.e. (figuratively) the brink of a precipice. In the KJV it is rendered: brow.
G3791: From ὄχλος; to mob, i.e. (by implication) to harass. In the KJV it is rendered: vex.
G3792: From ὄχλος and ποιέω; to make a crowd, i.e. raise a public disturbance. In the KJV it is rendered: gather a company.
G3793: From a derivative of ἔχω (meaning a vehicle); a throng (as borne along); by implication, the rabble; by extension, a class of people; figuratively, a riot. In the KJV it is rendered: company, multitude, number (of people), people, press.
G3794: From a remote derivative of ἔχω (meaning to fortify, through the idea of holding safely); a castle (figuratively, argument). In the KJV it is rendered: stronghold.
G3795: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of ὀπτός; a relish to other food (as if cooked sauce), i.e. (specially), fish (presumably salted and dried as a condiment). In the KJV it is rendered: fish.
G3796: From the same as ὀπίσω (through the idea of backwardness); (adverbially) late in the day; by extension, after the close of the day. In the KJV it is rendered: (at) even, in the end.
G3797: From ὀψέ; later, i.e. vernal (showering). In the KJV it is rendered: latter.
G3798: From ὀψέ; late; feminine (as noun) afternoon (early eve) or nightfall (later eve). In the KJV it is rendered: even(-ing, (-tide)).
G3799: From ὀπτάνομαι; properly, sight (the act), i.e. (by implication) the visage, an external show. In the KJV it is rendered: appearance, countenance, face.
G3800: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the same as ὀψάριον; rations for a soldier, i.e. (by extension) his stipend or pay. In the KJV it is rendered: wages.
G3801: Or ho en kai or ho erchomenos a phrase combining ὁ with the present participle and imperfect of εἰμί and the present participle of ἔρχομαι by means of καί; the one being and the one that was and the one coming, i.e. the Eternal, as a divine epithet of Christ. In the KJV it is rendered: which art (is, was), and (which) wast (is, was), and art (is) to come (shalt be).
G3802: From παγίς; to ensnare (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: entangle.
G3803: From πήγνυμι; a trap (as fastened by a noose or notch); figuratively, a trick or statagem (temptation). In the KJV it is rendered: snare.
G3804: From a presumed derivative of πάθος; something undergone, i.e. hardship or pain; subjectively, an emotion or influence. In the KJV it is rendered: affection, affliction, motion, suffering.
G3805: From the same as πάθημα; liable (i.e. doomed) to experience pain. In the KJV it is rendered: suffer.
G3806: From the alternate of πάσχω; properly, suffering ("pathos"), i.e. (subjectively) a passion (especially concupiscence). In the KJV it is rendered: (inordinate) affection, lust.
G3807: From παῖς and a reduplicated form of ἄγω; a boy-leader, i.e. a servant whose office it was to take the children to school; (by implication, (figuratively) a tutor ("pædagogue")). In the KJV it is rendered: instructor, schoolmaster.
G3808: Neuter of a presumed derivative of παῖς; a little boy. In the KJV it is rendered: child, lad.
G3809: From παιδεύω; tutorage, i.e. education or training; by implication, disciplinary correction. In the KJV it is rendered: chastening, chastisement, instruction, nurture.
G3810: From παιδεύω; a trainer, i.e. teacher or (by implication) discipliner. In the KJV it is rendered: which corrected, instructor.
G3811: From παῖς; to train up a child, i.e. educate, or (by implication), discipline (by punishment). In the KJV it is rendered: chasten(-ise), instruct, learn, teach.
G3812: Adverb (of source) from παιδίον; from infancy. In the KJV it is rendered: of a child.
G3813: Neuter diminutive of παῖς; a childling (of either sex), i.e. (properly), an infant, or (by extension) a half-grown boy or girl; figuratively, an immature Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: (little, young) child, damsel.
G3814: Feminine diminutive of παῖς; a girl, i.e. (specially), a female slave or servant. In the KJV it is rendered: bondmaid(-woman), damsel, maid(-en).
G3815: From παῖς; to sport (as a boy). In the KJV it is rendered: play.
G3816: Perhaps from παίω; a boy (as often beaten with impunity), or (by analogy), a girl, and (genitive case) a child; specially, a slave or servant (especially a minister to a king; and by eminence to God). In the KJV it is rendered: child, maid(-en), (man) servant, son, young man.
G3817: A primary verb; to hit (as if by a single blow and less violently than τύπτω); specially, to sting (as a scorpion). In the KJV it is rendered: smite, strike.
G3818: Feminine of an adjective of uncertain derivation; Pacatianian, a section of Phrygia. In the KJV it is rendered: Pacatiana.
G3819: Probably another form for πάλιν (through the idea of retrocession); (adverbially) formerly, or (by relatively) sometime since; (elliptically as adjective) ancient. In the KJV it is rendered: any while, a great while ago, (of) old, in time past.
G3820: From πάλαι; antique, i.e. not recent, worn out. In the KJV it is rendered: old.
G3821: From παλαιός; antiquatedness. In the KJV it is rendered: oldness.
G3822: From παλαιός; to make (passively, become) worn out, or declare obsolete. In the KJV it is rendered: decay, make (wax) old.
G3823: From pallo (to vibrate; another form for βάλλω); wrestling. In the KJV it is rendered: + wrestle.
G3824: From πάλιν and γένεσις; (spiritual) rebirth (the state or the act), i.e. (figuratively) spiritual renovation; specially, Messianic restoration. In the KJV it is rendered: regeneration.
G3825: Probably from the same as πάλη (through the idea of oscillatory repetition); (adverbially) anew, i.e. (of place) back, (of time) once more, or (conjunctionally) furthermore or on the other hand. In the KJV it is rendered: again.
G3826: Dative case (adverb) of a compound of πᾶς and πλῆθος; in full multitude, i.e. concertedly or simultaneously. In the KJV it is rendered: all at once.
G3827: From πᾶς and πολύς; full many, i.e. immense. In the KJV it is rendered: very great.
G3828: From a compound of πᾶς and πυρά; every-tribal, i.e. heterogeneous (χώρα being implied); Pamphylia, a region of Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Pamphylia.
G3829: Neuter of a presumed compound of πᾶς and a derivative of δέχομαι; all-receptive, i.e. a public lodging-place (caravanserai or khan). In the KJV it is rendered: inn.
G3830: From the same as πανδοχεῖον; an innkeeper (warden of a caravanserai). In the KJV it is rendered: host.
G3831: From πᾶς and a derivative of ἀγορά; a mass-meeting, i.e. (figuratively) universal companionship. In the KJV it is rendered: general assembly.
G3832: Adverb from πᾶς and οἶκος; with the whole family. In the KJV it is rendered: with all his house.
G3833: From a compound of πᾶς and ὅπλον; full armor ("panoply"). In the KJV it is rendered: all (whole) armour.
G3834: From πανοῦργος; adroitness, i.e. (in a bad sense) trickery or sophistry. In the KJV it is rendered: (cunning) craftiness, subtilty.
G3835: From πᾶς and ἔργον; all-working, i.e. adroit (shrewd). In the KJV it is rendered: crafty.
G3836: Adverb (of source) from πανταχοῦ; from all directions. In the KJV it is rendered: from every quarter.
G3837: Genitive case (as adverb of place) of a presumed derivative of πᾶς; universally. In the KJV it is rendered: in all places, everywhere.
G3838: From πᾶς and τέλος; full-ended, i.e. entire (neuter as noun, completion). In the KJV it is rendered: + in (no) wise, uttermost.
G3839: Adverb (of manner) from πᾶς; wholly. In the KJV it is rendered: always.
G3840: Adverb (of source) from πᾶς; from (i.e. on) all sides. In the KJV it is rendered: on every side, round about.
G3841: From πᾶς and κράτος; the all-ruling, i.e. God (as absolute and universal sovereign). In the KJV it is rendered: Almighty, Omnipotent.
G3842: From πᾶς and ὅτε; every when, i.e. at all times. In the KJV it is rendered: alway(-s), ever(-more).
G3843: Adverb from πᾶς; entirely; specially, at all events, (with negative, following) in no event. In the KJV it is rendered: by all means, altogether, at all, needs, no doubt, in (no) wise, surely.
G3844: A primary preposition; properly, near; i.e. (with genitive case) from beside (literally or figuratively), (with dative case) at (or in) the vicinity of (objectively or subjectively), (with accusative case) to the proximity with (local (especially beyond or opposed to) or causal (on account of). In the KJV it is rendered: above, against, among, at, before, by, contrary to, X friend, from, + give (such things as they), + that (she) had, X his, in, more than, nigh unto, (out) of, past, save, side…by, in the sight of, than, (there-)fore, with.
G3845: From παρά and the base of βάσις; to go contrary to, i.e. violate a command. In the KJV it is rendered: (by) transgress(-ion).
G3846: From παρά and βάλλω; to throw alongside, i.e. (reflexively) to reach a place, or (figuratively) to liken. In the KJV it is rendered: arrive, compare.
G3847: From παραβαίνω; violation. In the KJV it is rendered: breaking, transgression.
G3848: From παραβαίνω; a violator. In the KJV it is rendered: breaker, transgress(-or).
G3849: From παρά and the middle voice of βιάζω; to force contrary to (nature), i.e. compel (by entreaty). In the KJV it is rendered: constrain.
G3850: From παραβάλλω; a similitude ("parable"), i.e. (symbolic) fictitious narrative (of common life conveying a moral), apothegm or adage. In the KJV it is rendered: comparison, figure, parable, proverb.

G4018: Neuter of a presumed derivative of περιβάλλω; something thrown around one, i.e. a mantle, veil. In the KJV it is rendered: covering, vesture.
G4019: From περί and δέω; to bind around one, i.e. enwrap. In the KJV it is rendered: bind about.
G4020: From περί and ἐργάζομαι; to work all around, i.e. bustle about (meddle). In the KJV it is rendered: be a busybody.
G4021: From περί and ἔργον; working all around, i.e. officious (meddlesome, neuter plural magic). In the KJV it is rendered: busybody, curious arts.
G4022: From περί and ἔρχομαι (including its alternate); to come all around, i.e. stroll, vacillate, veer. In the KJV it is rendered: fetch a compass, vagabond, wandering about.
G4023: From περί and ἔχω; to hold all around, i.e. include, clasp (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: + astonished, contain, after (this manner).
G4024: From περί and ζώννυμι; to gird all around, i.e. (middle voice or passive) to fasten on one's belt (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: gird (about, self).
G4025: From περιτίθημι; a putting all around, i.e. decorating oneself with. In the KJV it is rendered: wearing.
G4026: From περί and ἵστημι; to stand all around, i.e. (near) to be a bystander, or (aloof) to keep away from. In the KJV it is rendered: avoid, shun, stand by (round about).
G4027: From a compound of περί and καθαίρω; something cleaned off all around, i.e. refuse (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: filth.
G4028: From περί and καλύπτω; to cover all around, i.e. entirely (the face, a surface). In the KJV it is rendered: blindfold, cover, overlay.
G4029: From περί and κεῖμαι; to lie all around, i.e. inclose, encircle, hamper (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: be bound (compassed) with, hang about.
G4030: Feminine of a compound of περί and κεφαλή; encirclement of the head, i.e. a helmet. In the KJV it is rendered: helmet.
G4031: From περί and κράτος; strong all around, i.e. a master (manager). In the KJV it is rendered: + come by.
G4032: From περί and κρύπτω; to conceal all around, i.e. entirely. In the KJV it is rendered: hide.
G4033: From περί and κυκλόω; to encircle all around, i.e. blockade completely. In the KJV it is rendered: compass round.
G4034: From περί and λάμπω; to illuminate all around, i.e. invest with a halo. In the KJV it is rendered: shine round about.
G4035: From περί and λείπω; to leave all around, i.e. (passively) survive. In the KJV it is rendered: remain.
G4036: From περί and λύπη; grieved all around, i.e. intensely sad. In the KJV it is rendered: exceeding (very) sorry(-owful).
G4037: From περί and μένω; to stay around, i.e. await. In the KJV it is rendered: wait for.
G4038: Adverb from περί; all around, i.e. (as an adjective) circumjacent. In the KJV it is rendered: round about.
G4039: From περί and οἰκέω; to reside around, i.e. be a neighbor. In the KJV it is rendered: dwell round about.
G4040: From περί and οἶκος; housed around, i.e. neighboring (used elliptically as a noun). In the KJV it is rendered: neighbour.
G4041: From the present participle feminine of a compound of περί and εἰμί; being beyond usual, i.e. special (one's own). In the KJV it is rendered: peculiar.
G4042: From περιέχω; a being held around, i.e. (concretely) a passage (of Scripture, as circumscribed). In the KJV it is rendered: place.
G4043: From περί and πατέω; to tread all around, i.e. walk at large (especially as proof of ability); figuratively, to live, deport oneself, follow (as a companion or votary). In the KJV it is rendered: go, be occupied with, walk (about).
G4044: From περί and the base of πέραν; to penetrate entirely, i.e. transfix (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: pierce through.
G4045: From περί and πίπτω; to fall into something that is all around, i.e. light among or upon, be surrounded with. In the KJV it is rendered: fall among (into).
G4046: Middle voice from περί and ποιέω; to make around oneself, i.e. acquire (buy). In the KJV it is rendered: purchase.
G4047: From περιποιέομαι; acquisition (the act or the thing); by extension, preservation. In the KJV it is rendered: obtain(-ing), peculiar, purchased, possession, saving.
G4048: From περί and ῥήγνυμι; to tear all around, i.e. completely away. In the KJV it is rendered: rend off.
G4049: From περί and σπάω; to drag all around, i.e. (figuratively) to distract (with care). In the KJV it is rendered: cumber.
G4050: From περισσεύω; surplusage, i.e. superabundance. In the KJV it is rendered: abundance(-ant, (-ly)), superfluity.
G4051: From περισσεύω; a surplus, or superabundance. In the KJV it is rendered: abundance, that was left, over and above.
G4052: From περισσός; to superabound (in quantity or quality), be in excess, be superfluous; also (transitively) to cause to superabound or excel. In the KJV it is rendered: (make, more) abound, (have, have more) abundance (be more) abundant, be the better, enough and to spare, exceed, excel, increase, be left, redound, remain (over and above).
G4053: From περί (in the sense of beyond); superabundant (in quantity) or superior (in quality); by implication, excessive; adverbially (with ἐκ) violently; neuter (as noun) preeminence. In the KJV it is rendered: exceeding abundantly above, more abundantly, advantage, exceedingly, very highly, beyond measure, more, superfluous, vehement(-ly).
G4054: Neuter of περισσότερος (as adverb); in a more superabundant way. In the KJV it is rendered: more abundantly, a great deal, far more.
G4055: Comparative of περισσός; more superabundant (in number, degree or character). In the KJV it is rendered: more abundant, greater (much) more, overmuch.
G4056: Adverb from περισσότερος; more superabundantly. In the KJV it is rendered: more abundant(-ly), X the more earnest, (more) exceedingly, more frequent, much more, the rather.
G4057: Adverb from περισσός; superabundantly. In the KJV it is rendered: exceedingly, out of measure, the more.
G4058: Of uncertain derivation; a pigeon. In the KJV it is rendered: dove, pigeon.
G4059: From περί and the base of τομώτερος; to cut around, i.e. (specially) to circumcise. In the KJV it is rendered: circumcise.
G4060: From περί and τίθημι; to place around; by implication, to present. In the KJV it is rendered: bestow upon, hedge round about, put about (on, upon), set about.
G4061: From περιτέμνω; circumcision (the rite, the condition or the people, literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: X circumcised, circumcision.
G4062: From περί and the base of τροπή; to turn around, i.e. (mentally) to craze. In the KJV it is rendered: + make mad.
G4063: From περί and τρέχω (including its alternate); to run around, i.e. traverse. In the KJV it is rendered: run through.
G4064: From περί and φέρω; to convey around, i.e. transport hither and thither. In the KJV it is rendered: bear (carry) about.
G4065: From περί and φρονέω; to think beyond, i.e. depreciate (contemn). In the KJV it is rendered: despise.
G4066: From περί and χώρα; around the region, i.e. circumjacent (as noun, with γῆ implied vicinity). In the KJV it is rendered: country (round) about, region (that lieth) round about.
G4067: From a comparative of περί and psao (to rub); something brushed all around, i.e. off-scrapings (figuratively, scum). In the KJV it is rendered: offscouring.
G4068: Middle voice from perperos (braggart; perhaps by reduplication of the base of πέραν); to boast. In the KJV it is rendered: vaunt itself.
G4069: A Persian woman; Persis, a Christian female. In the KJV it is rendered: Persis.
G4070: Adverb from πέρας; the by-gone, i.e. (as noun) last year. In the KJV it is rendered: + a year ago.
G4071: Neuter of a derivative of πέτομαι; a flying animal, i.e. bird. In the KJV it is rendered: bird, fowl.
G4072: Or prolongation petaomai, or contracted ptaomai middle voice of a primary verb; to fly. In the KJV it is rendered: fly(-ing).
G4073: Feminine of the same as Πέτρος; a (mass of) rock (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: rock.
G4074: Apparently a primary word; a (piece of) rock (larger than λίθος); as a name, Petrus, an apostle. In the KJV it is rendered: Peter, rock.
G4075: From πέτρα and εἶδος; rock-like, i.e. rocky. In the KJV it is rendered: stony.
G4076: From πήγνυμι; rue (from its thick or fleshy leaves). In the KJV it is rendered: rue.
G4077: Probably from πήγνυμι (through the idea of gushing plumply); a fount (literally or figuratively), i.e. source or supply (of water, blood, enjoyment) (not necessarily the original spring). In the KJV it is rendered: fountain, well.
G4078: A prolonged form of a primary verb (which in its simpler form occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to fix ("peg"), i.e. (specially) to set up (a tent). In the KJV it is rendered: pitch.
G4079: Neuter of a (presumed) derivative of pedon (the blade of an oar; from the same as πέδη); a "pedal", i.e. helm. In the KJV it is rendered: rudder.
G4080: A quantitative form (the feminine) of the base of πού; how much (as an indefinite), i.e. in size or (figuratively) dignity. In the KJV it is rendered: how great (large).
G4081: Perhaps a primary word; clay. In the KJV it is rendered: clay.
G4082: Of uncertain affinity; a wallet or leather pouch for food. In the KJV it is rendered: scrip.
G4083: Of uncertain affinity; the fore-arm, i.e. (as a measure) a cubit. In the KJV it is rendered: cubit.
G4084: Probably another form of βιάζω; to squeeze, i.e. seize (gently by the hand (press), or officially (arrest), or in hunting (capture)). In the KJV it is rendered: apprehend, catch, lay hand on, take.
G4085: Another form for πιάζω; to pack. In the KJV it is rendered: press down.
