G4086: From a compound of a derivative of πείθω and λόγος; persuasive language. In the KJV it is rendered: enticing words.
G4087: From πικρός; to embitter (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: be (make) bitter.
G4088: From πικρός; acridity (especially poison), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: bitterness.
G4089: Perhaps from πήγνυμι (through the idea of piercing); sharp (pungent), i.e. acrid (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: bitter.
G4090: Adverb from πικρός; bitterly, i.e. (figuratively) violently. In the KJV it is rendered: bitterly.
G4091: Of Latin origin; close-pressed, i.e. firm; Pilatus, a Roman. In the KJV it is rendered: Pilate.
G4092: A reduplicated and prolonged form of a primary preo which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to fire, i.e. burn (figuratively and passively, become inflamed with fever). In the KJV it is rendered: be (X should have) swollen.
G4093: Diminutive of πίναξ; a tablet (for writing on). In the KJV it is rendered: writing table.
G4094: Apparently a form of πλάξ; a plate. In the KJV it is rendered: charger, platter.
G4095: A prolonged form of pio, which (together with another form) poo occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses; to imbibe (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: drink.
G4096: From pion (fat; perhaps akin to the alternate of πίνω through the idea of repletion); plumpness, i.e. (by implication) richness (oiliness). In the KJV it is rendered: fatness.
G4097: A reduplicated and prolonged form of prao; (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); contracted from perao (to traverse; from the base of πέραν); to traffic (by travelling), i.e. dispose of as merchandise or into slavery (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: sell.
G4098: A reduplicated and contracted form of peto; (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); probably akin to πέτομαι through the idea of alighting; to fall (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: fail, fall (down), light on.
G4099: Probably of foreign origin; Pisidia, a region of Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Pisidia.
G4100: From πίστις; to have faith (in, upon, or with respect to, a person or thing), i.e. credit; by implication, to entrust (especially one's spiritual well-being to Christ). In the KJV it is rendered: believe(-r), commit (to trust), put in trust with.
G4101: From πίστις; trustworthy, i.e. genuine (unadulterated). In the KJV it is rendered: spike-(nard).
G4102: From πείθω; persuasion, i.e. credence; moral conviction (of religious truth, or the truthfulness of God or a religious teacher), especially reliance upon Christ for salvation; abstractly, constancy in such profession; by extension, the system of religious (Gospel) truth itself. In the KJV it is rendered: assurance, belief, believe, faith, fidelity.
G4103: From πείθω; objectively, trustworthy; subjectively, trustful. In the KJV it is rendered: believe(-ing, -r), faithful(-ly), sure, true.
G4104: From πιστός; to assure. In the KJV it is rendered: assure of.
G4105: From πλάνη; to (properly, cause to) roam (from safety, truth, or virtue). In the KJV it is rendered: go astray, deceive, err, seduce, wander, be out of the way.
G4106: Feminine of πλάνος (as abstractly); objectively, fraudulence; subjectively, a straying from orthodoxy or piety. In the KJV it is rendered: deceit, to deceive, delusion, error.
G4107: From πλάνος; a rover ("planet"), i.e. (figuratively) an erratic teacher. In the KJV it is rendered: wandering.
G4108: Of uncertain affinity; roving (as a tramp), i.e. (by implication) an impostor or misleader; --deceiver, seducing.
G4109: From πλάσσω; a moulding-board, i.e. flat surface ("plate", or tablet, literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: table.
G4110: From πλάσσω; something moulded. In the KJV it is rendered: thing formed.
G4111: A primary verb; to mould, i.e. shape or fabricate. In the KJV it is rendered: form.
G4112: From πλάσσω; moulded, i.e. (by implication) artificial or (figuratively) fictitious (false). In the KJV it is rendered: feigned.
G4113: Feminine of πλατύς; a wide "plat" or "place", i.e. open square. In the KJV it is rendered: street.
G4114: From πλατύς; width. In the KJV it is rendered: breadth.
G4115: From πλατύς; to widen (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: make broad, enlarge.
G4116: From πλάσσω; spread out "flat" ("plot"), i.e. broad. In the KJV it is rendered: wide.
G4117: From πλέκω; a plait (of hair). In the KJV it is rendered: broidered hair.
G4118: Irregular superlative of πολύς; the largest number or very large. In the KJV it is rendered: very great, most.
G4119: Or neuter pleion, or pleon comparative of πολύς; more in quantity, number, or quality; also (in plural) the major portion. In the KJV it is rendered: X above, + exceed, more excellent, further, (very) great(-er), long(-er), (very) many, greater (more) part, + yet but.
G4120: A primary word; to twine or braid. In the KJV it is rendered: plait.
G4121: From πλείων; to do, make or be more, i.e. increase (transitively or intransitively); by extension, to superabound. In the KJV it is rendered: abound, abundant, make to increase, have over.
G4122: From πλεονέκτης; to be covetous, i.e. (by implication) to over-reach. In the KJV it is rendered: get an advantage, defraud, make a gain.
G4123: From πλείων and ἔχω; holding (desiring) more, i.e. eager for gain (avaricious, hence a defrauder). In the KJV it is rendered: covetous.
G4124: From πλεονέκτης; avarice, i.e. (by implication) fraudulency, extortion. In the KJV it is rendered: covetous(-ness) practices, greediness.
G4125: Of uncertain affinity; a rib, i.e. (by extension) side. In the KJV it is rendered: side.
G4126: Another form for pleuo plyoo'-o; which is used as an alternate in certain tenses; probably a form of πλύνω (through the idea of plunging through the water); to pass in a vessel. In the KJV it is rendered: sail.
G4127: From πλήσσω; a stroke; by implication, a wound; figuratively, a calamity. In the KJV it is rendered: plague, stripe, wound(-ed).
G4128: From πλήθω; a fulness, i.e. a large number, throng, populace. In the KJV it is rendered: bundle, company, multitude.
G4129: From another form of πλῆθος; to increase (transitively or intransitively). In the KJV it is rendered: abound, multiply.
G4130: A prolonged form of a primary pleo (which appears only as an alternate in certain tenses and in the reduplicated form pimplemi); to "fill" (literally or figuratively (imbue, influence, supply)); specially, to fulfil (time). In the KJV it is rendered: accomplish, full (…come), furnish.
G4131: From πλήσσω; a smiter, i.e. pugnacious (quarrelsome). In the KJV it is rendered: striker.
G4132: Prolonged from πλήθω; flood-tide, i.e. (by analogy) a freshet. In the KJV it is rendered: flood.
G4133: From πλείων; moreover (besides), i.e. albeit, save that, rather, yet. In the KJV it is rendered: but (rather), except, nevertheless, notwithstanding, save, than.
G4134: From πλήθω; replete, or covered over; by analogy, complete. In the KJV it is rendered: full.
G4135: From πλήρης and φορέω; to carry out fully (in evidence), i.e. completely assure (or convince), entirely accomplish. In the KJV it is rendered: most surely believe, fully know (persuade), make full proof of.
G4136: From πληροφορέω; entire confidence. In the KJV it is rendered: (full) assurance.
G4137: From πλήρης; to make replete, i.e. (literally) to cram (a net), level up (a hollow), or (figuratively) to furnish (or imbue, diffuse, influence), satisfy, execute (an office), finish (a period or task), verify (or coincide with a prediction), etc. In the KJV it is rendered: accomplish, X after, (be) complete, end, expire, fill (up), fulfil, (be, make) full (come), fully preach, perfect, supply.
G4138: From πληρόω; repletion or completion, i.e. (subjectively) what fills (as contents, supplement, copiousness, multitude), or (objectively) what is filled (as container, performance, period). In the KJV it is rendered: which is put in to fill up, piece that filled up, fulfilling, full, fulness.
G4139: Neuter of a derivative of pelas (near); (adverbially) close by; as noun, a neighbor, i.e. fellow (as man, countryman, Christian or friend). In the KJV it is rendered: near, neighbour.
G4140: From a presumed derivative of πλήθω; a filling up, i.e. (figuratively) gratification. In the KJV it is rendered: satisfying.
G4141: Apparently another form of πλάσσω (through the idea of flattening out); to pound, i.e. (figuratively) to inflict with (calamity). In the KJV it is rendered: smite.
G4142: Neuter of a presumed derivative of πλοῖον; a boat. In the KJV it is rendered: boat, little (small) ship.
G4143: From πλέω; a sailer, i.e. vessel. In the KJV it is rendered: ship(-ing).
G4144: From πλέω; a sail, i.e. navigation. In the KJV it is rendered: course, sailing, voyage.
G4145: From πλοῦτος; wealthy; figuratively, abounding with. In the KJV it is rendered: rich.
G4146: Adverb from πλούσιος; copiously. In the KJV it is rendered: abundantly, richly.
G4147: From πλουτίζω; to be (or become) wealthy (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: be increased with goods, (be made, wax) rich.
G4148: From πλοῦτος; to make wealthy (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: en- (make) rich.
G4149: From the base of πλήθω; wealth (as fulness), i.e. (literally) money, possessions, or (figuratively) abundance, richness, (specially), valuable bestowment. In the KJV it is rendered: riches.
G4150: A prolonged form of an obsolete pluo (to "flow"); to "plunge", i.e. launder clothing. In the KJV it is rendered: wash.
G4151: From πνέω; a current of air, i.e. breath (blast) or a breeze; by analogy or figuratively, a spirit, i.e. (human) the rational soul, (by implication) vital principle, mental disposition, etc., or (superhuman) an angel, demon, or (divine) God, Christ's spirit, the Holy Spirit. In the KJV it is rendered: ghost, life, spirit(-ual, -ually), mind.
G4152: From πνεῦμα; non-carnal, i.e. (humanly) ethereal (as opposed to gross), or (dæmoniacally) a spirit (concretely), or (divinely) supernatural, regenerate, religious. In the KJV it is rendered: spiritual.
G4153: Adverb from πνευματικός; non-physically, i.e. divinely, figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: spiritually.
G4154: A primary word; to breathe hard, i.e. breeze. In the KJV it is rendered: blow.
G4155: Strengthened from πνέω; to wheeze, i.e. (causative, by implication) to throttle or strangle (drown). In the KJV it is rendered: choke, take by the throat.
G4156: From πνίγω; throttled, i.e. (neuter concretely) an animal choked to death (not bled). In the KJV it is rendered: strangled.
G4157: From πνέω; respiration, a breeze. In the KJV it is rendered: breath, wind.
G4158: From πούς and another element of uncertain affinity; a dress (ἐσθής implied) reaching the ankles. In the KJV it is rendered: garment down to the foot.
G4159: From the base of πόσις with enclitic adverb of origin; from which (as interrogative) or what (as relative) place, state, source or cause. In the KJV it is rendered: whence.
G4160: Apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary; to make or do (in a very wide application, more or less direct). In the KJV it is rendered: abide, + agree, appoint, X avenge, + band together, be, bear, + bewray, bring (forth), cast out, cause, commit, + content, continue, deal, + without any delay, (would) do(-ing), execute, exercise, fulfil, gain, give, have, hold, X journeying, keep, + lay wait, + lighten the ship, make, X mean, + none of these things move me, observe, ordain, perform, provide, + have purged, purpose, put, + raising up, X secure, shew, X shoot out, spend, take, tarry, + transgress the law, work, yield.
G4161: From ποιέω; a product, i.e. fabric (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: thing that is made, workmanship.
G4162: From ποιέω; action, i.e. performance (of the law). In the KJV it is rendered: deed.
G4163: From ποιέω; a performer; specially, a "poet"; --doer, poet.
G4164: Of uncertain derivation; motley, i.e. various in character. In the KJV it is rendered: divers, manifold.
G4165: From ποιμήν; to tend as a shepherd of (figuratively, superviser). In the KJV it is rendered: feed (cattle), rule.
G4166: Of uncertain affinity; a shepherd (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: shepherd, pastor.
G4167: Contraction from ποιμαίνω; a flock (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: flock, fold.
G4168: Neuter of a presumed derivative of ποίμνη; a flock, i.e. (figuratively) group (of believers). In the KJV it is rendered: flock.
G4169: From the base of ποῦ and οἷος; individualizing interrogative (of character) what sort of, or (of number) which one. In the KJV it is rendered: what (manner of), which.
G4170: From πόλεμος; to be (engaged) in warfare, i.e. to battle (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: fight, (make) war.
G4171: From pelomai (to bustle); warfare (literally or figuratively; a single encounter or a series). In the KJV it is rendered: battle, fight, war.
G4172: Probably from the same as πόλεμος, or perhaps from πολύς; a town (properly, with walls, of greater or less size). In the KJV it is rendered: city.
G4173: From πόλις and ἄρχω; a town-officer, i.e. magistrate. In the KJV it is rendered: ruler of the city.
G4174: From πολίτης ("polity"); citizenship; concretely, a community. In the KJV it is rendered: commonwealth, freedom.
G4175: From πολιτεύομαι; a community, i.e. (abstractly) citizenship (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: conversation.
G4176: Middle voice of a derivative of πολίτης; to behave as a citizen (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: let conversation be, live.
G4177: From πόλις; a townsman. In the KJV it is rendered: citizen.
G4178: Multiplicative adverb from πολύς; many times, i.e. frequently. In the KJV it is rendered: oft(-en, -entimes, -times).
G4179: From πολύς and probably a derivative of πλέκω; manifold, i.e. (neuter as noun) very much more. In the KJV it is rendered: manifold more.
G4180: From a compound of πολύς and λόγος; loquacity, i.e. prolixity. In the KJV it is rendered: much speaking.
G4181: Adverb from a compound of πολύς and μέρος; in many portions, i.e. variously as to time and agency (piecemeal). In the KJV it is rendered: at sundry times.
G4182: From πολύς and ποικίλος; much variegated, i.e. multifarious. In the KJV it is rendered: manifold.
G4183: Including the forms from the alternate pollos; (singular) much (in any respect) or (plural) many; neuter (singular) as adverbial, largely; neuter (plural) as adverb or noun often, mostly, largely. In the KJV it is rendered: abundant, + altogether, common, + far (passed, spent), (+ be of a) great (age, deal, -ly, while), long, many, much, oft(-en (-times)), plenteous, sore, straitly.
G4184: From πολύς and σπλάγχνον (figuratively); extremely compassionate. In the KJV it is rendered: very pitiful.
G4185: From πολύς and τέλος; extremely expensive. In the KJV it is rendered: costly, very precious, of great price.
G4186: From πολύς and τιμή; extremely valuable. In the KJV it is rendered: very costly, of great price.
G4187: Adverb from a compound of πολύς and τρόπος; in many ways, i.e. variously as to method or form. In the KJV it is rendered: in divers manners.
G4188: From the alternate of πίνω; a beverage. In the KJV it is rendered: drink.
G4189: From πονηρός; depravity, i.e. (specially), malice; plural (concretely) plots, sins. In the KJV it is rendered: iniquity, wickedness.
G4190: From a derivative of πόνος; hurtful, i.e. evil (properly, in effect or influence, and thus differing from κακός, which refers rather to essential character, as well as from σαπρός, which indicates degeneracy from original virtue); figuratively, calamitous; also (passively) ill, i.e. diseased; but especially (morally) culpable, i.e. derelict, vicious, facinorous; neuter (singular) mischief, malice, or (plural) guilt; masculine (singular) the devil, or (plural) sinners. In the KJV it is rendered: bad, evil, grievous, harm, lewd, malicious, wicked(-ness).
G4191: Comparative of πονηρός; more evil. In the KJV it is rendered: more wicked.
G4192: From the base of πένης; toil, i.e. (by implication) anguish. In the KJV it is rendered: pain.
G4193: From Πόντος; a Pontican, i.e. native of Pontus. In the KJV it is rendered: born in Pontus.
G4194: Of Latin origin; apparently bridged; Pontius, a Roman. In the KJV it is rendered: Pontius.
G4195: Of Latin origin; a sea; Pontus, a region of Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Pontus.
G4196: Of Latin origin; apparently "popular"; Poplius (i.e. Publius), a Roman. In the KJV it is rendered: Publius.
G4197: From πορεύομαι; travel (by land); figuratively (plural) proceedings, i.e. career. In the KJV it is rendered: journey(-ing), ways.
G4198: Middle voice from a derivative of the same as πεῖρα; to traverse, i.e. travel (literally or figuratively; especially to remove (figuratively, die), live, etc.); --depart, go (away, forth, one's way, up), (make a, take a) journey, walk.
G4199: Prolongation from pertho (to sack); to ravage (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: destroy, waste.
G4200: From a derivative of poros (a way, i.e. means); furnishing (procuring), i.e. (by implication) money-getting (acquisition). In the KJV it is rendered: gain.
G4201: Of Latin origin; apparently swinish; Porcius, a Roman. In the KJV it is rendered: Porcius.
G4202: From πορνεύω; harlotry (including adultery and incest); figuratively, idolatry. In the KJV it is rendered: fornication.
G4203: From πόρνη; to act the harlot, i.e. (literally) indulge unlawful lust (of either sex), or (figuratively) practise idolatry. In the KJV it is rendered: commit (fornication).
G4204: Feminine of πόρνος; a strumpet; figuratively, an idolater. In the KJV it is rendered: harlot, whore.
G4205: From pernemi (to sell; akin to the base of πιπράσκω); a (male) prostitute (as venal), i.e. (by analogy) a debauchee (libertine). In the KJV it is rendered: fornicator, whoremonger.
G4206: Adverb from πρό; forwards, i.e. at a distance. In the KJV it is rendered: far, a great way off.
G4207: From πόῤῥω with adverbial enclitic of source; from far, or (by implication) at a distance, i.e. distantly. In the KJV it is rendered: afar off.
G4208: Adverb comparative of πόῤῥω; further, i.e. a greater distance. In the KJV it is rendered: farther.
G4209: Of Latin origin; the "purple" mussel, i.e. (by implication) the red-blue color itself, and finally a garment dyed with it. In the KJV it is rendered: purple.
G4210: From πορφύρα; purpureal, i.e. bluish red. In the KJV it is rendered: purple.
G4211: Feminine of a compound of πορφύρα and πωλέω; a female trader in purple cloth. In the KJV it is rendered: seller of purple.
G4212: Multiplicative from πόσος; how many times. In the KJV it is rendered: how oft(-en).
G4213: From the alternate of πίνω; a drinking (the act), i.e. (concretely) a draught. In the KJV it is rendered: drink.
G4214: From an absolute pos (who, what) and ὅς; interrogative pronoun (of amount) how much (large, long or (plural) many). In the KJV it is rendered: how great (long, many), what.
G4215: Probably from a derivative of the alternate of πίνω (compare πότος); a current, brook or freshet (as drinkable), i.e. running water. In the KJV it is rendered: flood, river, stream, water.
G4216: From ποταμός and a derivative of φορέω; river-borne, i.e. overwhelmed by a stream. In the KJV it is rendered: carried away of the flood.
G4217: Apparently from πότε and the base of ποῦ; interrogatively, whatever, i.e. of what possible sort. In the KJV it is rendered: what (manner of).
G4218: From the base of πού and τέ; indefinite adverb, at some time, ever. In the KJV it is rendered: afore-(any, some-)time(-s), at length (the last), (+ n-)ever, in the old time, in time past, once, when.
G4219: From the base of ποῦ and τέ; interrogative adverb, at what time. In the KJV it is rendered: + how long, when.
G4220: Neuter of a comparative of the base of ποῦ; interrogative as adverb, which (of two), i.e. is it this or that. In the KJV it is rendered: whether.
G4221: Neuter of a derivative of the alternate of πίνω; a drinking-vessel; by extension, the contents thereof, i.e. a cupful (draught); figuratively, a lot or fate. In the KJV it is rendered: cup.
G4222: From a derivative of the alternate of πίνω; to furnish drink, irrigate. In the KJV it is rendered: give (make) to drink, feed, water.
G4223: Of Latin origin; little wells, i.e. mineral springs; Potioli (i.e. Puteoli), a place in Italy. In the KJV it is rendered: Puteoli.
G4224: From the alternate of πίνω; a drinking-bout or carousal. In the KJV it is rendered: banqueting.
G4225: Genitive case of an indefinite pronoun pos (some) otherwise obsolete (compare πόσος); as adverb of place, somewhere, i.e. nearly. In the KJV it is rendered: about, a certain place.
G4226: Genitive case of an interrogative pronoun pos (what) otherwise obsolete (perhaps the same as πού used with the rising slide of inquiry); as adverb of place; at (by implication, to) what locality. In the KJV it is rendered: where, whither.
G4227: Of Latin origin; modest; Pudes (i.e. Pudens), a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Pudens.
G4228: A primary word; a "foot" (figuratively or literally). In the KJV it is rendered: foot(-stool).
G4229: From πράσσω; a deed; by implication, an affair; by extension, an object (material). In the KJV it is rendered: business, matter, thing, work.
G4230: From πραγματεύομαι; a transaction, i.e. negotiation. In the KJV it is rendered: affair.
G4231: From πρᾶγμα; to busy oneself with, i.e. to trade. In the KJV it is rendered: occupy.
G4232: Of Latin origin; the prætorium or governor's courtroom (sometimes including the whole edifice and camp). In the KJV it is rendered: (common, judgment) hall (of judgment), palace, prætorium.
G4233: From a derivative of πράσσω; a practiser, i.e. (specially), an official collector. In the KJV it is rendered: officer.
G4234: From πράσσω; practice, i.e. (concretely) an act; by extension, a function. In the KJV it is rendered: deed, office, work.
G4235: A form of πραΰς, used in certain parts; gentle, i.e. humble. In the KJV it is rendered: meek.
G4236: From πρᾷος; gentleness, by implication, humility. In the KJV it is rendered: meekness.
G4237: Perhaps from prason (a leek, and so an onion-patch); a garden plot, i.e. (by implication, of regular beds) a row (repeated in plural by Hebraism, to indicate an arrangement). In the KJV it is rendered: in ranks.
G4238: A primary verb; to "practise", i.e. perform repeatedly or habitually (thus differing from ποιέω, which properly refers to a single act); by implication, to execute, accomplish, etc.; specially, to collect (dues), fare (personally). In the KJV it is rendered: commit, deeds, do, exact, keep, require, use arts.
G4239: Apparently a primary word; mild, i.e. (by implication) humble. In the KJV it is rendered: meek.
G4240: From πραΰς; mildness, i.e. (by implication) humility. In the KJV it is rendered: meekness.
G4241: Apparently a primary verb; to tower up (be conspicuous), i.e. (by implication) to be suitable or proper (third person singular present indicative, often used impersonally, it is fit or right). In the KJV it is rendered: become, comely.
G4242: From πρεσβεύω; seniority (eldership), i.e. (by implication) an embassy (concretely, ambassadors). In the KJV it is rendered: ambassage, message.
G4243: From the base of πρεσβύτερος; to be a senior, i.e. (by implication) act as a representative (figuratively, preacher). In the KJV it is rendered: be an ambassador.
G4244: Neuter of a presumed derivative of πρεσβύτερος; the order of elders, i.e. (specially), Israelite Sanhedrin or Christian "presbytery". In the KJV it is rendered: (estate of) elder(-s), presbytery.
G4245: Comparative of presbus (elderly); older; as noun, a senior; specially, an Israelite Sanhedrist (also figuratively, member of the celestial council) or Christian "presbyter". In the KJV it is rendered: elder(-est), old.
G4246: From the same as πρεσβύτερος; an old man. In the KJV it is rendered: aged (man), old man.
G4247: Feminine of πρεσβύτης; an old woman. In the KJV it is rendered: aged woman.
G4248: From πρό; leaning (falling) forward ("prone"), i.e. head foremost. In the KJV it is rendered: headlong.
G4249: A strengthened form of a primary prio (to saw); to saw in two. In the KJV it is rendered: saw asunder.
G4250: Adverb from πρό; prior, sooner. In the KJV it is rendered: before (that), ere.
G4251: Of Latin origin; feminine of Priscus, ancient; Priska, a Christian woman. In the KJV it is rendered: Prisca.
G4252: Diminutive of Πρίσκα; Priscilla (i.e. little Prisca), a Christian woman. In the KJV it is rendered: Priscilla.
G4253: A primary preposition; "fore", i.e. in front of, prior (figuratively, superior) to. In the KJV it is rendered: above, ago, before, or ever.
G4254: From πρό and ἄγω; to lead forward (magisterially); intransitively, to precede (in place or time (participle, previous)). In the KJV it is rendered: bring (forth, out), go before.
G4255: From πρό and αἱρέομαι; to choose for oneself before another thing (prefer), i.e. (by implication) to propose (intend). In the KJV it is rendered: purpose.
G4256: From πρό and a derivative of αἰτία; to accuse already, i.e. previously charge. In the KJV it is rendered: prove before.
G4257: From πρό and ἀκούω; to hear already,i.e. anticipate. In the KJV it is rendered: hear before.
G4258: From πρό and ἁμαρτάνω; to sin previously (to conversion). In the KJV it is rendered: sin already, heretofore sin.
G4259: Neuter of a presumed compound of πρό and αὐλή; a forecourt, i.e. vestibule (alley-way). In the KJV it is rendered: porch.
G4260: From πρό and the base of βάσις; to walk forward, i.e. advance (literally, or in years). In the KJV it is rendered: + be of a great age, go farther (on), be well stricken.
G4261: From πρό and βάλλω; to throw forward, i.e. push to the front, germinate. In the KJV it is rendered: put forward, shoot forth.
G4262: From πρόβατον; relating to sheep, i.e. (a gate) through which they were led into Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: sheep (market).
G4263: Probably neuter of a presumed derivative of προβαίνω; something that walks forward (a quadruped), i.e. (specially), a sheep (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: sheep(-fold).
G4264: From πρό and a reduplicated form of βιάζω; to force forward, i.e. bring to the front, instigate. In the KJV it is rendered: draw, before instruct.
G4265: From πρό and βλέπω; to look out beforehand, i.e. furnish in advance. In the KJV it is rendered: provide.
G4266: From πρό and γίνομαι; to be already, i.e. have previousy transpired. In the KJV it is rendered: be past.
G4267: From πρό and γινώσκω; to know beforehand, i.e. foresee. In the KJV it is rendered: foreknow (ordain), know (before).
G4268: From προγινώσκω; forethought. In the KJV it is rendered: foreknowledge.
G4269: From προγίνομαι; an ancestor, (grand-)parent. In the KJV it is rendered: forefather, parent.
G4270: From πρό and γράφω; to write previously; figuratively, to announce, prescribe. In the KJV it is rendered: before ordain, evidently set forth, write (afore, aforetime).
G4271: From πρό and δῆλος; plain before all men, i.e. obvious. In the KJV it is rendered: evident, manifest (open) beforehand.
G4272: From πρό and δίδωμι; to give before the other party has given. In the KJV it is rendered: first give.
G4273: From προδίδωμι (in the sense of giving forward into another's (the enemy's) hands); a surrender. In the KJV it is rendered: betrayer, traitor.
G4274: From the alternate of προτρέχω; a runner ahead, i.e. scout (figuratively, precursor). In the KJV it is rendered: forerunner.
G4275: From πρό and εἴδω; foresee. In the KJV it is rendered: foresee, saw before.
G4276: From πρό and ἐλπίζω; to hope in advance of other confirmation. In the KJV it is rendered: first trust.
G4277: From πρό and ἔπω; to say already, to predict. In the KJV it is rendered: forewarn, say (speak, tell) before.
G4278: From πρό and ἐνάρχομαι; to commence already. In the KJV it is rendered: begin (before).
G4279: Middle voice from πρό and ἐπαγγέλλω; to promise of old. In the KJV it is rendered: promise before.
G4280: From πρό and ἐρέω; used as alternate of προέπω; to say already, predict. In the KJV it is rendered: foretell, say (speak, tell) before.
G4281: From πρό and ἔρχομαι (including its alternate); to go onward, precede (in place or time). In the KJV it is rendered: go before (farther, forward), outgo, pass on.
G4282: From πρό and ἑτοιμάζω; to fit up in advance (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: ordain before, prepare afore.
G4283: Middle voice from πρό and εὐαγγελίζω; to announce glad news in advance. In the KJV it is rendered: preach before the gospel.
G4284: Middle voice from πρό and ἔχω; to hold oneself before others, i.e. (figuratively) to excel. In the KJV it is rendered: be better.
G4285: From πρό and ἡγέομαι; to lead the way for others, i.e. show deference. In the KJV it is rendered: prefer.
G4286: From προτίθεμαι; a setting forth, i.e. (figuratively) proposal (intention); specially, the show-bread (in the Temple) as exposed before God. In the KJV it is rendered: purpose, shew(-bread).
G4287: From πρό and a derivative of τίθημι; fixed beforehand, i.e. (feminine with ἡμέρα implied) a designated day. In the KJV it is rendered: time appointed.
G4288: From πρόθυμος; predisposition, i.e. alacrity. In the KJV it is rendered: forwardness of mind, readiness (of mind), ready (willing) mind.
G4289: From πρό and θυμός; forward in spirit, i.e. predisposed; neuter (as noun) alacrity. In the KJV it is rendered: ready, willing.
G4290: Adverb from πρόθυμος; with alacrity. In the KJV it is rendered: willingly.
G4291: From πρό and ἵστημι; to stand before, i.e. (in rank) to preside, or (by implication) to practise. In the KJV it is rendered: maintain, be over, rule.
G4292: Middle voice from πρό and καλέω; to call forth to oneself (challenge), i.e. (by implication) to irritate. In the KJV it is rendered: provoke.
G4293: From πρό and καταγγέλλω; to anounce beforehand, i.e. predict, promise. In the KJV it is rendered: foretell, have notice, (shew) before.
G4294: From πρό and καταρτίζω; to prepare in advance. In the KJV it is rendered: make up beforehand.
G4295: From πρό and κεῖμαι; to lie before the view, i.e. (figuratively) to be present (to the mind), to stand forth (as an example or reward). In the KJV it is rendered: be first, set before (forth).
G4296: From πρό and κηρύσσω; to herald (i.e. proclaim) in advance. In the KJV it is rendered: before (first) preach.
G4297: From προκόπτω; progress, i.e. advancement (subjectively or objectively). In the KJV it is rendered: furtherance, profit.
G4298: From πρό and κόπτω; to drive forward (as if by beating), i.e. (figuratively and intransitively) to advance (in amount, to grow; in time, to be well along). In the KJV it is rendered: increase, proceed, profit, be far spent, wax.
G4299: From a compound of πρό and κρίνω; a prejudgment (prejudice), i.e. prepossession. In the KJV it is rendered: prefer one before another.
G4300: From πρό and κυρόω; to ratify previously. In the KJV it is rendered: confirm before.
G4301: From πρό and λαμβάνω; to take in advance, i.e. (literally) eat before others have an opportunity; (figuratively) to anticipate, surprise. In the KJV it is rendered: come aforehand, overtake, take before.
G4302: From πρό and λέγω; to say beforehand, i.e. predict, forewarn. In the KJV it is rendered: foretell, tell before.
G4303: From πρό and μαρτύρομαι; to be a witness in advance i.e. predict. In the KJV it is rendered: testify beforehand.
G4304: From πρό and μελετάω; to premeditate. In the KJV it is rendered: meditate before.
G4305: From πρό and μεριμνάω; to care (anxiously) in advance. In the KJV it is rendered: take thought beforehand.
G4306: From πρό and νοιέω; to consider in advance, i.e. look out for beforehand (actively, by way of maintenance for others; middle voice by way of circumspection for oneself). In the KJV it is rendered: provide (for).
G4307: From προνοέω; forethought, i.e. provident care or supply. In the KJV it is rendered: providence, provision.
G4308: From πρό and ὁράω; to behold in advance, i.e. (actively) to notice (another) previously, or (middle voice) to keep in (one's own) view. In the KJV it is rendered: foresee, see before.
G4309: From πρό and ὁρίζω; to limit in advance, i.e. (figuratively) predetermine. In the KJV it is rendered: determine before, ordain, predestinate.
G4310: From πρό and πάσχω; to undergo hardship previously. In the KJV it is rendered: suffer before.
G4311: From πρό and πέμπω; to send forward, i.e. escort or aid in travel. In the KJV it is rendered: accompany, bring (forward) on journey (way), conduct forth.
G4312: From a compound of πρό and πίπτω; falling forward, i.e. headlong (figuratively, precipitate). In the KJV it is rendered: heady, rash(-ly).
G4313: From πρό and πορεύομαι; to precede (as guide or herald). In the KJV it is rendered: go before.
G4314: A strengthened form of πρό; a preposition of direction; forward to, i.e. toward (with the genitive case, the side of, i.e. pertaining to; with the dative case, by the side of, i.e. near to; usually with the accusative case, the place, time, occasion, or respect, which is the destination of the relation, i.e. whither or for which it is predicated). In the KJV it is rendered: about, according to, against, among, at, because of, before, between, (where-)by, for, X at thy house, in, for intent, nigh unto, of, which pertain to, that, to (the end that), X together, to (you) -ward, unto, with(-in).
G4315: From πρό and σάββατον; a fore-sabbath, i.e. the Sabbath-eve. In the KJV it is rendered: day before the sabbath.
G4316: From πρός and a derivative of ἀγορά (mean to harangue); to address, i.e. salute by name. In the KJV it is rendered: call.
G4317: From πρός and ἄγω; to lead towards, i.e. (transitively) to conduct near (summon, present), or (intransitively) to approach. In the KJV it is rendered: bring, draw near.
G4318: From προσάγω (compare ἀγωγή); admission. In the KJV it is rendered: access.
G4319: From πρός and αἰτέω; to ask repeatedly (importune), i.e. solicit. In the KJV it is rendered: beg.
G4320: From πρός and ἀναβαίνω; to ascend farther, i.e. be promoted (take an upper (more honorable) seat). In the KJV it is rendered: go up.
G4321: From πρός and ἀναλίσκω; to expend further. In the KJV it is rendered: spend.
G4322: From πρός and ἀναπληρόω; to fill up further, i.e. furnish fully. In the KJV it is rendered: supply.
G4323: From πρός and ἀνατίθεμαι; to lay up in addition, i.e. (middle voice and figuratively) to impart or (by implication) to consult. In the KJV it is rendered: in conference add, confer.
G4324: From πρός and ἀπειλέω; to menace additionally. In the KJV it is rendered: i.
G4325: From πρός and δαπανάω; to expend additionally. In the KJV it is rendered: spend more.
G4326: From πρός and δέομαι; to require additionally, i.e. want further. In the KJV it is rendered: need.
G4327: From πρός and δέχομαι; to admit (to intercourse, hospitality, credence, or (figuratively) endurance); by implication, to await (with confidence or patience). In the KJV it is rendered: accept, allow, look (wait) for, take.
G4328: From πρός and dokeuo (to watch); to anticipate (in thought, hope or fear); by implication, to await. In the KJV it is rendered: (be in) expect(-ation), look (for), when looked, tarry, wait for.
G4329: From προσδοκάω; apprehension (of evil); by implication, infliction anticipated. In the KJV it is rendered: expectation, looking after.
G4330: From πρός and ἐάω; to permit further progress. In the KJV it is rendered: suffer.
G4331: From πρός and ἐγγίζω; to approach near. In the KJV it is rendered: come nigh.
G4332: From a compound of πρός and the base of ἑδραῖος; to sit near, i.e. attend as a servant. In the KJV it is rendered: wait at.
G4333: From πρός and ἐργάζομαι; to work additionally, i.e. (by implication) acquire besides. In the KJV it is rendered: gain.
G4334: From πρός and ἔρχομαι (including its alternate); to approach, i.e. (literally) come near, visit, or (figuratively) worship, assent to. In the KJV it is rendered: (as soon as he) come (unto), come thereunto, consent, draw near, go (near, to, unto).
G4335: From προσεύχομαι; prayer (worship); by implication, an oratory (chapel). In the KJV it is rendered: X pray earnestly, prayer.
G4336: From πρός and εὔχομαι; to pray to God, i.e. supplicate, worship. In the KJV it is rendered: pray (X earnestly, for), make prayer.
G4337: From πρός and ἔχω; (figuratively) to hold the mind (νοῦς implied) towards, i.e. pay attention to, be cautious about, apply oneself to, adhere to. In the KJV it is rendered: (give) attend(-ance, -ance at, -ance to, unto), beware, be given to, give (take) heed (to unto); have regard.
G4338: From πρός and a derivative of ἧλος; to peg to, i.e. spike fast. In the KJV it is rendered: nail to.
G4339: From the alternate of προσέρχομαι; an arriver from a foreign region, i.e. (specially), an acceder (convert) to Judaism ("proselyte"). In the KJV it is rendered: proselyte.
G4340: From πρός and καιρός; for the occasion only, i.e. temporary. In the KJV it is rendered: dur-(eth) for awhile, endure for a time, for a season, temporal.
G4341: Middle voice from πρός and καλέω; to call toward oneself, i.e. summon, invite. In the KJV it is rendered: call (for, to, unto).
G4342: From πρός and καρτερέω; to be earnest towards, i.e. (to a thing) to persevere, be constantly diligent, or (in a place) to attend assiduously all the exercises, or (to a person) to adhere closely to (as a servitor). In the KJV it is rendered: attend (give self) continually (upon), continue (in, instant in, with), wait on (continually).
G4343: From προσκαρτερέω; persistancy. In the KJV it is rendered: perseverance.
G4344: Neuter of a presumed compound of πρός and κεφαλή; something for the head, i.e. a cushion. In the KJV it is rendered: pillow.
G4345: From πρός and κληρόω; to give a common lot to, i.e. (figuratively) to associate with. In the KJV it is rendered: consort with.
G4346: From a compound of πρός and κλίνω; a leaning towards, i.e. (figuratively) proclivity (favoritism). In the KJV it is rendered: partiality.
G4347: From πρός and κολλάω; to glue to, i.e. (figuratively) to adhere. In the KJV it is rendered: cleave, join (self).
G4348: From προσκόπτω; a stub, i.e. (figuratively) occasion of apostasy. In the KJV it is rendered: offence, stumbling(-block, (-stone)).
G4349: From προσκόπτω; a stumbling, i.e. (figuratively and concretely) occasion of sin. In the KJV it is rendered: offence.
G4350: From πρός and κόπτω; to strike at, i.e. surge against (as water); specially, to stub on, i.e. trip up (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: beat upon, dash, stumble (at).
G4351: From πρός and κυλιόω; to roll towards, i.e. block against. In the KJV it is rendered: roll (to).
G4352: From πρός and a probable derivative of κύων (meaning to kiss, like a dog licking his master's hand); to fawn or crouch to, i.e. (literally or figuratively) prostrate oneself in homage (do reverence to, adore). In the KJV it is rendered: worship.
G4353: From προσκυνέω; an adorer. In the KJV it is rendered: worshipper.
G4354: From πρός and λαλέω; to talk to, i.e. converse with. In the KJV it is rendered: speak to (with).
G4355: From πρός and λαμβάνω; to take to oneself, i.e. use (food), lead (aside), admit (to friendship or hospitality). In the KJV it is rendered: receive, take (unto).
G4356: From προσλαμβάνω; admission. In the KJV it is rendered: receiving.
G4357: From πρός and μένω; to stay further, i.e. remain in a place, with a person; figuratively, to adhere to, persevere in. In the KJV it is rendered: abide still, be with, cleave unto, continue in (with).
G4358: From πρός and a derivative of the same as ὁρμή (meaning to tie (anchor) or lull); to moor to, i.e. (by implication) land at. In the KJV it is rendered: draw to the shore.
G4359: From πρός and ὀφείλω; to be indebted additionally. In the KJV it is rendered: over besides.
G4360: From πρός and a form of ochtheo (to be vexed with something irksome); to feel indignant at. In the KJV it is rendered: be grieved at.
G4361: From πρός and the same as πεινάω; hungering further, i.e. intensely hungry. In the KJV it is rendered: very hungry.
G4362: From πρός and πήγνυμι; to fasten to, i.e. (specially), to impale (on a cross). In the KJV it is rendered: crucify.
G4363: From πρός and πίπτω; to fall towards, i.e. (gently) prostrate oneself (in supplication or homage), or (violently) to rush upon (in storm). In the KJV it is rendered: beat upon, fall (down) at (before).
G4364: Middle voice from πρός and ποιέω; to do forward for oneself, i.e. pretend (as if about to do a thing). In the KJV it is rendered: make as though.
G4365: From πρός and πορεύομαι; to journey towards, i.e. approach (not the same as προπορεύομαι). In the KJV it is rendered: go before.
G4366: From πρός and ῥήγνυμι; to tear towards, i.e. burst upon (as a tempest or flood). In the KJV it is rendered: beat vehemently against (upon).
G4367: From πρός and τάσσω; to arrange towards, i.e. (figuratively) enjoin. In the KJV it is rendered: bid, command.
G4368: Feminine of a derivative of προΐστημι; a patroness, i.e. assistant. In the KJV it is rendered: succourer.
G4369: From πρός and τίθημι; to place additionally, i.e. lay beside, annex, repeat. In the KJV it is rendered: add, again, give more, increase, lay unto, proceed further, speak to any more.
G4370: From πρός and τρέχω (including its alternate); to run towards, i.e. hasten to meet or join. In the KJV it is rendered: run (thither to, to).
G4371: Neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of πρός and φάγω; something eaten in addition to bread, i.e. a relish (specially, fish; compare ὀψάριον). In the KJV it is rendered: meat.
G4372: From πρό and a derivative of σφάζω; previously (recently) slain (fresh), i.e. (figuratively) lately made. In the KJV it is rendered: new.
G4373: Adverb from πρόσφατος; recently. In the KJV it is rendered: lately.
G4374: From πρός and φέρω (including its alternate); to bear towards, i.e. lead to, tender (especially to God), treat. In the KJV it is rendered: bring (to, unto), deal with, do, offer (unto, up), present unto, put to.
G4375: From a presumed compound of πρός and φιλέω; friendly towards, i.e. acceptable. In the KJV it is rendered: lovely.
G4376: From προσφέρω; presentation; concretely, an oblation (bloodless) or sacrifice. In the KJV it is rendered: offering (up).
G4377: From πρός and φωνέω; to sound towards, i.e. address, exclaim, summon. In the KJV it is rendered: call unto, speak (un-)to.
G4378: From a comparative of πρός and cheo (to pour); a shedding forth, i.e. affusion. In the KJV it is rendered: sprinkling.
G4379: From πρός and psauo (to touch); to impinge, i.e. lay a finger on (in order to relieve). In the KJV it is rendered: touch.
G4380: From προσωπολήπτης; to favor an individual, i.e. show partiality. In the KJV it is rendered: have respect to persons.
G4381: From πρόσωπον and λαμβάνω; an accepter of a face (individual), i.e. (specially), one exhibiting partiality. In the KJV it is rendered: respecter of persons.
G4382: From προσωπολήπτης; partiality, i.e. favoritism. In the KJV it is rendered: respect of persons.
G4383: From πρός and ops (the visage, from ὀπτάνομαι); the front (as being towards view), i.e. the countenance, aspect, appearance, surface; by implication, presence, person. In the KJV it is rendered: (outward) appearance, X before, countenance, face, fashion, (men's) person, presence.
G4384: From πρό and τάσσω; to pre-arrange, i.e. prescribe. In the KJV it is rendered: before appoint.
G4385: From πρό and teino (to stretch); to protend, i.e. tie prostrate (for scourging). In the KJV it is rendered: bind.
G4386: Neuter of πρότερος as adverb (with or without the article); previously. In the KJV it is rendered: before, (at the) first, former.
G4387: Comparative of πρό; prior or previous. In the KJV it is rendered: former.
G4388: Middle voice from πρό and τίθημι; to place before, i.e. (for oneself) to exhibit; (to oneself) to propose (determine). In the KJV it is rendered: purpose, set forth.
G4389: Middle voice from πρό and the base of τροπή; to turn forward for oneself, i.e. encourage. In the KJV it is rendered: exhort.
G4390: From πρό and τρέχω (including its alternate); to run forward, i.e. outstrip, precede. In the KJV it is rendered: outrun, run before.
G4391: From πρό and ὑπάρχω; to exist before, i.e. (adverbially) to be or do something previously. In the KJV it is rendered: + be before(-time).
G4392: From a compound of πρό and φαίνω; an outward showing, i.e. pretext. In the KJV it is rendered: cloke, colour, pretence, show.
G4393: From πρό and φέρω; to bear forward, i.e. produce. In the KJV it is rendered: bring forth.
G4394: From προφήτης ("prophecy"); prediction (scriptural or other). In the KJV it is rendered: prophecy, prophesying.
G4395: From προφήτης; to foretell events, divine, speak under inspiration, exercise the prophetic office. In the KJV it is rendered: prophesy.
G4396: From a compound of πρό and φημί; a foreteller ("prophet"); by analogy, an inspired speaker; by extension, a poet. In the KJV it is rendered: prophet.
G4397: From προφήτης; pertaining to a foreteller ("prophetic"). In the KJV it is rendered: of prophecy, of the prophets.
G4398: Feminine of προφήτης; a female foreteller or an inspired woman. In the KJV it is rendered: prophetess.
G4399: From πρό and φθάνω; to get an earlier start of, i.e. anticipate. In the KJV it is rendered: prevent.
G4400: Middle voice from πρό and a derivative of χείρ; to handle for oneself in advance, i.e. (figuratively) to purpose. In the KJV it is rendered: choose, make.
G4401: From πρό and χειροτονέω; to elect in advance. In the KJV it is rendered: choose before.
G4402: From πρό and χορός; before the dance; Prochorus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Prochorus.
G4403: Feminine of prumnus (hindmost); the stern of a ship. In the KJV it is rendered: hinder part, stern.
G4404: Adverb from πρό; at dawn; by implication, the day-break watch. In the KJV it is rendered: early (in the morning), (in the) morning.
G4405: Feminine of a derivative of πρωΐ as noun; day-dawn. In the KJV it is rendered: early, morning.
G4406: From πρωΐ; dawning, i.e. (by analogy) autumnal (showering, the first of the rainy season). In the KJV it is rendered: early.
G4407: From πρωΐ; pertaining to the dawn, i.e. matutinal. In the KJV it is rendered: morning.
G4408: Feminine of a presumed derivative of πρό as noun; the prow, i.e. forward part of a vessel. In the KJV it is rendered: forepart(-ship).
G4409: From πρῶτος; to be first (in rank or influence). In the KJV it is rendered: have the preeminence.
G4410: From πρῶτος and καθέδρα; a sitting first (in the front row), i.e. preeminence in council. In the KJV it is rendered: chief (highest, uppermost) seat.
G4411: From πρῶτος and κλισία; a reclining first (in the place of honor) at the dinner-bed, i.e. preeminence at meals. In the KJV it is rendered: chief (highest, uppermost) room.
G4412: Neuter of πρῶτος as adverb (with or without ὁ); firstly (in time, place, order, or importance). In the KJV it is rendered: before, at the beginning, chiefly (at, at the) first (of all).
G4413: Contracted superlative of πρό; foremost (in time, place, order or importance). In the KJV it is rendered: before, beginning, best, chief(-est), first (of all), former.
G4414: From πρῶτος and ἵστημι; one standing first in the ranks, i.e. a captain (champion). In the KJV it is rendered: ringleader.
G4415: From πρωτότοκος; primogeniture (as a privilege). In the KJV it is rendered: birthright.
G4416: From πρῶτος and the alternate of τίκτω; first-born (usually as noun, literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: firstbegotten(-born).
G4417: A form of πίπτω; to trip, i.e. (figuratively) to err, sin, fail (of salvation). In the KJV it is rendered: fall, offend, stumble.
G4418: Of uncertain derivation; the heel (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: heel.
G4419: Neuter of a presumed derivative of πτέρυξ; a winglet, i.e. (figuratively) extremity (top corner). In the KJV it is rendered: pinnacle.
G4420: From a derivative of πέτομαι (meaning a feather); a wing. In the KJV it is rendered: wing.
G4421: Contraction for πετεινόν; a bird. In the KJV it is rendered: bird.
G4422: Probably akin to the alternate of πίπτω (through the idea of causing to fall) or to πέτομαι (through that of causing to fly away); to scare. In the KJV it is rendered: frighten.
G4423: From πτοέω; alarm. In the KJV it is rendered: amazement.
G4424: From Ptolemaios (Ptolemy, after whom it was named); Ptolemais, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Ptolemais.
G4425: From πτύω; a winnowing-fork (as scattering like spittle). In the KJV it is rendered: fan.
G4426: From a presumed derivative of πτύω (and thus akin to πτοέω); to frighten. In the KJV it is rendered: terrify.
G4427: From πτύω; saliva. In the KJV it is rendered: spittle.
G4428: Probably akin to petannumi (to spread; and thus apparently allied to πέτομαι through the idea of expansion, and to πτύω through that of flattening; compare πατέω); to fold, i.e. furl a scroll. In the KJV it is rendered: close.
G4429: A primary verb (compare πτύσσω); to spit. In the KJV it is rendered: spit.
G4430: From the alternate of πίπτω; a ruin, i.e. (specially), lifeless body (corpse, carrion). In the KJV it is rendered: dead body, carcase, corpse.
G4431: From the alternate of πίπτω; a crash, i.e. downfall (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: fall.
G4432: From πτωχεύω; beggary, i.e. indigence (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: poverty.
G4433: From πτωχός; to be a beggar, i.e. (by implication) to become indigent (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: become poor.
G4434: From ptosso (to crouch); akin to πτοέω and the alternate of πίπτω); a beggar (as cringing), i.e. pauper (strictly denoting absolute or public mendicancy, although also used in a qualified or relative sense; whereas πένης properly means only straitened circumstances in private), literally (often as noun) or figuratively (distressed). In the KJV it is rendered: beggar(-ly), poor.
G4435: From a primary pux (the fist as a weapon); the clenched hand, i.e. (only in dative case as adverb) with the fist (hard scrubbing). In the KJV it is rendered: oft.
G4436: From Putho (the name of the region where Delphi, the seat of the famous oracle, was located); a Python, i.e. (by analogy, with the supposed diviner there) inspiration (soothsaying). In the KJV it is rendered: divination.
G4437: From the same as σκηνοποιός; clasped (thick), i.e. (figuratively) frequent; neuter plural (as adverb) frequently. In the KJV it is rendered: often(-er).
G4438: From a derivative of the same as πυγμή; to box (with the fist), i.e. contend (as a boxer) at the games (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: fight.
G4439: Apparently a primary word; a gate, i.e. the leaf or wing of a folding entrance (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: gate.
G4440: From πύλη; a gate-way, door-way of a building or city; by implication, a portal or vestibule. In the KJV it is rendered: gate, porch.
G4441: Middle voice prolonged from a primary putho (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to question, i.e. ascertain by inquiry (as a matter of information merely; and thus differing from ἐρωτάω, which properly means a request as a favor; and from αἰτέω, which is strictly a demand for something due; as well as from ζητέω, which implies a search for something hidden; and from δέομαι, which involves the idea of urgent need); by implication, to learn (by casual intelligence). In the KJV it is rendered: ask, demand, enquire, understand.
G4442: A primary word; "fire" (literally or figuratively, specially, lightning). In the KJV it is rendered: fiery, fire.
G4443: From πῦρ; a fire (concretely). In the KJV it is rendered: fire.
G4444: Apparently a primary word ("burgh"); a tower or castle. In the KJV it is rendered: tower.
G4445: From πυρά; to be on fire, i.e. (specially), to have a fever. In the KJV it is rendered: be sick of a fever.
G4446: From πυρέσσω; inflamed, i.e. (by implication) feverish (as noun, fever). In the KJV it is rendered: fever.
G4447: From πυρά; fiery, i.e. (by implication) flaming. In the KJV it is rendered: of fire.
G4448: From πῦρ; to kindle, i.e. (passively) to be ignited, glow (literally), be refined (by implication), or (figuratively) to be inflamed (with anger, grief, lust). In the KJV it is rendered: burn, fiery, be on fire, try.
G4449: From πυῤῥός; to redden (intransitively). In the KJV it is rendered: be red.
G4450: From πῦρ; fire-like, i.e. (specially), flame- colored. In the KJV it is rendered: red.
G4451: From πυρόω; ignition, i.e. (specially), smelting (figuratively, conflagration, calamity as a test). In the KJV it is rendered: burning, trial.
G4452: Another form of the base of -πώς; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness; yet, even; used only in the comparative. See μηδέπω, μήπω, οὐδέπω, οὔπω, πώποτε.
G4453: Probably ultimately from pelomai (to be busy, to trade); to barter (as a pedlar), i.e. to sell. In the KJV it is rendered: sell, whatever is sold.
G4454: Apparently a primary word; a "foal" or "filly", i.e. (specially), a young ass. In the KJV it is rendered: colt.
G4455: From -πω and ποτέ; at any time, i.e. (with negative particle) at no time. In the KJV it is rendered: at any time, + never (…to any man), + yet, never man.
G4456: Apparently from poros (a kind of stone); to petrify, i.e. (figuratively) to indurate (render stupid or callous). In the KJV it is rendered: blind, harden.
G4457: From πωρόω; stupidity or callousness. In the KJV it is rendered: blindness, hardness.
G4458: Adverb from the base of πού; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness of manner; somehow or anyhow; used only in composition. In the KJV it is rendered: haply, by any (some) means, perhaps.
G4459: Adverb from the base of ποῦ; an interrogative particle of manner; in what way? (sometimes the question is indirect, how?); also as exclamation, how much!. In the KJV it is rendered: how, after (by) what manner (means), that.
G4460: Of Hebrew origin (רָחָב); Raab (i.e. Rachab), a Canaanitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Rahab.
G4461: Of Hebrew origin (רָב with pronominal suffix); my master, i.e Rabbi, as an official title of honor. In the KJV it is rendered: Master, Rabbi.
G4462: Or rhabbouni of Chaldee origin; corresponding to ῥαββί. In the KJV it is rendered: Lord, Rabboni.
G4463: From ῥάβδος; to strike with a stick, i.e. bastinado. In the KJV it is rendered: beat (with rods).
G4464: From the base of ῥαπίζω; a stick or wand (as a cudgel, a cane or a baton of royalty). In the KJV it is rendered: rod, sceptre, staff.
G4465: From ῥάβδος and ἔχω; a rod- (the Latin fasces) holder, i.e. a Roman lictor (constable or executioner). In the KJV it is rendered: serjeant.
G4466: Of Hebrew origin (רְעוּ); Ragau (i.e. Reu), a patriarch. In the KJV it is rendered: Ragau.
G4467: From a comparative of rhaidios (easy, i.e. reckless) and ἔργον; easy-going behavior, i.e. (by extension) a crime. In the KJV it is rendered: lewdness.
G4468: From the same as ῥᾳδιούργημα; recklessness, i.e. (by extension) malignity. In the KJV it is rendered: mischief.
G4469: Of Chaldee origin (compare רֵק); O empty one, i.e. thou worthless (as a term of utter vilification). In the KJV it is rendered: Raca.
G4470: From ῥήγνυμι; a "rag," i.e. piece of cloth. In the KJV it is rendered: cloth.
G4471: Of Hebrew origin (רָמָה); Rama (i.e. Ramah), a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Rama.
G4472: From a derivative of rhaino (to sprinkle); to render besprinkled, i.e. asperse (ceremonially or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: sprinkle.
G4473: From ῥαντίζω; aspersion (ceremonially or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: sprinkling.
G4474: From a derivative of a primary rhepo (to let fall, "rap"); to slap. In the KJV it is rendered: smite (with the palm of the hand).
G4475: From ῥαπίζω; a slap. In the KJV it is rendered: (+ strike with the) palm of the hand, smite with the hand.
G4476: From a primary rhapto (to sew; perhaps rather akin to the base of ῥαπίζω through the idea of puncturing); a needle. In the KJV it is rendered: needle.
G4477: From the same as Ῥαάβ; Rachab, a Canaanitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Rachab.
G4478: Of Hebrew origin (רָחֵל); Rachel, the wife of Jacob. In the KJV it is rendered: Rachel.
G4479: Of Hebrew origin (רִבְקָה); Rebecca (i.e. Ribkah), the wife of Isaac. In the KJV it is rendered: Rebecca.
G4480: Of Latin origin; a rheda, i.e. four-wheeled carriage (wagon for riding). In the KJV it is rendered: chariot.
G4481: By incorrect transliteration for a word of Hebrew origin (כִּיּוּן); Remphan (i.e. Kijun), an Egyptian idol. In the KJV it is rendered: Remphan.
G4482: A primary verb; for some tenses of which a prolonged form rheuo is used; to flow ("run"; as water). In the KJV it is rendered: flow.
G4483: For certain tenses of which a prolonged form ereo is used; and both as alternate for ἔπω perhaps akin (or identical) with ῥέω (through the idea of pouring forth); to utter, i.e. speak or say. In the KJV it is rendered: command, make, say, speak (of).
G4484: Of Latin origin; Rhegium, a place in Italy. In the KJV it is rendered: Rhegium.
G4485: From ῥήγνυμι; something torn, i.e. a fragment (by implication and abstractly, a fall). In the KJV it is rendered: ruin.
G4486: Or rhesso both prolonged forms of rheko (which appears only in certain forms, and is itself probably a strengthened form of agnumi (see in κατάγνυμι)) to "break," "wreck" or "crack", i.e. (especially) to sunder (by separation of the parts; κατάγνυμι being its intensive (with the preposition in composition), and θραύω a shattering to minute fragments; but not a reduction to the constituent particles, like λύω) or disrupt, lacerate; by implication, to convulse (with spasms); figuratively, to give vent to joyful emotions. In the KJV it is rendered: break (forth), burst, rend, tear.
G4487: From ῥέω; an utterance (individually, collectively or specially),; by implication, a matter or topic (especially of narration, command or dispute); with a negative naught whatever. In the KJV it is rendered: + evil, + nothing, saying, word.
G4488: Probably of Hebrew origin (apparently for רְפָיָה); Resa (i.e. Rephajah), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Rhesa.
G4489: From ῥέω; a speaker, i.e. (by implication) a forensic advocate. In the KJV it is rendered: orator.
G4490: Adverb from a derivative of ῥέω; out-spokenly, i.e. distinctly. In the KJV it is rendered: expressly.
G4491: Apparently a primary word; a "root" (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: root.
G4492: From ῥίζα; to root (figuratively, become stable). In the KJV it is rendered: root.
G4493: From ῥίπτω; a jerk (of the eye, i.e. (by analogy) an instant). In the KJV it is rendered: twinkling.
G4494: From a derivative of ῥίπτω (meaning a fan or bellows); to breeze up, i.e. (by analogy) to agitate (into waves). In the KJV it is rendered: toss.
G4495: From a derivative of ῥίπτω; to toss up. In the KJV it is rendered: cast off.
G4496: A primary verb (perhaps rather akin to the base of ῥαπίζω, through the idea of sudden motion); to fling (properly, with a quick toss, thus differing from βάλλω, which denotes a deliberate hurl; and from teino (see in ἐκτείνω), which indicates an extended projection); by qualification, to deposit (as if a load); by extension, to disperse. In the KJV it is rendered: cast (down, out), scatter abroad, throw.
G4497: Of Hebrew origin (רְחַבְעָם); Roboam (i.e. Rechobam), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Roboam.
G4498: Probably for rhode (a rose); Rode, a servant girl. In the KJV it is rendered: Rhoda.
G4499: Probably from rhodon (a rose); Rhodus, an island of the Mediterranean. In the KJV it is rendered: Rhodes.
G4500: Adverb from a derivative of rhoizos (a whir); whizzingly, i.e. with a crash. In the KJV it is rendered: with a great noise.
G4501: Probably of foreign origin; a sabre, i.e. a long and broad cutlass (any weapon of the kind, literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: sword.
G4502: Of Hebrew origin (רְאוּבֵן); Ruben (i.e. Reuben), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Reuben.
G4503: Of Hebrew origin (רוּת); Ruth, a Moabitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Ruth.
G4504: Of Latin origin; red; Rufus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Rufus.
G4505: Prolongation from ῥύομαι in its original sense; an alley or avenue (as crowded). In the KJV it is rendered: lane, street.
G4506: Middle voice of an obsolete verb, akin to ῥέω (through the idea of a current; compare ῥύσις); to rush or draw (for oneself), i.e. rescue. In the KJV it is rendered: deliver(-er).
G4507: From ῥυπαρός; dirtiness (morally). In the KJV it is rendered: turpitude.
G4508: From ῥύπος; dirty, i.e. (relatively) cheap or shabby; morally, wicked. In the KJV it is rendered: vile.
G4509: Of uncertain affinity; dirt, i.e. (morally) depravity. In the KJV it is rendered: filth.
G4510: From ῥύπος; to soil, i.e. (intransitively) to become dirty (morally). In the KJV it is rendered: be filthy.
G4511: From ῥύομαι in the sense of its congener ῥέω; a flux (of blood). In the KJV it is rendered: issue.
G4512: From ῥύομαι; a fold (as drawing together), i.e. a wrinkle (especially on the face). In the KJV it is rendered: wrinkle.
G4513: From Ῥωμαῖος; Romaic, i.e. Latin. In the KJV it is rendered: Latin.
G4514: From Ῥώμη; Romæan, i.e. Roman (as noun). In the KJV it is rendered: Roman, of Rome.
G4515: Adverb from a presumed derivative of Ῥώμη; Romaistically, i.e. in the Latin language. In the KJV it is rendered: Latin.
G4516: From the base of ῥώννυμι; strength; Roma, the capital of Italy. In the KJV it is rendered: Rome.
G4517: Prolongation from rhoomai (to dart; probably akin to ῥύομαι); to strengthen, i.e. (impersonal passive) have health (as a parting exclamation, good-bye). In the KJV it is rendered: farewell.
G4518: Of Chaldee or (שְׁבַק with pronominal suffix); thou hast left me; sabachthani (i.e. shebakthani), a cry of distress. In the KJV it is rendered: sabachthani.
G4519: Of Hebrew origin (צָבָא in feminine plural); armies; sabaoth (i.e. tsebaoth), a military epithet of God. In the KJV it is rendered: sabaoth.
G4520: From a derivative of σάββατον; a "sabbatism", i.e. (figuratively) the repose of Christianity (as a type of heaven). In the KJV it is rendered: rest.
G4521: Of Hebrew origin (שַׁבָּת); the Sabbath (i.e. Shabbath), or day of weekly repose from secular avocations (also the observance or institution itself); by extension, a se'nnight, i.e. the interval between two Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above applications. In the KJV it is rendered: sabbath (day), week.
G4522: From a derivative of satto (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a pack-saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope); a "seine" for fishing. In the KJV it is rendered: net.
G4523: Probably from Σαδώκ; a Sadducæan (i.e. Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Sadducee.
G4524: Of Hebrew origin (צָדוֹק); Sadoc (i.e. Tsadok), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Sadoc.
G4525: Akin to σείω; to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), i.e. (generally) to shake (figuratively, disturb). In the KJV it is rendered: move.
G4526: Of Hebrew origin (שָׂק); "sack"-cloth, i.e. mohair (the material or garments made of it, worn as a sign of grief). In the KJV it is rendered: sackcloth.
G4527: Of Hebrew origin (שָׁ֫לַח); Sala (i.e. Shelach), a patriarch. In the KJV it is rendered: Sala.
G4528: Of Hebrew origin (שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל); Salathiel (i.e. Shealtiel), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Salathiel.
G4529: Probably from σάλος (from the surge on the shore); Salamis, a place in Cyprus. In the KJV it is rendered: Salamis.
G4530: Probably from the same as σαλεύω; Salim, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Salim.
G4531: From σάλος; to waver, i.e. agitate, rock, topple or (by implication) destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite. In the KJV it is rendered: move, shake (together), which can(-not) be shaken, stir up.
G4532: Of Hebrew origin (שָׁלֵם); Salem (i.e. Shalem), a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Salem.
G4533: Of Hebrew origin (שַׂלְמוֹן); Salmon, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Salmon.
G4534: Perhaps of similar origin to Σαλαμίς; Salmone, a place in Crete. In the KJV it is rendered: Salmone.
G4535: Probably from the base of σαίνω; a vibration, i.e. (specially), billow. In the KJV it is rendered: wave.
G4536: Perhaps from σάλος (through the idea of quavering or reverberation); a trumpet. In the KJV it is rendered: trump(-et).
G4537: From σάλπιγξ; to trumpet, i.e. sound a blast (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: (which are yet to) sound (a trumpet).
G4538: From σαλπίζω; a trumpeter. In the KJV it is rendered: trumpeter.
G4539: Probably of Hebrew origin (feminine from שָׁלוֹם); Salome (i.e. Shelomah), an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Salome.
G4540: Of Hebrew origin (שֹׁמְרוֹן); Samaria (i.e. Shomeron), a city and region of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Samaria.
G4541: From Σαμάρεια; a Samarite, i.e. inhabitant of Samaria. In the KJV it is rendered: Samaritan.
G4542: Feminine of Σαμαρείτης; a Samaritess, i.e. woman of Samaria. In the KJV it is rendered: of Samaria.
G4543: From Σάμος and Thraike (Thrace); Samo-thrace (Samos of Thrace), an island in the Mediterranean. In the KJV it is rendered: Samothracia.
G4544: Of uncertain affinity; Samus, an island of the Mediterranean. In the KJV it is rendered: Samos.
G4545: Of Hebrew origin (שְׁמוּאֵל); Samuel (i.e. Shemuel), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Samuel.
G4546: Of Hebrew origin (שִׁמְשׁוֹן); Sampson (i.e. Shimshon), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Samson.
G4547: Neuter of a derivative of sandalon (a "sandal"; of uncertain origin); a slipper or sole-pad. In the KJV it is rendered: sandal.
G4548: Of uncertain affinity; a plank. In the KJV it is rendered: board.
G4549: Of Hebrew origin (שָׁאוּל); Saul (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul. In the KJV it is rendered: Saul.
G4550: From σήπω; rotten, i.e. worthless (literally or morally). In the KJV it is rendered: bad, corrupt.
G4551: Feminine of σάπφειρος; Sapphire, an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Sapphira.
G4552: Of Hebrew origin (סַפִּיר); a "sapphire" or lapis-lazuli gem. In the KJV it is rendered: sapphire.
G4553: Apparently of Hebrew origin (שָׂרַג); a basket (as interwoven or wicker-work. In the KJV it is rendered: basket.
G4554: Plural of uncertain derivation; Sardis, a place in Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Sardis.
G4555: From the same as σάρδιος; sardine (λίθος being implied), i.e. a gem, so called. In the KJV it is rendered: sardine.
G4556: Properly, an adjective from an uncertain base; sardian (λίθος being implied), i.e. (as noun) the gem so called. In the KJV it is rendered: sardius.
G4557: From the base of σάρδιος and onux (the nail of a finger; hence the "onyx" stone); a "sardonyx", i.e. the gem so called. In the KJV it is rendered: sardonyx.
G4558: Of Hebrew origin (צָרְפַת); Sarepta (i.e. Tsarephath), a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Sarepta.
G4559: From σάρξ; pertaining to flesh, i.e. (by extension) bodily, temporal, or (by implication) animal, unregenerate. In the KJV it is rendered: carnal, fleshly.
G4560: From σάρξ; similar to flesh, i.e. (by analogy) soft. In the KJV it is rendered: fleshly.
G4561: Probably from the base of σαρόω; flesh (as stripped of the skin), i.e. (strictly) the meat of an animal (as food), or (by extension) the body (as opposed to the soul (or spirit), or as the symbol of what is external, or as the means of kindred), or (by implication) human nature (with its frailties (physically or morally) and passions), or (specially), a human being (as such). In the KJV it is rendered: carnal(-ly, + -ly minded), flesh(-ly).
G4562: Of Hebrew origin (שְׂרוּג); Saruch (i.e. Serug), a patriarch. In the KJV it is rendered: Saruch.
G4563: From a derivative of sairo (to brush off; akin to σύρω); meaning a broom; to sweep. In the KJV it is rendered: sweep.
G4564: Of Hebrew origin (שָׂרָה); Sarra (i.e. Sarah), the wife of Abraham. In the KJV it is rendered: Sara, Sarah.
G4565: Of Hebrew origin (NONE); Saron (i.e. Sharon), a district of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Saron.
G4566: Of Hebrew origin (שָׂטָן); Satan, i.e. the devil. In the KJV it is rendered: Satan.
G4567: Of Chaldee origin corresponding to מַעְבָּדִים (with the definite affix); the accuser, i.e. the devil. In the KJV it is rendered: Satan.
G4568: Of Hebrew origin (סְאָה־); a certain measure for things dry. In the KJV it is rendered: measure.
G4569: Of Hebrew origin, the same as Σαούλ; Saulus (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul. In the KJV it is rendered: Saul.
G4570: A prolonged form of an apparently primary verb; to extinguish (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: go out, quench.
G4571: Accusative case singular of σύ; thee. In the KJV it is rendered: thee, thou, X thy house.
G4572: Genitive case from σέ and αὐτός, also dative case of the same, seautoi, and accusative case seauton, likewise contracted sautou, sautoi, and sauton, respectively; of (with, to) thyself. In the KJV it is rendered: thee, thine own self, (thou) thy(-self).
G4573: Middle voice from a derivative of σέβομαι; to venerate, i.e. adore. In the KJV it is rendered: worship.
G4574: From σεβάζομαι; something adored, i.e. an object of worship (god, altar, etc). In the KJV it is rendered: devotion, that is worshipped.
G4575: From σεβάζομαι; venerable (august), i.e. (as noun) a title of the Roman Emperor, or (as adjective) imperial. In the KJV it is rendered: Augustus(-').
G4576: Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to revere, i.e. adore. In the KJV it is rendered: devout, religious, worship.
G4577: Probably from σύρω through its congener eiro (to fasten; akin to αἱρέομαι); a chain (as binding or drawing). In the KJV it is rendered: chain.
G4578: From σείω; a commotion, i.e. (of the air) a gale, (of the ground) an earthquake. In the KJV it is rendered: earthquake, tempest.
G4579: Apparently a primary verb; to rock (vibrate, properly, sideways or to and fro), i.e. (generally) to agitate (in any direction; cause to tremble); figuratively, to throw into a tremor (of fear or concern). In the KJV it is rendered: move, quake, shake.
G4580: Of Latin origin; "second"; Secundus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Secundus.
G4581: From Seleukos (Seleucus, a Syrian king); Seleuceia, a place in Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Seleucia.
G4582: From selas (brilliancy; probably akin to the alternate of αἱρέομαι, through the idea of attractiveness); the moon. In the KJV it is rendered: moon.
G4583: Middle voice or passive from a presumed derivative of σελήνη; to be moon-struck, i.e. crazy. In the KJV it is rendered: be a lunatic.
G4584: Of Hebrew origin (שִׁמְעִי); Semei (i.e. Shimi), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Semei.
G4585: Probably of foreign origin; fine wheaten flour. In the KJV it is rendered: fine flour.
G4586: From σέβομαι; venerable, i.e. honorable. In the KJV it is rendered: grave, honest.
G4587: From σεμνός; venerableness, i.e. probity. In the KJV it is rendered: gravity, honesty.
G4588: Of Latin origin; Sergius, a Roman. In the KJV it is rendered: Sergius.
G4589: Of Hebrew origin (שֵׁת); Seth (i.e. Sheth), a patriarch. In the KJV it is rendered: Seth.
G4590: Of Hebrew origin (שֵׁם); Sem (i.e. Shem), a patriarch. In the KJV it is rendered: Sem.
G4591: From sema (a mark; of uncertain derivation); to indicate. In the KJV it is rendered: signify.
G4592: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of σημαίνω; an indication, especially ceremonially or supernaturally. In the KJV it is rendered: miracle, sign, token, wonder.
G4593: From σημεῖον; to distinguish, i.e. mark (for avoidance). In the KJV it is rendered: note.
G4594: Neuter (as adverb) of a presumed compound of the article ὁ (t changed to s) and ἡμέρα; on the (i.e. this) day (or night current or just passed); generally, now (i.e. at present, hitherto). In the KJV it is rendered: this (to-)day.
G4595: Apparently a primary verb; to putrefy, i.e. (figuratively) perish. In the KJV it is rendered: be corrupted.
G4596: From Ser (an Indian tribe from whom silk was procured; hence the name of the silk-worm); Seric, i.e. silken (neuter as noun, a silky fabric). In the KJV it is rendered: silk.
G4597: Apparently of Hebrew origin (סָס); a moth. In the KJV it is rendered: moth.
G4598: From σής and a derivative of βιβρώσκω; moth-eaten. In the KJV it is rendered: motheaten.
G4599: From sthenos (bodily vigor; probably akin to the base of ἵστημι); to strengthen, i.e. (figuratively) confirm (in spiritual knowledge and power). In the KJV it is rendered: strengthen.
G4600: Of uncertain derivation; the jaw-bone, i.e. (by implication) the cheek or side of the face. In the KJV it is rendered: cheek.
G4601: From σιγή; to keep silent (transitively or intransitively). In the KJV it is rendered: keep close (secret, silence), hold peace.
G4602: Apparently from sizo (to hiss, i.e. hist or hush); silence. In the KJV it is rendered: silence.
G4603: From σίδηρος; made of iron. In the KJV it is rendered: (of) iron.
G4604: Of uncertain derivation; iron. In the KJV it is rendered: iron.
G4605: Of Hebrew origin (צִידוֹן); Sidon (i.e. Tsidon), a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Sidon.
G4606: From Σιδών; a Sidonian, i.e. inhabitant of Sidon. In the KJV it is rendered: of Sidon.
G4607: Of Latin origin; a dagger-man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish fanatic outlawed by the Romans). In the KJV it is rendered: murderer.
G4608: Of Hebrew origin (שֵׁכָר); an intoxicant, i.e. intensely fermented liquor. In the KJV it is rendered: strong drink.
G4609: Contraction for Σιλουανός; Silas, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Silas.
G4610: Of Latin origin; "silvan"; Silvanus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Silvanus.
G4611: Of Hebrew origin (שִׁלֹ֫חַ); Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool of Jerusalem. In the KJV it is rendered: Siloam.
G4612: Of Latin origin; a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. narrow covering (apron). In the KJV it is rendered: apron.
G4613: Of Hebrew origin (שִׁמְעוֹן); Simon (i.e. Shimon), the name of nine Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Simon.
G4614: Of Hebrew origin (סִינַי); Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain in Arabia. In the KJV it is rendered: Sina.
G4615: Perhaps from sinomai (to hurt, i.e. sting); mustard (the plant). In the KJV it is rendered: mustard.
G4616: Of uncertain (perhaps foreign) origin; byssos, i.e. bleached linen (the cloth or a garment of it). In the KJV it is rendered: (fine) linen (cloth).
G4617: From sinion (a sieve); to riddle (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: sift.
G4618: From a derivative of σῖτος; grain-fed, i.e. fattened. In the KJV it is rendered: fatted.
G4619: From a derivative of σῖτος; grained, i.e. fatted. In the KJV it is rendered: fatling.
G4620: From σῖτος and μέτρον; a grain-measure, i.e. (by implication) ration (allowance of food). In the KJV it is rendered: portion of meat.
G4621: Also plural irregular neuter sita of uncertain derivation; grain, especially wheat. In the KJV it is rendered: corn, wheat.
G4622: Of Hebrew origin (צִיּוֹן); Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant). In the KJV it is rendered: Sion.
G4623: From siope (silence, i.e. a hush; properly, muteness, i.e. involuntary stillness, or inability to speak; and thus differing from σιγή, which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb (but not deaf also, like κωφός properly); figuratively, to be calm (as quiet water). In the KJV it is rendered: dumb, (hold) peace.
G4624: From σκάνδαλον; to entrap, i.e. trip up (figuratively, stumble (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure). In the KJV it is rendered: (make to) offend.
G4625: ("scandal"); probably from a derivative of κάμπτω; a trap-stick (bent sapling), i.e. snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure or sin). In the KJV it is rendered: occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumblingblock.
G4626: Apparently a primary verb; to dig. In the KJV it is rendered: dig.
G4627: A "skiff" (as if dug out), or yawl (carried aboard a large vessel for landing). In the KJV it is rendered: boat.
G4628: Apparently from skello (to parch; through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank). In the KJV it is rendered: leg.
G4629: From a derivative of skepas (a covering; perhaps akin to the base of σκοπός through the idea of noticeableness); clothing. In the KJV it is rendered: raiment.
G4630: Apparently of Latin origin; left-handed; Scevas (i.e. Scævus), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Sceva.
G4631: From σκεῦος; furniture, i.e. spare tackle. In the KJV it is rendered: tackling.
G4632: Of uncertain affinity; a vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus (literally or figuratively [specially, a wife as contributing to the usefulness of the husband]). In the KJV it is rendered: goods, sail, stuff, vessel.
G4633: Apparently akin to σκεῦος and σκιά; a tent or cloth hut (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: habitation, tabernacle.
G4634: From σκῆνος and πήγνυμι; the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes). In the KJV it is rendered: tabernacles.
G4635: From σκηνή and ποιέω; a manufacturer of tents. In the KJV it is rendered: tent-maker.
G4636: From σκηνή; a hut or temporary residence, i.e. (figuratively) the human body (as the abode of the spirit). In the KJV it is rendered: tabernacle.
G4637: From σκῆνος; to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as a mansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol of protection and communion). In the KJV it is rendered: dwell.
G4638: From σκηνόω; an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul). In the KJV it is rendered: tabernacle.
G4639: Apparently a primary word; "shade" or a shadow (literally or figuratively (darkness of error or an adumbration)). In the KJV it is rendered: shadow.
G4640: Akin to skairo (to skip); to jump, i.e. sympathetically move (as the quickening of a fetus). In the KJV it is rendered: leap (for joy).
G4641: Feminine of a compound of σκληρός and καρδία; hard-heartedness, i.e. (specially), destitution of (spiritual) perception. In the KJV it is rendered: hardness of heart.
G4642: From the base of σκέλος; dry, i.e. hard or tough (figuratively, harsh, severe). In the KJV it is rendered: fierce, hard.
G4643: From σκληρός; callousness, i.e. (figuratively) stubbornness. In the KJV it is rendered: hardness.
G4644: From σκληρός and τράχηλος; hardnaped, i.e. (figuratively) obstinate. In the KJV it is rendered: stiffnecked.
G4645: From σκληρός; to indurate, i.e. (figuratively) render stubborn. In the KJV it is rendered: harden.
G4646: From the base of σκέλος; warped, i.e. winding; figuratively, perverse. In the KJV it is rendered: crooked, froward, untoward.
G4647: Perhaps from the base of σκέλος and ὀπτάνομαι; withered at the front, i.e. a point or prickle (figuratively, a bodily annoyance or disability). In the KJV it is rendered: thorn.
