G4648: From σκοπός; to take aim at (spy), i.e. (figuratively) regard. In the KJV it is rendered: consider, take heed, look at (on), mark.
G4649: From skeptomai (to peer about ("skeptic"); perhaps akin to σκάπτω through the idea of concealment; compare σκέπασμα); a watch (sentry or scout), i.e. (by implication) a goal. In the KJV it is rendered: mark.
G4650: Apparently from the same as σκορπίος (through the idea of penetrating); to dissipate, i.e. (figuratively) put to flight, waste, be liberal. In the KJV it is rendered: disperse abroad, scatter (abroad).
G4651: Probably from an obsolete skerpo (perhaps strengthened from the base of σκοπός and meaning to pierce); a "scorpion" (from its sting). In the KJV it is rendered: scorpion.
G4652: From σκότος; opaque, i.e. (figuratively) benighted. In the KJV it is rendered: dark, full of darkness.
G4653: From σκότος; dimness, obscurity (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: dark(-ness).
G4654: From σκότος; to obscure (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: darken.
G4655: From the base of σκιά; shadiness, i.e. obscurity (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: darkness.
G4656: From σκότος; to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: be full of darkness.
G4657: Neuter of a presumed derivative of εἰς and κύων and βάλλω; what is thrown to the dogs, i.e. refuse (ordure). In the KJV it is rendered: dung.
G4658: Probably of foreign origin; a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (by implication) a savage. In the KJV it is rendered: Scythian.
G4659: From skuthros (sullen) and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι; angry-visaged, i.e. gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance. In the KJV it is rendered: of a sad countenance.
G4660: Apparently a primary verb; to flay, i.e. (figuratively) to harass. In the KJV it is rendered: trouble(self).
G4661: Neuter from σκύλλω; something stripped (as a hide), i.e. booty. In the KJV it is rendered: spoil.
G4662: From σκώληξ and a derivative of βιβρώσκω; worm-eaten, i.e. diseased with maggots. In the KJV it is rendered: eaten of worms.
G4663: Of uncertain derivation; a grub, maggot or earth-worm. In the KJV it is rendered: worm.
G4664: From σμάραγδος; consisting of emerald. In the KJV it is rendered: emerald.
G4665: Of uncertain derivation; the emerald or green gem so called. In the KJV it is rendered: emerald.
G4666: Apparently strengthened for μύρον; myrrh. In the KJV it is rendered: myrrh.
G4667: The same as σμύρνα; Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Smyrna.
G4668: From Σμύρνα; a Smyrnæan. In the KJV it is rendered: in Smyrna.
G4669: From Σμύρνα; to tincture with myrrh, i.e. embitter (as a narcotic). In the KJV it is rendered: mingle with myrrh.
G4670: Plural of Hebrew origin (סְדֹם); Sodoma (i.e. Sedom), a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Sodom.
G4671: Dative case of σύ; to thee. In the KJV it is rendered: thee, thine own, thou, thy.
G4672: Of Hebrew origin (שְׁלֹמֹה); Solomon (i.e. Shelomoh), the son of David. In the KJV it is rendered: Solomon.
G4673: Probably akin to the base of σωρεύω; a funereal receptacle (urn, coffin), i.e. (by analogy) a bier. In the KJV it is rendered: bier.
G4674: From σύ; thine. In the KJV it is rendered: thine (own), thy (friend).
G4675: Genitive case of σύ; of thee, thy. In the KJV it is rendered: X home, thee, thine (own), thou, thy.
G4676: Of Latin origin; a sudarium (sweat-cloth), i.e. towel (for wiping the perspiration from the face, or binding the face of a corpse). In the KJV it is rendered: handkerchief, napkin.
G4677: Of Hebrew origin (שׁוֹשָׁן feminine); lily; Susannah (i.e. Shoshannah), an Israelitess. In the KJV it is rendered: Susanna.
G4678: From σοφός; wisdom (higher or lower, worldly or spiritual). In the KJV it is rendered: wisdom.
G4679: From σοφός; to render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form "sophisms", i.e. continue plausible error. In the KJV it is rendered: cunningly devised, make wise.
G4680: Akin to saphes (clear); wise (in a most general application). In the KJV it is rendered: wise.
G4681: Probably of foreign origin; Spania, a region of Europe. In the KJV it is rendered: Spain.
G4682: Prolongation from spairo (to grasp; apparently strengthened from σπάω through the idea of spasmodic contraction); to mangle, i.e. convluse with epilepsy. In the KJV it is rendered: rend, tear.
G4683: From sparganon (a strip; from a derivative of the base of σπαράσσω meaning to strap or wrap with strips); to swathe (an infant after the Oriental custom). In the KJV it is rendered: wrap in swaddling clothes.
G4684: From spatale (luxury); to be voluptuous. In the KJV it is rendered: live in pleasure, be wanton.
G4685: A primary verb; to draw. In the KJV it is rendered: draw (out).
G4686: Of immediate Latin origin, but ultimately a derivative of αἱρέομαι in the sense of its cognate εἱλίσσω; a coil (spira, "spire"), i.e. (figuratively) a mass of men (a Roman military cohort; also (by analogy) a squad of Levitical janitors). In the KJV it is rendered: band.
G4687: Probably strengthened from σπάω (through the idea of extending); to scatter, i.e. sow (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: sow(- er), receive seed.
G4688: Of Latin origin; a speculator, i.e. military scout (spy or (by extension) life-guardsman). In the KJV it is rendered: executioner.
G4689: Apparently a primary verb; to pour out as a libation, i.e. (figuratively) to devote (one's life or blood, as a sacrifice) ("spend"). In the KJV it is rendered: (be ready to) be offered.
G4690: From σπείρω; something sown, i.e. seed (including the male "sperm"); by implication, offspring; specially, a remnant (figuratively, as if kept over for planting). In the KJV it is rendered: issue, seed.
G4691: From σπέρμα and λέγω; a seed-picker (as the crow), i.e. (figuratively) a sponger, loafer (specially, a gossip or trifler in talk). In the KJV it is rendered: babbler.
G4692: Probably strengthened from πούς; to "speed" ("study"), i.e. urge on (diligently or earnestly); by implication, to await eagerly. In the KJV it is rendered: (make, with) haste unto.
G4693: Neuter of a presumed derivative of speos (a grotto); a cavern; by implication, a hiding-place or resort. In the KJV it is rendered: cave, den.
G4694: Of uncertain derivation; a ledge or reef of rock in the sea. In the KJV it is rendered: spot (by confusion with spilos).
G4695: From σπίλος; to stain or soil (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: defile, spot.
G4696: Of uncertain derivation; a stain or blemish, i.e. (figuratively) defect, disgrace. In the KJV it is rendered: spot.
G4697: Middle voice from σπλάγχνον; to have the bowels yearn, i.e. (figuratively) feel sympathy, to pity. In the KJV it is rendered: have (be moved with) compassion.
G4698: Probably strengthened from splen (the "spleen"); an intestine (plural); figuratively, pity or sympathy. In the KJV it is rendered: bowels, inward affection, + tender mercy.
G4699: Perhaps of foreign origin; a "sponge". In the KJV it is rendered: spunge.
G4700: Of uncertain derivation; ashes. In the KJV it is rendered: ashes.
G4701: From σπείρω; a sowing, i.e. (by implication) parentage. In the KJV it is rendered: seed.
G4702: From σπόρος; sown, i.e. (neuter plural) a planted field. In the KJV it is rendered: corn(-field).
G4703: From σπείρω; a scattering (of seed), i.e. (concretely) seed (as sown). In the KJV it is rendered: seed (X sown).
G4704: From σπουδή; to use speed, i.e. to make effort, be prompt or earnest. In the KJV it is rendered: do (give) diligence, be diligent (forward), endeavour, labour, study.
G4705: From σπουδή; prompt, energetic, earnest. In the KJV it is rendered: diligent.
G4706: Neuter of σπουδαιότερος as adverb; more earnestly than others), i.e. very promptly. In the KJV it is rendered: very diligently.
G4707: Comparative of σπουδαῖος; more prompt, more earnest. In the KJV it is rendered: more diligent (forward).
G4708: Adverb from σπουδαιότερος; more speedily, i.e. sooner than otherwise. In the KJV it is rendered: more carefully.
G4709: Adverb from σπουδαῖος; earnestly, promptly. In the KJV it is rendered: diligently, instantly.
G4710: From σπεύδω; "speed", i.e. (by implication) despatch, eagerness, earnestness. In the KJV it is rendered: business, (earnest) care(-fulness), diligence, forwardness, haste.
G4711: From σπείρω (as woven); a hamper or lunch-receptacle. In the KJV it is rendered: basket.
G4712: Or masculine (in plural) stadios from the base of ἵστημι (as fixed); a stade or certain measure of distance; by implication, a stadium or race-course. In the KJV it is rendered: furlong, race.
G4713: From the base of ἵστημι (as stationary); a jar or earthen tank. In the KJV it is rendered: pot.
G4714: From the base of ἵστημι; a standing (properly, the act), i.e. (by analogy) position (existence); by implication, a popular uprising; figuratively, controversy. In the KJV it is rendered: dissension, insurrection, X standing, uproar.
G4715: From the base of καύχησις; a stander (standard of value), i.e. (specially), a stater or certain coin. In the KJV it is rendered: piece of money.
G4716: From the base of ἵστημι; a stake or post (as set upright), i.e. (specially), a pole or cross (as an instrument of capital punishment); figuratively, exposure to death, i.e. self-denial; by implication, the atonement of Christ. In the KJV it is rendered: cross.
G4717: From σταυρός; to impale on the cross; figuratively, to extinguish (subdue) passion or selfishness. In the KJV it is rendered: crucify.
G4718: Probably from the base of στέφανος; a cluster of grapes (as if intertwined). In the KJV it is rendered: grapes.
G4719: From the base of ἵστημι; a head of grain (as standing out from the stalk). In the KJV it is rendered: ear (of corn).
G4720: The same as στάχυς; Stachys, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Stachys.
G4721: Strengthened from a primary tegos (a "thatch" or "deck" of a building); a roof. In the KJV it is rendered: roof.
G4722: From στέγη; to roof over, i.e. (figuratively) to cover with silence (endure patiently). In the KJV it is rendered: (for-)bear, suffer.
G4723: A contraction from στερεός (as stiff and unnatural); "sterile". In the KJV it is rendered: barren.
G4724: Probably strengthened from the base of ἵστημι; properly, to set fast ("stall"), i.e. (figuratively) to repress (reflexively, abstain from associating with). In the KJV it is rendered: avoid, withdraw self.
G4725: From the base of στέφανος; a wreath for show. In the KJV it is rendered: garland.
G4726: From στενάζω; a sigh. In the KJV it is rendered: groaning.
G4727: From στενός; to make (intransitively, be) in straits, i.e. (by implication) to sigh, murmur, pray inaudibly. In the KJV it is rendered: with grief, groan, grudge, sigh.
G4728: Probably from the base of ἵστημι; narrow (from obstacles standing close about). In the KJV it is rendered: strait.
G4729: From the same as στενοχωρία; to hem in closely, i.e. (figuratively) cramp. In the KJV it is rendered: distress, straiten.
G4730: From a compound of στενός and χώρα; narrowness of room, i.e. (figuratively) calamity. In the KJV it is rendered: anguish, distress.
G4731: From ἵστημι; stiff, i.e. solid, stable (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: stedfast, strong, sure.
G4732: From στερεός; to solidify, i.e. confirm (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: establish, receive strength, make strong.
G4733: From στερεόω; something established, i.e. (abstractly) confirmation (stability). In the KJV it is rendered: stedfastness.
G4734: Probably contraction for stephanotos (crowned; from στεφανόω); Stephanas, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Stephanas.
G4735: From an apparently primary stepho (to twine or wreathe); a chaplet (as a badge of royalty, a prize in the public games or a symbol of honor generally; but more conspicuous and elaborate than the simple fillet, διάδημα), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: crown.
G4736: The same as στέφανος; Stephanus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Stephen.
G4737: From στέφανος; to adorn with an honorary wreath (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: crown.
G4738: From ἵστημι (as standing prominently); the (entire external) bosom, i.e. chest. In the KJV it is rendered: breast.
G4739: From the perfect tense of ἵστημι; to be stationary, i.e. (figuratively) to persevere. In the KJV it is rendered: stand (fast).
G4740: From στηρίζω; stability (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: stedfastness.
G4741: From a presumed derivative of ἵστημι (like στερεός); to set fast, i.e. (literally) to turn resolutely in a certain direction, or (figuratively) to confirm. In the KJV it is rendered: fix, (e-)stablish, stedfastly set, strengthen.
G4742: From a primary stizo (to "stick", i.e. prick); a mark incised or punched (for recognition of ownership), i.e. (figuratively) scar of service. In the KJV it is rendered: mark.
G4743: Feminine of στίγμα; a point of time, i.e. an instant. In the KJV it is rendered: moment.
G4744: Apparently a primary verb; to gleam, i.e. flash intensely. In the KJV it is rendered: shining.
G4745: Probably from ἵστημι; a colonnade or interior piazza. In the KJV it is rendered: porch.
G4746: From a primary steibo (to "step" or "stamp"); a spread (as if tramped flat) of loose materials for a couch, i.e. (by implication) a bough of a tree so employed. In the KJV it is rendered: branch.
G4747: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of στοιχέω; something orderly in arrangement, i.e. (by implication) a serial (basal, fundamental, initial) constituent (literally), proposition (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: element, principle, rudiment.
G4748: From a derivative of steicho (to range in regular line); to march in (military) rank (keep step), i.e. (figuratively) to conform to virtue and piety. In the KJV it is rendered: walk (orderly).
G4749: From στέλλω; equipment, i.e. (specially), a "stole" or long-fitting gown (as a mark of dignity). In the KJV it is rendered: long clothing (garment), (long) robe.
G4750: Probably strengthened from a presumed derivative of the base of τομώτερος; the mouth (as if a gash in the face); by implication, language (and its relations); figuratively, an opening (in the earth); specially, the front or edge (of a weapon). In the KJV it is rendered: edge, face, mouth.
G4751: From στόμα; an orifice (the gullet), i.e. (specially), the "stomach". In the KJV it is rendered: stomach.
G4752: From στρατεύομαι; military service, i.e. (figuratively) the apostolic career (as one of hardship and danger). In the KJV it is rendered: warfare.
G4753: From στρατεύομαι; an armament, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops (more or less extensive or systematic). In the KJV it is rendered: army, soldier, man of war.
G4754: Middle voice from the base of στρατιά; to serve in a military campaign; figuratively, to execute the apostolate (with its arduous duties and functions), to contend with carnal inclinations. In the KJV it is rendered: soldier, (go to) war(-fare).
G4755: From the base of στρατιά and ἄγω or ἡγέομαι; a general, i.e. (by implication or analogy) a (military) governor (prætor), the chief (præfect) of the (Levitical) temple-wardens. In the KJV it is rendered: captain, magistrate.
G4756: Feminine of a derivative of stratos (an army; from the base of στρώννυμι, as encamped); camp-likeness, i.e. an army, i.e. (figuratively) the angels, the celestial luminaries. In the KJV it is rendered: host.
G4757: From a presumed derivative of the same as στρατιά; a camper-out, i.e. a (common) warrior (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: soldier.
G4758: From a compound of the base of στρατιά and λέγω (in its original sense); to gather (or select) as a warrior, i.e. enlist in the army. In the KJV it is rendered: choose to be a soldier.
G4759: From στρατόπεδον and ἄρχω; a ruler of an army, i.e. (specially), a from στρατόπεδον and ἄρχω; a ruler of an army, i.e. præfect. In the KJV it is rendered: captain of the guard.
G4760: From the base of στρατιά and the same as πεδινός; a camping-ground, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops. In the KJV it is rendered: army.
G4761: From a derivative of στρέφω; to wrench, i.e. (specially), to torture (by the rack), but only figuratively, to pervert. In the KJV it is rendered: wrest.
G4762: Strengthened from the base of τροπή; to twist, i.e. turn quite around or reverse (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: convert, turn (again, back again, self, self about).
G4763: From a presumed derivative of στρῆνος; to be luxurious. In the KJV it is rendered: live deliciously.
G4764: Akin to στερεός; a "straining", "strenuousness" or "strength", i.e. (figuratively) luxury (voluptuousness). In the KJV it is rendered: delicacy.
G4765: Diminutive of strouthos (a sparrow); a little sparrow. In the KJV it is rendered: sparrow.
G4766: Or simpler stronnuo, prolongation from a still simpler stroo, (used only as an alternate in certain tenses) (probably akin to στερεός through the idea of positing); to "strew," i.e. spread (as a carpet or couch). In the KJV it is rendered: make bed, furnish, spread, strew.
G4767: From a derivative of an obsolete apparently primary stugo (to hate); hated, i.e. odious. In the KJV it is rendered: hateful.
G4768: From the same as στυγνητός; to render gloomy, i.e. (by implication) glower (be overcast with clouds, or sombreness of speech). In the KJV it is rendered: lower, be sad.
G4769: From stuo (to stiffen; properly akin to the base of ἵστημι); a post ("style"), i.e. (figuratively) support. In the KJV it is rendered: pillar.
G4770: From στοά; a "Stoic" (as occupying a particular porch in Athens), i.e. adherent of a certin philosophy. In the KJV it is rendered: Stoick.
G4771: The personal pronoun of the second person singular; thou. In the KJV it is rendered: thou.
G4772: From συγγενής; relationship, i.e. (concretely) relatives. In the KJV it is rendered: kindred.
G4773: From σύν and γένος; a relative (by blood); by extension, a fellow countryman. In the KJV it is rendered: cousin, kin(-sfolk, -sman).
G4774: From a compound of σύν and γινώσκω; fellow knowledge, i.e. concession. In the KJV it is rendered: permission.
G4775: From σύν and κάθημαι; to seat oneself in company with. In the KJV it is rendered: sit with.
G4776: From σύν and καθίζω; to give (or take) a seat in company with. In the KJV it is rendered: (make) sit (down) together.
G4777: From σύν and κακοπαθέω; to suffer hardship in company with. In the KJV it is rendered: be partaker of afflictions.
G4778: From σύν and κακουχέω; to maltreat in company with, i.e. (passively) endure persecution together. In the KJV it is rendered: suffer affliction with.
G4779: From σύν and καλέω; to convoke. In the KJV it is rendered: call together.
G4780: From σύν and καλύπτω; to conceal altogether. In the KJV it is rendered: cover.
G4781: From σύν and κάμπτω; to bend together, i.e. (figuratively) to afflict. In the KJV it is rendered: bow down.
G4782: From σύν and καταβαίνω; to descend in company with. In the KJV it is rendered: go down with.
G4783: From συγκατατίθεμαι; a deposition (of sentiment) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) accord with. In the KJV it is rendered: agreement.
G4784: Middle from σύν and κατατίθημι; to deposit (one's vote or opinion) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to accord with. In the KJV it is rendered: consent.
G4785: From σύν and a compound of κατά and ψηφίζω; to count down in company with, i.e. enroll among. In the KJV it is rendered: number with.
G4786: From σύν and κεράννυμι; to commingle, i.e. (figuratively) to combine or assimilate. In the KJV it is rendered: mix with, temper together.
G4787: From σπαράσσω and κινέω; to move together, i.e. (specially), to excite as a mass (to sedition). In the KJV it is rendered: stir up.
G4788: From σύν and κλείω; to shut together, i.e. include or (figuratively) embrace in a common subjection to. In the KJV it is rendered: conclude, inclose, shut up.
G4789: From σύν and κληρονόμος; a co-heir, i.e. (by analogy) participant in common. In the KJV it is rendered: fellow (joint)-heir, heir together, heir with.
G4790: From σύν and κοινωνέω; to share in company with, i.e. co-participate in. In the KJV it is rendered: communicate (have fellowship) with, be partaker of.
G4791: From σύν and κοινωνός; a co-participant. In the KJV it is rendered: companion, partake(-r, -r with).
G4792: From σύν and κομίζω; to convey together, i.e. collect or bear away in company with others. In the KJV it is rendered: carry.
G4793: From σύν and κρίνω; to judge of one thing in connection with another, i.e. combine (spiritual ideas with appropriate expressions) or collate (one person with another by way of contrast or resemblance). In the KJV it is rendered: compare among (with).
G4794: From σύν and κύπτω; to stoop altogether, i.e. be completely overcome by. In the KJV it is rendered: bow together.
G4795: From a comparative of σύν and kureo (to light or happen; from the base of κύριος); concurrence, i.e. accident. In the KJV it is rendered: chance.
G4796: From σύν and χαίρω; to sympathize in gladness, congratulate. In the KJV it is rendered: rejoice in (with).
G4797: Or sugchuno from σύν and cheo (to pour) or its alternate; to commingle promiscuously, i.e. (figuratively) to throw (an assembly) into disorder, to perplex (the mind). In the KJV it is rendered: confound, confuse, stir up, be in an uproar.
G4798: From σύν and χράομαι; to use jointly, i.e. (by implication) to hold intercourse in common. In the KJV it is rendered: have dealings with.
G4799: From συγχέω; commixture, i.e. (figuratively) riotous disturbance. In the KJV it is rendered: confusion.
G4800: From σύν and ζάω; to continue to live in common with, i.e. co-survive (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: live with.
G4801: From σύν and the base of ζεῦγος; to yoke together, i.e. (figuratively) conjoin (in marriage). In the KJV it is rendered: join together.
G4802: From σύν and ζητέω; to investigate jointly, i.e. discuss, controvert, cavil. In the KJV it is rendered: dispute (with), enquire, question (with), reason (together).
G4803: From συζητέω; mutual questioning, i.e. discussion. In the KJV it is rendered: disputation(-ting), reasoning.
G4804: From συζητέω; a disputant, i.e. sophist. In the KJV it is rendered: disputer.
G4805: From συζεύγνυμι; co-yoked, i.e. (figuratively) as noun, a colleague; probably rather as a proper name; Syzygus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: yokefellow.
G4806: From σύν and ζωοποιέω; to reanimate conjointly with (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: quicken together with.
G4807: Of Hebrew origin (שִׁקְמִים) in imitation of συκομωραία; a sycamore-fig tree. In the KJV it is rendered: sycamine tree.
G4808: From σῦκον; a fig-tree. In the KJV it is rendered: fig tree.
G4809: From σῦκον and moron (the mulberry); the "sycamore"-fig tree. In the KJV it is rendered: sycamore tree.
G4810: Apparently a primary word; a fig. In the KJV it is rendered: fig.
G4811: From a compound of σῦκον and a derivative of φαίνω; to be a fig-informer (reporter of the law forbidding the exportation of figs from Greece), "sycophant", i.e. (genitive and by extension) to defraud (exact unlawfully, extort). In the KJV it is rendered: accuse falsely, take by false accusation.
G4812: From the base of συλάω and (the reduplicated form of) ἄγω; to lead away as booty, i.e. (figuratively) seduce. In the KJV it is rendered: spoil.
G4813: From a derivative of sullo (to strip; probably akin to αἱρέομαι; compare σκῦλον); to despoil. In the KJV it is rendered: rob.
G4814: From σύν and λαλέω; to talk together, i.e. converse. In the KJV it is rendered: commune (confer, talk) with, speak among.
G4815: From σύν and λαμβάνω; to clasp, i.e. seize (arrest, capture); specially, to conceive (literally or figuratively); by implication, to aid. In the KJV it is rendered: catch, conceive, help, take.
G4816: From σύν and λέγω in its original sense; to collect. In the KJV it is rendered: gather (together, up).
G4817: From σύν and λογίζομαι; to reckon together (with oneself), i.e. deliberate. In the KJV it is rendered: reason with.
G4818: From σύν and λυπέω; to afflict jointly, i.e. (passive) sorrow at (on account of) someone. In the KJV it is rendered: be grieved.
G4819: From σύν and the base of βάσις; to walk (figuratively, transpire) together, i.e. concur (take place). In the KJV it is rendered: be(-fall), happen (unto).
G4820: From σύν and βάλλω; to combine, i.e. (in speaking) to converse, consult, dispute, (mentally) to consider, (by implication) to aid, (personally) to join, attack. In the KJV it is rendered: confer, encounter, help, make, meet with, ponder.
G4821: From σύν and βασιλεύω; to be co-regent (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: reign with.
G4822: From σύν and bibazo (to force; causative (by reduplication) of the base of βάσις); to drive together, i.e. unite (in association or affection), (mentally) to infer, show, teach. In the KJV it is rendered: compact, assuredly gather, intrust, knit together, prove.
G4823: From σύν and βουλεύω; to give (or take) advice jointly, i.e. recommend, deliberate or determine. In the KJV it is rendered: consult, (give, take) counsel (together).
G4824: Neuter of a presumed derivative of σύμβουλος; advisement; specially, a deliberative body, i.e. the provincial assessors or lay-court. In the KJV it is rendered: consultation, counsel, council.
G4825: From σύν and βουλή; a consultor, i.e. adviser. In the KJV it is rendered: counsellor.
G4826: From the same as Σίμων; Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Simeon, Simon.
G4827: From a compound of σύν and μανθάνω; a co-learner (of Christianity). In the KJV it is rendered: fellow disciple.
G4828: From σύν and μαρτυρέω; to testify jointly, i.e. corroborate by (concurrent) evidence. In the KJV it is rendered: testify unto, (also) bear witness (with).
G4829: Middle voice from σύν and μερίζω; to share jointly, i.e. participate in. In the KJV it is rendered: be partaker with.
G4830: From σύν and μέτοχος; a co-participant. In the KJV it is rendered: partaker.
G4831: From a presumed compound of σύν and μιμέομαι; a co-imitator, i.e. fellow votary. In the KJV it is rendered: follower together.
G4832: From σύν and μορφή; jointly formed, i.e. (figuratively) similar. In the KJV it is rendered: conformed to, fashioned like unto.
G4833: From σύμμορφος; to render like, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate. In the KJV it is rendered: make conformable unto.
G4834: From συμπαθής; to feel "sympathy" with, i.e. (by implication) to commiserate. In the KJV it is rendered: have compassion, be touched with a feeling of.
G4835: From συμπάσχω; having a fellow-feeling ("sympathetic"), i.e. (by implication) mutually commiserative. In the KJV it is rendered: having compassion one of another.
G4836: From σύν and παραγίνομαι; to be present together, i.e. to convene; by implication, to appear in aid. In the KJV it is rendered: come together, stand with.
G4837: From σύν and παρακαλέω; to console jointly. In the KJV it is rendered: comfort together.
G4838: From σύν and παραλαμβάνω; to take along in company. In the KJV it is rendered: take with.
G4839: From σύν and παραμένω; to remain in company, i.e. still live. In the KJV it is rendered: continue with.
G4840: From σύν and πάρειμι; to be at hand together, i.e. now present. In the KJV it is rendered: be here present with.
G4841: From σύν and πάσχω (including its alternate); to experience pain jointly or of the same kind (specially, persecution; to "sympathize"). In the KJV it is rendered: suffer with.
G4842: From σύν and πέμπω; to despatch in company. In the KJV it is rendered: send with.
G4843: From σύν and a compound of περί and λαμβάνω; to take by enclosing altogether, i.e. earnestly throw the arms about one. In the KJV it is rendered: embrace.
G4844: From σύν and πίνω; to partake a beverage in company. In the KJV it is rendered: drink with.
G4845: From σύν and πληρόω; to implenish completely, i.e. (of space) to swamp (a boat), or (of time) to accomplish (passive, be complete). In the KJV it is rendered: (fully) come, fill up.
G4846: From σύν and πνίγω; to strangle completely, i.e. (literally) to drown, or (figuratively) to crowd. In the KJV it is rendered: choke, throng.
G4847: From σύν and πολίτης; a native of the same town, i.e. (figuratively) co-religionist (fellow-Christian). In the KJV it is rendered: fellow- citizen.
G4848: From σύν and πορεύομαι; to journey together; by implication, to assemble. In the KJV it is rendered: go with, resort.
G4849: Neuter of a derivative of the alternate of συμπίνω; a drinking-party ("symposium"), i.e. (by extension) a room of guests. In the KJV it is rendered: company.
G4850: From σύν and πρεσβύτερος; a co-presbyter. In the KJV it is rendered: presbyter, also an elder.
G4851: From σύν and φέρω (including its alternate); to bear together (contribute), i.e. (literally) to collect, or (figuratively) to conduce; especially (neuter participle as a noun) advantage. In the KJV it is rendered: be better for, bring together, be expedient (for), be good, (be) profit(-able for).
G4852: From σύν and φημί; to say jointly, i.e. assent to. In the KJV it is rendered: consent unto.
G4853: From σύν and a derivative of φυλή; a co-tribesman, i.e. native of the same country. In the KJV it is rendered: countryman.
G4854: From σύν and a derivative of φύω; grown along with (connate), i.e. (figuratively) closely united to. In the KJV it is rendered: planted together.
G4855: From σύν and φύω; passive, to grow jointly. In the KJV it is rendered: spring up with.
G4856: From σύμφωνος; to be harmonious, i.e. (figuratively) to accord (be suitable, concur) or stipulate (by compact). In the KJV it is rendered: agree (together, with).
G4857: From συμφωνέω; accordance. In the KJV it is rendered: concord.
G4858: From σύμφωνος; unison of sound ("symphony"), i.e. a concert of instruments (harmonious note). In the KJV it is rendered: music.
G4859: From σύν and φωνή; sounding together (alike), i.e. (figuratively) accordant (neuter as noun, agreement). In the KJV it is rendered: consent.
G4860: From σύν and ψηφίζω; to compute jointly. In the KJV it is rendered: reckon.
G4861: From σύν and ψυχή; co-spirited, i.e. similar in sentiment. In the KJV it is rendered: like-minded.
G4862: A primary preposition denoting union; with or together (but much closer than μετά or παρά), i.e. by association, companionship, process, resemblance, possession, instrumentality, addition, etc. In the KJV it is rendered: beside, with.
G4863: From σύν and ἄγω; to lead together, i.e. collect or convene; specially, to entertain (hospitably). In the KJV it is rendered: + accompany, assemble (selves, together), bestow, come together, gather (selves together, up, together), lead into, resort, take in.
G4864: From (the reduplicated form of) συνάγω; an assemblage of persons; specially, a Jewish "synagogue" (the meeting or the place); by analogy, a Christian church. In the KJV it is rendered: assembly, congregation, synagogue.
G4865: From σύν and ἀγωνίζομαι; to struggle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to be a partner (assistant). In the KJV it is rendered: strive together with.
G4866: From σύν and ἀθλέω; to wrestle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to seek jointly. In the KJV it is rendered: labour with, strive together for.
G4867: From σύν and athroizo (to hoard); to convene. In the KJV it is rendered: call (gather) together.
G4868: From σύν and αἴρω; to make up together, i.e. (figuratively) to compute (an account). In the KJV it is rendered: reckon, take.
G4869: From σύν and αἰχμάλωτος; a co-captive. In the KJV it is rendered: fellowprisoner.
G4870: From σύν and ἀκολουθέω; to accompany. In the KJV it is rendered: follow.
G4871: From σύν and halizo (to throng); to accumulate, i.e. convene. In the KJV it is rendered: assemble together.
G4872: From σύν and ἀναβαίνω; to ascend in company with. In the KJV it is rendered: come up with.
G4873: From σύν and ἀνακεῖμαι; to recline in company with (at a meal). In the KJV it is rendered: sit (down, at the table, together) with (at meat).
G4874: From σύν and a compound of ἀνά and μίγνυμι; to mix up together, i.e. (figurative) associate with. In the KJV it is rendered: (have, keep) company (with).
G4875: Middle from σύν and ἀναπαύω; to recruit oneself in company with. In the KJV it is rendered: refresh with.
G4876: From σύν and a derivative of ἀντί; to meet with; figuratively, to occur. In the KJV it is rendered: befall, meet.
G4877: From συναντάω; a meeting with. In the KJV it is rendered: meet.
G4878: From σύν and ἀντιλαμβάνομαι; to take hold of opposite together, i.e. co-operate (assist). In the KJV it is rendered: help.
G4879: From σύν and ἀπάγω; to take off together, i.e. transport with (seduce, passively, yield). In the KJV it is rendered: carry (lead) away with, condescend.
G4880: From σύν and ἀποθνήσκω; to decease (literally) in company with, or (figuratively), similarly to. In the KJV it is rendered: be dead (die) with.
G4881: From σύν and ἀπόλλυμι; to destroy (middle voice or passively, be slain) in company with. In the KJV it is rendered: perish with.
G4882: From σύν and ἀποστέλλω; to despatch (on an errand) in company with. In the KJV it is rendered: send with.
G4883: From σύν and a derivative of a compound of ἁρμός and λέγω (in its original sense of laying); to render close-jointed together, i.e. organize compactly. In the KJV it is rendered: be fitly framed (joined) together.
G4884: From σύν and ἁρπάζω; to snatch together, i.e. seize. In the KJV it is rendered: catch.
G4885: From σύν and αὐξάνω; to increase (grow up) together. In the KJV it is rendered: grow together.
G4886: From σύν and δεσμόν; a joint tie, i.e. ligament, (figuratively) uniting principle, control. In the KJV it is rendered: band, bond.
G4887: From σύν and δέω; to bind with, i.e. (passively) be a fellow-prisoner (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: be bound with.
G4888: From σύν and δοξάζω; to exalt to dignity in company (i.e. similarly) with. In the KJV it is rendered: glorify together.
G4889: From σύν and δοῦλος; a co-slave, i.e. servitor or ministrant of the same master (human or divine). In the KJV it is rendered: fellowservant.
G4890: From (the alternate of) συντρέχω; a running together, i.e. (riotous) concourse. In the KJV it is rendered: run together.
G4891: From σύν and ἐγείρω; to rouse (from death) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to revivify (spirtually) in resemblance to. In the KJV it is rendered: raise up together, rise with.
G4892: Neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of σύν and the base of ἑδραῖος; a joint session, i.e. (specially), the Jewish Sanhedrin; by analogy, a subordinate tribunal. In the KJV it is rendered: council.
G4893: From a prolonged form of συνείδω; co-perception, i.e. moral consciousness. In the KJV it is rendered: conscience.
G4894: From σύν and εἴδω; to see completely; used (like its primary) only in two past tenses, respectively meaning to understand or become aware, and to be conscious or (clandestinely) informed of. In the KJV it is rendered: consider, know, be privy, be ware of.
G4895: From σύν and εἰμί (including its various inflections); to be in company with, i.e. present at the time. In the KJV it is rendered: be with.
G4896: From σύν and eimi (to go); to assemble. In the KJV it is rendered: gather together.
G4897: From σύν and εἰσέρχομαι; to enter in company with. In the KJV it is rendered: go in with, go with into.
G4898: From σύν and the base of ἐκδημέω; a co-absentee from home, i.e. fellow-traveller. In the KJV it is rendered: companion in travel, travel with.
G4899: From a compound of σύν and ἐκλέγομαι; chosen in company with, i.e. co-elect (fellow Christian). In the KJV it is rendered: elected together with.
G4900: From σύν and ἐλαύνω; to drive together, i.e. (figuratively) exhort (to reconciliation). In the KJV it is rendered: + set at one again.
G4901: From σύν and ἐπιμαρτυρέω; to testify further jointly, i.e. unite in adding evidence. In the KJV it is rendered: also bear witness.
G4902: Middle voice from σύν and a primary hepo (to follow); to attend (travel) in company with. In the KJV it is rendered: accompany.
G4903: From συνεργός; to be a fellow-worker, i.e. co-operate. In the KJV it is rendered: help (work) with, work(-er) together.
G4904: From a presumed compound of σύν and the base of ἔργον; a co-laborer, i.e. coadjutor. In the KJV it is rendered: companion in labour, (fellow-)helper(-labourer, -worker), labourer together with, workfellow.
G4905: From σύν and ἔρχομαι; to convene, depart in company with, associate with, or (specially), cohabit (conjugally). In the KJV it is rendered: accompany, assemble (with), come (together), come (company, go) with, resort.
G4906: From σύν and ἐσθίω (including its alternate); to take food in company with. In the KJV it is rendered: eat with.
G4907: From συνίημι; a mental putting together, i.e. intelligence or (concretely) the intellect. In the KJV it is rendered: knowledge, understanding.
G4908: From συνίημι; mentally put (or putting) together, i.e. sagacious. In the KJV it is rendered: prudent.
G4909: From σύν and εὐδοκέω; to think well of in common, i.e. assent to, feel gratified with. In the KJV it is rendered: allow, assent, be pleased, have pleasure.
G4910: From σύν and a derivative of a presumed compound of εὖ and a derivative of ἔχω (meaning to be in good condition, i.e. (by implication) to fare well, or feast); to entertain sumptuously in company with, i.e. (middle voice or passive) to revel together. In the KJV it is rendered: feast with.
G4911: From σύν and ἐφίστημι; to stand up together, i.e. to resist (or assault) jointly. In the KJV it is rendered: rise up together.
G4912: From σύν and ἔχω; to hold together, i.e. to compress (the ears, with a crowd or siege) or arrest (a prisoner); figuratively, to compel, perplex, afflict, preoccupy. In the KJV it is rendered: constrain, hold, keep in, press, lie sick of, stop, be in a strait, straiten, be taken with, throng.
G4913: Middle voice from σύν and the base of ἡδονή; to rejoice in with oneself, i.e. feel satisfaction concerning. In the KJV it is rendered: delight.
G4914: From a compound of σύν and ἦθος; mutual habituation, i.e. usage. In the KJV it is rendered: custom.
G4915: From σύν and a derivative of ἡλικία; a co-aged person, i.e. alike in years. In the KJV it is rendered: equal.
G4916: From σύν and θάπτω; to inter in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate spiritually (to Christ by a sepulture as to sin). In the KJV it is rendered: bury with.
G4917: From σύν and thlao (to crush); to dash together, i.e. shatter. In the KJV it is rendered: break.
G4918: From σύν and θλίβω; to compress, i.e. crowd on all sides. In the KJV it is rendered: throng.
G4919: From σύν and thrupto (to crumble); to crush together, i.e. (figuratively) to dispirit. In the KJV it is rendered: break.
G4920: From σύν and hiemi (to send); to put together, i.e. (mentally) to comprehend; by implication, to act piously. In the KJV it is rendered: consider, understand, be wise.
G4921: Or (strengthened) sunistano, or sunistemi from σύν and ἵστημι (including its collateral forms); to set together, i.e. (by implication) to introduce (favorably), or (figuratively) to exhibit; intransitively, to stand near, or (figuratively) to constitute. In the KJV it is rendered: approve, commend, consist, make, stand (with).
G4922: From σύν and ὁδεύω; to travel in company with. In the KJV it is rendered: journey with.
G4923: From a compound of σύν and ὁδός ("synod"); companionship on a journey, i.e. (by implication), a caravan. In the KJV it is rendered: company.
G4924: From σύν and οἰκέω; to reside together (as a family). In the KJV it is rendered: dwell together.
G4925: From σύν and οἰκοδομέω; to construct, i.e. (passively) to compose (in company with other Christians, figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: build together.
G4926: From σύν and ὁμιλέω; to converse mutually. In the KJV it is rendered: talk with.
G4927: From σύν and a derivative of a compound of the base of ὁμοῦ and the base of ὅριον; to border together, i.e. adjoin. In the KJV it is rendered: join hard.
G4928: From συνέχω; restraint, i.e. (figuratively) anxiety. In the KJV it is rendered: anguish, distress.
G4929: From σύν and τάσσω; to arrange jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to direct. In the KJV it is rendered: appoint.
G4930: From συντελέω; entire completion, i.e. consummation (of a dispensation). In the KJV it is rendered: end.
G4931: From σύν and τελέω; to complete entirely; generally, to execute (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: end, finish, fulfil, make.
G4932: From σύν and the base of τομώτερος; to contract by cutting, i.e. (figuratively) do concisely (speedily). In the KJV it is rendered: (cut) short.
G4933: From σύν and τηρέω; to keep closely together, i.e. (by implication) to conserve (from ruin); mentally, to remember (and obey). In the KJV it is rendered: keep, observe, preserve.
G4934: Middle voice from σύν and τίθημι; to place jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to consent (bargain, stipulate), concur. In the KJV it is rendered: agree, assent, covenant.
G4935: Adverb from a derivative of συντέμνω; concisely (briefly). In the KJV it is rendered: a few words.
G4936: From σύν and τρέχω (including its alternate); to rush together (hastily assemble) or headlong (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: run (together, with).
G4937: From σύν and the base of τρίβος; to crush completely, i.e. to shatter (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: break (in pieces), broken to shivers (+ -hearted), bruise.
G4938: From συντρίβω; concussion or utter fracture (properly, concretely), i.e. complete ruin. In the KJV it is rendered: destruction.
G4939: From σύν and τροφός (in a passive sense); a fellow-nursling, i.e. comrade. In the KJV it is rendered: brought up with.
G4940: From σύν and τυγχάνω; to chance together, i.e. meet with (reach). In the KJV it is rendered: come at.
G4941: From συντυγχάνω; an accident; Syntyche, a Christian female. In the KJV it is rendered: Syntyche.
G4942: From σύν and ὑποκρίνομαι; to act hypocritically in concert with. In the KJV it is rendered: dissemble with.
G4943: From σύν and a derivative of a compound of ὑπό and the base of ἔργον; to be a co-auxiliary, i.e. assist. In the KJV it is rendered: help together.
G4944: From σύν and ὠδίνω; to have (parturition) pangs in company (concert, simultaneously) with, i.e. (figuratively) to sympathize (in expectation of relief from suffering). In the KJV it is rendered: travail in pain together.
G4945: From a compound of σύν and ὀμνύω; a swearing together, i.e. (by implication) a plot. In the KJV it is rendered: comspiracy.
G4946: Plural of uncertain derivation; Syracuse, the capital of Sicily. In the KJV it is rendered: Syracuse.
G4947: Probably of Hebrew origin (צֹר); Syria (i.e. Tsyria or Tyre), a region of Asia. In the KJV it is rendered: Syria.
G4948: From the same as Συρία; a Syran (i.e. probably Tyrian), a native of Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Syrian.
G4949: Feminine of a compound of Σύρος and the same as Φοινίκη; a Syro-phœnician woman, i.e. a female native of Phœnicia in Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Syrophenician.
G4950: From σύρω; a shoal (from the sand drawn thither by the waves), i.e. the Syrtis Major or great bay on the north coast of Africa. In the KJV it is rendered: quicksands.
G4951: Probably akin to αἱρέομαι; to trail. In the KJV it is rendered: drag, draw, hale.
G4952: From σύν and σπαράσσω; to rend completely, i.e. (by analogy) to convulse violently. In the KJV it is rendered: throw down.
G4953: Neuter of a compound of σύν and the base of σημαίνω; a sign in common, i.e. preconcerted signal. In the KJV it is rendered: token.
G4954: From σύν and σῶμα; of a joint body, i.e. (figuratively) a fellow-member of the Christian community. In the KJV it is rendered: of the same body.
G4955: From a compound of σύν and a derivative of στάσις; a fellow-insurgent. In the KJV it is rendered: make insurrection with.
G4956: From a derivative of συνιστάω; introductory, i.e. recommendatory. In the KJV it is rendered: of commendation.
G4957: From σύν and σταυρόω; to impale in company with (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: crucify with.
G4958: From σύν and στέλλω; to send (draw) together, i.e. enwrap (enshroud a corpse for burial), contract (an interval). In the KJV it is rendered: short, wind up.
G4959: From σύν and στενάζω; to moan jointly, i.e. (figuratively) experience a common calamity. In the KJV it is rendered: groan together.
G4960: From σύν and στοιχέω; to file together (as soldiers in ranks), i.e. (figuratively) to correspond to. In the KJV it is rendered: answer to.
G4961: From σύν and στρατιώτης; a co-campaigner, i.e. (figuratively) an associate in Christian toil. In the KJV it is rendered: fellowsoldier.
G4962: From σύν and στρέφω; to twist together, i.e. collect (a bundle, a crowd). In the KJV it is rendered: gather.
G4963: From συστρέφω; a twisting together, i.e. (figuratively) a secret coalition, riotous crowd. In the KJV it is rendered: + band together, concourse.
G4964: From σύν and a derivative of σχῆμα; to fashion alike, i.e. conform to the same pattern (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: conform to, fashion self according to.
G4965: Of Hebrew origin (שֵׁכָר); Sychar (i.e. Shekar), a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Sychar.
G4966: Of Hebrew origin (שְׁכֶם); Sychem (i.e. Shekem), the name of a Canaanite and of a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Sychem.
G4967: From σφάζω; butchery (of animals for food or sacrifice, or (figuratively) of men (destruction)). In the KJV it is rendered: slaughter.
G4968: Neuter of a derivative of σφαγή; a victim (in sacrifice). In the KJV it is rendered: slain beast.
G4969: A primary verb; to butcher (especially an animal for food or in sacrifice) or (generally) to slaughter, or (specially), to maim (violently). In the KJV it is rendered: kill, slay, wound.
G4970: Neuter plural of sphodros (violent; of uncertain derivation) as adverb; vehemently, i.e. in a high degree, much. In the KJV it is rendered: exceeding(-ly), greatly, sore, very.
G4971: Adverb from the same as σφόδρα; very much. In the KJV it is rendered: exceedingly.
G4972: From σφραγίς; to stamp (with a signet or private mark) for security or preservation (literally or figuratively); by implication, to keep secret, to attest. In the KJV it is rendered: (set a, set to) seal up, stop.
G4973: Probably strengthened from φράσσω; a signet (as fencing in or protecting from misappropriation); by implication, the stamp impressed (as a mark of privacy, or genuineness), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: seal.
G4974: Neuter of a presumed derivative probably of the same as sphaira (a ball, "sphere"; compare the feminine sphura, a hammer); the ankle (as globular). In the KJV it is rendered: ancle bone.
G4975: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the alternate of ἔχω as adverb; nigh, i.e. nearly. In the KJV it is rendered: almost.
G4976: From the alternate of ἔχω; a figure (as a mode or circumstance), i.e. (by implication) external condition. In the KJV it is rendered: fashion.
G4977: Apparently a primary verb; to split or sever (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: break, divide, open, rend, make a rent.
G4978: From σχίζω; a split or gap ("schism"), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: division, rent, schism.
G4979: Diminutive of schoinos (a rush or flag-plant; of uncertain derivation); a rushlet, i.e. grass-withe or tie (generally). In the KJV it is rendered: small cord, rope.
G4980: From σχολή; to take a holiday, i.e. be at leisure for (by implication, devote oneself wholly to); figuratively, to be vacant (of a house). In the KJV it is rendered: empty, give self.
G4981: Probably feminine of a presumed derivative of the alternate of ἔχω; properly, loitering (as a withholding of oneself from work) or leisure, i.e. (by implication) a "school" (as vacation from physical employment). In the KJV it is rendered: school.
G4982: From a primary sos (contraction for obsolete saos, "safe"); to save, i.e. deliver or protect (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: heal, preserve, save (self), do well, be (make) whole.
G4983: From σώζω; the body (as a sound whole), used in a very wide application, literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: bodily, body, slave.
G4984: From σῶμα; corporeal or physical. In the KJV it is rendered: bodily.
G4985: Adverb from σωματικός; corporeally or physically. In the KJV it is rendered: bodily.
G4986: From the base of σώζω and πατήρ; of a safe father; Sopatrus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Sopater.
G4987: From another form of σορός; to pile up (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: heap, load.
G4988: From the base of σώζω and that of σθενόω; of safe strength; Sosthenes, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Sosthenes.
G4989: Prolongation for Σώπατρος; Sosipatrus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Sosipater.
G4990: From σώζω; a deliverer, i.e. God or Christ. In the KJV it is rendered: saviour.
G4991: Feminine of a derivative of σωτήρ as (properly, abstract) noun; rescue or safety (physically or morally). In the KJV it is rendered: deliver, health, salvation, save, saving.
G4992: Neuter of the same as σωτηρία as (properly, concretely) noun; defender or (by implication) defence. In the KJV it is rendered: salvation.
G4993: From σώφρων; to be of sound mind, i.e. sane, (figuratively) moderate. In the KJV it is rendered: be in right mind, be sober (minded), soberly.
G4994: From σώφρων; to make of sound mind, i.e. (figuratively) to discipline or correct. In the KJV it is rendered: teach to be sober.
G4995: From σωφρονίζω; discipline, i.e. self-control. In the KJV it is rendered: sound mind.
G4996: Adverb from σώφρων; with sound mind, i.e. moderately. In the KJV it is rendered: soberly.
G4997: From σώφρων; soundness of mind, i.e. (literally) sanity or (figuratively) self-control. In the KJV it is rendered: soberness, sobriety.
G4998: From the base of σώζω and that of φρήν; safe (sound) in mind, i.e. self-controlled (moderate as to opinion or passion). In the KJV it is rendered: discreet, sober, temperate.
G4999: Plural of Latin origin; huts or wooden-walled buildings; Tabernæ. In the KJV it is rendered: taverns.
G5000: Of Chaldee origin (compare צְבִיָּה); the gazelle; Tabitha (i.e. Tabjetha), a Christian female. In the KJV it is rendered: Tabitha.
G5001: From τάσσω; something orderly in arrangement (a troop), i.e. (figuratively) a series or succession. In the KJV it is rendered: order.
G5002: From τάσσω; arranged, i.e. appointed or stated. In the KJV it is rendered: set.
G5003: From ταλαίπωρος; to be wretched, i.e. realize one's own misery. In the KJV it is rendered: be afflicted.
G5004: From ταλαίπωρος; wretchedness, i.e. calamity. In the KJV it is rendered: misery.
G5005: From the base of τάλαντον and a derivative of the base of πεῖρα; enduring trial, i.e. miserable. In the KJV it is rendered: wretched.
G5006: From τάλαντον; talent-like in weight. In the KJV it is rendered: weight of a talent.
G5007: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the original form of tlao (to bear; equivalent to φέρω); a balance (as supporting weights), i.e. (by implication) a certain weight (and thence a coin or rather sum of money) or "talent". In the KJV it is rendered: talent.
G5008: Of Chaldee origin (compare טָלֶה); the fresh, i.e. young girl; talitha (O maiden). In the KJV it is rendered: talitha.
G5009: Neuter contraction of a presumed derivative of tamias (a dispenser or distributor; akin to temno, to cut); a dispensary or magazine, i.e. a chamber on the ground-floor or interior of an Oriental house (generally used for storage or privacy, a spot for retirement). In the KJV it is rendered: secret chamber, closet, storehouse.
G5010: From τάσσω; regular arrangement, i.e. (in time) fixed succession (of rank or character), official dignity. In the KJV it is rendered: order.
G5011: Of uncertain derivation; depressed, i.e. (figuratively) humiliated (in circumstances or disposition). In the KJV it is rendered: base, cast down, humble, of low degree (estate), lowly.
G5012: From a compound of ταπεινός and the base of φρήν; humiliation of mind, i.e. modesty. In the KJV it is rendered: humbleness of mind, humility (of mind, loneliness (of mind).
G5013: From ταπεινός; to depress; figuratively, to humiliate (in condition or heart). In the KJV it is rendered: abase, bring low, humble (self).
G5014: From ταπεινόω; depression (in rank or feeling). In the KJV it is rendered: humiliation, be made low, low estate, vile.
G5015: Of uncertain affinity; to stir or agitate (roil water). In the KJV it is rendered: trouble.
G5016: Feminine from ταράσσω; disturbance, i.e. (of water) roiling, or (of a mob) sedition. In the KJV it is rendered: trouble(-ing).
G5017: Masculine from ταράσσω; a disturbance, i.e. (popular) tumult. In the KJV it is rendered: stir.
G5018: From Ταρσός; a Tarsean, i.e. native of Tarsus. In the KJV it is rendered: of Tarsus.
G5019: Perhaps the same as tarsos (a flat basket); Tarsus, a place in Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Tarsus.
G5020: From Tartaros (the deepest abyss of Hades); to incarcerate in eternal torment. In the KJV it is rendered: cast down to hell.
G5021: A prolonged form of a primary verb (which latter appears only in certain tenses); to arrange in an orderly manner, i.e. assign or dispose (to a certain position or lot). In the KJV it is rendered: addict, appoint, determine, ordain, set.
G5022: Apparently a primary word (compare תּוֹרִין, "steer"); a bullock. In the KJV it is rendered: bull, ox.
G5023: Nominative or accusative case neuter plural of οὗτος; these things. In the KJV it is rendered: + afterward, follow, + hereafter, X him, the same, so, such, that, then, these, they, this, those, thus.
G5024: Neuter plural of ὁ and αὐτός as adverb; in the same way. In the KJV it is rendered: even thus, (manner) like, so.
G5025: And tautas dative case and accusative case feminine plural respectively of οὗτος; (to or with or by, etc.) these. In the KJV it is rendered: hence, that, then, these, those.
G5026: And tauten, and tautes dative case, accusative case and genitive case respectively of the feminine singular of οὗτος; (towards or of) this. In the KJV it is rendered: her, + hereof, it, that, + thereby, the (same), this (same).
G5027: Feminine from θάπτω; burial (the act). In the KJV it is rendered: X bury.
G5028: Masculine from θάπτω; a grave (the place of interment). In the KJV it is rendered: sepulchre, tomb.
G5029: As if neuter plural of ταχύς (adverbially); shortly, i.e. (figuratively) possibly. In the KJV it is rendered: peradventure(-haps).
G5030: Adverb from ταχύς; briefly, i.e. (in time) speedily, or (in manner) rapidly. In the KJV it is rendered: hastily, quickly, shortly, soon, suddenly.
G5031: From τάχος; curt, i.e. impending. In the KJV it is rendered: shortly, swift.
G5032: Neuter singular of the comparative of ταχύς (as adverb); more swiftly, i.e. (in manner) more rapidly, or (in time) more speedily. In the KJV it is rendered: out (run), quickly, shortly, sooner.
G5033: Neuter plural of the superlative of ταχύς (as adverb); most quickly, i.e. (with ὡς prefixed) as soon as possible. In the KJV it is rendered: + with all speed.
G5034: From the same as ταχύς; a brief space (of time), i.e. (with ἐν prefixed) in haste. In the KJV it is rendered: + quickly, + shortly, + speedily.
G5035: Neuter singular of ταχύς (as adverb); shortly, i.e. without delay, soon, or (by surprise) suddenly, or (by implication, of ease) readily. In the KJV it is rendered: lightly, quickly.
G5036: Of uncertain affinity; fleet, i.e. (figuratively) prompt or ready. In the KJV it is rendered: swift.
G5037: A primary particle (enclitic) of connection or addition; both or also (properly, as correlation of καί). In the KJV it is rendered: also, and, both, even, then, whether.
G5038: Akin to the base of τίκτω; a wall (as formative of a house). In the KJV it is rendered: wall.
G5039: Neuter of a presumed derivative of tekmar (a goal or fixed limit); a token (as defining a fact), i.e. criterion of certainty. In the KJV it is rendered: infallible proof.
G5040: Diminutive of τέκνον; an infant, i.e. (plural figuratively) darlings (Christian converts). In the KJV it is rendered: little children.
G5041: From a compound of τέκνον and the base of γίνομαι; to be a child-bearer, i.e. parent (mother). In the KJV it is rendered: bear children.
G5042: From the same as τεκνογονέω; childbirth (parentage), i.e. (by implication) maternity (the performance of maternal duties). In the KJV it is rendered: childbearing.
G5043: From the base of τιμωρία; a child (as produced). In the KJV it is rendered: child, daughter, son.
G5044: From a compound of τέκνον and τρέφω; to be a childrearer, i.e. fulfil the duties of a female parent. In the KJV it is rendered: bring up children.
G5045: From the base of τιμωρία; an artificer (as producer of fabrics), i.e. (specially), a craftsman in wood. In the KJV it is rendered: carpenter.
G5046: From τέλος; complete (in various applications of labor, growth, mental and moral character, etc.); neuter (as noun, with ὁ) completeness. In the KJV it is rendered: of full age, man, perfect.
G5047: From τέλειος; (the state) completeness (mentally or morally). In the KJV it is rendered: perfection(-ness).
G5048: From τέλειος; to complete, i.e. (literally) accomplish, or (figuratively) consummate (in character). In the KJV it is rendered: consecrate, finish, fulfil, make) perfect.
G5049: Adverb from τέλειος; completely, i.e. (of hope) without wavering. In the KJV it is rendered: to the end.
G5050: From φυσιόω; (the act) completion, i.e. (of prophecy) verification, or (of expiation) absolution. In the KJV it is rendered: perfection, performance.
G5051: From τελειόω; a completer, i.e. consummater. In the KJV it is rendered: finisher.
G5052: From a compound of τέλος and φέρω; to be a bearer to completion (maturity), i.e. to ripen fruit (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: bring fruit to perfection.
G5053: From a presumed derivative of τελέω; to finish life (by implication, of βίος), i.e. expire (demise). In the KJV it is rendered: be dead, decease, die.
G5054: From τελευτάω; decease. In the KJV it is rendered: death.
G5055: From τέλος; to end, i.e. complete, execute, conclude, discharge (a debt). In the KJV it is rendered: accomplish, make an end, expire, fill up, finish, go over, pay, perform.
G5056: From a primary tello (to set out for a definite point or goal); properly, the point aimed at as a limit, i.e. (by implication) the conclusion of an act or state (termination (literally, figuratively or indefinitely), result (immediate, ultimate or prophetic), purpose); specially, an impost or levy (as paid). In the KJV it is rendered: + continual, custom, end(-ing), finally, uttermost.
G5057: From τέλος and ὠνέομαι; a tax-farmer, i.e. collector of public revenue. In the KJV it is rendered: publican.
G5058: Neuter of a presumed derivative of τελώνης; a tax-gatherer's place of business. In the KJV it is rendered: receipt of custom.
G5059: Of uncertain affinity; a prodigy or omen. In the KJV it is rendered: wonder.
G5060: Of Latin origin; third; Tertius, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Tertius.
G5061: Of uncertain derivation; Tertullus, a Roman. In the KJV it is rendered: Tertullus.
G5062: The decade of τέσσαρες; forty. In the KJV it is rendered: forty.
G5063: From τεσσαράκοντα and ἔτος; of forty years of age. In the KJV it is rendered: (+ full, of) forty years (old).
G5064: Or neuter tessara a plural number; four. In the KJV it is rendered: four.
G5065: From τέσσαρες and καί and δέκατος; fourteenth. In the KJV it is rendered: fourteenth.
G5066: From τέσσαρες; pertaining to the fourth day. In the KJV it is rendered: four days.
G5067: Ordinal from τέσσαρες; fourth. In the KJV it is rendered: four(-th).
G5068: From τέσσαρες and γωνία; four-cornered, i.e. square. In the KJV it is rendered: foursquare.
G5069: Neuter of a presumed derivative of tetras (a tetrad; from τέσσαρες); a quaternion or squad (picket) of four Roman soldiers. In the KJV it is rendered: quaternion.
G5070: From the multiplicative adverb of τέσσαρες and χίλιοι; four times a thousand. In the KJV it is rendered: four thousand.
G5071: Or neuter tetrakosia plural from τέσσαρες and ἑκατόν; four hundred. In the KJV it is rendered: four hundred.
G5072: Neuter of a compound of τέσσαρες and μήν; a four months' space. In the KJV it is rendered: four months.
G5073: From τέσσαρες and a derivative of the base of πλεῖστος; quadruple. In the KJV it is rendered: fourfold.
G5074: From τέσσαρες and πούς; a quadruped. In the KJV it is rendered: fourfooted beast.
G5075: From τετράρχης; to be a tetrarch. In the KJV it is rendered: (be) tetrarch.
G5076: From τέσσαρες and ἄρχω; the ruler of a fourth part of a country ("tetrarch"). In the KJV it is rendered: tetrarch.
G5077: From tephra (ashes); to incinerate, i.e. consume. In the KJV it is rendered: turn to ashes.
G5078: From the base of τίκτω; art (as productive), i.e. (specially), a trade, or (generally) skill. In the KJV it is rendered: art, craft, occupation.
G5079: From τέχνη; an artisan; figuratively, a founder (Creator). In the KJV it is rendered: builder, craftsman.
G5080: Apparently a primary verb; to liquefy. In the KJV it is rendered: melt.
G5081: Adverb from a compound of a derivative of τέλος and αὐγή; in a far-shining manner, i.e. plainly. In the KJV it is rendered: clearly.
G5082: Or feminine telikaute from a compound of ὁ with ἡλίκος and οὗτος; such as this, i.e. (in (figurative) magnitude) so vast. In the KJV it is rendered: so great, so mighty.
G5083: From teros (a watch; perhaps akin to θεωρέω); to guard (from loss or injury, properly, by keeping the eye upon; and thus differing from φυλάσσω, which is properly to prevent escaping; and from κουστωδία, which implies a fortress or full military lines of apparatus), i.e. to note (a prophecy; figuratively, to fulfil a command); by implication, to detain (in custody; figuratively, to maintain); by extension, to withhold (for personal ends; figuratively, to keep unmarried); by extension, to withhold (for personal ends; figuratively, to keep unmarried). In the KJV it is rendered: hold fast, keep(- er), (pre-, re-)serve, watch.
G5084: From τηρέω; a watching, i.e. (figuratively) observance, or (concretely) a prison. In the KJV it is rendered: hold.
G5085: From Τιβέριος; Tiberias, the name of a town and a lake in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Tiberias.
G5086: Of Latin origin; probably pertaining to the river Tiberis or Tiber; Tiberius, a Roman emperor. In the KJV it is rendered: Tiberius.
G5087: A prolonged form of a primary theo (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses); to place (in the widest application, literally and figuratively; properly, in a passive or horizontal posture, and thus different from ἵστημι, which properly denotes an upright and active position, while κεῖμαι is properly reflexive and utterly prostrate). In the KJV it is rendered: + advise, appoint, bow, commit, conceive, give, X kneel down, lay (aside, down, up), make, ordain, purpose, put, set (forth), settle, sink down.
G5088: A strengthened form of a primary teko tek'-o (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses); to produce (from seed, as a mother, a plant, the earth, etc.), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: bear, be born, bring forth, be delivered, be in travail.
G5089: Perhaps akin to the alternate of αἱρέομαι, and thus to σύρω; to pull off. In the KJV it is rendered: pluck.
G5090: Probably of Chaldee origin (compare טָמֵא); Timæus (i.e. Timay), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Timæus.
G5091: From τίμιος; to prize, i.e. fix a valuation upon; by implication, to revere. In the KJV it is rendered: honour, value.
G5092: From τίνω; a value, i.e. money paid, or (concretely and collectively) valuables; by analogy, esteem (especially of the highest degree), or the dignity itself. In the KJV it is rendered: honour, precious, price, some.
G5093: Including the comparative timioteros, and the superlative timiotatos from τιμή; valuable, i.e. (objectively) costly, or (subjectively) honored, esteemed, or (figuratively) beloved. In the KJV it is rendered: dear, honourable, (more, most) precious, had in reputation.
G5094: From τίμιος; expensiveness, i.e. (by implication) magnificence. In the KJV it is rendered: costliness.
G5095: From τιμή and θεός; dear to God; Timotheus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Timotheus, Timothy.
G5096: From τιμή; valuable; Timon, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Timon.
G5097: From a comparative of τιμή and ouros (a guard); properly, to protect one's honor, i.e. to avenge (inflict a penalty). In the KJV it is rendered: punish.
G5098: From τιμωρέω; vindication, i.e. (by implication) a penalty. In the KJV it is rendered: punishment.
G5099: Strengthened for a primary tio (which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses) to pay a price, i.e. as a penalty. In the KJV it is rendered: be punished with.
G5100: An enclitic indefinite pronoun; some or any person or object. In the KJV it is rendered: a (kind of), any (man, thing, thing at all), certain (thing), divers, he (every) man, one (X thing), ought, + partly, some (man, -body, - thing, -what), (+ that no-)thing, what(-soever), X wherewith, whom(-soever), whose(-soever).
G5101: Probably emphatic of τὶς; an interrogative pronoun, who, which or what (in direct or indirect questions). In the KJV it is rendered: every man, how (much), + no(-ne, thing), what (manner, thing), where (-by, -fore, -of, -unto, - with, -withal), whether, which, who(-m, -se), why.
G5102: Of Latin origin; a titulus or "title" (placard). In the KJV it is rendered: title.
G5103: Of Latin origin but uncertain significance; Titus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Titus.
G5104: Probably for the dative case of ὁ; an enclitic particle of asseveration by way of contrast; in sooth. In the KJV it is rendered: (used only with other particles in the comparative, as kaitoige, mentoi, toigaroun, toinun, etc.
G5105: From τοί and γάρ and οὖν; truly for then, i.e. consequently. In the KJV it is rendered: there-(where-)fore.
G5106: From τοί and νῦν; truly now, i.e. accordingly. In the KJV it is rendered: then, therefore.
G5107: (including the other inflections); from a derivative of τοί and δέ; such-like then, i.e. so great. In the KJV it is rendered: such.
G5108: (including the other inflections); from τοί and οὗτος; truly this, i.e. of this sort (to denote character or individuality). In the KJV it is rendered: like, such (an one).
G5109: Another form of τεῖχος; a wall. In the KJV it is rendered: wall.
G5110: From the base of τίκτω; interest on money loaned (as a produce). In the KJV it is rendered: usury.
G5111: From tolma (boldness; probably itself from the base of τέλος through the idea of extreme conduct); to venture (objectively or in act; while θαῤῥέω is rather subjective or in feeling); by implication, to be courageous. In the KJV it is rendered: be bold, boldly, dare, durst.
G5112: Neuter of the compound of a derivative of the base of τολμάω (as adverb); more daringly, i.e. with greater confidence than otherwise. In the KJV it is rendered: the more boldly.
G5113: From τολμάω; a daring (audacious) man. In the KJV it is rendered: presumptuous.
G5114: Comparative of a derivative of the primary temno (to cut; more comprehensive or decisive than κόπτω, as if by a single stroke; whereas that implies repeated blows, like hacking); more keen. In the KJV it is rendered: sharper.
G5115: From the base of τίκτω; a bow (apparently as the simplest fabric). In the KJV it is rendered: bow.
G5116: Neuter of a presumed derivative (alternately) of topazos (a "topaz"; of uncertain origin); a gem, probably the chrysolite. In the KJV it is rendered: topaz.
G5117: Apparently a primary word; a spot (general in space, but limited by occupancy; whereas χώρα is a large but participle locality), i.e. location (as a position, home, tract, etc.); figuratively, condition, opportunity; specially, a scabbard. In the KJV it is rendered: coast, licence, place, X plain, quarter, + rock, room, where.
G5118: From tosos (so much; apparently from ὁ and ὅς) and οὗτος (including its variations); so vast as this, i.e. such (in quantity, amount, number of space). In the KJV it is rendered: as large, so great (long, many, much), these many.
G5119: From (the neuter of) ὁ and ὅτε; the when, i.e. at the time that (of the past or future, also in consecution). In the KJV it is rendered: that time, then.
G5120: Properly, the genitive case of ὁ; sometimes used for τούτου; of this person. In the KJV it is rendered: his.
G5121: Contraction for the neuter of ὁ and ἐναντίον; on the contrary. In the KJV it is rendered: contrariwise.
G5122: Contraction for the neuter of ὁ and ὄνομα; the name (is). In the KJV it is rendered: named.
G5123: Contraction for τοῦτο and ἐστί; that is. In the KJV it is rendered: that is (to say).
G5124: Neuter singular nominative or accusative case of οὗτος; that thing. In the KJV it is rendered: here (-unto), it, partly, self(-same), so, that (intent), the same, there(-fore, -unto), this, thus, where(-fore).
G5125: Dative case plural masculine or neuter of οὗτος; to (for, in, with or by) these (persons or things). In the KJV it is rendered: such, them, there(-in, -with), these, this, those.
G5126: Accusative case singular masculine of οὗτος; this (person, as objective of verb or preposition). In the KJV it is rendered: him, the same, that, this.
G5127: Genitive case singular masculine or neuter of οὗτος; of (from or concerning) this (person or thing). In the KJV it is rendered: here(-by), him, it, + such manner of, that, thence(-forth), thereabout, this, thus.
G5128: Accusative case plural masculine of οὗτος; these (persons, as objective of verb or preposition). In the KJV it is rendered: such, them, these, this.
G5129: Dative case singular masculine or neuter of οὗτος; to (in, with or by) this (person or thing). In the KJV it is rendered: here(-by, -in), him, one, the same, there(-in), this.
G5130: Genitive case plural masculine or neuter of οὗτος; of (from or concerning) these (persons or things). In the KJV it is rendered: such, their, these (things), they, this sort, those.
G5131: From the base of τρώγω; a he-goat (as a gnawer). In the KJV it is rendered: goat.
G5132: Probably contracted from τέσσαρες and πεζῇ; a table or stool (as being four-legged), usually for food (figuratively, a meal); also a counter for money (figuratively, a broker's office for loans at interest). In the KJV it is rendered: bank, meat, table.
G5133: From τράπεζα; a money-broker or banker. In the KJV it is rendered: exchanger.
G5134: From the base of titrosko (to wound; akin to the base of θραύω, τρίβος, τρίζω, etc.); a wound. In the KJV it is rendered: wound.
G5135: From τραῦμα; to inflict a wound. In the KJV it is rendered: wound.
G5136: From τράχηλος; to seize by the throat or neck, i.e. to expose the gullet of a victim for killing (generally, to lay bare). In the KJV it is rendered: opened.
G5137: Probably from τρέχω (through the idea of mobility); the throat (neck), i.e. (figuratively) life. In the KJV it is rendered: neck.
G5138: Perhaps strengthened from the base of ῥήγνυμι (as if jagged by rents); uneven, rocky (reefy). In the KJV it is rendered: rock, rough.
G5139: From a derivative of τραχύς; rough district; Trachonitis, a region of Syria. In the KJV it is rendered: Trachonitis.
G5140: Or neuter tria a primary (plural) number; "three". In the KJV it is rendered: three.
G5141: Strengthened from a primary treo (to "dread", "terrify"); to "tremble" or fear. In the KJV it is rendered: be afraid, trembling.
G5142: A primary verb (properly, threpho; but perhaps strengthened from the base of τροπή through the idea of convolution); properly, to stiffen, i.e. fatten (by implication, to cherish (with food, etc.), pamper, rear). In the KJV it is rendered: bring up, feed, nourish.
G5143: Apparently a primary verb (properly, threcho; compare θρίξ); which uses dremo drem'-o (the base of δρόμος) as alternate in certain tenses; to run or walk hastily (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: have course, run.
G5144: The decade of τρεῖς; thirty. In the KJV it is rendered: thirty.
G5145: Plural from τρεῖς and ἑκατόν; three hundred. In the KJV it is rendered: three hundred.
G5146: From τρεῖς and βέλος; properly, a crow-foot (three-pronged obstruction in war), i.e. (by analogy) a thorny plant (caltrop). In the KJV it is rendered: brier, thistle.
G5147: From tribo (to "rub"; akin to teiro, truo, and the base of τράγος, τραῦμα); a rut or worn track. In the KJV it is rendered: path.
G5148: From a compound of τρεῖς and ἔτος; a three years' period (triennium). In the KJV it is rendered: space of three years.
G5149: Apparently a primary verb; to creak (squeak), i.e. (by analogy) to grate the teeth (in frenzy). In the KJV it is rendered: gnash.
G5150: Neuter of a compound of τρεῖς and μήν as noun; a three months' space. In the KJV it is rendered: three months.
G5151: Adverb from τρεῖς; three times. In the KJV it is rendered: three times, thrice.
G5152: Neuter of a compound of τρεῖς and στέγη as noun; a third roof (story). In the KJV it is rendered: third loft.
G5153: From τρίς and χίλιοι; three times a thousand. In the KJV it is rendered: three thousand.
G5154: Ordinal from τρεῖς; third; neuter (as noun) a third part, or (as adverb) a (or the) third time, thirdly. In the KJV it is rendered: third(-ly).
G5155: From θρίξ; hairy, i.e. made of hair (mohair). In the KJV it is rendered: of hair.
G5156: From τρέμω; a "trembling", i.e. quaking with fear. In the KJV it is rendered: + tremble(-ing).
G5157: From an apparently primary trepo to turn; a turn ("trope"), i.e. revolution (figuratively, variation). In the KJV it is rendered: turning.
G5158: From the same as τροπή; a turn, i.e. (by implication) mode or style (especially with preposition or relative prefix as adverb, like); figuratively, deportment or character. In the KJV it is rendered: (even) as, conversation, (+ like) manner, (+ by any) means, way.
G5159: From τρόπος and φορέω; to endure one's habits. In the KJV it is rendered: suffer the manners.
G5160: From τρέφω; nourishment (literally or figuratively); by implication, rations (wages). In the KJV it is rendered: food, meat.
G5161: From τροφή; nutritive; Trophimus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Trophimus.
G5162: From τρέφω; a nourisher, i.e. nurse. In the KJV it is rendered: nurse.
G5163: From τροχός; a track (as a wheel-rut), i.e. (figuratively) a course of conduct. In the KJV it is rendered: path.
G5164: From τρέχω; a wheel (as a runner), i.e. (figuratively) a circuit of physical effects. In the KJV it is rendered: course.
G5165: Neuter of a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity; a bowl. In the KJV it is rendered: dish.
G5166: From a derivative of trugo (to dry) meaning ripe fruit (as if dry); to collect the vintage. In the KJV it is rendered: gather.
G5167: From truzo (to murmur; akin to τρίζω, but denoting a duller sound); a turtle-dove (as cooing). In the KJV it is rendered: turtle-dove.
G5168: From a derivative of truo (to wear away; akin to the base of τραῦμα, τρίβος and τρώγω); an orifice, i.e. needle's eye. In the KJV it is rendered: eye.
G5169: From a derivative of the base of τρυμαλιά; an aperture, i.e. a needle's eye. In the KJV it is rendered: eye.
G5170: From τρυφή; luxurious; Tryphæna, a Christian woman. In the KJV it is rendered: Tryphena.
G5171: From τρυφή; to indulge in luxury. In the KJV it is rendered: live in pleasure.
G5172: From thrupto (to break up or (figuratively) enfeeble, especially the mind and body by indulgence); effeminacy, i.e. luxury or debauchery. In the KJV it is rendered: delicately, riot.
G5173: From τρυφή; luxuriating; Tryphosa, a Christian female. In the KJV it is rendered: Tryphosa.
G5174: From Tros (a Trojan); the Troad (or plain of Troy), i.e. Troas, a place in Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Troas.
G5175: Of uncertain derivation; Trogyllium, a place in Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Trogyllium.
G5176: Probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of τραῦμα and τρίβος through the idea of corrosion or wear; or perhaps rather of a base of τρυγών and τρίζω through the idea of a craunching sound; to gnaw or chew, i.e. (generally) to eat. In the KJV it is rendered: eat.
G5177: Probably for an obsolete tucho (for which the middle voice of another alternate teucho (to make ready or bring to pass) is used in certain tenses; akin to the base of τίκτω through the idea of effecting; properly, to affect; or (specially), to hit or light upon (as a mark to be reached), i.e. (transitively) to attain or secure an object or end, or (intransitively) to happen (as if meeting with); but in the latter application only impersonal (with εἰ), i.e. perchance; or (present participle) as adjective, usual (as if commonly met with, with οὐ, extraordinary), neuter (as adverb) perhaps; or (with another verb) as adverb, by accident (as it were). In the KJV it is rendered: be, chance, enjoy, little, obtain, X refresh…self, + special.
G5178: From a derivative of τύπτω (meaning a drum, "tympanum"); to stretch on an instrument of torture resembling a drum, and thus beat to death. In the KJV it is rendered: torture.
G5179: From τύπτω; a die (as struck), i.e. (by implication) a stamp or scar; by analogy, a shape, i.e. a statue, (figuratively) style or resemblance; specially, a sampler ("type"), i.e. a model (for imitation) or instance (for warning). In the KJV it is rendered: en-(ex-)ample, fashion, figure, form, manner, pattern, print.
G5180: A primary verb (in a strengthened form); to "thump", i.e. cudgel or pummel (properly, with a stick or bastinado), but in any case by repeated blows; thus differing from παίω and πατάσσω, which denote a (usually single) blow with the hand or any instrument, or πλήσσω with the fist (or a hammer), or ῥαπίζω with the palm; as well as from τυγχάνω, an accidental collision); by implication, to punish; figuratively, to offend (the conscience). In the KJV it is rendered: beat, smite, strike, wound.
G5181: A provincial form of the derivative of the base of κύριος; a "tyrant"; Tyrannus, an Ephesian. In the KJV it is rendered: Tyrannus.
G5182: From turbe (Latin turba, a crowd; akin to θόρυβος); to make "turbid", i.e. disturb. In the KJV it is rendered: trouble.
G5183: From Τύρος; a Tyrian, i.e. inhabitant of Tyrus. In the KJV it is rendered: of Tyre.
G5184: Of Hebrew origin (צֹר): Tyrus (i.e. Tsor), a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Tyre.
G5185: From, τυφόω; opaque (as if smoky), i.e. (by analogy) blind (physically or mentally). In the KJV it is rendered: blind.
G5186: From τυφλός; to make blind, i.e. (figuratively) to obscure. In the KJV it is rendered: blind.
G5187: From a derivative of τύφω; to envelop with smoke, i.e. (figuratively) to inflate with self-conceit. In the KJV it is rendered: high-minded, be lifted up with pride, be proud.
G5188: Apparently a primary verb; to make a smoke, i.e. slowly consume without flame. In the KJV it is rendered: smoke.
G5189: From a derivative of τύφω; stormy (as if smoky). In the KJV it is rendered: tempestuous.
G5190: From a derivative of τυγχάνω; fortuitous, i.e. fortunate; Tychicus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Tychicus.
