G5191: From ὑάκινθος; "hyacinthine" or "jacinthine", i.e. deep blue. In the KJV it is rendered: jacinth.
G5192: Of uncertain derivation; the "hyacinth" or "jacinth", i.e. some gem of a deep blue color, probably the zirkon. In the KJV it is rendered: jacinth.
G5193: From ὕαλος; glassy, i.e. transparent. In the KJV it is rendered: of glass.
G5194: Perhaps from the same as ὑετός (as being transparent like rain); glass. In the KJV it is rendered: glass.
G5195: From ὕβρις; to exercise violence, i.e. abuse. In the KJV it is rendered: use despitefully, reproach, entreat shamefully (spitefully).
G5196: From ὑπέρ; insolence (as over-bearing), i.e. insult, injury. In the KJV it is rendered: harm, hurt, reproach.
G5197: From ὑβρίζω; an insulter, i.e. maltreater. In the KJV it is rendered: despiteful, injurious.
G5198: From ὑγιής; to have sound health, i.e. be well (in body); figuratively, to be uncorrupt (true in doctrine). In the KJV it is rendered: be in health, (be safe and) sound, (be) whole(-some).
G5199: From the base of αὐξάνω; healthy, i.e. well (in body); figuratively, true (in doctrine). In the KJV it is rendered: sound, whole.
G5200: From the base of ὑετός; wet (as if with rain), i.e. (by implication) sappy (fresh). In the KJV it is rendered: green.
G5201: From ὕδωρ; a water-jar, i.e. receptacle for family supply. In the KJV it is rendered: water-pot.
G5202: From a compound of ὕδωρ and a derivative of πίνω; to be a water-drinker, i.e. to abstain from vinous beverages. In the KJV it is rendered: drink water.
G5203: From a compound of ὕδωρ and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι (as if looking watery); to be "dropsical". In the KJV it is rendered: have the dropsy.
G5204: And genitive case, hudatos, etc. from the base of ὑετός; water (as if rainy) literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: water.
G5205: From a primary huo (to rain); rain, especially a shower. In the KJV it is rendered: rain.
G5206: From a presumed compound of υἱός and a derivative of τίθημι; the placing as a son, i.e. adoption (figuratively, Christian sonship in respect to God). In the KJV it is rendered: adoption (of children, of sons).
G5207: Apparently a primary word; a "son" (sometimes of animals), used very widely of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship. In the KJV it is rendered: child, foal, son.
G5208: Perhaps akin to ξύλον; a forest, i.e. (by implication) fuel. In the KJV it is rendered: matter.
G5209: Accusative case of ὑμεῖς; you (as the objective of a verb or preposition). In the KJV it is rendered: ye, you (+ -ward), your (+ own).
G5210: Irregular plural of σύ; you (as subjective of verb). In the KJV it is rendered: ye (yourselves), you.
G5211: From Humen (the god of weddings); "hymenæal"; Hymenæus, an opponent of Christianity. In the KJV it is rendered: Hymenæus.
G5212: From ὑμεῖς; yours, i.e. pertaining to you. In the KJV it is rendered: your (own).
G5213: Irregular dative case of ὑμεῖς; to (with or by) you. In the KJV it is rendered: ye, you, your(-selves).
G5214: From ὕμνος; to hymn, i.e. sing a religious ode; by implication, to celebrate (God) in song. In the KJV it is rendered: sing a hymn (praise unto).
G5215: Apparently from a simpler (obsolete) form of hudeo (to celebrate; probably akin to ᾄδω; compare עֲבוֹט); a "hymn" or religious ode (one of the Psalms). In the KJV it is rendered: hymn.
G5216: Genitive case of ὑμεῖς; of (from or concerning) you. In the KJV it is rendered: ye, you, your (own, -selves).
G5217: From ὑπό and ἄγω; to lead (oneself) under, i.e. withdraw or retire (as if sinking out of sight), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: depart, get hence, go (a-)way.
G5218: From ὑπακούω; attentive hearkening, i.e. (by implication) compliance or submission. In the KJV it is rendered: obedience, (make) obedient, obey(-ing).
G5219: From ὑπό and ἀκούω; to hear under (as a subordinate), i.e. to listen attentively; by implication, to heed or conform to a command or authority. In the KJV it is rendered: hearken, be obedient to, obey.
G5220: From ὑπό and ἀνήρ; in subjection under a man, i.e. a married woman. In the KJV it is rendered: which hath an husband.
G5221: From ὑπό and a derivative of ἀντί; to go opposite (meet) under (quietly), i.e. to encounter, fall in with. In the KJV it is rendered: (go to) meet.
G5222: From ὑπαντάω; an encounter or concurrence (with εἰς for infinitive, in order to fall in with). In the KJV it is rendered: meeting.
G5223: From ὑπάρχω; existency or proprietorship, i.e. (concretely) property, wealth. In the KJV it is rendered: goods, substance.
G5224: Neuter plural of present participle active of ὑπάρχω as noun; things extant or in hand, i.e. property or possessions. In the KJV it is rendered: goods, that which one has, things which (one) possesseth, substance, that hast.
G5225: From ὑπό and ἄρχομαι; to begin under (quietly), i.e. come into existence (be present or at hand); expletively, to exist (as copula or subordinate to an adjective, participle, adverb or preposition, or as an auxiliary to a principal (verb). In the KJV it is rendered: after, behave, live.
G5226: From ὑπό and eiko (to yield, be "weak"); to surrender. In the KJV it is rendered: submit self.
G5227: From ὑπό and ἐναντίος; under (covertly) contrary to, i.e. opposed or (as noun) an opponent. In the KJV it is rendered: adversary, against.
G5228: A primary preposition; "over", i.e. (with the genitive case) of place, above, beyond, across, or causal, for the sake of, instead, regarding; with the accusative case superior to, more than. In the KJV it is rendered: (+ exceeding, abundantly) above, in (on) behalf of, beyond, by, + very chiefest, concerning, exceeding (above, -ly), for, + very highly, more (than), of, over, on the part of, for sake of, in stead, than, to(-ward), very.
G5229: Middle voice from ὑπέρ and αἴρω; to raise oneself over, i.e. (figuratively) to become haughty. In the KJV it is rendered: exalt self, be exalted above measure.
G5230: From ὑπέρ and the base of ἀκμήν; beyond the "acme", i.e. figuratively (of a daughter) past the bloom (prime) of youth. In the KJV it is rendered: + pass the flower of (her) age.
G5231: From ὑπέρ and ἄνω; above upward, i.e. greatly higher (in place or rank). In the KJV it is rendered: far above, over.
G5232: From ὑπέρ and αὐξάνω; to increase above ordinary degree. In the KJV it is rendered: grow exceedingly.
G5233: From ὑπέρ and the base of βάσις; to transcend, i.e. (figuratively) to overreach. In the KJV it is rendered: go beyond.
G5234: Adverb from present participle active of ὑπερβάλλω; excessively. In the KJV it is rendered: beyond measure.
G5235: From ὑπέρ and βάλλω; to throw beyod the usual mark, i.e. (figuratively) to surpass (only active participle supereminent). In the KJV it is rendered: exceeding, excel, pass.
G5236: From ὑπερβάλλω; a throwing beyond others, i.e. (figuratively) supereminence; adverbially (with εἰς or κατά) pre- eminently. In the KJV it is rendered: abundance, (far more) exceeding, excellency, more excellent, beyond (out of) measure.
G5237: From ὑπέρ and εἴδω; to overlook, i.e. not punish. In the KJV it is rendered: wink at.
G5238: From ὑπέρ and the neuter plural of ἐκεῖνος; above those parts, i.e. still farther. In the KJV it is rendered: beyond.
G5239: From ὑπέρ and ἐκτείνω; to extend inordinately. In the KJV it is rendered: stretch beyond.
G5240: From ὑπέρ and the alternate form of ἐκχέω; to pour out over, i.e. (passively) to overflow. In the KJV it is rendered: run over.
G5241: From ὑπέρ and ἐντυγχάνω; to intercede in behalf of. In the KJV it is rendered: make intercession for.
G5242: From ὑπέρ and ἔχω; to hold oneself above, i.e. (figuratively) to excel; participle (as adjective, or neuter as noun) superior, superiority. In the KJV it is rendered: better, excellency, higher, pass, supreme.
G5243: From ὑπερήφανος; haughtiness. In the KJV it is rendered: pride.
G5244: From ὑπέρ and φαίνω; appearing above others (conspicuous), i.e. (figuratively) haughty. In the KJV it is rendered: proud.
G5245: From ὑπέρ and νικάω; to vanquish beyond, i.e. gain a decisive victory. In the KJV it is rendered: more than conquer.
G5246: From ὑπέρ and ὄγκος; bulging over, i.e. (figuratively) insolent. In the KJV it is rendered: great swelling.
G5247: From ὑπερέχω; prominence, i.e. (figuratively) superiority (in rank or character). In the KJV it is rendered: authority, excellency.
G5248: From ὑπέρ and περισσεύω; to super-abound. In the KJV it is rendered: abound much more, exceeding.
G5249: From ὑπέρ and περισσῶς; superabundantly, i.e. exceedingly. In the KJV it is rendered: beyond measure.
G5250: From ὑπέρ and πλεονάζω; to superabound. In the KJV it is rendered: be exceeding abundant.
G5251: From ὑπέρ and ὑψόω; to elevate above others, i.e. raise to the highest position. In the KJV it is rendered: highly exalt.
G5252: From ὑπέρ and φρονέω; to esteem oneself overmuch, i.e. be vain or arrogant. In the KJV it is rendered: think more highly.
G5253: Neuter of a derivative of ὑπέρ; a higher part of the house, i.e. apartment in the third story. In the KJV it is rendered: upper chamber (room).
G5254: From ὑπό and ἔχω; to hold oneself under, i.e. endure with patience. In the KJV it is rendered: suffer.
G5255: From ὑπακούω; attentively listening, i.e. (by implication) submissive. In the KJV it is rendered: obedient.
G5256: From ὑπηρέτης; to be a subordinate, i.e. (by implication) subserve. In the KJV it is rendered: minister (unto), serve.
G5257: From ὑπό and a derivative of eresso (to row); an under-oarsman, i.e. (generally) subordinate (assistant, sexton, constable). In the KJV it is rendered: minister, officer, servant.
G5258: From an obsolete primary (perhaps akin to ὑπό through the idea of subsilience); sleep, i.e. (figuratively) spiritual torpor. In the KJV it is rendered: sleep.
G5259: A primary preposition; under, i.e. (with the genitive case) of place (beneath), or with verbs (the agency or means, through); (with the accusative case) of place (whither (underneath) or where (below) or time (when (at)). In the KJV it is rendered: among, by, from, in, of, under, with.
G5260: From ὑπό and βάλλω; to throw in stealthily, i.e. introduce by collusion. In the KJV it is rendered: suborn.
G5261: From a compound of ὑπό and γράφω; an underwriting, i.e. copy for imitation (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: example.
G5262: From ὑποδείκνυμι; an exhibit for imitation or warning (figuratively, specimen, adumbration). In the KJV it is rendered: en-(ex-)ample, pattern.
G5263: From ὑπό and δεικνύω; to exhibit under the eyes, i.e. (figuratively) to exemplify (instruct, admonish). In the KJV it is rendered: show, (fore-)warn.
G5264: From ὑπό and δέχομαι; to admit under one's roof, i.e. entertain hospitably. In the KJV it is rendered: receive.
G5265: From ὑπό and δέω; to bind under one's feet, i.e. put on shoes or sandals. In the KJV it is rendered: bind on, (be) shod.
G5266: From ὑποδέω; something bound under the feet, i.e. a shoe or sandal. In the KJV it is rendered: shoe.
G5267: From ὑπό and δίκη; under sentence, i.e. (by implication) condemned. In the KJV it is rendered: guilty.
G5268: Neuter of a compound of ὑπό and ζυγός; an animal under the yoke (draught-beast), i.e. (specially), a donkey. In the KJV it is rendered: ass.
G5269: From ὑπό and ζώννυμι; to gird under, i.e. frap (a vessel with cables across the keel, sides and deck). In the KJV it is rendered: undergirt.
G5270: From ὑπό and κάτω; down under, i.e. beneath. In the KJV it is rendered: under.
G5271: Middle voice from ὑπό and κρίνω; to decide (speak or act) under a false part, i.e. (figuratively) dissemble (pretend). In the KJV it is rendered: feign.
G5272: From ὑποκρίνομαι; acting under a feigned part, i.e. (figuratively) deceit ("hypocrisy"). In the KJV it is rendered: condemnation, dissimulation, hypocrisy.
G5273: From ὑποκρίνομαι; an actor under an assumed character (stage-player), i.e. (figuratively) a dissembler ("hypocrite". In the KJV it is rendered: hypocrite.
G5274: From ὑπό and λαμβάνω; to take from below, i.e. carry upward; figuratively, to take up, i.e. continue a discourse or topic; mentally, to assume (presume). In the KJV it is rendered: answer, receive, suppose.
G5275: From ὑποτρέχω and λείπω; to leave under (behind), i.e. (passively) to remain (survive). In the KJV it is rendered: be left.
G5276: Neuter of a presumed compound of ὑπό and ληνός; vessel or receptacle under the press, i.e. lower wine-vat. In the KJV it is rendered: winefat.
G5277: A prolonged form for ὑπολείπω; to leave behind, i.e. bequeath. In the KJV it is rendered: leave.
G5278: From ὑπό and μένω; to stay under (behind), i.e. remain; figuratively, to undergo, i.e. bear (trials), have fortitude, persevere. In the KJV it is rendered: abide, endure, (take) patient(-ly), suffer, tarry behind.
G5279: From ὑπό and μιμνήσκω; to remind quietly, i.e. suggest to the (middle voice, one's own) memory. In the KJV it is rendered: put in mind, remember, bring to (put in) remembrance.
G5280: From ὑπομιμνήσκω; a reminding or (reflexively) recollection. In the KJV it is rendered: remembrance.
G5281: From ὑπομένω; cheerful (or hopeful) endurance, constancy. In the KJV it is rendered: enduring, patience, patient continuance (waiting).
G5282: From ὑπό and νοιέω; to think under (privately), i.e. to surmise or conjecture. In the KJV it is rendered: think, suppose, deem.
G5283: From ὑπονοέω; suspicion. In the KJV it is rendered: surmising.
G5284: From ὑπό and πλέω; to sail under the lee of. In the KJV it is rendered: sail under.
G5285: From ὑπό and πνέω; to breathe gently, i.e. breeze. In the KJV it is rendered: blow softly.
G5286: Neuter of a compound of ὑπό and πούς; something under the feet, i.e. a foot-rest (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: footstool.
G5287: From a compound of ὑπό and ἵστημι; a setting under (support), i.e. (figuratively) concretely, essence, or abstractly, assurance (objectively or subjectively). In the KJV it is rendered: confidence, confident, person, substance.
G5288: From ὑπό and στέλλω; to withhold under (out of sight), i.e. (reflexively) to cower or shrink, (figuratively) to conceal (reserve). In the KJV it is rendered: draw (keep) back, shun, withdraw.
G5289: From ὑποστέλλω; shrinkage (timidity), i.e. (by implication) apostasy. In the KJV it is rendered: draw back.
G5290: From ὑπό and στρέφω; to turn under (behind), i.e. to return (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: come again, return (again, back again), turn back (again).
G5291: From ὑπό and στρώννυμι; to strew underneath (the feet as a carpet). In the KJV it is rendered: spread.
G5292: From ὑποτάσσω; subordination. In the KJV it is rendered: subjection.
G5293: From ὑπό and τάσσω; to subordinate; reflexively, to obey. In the KJV it is rendered: be under obedience (obedient), put under, subdue unto, (be, make) subject (to, unto), be (put) in subjection (to, under), submit self unto.
G5294: From ὑπό and τίθημι; to place underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to hazard, (reflexively) to suggest. In the KJV it is rendered: lay down, put in remembrance.
G5295: From ὑπό and τρέχω (including its alternate); to run under, i.e. (specially), to sail past. In the KJV it is rendered: run under.
G5296: From a compound of ὑπό and a derivative of τύπος; typification under (after), i.e. (concretely) a sketch (figuratively) for imitation. In the KJV it is rendered: form, pattern.
G5297: From ὑπό and φέρω; to bear from underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to undergo hardship. In the KJV it is rendered: bear, endure.
G5298: From ὑπό and χωρέω; to vacate down, i.e. retire quietly. In the KJV it is rendered: go aside, withdraw self.
G5299: From a compound of ὑπό and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι; to hit under the eye (buffet or disable an antagonist as a pugilist), i.e. (figuratively) to tease or annoy (into compliance), subdue (one's passions). In the KJV it is rendered: keep under, weary.
G5300: Apparently a primary word; a hog ("swine"). In the KJV it is rendered: sow.
G5301: Of foreign origin (אֵזוֹב); "hyssop". In the KJV it is rendered: hyssop.
G5302: From ὕστερος; to be later, i.e. (by implication) to be inferior; generally, to fall short (be deficient). In the KJV it is rendered: come behind (short), be destitute, fail, lack, suffer need, (be in) want, be the worse.
G5303: From ὑστερέω; a deficit; specially, poverty. In the KJV it is rendered: that which is behind, (that which was) lack(-ing), penury, want.
G5304: From ὑστερέω; a falling short, i.e. (specially), penury. In the KJV it is rendered: want.
G5305: Neuter of ὕστερος as adverb; more lately, i.e. eventually. In the KJV it is rendered: afterward, (at the) last (of all).
G5306: Comparative from ὑπό (in the sense of behind); later. In the KJV it is rendered: latter.
G5307: From huphaino to weave; woven, i.e. (perhaps) knitted. In the KJV it is rendered: woven.
G5308: From ὕψος; lofty (in place or character). In the KJV it is rendered: high(-er, -ly) (esteemed).
G5309: From a compound of ὑψηλός and φρήν; to be lofty in mind, i.e. arrogant. In the KJV it is rendered: be highminded.
G5310: Superlative from the base of ὕψος; highest, i.e. (masculine singular) the Supreme (God), or (neuter plural) the heavens. In the KJV it is rendered: most high, highest.
G5311: From a derivative of ὑπέρ; elevation, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, (specially), the sky, or (figuratively) dignity. In the KJV it is rendered: be exalted, height, (on) high.
G5312: From ὕψος; to elevate (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: exalt, lift up.
G5313: From ὑψόω; an elevated place or thing, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, or (by implication) a barrier (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: height, high thing.
G5314: From φάγω; a glutton. In the KJV it is rendered: gluttonous.
G5315: A primary verb (used as an alternate of ἐσθίω in certain tenses); to eat (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: eat, meat.
G5316: Prolongation for the base of φῶς; to lighten (shine), i.e. show (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative). In the KJV it is rendered: appear, seem, be seen, shine, X think.
G5317: Of Hebrew origin (פָּ֫לֶג); Phalek (i.e. Peleg), a patriarch. In the KJV it is rendered: Phalec.
G5318: From φαίνω; shining, i.e. apparent (literally or figuratively); neuter (as adverb) publicly, externally. In the KJV it is rendered: abroad, + appear, known, manifest, open (+ -ly), outward (+ -ly).
G5319: From φανερός; to render apparent (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: appear, manifestly declare, (make) manifest (forth), shew (self).
G5320: Adverb from φανερός; plainly, i.e. clearly or publicly. In the KJV it is rendered: evidently, openly.
G5321: From φανερόω; exhibition, i.e. (figuratively) expression, (by extension) a bestowment. In the KJV it is rendered: manifestation.
G5322: From φαίνω; a lightener, i.e. light; lantern. In the KJV it is rendered: lantern.
G5323: Of Hebrew origin (פְּנוּאֵל); Phanuel (i.e. Penuel), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Phanuel.
G5324: From a derivative of φαίνω; to make apparent, i.e. (passively) to appear (neuter participle as noun, a spectacle). In the KJV it is rendered: sight.
G5325: From a derivative of φαντάζω; (properly abstract) a (vain) show ("fantasy"). In the KJV it is rendered: pomp.
G5326: From φαντάζω; (properly concrete) a (mere) show ("phantasm"), i.e. spectre. In the KJV it is rendered: spirit.
G5327: Properly, strengthened from the base of πέραν or rather of ῥήγνυμι; a gap or chasm, i.e. ravine (winter-torrent). In the KJV it is rendered: valley.
G5328: Of foreign origin (פַּרְעֹה); Pharao (i.e. Pharoh), an Egyptian king. In the KJV it is rendered: Pharaoh.
G5329: Of Hebrew origin (פָּ֫רֶץ); Phares (i.e. Perets), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Phares.
G5330: Of Hebrew origin (compare פָּרַשׁ); a separatist, i.e. exclusively religious; a Pharisean, i.e. Jewish sectary. In the KJV it is rendered: Pharisee.
G5331: From φαρμακεύς; medication ("pharmacy"), i.e. (by extension) magic (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: sorcery, witchcraft.
G5332: From pharmakon (a drug, i.e. spell-giving potion); a druggist ("pharmacist") or poisoner, i.e. (by extension) a magician. In the KJV it is rendered: sorcerer.
G5333: The same as φαρμακεύς. In the KJV it is rendered: sorcerer.
G5334: From φημί (not the same as "phase", which is from φαίνω); a saying, i.e. report. In the KJV it is rendered: tidings.
G5335: Prolongation from the same as φημί; to assert. In the KJV it is rendered: affirm, profess, say.
G5336: From pateomai (to eat); a crib (for fodder). In the KJV it is rendered: manager, stall.
G5337: Apparently a primary word; "foul" or "flawy", i.e. (figuratively) wicked. In the KJV it is rendered: evil.
G5338: Probably akin to the base of φῶς (compare φθέγγομαι); brilliancy. In the KJV it is rendered: light.
G5339: Of uncertain affinity; to be chary of, i.e. (subjectively) to abstain or (objectively) to treat leniently. In the KJV it is rendered: forbear, spare.
G5340: Adverb from participle of φείδομαι; abstemiously, i.e. stingily. In the KJV it is rendered: sparingly.
G5341: By transposition for a derivative probably of φαίνω (as showing outside the other garments); a mantle (surtout). In the KJV it is rendered: cloke.
G5342: A primary verb -- for which other, and apparently not cognate ones are used in certain tenses only; namely, oio oy'-o; and enegko en-eng'-ko; to "bear" or carry (in a very wide application, literally and figuratively, as follows). In the KJV it is rendered: be, bear, bring (forth), carry, come, + let her drive, be driven, endure, go on, lay, lead, move, reach, rushing, uphold.
G5343: Apparently a primary verb; to run away (literally or figuratively); by implication, to shun; by analogy, to vanish. In the KJV it is rendered: escape, flee (away).
G5344: Of Latin origin; happy; Phelix (i.e. Felix), a Roman. In the KJV it is rendered: Felix.
G5345: From φημί; a saying, i.e. rumor ("fame"). In the KJV it is rendered: fame.
G5346: Properly, the same as the base of φῶς and φαίνω; to show or make known one's thoughts, i.e. speak or say. In the KJV it is rendered: affirm, say.
G5347: Of Latin derivation; festal; Phestus (i.e. Festus), a Roman. In the KJV it is rendered: Festus.
G5348: Apparently a primary verb; to be beforehand, i.e. anticipate or precede; by extension, to have arrived at. In the KJV it is rendered: (already) attain, come, prevent.
G5349: From φθείρω; decayed, i.e. (by implication) perishable. In the KJV it is rendered: corruptible.
G5350: Probably akin to φέγγος and thus to φημί; to utter a clear sound, i.e. (generally) to proclaim. In the KJV it is rendered: speak.
G5351: Probably strengthened from phthio (to pine or waste); properly, to shrivel or wither, i.e. to spoil (by any process) or (generally) to ruin (especially figuratively, by moral influences, to deprave). In the KJV it is rendered: corrupt (self), defile, destroy.
G5352: From derivative of phthino (to wane; akin to the base of φθείρω) and ὀπώρα (meaning late autumn); autumnal (as stripped of leaves). In the KJV it is rendered: whose fruit withereth.
G5353: From φθέγγομαι; utterance, i.e. a musical note (vocal or instrumental). In the KJV it is rendered: sound.
G5354: From φθόνος; to be jealous of. In the KJV it is rendered: envy.
G5355: Probably akin to the base of φθείρω; ill-will (as detraction), i.e. jealousy (spite). In the KJV it is rendered: envy.
G5356: From φθείρω; decay, i.e. ruin (spontaneous or inflicted, literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: corruption, destroy, perish.
G5357: Of uncertain affinity; a broad shallow cup ("phial"). In the KJV it is rendered: vial.
G5358: From φίλος and ἀγαθός; fond to good, i.e. a promoter of virtue. In the KJV it is rendered: love of good men.
G5359: From Philadelphos (the same as φιλάδελφος), a king of Pergamos; Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Philadelphia.
G5360: From φιλάδελφος; fraternal affection. In the KJV it is rendered: brotherly love (kindness), love of the brethren.
G5361: From φίλος and ἀδελφός; fond of brethren, i.e. fraternal. In the KJV it is rendered: love as brethren.
G5362: From φίλος and ἀνήρ; fond of man, i.e. affectionate as a wife. In the KJV it is rendered: love their husbands.
G5363: From the same as φιλανθρώπως; fondness of mankind, i.e. benevolence ("philanthropy"). In the KJV it is rendered: kindness, love towards man.
G5364: Adverb from a compound of φίλος and ἄνθρωπος; fondly to man ("philanthropically"), i.e. humanely. In the KJV it is rendered: courteously.
G5365: From φιλάργυρος; avarice. In the KJV it is rendered: love of money.
G5366: From φίλος and ἄργυρος; fond of silver (money), i.e. avaricious. In the KJV it is rendered: covetous.
G5367: From φίλος and αὐτός; fond of self, i.e. selfish. In the KJV it is rendered: lover of own self.
G5368: From φίλος; to be a friend to (fond of (an individual or an object)), i.e. have affection for (denoting personal attachment, as a matter of sentiment or feeling; while ἀγαπάω is wider, embracing especially the judgment and the deliberate assent of the will as a matter of principle, duty and propriety: the two thus stand related very much as θέλω and βούλομαι, or as θυμός and νοῦς respectively; the former being chiefly of the heart and the latter of the head); specially, to kiss (as a mark of tenderness). In the KJV it is rendered: kiss, love.
G5369: From φίλος and ἡδονή; fond of pleasure, i.e. voluptuous. In the KJV it is rendered: lover of pleasure.
G5370: From φιλέω; a kiss. In the KJV it is rendered: kiss.
G5371: From φιλέω; friendly; Philemon, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Philemon.
G5372: From φιλέω; amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity. In the KJV it is rendered: Philetus.
G5373: From φίλος; fondness. In the KJV it is rendered: friendship.
G5374: From Φίλιπποι; a Philippesian (Philippian), i.e. native of Philippi. In the KJV it is rendered: Philippian.
G5375: Plural of Φίλιππος; Philippi, a place in Macedonia. In the KJV it is rendered: Philippi.
G5376: From φίλος and ἵππος; fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites. In the KJV it is rendered: Philip.
G5377: From φίλος and θεός; fond of God, i.e. pious. In the KJV it is rendered: lover of God.
G5378: From φίλος and λόγος; fond of words, i.e. talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Philologus.
G5379: From φιλόνεικος; quarrelsomeness, i.e. a dispute. In the KJV it is rendered: strife.
G5380: From φίλος and neikos (a quarrel; probably akin to νῖκος); fond of strife, i.e. disputatious. In the KJV it is rendered: contentious.
G5381: From φιλόξενος; hospitableness. In the KJV it is rendered: entertain stranger, hospitality.
G5382: From φίλος and ξένος; fond of guests, i.e. hospitable. In the KJV it is rendered: given to (lover of, use) hospitality.
G5383: From a compound of φίλος and πρῶτος; to be fond of being first, i.e. ambitious of distinction. In the KJV it is rendered: love to have the preeminence.
G5384: Properly, dear, i.e. a friend; actively, fond, i.e. friendly (still as a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: friend.
G5385: From φιλόσοφος; "philosophy", i.e. (specially), Jewish sophistry. In the KJV it is rendered: philosophy.
G5386: From φίλος and σοφός; fond of wise things, i.e. a "philosopher". In the KJV it is rendered: philosopher.
G5387: From φίλος and storge (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children); fond of natural relatives, i.e. fraternal towards fellow Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: kindly affectioned.
G5388: From φίλος and τέκνον; fond of one's children, i.e. maternal. In the KJV it is rendered: love their children.
G5389: Middle voice from a compound of φίλος and τιμή; to be fond of honor, i.e. emulous (eager or earnest to do something). In the KJV it is rendered: labour, strive, study.
G5390: Adverb from φιλόφρων; with friendliness of mind, i.e. kindly. In the KJV it is rendered: courteously.
G5391: From φίλος and φρήν; friendly of mind, i.e. kind. In the KJV it is rendered: courteous.
G5392: From phimos (a muzzle); to muzzle. In the KJV it is rendered: muzzle.
G5393: Active participle of the base of φλόξ; blazing; Phlegon, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Phlegon.
G5394: From φλόξ; to cause a blaze, i.e. ignite (figuratively, to inflame with passion). In the KJV it is rendered: set on fire.
G5395: From a primary phlego (to "flash" or "flame"); a blaze. In the KJV it is rendered: flame(-ing).
G5396: From φλύαρος; to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously. In the KJV it is rendered: prate against.
G5397: From phluo (to bubble); a garrulous person, i.e. prater. In the KJV it is rendered: tattler.
G5398: From φόβος; frightful, i.e. (objectively) formidable. In the KJV it is rendered: fearful, terrible.
G5399: From φόβος; to frighten, i.e. (passively) to be alarmed; by analogy, to be in awe of, i.e. revere. In the KJV it is rendered: be (+ sore) afraid, fear (exceedingly), reverence.
G5400: Neuter of a derivative of φοβέω; a frightening thing, i.e. terrific portent. In the KJV it is rendered: fearful sight.
G5401: From a primary phebomai (to be put in fear); alarm or fright. In the KJV it is rendered: be afraid, + exceedingly, fear, terror.
G5402: Feminine of phoibos (bright; probably akin to the base of φῶς); Phœbe, a Christian woman. In the KJV it is rendered: Phebe.
G5403: From φοῖνιξ; palm-country; Phœnice (or Phœnicia), a region of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Phenice, Phenicia.
G5404: Of uncertain derivation; a palm-tree. In the KJV it is rendered: palm (tree).
G5405: Probably the same as φοῖνιξ; Phœnix, a place in Crete. In the KJV it is rendered: Phenice.
G5406: From φόνος; a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional) homicide; which ἀνθρωποκτόνος does not necessarily imply; while σικάριος is a special term for a public bandit). In the KJV it is rendered: murderer.
G5407: From φονεύς; to be a murderer (of). In the KJV it is rendered: kill, do murder, slay.
G5408: From an obsolete primary pheno (to slay); murder. In the KJV it is rendered: murder, + be slain with, slaughter.
G5409: From φόρος; to have a burden, i.e. (by analogy) to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment. In the KJV it is rendered: bear, wear.
G5410: Of Latin origin; a forum or market-place; only in comparative with Ἄππιος; a station on the Appian road. In the KJV it is rendered: forum.
G5411: From φέρω; a load (as borne), i.e. (figuratively) a tax (properly, an individual assessment on persons or property; whereas τέλος is usually a general toll on goods or travel). In the KJV it is rendered: tribute.
G5412: From φόρτος; to load up (properly, as a vessel or animal), i.e. (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual anxiety). In the KJV it is rendered: lade, by heavy laden.
G5413: Diminutive of φόρτος; an invoice (as part of freight), i.e. (figuratively) a task or service. In the KJV it is rendered: burden.
G5414: From φέρω; something carried, i.e. the cargo of a ship. In the KJV it is rendered: lading.
G5415: Of Latin origin; "fortunate"; Fortunatus, a Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Fortunatus.
G5416: Neuter of a derivative from the base of φραγελλόω; a whip, i.e. Roman lash as a public punishment. In the KJV it is rendered: scourge.
G5417: From a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum; to whip, i.e. lash as a public punishment. In the KJV it is rendered: scourge.
G5418: From φράσσω; a fence, or inclosing barrier (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: hedge (+ round about), partition.
G5419: Probably akin to φράσσω through the idea of defining; to indicate (by word or act), i.e. (specially), to expound. In the KJV it is rendered: declare.
G5420: Apparently a strengthening form of the base of φρήν; to fence or inclose, i.e. (specially), to block up (figuratively, to silence). In the KJV it is rendered: stop.
G5421: Of uncertain derivation; a hole in the ground (dug for obtaining or holding water or other purposes), i.e. a cistern or well; figuratively, an abyss (as a prison). In the KJV it is rendered: well, pit.
G5422: From φρεναπάτης; to be a mind-misleader, i.e. delude. In the KJV it is rendered: deceive.
G5423: From φρήν and ἀπάτη; a mind-misleader, i.e. seducer. In the KJV it is rendered: deceiver.
G5424: Probably from an obsolete phrao (to rein in or curb; compare φράσσω); the midrif (as a partition of the body), i.e. (figuratively and by implication, of sympathy) the feelings (or sensitive nature; by extension (also in the plural) the mind or cognitive faculties). In the KJV it is rendered: understanding.
G5425: Apparently a primary verb; to "bristle" or chill, i.e. shudder (fear). In the KJV it is rendered: tremble.
G5426: From φρήν; to exercise the mind, i.e. entertain or have a sentiment or opinion; by implication, to be (mentally) disposed (more or less earnestly in a certain direction); intensively, to interest oneself in (with concern or obedience). In the KJV it is rendered: set the affection on, (be) care(-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind(-ed), regard, savour, think.
G5427: From φρονέω; (mental) inclination or purpose. In the KJV it is rendered: (be, + be carnally, + be spiritually) mind(-ed).
G5428: From φρονέω; mental action or activity, i.e. intellectual or moral insight. In the KJV it is rendered: prudence, wisdom.
G5429: From φρήν; thoughtful, i.e. sagacious or discreet (implying a cautious character; while σοφός denotes practical skill or acumen; and συνετός indicates rather intelligence or mental acquirement); in a bad sense conceited (also in the comparative). In the KJV it is rendered: wise(-r).
G5430: Adverb from φρόνιμος; prudently. In the KJV it is rendered: wisely.
G5431: From a derivative of φρήν; to exercise thought, i.e. be anxious. In the KJV it is rendered: be careful.
G5432: From a compound of πρό and ὁράω; to be a watcher in advance, i.e. to mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem in, protect. In the KJV it is rendered: keep (with a garrison).
G5433: Akin to βρύω, βρύχω; to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e. (figuratively) to make a tumult. In the KJV it is rendered: rage.
G5434: Neuter of a presumed derivative of phrugo (to roast or parch; akin to the base of φλόξ); something desiccated, i.e. a dry twig. In the KJV it is rendered: stick.
G5435: Probably of foreign origin; Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor. In the KJV it is rendered: Phrygia.
G5436: Probably from φεύγω; fugitive; Phygellus, an apostate Christian. In the KJV it is rendered: Phygellus.
G5437: From φεύγω; a fleeing, i.e. escape. In the KJV it is rendered: flight.
G5438: From φυλάσσω; a guarding or (concretely, guard), the act, the person; figuratively, the place, the condition, or (specially), the time (as a division of day or night), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: cage, hold, (im-)prison(-ment), ward, watch.
G5439: From φύλαξ; to incarcerate. In the KJV it is rendered: imprison.
G5440: Neuter of a derivative of φυλάσσω; a guard-case, i.e. "phylactery" for wearing slips of Scripture texts. In the KJV it is rendered: phylactery.
G5441: From φυλάσσω; a watcher or sentry. In the KJV it is rendered: keeper.
G5442: Probably from φυλή through the idea of isolation; to watch, i.e. be on guard (literally of figuratively); by implication, to preserve, obey, avoid. In the KJV it is rendered: beward, keep (self), observe, save.
G5443: From φύω (compare φύλλον); an offshoot, i.e. race or clan. In the KJV it is rendered: kindred, tribe.
G5444: From the same as φυλή; a sprout, i.e. leaf. In the KJV it is rendered: leaf.
G5445: From a prolonged form of phuro (to mix a liquid with a solid; perhaps akin to φύω through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a mass of dough. In the KJV it is rendered: lump.
G5446: From φύσις; "physical", i.e. (by implication) instinctive. In the KJV it is rendered: natural.
G5447: Adverb from φυσικός; "physically", i.e. (by implication) instinctively. In the KJV it is rendered: naturally.
G5448: From φύσις in the primary sense of blowing; to inflate, i.e. (figuratively) make proud (haughty). In the KJV it is rendered: puff up.
G5449: From φύω; growth (by germination or expansion), i.e. (by implication) natural production (lineal descent); by extension, a genus or sort; figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage. In the KJV it is rendered: (man-)kind, nature(-al).
G5450: From φυσιόω; inflation, i.e. (figuratively) haughtiness. In the KJV it is rendered: swelling.
G5451: From φυτεύω; trans-planting, i.e. (concretely) a shrub or vegetable. In the KJV it is rendered: plant.
G5452: From a derivative of φύω; to set out in the earth, i.e. implant; figuratively, to instil doctrine. In the KJV it is rendered: plant.
G5453: A primary verb; probably originally, to "puff" or blow, i.e. to swell up; but only used in the implied sense, to germinate or grow (sprout, produce), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: spring (up).
G5454: Of uncertain derivative; a burrow or lurking-place. In the KJV it is rendered: hole.
G5455: From φωνή; to emit a sound (animal, human or instrumental); by implication, to address in words or by name, also in imitation. In the KJV it is rendered: call (for), crow, cry.
G5456: Probably akin to φαίνω through the idea of disclosure; a tone (articulate, bestial or artificial); by implication, an address (for any purpose), saying or language. In the KJV it is rendered: noise, sound, voice.
G5457: From an obsolete phao (to shine or make manifest, especially by rays; compare φαίνω, φημί); luminousness (in the widest application, natural or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative). In the KJV it is rendered: fire, light.
G5458: From φῶς; an illuminator, i.e. (concretely) a luminary, or (abstractly) brilliancy. In the KJV it is rendered: light.
G5459: From φῶς and φέρω; light-bearing ("phosphorus"), i.e. (specially), the morning-star (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: day star.
G5460: From φῶς; lustrous, i.e. transparent or well-illuminated (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: bright, full of light.
G5461: From φῶς; to shed rays, i.e. to shine or (transitively) to brighten up (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: enlighten, illuminate, (bring to, give) light, make to see.
G5462: From φωτίζω; illumination (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: light.
G5463: A primary verb; to be "cheer"ful, i.e. calmly happy or well-off; impersonally, especially as salutation (on meeting or parting), be well. In the KJV it is rendered: farewell, be glad, God speed, greeting, hall, joy(- fully), rejoice.
G5464: Probably from χαλάω; hail. In the KJV it is rendered: hail.
G5465: From the base of χάσμα; to lower (as into a void). In the KJV it is rendered: let down, strike.
G5466: Probably of Hebrew or (כַּשְׂדִּי); a Chaldæan (i.e. Kasdi), or native or the region of the lower Euphrates. In the KJV it is rendered: Chaldæan.
G5467: Perhaps from χαλάω through the idea of reducing the strength; difficult, i.e. dangerous, or (by implication) furious. In the KJV it is rendered: fierce, perilous.
G5468: From a compound of χαλινός and the reduplicated form of ἄγω; to be a bit-leader, i.e. to curb (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: bridle.
G5469: From χαλάω; a curb or head-stall (as curbing the spirit). In the KJV it is rendered: bit, bridle.
G5470: From χαλκός; coppery. In the KJV it is rendered: brass.
G5471: From χαλκός; a copper-worker or brazier. In the KJV it is rendered: coppersmith.
G5472: From χαλκός and perhaps εἶδος; copper-like, i.e. "chalcedony". In the KJV it is rendered: chalcedony.
G5473: Diminutive from χαλκός; a copper dish. In the KJV it is rendered: brazen vessel.
G5474: Neuter of a compound of χαλκός and λίβανος (in the implied mean of whiteness or brilliancy); burnished copper, an alloy of copper (or gold) and silver having a brilliant lustre. In the KJV it is rendered: fine brass.
G5475: Perhaps from χαλάω through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this metal being chiefly used for that purpose); copper (the substance, or some implement or coin made of it). In the KJV it is rendered: brass, money.
G5476: Adverb perhaps from the base of χάσμα through the idea of a fissure in the soil; earthward, i.e. prostrate. In the KJV it is rendered: on (to) the ground.
G5477: Of Hebrew origin (כְּנַ֫עַן); Chanaan (i.e. Kenaan), the early name of Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Chanaan.
G5478: From Χαναάν; a Chanaanæan (i.e. Kenaanite), or native of gentile Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: of Canaan.
G5479: From χαίρω; cheerfulness, i.e. calm delight. In the KJV it is rendered: gladness, X greatly, (X be exceeding) joy(-ful, -fully, -fulness, -ous).
G5480: From the same as χάραξ; a scratch or etching, i.e. stamp (as a badge of servitude), or scupltured figure (statue). In the KJV it is rendered: graven, mark.
G5481: From the same as χάραξ; a graver (the tool or the person), i.e. (by implication) engraving (("character"), the figure stamped, i.e. an exact copy or (figuratively) representation). In the KJV it is rendered: express image.
G5482: From charasso (to sharpen to a point; akin to γράφω through the idea of scratching); a stake, i.e. (by implication) a palisade or rampart (military mound for circumvallation in a siege). In the KJV it is rendered: trench.
G5483: Middle voice from χάρις; to grant as a favor, i.e. gratuitously, in kindness, pardon or rescue. In the KJV it is rendered: deliver, (frankly) forgive, (freely) give, grant.
G5484: Accusative case of χάρις as preposition; through favor of, i.e. on account of. In the KJV it is rendered: be-(for) cause of, for sake of, +…fore, X reproachfully.
G5485: From χαίρω; graciousness (as gratifying), of manner or act (abstract or concrete; literal, figurative or spiritual; especially the divine influence upon the heart, and its reflection in the life; including gratitude). In the KJV it is rendered: acceptable, benefit, favour, gift, grace(- ious), joy, liberality, pleasure, thank(-s, -worthy).
G5486: From χαρίζομαι; a (divine) gratuity, i.e. deliverance (from danger or passion); (specially), a (spiritual) endowment, i.e. (subjectively) religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty. In the KJV it is rendered: (free) gift.
G5487: From χάρις; to grace, i.e. indue with special honor. In the KJV it is rendered: make accepted, be highly favoured.
G5488: Of Hebrew origin (חָרָן); Charrhan (i.e. Charan), a place in Mesopotamia. In the KJV it is rendered: Charran.
G5489: From the same as χάραξ; a sheet ("chart") of writing-material (as to be scribbled over). In the KJV it is rendered: paper.
G5490: From a form of an obsolete primary chao (to "gape" or "yawn"); a "chasm" or vacancy (impassable interval). In the KJV it is rendered: gulf.
G5491: From a form of the same as χάσμα; a lip (as a pouring place); figuratively, a margin (of water). In the KJV it is rendered: lip, shore.
G5492: From the same as χειμών; to storm, i.e. (passively) to labor under a gale. In the KJV it is rendered: be tossed with tempest.
G5493: From the base of χειμών and ῥέω; a storm-runlet, i.e. winter-torrent. In the KJV it is rendered: brook.
G5494: From a derivative of cheo (to pour; akin to the base of χάσμα through the idea of a channel), meaning a storm (as pouring rain); by implication, the rainy season, i.e. winter. In the KJV it is rendered: tempest, foul weather, winter.
G5495: Perhaps from the base of χειμών in the sense of its congener the base of χάσμα (through the idea of hollowness for grasping); the hand (literally or figuratively (power); especially (by Hebraism) a means or instrument). In the KJV it is rendered: hand.
G5496: From χειραγωγός; to be a hand-leader, i.e. to guide (a blind person). In the KJV it is rendered: lead by the hand.
G5497: From χείρ and a reduplicated form of ἄγω; a hand-leader, i.e. personal conductor (of a blind person). In the KJV it is rendered: some to lead by the hand.
G5498: Neuter of a compound of χείρ and γράφω; something hand-written ("chirograph"), i.e. a manuscript (specially, a legal document or bond (figuratively)). In the KJV it is rendered: handwriting.
G5499: From χείρ and a derivative of ποιέω; manufactured, i.e. of human construction. In the KJV it is rendered: made by (make with) hands.
G5500: From a comparative of χείρ and teino (to stretch); to be a hand-reacher or voter (by raising the hand), i.e. (generally) to select or appoint. In the KJV it is rendered: choose, ordain.
G5501: Irregular comparative of κακός; from an obsolete equivalent cheres (of uncertain derivation); more evil or aggravated (physically, mentally or morally). In the KJV it is rendered: sorer, worse.
G5502: Plural of Hebrew origin (כְּרוּב); "cherubim" (i.e. cherubs or kerubim). In the KJV it is rendered: cherubims.
G5503: Feminine of a presumed derivative apparently from the base of χάσμα through the idea of deficiency; a widow (as lacking a husband), literally or figuratively. In the KJV it is rendered: widow.
G5504: Of uncertain derivation; "yesterday"; by extension, in time past or hitherto. In the KJV it is rendered: yesterday.
G5505: From χίλιοι; one thousand ("chiliad"). In the KJV it is rendered: thousand.
G5506: From χίλιοι and ἄρχω; the commander of a thousand soldiers ("chiliarch"; i.e. colonel. In the KJV it is rendered: (chief, high) captain.
G5507: Plural of uncertain affinity; a thousand. In the KJV it is rendered: thousand.
G5508: Of uncertain derivation; Chios, an island in the Mediterranean. In the KJV it is rendered: Chios.
G5509: Of foreign origin (כֻּתֹּ֫נֶת); a tunic or shirt. In the KJV it is rendered: clothes, coat, garment.
G5510: Perhaps akin to the base of χάσμα (χαλάω) or χειμών (as descending or empty); snow. In the KJV it is rendered: snow.
G5511: Of uncertain derivation; a military cloak. In the KJV it is rendered: robe.
G5512: From a derivative probably of χεῖλος; to throw out the lip, i.e. jeer at. In the KJV it is rendered: mock.
G5513: From chlio (to warm); tepid. In the KJV it is rendered: lukewarm.
G5514: Feminine of apparently a primary word; "green"; Chloë, a Christian female. In the KJV it is rendered: Chloe.
G5515: From the same as Χλόη; greenish, i.e. verdant, dun-colored. In the KJV it is rendered: green, pale.
G5516: The 22nd, 14th and an obsolete letter (στίγμα as a cross) of the Greek alphabet (intermediate between the 5th and 6th), used as numbers; denoting respectively 600, 60 and 6; 666 as a numeral. In the KJV it is rendered: six hundred threescore and six.
G5517: From χόος; dusty or dirty (soil-like), i.e. (by implication) terrene. In the KJV it is rendered: earthy.
G5518: Of uncertain derivation; a chœnix or certain dry measure. In the KJV it is rendered: measure.
G5519: Of uncertain derivation; a hog. In the KJV it is rendered: swine.
G5520: From χολή; to be bilious, i.e. (by implication) irritable (enraged, "choleric"). In the KJV it is rendered: be angry.
G5521: Feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as Χλόη (from the greenish hue); "gall" or bile, i.e. (by analogy) poison or an anodyne (wormwood, poppy, etc.). In the KJV it is rendered: gall.
G5522: From the base of χειμών; a heap (as poured out), i.e. rubbish; loose dirt. In the KJV it is rendered: dust.
G5523: Of uncertain derivation; Chorazin, a place in Palestine. In the KJV it is rendered: Chorazin.
G5524: From a compound of χορός and ἄγω; to be a dance-leader, i.e. (generally) to furnish. In the KJV it is rendered: give, minister.
G5525: Of uncertain derivation; a ring, i.e. round dance ("choir". In the KJV it is rendered: dancing.
G5526: From χόρτος; to fodder, i.e. (generally) to gorge (supply food in abundance). In the KJV it is rendered: feed, fill, satisfy.
G5527: From χορτάζω; forage, i.e. food. In the KJV it is rendered: sustenance.
G5528: Apparently a primary word; a "court" or "garden", i.e. (by implication, of pasture) herbage or vegetation. In the KJV it is rendered: blade, grass, hay.
G5529: Of uncertain origin; Chuzas, an officer of Herod. In the KJV it is rendered: Chuza.
G5530: Middle voice of a primary verb (perhaps rather from χείρ, to handle); to furnish what is needed; (give an oracle, "graze" (touch slightly), light upon, etc.), i.e. (by implication) to employ or (by extension) to act towards one in a given manner. In the KJV it is rendered: entreat, use.
G5531: Probably the same as the base of χράομαι; to loan. In the KJV it is rendered: lend.
G5532: From the base of χράομαι or χρή; employment, i.e. an affair; also (by implication) occasion, demand, requirement or destitution. In the KJV it is rendered: business, lack, necessary(-ity), need(-ful), use, want.
G5533: From a derivative of χράω and ὀφειλέτης; a loan-ower, i.e. indebted person. In the KJV it is rendered: debtor.
G5534: Third person singular of the same as χράομαι or χράω used impersonally; it needs (must or should) be. In the KJV it is rendered: ought.
G5535: From χρεία; to make (i.e. have) necessity, i.e. be in want of. In the KJV it is rendered: (have) need.
G5536: Something useful or needed, i.e. wealth, price. In the KJV it is rendered: money, riches.
G5537: From χρῆμα; to utter an oracle (compare the original sense of χράομαι), i.e. divinely intimate; by implication, (compare the secular sense of χρεία) to constitute a firm for business, i.e. (generally) bear as a title. In the KJV it is rendered: be called, be admonished (warned) of God, reveal, speak.
G5538: From χρηματίζω; a divine response or revelation. In the KJV it is rendered: answer of God.
G5539: From χρῆσις; serviceable. In the KJV it is rendered: profit.
G5540: From χράομαι; employment, i.e. (specially), sexual intercourse (as an occupation of the body). In the KJV it is rendered: use.
G5541: Middle voice from χρηστός; to show oneself useful, i.e. act benevolently. In the KJV it is rendered: be kind.
G5542: From a compound of χρηστός and λέγω; fair speech, i.e. plausibility. In the KJV it is rendered: good words.
G5543: From χράομαι; employed, i.e. (by implication) useful (in manner or morals). In the KJV it is rendered: better, easy, good(-ness), gracious, kind.
G5544: From χρηστός; usefulness, i.e. morally, excellence (in character or demeanor). In the KJV it is rendered: gentleness, good(-ness), kindness.
G5545: From χρίω; an unguent or smearing, i.e. (figuratively) the special endowment ("chrism") of the Holy Spirit. In the KJV it is rendered: anointing, unction.
G5546: From Χριστός; a Christian, i.e. follower of Christ. In the KJV it is rendered: Christian.
G5547: From χρίω; anointed, i.e. the Messiah, an epithet of Jesus. In the KJV it is rendered: Christ.
G5548: Probably akin to χράομαι through the idea of contact; to smear or rub with oil, i.e. (by implication) to consecrate to an office or religious service. In the KJV it is rendered: anoint.
G5549: From χρόνος; to take time, i.e. linger. In the KJV it is rendered: delay, tarry.
G5550: Of uncertain derivation; a space of time (in general, and thus properly distinguished from καιρός, which designates a fixed or special occasion; and from αἰών, which denotes a particular period) or interval; by extension, an individual opportunity; by implication, delay. In the KJV it is rendered: + years old, season, space, (X often-)time(-s), (a) while.
G5551: From a presumed compound of χρόνος and the base of τρίβος; to be a time-wearer, i.e. to procrastinate (linger). In the KJV it is rendered: spend time.
G5552: From χρυσός; made of gold. In the KJV it is rendered: of gold, golden.
G5553: Diminutive of χρυσός; a golden article, i.e. gold plating, ornament, or coin. In the KJV it is rendered: gold.
G5554: From χρυσός and δακτύλιος; gold-ringed, i.e. wearing a golden finger-ring or similar jewelry. In the KJV it is rendered: with a gold ring.
G5555: From χρυσός and λίθος; gold-stone, i.e. a yellow gem ("chrysolite"). In the KJV it is rendered: chrysolite.
G5556: From χρυσός and prason (a leek); a greenish-yellow gem ("chrysoprase"). In the KJV it is rendered: chrysoprase.
G5557: Perhaps from the base of χράομαι (through the idea of the utility of the metal); gold; by extension, a golden article, as an ornament or coin. In the KJV it is rendered: gold.
G5558: From χρυσός; to gild, i.e. bespangle with golden ornaments. In the KJV it is rendered: deck.
G5559: Probably akin to the base of χράομαι through the idea of handling; the body (properly, its surface or skin). In the KJV it is rendered: body.
G5560: Apparently a primary word; "halt", i.e. limping. In the KJV it is rendered: cripple, halt, lame.
G5561: Feminine of a derivative of the base of χάσμα through the idea of empty expanse; room, i.e. a space of territory (more or less extensive; often including its inhabitants). In the KJV it is rendered: coast, county, fields, ground, land, region.
G5562: From χώρα; to be in (give) space, i.e. (intransitively) to pass, enter, or (transitively) to hold, admit (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: come, contain, go, have place, (can, be room to) receive.
G5563: From χώρα; to place room between, i.e. part; reflexively, to go away. In the KJV it is rendered: depart, put asunder, separate.
G5564: Diminutive of χώρα; a spot or plot of ground. In the KJV it is rendered: field, land, parcel of ground, place, possession.
G5565: Adverb from χώρα; at a space, i.e. separately or apart from (often as preposition). In the KJV it is rendered: beside, by itself, without.
G5566: Of Latin origin; the north-west wind. In the KJV it is rendered: north west.
G5567: Probably strengthened from psao (to rub or touch the surface; compare ψώχω); to twitch or twang, i.e. to play on a stringed instrument (celebrate the divine worship with music and accompanying odes). In the KJV it is rendered: make melody, sing (psalms).
G5568: From ψάλλω; a set piece of music, i.e. a sacred ode (accompanied with the voice, harp or other instrument; a "psalm"); collectively, the book of the Psalms. In the KJV it is rendered: psalm.
G5569: From ψευδής and ἀδελφός; a spurious brother, i.e. pretended associate. In the KJV it is rendered: false brethren.
G5570: From ψευδής and ἀπόστολος; a spurious apostle, i.e. pretended pracher. In the KJV it is rendered: false teacher.
G5571: From ψεύδομαι; untrue, i.e. erroneous, deceitful, wicked. In the KJV it is rendered: false, liar.
G5572: From ψευδής and διδάσκαλος; a spurious teacher, i.e. propagator of erroneous Christian doctrine. In the KJV it is rendered: false teacher.
G5573: From ψευδής and λέγω; mendacious, i.e. promulgating erroneous Christian doctrine. In the KJV it is rendered: speaking lies.
G5574: Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to utter an untruth or attempt to deceive by falsehood. In the KJV it is rendered: falsely, lie.
G5575: From ψευδής and a kindred form of μάρτυς; a spurious witness, i.e. bearer of untrue testimony. In the KJV it is rendered: false witness.
G5576: From ψευδομάρτυρ; to be an untrue testifier, i.e. offer falsehood in evidence. In the KJV it is rendered: be a false witness.
G5577: From ψευδομάρτυρ; untrue testimony. In the KJV it is rendered: false witness.
G5578: From ψευδής and προφήτης; a spurious prophet, i.e. pretended foreteller or religious impostor. In the KJV it is rendered: false prophet.
G5579: From ψεύδομαι; a falsehood. In the KJV it is rendered: lie, lying.
G5580: From ψευδής and Χριστός; a spurious Messiah. In the KJV it is rendered: false Christ.
G5581: From ψευδής and ὄνομα; untruly named. In the KJV it is rendered: falsely so called.
G5582: From ψεύδομαι; a fabrication, i.e. falsehood. In the KJV it is rendered: lie.
G5583: From ψεύδομαι; a falsifier. In the KJV it is rendered: liar.
G5584: From the base of ψάλλω (compare ψῆφος); to manipulate, i.e. verify by contact; figuratively, to search for. In the KJV it is rendered: feel after, handle, touch.
G5585: From ψῆφος; to use pebbles in enumeration, i.e. (generally) to compute. In the KJV it is rendered: count.
G5586: From the same as ψηλαφάω; a pebble (as worn smooth by handling), i.e. (by implication, of use as a counter or ballot) a verdict (of acquittal) or ticket (of admission); a vote. In the KJV it is rendered: stone, voice.
G5587: From a derivative of psithos (a whisper; by implication, a slander; probably akin to ψεύδομαι); whispering, i.e. secret detraction. In the KJV it is rendered: whispering.
G5588: From the same as ψιθυρισμός; a secret calumniator. In the KJV it is rendered: whisperer.
G5589: Diminutive from a derivative of the base of ψάλλω (meaning a crumb); a little bit or morsel. In the KJV it is rendered: crumb.
G5590: From ψύχω; breath, i.e. (by implication) spirit, abstractly or concretely (the animal sentient principle only; thus distinguished on the one hand from πνεῦμα, which is the rational and immortal soul; and on the other from ζωή, which is mere vitality, even of plants: these terms thus exactly correspond respectively to the Hebrew נָ֫פֶשׁ, ר֫וּחַ and חָי). In the KJV it is rendered: heart (+ -ily), life, mind, soul, + us, + you.
G5591: From ψυχή; sensitive, i.e. animate (in distinction on the one hand from πνευματικός, which is the higher or renovated nature; and on the other from φυσικός, which is the lower or bestial nature). In the KJV it is rendered: natural, sensual.
G5592: From ψύχω; coolness. In the KJV it is rendered: cold.
G5593: From ψύχος; chilly (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: cold.
G5594: A primary verb; to breathe (voluntarily but gently, thus differing on the one hand from πνέω, which denotes properly a forcible respiration; and on the other from the base of ἀήρ, which refers properly to an inanimate breeze), i.e. (by implication, of reduction of temperature by evaporation) to chill (figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: wax cold.
G5595: From the base of ψωμίον; to supply with bits, i.e. (generally) to nourish. In the KJV it is rendered: (bestow to) feed.
G5596: Diminutive from a derivative of the base of ψώχω; a crumb or morsel (as if rubbed off), i.e. a mouthful. In the KJV it is rendered: sop.
G5597: Prolongation from the same base as ψάλλω; to triturate, i.e. (by analogy) to rub out (kernels from husks with the fingers or hand). In the KJV it is rendered: rub.
G5598: The last letter of the Greek alphabet, i.e. (figuratively) the finality. In the KJV it is rendered: Omega.
G5599: A primary interjection; as a sign of the vocative case, O; as a note of exclamation, oh. In the KJV it is rendered: O.
G5600: Including the oblique forms, as well as es; e; etc. the subjunctive of εἰμί; (may, might, can, could, would, should, must, etc.; also with εἰ and its comparative, as well as with other particles) be. In the KJV it is rendered: + appear, are, (may, might, should) be, X have, is, + pass the flower of her age, should stand, were.
G5601: Of Hebrew origin (עוֹבֵד); Obed, an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Obed.
G5602: From an adverb form of ὅδε; in this same spot, i.e. here or hither. In the KJV it is rendered: here, hither, (in) this place, there.
G5603: From ᾄδω; a chant or "ode" (the general term for any words sung; while ὕμνος denotes especially a religious metrical composition, and ψαλμός still more specially, a Hebrew cantillation). In the KJV it is rendered: song.
G5604: Akin to ὀδύνη; a pang or throe, especially of childbirth. In the KJV it is rendered: pain, sorrow, travail.
G5605: From ὠδίν; to experience the pains of parturition (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: travail in (birth).
G5606: Perhaps from the alternate of φέρω; the shoulder (as that on which burdens are borne). In the KJV it is rendered: shoulder.
G5607: Including the feminine ousa; and the neuter on present participle of εἰμί; being. In the KJV it is rendered: be, come, have.
G5608: Middle voice from an apparently primary onos (a sum or price); to purchase (synonymous with the earlier πίμπρημι). In the KJV it is rendered: buy.
G5609: Apparently a primary word; an "egg". In the KJV it is rendered: egg.
G5610: Apparently a primary word; an "hour" (literally or figuratively). In the KJV it is rendered: day, hour, instant, season, X short, (even-)tide, (high) time.
G5611: From ὥρα; belonging to the right hour or season (timely), i.e. (by implication) flourishing (beauteous (figuratively)). In the KJV it is rendered: beautiful.
G5612: Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to "roar". In the KJV it is rendered: roar.
G5613: Probably adverb of comparative from ὅς; which how, i.e. in that manner (very variously used, as follows). In the KJV it is rendered: about, after (that), (according) as (it had been, it were), as soon (as), even as (like), for, how (greatly), like (as, unto), since, so (that), that, to wit, unto, when(-soever), while, X with all speed.
G5614: Of Hebrew origin (יָשַׁע and נָא); oh save!; hosanna (i.e. hoshia-na), an exclamation of adoration. In the KJV it is rendered: hosanna.
G5615: From ὡς and an adverb from αὐτός; as thus, i.e. in the same way. In the KJV it is rendered: even so, likewise, after the same (in like) manner.
G5616: From ὡς and εἰ; as if. In the KJV it is rendered: about, as (it had been, it were), like (as).
G5617: Of Hebrew origin (הוֹשֵׁ֫עַ); Hosee (i.e. Hoshea), an Israelite. In the KJV it is rendered: Osee.
G5618: From ὡς and περ; just as, i.e. exactly like. In the KJV it is rendered: (even, like) as.
G5619: From ὥσπερ and εἰ; just as if, i.e. as it were. In the KJV it is rendered: as.
G5620: From ὡς and τέ; so too, i.e. thus therefore (in various relations of consecution, as follow). In the KJV it is rendered: (insomuch) as, so that (then), (insomuch) that, therefore, to, wherefore.
G5621: Diminutive of οὖς; an earlet, i.e. one of the ears, or perhaps the lobe of the ear. In the KJV it is rendered: ear.
G5622: From a derivative of the base of ὠφέλιμος; usefulness, i.e. benefit. In the KJV it is rendered: advantage, profit.
G5623: From the same as ὠφέλεια; to be useful, i.e. to benefit. In the KJV it is rendered: advantage, better, prevail, profit.
G5624: From a form of ὄφελος; helpful or serviceable, i.e. advantageous. In the KJV it is rendered: profit(-able).
